 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY-This is Ben Marks first season running cross country.Some may have wanted to argue that point Wednesday after the Queen Anne's County High junior ran a sub 5-minute opening mile while building a lead he never relinquished on the way to winning the boys' title at the 51st annual Tidewater Classic."He just has some great natural speed, and he's one of those kids who just loves to run," Queen Anne's head coach Kim Agee said of Marks, who covered the 3-mile course in 16 minutes, 10.80 seconds - 5 seconds ahead of runner-up Jason Baker of Cape Henlopen (Delaware)."He and I chatted just before the (outdoor) track season started last year," Agee said of Marks, who placed third in the 3,200 meters at last spring's Class 2A state outdoor championships. "He started running over the summer and increased his mileage and inceased his mileage. So he came into the season running six and seven miles. He was very solid coming into the season."And he was very solid on this unseasonably warm, sun-splashed afternoon."Number one, he's a natural," Agee said of Marks. "When you watch him run, he's so comfortable and happy out there."Despite those qualities, Marks admitted he went out faster than he wanted over the first mile, clocking a 4:55."I kind of wanted to get out hard, get the early lead; kind of set the pace for the race," Marks said. "But I went out a little too fast. I was shooting for a little over 5, maybe a 5:02,5:03."The fast start didn't hurt Marks, as he worked his way through the course's first loop, glided over the blacktopped stretch shaded by trees before disappearing into the woods. When he reemerged from the trees, he held a 5-to 7-second lead over Baker, who would not get any closer."I was aiming for a really fast time," said Marks, who did not hit a personal-record. "It wasn't the time I wanted today, but I will get there. I felt pretty controlled through it. Unfortunately, I did slow down a little bit. But that's OK I was feeling a little bit off before the race. I'm looking forward to being able to run that time consistently through all three miles."Marks had a familiar follower over the first mile, as Gunston School senior Colin Hallmark stayed close, much like he did during the elite race at Cambridge-South Dorchester's annual Rumble in the Jungle last month."In Rumble in the Jungle, I came out pretty fast," Hallmark said. "I didn't want to get caught with the (lead) pack and so I ended up with Ben. He was running a little bit faster than I could run so I just thought I would stay with him as long as I can."I tried the exact same thing here," Hallmark continued. "We went sub-5 in the first mile, which I was not anticipating. But that's what Ben (did), so that's what I tried to go. I stayed with Ben a long as I can and eventually he pulled away.Eventually Baker and Milford's Nate Waydelis passed Hallmark. But no one else got past the Heron standout, who finished fourth in 16:48.30 - one of only four runners to run under 17 minutes in the boys' field of 347.Led by Baker's runner-up effort - and three other top-25 finishers - Frederick won the boys' team title with 46 points. A distant second was Kent Island, which was led by senior Trey Donnelly's ninth-place finish and sophomore Gunner Hansard finishing 24th."They're pouring it on," said Kent Island assistant Rick Unger, whose top five was rounded out senior Ryan McCann, sophomore Jacob Keever and junior Van Delp. "We've got three seniors. And our sophomores and ninth-graders, they are really getting strong. They see the big picture; what they've got to do to get better. And chasing those seniors doesn't hurt."Indian River (Delaware) senior Brynn Crandell set a new meet record of 17:36.50 on the way to winning the girls' title, breaking the mark set by former Easton star Kathryn Gearhart (18:02). Crandell finished 1:12 ahead of her nearest competitor, Paige Ballinger, an eighthgrader from Sussex Academy (Delaware).Clocking the Mid-Shore's fastest time on the girls' side was Gunston senior Zoe Buzzelli, who finished 13th with a PR of21:03.00."I found someone that was kind of running faster than the pace I wanted to and tried to stick with them," Buzzelli said. "I tried to get out in front a little bit at the start. I'm not a fan of getting caught in the pack in the bottle neck, so I tried to get out in the front for that. And then I just tried to keep a higher tempo than I usually do."Kent County sophomore Aiden Swanson was the top finisher from a North Bayside school in the girls' race, taking 19th in 21:31.20.Notes: There were 30 complete teams in the boys' competition, and five incomplete teams. The girls' field had 28 complete teams - eight incomplete teams - and 248 runners. Stephen Decatur senior Macy Woroniecki had the highest finish from a Bayside school on the girls' side, placing ninth.. Also placing in the boys' top 25 were Cambridge-South Dorchester junior Tekai Drummond (17th), Easton sophomore Jacob Camper (24th) and Easton junior William Orndoff (25th).FIELD HOCKEYGUNSTON 5 INDIAN CREEK 0CROWNSVILLE - Grace Shepherd had two goals and an assist as the Herons improved to 6-2.Layla Kent had one goal and one assist for Gunston, and Abbie Housekencht and Tor Nessly added a goal apiece. Samantha Jayne was credited with an assist.

title: QA's Smith wins playoff for second consecutive crown - Kent Island's Kurtz defends girls' title; Bucs earn runner-up honors
author: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com
content:
QA's Smith wins playoff for second consecutive crown - Kent Island's Kurtz defends girls' title; Bucs earn runner-up honors

 October 11, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: 22A | Section: Sports 
 
 1005
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE - Even on a day when he didn't have his best stuff, Queen Anne's County High's Nate Smith found a way to win.It just took an extra hole.Smith drained a 10-foot putt on the first playoff hole Monday to defeat Stephen Decatur's Kole Kohut by one stroke to win his second consecutive boys' title during the District VIII golf championships at the Hyatt Regency Chesapeake Bay Golf Resort."I thought I left it short," Smith said of his winning putt. "I was kind of shaken a little bit, but it felt good when it kept rolling. I was a little too nervous. Just didn't hit a great putt but it went in." Smith, who won all eight North Bayside tournaments he played in this year, advances to his third straight Class 2A/1A state tournament at the University of Maryland's Golf Course, with the semifinal round slated for Tuesday, Oct.24, and the finals scheduled for Oct.25.Kent Island junior Brianna Kurtz, who for a second straight year did not win a regular-season meet, won her second consecutive girls' district championship with an 83."I don't know," said Kurtz when asked to explain her winning touch at districts. "It's just something about the day of districts. I just put everything that I know into golf and I shoot the best like every year. Last year was the best (round) I ever shot.And this year is now my new best." Kurtz said she was not nervous about defending her title."It was definitely in the back of my mind, trying to defend the number one title," Kurtz said. "But I wasn't necessarily worried about that. I was just focused on shooting good and that's what came out of it." Kurtz will be accompanied to College Park by familiar faces, as Kent Island's Josh David (79), Owen Wynot (81), Grant Ferrier (81) and Steven Nichols (83) totaled a 324 to take runner-up honors in the boys' team competition, finishing 10 strokes behind champion Stephen Decatur."Super impressed with the way they came out," Kent Island firstyear head coach Josh Dishong said of his team. "We had a couple of kids that were veterans coming back, but a lot of new players on the team.They just battled all season and they came out and shot their best round today." Though he admittedly wasn't at his best, Smith carried a one-stroke lead onto the 18th tee. Kohut forged a tie though with a birdie on the final hole while Smith made par, leaving both players at 74 to set up a playoff."I definitely was nervous, but I've been there before," said Smith, who has played multiple playoff rounds in junior tournaments.A junior, Smith hit a 4-iron off the tee on the 350-yard first hole and landed in the middle of the fairway. Kohut used a 3-wood to drive his tee shot an equal distance, though it landed on the right side of the fairway.Kohut's high-arcing second shot bounced on the backside of the flag and rolled before stopping about 35 feet from the hole. Using a 60 angle wedge, Smith neatly chipped within 10 feet of the cup on his second shot.Kohut's lengthy putt looked plenty straight but stopped about 3 feet shy of the hole. Smith then settled over his ball."Pressure was definitely higher this year," Smith said comparing his district play to last year. "Just the way I played all season.Everyone expects me to play well." But the junior blocked all that out."Nothing was going through my head; I was totally blank," Smith said."I was trying to not overthink it and just hit the putt in." And it had just enough on it to drop, bringing a smile to Smith's face and he walked across the green to shake hands with Kohut."He really understands that it's just one hole, and it's one shot at a time," Queen Anne's head coach Brad Niesz said of Smith."He understands you don't get too high, you don't get too low. A lot of people can make a birdie and follow that up with a triple (bogey) because they're so excited about the birdie." North Caroline's Taryn Brandt, who finished second to Smith throughout the season, struggled to a 48 on the front nine, leaving her in jeopardy of getting the 94 needed to qualify for states."I was driving the ball pretty good, but my chipping wasn't the best," Brandt said. "I was more focused on the back nine than the front nine." That was evident, as the junior shot a 38 over the last nine holes for an 86, earning her a second trip to states in three years."She told me on the 10th green that she was going to shoot 10 shots better on the back nine and she shot 10 shots better on the back nine," North Caroline head coach Nash Ireland said of Brandt. "She played great on the back; showed a lot of poise."She has much better scores in her than today," Ireland said. "She finished second for the season in the North Bayside and was the top female. She's having a great year." Seventeen players qualified for states, including North Caroline's Will Davis (83).Qualifying on the girls' side along with Kurtz, was St. Michaels' Lexi Rockwell and Stephen Decatur's Sam Boger, who each shot 85 to finish two strokes behind Kurtz.Also advancing to College Park were Easton's Isabella Westerfield (91) and Queen Anne's Keira Cororan (93).In addition to Kohut's 74, Stephen Decatur got a 77 from Clay McCabe and a 78 from Evan Oglesby, who played in the first group with Kohut, Smith and Brandt. Parkside's Cade Byer (81) and James M. Bennett's Colton Thomas (82) advanced on the boys' side. The qualifying score for the boys was an 83 or under.

title: Sabres ride Webb's goal past Warriors - Freshman's early strike proves decisive in county showdown
author: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com
content:
Sabres ride Webb's goal past Warriors - Freshman's early strike proves decisive in county showdown

 October 11, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: 22A | Section: Sports 
 
 824
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON - Angie Webb wasn't sure what she did.But Saints Peter and Paul High's freshman knew the way her field hockey teammates were celebrating it must have been something good.It also proved to be the difference Tuesday, as Webb ripped the game's lone goal into the right side of the cage with 3:50 remaining in the first quarter, helping the Sabres to a 1-0 victory over Easton."It was a beautiful goal," Sts. Peter & Paul head coach Debbie McQuaid said after the Sabres improved to 10-2 with their fourth straight victory, the last three by shutout.Webb gained possession of the ball from about 25 yards away from Easton's cage near the 4-minute mark of the first period. She circled left, then moved right before unloading a hard drive from the left side that got past Warrior goalie Alli Newman before banging into the far right corner of the cage."My teammates basically helped us all get up the field," Webb said. "I just took it and I don't know what really happened.I was just really determined to get that goal. I knew I had to get off a shot real quickly. I just hit it and it went in. I was really shocked." Easton (5-4) earned two of its nine penalty corners in the final 1:15 of the first quarter, getting one shot off that was wide of the mark. Both teams each picked up one corner in the second quarter, but could not capitalize.The game remained even through the third, as the Warriors picked up three more corners, with Easton's Bis Johnson firing wide left.Sts. Peter & Paul had one corner in the third, with Gennie Webb shooting wide right."They came out and they scored on us, and it was a beautiful goal," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, whose team lost its second straight by shutout. "I do feel like the rest of the game we picked up our pace, we had good passing.I felt like our defense and middies played a really great game."They just struck first and we just couldn't capitalize on our opportunities," Neff continued."We had plenty of corners. We had plenty of shots. We just couldn't put it in today." The Sabres earned their fourth and final corner with 11 minutes remaining but didn't managed anything on goal. Easton had two more corner chances, the last with a minute remaining but could not get the equalizer."We really had the determination to win," Sts. Peter & Paul's Jules Stepp said. "They're our friends, and even though they're our friends, we like to have our friendly competition with them."I really think we communicated well and we looked up and we passed to each other," Stepp continued. author: Natalie Jones; njones@chespub.com
content:
Easton ice cool place to be - Capitals hold practice at Easton Community Center

 EASTON - Local hockey fans enjoyed an unexpected visit from the Washington Capitals Wednesday morning as the team wrapped up their Eastern Shore team building retreat with a practice at the Talbot County Community Center's ice rink.The team's visit to the Mid-Shore kicked off Monday after a practice at the Capitals' home rink in Arlington, about 75 miles away from Talbot County's rink. Team members were spotted visiting RAR Brewing in Cambridge that night, where several lucky fans grabbed photos with a few players.Tuesday's activities included a golf tournament - a warm change from the team's normal playing field."I made (a) couple of shots, but I retire after my hole-in-one," said Capitals captain and left winger Alex Ovechkin, drawing laughs from those gathered around.Capitals head coach Spencer Carbery said he was looking to get the team out of Arlington and into a different environment to prepare for the season opener against the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday, Oct. 14."It looked like a fantastic spot with exactly what we're looking for - to be able to get away, enjoy each other's company, do some team building exercises and be able to skate at a local rink, which also is a really cool experience for a lot of our guys that grew up playing on rinks like this all over the world," he said.He added: "And to be able to change that every once in a while and be able to come out and practice like we are here in Easton is a great opportunity, and I know the guys enjoy it." Right winger T.J. Oshie said the Eastern Shore reminded him of home in some ways."We went and got some crab on the first night, right on the table and paper bags on the side, so I think that was the thing that really stuck out for me," he said after practice Wednesday. "I grew up on Dungeness crab - obviously it's blue crab out here, but it was phenomenal, it was great, felt like I was back at home, but with the fellas." Though the practice was closed to the public, several dozen fans waited outside the community center's hockey entrance for a chance to see their favorite players or grab an autograph.Patrick Allen and his 10-year-old son Kellan were in Canada visiting family Tuesday when they caught wind that the Capitals would be practicing in Easton. The Allens drove home earlier than expected so that Kellan, who plays for the Easton Icehawks, could see his favorite players in person.Grasonville resident Mike Mattison said he took his 9-year-old son Ben out of school for the day for a chance to see the Capitals in Easton."Are you crazy? The opportunity - absolutely," Mattison said of waiting outside the rink for the players."There's got to be a possibility we can at least get an autograph or maybe even get a picture with somebody, so when (Ben) grows up or when he becomes an NHL player, he can show that in 2023 he was here," he said.And by 1 p.m., the Mattisons' mission was successful - Ben's Capitals shirt bore nearly half a dozen signatures from Capitals players.Luke Webber was also on a mission, both for himself and his boss at Mid Shore Graphics."He told me to leave immediately," Webber said, gesturing to a jersey his boss gave him to hopefully get signed. "He told me to come out here, and he was like, 'Take the time.'" And sure enough, the three-hour wait was worth it. Webber succeeded in securing Ovechkin's signature on his boss' jersey and numerous signatures on a special print of the Capitals' logo.For Kent County resident Jaclyn Kelleher, the Capitals' practice in Easton was her lucky third try at seeing the team while they were on the Shore.Kelleher missed seeing the team by 2 minutes when players were spotted at RAR Brewing in Cambridge Monday night, then missed the players signing autographs outside of the ice rink Wednesday morning.But by Wednesday afternoon, Kelleher left the rink happy, her white Ovechkin jersey now bearing Ovechkin's signature and more.The next stop? Framing it.

title: WINNING TOUCH - Bucs answer Easton's triple-block scheme to remain atop division
author: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com
content:
WINNING TOUCH - Bucs answer Easton's triple-block scheme to remain atop division

 October 13, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: 32 | Section: Sports

 Words

 EASTON - Kent Island High head volleyball coach Glenn Brainer admitted Easton has improved since the first time the two teams met Sept. 19."That coach over there, he knows what he's doing," Brainer said of Warrior firstyear head coach James Foo."The first time we beat them three straight, and it wasn't even close. This time every set was close." And while Easton has made adjustments since that first encounter, Kent Island made mid-match adjustments that proved decisive Thursday.Lillian Dauses and Gianna King racked up their share of monster kills, but shifted gears, especially in the third and fourth games, as they began tipping the ball over Easton's triple-block package at the net en route to a 25-20, 19-25, 25-16, 25-18 victory."Triple blocking, we don't usually see that," said Brainer after the Buccaneers improved to 9-1 overall, 8-1 North Bayside. "Now that we've seen that, we've already talked about what we're going to do to counter that. And we started it right there. If they're going to do that then we're going to tip and then hit a couple so the back row can cheat up." With Gabriella Polk serving, Kent Island jumped to a 6-1 lead in the opening game, and three times extended its lead to 10 - the last one at 20-10. But Easton (6-5, 5-5) rallied behind Ayden Jimenez' service game, pulling within 20-16.The Warriors whittled their deficit to 23-20 before Dauses put down a kill and Alana Van Ornum drilled a winner for a 25-20 win.Easton rebounded in the second game, as Parker Jimenez helped serve the hosts to a 5-1 lead. Kent Island chipped away, but wouldn't get any closer than 7-5 as the Warriors, behind some outstanding net play from Kaleigh Hammond, and another Parker Jimenez service run, pushed their lead to as much as 18-10 before a long Bucs' return sealed a 25-19 Easton win."I think what happened in the second game is sometimes the girls are just off a little bit," Brainer said of his team. "And you saw we hit a lot of balls out. We were attacking. But give credit to Easton. Their girls were smacking the ball." Game 3 was back and forth from the beginning and featured six ties.But King tapped a winner for a 10-9 Kent Island lead that was steadily widened.Easton continued to try and rally but a low serve into the net by the Warriors clinched a 25-16 win for the Bucs.Instead of trying to drive the ball through the Warriors, Kent Island began touching more and more winners in the fourth game over Easton's three-blocker scheme.Dauses then took control.The senior touched a winner over three Warriors, blasted a kill off an Easton defender, then made a block, turning a 17-13 Bucs lead into a 20-13 cushion. Easton rallied within 22-18 before hitting a net serve. With Dauses serving, the Warriors hit a return short, then sent another wide to cement Kent Island's 25-18 victory in Game 4.

author: Natalie Jones; njones@chespub.com
content:
St. Michaels YMCA director wins second bodybuilding competition

 ST. MICHAELS - Tracy Eutsler did it again.After competing in and winning her first all-natural bodybuilding competition as an amateur in August, Eutsler kept her momentum going with two additional competitions, but at the pro level this time.Thanks to her first qualifying win, Eutsler, the executive director of the Perkins Family YMCA in St. Michaels, was eligible to compete at the Organization of Competitive Bodies' Yorton Cup in Charlotte, North Carolina in September - an allpro event that's regarded as one of the highest honors for natural bodybuilders to achieve.While Eutsler performed well in the Yorton Cup, earning a second place win in her class and a fifth place win overall, it wasn't until the OCB Chesapeake Classic competition in Baltimore on Saturday, Oct. 7 that Eutsler achieved first place wins at the pro level.Wearing a glittery turquoise competition bikini, Eutsler took to the stage easily to flex and pose, competing first in the pro women's master's 35+ figure category. Nine women competed in the category, which was divided into two classes: taller and shorter, she said.Having competed in three shows now, Eutsler said her confidence in being onstage remained the same. She also experienced a new level of comfort and relaxation with the process that she hadn't felt at first, but some worry about posing remained."There's still that level of nerves that when you're standing up in front of people and you want to do your best, and you can't see what you're doing like you can at home when you're practicing," she said. "There's still in your head (thoughts) like, 'Am I holding this the right way?'" Eutsler placed first in her height class, and the top three winners from both classes went on to compete in the overall pro master's figure competition.After all six women took turns onstage again, Eutsler remembered the anticipation she felt while waiting for the final results.She'd heard it was more difficult to compete against taller women, and as the second and third place winners were announced, she looked at her remaining competitors."I thought, 'Gosh, they've got such nice shoulders and arms,' (I) was like 'I don't know at all, I don't think I've got it,' and then they called my name and I was quite surprised," she said, laughing.The win at Chesapeake Classic, which earned Eutsler a bedazzled championship belt and a $1,500 check, wraps up her competition season for this year, but the work isn't over yet.Eutsler is already planning to compete in two events in 2024: The Conquer, a Baltimore pro competition, along with a trip back to Charlotte for a second try at the Yorton Cup.But before then, she aims to build more muscle mass in her shoulders and back, which means six months of building and two months of leaning out, she said.Eutsler compared her upcoming training period, which is significantly longer than the two months she had to prepare for this year's events, to an artist or sculptor working with a block of clay and trimming it down to reveal what's underneath."I don't know if six months is long enough to put on the size that I want to, but that's the time I'm giving myself, because I don't want to say I'm going to wait until 2025," she said, laughing again. "I need something to work towards." Despite having a diet and training plan, some worries still remain for Eutsler, primarily with building and gaining weight intentionally, something she's never done before."But on a 5-foot, maybe 2-inch, frame, and (as) somebody who's had body image issues as I was going through cheerleading putting an extra 10 to 12, 15 pounds on my body - it worries me how I'm mentally going to handle that," she said.Eutsler shared those worries with friends in social media postings, and found that many reached out thanking her for her candidness in sharing her fears."We all deal with our own issues, right? So, that's mine, and (I'm) just laying it out and being honest with anybody who might ask or want to know," she said. "I may look like I've got everything under control, and I do, but this is my comfort zone, so I'm getting ready to be pushed out of my comfort zone, so we'll see how that goes."

title: BANNER NIGHT - Outten earns 100th career victory as Bucs top Caroline, setting up clash with QA
author: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com
content:
BANNER NIGHT - Outten earns 100th career victory as Bucs top Caroline, setting up clash with QA

 October 18, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: A28 | Section: Sports 
 
 1192
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE - Lin Outten's family started asking him last year how many wins he had."I wasn't sure because we hadn't added them up," said Outten, Kent Island High's boys' head soccer coach. "But I found out our athletic director tracks it." The Buccaneers tracked down victory No. 100 for their coach Monday night with a tightly-contested 2-1 win over North Caroline at Andy Schipul Stadium, then rushed toward Outten with a large blue banner to commemorate the milestone as if they were going to gift-wrap him."That was really cool. I didn't know they made a sign," said Outten, whose career record now stands at 100-21-5 over nine seasons."That was pretty neat. Even spelled my name right."I feel super fortunate that I've had this opportunity to coach here," Outten continued."(Coached) both my boys (Liam and Patrick) for awhile. Coaching now with my friend Steve (Abplanalp); he's my assistant.Our goalie coach Bobby Masters has been with us several years too.And this is just an awesome soccer community and sports community to be apart of. I feel very fortunate." Kent Island (9-1-1 overall, 7-0 North Bayside) will bid for its fifth division title under Outten on Wednesday, when it hosts Queen Anne's (8-1-1, 6-0) at 5:45 p.m. in a match that will determine the North champion."I think we're playing our best right now," said Outten, who almost collected his 100th win last Wednesday at Parkside before the Rams rallied from a two-goal deficit in an eventual 3-3 double-overtime stalemate. "Coming off that Parkside game, we had a good lead in that game, ended up with a draw. Now, we come out here and get a lead as well." Kent Island had multiple chances to take a first-half lead Monday, firing wide left, and banging another drive off the football crossbar over the goal frame in the opening 10 minutes.The Bucs had a third quality chance denied by North Caroline back Yossin Roblero, who stopped a sharp-angled cross at the right post with 16 minutes left in the opening half."I thought we should have gotten one in the first half," said Outten, who later in the half watched Lane Steinbruck unload a hard drive that North Caroline keeper Gavin O'Brien (10 saves) made a chest-high stop on. "He's a very good goalie." The Buccaneers broke through in the 10th minute of the second half, when sophomore forward AJ Miller, after the ball pinballed off seemingly everyone in a crowded goalmouth, parked a right-footed shot into the upper left corner for a 1-0 lead."It was all over the place," Miller said of the ball. "It ricocheted through. I think it (nicked) two people, three people, and I just grabbed the ball, turned around and shot it." A little over 3 minutes later, Kent Island junior midfielder Simon Vujinovic worked a give-and-go with Isaiah Knowles, took a touch to Steinbruck, kept pushing down the left side and drove a left-footed strike into the net for a 2-0 lead."We worked on covering set pieces and we just didn't do the job," North Caroline head coach John Austin said. "We covered the initial set piece really well, and it's like the second or third shot went in, and we just didn't clear it. We just got to be a little more focused on clearing the ball instead of just touching it."They do flood numbers," Austin said of Kent Island. "They're very tall.But we knew that going in. We just didn't defend it well." North Caroline (7-4, 5-2) cut the lead in half with 14:29 remaining when Heath Frantum directed a cross from right wing toward the far post where Kevin Godinez leaped and headed a shot past Bucs keeper Matt Guerra (three saves) into the left side of the net."Goal was really pretty," Austin said."At halftime we talked about, 'Put the ball first time across,' and that's what Heath did; put a ball first time across to Kevin on a beautiful goal."It's two even teams," Austin continued."This is an intense, even high school soccer game. They just got one more than us tonight." Both teams had scoring opportunities over the final 14-plus minutes, but nothing else would get past O'Brien or Guerra."North Caroline did a good job, kind of wrestling back the momentum," Outten said. "But I was really happy with the way we were passing the ball. Such a difficult part of the field (in front of the goal) to play in because it's so crowded. And they got a lot of players back on defense, and we were still able to make good passes between them and through them and around them. I'm glad we got the two, but I wish we could have got more for that effort. That was a lot of shots. We were in front of their goal a lot." The Bucs hope to be in front of the Lions' goal Wednesday in what figures to be another tight contest."I think we're on form," Vujinovic said. "Everyone has been thinking about this game. I think it's going to be the culmination of the (regular) season. But it's not the end. After this game we still have playoffs and we're probably going to go far." title: All things equine - Tuckahoe Equestrian Center holds annual Celebration of the Horse
author: Annie Hasselgren/Special To The Bay Times Record Observer
content:
All things equine - Tuckahoe Equestrian Center holds annual Celebration of the Horse

 October 18, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 QUEEN ANNE - It's an event of all things equine for those who look forward to the annual Celebration of the Horse. Originally created to mark the 25th anniversary of the Tuckahoe Equestrian Center, a family and youth oriented non-profit organization, the Celebration of the Horse has become an annual event. This year's celebration was held Saturday, Oct. 7, despite cloudy skies and wind blown conditions.From plowing fields to military pursuits to companionship, TEC established the Celebration of the Horse to further its mission to promote all things equestrian. The seventh event of its kind, welcomed equestrian enthusiasts at the Center on Crouse Mill Lane to view exhibitions of dressage, mounted archery, sidesaddle riding, and more.As is tradition, the event kicked off with the National Anthem and the reading of Maryland Governor Wes Moore's proclamation continuing October as the Month of the Horse. The proclamation acknowledges Maryland is home to more horses per square mile than any other American state and that the horse industry contributes more than $2 billion per year to the state's economy.Over the day long event, activities began in the main arena with a performance by the Rough Riders, a drill team of about a dozen men and women who perform throughout the Delmarva peninsula. The group captivated the audience with a 30 minute show set to music. The Rough Riders were followed by the Queen Anne's County Pony Express 4-H Drill Team, who performed its routine to music as well. The Club was founded in 1976 and is one of the oldest and most active clubs in Queen Anne's County. The team spends all summer learning that year's routine to prepare for the event.This year, said TEC Treasurer and event organizer Stacy Frank, they had only about half their usual attendance, likely due to the inclement weather. In years past, she said, they average over 300 spectators, 50 horses, and dozens of equine and non-equine vendors and rescue groups."The Celebration of the Horse, is of course to celebrate all things equine," said Frank, "but also aims to promote the fun and love of the sport, and encourage the public to see the enjoyment that comes from horses.The Parade of Breeds showcases horses from Welsh ponies, Gypsy Vanners, Percheron, Shires, Appaloosas, Quarter Horses and Thoroughbreds." "It's a good opportunity, not only to learn more about horses," she said, but allows vendors and exhibitors in the industry to showcase their skills and make connections." Other performers included Heidi Feustel-Ferguson riding sidesaddle, Brendan Wise with Bridleless Dressage, the Parade of Breeds, and many others.Food, vendors, and demonstrations in other areas rounded out the event, including blacksmithing by Oakview Forge.The event was representative of the Tuckahoe Equestrian Center's ongoing efforts to support the equine community in Maryland through youth activities, parades and horse shows."Whether dressage, jumping, driving, jousting, western pleasure or therapeutic or trick riding, we all have something in common," Frank said, "the love of horses and what we do." Formerly Crouse Farm, TEC is a nonprofit organization with a barn, clubhouse, shaded picnic area, a 300'x150' arena, and more than 30 miles of trails. Learn more at www.tuckahoeequstriancenter.com.

title: Maryland author looks at the 'Losing' New York Yankees - Books & Authors
content:
Maryland author looks at the 'Losing' New York Yankees - Books & Authors

 October 19, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: A7 | Section: News 
 
 626
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Swan Point resident William Klink recently penned "The New York Yankees in the Twentieth Century: You Can See a Lot From Losing" through Cambridge Scholars Press.Klink, who is a professor emeritus at the College ofSouthern Maryland, examines the impact of several Yankees, including Miller Huggins' "scientific management," Billy Martin's alcoholism, Joe Torre's group counseling sessions and Whitey Ford's cheating.The co-authors were Bonnie Castleberry ad Diane Gaede.The 146-page book is available at www.amazon.com.HOW LONG HAVE YOU BEEN WRITING, AND HOW DID YOU GET STARTED?I've been writing since high school, when I edited the sports column in the school newspaper. And I continued to write through my undergraduate and graduate degrees and as a professor of English at the College of Southern Maryland.WHAT INSPIRES YOU TO WRITE?Usually I become intrigued by a topic and begin to research it. At a certain point, I decide I want to further explore the topic by writing about it.DO YOU CONSIDER WRITING TO BE A CAREER?No, but part of a successful academic career is writing and publishing.WHAT KIND OF WRITING PROCESS DO YOU USE?Having watched baseball games for seven decades, I've seen a lot of the same things and I've probably missed even more than I've seen, so the book's subtitle, 'You can see a lot just by looking', comes from my exploration of the gap between perception and reality.HOW DID YOU PUBLISH YOUR BOOK?An editor at Cambridge University Press was interested in the book, but decided it wouldn't sell as a textbook, so she recommended Cambridge Scholars Press, which immediately accepted my proposal.WHO ARE SOME OF YOUR FAVORITE AUTHORS AND WHY?I like authors who help me look at issues from a fresh perspective, such as Malcolm Gladwell does in "Outliers." Gladwell influenced me to take a new look at Yankee outliers such as Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez, and Joe Torre.PLEASE INCLUDE A BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF YOUR BOOK"The New York Yankees in the Twentieth Century: You Can See a Lot Just by Looking: is about far more than baseball. As one reviewer said, Dr. Klink discusses "baseball, sports, philosophy, design, leisure, capitalism, and the Yankees" and "quirkily connects these seemingly disparate topics in an often brilliant, always entertaining way."PLEASE INCLUDE AN EXCERPT FROMTHEBOOKFrom the start though, your senses press on you, the sounds of the vendors selling their food, their pennants, and their clothing, cut through the mass of sound created by other fans. In the air is the smell of hot dogs, popcorn, peanuts, Cracker Jack, and jelly apples, all the kinds of foods nannies don't want you to eat. You are clutching your ticket in a tight hand, so you don't lose it and can't get to your seat, and you feel the tension as you press the thin cardboard rectangle. You have to move fast, as people overtake you as you go to your rightful place. There is noise of all sorts, shouting, music, car horns blaring; a cacophony echoes off the concrete that surrounds your moving body, then up up, and then inevitably down you go to your seat. You will be in touch with your seat now for the following hours unless you wander around during the game. When you try to recapture that high moment of entry into Yankee Stadium, home of the gods of baseball, smell, taste, touch, and hearing all work together, but mostly sight dominates. Things are moving, you are moving, faster than your usual gait. Your pulse is high as your brain tries to process what has happened, what is happening, and what will happen. Even the music bounces offyou as ifyou are in a whirlpool of sound.

 CENTREVILLE - Shana Corder said in August her defense was the best she'd had in her 11 years as Queen Anne's County High's head field hockey coach.She wasn't kidding.Aly Edwards and Jordan Bilbo each scored first-half goals, and the defense did not allow Kent Island one shot on goal Wednesday, as the Lions defeated their county rival 2-0 to clinch their first North Bayside championship since 2017."It's the best defense we've ever had come through this school," Corder said of a group that includes goalie Cassidy Alexander and backs Julia Reburn, Abbie Denes and Molly Holthaus. "We didn't give up any corners, and most of our games have been like that."Oh, and for the 10th time in 10 games the Lions (10-0 overall, 5-0 North Bayside) did not give up a goal."They have a very good defense," said Kent Island head coach Laura Harding, who along with Corder and Lions assistant Paul Masucci coached over half Queen Anne's players on Team Chesapeake.Kent Island (7-5, 3-2), which won the last four North Bayside titles, entered Wednesday having won seven of its last eight games. The Bucs managed to get deep into Lions territory in the first half, but as the game progressed, those ventures became rare, especially in the second half when Kent Island only crossed the 50-yard line a handful of times."The defense is doing amazing right now," Corder said. "They're just a great working unit. And kudos to Paul. That's his job. He calls the defense; sets 'em up And we've had this defense since they've all been freshmen. So they're very accustomed to our way and our words."After a scoreless first period, Queen Anne's earned its second penalty corner and converted when Haley Cole dished to Aly Edwards, who pushed the ball past Bucs goalie Brynja Peturs-son with 5:47 remaining in the half."Every day we practice on shooting and getting it down to the goal," Edwards said. "And that's how I got my goal."A little over 3 minutes later, Kent Island earned its third corner of the quarter and again converted, as scored as Gabrielle Scully found Bilbo on the right side and watched her teammate bump the Lions lead to 2-0."We all had some great passing patterns working on the right side," Bilbo said. "And we've been working on circle play down towards the goal, and we just all passed around the goalie. And I happened to be the one to tap it in."Queen Annes' picked up five more corners in the second half - for a 9-0 advantage in the game - but couldn't increase its lead. But the Lions didn't need any more scoring. Seemingly every time Kent Island tried mounting a rush, Reburn, Denes, Holthaus, Elle McLean or Faith Novak got in the way and started working the ball back toward the Bucs' end of the field."We were able to see what they were doing and then we were able to make offense off of it," Corder said. "Just made the adjustment after the first quarter."BOYS' SOCCERQUEEN ANNE'S 3KENT ISLAND 2STEVENSVILLE- Ryan Lee scored a pair of goals and Cooper Nevins had one goal and one assist as the Lions clinched their second North Bayside title in three years.Adan Canales and Nic Esper each had an assist for Queen Anne's County.

title: Letter To The Editor - Athletes doing amazing things
content:
Letter To The Editor - Athletes doing amazing things

 From August to May, students around the Mid-Shore compete in athletic competitions against schools in neighboring counties. These athletes practice several days a week and compete in games and competitions at least two days a week.At the beginning of this year's soccer season I subscribed to the Star Democrat online, anticipating the articles that were sure to be written about all the teams on the Mid-Shore. I remember as a young athlete at Sts. Peter and Paul School the excitement we had when our team would be spotlighted after a big game the evening before. Since the fall sports season started, I've been so disappointed with the amount of coverage these teams receive. Perhaps it's different in the hard copy of the paper, but online articles are published two times a week, maybe?Our son plays soccer for the Kent Island Buccaneers and what an amazing team to watch. I'm continually in awe with the talent and athleticism we are fortunate enough to have a front-row seat to watch. But you know what I don't see? Reporters. Anywhere. No photographers. Only parents there to cheer on their players.I imagine employing enough sports reporters in this area to cover all the games during any given season is a big ask. But just a few, available to cover even just some of the games? Is that too much to ask?Our student athletes do amazing things each and every day - balancing a full course load of classes (and maintaining a certain GPA to remain eligible for the team) while committing to their sport at least five days a week. They deserve some recognition for that.Also any local residents who may no longer have children in the school system: I promise you the money it costs to get into a game to watch these athletes do amazing things is so worth it. You can spend hundreds of dollars to watch the professional athletes compete in a stadium on Sundays; or you can pay $5 to watch your neighbors give it their all on the field. Your heart will beam with pride when watching your local school's team do their very best on the field. You'll be amazed at the level of competition and talent displayed each and every evening - on the soccer pitch, the football field, the field hockey field KIMBERLYMILLERChester

title: SABRES CORNER ANOTHER TITLE - Sweeney, Stepp score as Sts. Peter & Paul wins third conference championship in four years
author: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com
content:
SABRES CORNER ANOTHER TITLE - Sweeney, Stepp score as Sts. Peter & Paul wins third conference championship in four years

 October 20, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: 32 | Section: Sports

 EASTON - They were nervous before the game, and frustrated during it.But in the end those emotions were replaced by smiles, high fives, hugs - individual and group - and pure jubilation.Emmary Sweeney scored early in the third quarter, and Jules Stepp added an insurance goal in the closing minutes Thursday, as Saints Peter and Paul High's field hockey team defeated Gunston, 2-0, to win its third Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference championship in four years."I think our team has grown so much," said senior Gennie Webb, whose overtime goal against Holly Grove lifted the Sabres to the 2020 ESIAC title. "Ever since I was a freshman each year we just grew closer and closer together. And this year I think we bonded so well."I feel like we wanted it so bad and we worked so well today," added Webb, who afterwards was honored as the ESIAC Player of the Year. "We just were not going to let them win. We were dominating the whole game." But the Sabres (14-2) could not score.Sts. Peter & Paul earned four penalty corners in the first quarter, which resulted in Webb firing wide left and Herons goalie Sophia Kent making the first of her 25 saves."She's amazing," Webb said of Kent. "She played a great game today."The Sabres picked up nine more corners in the second quarter, but couldn't stick one past Kent."She's amazing," senior Morgan Quade said of Gunston's goalie. "Her initial saves are just crazy and we worked on trying to get the ball off the pads because she's so good at that initial stop."So many corners," added Quade of the Sabres' 25-0 advantage for the game."We were just like, we didn't know what to do to get it in because we were getting so many opportunities."Sabres senior Cadence Kelley admitted that inability to convert any of the 13 first-half corners got her pondering the unthinkable."It was getting a little sketchy," Kelley said. "I was almost mentally preparing myself like, 'OK, if we lose I have to be prepared.' But then we got that one goal, and I was like, 'We got it.'"And that one goal came from an unlikely source - Sweeney, who'd been sidelined the bulk of the season due to health reasons, and was playing in just her second game of the season.One minute into the second half, the Sabres earned their 14th penalty corner. Again, Kent made an initial stop, but this time Sweeney came in and lifted a rebound into the back of the cage, giving Sts. Peter & Paul a 1-0 lead 1:21 into the third quarter."Just pure excitement," said Sweeney, who was immediately mobbed by her teammates after scoring."Getting that was really special and a good way to end the year. All four years, it just wraps it up. Just a cherry on top. It was very surreal.Amazing."Said Webb: "Emma had a beautiful first goal to start us, boost our confidence. From there we just knew what to do."But the Sabres could not widen their lead, as they continued getting corner chances, but either missed the mark or were foiled by Kent."Just needed to capitalize," Sabres head coach Debbie McQuaid said. "They just needed to take the shot.They (Gunston) were on to our dump to the right, so we just had to start going to a direct shot and hope for the rebound."The Sabres carried their 1-0 lead into the fourth quarter. Gunston (7-3) pushed into the Sabres end a few times before McQuaid called time with 8:26 remaining."Calm down. Slow it down," McQuaid told her team. "Use the clock. Don't rush. Settle back."Sts. Peter & Paul began reestablishing control, field position and corners. Webb then hit a drive that Kent stopped. Webb quickly collected the rebound, spotted and passed to Stepp, who scored to give the Sabres cushion with 2:25 left."That last goal. across the goal and Jules was in the right spot, as she's been most of the year," McQuaid said."I expected Gunston to come out and play hard," McQuaid continued. "And even our last game (a 4-1 Sabres win at Gunston on Sept. 29) when we were up, they never gave up."Sts. Peter & Paul closed the season with an eightgame win streak, with goalie Maddie Maloney logging six shutouts. The Sabres outscored their last eight opponents, 55-2."It feels amazing," Kelley said of the third title in four years. "I'm so glad I got to end my high school career with this. It feels so good."Despite the loss, Gunston head coach Yvonne Gazelle also felt good about her team."Our girls played an amazing game," Gazelle said. "We couldn't get our passes up the field. But I'm proud of them."GIRLS' SOCCEREASTON 4, NORTH CAROLINE 1RIDGELY - Dafny Vasquez had a hat trick and Claire Adelman made 13 saves as Easton clinched the No. 3 seed for the approaching Class 2A East regional playoffs.Kate Adelman added a goal and set up all three of Vasquez's goals as the Warriors improved to 7-5.Maddie McNinch scored for North Caroline.

title: Navy seeks upset of unbeaten Air Force
content:
Navy seeks upset of unbeaten Air Force

 October 20, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 32 | Section: Sports

 Air Force is undefeated, leads its conference and recently joined the Top 25 for the first time in four years.As always, this next game will be a big one for the Falcons.That's because it's against Navy, the first matchup in the annual round-robin competition among service academies in which the Falcons, Midshipmen and Army compete for the Commander-In-Chief's Trophy.Air Force faces Army next month, and then Army and Navy play in their usual December spot."It's always a big deal," said Falcons coach Troy Calhoun, whose team is 6-0 for the first time since 2002. "It just moves you beyond football, too. You have future service members that have made a commitment to do everything they can to make our country a better place. I think that's awesome." No. 22 Air Force is 4-0 in Mountain West play for the first time in program history.Now the Falcons take a break from the conference schedule to face Navy (3-3) on Saturday in Annapolis, Maryland.The home team has won nine of the past 10 games in this series, the lone exception being a 23-3 victory by Air Force at Navy two years ago.The Midshipmen are in their first season after Brian Newberry replaced Ken Niumatalolo as coach.But Newberry was previously Navy's defensive coordinator, so he's plenty familiar with Air Force."Since I've been here, they've been really really good. I think they've won close to 10 games every year since I got here in '19," Newberry said. "They're extremely well coached. I think their personnel is really good. They always have a few really good players, and they always seem to replace them with a few really good players every year."NEXT MAN UPJensen Jones is next on the depth chart for Air Force after Calhoun said this week injured quarterback Zac Larrier will be out "a while."Navy's Braxton Woodson relieved injured QB Tai Lavatai in a 14-0 win over Charlotte last weekend.Newberry wouldn't say what his plan for the position is this weekend.HONOREESNavy is set to honor Roger Staubach and Paul Johnson during the game. That includes putting Staubach's No. 12 on the turf. The star quarterback is one of Navy's two Heisman Trophy winners, along with Joe Bellino, whose No. 27 was placed on the field in 2019.Johnson, who went 45-29 in six seasons as Navy's coach, is being honored after being named to this year's College Football Hall of Fame class.THE STREAKSAir Force has won 11 straight games dating to last season, which is tied for the second-longest streak in team history. The Falcons ran off 13 in a row from 1984-85.Navy is trying for its first three game winning streak since 2019 after beating Charlotte and North Texas.THE TROPHYAir Force won its series-record 21st CIC title last season, beating Navy 13-10 and Army 13-7.The winner visits the White House, where the trophy is presented by the President."Before we start the season, our goals are to be the best we can be as a team, and that includes winning the CIC, going to the White House, being ranked and being conference champions," Falcons running back John Lee Eldridge III said.Navy last won the CIC championship in 2019.MORE CARRIES?Eldridge has carried the ball 34 times for 343 yards and four touchdowns this season. That's 10.1 yards per carry. So why not call on No. 24 more often? Part of the reason is to keep his home-run capability at full power on each rushing attempt."Fair question," Calhoun said. "If you're knocking down shots, how do you not keep finding ways to get that guy open looks? Anything we've ever asked him to do he's been outstanding."For his career, Eldridge is averaging 8.3 yards per carry, which currently makes him the school's all-time leader."Whether it be 10, five, 15, whatever (carries) I get, I know I'm going to leave no regrets out there," Eldridge said.

title: 4-time US Open champion dies at 95
author: Assoclated Press
content:
4-time US Open champion dies at 95

 October 25, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Assoclated Press | Page: 9 | Section: News 
 
 569
 Words

 LEWES, Del. - Betsy Rawls trained to be a physicist and instead devoted her life to golf, first as a fourtime U.S. Women's Open champion and later as a tournament administrator, a remarkable career that landed her in the World Golf Hall of Fame.Rawls, who won eight majors in her 55 LPGA Tour titles, died Saturday at her beach home in Delaware, the LPGA Tour confirmed. She was 95."There are simply not many careers that can compare to Betsy's," said Mike Whan, the CEO of the USGA and former LPGA Tour commissioner.He cited her 55 wins and eight majors - Rawls ranks sixth on both lists - along with her induction into the LPGA and World Golf Hall of Fame, the Bob Jones Award and her 17 years as tournament director of what was then the LPGA Championship."She was a legend in the game who would have been successful in anything she pursued, so we are all lucky she made golf her passion,"Whan said.The intention was always in the field of physics. That's what Rawls was studying at the University ofTexas when she connected with fabled swing coach Harvey Penick. She won the Texas Women's Amateur in 1949 and 1950, and she finished runner-up to Babe Zaharias in the 1950 U.S. Women's Open."I had every intention of being a physicist," Rawls said in a story posted on the LPGA's website. "I played golf for fun and never considered turning professional. Then I decided it would be more fun to be in golf than physics, and Wilson paid me a salary and all my expenses. They paid my expenses for 20 years. One year, I gave 120 clinics."She won the U.S. Women's Open by five shots over Louise Suggs in 1951, the first of four titles in the biggest event in women's golf. Only the late Mickey Wright won as many Opens.Wright once said, "Betsy has always been committed to work and dedicated to the game. I can think of only two women who have achieved as much, not only as players but for their lifetime contributions, and that's Betsy and Patty Berg." Rawls was born May 4, 1928, in Spartanburg, South Carolina, though she moved to Texas in 1940 and grew up mostly in Arlington.She won at least once a year from 1951 through 1965. She won the last of her eight majors at age 41 in the 1969 LPGA Championship by four shots.Rawls led the LPGA Tour money list in 1952 and 1959. She won the Vare Trophy for the lowest scoring average in 1959 and led the LPGA in victories three times.She was part of the inaugural class for the LPGA Hall of Fame in 1967 and in 1996 received the Bob Jones Award, the highest honor by the USGA. She became the first woman to work the men's U.S. Open as a rules official in 1980.She also was the LPGA president in 1961 and 1962, and after retiring from full-time competition in 1975, she worked a tournament director and later ran the LPGA Championship."Anyone who can make a living in golf is lucky," Rawls once said. "Then to receive all the benefits accorded to me in the process well, that makes me feel fortunate. It's more than I could possibly deserve."

title: Clipped - Blankensop's two second-half goals lift Clippers over Queen Anne's
author: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com
content:
Clipped - Blankensop's two second-half goals lift Clippers over Queen Anne's

 October 25, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: 26 | Section: Sports

 STEVENSVILLE - Their first meeting was a draw.Their second encounter was trending in that same direction. For over 70 minutes Monday night, the Queen Anne's County and James M. Bennett High boys' soccer teams pursued every 50-50 ball with unbridled tenacity in a Bayside Conference championship that featured big saves, near misses and collisions at break-neck speed.Then Bennett's Noah Blan-kensop stepped in.Blankensop parked a hard angled shot into the far right corner of the net with 8:37 remaining, then added a second goal on a breakaway less than 3 minutes later, lifting the Clippers to a 2-0 victory over the Lions in the chill ofKent Island High's Andy Schipul Stadium."That was an epic battle for a trophy," Bennett head coach Gabe Kane said after his team improved to 12-0-1 with its ninth shutout of the season. "It's going to take me awhile to settle down. I might sleep sometime tomorrow."Queen Anne's (10-2-1) played Bennett to a 1-1 double-overtime stalemate in Centreville on Oct. 2. Neither had lost since, both teams closing the regular season on five-game winning streaks, with the Clippers yielding just one goal and the Lions four.But Bennett tested Lions keeper Ethan Keppler (8 saves) early. The junior stopped Bennett's Sebastien Dorvelus in the 12th minute, then made another huge save on Grason Adkins a little over 8 minutes later."Ethan's been solid all year long," Queen Anne's head coach Wade Hosler said. "He's been huge for us. He makes huge saves when we need him to. He really does. I'm proud of what we did."Bennett goalie Jake Ziervogel showed why his defensive side has surrendered just three goals all year, stopping a shot off a direct-kick piece with 15 minutes left in the first half, then falling on Ryan Lee's low, hard shot with 6 minutes to go in the half.Keppler capped the first-half goalie showcase by intercepting a Bennett corner kick in the final minute, then made a big stop on Evan Creese 9 minutes into the first half.Queen Anne's Casey McLaughlin made the Lions faithful groan when he took a shot that skidded past Ziervogel and the left post in the 11th minute of the second half. The Lions repeated that near miss from almost the same spot 9 minutes later."Man, Queen Anne's is a heckuva team," Kane said. "He (Hosler) always has them well prepared. There were some scary moments in the second half. But our defense seems to bend tremendously without ever breaking. It's very difficult to get around them."With 9 minutes remaining, Dorvelus blasted a shot that caromed harmlessly off the football crossbar stationed about the soccer goal frame.Then in the 72nd minute, Bennett's Tristan Wieland got a ball on the left wing and found Blankensop, who drilled a hard grounder past Keppler and into the right corner before heading for the far flag in celebration."He's just an elite ball-handler with the ball on the outside," Kane said of Wieland. "And he turned the corner probably three times in the first half and had some great negative passes in their six and we just didn't get on the end of it. Then finally Noah got on the end of one of those cutback passes."We just said their goalie's too good to beat from distance," Kane said of Keppler. "He's too good to beat in front of him. We've got to pass around him and try to get on the back-stick because he was in the zone tonight. That was really the only way around him. That, and the breakaway."That breakaway came with 5:47 remaining. Blankensop settled a ball between the 25 and 30. Then with a defender on his back, the junior spun and broke in alone on Keppler, veered slightly left, before tapping the ball neatly into the right corner for a two-goal lead."He is quite a handful," Kane said of Blankensop. "Just a physical specimen. And honestly, they did well to keep him intact in the first half, 'cause he had two, three really good shots on goal.And their goalie. Man, he's really good. He doesn't just stop it. He catches it and then he kicks it into your half. He's a real weapon defensively."But eventually, Noah gets free," Kane continued. "At this level, he almost doesn't belong. He's a grown man. He'll do anything he possibly can to get a goal. I don't know what you do to contain him because he's got moves. And he's got physicality and a mentality that's just downhill aggression. You don't even have to slip up for him to get around you and beat you."The intense play continued over the final 5:47, with Bennett's Nick Kadera drawing a yellow. Queen Anne's final quality chance came off another direct kick piece, but again Ziervogel made the save."Congratulations to Bennett," Hosler said. "They're a great team. But yeah, it was a good game. I'm proud of our guys. We came out and we fought, and we played the way that we're capable of playing. We played well. We just came up a little short."We've been playing good soccer, especially the second half of the year," Hosler continued. "This is a really good 3A team and we played with them twice. So it gives us encouragement and confidence going into the 2As (playoffs), that if we play to our potential we're going to be tough to beat."

 COLLEGE PARK - In Kevin Willard's first season as Maryland coach, the Terrapins made it to the NCAA Tournament and won a first-round game.They also had one obvious area for improvement."I always respected the Big Ten looking at it from the outside," Willard said. "Going through the league was really eye-opening. I learned a lot about how we have to play at home to win, how you have to play on the road to win - which we didn't do a good job of, obviously, last year."The Terps went 16-1 at home, 2-9 on the road and 4-3 at neutral sites in 202223. That wasn't such a bad tradeoff for a new coach - if you're trying to win over a fan base, playing well at home is an important first step. Still, if Maryland is going to compete for Big Ten titles, the Terrapins are going to need more success on opposing courts.Maryland returns three of its top four scorers from last season in Jahmir Young, Donta Scott and Julian Reese. Young averaged 15.8 points per game in his first season with the Terps after transferring from Charlotte.Scott is entering his fifth season at Maryland and has scored 1,320 points in his career."Practices have been unbelievable. We can't go that long because they're so competitive, they're so physical," Willard said. "We look like a Big Ten team, where last year we had to really fight to be a Big Ten team. This year we look like a Big Ten team, and I think we can compete a little bit higher level because of that."FROM THE PORTALThe Terps welcome 6-foot-6 transfer Jordan Geronimo, who played three seasons at Indiana. He averaged 4.2 points last season with the Hoosiers.Willard said Maryland's 73-51 loss to top-seeded Alabama in the NCAA Tournament last season made his team's shortcomings clear."We really needed to change our athleticism. Again, I had a great team last year. They were so fun to coach, but there was some limits on what we could do physically and athletically," he said.Mady Traore, a transfer from New Mexico State, brings some size to the roster at 6-11.SOLID CLASSMaryland has the nation's No. 19 recruiting class arriving this season, according to 247 Sports. Guards DeShawn Harris-Smith and Jaime Kaiser were both four-star recruits."Our freshman class is the best freshman class I've ever had," said Willard, who previously coached at Seton Hall. "DeShawn Harris-Smith is by far the most talented player, probably the most physically gifted basketball player I've ever been able to coach so far. Jamie Kaiser was a former quarterback and played football. So they've been able to come in with Jordan and really kind of embrace how we want to play at the level we want to play at."

title: Record Days - Novak's penalty stroke in double overtime lifts Queen Anne's to first conference title in school history
author: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com
content:
Record Days - Novak's penalty stroke in double overtime lifts Queen Anne's to first conference title in school history

 October 26, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: 18 | Section: Sports

 CENTREVILLE - There are birthday celebrations and then there are well, birthday celebrations.So how did Queen Anne's County High senior Faith Novak celebrate her 18 th birthday? By making history.Novak scored on a penalty stroke with 1 minute, 4 seconds remaining in the second overtime period Tuesday night, lifting Queen Anne's County to its first Bayside Conference field hockey championship in school history with a 1-0 victory over Pocomoke at Lions Stadium."I knew if I didn't put it in we'd have to do strokes and shootouts anyway," Novak said. "So I just really wanted to put it in and finish it off for my team."Novak did just that, firing a rising shot past Warrior goalie Maddie Castaneda into the left side of the cage. N ovak then turned toward her teammates and let out a victory scream that was soon muffled when she was buried under a avalanche ofjubilant teammates."I'm just happy for the girls," Queen Anne's head coach Shana Corder said after the Lions improved to 13-0 with their 12th shutout of the season. "I was talking to them about our (2021 Class 2A) state championship team with softball. I just told them, 'That feeling is like no other.' I want them to feel what (former head softball coach) Kimmy (Betts) and I felt and those girls."It doesn't happen for Queen Anne's County much," Corder continued of championships. "We're not like these schools like the Broadnecks and the Pocomokes that get championship after championship. I want them to feel what I feel. I've been telling them for weeks, 'Pressure is a priv-ilege.'This game was pressure. Being undefeated was pressure. I really wanted this for these kids."Queen Anne's opened its season Sept. 11 with a 1-0 overtime victory over Pocomoke, the defending Class 1A state champion. Forty-three days later, the Lions and Warriors (9-4) had played yet another 60 minutes of scoreless regulation, and solved nothing through one 10-minute overtime.Then with 2 minutes remaining in the second overtime, Queen Anne's Jordan Bilbo sprinted downfield on a breakaway. Bilbo slowed down as she got inside the circle and drew a breakdown foul on Pocomoke, setting up Novak's stroke."As soon as I saw Jen, the umpire, go stroke, I immediately called for Faith to take the stroke," Corder said. "I have full confidence in her. I put my clipboard in my book bag 'cause I knew she was going to score and I zipped up because I was ready to celebrate."I have confidence in these kids because I know what they can do," Corder continued. "We spend so much time on mental mentality. We just did a video on it today. I knew mentally she was ready for that moment."And while Corder had no doubt she'd made the right choice for the shot, Novak's nerves were getting a real workout."I was really nervous," Novak said. "I always have a ritual that I do (on a stroke). I take a step back, do two bounces, and then I let it rip. I was really nervous because I wanted to do really well for my team. I really wanted to put it in the back of the net. I love going to the left side. Every now and then I change it up and go opposite. But I like that back corner."Pocomoke has an amazing team, so I really wanted to finish it off right there," Novak added. "We really had to bring it. We were all about a fighting championship mentality; all teamwork. I can't take credit for the one goal. Everyone getting up there, the person (Bilbo) that earned the stroke. It's all them too just as it is mine. "There was a second part to championship talk given by Corder, whose team received a first-round bye in the Class 2A East Regional playoffs."It was a blessing for us, when we found out we got the bye on Thursday," Corder said. "My message to the girls was, 'You have no excuse. You have a whole week off to rest these legs.'They were tired from (Monday night's 3-1 victory at Stephen Decatur). But I told them 'Ifyou guys want this championship and make school history, play 60 minutes' -well, we played 80. 'Just leave it out here on the field right now. You can rest tomorrow.'"The Lions finished with an 11-2 advantage in penalty corners."They gave it their all," Pocomoke head coach Kasey Hickman said of her team."We asked them to play with heart and give 110 percent, and that's what they did. It just didn't unfortunately come out in our favor tonight. Everybody played their part, especially our defense."

title: QA's Marks sets conference, course records on way to title - Donnelly leads Kent Island to boys' team crown
author: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com
content:
QA's Marks sets conference, course records on way to title - Donnelly leads Kent Island to boys' team crown

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: 18 | Section: Sports

 CAMBRIDGE - Ben Marks set goals at the outset of this his first cross country season.But the Queen Anne's County High junior admitted he wasn't necessarily looking for a certain time Wednesday at the annual Bayside Conference championships at Cambridge-South Dorchester."I was kind of like, I'm on a flat course," Marks said. "Let's just see what I got."What Marks got on this warm, yet beautiful autumn afternoon was a new course and conference record, clocking a first-place time of 15 minutes, 17.94 seconds to become Queen Anne's first boys' individual champion since Mike Rea in 1997."My plan was like, 'Put it all out there," said Marks after breaking the previous conference (15:28.54) and course (15:24.72) records set by Kent Island's Finn Walsh in 2019. "I originally had goals that I set at the beginning of the season, just like lofty goals. Like, 'Oh, I 'm going to do this.' And I think I'm finally getting there."Bayside record was a goal," Marks continued. "It was a medium goal. Like'Get that, and then more.' That was a start."Marks wasted little time in moving to the front of the pack from the start yesterday, and had already established a substantial lead by the time he emerged from the woods the first time."Didn't want to go out too hard," Marks said. "I wanted to even split the race. I went out just under five (minutes) and then I came through at mile two around 10:03. So kind of even. The last mile was a little slow."Marks' final mile may have been a bit slower than his first two, but his final kick was anything but, as he blazed toward the finish line, winning by a 1:33 margin."It was that kick at the end that got me that time," said Marks, who blew his old personal-record away by a stunning 18 seconds."Not surprised, but always impressed for sure," Queen Anne's head coach Kim Agee said of Marks. "But not surprised because he's been working towards that. He's had a couple of races where he's definitely in the 15s. And so he was looking for that course record."Kent Island senior Trey Donnelly was also looking for something yesterday, and made that objective clear to his teammates in a pre-race huddle."KI's b een going at it for years, ever since our school's been built," Donnelly said of the Bucs' rich cross country tradition at the conference level. "We've always dominated the Baysides almost every single year and I told our guys, 'You know there's a team (Stephen Decatur) ranked ahead of us and we've got to show them who we are and make that ours.'"Donnelly and company did that, totaling 70 points to defeat the Seahawks by 18 points en route to winning their 14th boys' team championship in 17 years."I told our guys, 'If you see a Decatur guy ahead of you, make sure you beat 'em because this is our Bayside championship,'" Donnelly said. "'We got to take it.'"Donnelly did his part, taking runner-up honors to Marks in a personal-record 16:50.82. Following Donnelly were teammates Gunner Hansard (4th, 17:12.06), Giovanni Aguirre (19th, 18:00.15); Ryan McCann (21st, 18:01.64) and Oliver Redgraves (24th, 18:12.92)."This feels amazing," Donnelly said. "Finished strong for my last race, especially at this course. It's my favorite course."Kent Island's second straight conference title was also the first for new head coach Andrew MacIntire."Felt very confident," MacIn-tire said of the Bucs' chances for another crown. "We put the work in all season long. We made sure week in and week out we ran in large groups because we have a lot of competition from the top all the way down to the bottom. They used their watches. They kept track of their times. They knew exactly what to do coming into today."We have a lot of experience around us," MacIntire continued. "I just pulled from my expertise around me, and I just knew that we had a lot going for us in the right direction, and we just pulled through. I'm happy for them. They absolutely deserve this."Cambridge-South Dorchester's Tekai Drummond was third (16:57.78), as the Vikings finished one point behind Decatur in the boys' team standings with 89. Easton's William Ornd-off was fifth (17:22.31), and Cambridge-SD's Josiah Harris (17:32.39) and Preston Adkins (17:34.75) finished ninth and 10th, respectively.Parkside sophomore Logan Newton won the girls' individual competition with a winning mark of20:24.02, becoming the Rams' first female champion since Hailey Spinapont in 2009.Paced by senior Macy Woroniecki's second-place finish (20:39.71), Stephen Decatur won the girls' team championship for the first time since 2008, as the Seahawks (41 points) easily outpointed defending champion Kent Island by 33 points.Cambridge-SD junior Cam-ryn Russum was the top North Bayside finisher, placing fourth in 20:59.34. Kent Island's Gabrielle Bernhard (6th, 21:32.58), North Caroline's Brooke Sullivan (7th, 21:36.45), North Dorchester's Adison Thomas (ninth, 21:52.66), and Kent Island's Kaitlyn Stevens (10th, 22:01.03) rounded out the top 10 from North schools.
