title: Lions ride 1-2 punch past Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions ride 1-2 punch past Easton

 January 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 850
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Queen Anne's County High's Bea Holthaus and Laila Coles are one of the top freshmen combinations to hit the North Bayside hardwood in a long, long time.But Lions girls' head basketball coach Mike Kern knows there are going to be nights when his team isn't at its best.
Tuesday was shaping up to be one of those nights, as Easton went on an 8-0 run to open the second half for one-point lead. But that only seemed to wake up the Lions, who proceeded to go on a 17-3 tear to close the third quarter on the way to a 53-42 victory.
"We're young," said Kern, whose team improved to 14-0 overall, 12-0 North Bayside. "We're playing in a tough environment. We're going to have these games where we don't play our best. But will still overcome. I'm proud of them for overcoming."
Holthaus, who had a game-high 25 points to go with 13 rebounds and five blocked shots, and Coles (16 points) helped Queen Anne's build a 24-17 halftime lead.
But Easton (7-8, 7-5), which lost to the Lions by 32 on Jan. 2 in Centreville, erased that deficit in the opening two minutes of the second half. Addison Chandler (10 points) buried a 3-pointer. Sisi Sama (10 points) scored inside, hit one of two free throws, then drove the lane for a basket and a 25-24 Warriors lead.
"I thought Easton came out a little hungrier than we were tonight," Kern said. "And they out-rebounded us, which is a little disappointing. But they were going hard to the ball. I think Easton deserves a lot of credit. They did a great job on the boards. And they were getting second and third opportunities, and that's what kept them in the game. We've got to do better."
The Lions may not have done better immediately on the glass, but they improved on the scoreboard. After Kern called time with 5:45 remaining in the third, Queen Anne's returned to the floor and took control of the game, outscoring the Warriors 25-5 over the next 7-plus minutes.
Leading the charge was Holthaus, who accounted for 17 points in the surge, which included burying three baseline jumpers and a 5-for-6 effort from the foul line.
"Bea is just a phenomenal athlete," Kern said. "She's sees the court really well. She makes everybody around her better. She's very unselfish. She can go inside. She can go outside. She's an all-around player. We're lucky to have her for four years."
The same can be said of Coles, who in addition to her 16 points, totaled seven steals, five assists and five rebounds.
"Her (Holthaus) and Coles both as freshmen are just going to be amazing kids coming up," Easton head coach Lesley Staehli said.
And while Holthaus and Coles proved a formidable one-two punch, the Warriors hurt themselves with a 10-for-25 performance from the free-throw line.
"We missed 15 free throws," Staehli said. "Had we made some of them, and then stopped the turnovers; taken care of the ball a little bit better (against Coles). And then shutting Bea down a little bit with hands in her face with her shot."
Queen Anne's 17-3 surge to close the third, and an 8-2 burst to open the fourth gave it a 49-30 cushion with 6:21 remaining. Easton made the score more respectable as Chandler's third 3-pointer of the game started a 12-4 Warriors' game-ending run.
"We did well I thought considering we got blown out the last time we played them," said Staehli, who got a team-high 11 points from Kate Adelman and 10 from Serenity Velez. "But we're going to be working on our foul shots."

title: Four players charged with sexual assault
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Four players charged with sexual assault

 January 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 796
 Words 

 Read News Document

 NHL players Carter Hart of the Philadelphia Flyers, Michael McLeod and Cal Foote of the New Jersey Devils and Dillon Dube of the Calgary Flames have been charged with sexual assault in connection with an alleged assault by several members of Canada's 2018 world junior team.Attorneys representing Hart, McLeod, Foote and Dube said Tuesday that each player has been charged with sexual assault by police in London, Ontario. They denied any wrongdoing on behalf of their clients.
Hart's lawyers, Megan Savard and Riaz Sayani, said their client is facing one count of sexual assault, adding, "He is innocent and will provide a full response to this false accusation in the proper forum, a court of law."
Legal teams representing McLeod and Dube said the players would be pleading not guilty.
"(We) will vigorously defend the case," McLeod's attorneys, David Humphrey and Seth Weinstein, said in a statement. "We ask that the public respect Mr. McLeod's privacy, and his family's privacy. Because the matter is now before the court, we will not comment further at this time."
Dube's lawyers, Louis Strezos and Kayleigh Davidson, said their client "maintains his innocence (and) will defend the allegations in court."
Foote's lawyer, Julianna Greenspan, said her client was "innocent of the charge and will defend himself against this allegation to clear his name."
"What is most critical at this time is the presumption of innocence, and the right to a fair trial that everyone in Canada is entitled to," Greenspan said in a statement emailed to The Associated Press. "As the matter is before the court, I ask that Cal's and his family's privacy be respected."
A Devils spokesperson said the organization is aware of the reports and have been told to refer all inquiries to the league. A Flyers spokesman echoed a similar sentiment, saying the team "will respond appropriately to this very serious matter when the outcomes of the investigations are made public."
"We have now become aware of the charge of sexual assault that has been laid against Dillon Dube," the Flames said in a statement. "We take this matter very seriously. Because the matter is now pending legal proceedings, we will have no further comment at this time."
The NHL was not expected to address the situation Tuesday. Commissioner Gary Bettman is set to speak at the league's upcoming All-Star Weekend.
The latest developments in the case come two days after former NHL player Alex Formenton surrendered to police to face charges. Attorney Daniel Brown said Formenton is innocent "and asks that people not rush to judgment without hearing all of the evidence."
All five players have taken leave from their current clubs over the past 10 days. Their agents have not spoken publicly since.
London police have scheduled a news conference for Monday to address the situation. A spokesperson for police told the AP by email no updates on the investigation will be provided before the news conference.
London police launched their investigation in 2022 after it was disclosed that Hockey Canada had settled a lawsuit with a woman who said she was sexually assaulted by eight members of that gold medal-winning team after a Hockey Canada Foundation fundraising gala. London is approximately halfway between Toronto and Detroit.
According to court documents, the woman, then 20, alleged that a man, identified only as "John Doe #1," took her from a bar to a hotel room and invited seven other people into the room to perform undisclosed sexual acts, intimidating her and preventing her from leaving. The woman said in the lawsuit the men directed her to take a shower and asked her to say on video that she was sober.
The woman sought $3.55 million in damages and dropped the lawsuit after reaching a settlement with Hockey Canada.
The NHL opened its own investigation in 2022 and has pledged to make those findings public. Deputy Commissioner Bill Daly last week said the league would issue a statement if and when it is appropriate.
The Flyers said Hart requested and was granted a leave of absence for personal reasons. General manager Daniel Briere declined to provide details when asked follow-up questions related to the 25-year-old No. 1 goaltender's departure.
The Devils did not give a reason when announcing McLeod and Foote were granted indefinite leaves of absence. McLeod, who turns 26 on Saturday, is in the middle of his fourth full season with the team, while Foote — son of former NHL player Adam Foote — has spent much of this season in the American Hockey League and appeared in four games for New Jersey.
The Flames said Dube was on indefinite leave to tend to his mental health. As part of their statement Tuesday, they said they "had no knowledge of pending charges at the time Dillon's request for a leave of absence was granted."
The 25-year-old Dube has played for Calgary since 2018.

title: Ripken, Hill part O's buy-in team
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Ripken, Hill part O's buy-in team

 January 31, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 718
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Cal Ripken Jr. and Grant Hill are part of the investor group that has agreed to buy the Baltimore Orioles, and so are former New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg and former Baltimore Mayor Kurt Schmoke.The group is headed by Baltimore native David Rubenstein, co-founder of the Carlyle Group. Additional investors were revealed in a news release Wednesday announcing the agreement between Rubenstein and the Angelos family.
"I am excited to once again be a part of the Orioles organization and I thank David for including me in the ownership group," Ripken said in a statement. "The Orioles have been a part of my life since I was a child, and this is a special day."
The Angelos family has run the team for the past three decades and is selling a control stake in the team to Rubenstein for $1.725 billion.
"I am grateful to the Angelos family for the opportunity to join the team I have been a fan of my entire life. I look forward to working with all the Orioles owners, players and staff to build upon the incredible success the team has achieved in recent seasons," Rubenstein said. "Our collective goal will be to bring a World Series trophy back to the city of Baltimore. To the fans I say: We do it for you and can't do it without you."
John Angelos, the club's current chairman, will remain as a senior adviser.
"I am personally committed to helping David and his partners take the franchise to the next level," Angelos said. "We think this transaction is great for Major League Baseball and great for the city of Baltimore and Maryland. We are thankful to the fans and supporters cheering on the O's as we reached this important goal — and who will be with us celebrating more success to come."
Rubenstein's investment team includes Ripken and Hill, who in addition to being Hall of Famers in baseball and basketball have ties to the extended area. Ripken, of course, is an Orioles legend who was born in Havre de Grace, Maryland. Hill is from northern Virginia, not far from Washington.
Other members of the investment group include Bloomberg, Schmoke, Ares Management co-founder Michael Arougheti, Ares Credit Group co-heads Mitchell Goldstein and Michael Smith, and Cognosante founder Michele Kang, who also owns the Washington Spirit of the NWSL.
The sale is subject to a full vote of Major League Baseball ownership and must receive 75% approval.
The Angelos family has been in control of the Orioles since 1993, when Peter Angelos purchased the team for $173 million. Angelos' son John is the team's current chairman, and the Orioles recently reached a deal on a new lease extension at Camden Yards.
"Governor Moore, the Maryland Stadium Authority, and the entire Moore-Miller Administration send their congratulations to Baltimore native David Rubenstein, Michael Bloomberg, Kurt Schmoke, Mike Arougheti, NBA legend Grant Hill, and Maryland native and Orioles legend Cal Ripken Jr. on their deal to purchase the Baltimore Orioles. The governor looks forward to continuing the strong relationship between the State of Maryland and the Baltimore Orioles," said Carter Elliott, a spokesman for Maryland Gov. Wes Moore.
"Governor Moore would like to thank the Angelos family for their contributions to the Orioles community and this storied franchise. Keeping the Orioles in Baltimore for the long term was a key priority for this administration and we are proud that this transaction won't change that."
The Angelos family will keep a significant investment in the team.
"When I took on the role of chair and CEO of the Orioles, we had the objective of restoring the franchise to elite status in major league sports, keeping the team in Baltimore for years to come, and revitalizing our partnership group," John Angelos said. "This relationship with David Rubenstein and his partners validates that we have not only met but exceeded our goals."
The Orioles won 101 games last season, their most since 1979, and their future is bright thanks to young stars Adley Rutschman and Gunnar Henderson — as well as a farm system that has remained loaded even as top prospects moved on to the big leagues.
The team's low payroll has been a sore spot with fans, but this sale offers hope that the Orioles might spend aggressively enough to make the most of the impressive foundation of talent they've built in recent years.

title: Buccaneers fall to Decatur, bounce back against Tech
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Buccaneers fall to Decatur, bounce back against Tech

 February 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1052
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — The streak — which unofficially reached 61 consecutive victories against Bayside Conference opponents Wednesday night — is not the overwhelming driving force.No, what really pushes Stephen Decatur High's wrestling team is the idea it won't be good enough after graduating its state champions and finishers from the previous year.
"The kids know we haven't lost a Bayside match in awhile," Seahawks head coach Josh August said. "But I feel like each year, we have like really good guys, state champs that graduated and go off to college, and then the guys that are left feel like they have something to prove. Because when you have a state champ, or two state champs leave, (people) think that you are not going to be as good. I think our guys use that to motivate themselves, keep on carrying on with the wins and making states."
Decatur kept carrying on Wednesday night, routing non-conference foe Harford Vo-Tech, 61-9, before defeating Kent Island, 44-23, to extend its Bayside dominance while remaining undefeated heading Friday's showdown with unbeaten Rising Sun.
"I thought we wrestled really good against Harford Tech," said August, after the Seahawks improved to 13-0 overall, 10-0 Bayside. "Some of our guys stepped up big, went up a couple weights for the Kent Island match. Not a lot of guys do that. We got guys wanting to wrestle big matches. Overall, I think the team is clicking pretty good."
Overall, Kent Island head coach Tommy Sitar was happy with how his team battled against Decatur, which routed the Buccaneers, 60-18 at the Iron Duals in early January.
"We won only three matches against them," Sitar said of the Iron Horse dual against Decatur. "(Tonight) we won six matches, doubled our output, which is nice."
Perhaps the nicest part of the Decatur match for Kent Island was after losing the first three weight classes to Juan Hinojosa (113), Liam Hugues (120) and Reid Caimi (126) by pin to fall behind 18-0, the Bucs (10-3, 8-1) won the next four weights to pull within 18-14.
"They definitely looked strong," Sitar said of Silas Brobst (132), Greg Couch (138), Cody Sandefer (144) and Ashton Main (150). "I was impressed with the way they were able to dictate to the other wrestlers what was going to happen."
Brobst start the mini-rally when he went into overtime tied 1-1 with Aaron August then scored a takedown with 26 seconds left in the 1-minute overtime for a 3-1 sudden victory.
"Silas wrestled his best match definitely on his feet," Sitar said. "The way he was moving and setting him up was awesome."
Kent Island's next three wrestlers would each score the first takedown in their respective matches. Couch scored a late takedown for a 9-1 major decision over Jake Saullo. Sandefer built a 10-0 lead over two periods en route to a 12-3 major over Alex Riehl. Main capped the run with a 10-3 decision over Braydon Bell at 150.
Despite having its lead trimmed to four, Coach August was pleased with how his team wrestled through the middleweights.
"The score looked closer than the last time we went against Kent Island," Josh August said. "They're a solid team every year. We came away with the victory. It was a little close in the middle, but they are strong right there. One of our things was our guys weren't getting pinned. Our guys that were outmatched were hanging in there, wrestling the full six minutes."
The Seahawks seized full control from there, packaging three pinfalls and two major decisions over the next five bouts for a 44-23 lead.
Decatur's Amarian Manuel earned a 16-8 major over Brandon Adler at 157. Parker Intrieri pinned Chris Kougoures in 47 seconds at 165. Gavin Solito — wrestling up from 157 — put together a 9-1 major over Giuseppe Mellinger at 175. Kole Kohut (190) pinned Brian Potter in 1:49, and Nate McDaniel pinned Nick Morey with 28 seconds remaining in the 215-pound match.
"I think it's an expectation by them," Josh August said of his team's mindset. "It's an expectation that they wrestle to the level to get there, not that they are just going to get there."
Kent Island came back to win the last two bouts, Greg Coffey winning a 4-2 decision over Price Hill at 285, and Gavin Lindner pinning Jaxon Archer in 3:08 at 106.
The 21-point difference was the closest any Bayside team has come to Decatur this season.
The Bucs fell behind 7-0 to Harford Vo Tech, but then regrouped to win 10 of the remaining 12 bouts, which included pinfalls from Couch (138), Adler (157), Kougoures (166), Potter (190), Morey (215), Coffey (285) and Lindner (106).
"I talked to the guys after the Decatur match 'cause it appeared we started at a weight (120) where had kind of a letdown," Sitar said. "I let them know, 'We're peaking. We haven't peaked. Decatur was not the peak. We don't stop now just because we wrestled a team tough. We keep on peaking."
Wedged in the Bucs' rally was Sitar's decision to insert Potter, a 175-pound backup, in at 190 and bump Morey from 190 to 215.
"At the end of the match we had a situation where we were going to be (potentially) down 15 with five bouts left, or we could be down potentially 15 with three bouts left," Sitar said. "So I opted with the strategy of going down 15 with three bouts, and bumped our 190 (Morey) to 215, where I was 100 percent sure he could get a pinfall. And our backup 175-pounder, Brian Potter ended up getting a pin over Jack Ryder of Harford Tech, who I guess was ranked in the state."
Brobst won a 13-3 major decision at 132 and Sandefer got a 7-3 decision at 144 to help the Bucs take a 13-7 lead. Tech's Ryan Sewell pinned Main at 150 to tie the match at 13-all before Kent Island won the next seven straight matches, which included a 6-2 decision by Mellinger at 175.
"It's nice to immediately erase it from the forefront," Sitar said of coming back and beating Harford Tech after the Decatur loss.
Notes: Kent Island's three losses this season have come against Decatur, which is bidding for a fifth consecutive state dual-meet title — excluding the COVID-19 canceled 2021 season — two-time defending 1A state dual-meet champ and unbeaten South Carroll, and Class 4A Broadneck (9-3).

title: Clark, Iowa drawing sold-out crowds even on the road
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Clark, Iowa drawing sold-out crowds even on the road

 February 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 887
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Caitlin Clark has been a must-see attraction all season, with sold-out arenas where some tickets have gone for thousands of dollars on the secondary market.The prices are only expected to go higher as the Iowa star approaches the NCAA all-time scoring record over the next few weeks.
While teams like Tennessee and UConn would draw huge crowds on the road in the past and South Carolina has had a strong fan base the last few years, Clark is different. There has never been anything like it in women's basketball when an individual player has drawn so much interest from fans wanting to see her play.
"Nobody's ever had a player like this. She's a combination of Pete Maravich and Steph Curry," said Fox announcer Gus Johnson. "She plays in a different dimension and realm. Her ability to see, understand and anticipate the game and then from a physical aspect shoot the ball from almost anywhere when she gets into the frontcourt. Not even Diana Taurasi had this kind of range."
Schools that have hosted Iowa have seen an attendance increase over 150% compared to their other home games on average. Northwestern had the first sellout in school history on Wednesday night when Clark and Iowa came to visit.
According to ticket marketplace Vivid Seats, the top five most in-demand NCAA women's games this year have featured Iowa. The average price of tickets for the Hawkeyes since Clark joined the team in 2020 is up 224% and the average distance traveled by a fan to watch Iowa play is up 34% from last season.
"It's honestly, hard for me to wrap my head around. It's crazy, it's crazy the way people scream my name and really support us and I try to make time for as many as them as I can," Clark said. "Like whenever I walk off the court, it's so special just the way people scream our names and are so excited for our team. And that's something that never gets old. I was that kid a few years back, so it's crazy how time flies and I just try to soak it all in, every single moment."
It's not just kids who want to see Clark and her deep 3's in action.
Former Iowa high school teammates Susan Johnstad, Deb Littlefield and Stephanie Fournier met at the Iowa-Rutgers game on Jan. 5 in Piscataway, New Jersey. They played basketball and softball together at Roland Story High School, about 45 miles from where Clark grew up in Des Moines.
"It's been 30 years since we've all been together," said Johnstad, who suggested they travel from their current homes in Virginia, Massachusetts and Iowa to watch Clark. "We played six-on-six basketball, and Iowa has such a tradition of supporting women's basketball. Clark's skill set is just amazing. In her recent commercial for Gatorade, she said she dreams big — and it shows."
Johnstad says she's proud to see the joy last year's AP player of the year brings to fans wearing her No. 22 jersey, young and old.
"I'm a fan girl, for sure," said Johnstad, who is an administrator at Virginia Tech. "I can see her play on television. But (it's fun) to be able to see the people lined up beforehand and the girls working on their signs and doing the face paints."
Clark is part of a new generation of stars that fans can easily and constantly see, through highlights on social media and games available on a whole host of networks and streaming services.
Back when Candace Parker, Diana Taurasi, Maya Moore and Sheryl Swoopes were dominating the game it was harder to see them play. Twitter and Instagram weren't around — YouTube was launched in 2005 — and players weren't allowed to star in national commercial campaigns like Clark is doing with State Farm and Nike.
Last year's national championship game that featured Iowa and LSU drew almost 10 million viewers. This year, the Hawkeyes have already had games on NBC, Fox and ESPN. The overtime loss to Ohio State on NBC averaged 1.93 million viewers across the network and Peacock, peaking at 3.9 million during overtime. Over a million fans tuned in for Iowa's win over Indiana on Fox.
Also in that crowd for the game at Rutgers was New Jersey Devils President Jake Reynolds. With him were his three daughters, Makenzie, 13, Katelyn, 10, and Harper, 8.
"This is something we decided to go to. Not a Rutgers season ticket holder, but this was part of the Caitlin Clark phenomenon," he said. "It was something that I sat there in amazement, just looking at the energy of what was going on around this event. Then I was blown away by just the response from so many fans. And then I was really proud to see so many young girls there."
Reynolds said watching Clark play in person has had a lasting effect on his daughters.
"To be able to, one, just witness the phenomenon that it is," he said. "To be able to give my girls the opportunity and the experience to see that firsthand, someone that inspires them and someone that they aspire to be like, to be able to give them that experience and be able to share that experience with them is something that here we are several weeks later and it is still something that is talked about in our house."

title: Queen Anne's rallies, stuns Cambridge-SD
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's rallies, stuns Cambridge-SD

 February 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 743
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — It may not have been the best half of basketball Queen Anne's County High's boys team has played this season, but it was pretty close.Hollace Branch's three-point play with 1.5 seconds remaining Thursday night capped a 17-point comeback, as the Lions pulled out a 58-57 victory to stun unbeaten Cambridge-South Dorchester.
"Man, we played as a team," Queen Anne's head coach Jeff Hollis said as tears welled up in his eyes. "They played hard. That's probably the hardest we've played all year."
Cambridge-SD (13-1 overall, 11-1 North Bayside) led 36-21 at halftime and bumped that lead to 17 early in the third quarter.
Queen Anne's (12-4, 11-2), which was without leading scorer Vince Gilberto, went on a 14-4 run that was capped by Jadereon Thompson's layup with 3:09 left in the third. Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Tucker called time, and the Vikings responded as Semay Pinder and LaShaun Moody (11 points) hit consecutive baskets, extending the lead to 44-35.
The Vikings maintained that nine-point edge at 48-39 heading into the fourth quarter. Cambridge-SD looked to be regaining control, as Moody dished to Koby Ennals for a basket, converted a steal into a layup, before Pinder scored a layup for a 54-41 lead with over 5 minutes remaining.
But the North Bayside leaders scored only three more points the rest of the game while Queen Anne's was piecing together a 17-point rally over the final 4:39, with seemingly someone different scoring every time down the floor.
DJ Smith started the rally with a bucket. Nickai Gross made a free throw. Branch scored on a left-handed drive before Amari Baynard's layup pulled Queen Anne's within 54-48 with 3:36 to play.
Cambridge-SD's Pinder missed a pair of free throws.
Queen Anne's kept closing.
Baynard buried a 3-pointer with 2:10 left, drawing the Lions within 54-51. After Cambridge-SD was whistled for a moving screen, Jimmy Holthaus (game-high 14 points) scored, making it a one-point game at 54-53 with 1:34 left.
Anthony Hughes (13 points) scored on a follow shot with 1:18 to go, nudging the Vikings' lead to 56-53. Moody converted one of two free throws with 1:06 left, making it 57-53.
But Smith drove down the right side of the lane for a basket with 41.8 seconds left, shaving the Vikings lead to 57-55. Baynard blocked a shot by Hughes, but Moody retrieved the ball and was fouled. But the senior guard missed both free throws with 15.8 seconds left.
Queen Anne's got the ball back and worked it inside to Branch who scored the tying basket and was fouled. With 1.5 seconds left, the Lions senior made the free throw to complete the three-point play.
Cambridge-SD inbounded the ball, but could not get a shot off.
"Unfortunately, we're a terrible first-half team," Hollis said. "The second half, they brought the energy and it made a difference and they started believing. You could tell.
Queen Anne's defense forced multiple turnovers during a chaotic fourth quarter.
"We've been working on defense all year," Hollis said. "And finally something must have finally hit today. I don't know. But yeah, this was definitely their best game on defense by far this year.
"We were telling them we were getting ready for the playoffs and every game means something, and they took it to heart today," Hollis continued. "I'm really proud of these guys."
Woolford finished with 13 points for Queen Anne's.

Griffin, Sabres stay in playoff hunt

 February 3, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 848
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Brennen Griffin found an isolated, off-ice spot and went through his motions.Resting on his bulky leg pads, Saints Peter and Paul High's freshman goalie stared at the white board in front of him while extending his arms out to his sides. Moving like the second hand on a clock, Griffin steadily clicked his left arm upward, then brought his right arm up, up, and up.
"It's my pregame ritual basically," Griffin said. "Every game, come into the rink, get dressed and find a quiet spot. And it's just for myself. It's time for me to focus. Time for me to lock myself in mentally."
The 6-foot-3 Griffin looked plenty locked in Friday, stopping 32 of the 33 shots he faced while helping Saints Peter and Paul to a huge 4-1 victory Loyola-Blakefield on senior night in a Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association B Conference game at the Talbot County Community Center.
"The door is still open," Sabres head coach Sam Gerdano said of Sts. Peter and Paul's chances at qualifying for the fourth and final spot in the MIAA B playoffs.
The Sabres (3-6 overall, 3-5 conference, 6 points) ended a four-game skid and remained two points behind St. Paul's (4-4, 8 points) for the fourth postseason spot. Boys Latin (8-1, 16), Loyola-Blakefield (6-2, 12) and Gilman (4-5, 8) currently hold down the top three spots.
"They really wanted it tonight," said Gerdano, whose team was shutout 5-0 by Loyola on Dec. 6. "They knew it was going to be a hard game. But we talked about, 'This is our building. Nobody outworks us in this building.' And we didn't let that happen today."
Outscored 22-4 in its previous four games, the Sabres took a 1-0 lead 1:40 into the game, when senior captain Robbie O'Connor took a pass from Griffin Fritzsche, got behind a pair of defenders, and tucked a shot past Dons goalie Tommy Bunte.
"I think that was really important because we scored like a minute or two in, and that really set the energy for the entire team," O'Connor said. "We just kept that the whole way."
Sts. Peter & Paul also kept scoring.
Daniel Schwaninger set up Fritzsche's goal with 3:44 remaining in the first period for a 2-0 lead. Loyola killed off a Sabres power play later in the first, but with 36 seconds left on the clock, Schwaninger scored unassisted for a three-goal cushion.
"We had a pretty decent first period when we played this team last, but we weren't able to score any goals on 'em," Gerdano said. "Today we got a few past them and then it helped our confidence.
"But the second period is what I was more impressed with because while we didn't score, that period has really hurt us this season, especially against this team," Gerdano added. "I think they scored four goals to last second period we played 'em. So I was really concerned about that, but they played really well."
Again, the Sabres struck quickly, as Jackson Steppe scored just 1:24 into the second for a 4-0 lead.
"Everyone just bought in," O'Connor said. "Everyone put full effort the entire game. It was just great. Everyone was ready to play. Everyone was physical. They were hustling out there. We just made the plays at the right time."
Griffin and defensemen Tyler Watson, Schwaninger, Gavin Corley and Zack Werner also made plays at the right time, as the Sabres' killed off all five Loyola power-play chances, including a two-man advantage midway through the third period.
"It was impressive," Gerdano said of his team's penalty kill. "They picked their heads up. They found a lane to get it down the ice, blocked some shots. And Brennen played unbelievable. "
Loyola foiled Griffin's shutout bid with 1:09 remaining in the second period, when Ryder McClure scored off a feed from Josh Goloboski.
But Griffin and company blanked the Dons, who had scored 12 goals in their previous two games, the rest of the way.
"Goalie needs to be your best penalty killer, and Brennen was that, and even more than that today," Gerdano said. "He's obviously a big goalie. Takes up a lot of the net. He's got a lot of skill to that as well. He's all over the place, making big stops for us. I think he was frustrating the other team for sure. That team is used to scoring goals and they had a really hard time because of our goalie, and just our defense in front of him, keeping the shots from the outside."
And while Griffin impressed, the young goalie redirected praise toward those fronting him as if he were steering away one of Loyola's many shot on net.
"My defense was making sure I saw everything; weren't giving up too many good opportunities in front. That's how we got to 4-1," Griffin said. "That's the best game I've seen them play. It was unreal what they were doing. Just when I thought we were going to let one up, somebody was sliding in blocking a shot. It was something special."
"Best experience I've ever been apart of," Griffin added. "Especially on senior night, doing this for the seniors is unreal."

author: Bill Haufe
content:
TITLE WAVE

 February 3, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 832
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — Bayside Conference swim teams be warned. Kent Island High may be preparing for an extended stay at the top."The kind of drought of young swimmers that some of the teams are experiencing. … like Easton, they lost a lot of seniors and really did not fill those spots," Kent Island head coach Corey Coulbourn said. "We, knock on wood, we are fortunate enough this year not to experience that."
That influx of youth was on display at the Pauline F. and W. David Robbins Family YMCA Saturday, as Kent Island freshmen combined for five individual titles and were part of two winning relays, leading the Buccaneers to a sweep of the boys and girls titles during the Bayside swimming championships.
"We only had two senior girls swimming here today," Coulbourn said of Marissa White and Maddie Hull. "They both earned us tons of points. We're also really fortunate to have a lot of young girls, including those freshmen who are coming to us from a club swimming background. So we've really been able to maintain the skills that they've already come to us with."
Kent Island's girls totaled 442 points, outdistancing runner-up Stephen Decatur by 54 points.
Leading that effort was freshman Maddie Parks, who joined classmates Kara Seymour and Clare O'Keefe, and senior White to win the meet-opening 200-yard medley relay in 1:59.36. Parks went on to win the 100 freestyle (59.02) — edging White who placed second in 59.49 — and the 100 backstroke (1:05.46) by more than 2 seconds.
Bolstering the Bucs were Seymour, who won the 200 individual medley in 2:27.82 — almost 7 full seconds ahead of second-place Kendall Bagley of Decatur (2:34.70) — and O'Keefe, first in the 50 freestyle sprint (25.83).
But the Bucs' most impressive performance came in the 200 freestyle relay, when confusion as to who was swimming the lead leg had the team not even in the water until most of the competition was at the other end of the pool.
"It was just miscommunication," Coulbourn said. "When we were brainstorming entries, I typed it up in a different order than what it got entered in the computer. We made some changes based on the events swimmers had right after the relay. So we just moved some people around. So what the girls had looked at on the wall was different from what (the) clerk of course was telling them."
Despite that late start, Seymour, Parks, White and O'Keefe finished third (1:59.64) behind first-place Decatur (1:57.74) and second-place Queen Anne's (1:59.37).
"I'm super impressed that they made up that time to the degree that they did," Coulbourn said. "One of our parents was watching the clock and said that they left about 15 seconds late. So to make up that. … we have an amazing group of freshmen, and three of them are on that relay."
Easton, the two-time defending girls champion, finished third behind Maddie Weems, who won the 100 butterfly (1:03.53), the 100 breaststroke (1:09.62) before teaming with Isabella Westerfield, Katheryne Kelsey and Claire Morris to destroy the field in the 400 freestyle relay (3:59.20), winning by 15 seconds.
The Warriors also got a strong performance from Westerfield, who was second in the 50 free (26.11) and first in the 500 freestyle (5:47.64) — winning by 15 seconds. Westerfield anchored Easton's second-place 200 medley team, and gave the Warriors a lead they never surrendered in the 400 free relay. Mae Jennings' first-place effort in the 200 freestyle (1:59.20) bolstered the Warriors' point total.
Kent Island's boys also got a lift from their freshmen, as Jacob Reeder won the 200 IM (2:17.35), and joined classmate Jack Da Rosa, junior Giovanni Aguirre and senior John Mangold to win the 200 freestyle relay in 1:38.75.
"Similar situation with the boys," Coulbourn said in regard to Kent Island's youth. "We only have one senior boy, our captain, John Mangold, who was on all three relays. And then we lucked out with our freshman crew this year. We have seven or eight freshman boys, and I think six or seven were here today. It's just amazing."
Kent Island won the boys' title with 358 points, with Decatur again taking second with 318.
The lone two-time winner in individual competition on the boys' side was Kent County's Henry Martinez, who won the 50 freestyle (23.08) and the 100 free (50.49).
Decatur's Daniel Karcheuski was first in the 200 freestyle, but was disqualified, making Easton's Brady Tipton the champion with a time of 2:00.43. Karcheuski, who swam the second leg on the Seahawks' winning 200 medley relay, rebounded, winning the 100 breaststroke in a meet-record 1:03.05, before swimming a huge anchor leg to rally Decatur to victory in the 400 free relay (3:44.51).
North Bayside swimmers brought home two other titles, as Queen Anne's County's William Meyer won the 100 butterfly (1:00.71) by 2 seconds, and Cambridge-South Dorchester's Hayden Hudson pulled away to win the 500 free (5:39.47) by 16 seconds.
Stephen Decatur's Chase Ponton won the 100 backstroke in 1:02.26.
Kent Island finished second in the boys and girls competitions last year.

title: RISING TO THE OCCASION
author: Bill Haufe
content:
RISING TO THE OCCASION

 February 6, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1290
 Words 

 Read News Document

 LANDOVER — Kent Island High's girls team was a strong contender to win Monday's Class 2A East Region indoor track and field championship.Bucs' longtime head coach Justin Holland felt even stronger about those title chances after Gabi Bernhard won the 500 meters and 55-meter hurdles less than 30 minutes apart. The top seed in the pole vault, Holland figured all Bernhard needed to do was clear her opening height of 9 feet, 6 inches and the team championship was a near lock.
"She's cleared 9-6 all year," Holland said. "In fact, we were about to start at 10 feet from now on. But it was an easy meet, so she decided she was going to come in at 9-6, like she's done all year."
Less than 5 minutes after winning the hurdles, Bernhard missed on the first of her three attempts at 9-6. Then she missed again.
"So I'm thinking, 'Oh my gosh. If she scratches this last one," Holland said.
She didn't.
Bernhard made her third and final attempt at 9-6, hugged her coach, then went on to clear 10-6 to win her third individual title while helping the Bucs seal the team crown at the Prince George's Sports and Learning Complex.
"I talked to her about how nervous (I was)," Holland said of his post-victory chat with his three-time champion. "That's the most (nervous) I've been in forever. I said, 'Don't do that to me ever again.' And I'm like, I'm just going to have to deal with a crying Gabi (if she missed on her third try). And she's like, 'Oh, I wasn't going to cry.' And I said, 'Yeah, but then I was going to let you know that probably cost us the regional championship as well. And she's like, 'Oh, yeah I would have cried as soon as you said that.' But I didn't say that was what was riding (on it)."
Bernhard's victory, coupled with teammates' Siena Koch (7-6) and Nora Koch (6-6) finishing second and third, respectively, gave Kent Island a 24-point haul in the event, and more than sealed the title, as the Bucs totaled 69 points to outdistance runner-up Parkside (57), third-place Patuxent (52) and fourth-place North Caroline (43).
Bernhard's three titles highlighted an impressive day for North Bayside athletes, who won six other championships.
Queen Anne's County junior Ben Marks routed the field to win the boys 800- and 1,600-meter titles. Easton senior Jed Smith teamed with Colin Smith, Jacob Camper and Sy Orndoff to win the boys 4x800 relay, then pulled away over the final laps to win the 3,200. Warrior teammate Sumayah Wilkins won the girls' high jump. And North Caroline's Morgan Knott, Linda Ridgell, Brooke Sullivan and Seanna Rupp took first in the girls' 4x800 relay.
"I think everybody stepped it up and did their part," Holland said of his girls team. "We do our team chemistry and it works out. They worked hard and I'm proud of all of them. And obviously I think Gabi helped us out quite a bit."
But Bernhard didn't exactly have a whole lot of time between events.
After qualifying in the preliminaries for the 55 hurdles, Bernhard had a little wait before doing a couple practice vaults. Then her schedule began to accelerate. She won the 500 in 1:22.94, as Easton's Emily Branic (2nd, 1:23.13) and Kent Island teammate Reese Heyliger (3rd, 1:23.28) chased her across the finish line.
After a few more run-throughs in the vault, Bernhard was back on the track, outdueling Patuxent's Jordan Estrella in the 55 hurdles, clocking a first-place 9.08 to Estrella's 9.12.
"The goal for today was to come out, do my best," Bernhard said. "Take it one event at a time. I did want to break 9 seconds in the hurdles, but I came really close. My (personal) record is 8.88. I'm going for that for states. And I'm happy to have cleared 10-6 in pole vault. I was a little worried there at 9-6."
Part of that can be attributed to Bernhard just coming off her victory in the hurdles. With only four competitors in the pole vault, the height was raised quickly. Bernhard hit the bar on the way up on her first try, then brushed it off on the second. After conferencing with Holland, she easily cleared her opening height.
"I was like 'Don't worry about it,'" Bernhard said. "'Don't get stressed.' Settle yourself. Just know that you're going to do your best. If you don't worry about it you're guaranteed to do your best."
Bernhard also was a member of the Bucs' third-place 4x200 relay, joining Heyliger, Kendra Coffey and Siena Koch for a 1:51.91.
Marks left little doubt who the winner of the 1,600 meters was going to be, as he broke from the field on the first backstretch and opened a commanding lead en route to a first-place 4:22.79 — 24 seconds ahead of runner-up Trevor Thompson of La Plata.
"I didn't want to get boxed because that would have totally messed up my race," said Marks, who finished 3 seconds off his personal-best. "So I just wanted to get free from any barriers in front of me. I went out in 29-, 30-(second first lap). Honestly it felt really smooth. That was good.
"It was a solo effort today so it's a little different than what I've been used to," Marks said of his dominating performance in the 1,600. "I knew there were some boys who maybe wanted to stay with me for a couple of laps. "But I wanted to take it out (fast) and leave everybody in the dust."
Though the pursuit was closer, and his margin of victory not as great, Marks wasn't really pushed in the 800, rolling to a first-place mark of 1:58.43, followed by La Plata's Kohl Girley (2:01.91), and Easton's Colin Smith (2:06.03) and Jed Smith (2:06.29).
"I thought there was going to be a little bit more of a push," Marks said of the 800. "I took the lead right away so I really didn't see a single runner the entire race. When I got to the front I was able to keep running and (didn't) look behind me. I just stayed focused. Got to just run my race."
Jed Smith battled Huntingtown's Brendan Bischof through the majority of the 3,200. But the Easton senior steadily began a surge over the final laps that would not be answered, winning in 10:27.84 — 7 seconds ahead of Bishof.
"I felt strong throughout the race," Smith said. "I was pacing my own game, kind of looking at the clock. I kind of felt like he went out a little too quick so I used that to my advantage, and was smart and stayed back. Once he started to slow down a bit I made my move on the straight, and then I think he got (close) again at the end. But I knew I had enough in me for that final push."
Smith anchored Easton's winning 4x800 relay, which won in 8:30.24, well ahead of second-place Westlake (8:41.77).
Caroline's Knott, Ridgell, Sullivan and Rupp opened the meet with one of the day's more decisive victories, rolling away with the 4x800 relay in 10:34.36, easily outdistancing runner-up La Plata (11:15.09).
Easton head coach Beth Heinsohn, who was left in tears after the Warriors' convincing win in the boys 4x800 relay, was again in tears, when Wilkins angled over the bar at 5-3 to win the high jump.
"I was just thinking to myself, I've got so much confidence," Wilkins said. "I was like, 'I'm going to clear it.' I was pushing for 5-4. But 5-3. I'll take it. I'm just so proud of myself I cried. And my coach cried as well."
Notes: La Plata won the boys team title with 96 points, edging Westlake by one point. Huntingtown was third followed by Easton (44) and Kent Island (32).

SEEING DOUBLE

 February 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — Katie Murphy has seen it all season."They tried to shut Morgan (Quade) down. They tried to shut Avery (McCall) down," Saints Peter and Paul High's girls head basketball coach said of Worcester Prep trying to clamp down on her top two leading scorers. "We needed everybody to step up and Lucy did it."
Sophomore Lucy Rankin stepped up like never before Wednesday, notching a career-high 16 points to go with 10 rebounds for her first-ever double-double, as the Sabres romped to a 49-15 victory over Worcester Prep in an Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference clash on senior night.
"She really stepped up, 'cause when that stuff happens we need the other three (starters) to step up," Quade said of Rankin. "She did really good with that tonight."
Rankin hit two free throws to give the Sabres their first points and a 2-2 tie, scored a layup midway through the first quarter to give Sts. Peter & Paul a lead it steadily widened, then made another foul shot to cap a 17-5 first quarter for the home team.
"Our coaches told us that this would happen," said Rankin of the Mallards trying to limit Quade and McCall. "So they said I needed to step up and move the ball and drive to the basket more. Once I started to get more comfortable I loosened up a bit and started to just go with the flow. This is a surprise to me."
Rankin scored on a layup and a put-back as the Sabres outscored Worcester, 15-0, in the second quarter to take a commanding 32-5 lead into the locker room.
"She really came through," Murphy said of Rankin, who had nine first-half points. "And everybody played the role they needed to play today."
One night after losing to ESIAC rival Delmarva Christian by 10, the Sabres cranked up the defensive pressure on Worcester early in the first quarter. Sts. Peter & Paul pressed Worcester full court, creating multiple turnovers while holding the Mallards scoreless the final 14 minutes of the first half.
"We've been fine tuning the press and changing different roles and different positions, and making sure that they're cutting off that middle person," Murphy said. "They did it pretty well today. And they were jumping for balls and getting the steals."
Despite Worcester's defensive efforts, Quade and McCall each finished in double figures. Quade, the Sabres' lone senior, finished with 14 points, eight rebounds and six steals. A sophomore, McCall scored all 12 of her points in the first half, and totaled four rebounds, three steals and three blocked shots.
Worcester ended an 18-plus minute scoring drought with just under 4 minutes remaining in the third quarter, and matched the Sabres in scoring during a 7-7 third. But Sts. Peter & Paul continued to play solid half-court defense in the fourth, limiting the visitors to just one basket from the field — that coming with 4 minutes left when Sydney Mize hit a 3-pointer.
"I think today we moved the ball quicker," said Quade, comparing the Sabres' loss Tuesday to Delmarva Christian to Wednesday's rout. "I think that's what kind of killed us last night. They were trapping us and we weren't moving it fast enough to get it around their traps, and if we did we would have found the open person really easily. Today I think we definitely moved it better. And honestly with them taking me and Avery out it kind of opened it up for the other three (Rankin, Sam Murphy and Annie Albright)."
With another potential showdown with Delmarva Christian in the playoffs looming, Coach Murphy was pleased with how her team rebounded from Tuesday's loss.
"Our defense is doing very well right now," Murphy said. "Every ball is a Sabre ball. They are supposed to go after it. I'm very happy with our underclassmen because they took the lead from our starters and they were after every ball, causing a bunch of jump balls. It's probably the most jump balls we've had in a game so far. Boxing out, rebounding, looking for the open player, making sure everybody was covered, they also did very well."

title: DELAY OF GAME
author: Bill Haufe
content:
DELAY OF GAME

 February 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 856
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Domonique Foxworth played his first organized tackle football game at 10 years old.Now Foxworth has a son who turns 11 on Super Bowl Sunday who wants to play tackle. Foxworth won't allow it. His son is playing flag football instead.
When might he allow his son to play tackle? Foxworth said, "We'll see."
"It's definitely not going to be before high school," said Foxworth, a former NFL cornerback and former president of the NFL Players Association. "I guess that would be the first time that we even consider the conversation. Right now he's in the fifth grade, so we've got some time for him to fall in love with something else."
Interviews with several former NFL players, some of whom played tackle football before high school, revealed a range of opinions about whether children should participate in tackle leagues.
Some are categorically opposed to youth playing tackle before age 12 or 14. Others said they would consider what a child wanted. All interviewed for this article said their thoughts about the sport had evolved since their days as youth players.
"I honestly don't see the benefit of playing tackle football at a young age because flag football now is so available," said Muhammad Oliver, a former defensive back who played four years in the NFL.
Oliver said if taught correctly the skills learned in flag football can translate to tackle football. He said flag football allows kids to pick up the fundamentals of the sport and understand how it's played.
Oliver has seven children, four of whom are boys ages 27, 23, 12 and 9. His oldest son, Isaiah, plays for the San Francisco 49ers. Oliver allowed Isaiah to begin playing in a tackle league at age 8. If he had it to do over again, he said, Isaiah wouldn't have played tackle football until he was 12.
Oliver said his experience as a youth tackle football coach and as president of NX Level AthletX, a youth multisport development program in Goodyear, Arizona, has influenced his thinking. So has recent medical research linking youth tackle football to later-life challenges, such as impulse control and cognitive decline.
"With all the information now about concussions and how often concussions are happening and the number of concussions that players have had over their lifetime, I just don't feel like the contact is necessary young," Oliver said.
Former Super Bowl champion and Hall of Fame linebacker Harry Carson has been outspoken in warning of the risks of brain injury from the sport.
In 2018, Carson was one of the ex-players to appear at a news conference sponsored by the Concussion Legacy Foundation announcing a campaign to discourage tackle football before the age of 14. Carson has repeatedly said in interviews that if he had it to do again, he would not have played football.
Neither of Carson's two sons played football at a competitive level, he said. Carson, who played 13 seasons for the New York Giants, has discouraged his grandson from playing.
Carson advocates for transparency and education. "I would like for the surgeon general to issue a warning to parents," he said, adding that adults should understand the risks of the sport.
"Every parent should sign a waiver to fully understand what they are signing their kids up for when they play football or a contact sport," Carson said.
"Most parents of little boys of color will continue to allow their kids to play," Carson said, "because, you know, they don't want to deny their kids the opportunity to play because he has talent … not fully understanding that their kids may suffer the consequences down the road."
That differs somewhat from the view of Bruce Harper, a former New York Jets running back and kick returner whose NFL career lasted from 1977 to 1984. Harper never had to face a parental decision about youth football. He has two daughters, neither of whom played the sport.
However, Harper said the decision should be left to the child.
"It's a decision each kid individually has to make. I don't think the parents should decide for the kid if they can play or not," he said.
The NFLPA has no formal policy regarding tackle football for kids. However, the players union has backed several youth initiatives including both tackle and flag football. The players union also supports members serving on the boards of USA Football and other youth leagues. Additionally, the union provides financial and community support to players running football camps for kids, but these camps primarily stay away from tackle.
"We encourage every level of football … to implement the health and safety protocols we have at the NFL level," said George Atallah, the NFLPA's assistant executive director of external affairs. "We don't have a specific position on when we think young people should play it. That's for the medical experts to determine."
Foxworth, who played for three teams from 2005-2011, sustained many injuries throughout his career. He's been able to deal with injuries to his body, but brain injury will always be something he's mindful of.
"I still wouldn't trade it for the life that I've had access to," Foxworth said of his football career. "But it's all a different conversation when you start talking about your brain."

title: Delle Donne taking break
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Delle Donne taking break

 February 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 253
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Washington Mystics star Elena Delle Donne is stepping away from basketball, potentially for the entire season, a person familiar with the decision said Thursday.The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because no official announcement had been made.
The two-time MVP was designated as a core player by the Mystics before free agency began last week. She has been at an impasse with Washington regarding her contract. The core designation guaranteed Delle Donne the WNBA's maximum salary of $241,984.
ESPN first reported Delle Donne's decision.
The 34-year-old star had a few options once the Mystics used the core designation. She could sign the one-year deal and play for Washington; sit out the season; or agree to a sign-and-trade and play elsewhere.
The Mystics were looking for high draft picks for Delle Donne if they were going to trade her, and there have been limited options. She's only played in 51 games since Washington won the franchise's only league title in 2019 because of the COVID-19 pandemic and injury issues.
The All-Star averaged 16.7 points and 5.4 rebounds in 23 games last season.
Delle Donne has been busy in the offseason, starting Deldon Wines — the first-ever wine brand from a WNBA star.
Delle Donne, who has undergone multiple back surgeries, was the No. 2 overall pick in the 2013 draft. She was league MVP in 2015 with Chicago and 2019 with Washington.
Off the court, Delle Donne is co-chair of the President's Council on Sports, Fitness and Nutrition, an advisory body that promotes healthy eating and exercise.

title: Knicks more formidable with addition of Bogdanovic
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Knicks more formidable with addition of Bogdanovic

 February 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 925
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Bojan Bogdanovic left Detroit to join a now even-more-formidable contender in New York. Gordon Hayward is leaving Charlotte for one of the NBA's best surprise stories this season in Oklahoma City. Doug McDermott was once traded by Indiana to San Antonio, and now, the Spurs have traded him back to the Pacers.None of those shooters were making playoff plans when Thursday started.
Trade deadline day in the NBA gave them and plenty of other players an entirely new outlook, plus might have even reshaped the start of the playoff push as well.
The Knicks made some big moves with eyes on contending in the Eastern Conference, Philadelphia added a sharpshooter in Buddy Hield with hopes that it can get back on track when — or if — reigning MVP Joel Embiid returns from injury, while Phoenix and Dallas added frontcourt depth. The Suns landed Royce O'Neale from Brooklyn and the Mavericks are bringing in P.J. Washington from Charlotte.
"Lots of people got better!!! That's fun for competition…" Embiid wrote on social media.
Bogdanovic averaged 20.2 points this season for the Pistons, who have the NBA's worst record so far at 7-43. He and Alec Burks are headed to the Knicks, a team that entered Thursday a game out of the No. 2 spot in the East and managed to add without really subtracting — the price was Quentin Grimes, Evan Fournier and Ryan Arcidiacono.
"The shooting piece was so important," Knicks coach Tom Thibodeau said. "I just think the more we can open up the floor, particularly as you go forward, that's a key ingredient."
Grimes began the year as a starter, then played off the bench. Fournier only appeared in three games and Arcidiacono made 20 appearances — without scoring a single point in any of them.
Hayward joins an Oklahoma City team that started Thursday as the No. 1 seed in the Western Conference. The Thunder are 35-16, entering the day with tiebreaker edges over two other teams — Minnesota and Denver — with the same record and a half-game up on the Los Angeles Clippers at 34-16.
Hield left Indiana in a trade to the 76ers, and the Pacers seemed to try and replace his shooting by bringing back McDermott in a move with San Antonio. McDermott spent three seasons, 2018 through 2021, with Indiana, so the trade was a homecoming of sorts.
"He's going to go down as one of the best 3-point shooters in the history of this league, and he'll make an awful lot of them because he doesn't miss," Pacers coach Rick Carlisle said, referring to Hield. "He rarely misses a game, either. So it's a good opportunity for him and we move forward from there."
Another homecoming: Kelly Olynyk is headed back to his native Canada, the veteran forward getting acquired by Toronto in a deal with Utah.
Milwaukee made a couple of notable moves, one by landing Patrick Beverley from the 76ers and pairing him with Bucks guard Damian Lillard; those two exchanged some heated words last season. The Bucks then sent center Robin Lopez to Sacramento; it is expected that Lopez will be waived by the Kings.
"I enjoyed being teammates with Patrick Beverley for all of an hour and 45 minutes I'll never forget those times," Lopez wrote on X, the social media site formerly known as Twitter.
Meanwhile, Dejounte Murray — maybe one of the most talked-about players over the past few weeks of trade speculation — remained in Atlanta, and plenty of other teams stood pat on Thursday. Defending NBA champion Denver didn't make a move on deadline day, nor did reigning East champion Miami, though the Heat did their trade-season work a couple weeks ago by bringing in Terry Rozier from Charlotte for Kyle Lowry.
LeBron James' Los Angeles Lakers didn't make any trade-deadline deals, nor did a Golden State team that entered the season with championship hopes and finds itself in a dogfight at the bottom of the West playoff picture.
"I think we're in a good place," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said. "I think we've been through a lot but really guys have stepped up and are playing better."
Said Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka: "If the right move would have been there at the right price, we would have pulled the trigger."
Another team that didn't make a trade: Cleveland, which has won 15 of its last 16 games to move to No. 2 in the East.
"Sometimes you don't want to mess up a good thing," Koby Altman, the Cavs' president of basketball operations, said on a conference call shortly after the deadline passed. "So, we're going to roll with what we have."
Adding to the challenge of deadline day is this: Only five teams entered Thursday more than four games out of the final play-in tournament spots in the East and West. That means that 25 of the NBA's 30 clubs either can reasonably believe they're headed to the playoffs, or still can realistically say they have a shot.
"I can only focus on us," Altman said. "The bulk of our work was done in the offseason. We will certainly monitor the buyout market. Is there a depth piece in there to help? It has to be a character fit as well."
The Lakers and Warriors — and plenty of other teams — will now likely be active in the buyout market. Lowry would be in high demand if he accepts a buyout from Charlotte, and Spencer Dinwiddie will be on the market as well. He was traded from Brooklyn to Toronto on Thursday for Dennis Schroder and Thaddeus Young, and the Raptors waived him immediately.

title: Delle Donne taking break
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Delle Donne taking break

 February 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 253
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Washington Mystics star Elena Delle Donne is stepping away from basketball, potentially for the entire season, a person familiar with the decision said Thursday.The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because no official announcement had been made.
The two-time MVP was designated as a core player by the Mystics before free agency began last week. She has been at an impasse with Washington regarding her contract. The core designation guaranteed Delle Donne the WNBA's maximum salary of $241,984.
ESPN first reported Delle Donne's decision.
The 34-year-old star had a few options once the Mystics used the core designation. She could sign the one-year deal and play for Washington; sit out the season; or agree to a sign-and-trade and play elsewhere.
The Mystics were looking for high draft picks for Delle Donne if they were going to trade her, and there have been limited options. She's only played in 51 games since Washington won the franchise's only league title in 2019 because of the COVID-19 pandemic and injury issues.
The All-Star averaged 16.7 points and 5.4 rebounds in 23 games last season.
Delle Donne has been busy in the offseason, starting Deldon Wines — the first-ever wine brand from a WNBA star.
Delle Donne, who has undergone multiple back surgeries, was the No. 2 overall pick in the 2013 draft. She was league MVP in 2015 with Chicago and 2019 with Washington.
Off the court, Delle Donne is co-chair of the President's Council on Sports, Fitness and Nutrition, an advisory body that promotes healthy eating and exercise.

title: Vikings win title after scare
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings win title after scare

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 934
 Words 

 Read News Document

 LANDOVER — Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys indoor track and field team was on its way to a third consecutive Class 1A East Region championship Friday night.Then confusion stepped in.
Boys head coach Clint Falduto and assistant Lois Narr couldn't figure out how the Vikings' lead over Largo had suddenly evaporated to almost nothing after the second-to-last race on the boys 1A schedule — the 800 meters.
"Lois was like, 'We should be up by so much further.' And I was like, 'I know. I don't know what happened,'" Falduto said.
As Falduto and Narr continued trying to understand how their comfortable lead had suddenly gone poof, the boys 800 for the Class 4A East meet — which was being held simultaneously with the 1A meet at the Prince George's Sports and Learning Complex — was being run.
That's when Cambridge-SD's Tekai Drummond approached Falduto and Narr with the answer.
"Tekai came up and said, 'That kid that just beat me, he's in 4A,'" Falduto said. "And we're like, 'What?'"
Falduto and Narr went to the officials' table where it was confirmed a 4A runner — wearing the same hip number as a Largo runner — had run the wrong race, and that his points had initially been counted toward Largo's point total. As officials corrected the mistake, Cambridge-SD was getting ready to run its heat of the boys 4x400 relay.
Though Largo won the 4x400, Antonio Blueford, Tori Willis, Tekai Drummond and Teshar Drummond's runner-up finish in the event capped a third regional title for the Vikings, who totaled 91 points to the Lions' 84.
"They were beating us at one point," Falduto said of Largo. "My head was spinning. Oh my goodness, it was exciting. So, so exciting. Freaking bizarre.
"The boys have worked so tremendously hard," Falduto continued. "This group has been together for a good solid three years, the majority of them. And knowing the competition around the state, they knew it was possible. But they knew it was going to be a lot of hard work."
Cambridge-SD's bid for a third straight 1A East crown became even harder because a number of key team members were unable to compete, including Jayden Smith, who was sidelined by an illness.
Despite those losses, the Vikings scored in 10 of the 11 events.
Leading that effort was Willis, who won the 55-meter hurdles in a personal-record 7.87 seconds, placed second in the 55-meter sprint (6.55), and ran a leg on the second-place 4x800 relay, joining Christian Dockins and the Drummonds for a time of 8:54.92.
"Fifty-five-meter hurdles, I really think it was just push and get out, and tried to keep my pace and keep my energy going through the hurdles," said Willis, who took the lead after clearing the second hurdle. "I just wanted to make sure I qualified and made it to states again. Once I get a good start, I know I'm going to push through the hurdles and get the win."
Edwind Torres of Chesapeake Science Point was second in the hurdles with an 8.11, followed by Cambridge-SD's Blueford in third (8.28).
"Fifty-five, there's room to improve," said Willis, who clocked a 6.55, finishing second to Friendly's Donte Long (6.48). Kent County's Tyrell Fennell was third in 6.58.
In addition to their second-places in the 4x800 and 4x400 relays, Cambridge-SD was also second in the 4x200, as Teshar Drummond, Kay'lon Marine, William Jackson and Jakuez combined for a 1:34.55.
The Vikings were second to Largo in all three relays.
Fourth in the controversial 800, Tekai Drummond, who was running sprints a year ago, finished second in the 1,600 with a 4:49.61.
Bolstering the Vikings' fortunes were the second- and third-place finishes by Jackson (11-5) and Preston Adkins (8-11) in the pole vault.
Cambridge-SD swept the hurdles titles, as Enazajah Young broke her own school record to win the girls title in 8.28, beating Largo's Ayniah Fersner (8.56) and Lailah Fersner (8.65).
"By the third hurdle," said Young, when asked when she thought she had the hurdles won. "When you race you can hear people's footsteps. I didn't hear nothing. I was like, 'You got to push through the rest.'"
The defending state champion in the 55 meters, Young got off to a slow start in the sprint after a teammate had been disqualified for a false start. Young finished fourth in 7.34, but qualified for the state championships on Feb. 20.
"She watched her teammate false start right before," Cambridge-SD girls head coach Stacey Brown said of Young in the 55. "It's nerve racking when you're out there. You false start one time and you miss states. I think that goes through a lot of their heads when they're out there. They want to come out of those blocks fast, but they know one false start and they're done."
Young finished sixth in the 300 with a 44.81.
The only other North Bayside athlete to earn a first place in the girls competition was Kent County's Ke'yare Hawkins, who won the shot put with a heave of 35 feet, 3¼ inches.
The Trojans earned a second regional champion, as Larry Steward, competing in just his third competition of the season, won the boys high jump, clearing the bar at 6-2.
"I was pretty confident coming in because I know I can jump high," Steward said. "I'm not so confident in my technique in jumping. I surprised myself with 6-2. I tried to get 6-5, but I plan on getting that at states."
Colonel Richardson's Jackson Jean was second in the high jump at 5-10, followed by Kent County's Rah'zir Wilson in fourth (5-10).
Colonel Richardson also had a runner-up finish in the girls high jump, with Addison Chandler clearing 4-6. Mardela's Lexie Guy won with a 4-10.

title: CHANGING THEIR TUNE
author: Bill Haufe
content:
CHANGING THEIR TUNE

 February 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 851
 Words 

 Read News Document

 WYE MILLS — The talk surrounding St. Michaels High's boys basketball team used to be could it win just one game.That narrative has changed drastically this season. Now, as they enter the second week of February, the Saints are asking themselves can they earn a home-court playoff game?
St. Michaels kept that scenario alive Saturday afternoon, as senior Nakhi Miller scored a game-high 34 points and sophomore Johnny Mautz had 20, pacing the Saints to a 79-47 rout of Mardela in the boys opener of the Peake Challenge at Chesapeake College.
"I told them these last few games, 'No, we can't win the (North) Bayside, but you can set yourselves up to have a home game as far as the seeding goes for the playoffs,'" St. Michaels second-year head coach Boo Ricketts said. "We're not just playing to beat teams. We're playing to make progress and put ourselves in a good position as a team. This is all about the Saints."
While Perryville (12-3) and Colonel Richardson (11-7) hold the top two seeds in Class 1A East Region I, St. Michaels (6-11 overall, 4-10 North Bayside) stayed within reach of No. 3 Bohemia Manor (8-9) and just ahead of Kent County (5-11) in the region field.
"We really didn't lose any pieces from last season," Mautz said. "Just been working and it's starting to come together. I mean I think we should have more than six wins to be honest."
Mautz could certainly point toward a four-point loss to North Caroline on Dec. 12, or Thursday's loss on senior night against Gunston.
"As I tell my guys, 'We're not playing against teams this year,'" Ricketts said. "'We're playing against us. It's all about growing. It's all about progress.' They always ask me, 'Is this team good?' I said, 'We're not assessing teams. Every team is good. Let's show up and play our brand of basketball.'"
The Saints did that against Mardela (1-16), as Miller and Mautz established an early trend of attacking the rim, while helping St. Michaels build a 21-6 lead after the first quarter.
"This game we definitely made up for it," said Miller, referring to the Gunston loss. "We just have to become better. Go to practice and give 100 percent every day."
Mardela actually took a 2-0 lead before the game-clock even started because St. Michaels' Hunter Gottlieb drew a technical for dunking during pre-game warm-ups.
"No coach wants to start the game that way," Ricketts said. "So I pulled Hunter in our huddle and I said, 'If you want to dunk the ball make sure you get one in the game."
Gottlieb did just that with under 2 minutes remaining in the first half, when he got a breakaway and hammered a one-handed slam that brought the crowd to its highest volume of the opening 16 minutes and gave the Saints a 33-15 lead.
"I guess he made me eat my words," Ricketts said laughing.
Up 39-18 at halftime, Miller and Mautz continued driving to the basket in the second half. Mautz drilled one of his two 3-pointers less than 3 minutes into the third quarter, extending the Saints' cushion to 45-22. Mardela's Wyatt Livingstone answered with a trey to get the Warriors back within 20, But St. Michaels closed the third on a 16-6 run, with Miller accounting for 13 in the rally.
"It was just a team effort," Miller said.
A theme the senior guard has undoubtedly picked up from his head coach this season.
"I tell them every time we win games it's a collective effort," Ricketts said. "In the games we've won there's been no one man or two men that are showing up and doing it by themselves. The games we win is when they play together and everybody believes in it. Even our bench. That's what a basketball team is."
The Saints led 61-31 heading into the fourth quarter and watched Mautz reel off seven consecutive points, widening the lead to 68-33. The Warriors put together a 9-0 run to pull within 68-42, but wouldn't get any closer as Ricketts sat his starters late.
"I feel we can always be better," Mautz said. "There's always levels to go up, but I'm decently happy about where we're at right now. Play hard it practice, start to knock down our free throws, there's really no reason why we shouldn't make a run in the playoffs this year."
Christian Elsey led Mardela with 15 points.

 AMERICAN CORNER — Any residue from Saturday night's loss to James M. Bennett at the Peake Challenge was gone.And Easton High's boys basketball team made sure this wasn't going to be a bump in the road as it tried to re-establish its momentum with the postseason approaching.
The Warriors buried five 3-pointers in the first quarter and sophomore guard Marshall Bailey scored a game-high 22 points Tuesday night, pacing Easton to a 73-65 victory over Colonel Richardson.
"We want to establish like a mindset and try to come out and punch 'em in the mouth first and see what happens, and then adjust after that," Easton head coach Dionte Hynson said after the Warriors improved to 14-5 overall, 13-2 North Bayside. "I think we came out and played real well defensively, got up and down a little bit, and that got our offense flowing a little bit."
So did the three-ball.
Ja'Kai Brooks (18 points) drilled the first of his two 3-pointers in the opening minute and Easton never trailed. Brooks popped another trey midway through the first quarter for an 8-2 Easton lead. Bailey, who had three 3-pointers, canned a 3 for an 11-4 lead. Diontaye Copper (13 points) drained one of his three 3-pointers with 1:40 left in the first period before Bailey connected on Easton's fifth of the quarter for a 21-10 lead after one period.
"Our guards were shooting the ball real well," Hynson said.
The Warriors extended their lead in the second quarter behind strong inside play from Tymire Thomas and Kahlil Batson, who each took entry passes and made quick spin moves inside the paint for buckets and a 40-24 halftime cushion.
"The halfcourt offense was really flowing I thought," Hynson said. "We hit a couple high-lows too. We made some really nice passes. Our bigs, they were hitting the high-lows. Even Tymire came off the bench with his high-low."
Three-pointers from Makiah Batson (12 points) and Manny Wallace (13 points) helped Colonel Richardson (11-8, 7-8) trim its 16-point halftime deficit to 10 with 3:46 remaining in the third quarter.
But Easton outscored the Colonels, 14-5, over the final 3-plus minutes of the third, including a 6-point frenzy in the last 30 seconds. Bailey turned a steal into a layup and was fouled. Though Bailey missed the free throw, Zymier Ramirez grabbed the rebound and scored on a put-back. Bailey then made a steal on the inbounds pass and laid the ball in for a 59-40 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
"We just lost our focus there a little at the end of the quarter," Colonels head coach Brad Plutschak said. "We just couldn't get right. I was hoping if we could get it inside 10 we could see what could happen. But we had given up some pretty open looks there in the first quarter. We were chasing points all night at that's tough."
Colonel creeped back within 15, but back-to-back 3-pointers from Copper gave the Warriors a 65-47 lead with just under 6 minutes left in the game.
Up 19, Hynson pulled most of his starting lineup with a little over 2 minutes remaining. Colonel scored the game's final 10 points to make the final more respectable.
"We played a good team on Saturday," Hynson said of Bennett. "We didn't play that bad but we got some stuff straightened out. I thought we bounced back real nice. I told them this is the last week (of the regular season) and we've got to get ready for the playoffs. I think we're headed in the right direction."
Easton is scheduled to host North Bayside-leading Cambridge-South Dorchester (19-1, 15-1) on Thursday.
