title: STRONGHOLD
author: Bill Haufe
content:
STRONGHOLD

 March 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Stronghold 
 
 2225
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Colonel Richardson and St. Michaels baseball.It's one of the Bayside Conference's finer —if not finest — high school rivalries in any sport, and there's no signs why it shouldn't continue to be just that heading into this season.
Excluding the 2020 and '21 seasons, when the conference championship was not held due to COVID-19, either the Colonels or Saints have won the last nine North Bayside titles, with Colonel winning six and St. Michaels three.
Those two Class 1A heavyweights figure to be at the top of the division again this spring, though longtime Saints head coach Brian Femi wouldn't be surprised if there's company at the top.
"Kent Island and Queen Anne's always have a load of talent," Femi said. "And both are well coached, and both have a couple really good pitchers that can stifle you. And (North) Caroline has an amazing amount of young talent."
North Caroline, the last team other than Colonel or St. Michaels to win the North title back in 2012, is one of three area teams with a new head coach, as Vince Manetti takes the reins in Ridgely. Joe Brzeczek begins his first year as head coach at Saints Peter and Paul, while Garrett Nepert takes over at Colonel Richardson after Ryan Blanchfield's decision to step down during the preseason.
"I'm excited," said Nepert, a Colonel graduate who takes the helm of a program that has gone 39-9 over the past two years and reached back-to-back state finals under Blanchfield. "We've got a great group of guys. I couldn't be more thankful to walk in a couple weeks into the season with the group of guys we have."
Two of the guys who again make Colonel a state-title contender are senior Daniel Hesson, the 2023 North Bayside Player of the Year who recently signed with Salisbury University, and junior Jordan Regulski, a transfer from North Dorchester, who dueled Hesson in last year's Class 1A East Region II final.
Adding intrigue to the two regular-season dates between the Colonels and Saints — and potentially a Class 1A East Region I postseason showdown — is the return of Jacob Seek to St. Michaels. After spending last year at the Pro5 Baseball Academy in Fredericksburg, Virginia, Seek is back with the Saints for his senior year, bolstering one of the area's tougher staffs.
"Jake Seek coming back is certainly a big plus," Femi said.
Here's a look at this year's teams:
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Mike Tremper.
Who's Where: Noah Marshall (So., C); Nate Huber (Jr., 1B); Justin Marshall (So., 2B/RHP); Tanner Coulbourne (So., SS/RHP); Jacob Mitchell (Jr., 3B); Jaden Ferguson (Sr., LF); Collin Bair (So., CF); Donnell Cephas (Jr., RF); Kamarii Stanley (Jr., DH); Blake LaBelle (Sr., RHP); Landon Ludolph (Jr., RHP); Darnell Matthews (Sr.); Marvin Passmore (Sr.); Jacob Perry (Sr.); George Spry (Sr.).
Outlook: "It's just a rebuilding kind of season," said Tremper, who watched the Vikings go 2-17 last season. "Things are looking good for us. We just got to tie up some loose ends."
COLONEL RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Garrett Nepert.
Who's Where: Brayden Dadds (Sr., C); Daniel Hesson (Sr., LHP/1B); John Beaven (Fr., 2B/SS); Caleb Rouser (Fr., 2B/OF); Cam Todd (Sr., 2B); Jordan Regulski (Jr., RHP/SS); Gavin Whitby (Sr., 3B); Jack Walls (So., LHP/CF); Manny Wallace (Sr., OF/1B); Derrick Mitchell (So., OF).
Outlook: After helping call the shots as the starting catcher at Lock Raven (Pa.) University, Nepert returns to Colonel to begin his first head coaching job.
He takes over a program that went 19-5 last season and had two title bids ended by state champions, falling to 2A state champion Parkside in the Bayside championship before a heart-wrenching 3-2 loss in 11 innings to Clear Spring in the Class 1A state final. Those two losses alone could be enough motivation for the Colonels to push for return trips to both championship games this year.
Leading the way again is Hesson, a senior left-hander who last year went 3-0 with a 1.25 earned-run average, 92 strikeouts, 14 walks and two saves over 56 innings. Hesson was almost as troublesome at the plate, hitting a team-high .390 with 18 RBIs.
He is joined by Regulski, who was 4-1 with a 1.28 ERA and 59 strikeouts last year at North Dorchester where he earned the North Bayside Pitcher of the Year honor. Regulski was also more than solid at the plate, batting .377 with 14 RBIs and 17 runs scored.
"We're pretty confident in our pitching," said Nepert, whose rotation also includes Walls, a sophomore lefty. "We think we're going to be pretty strong on the mound. That's something typical of I guess the best teams at Colonel. We're feeling pretty good about the mound."
Nepert may also be excited as he looks around the field at what figures to be a solid defense, and his batting order.
"There's always pressure," Nepert said of trying to fill Blanchfield's shoes. "But pressure's a privilege.
"We want to be good in all three of those big parts of the game," Nepert continued. "I have a lot of confidence in our team, in our hitters and our fielders. And really I expect a lot out of them because I see how hard they work each and every day. So I'm expecting a lot out of our offense, defense and pitching.
EASTON
Head Coach: Albert Pritchett.
Who's Where: Colin Mooney (Jr., C); Josh Dressler (Sr., C/2B); Cullen Murphy (Sr., 1B/LHP); Alex Rhodes (Jr., 2B); Dustin Blue (So., SS/RHP); CJ Dugan (Sr., 3B); Dylan Cassell (Jr., LF); Kayden Webb (Jr., CF/RHP); Fin McGuckin (Sr., RF); Carter Mooney (So., LF); Garrett Fink (Jr., RHP); Dylan Fink (Sr., RHP); Michael O'Connor (Jr., 1B/LHP); Jonah Rich (Sr., IF); Noah George (Sr., IF); Evan Ensminger (Sr., OF).
Outlook: Pritchett hopes Monday's 18-1 loss to defending 2A state champion Parkside was just one of those bad days.
The Warriors certainly appear to have the personnel to move forward from that setback and perhaps push for their first division title since 2007. A first-team infield pick a year ago, Dugan (.355) starts at third base for the graduated Carson Brown, who led the North in homers (six) and RBIs (24) a year ago. Easton also returns Dressler (.395), Cassell (.317) and Webb (.333) — all second-team choices — from last year's 8-11 team.
"I think we've got pitching," Pritchett said. "Got a great outfield I think. We had no errors on Friday (against Washington), so I think we're going to have a good defense."
If Easton can hit it could contend, but Pritchett cautioned, "I think it's too early to tell."
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Jason Conner.
Who's Where: Scottie Ford (So., C/RHP); Noah Iacona (So., 1B); Liam Tidaback (Jr., 2B); Jack Walters (Sr., 2B/RF); Jace Conner (Jr., SS/RHP); BB Dean (So., 3B/RHP); Tanner Beck (Jr., LF/RHP); Trice Moore (Sr., CF); Aiden Crouch (So., LHP).
Outlook: The Trojans got off to a 3-1 start a year ago which included back-to-back wins over St. Michaels and Colonel Richardson, and finished 11-7, losing a 2-1 heartbreaker in the regional playoffs to North Dorchester.'
But with the graduation of all-North first-team picks Ryan Miller and Brandon Cannon, Kent lost the bulk of its pitching and a good chunk of offense.
"It's definitely different this year than last year for sure," said Jason Conner, who also graduated starting catcher Matt Wade. "We have a very young team."
With no junior varsity, the Trojans will carry 17 on varsity, including four freshman. Coach Conner will look to build around his son, Jace, and Dean, Ford, Beck and Iacona.
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Brendan Schulte.
Who's Where: Aiden Bonds (Jr., C); Patrick Reilly (Sr., 1B); Jack Grossi (So., 2B/RHP); Noah Anthony (Sr., SS); Hunter Austin (Sr., 3B/RHP); Kerry O'Brien (So., LF); Shane Bogardus (Sr., CF); Gavin Schulte (Jr., RF); Wyatt Offutt (Jr., OF/RHP); Traise Woolford (Jr., LHP); Logan Baierlien (So., RHP); Paul Horner (Jr., RHP).
Outlook: The return of first-team all-North picks Anthony (.340) and Grossi (.342) give the Bucs one of the division's more solid middle infields. The pitching staff looks strong with Austin (3-1 last year) joining Grossi, Offutt, Woolford, Baierlien and Horner.
"Definitely got some guys who can get on the bump and throw well," Schulte said.
Because he rotated players in and out of the lineup in preseason, Schulte was hesitant to judge his hitting, but does like what he has returning.
"Our top six in our lineup can definitely swing it, and we got some guys at the bottom end of the order who got some pretty solid swings," Schulte said. "What they are lacking right now is the experience of the varsity pitching.
After a slow start last year, the Bucs (13-6) went on a nine-game win streak before falling to Parkside, 2-1, in the 2A East II final.
"I like the chemistry," Schulte said. "We've got a young group of guys mixed in with a solid group of upperclassmen that are learning to work together very well. Each day gets a little bit better."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: Vince Manetti.
Who's Where: Caden Deavers (So., C); Cam King (Jr., 1B/RHP); Will Davis (Sr., 1B); Eric Deck (So., 2B); Thomas Necessary (Fr., SS); David Saathoff (Sr., 3B); Owen Carraballo (Fr., LF); Lewis Higgs (So., CF); Hayden Ogden (Sr., RF); Daylon Strange (Jr., LHP/LF); Johnny Radcliffe (Jr., 1B/LHP); Ethan Poore (So., RHP); Austin White-Eagle (Sr., OF); Jack Myers (Sr., OF); Colson Strange (Jr., OF); Wyatt Eaton (So., 1B/3B); Austin Frank (Jr., C/OF); Nathan D'Orlando (Sr., 1B/LHP); Jordan Kelley (Sr., OF/IF).
Outlook: After one year of coaching the junior varsity, Manetti succeeds Andrew Bishop, who stepped down after last season. The Bulldogs may not challenge for a division title, but that's not Manetti's focus in year one.
"My goal for this team is to just to start to play fundamental baseball," Manetti said. "I want them to do the little things right; moving runners over, playing solid defense. I'm just really looking to kind of build a good foundation for the future."
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Dave Morrissette.
Who's Where: TJ Leonard (Jr., C/RHP); Calvin Simms (Sr., 1B); Manny Reyes (So., 2B); Wes Windsor (Sr., SS/RHP); John Boyle (Sr., SS/RHP); Blake Bramble (Jr., 3B); Nate Fracaroli (So., LF); Vernon Price (Sr., CF); Nate Swann (Jr., RF); Brock Warrell (Jr., DH); Brayden Phippen (Fr., IF/OF/RHP).
Outlook: The Eagles went 13-7 last year, closing on a six-game win streak before losing 5-4 to Colonel in the 1A East II final. Morrissette's big challenge will be finding replacements for Regulski — now at Colonel — at Bradley (4-2) — now at Rutgers-Camden (N.J.) College — on the mound.
"We got to figure out pitching wise who's going to make these plays and who's going to step in and fill those two holes," Morrissette said.
Windsor and Boyle should give the Eagles a solid one-two at the top of the rotation with Leonard at three.
A first-team all-North choice a year ago, Bramble led ND in hitting (.451, 23 RBIs, 18 runs) and Boyle hit .364 with 13 RBIs.
"I think offensively we'll be pretty good for the most part," Morrissette said. "We're still going to hit the ball really well."

Outlook: Despite losing 10 seniors from last year's 12-7 team, Fitzgerald is stoked for the season.
"It's just a really good group of kids that are coachable," Fitzgerald said. "I'm really excited about this year. Our jayvee looks good. I think we have enough arms at the varsity level, and enough seniors that we could really be good this year."
The Lions could be really good at the plate with the return of first-team all-North picks Brown (.435, 10 RBIs) and Dickey (.431, 22 RBIs), and second-teamers Clark (.407, 13 RBIs) and Siwald (.395, 13 RBIs).
The graduated Devin Canter and Cole Glanding combined for nine wins last year, but Dickey (2-4) had a team-low 0.98 ERA and a team-high 46 strikeouts against just 15 walks.

Outlook: The Saints figure to improve on last year's 10-10 slate with the return of not only Seek. Wheeler, who led the team in hitting last year as a freshman (.429), and the versatile Sherwood (.380), who in addition to providing another strong arm, can DH and play almost anywhere in the field, were both first-team all-North picks a year ago.
They are joined by Wallace, who had the team's best record on the mound (3-1) last year as a freshman, fellow all-North second teamer Massaro, as well as Grow, Bealefeld and Queen Anne's transfer Fink.
"I think that's been our strength in the preseason" Femi said of his pitching." They've thrown really well. That's been a real plus for us. And we've actually played pretty good defense. We need to hit better. That's a big part of baseball."
The fact the Saints faced Wallenpaupack (Pa.), Patuxent, Severna Park and Stephen Decatur during the preseason was a large factor for that lack of preseason hitting.
"We're still trying to figure out how we can get our best nine batters in the lineup," said Femi, whose team has opened the season 2-0.

title: Runners, walkers brave rain in Denton Saturday
author: Maggie Trovato
content:
Runners, walkers brave rain in Denton Saturday

 March 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Maggie Trovato | Section: Local News 
 
 376
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON — Rain didn't stop the approximately 45 runners and walkers who came out to support efforts to supply clean water in rural Ghana and Tanzania at the 14th Annual Walk for the "WELL" of it 5k Saturday morning in Denton.The race was organized by local nonprofit Lifetime Wells International and held at Lifetime Well Drilling off MD Route 404. The nonprofit has raised around $25,600, with donations still coming in.
Those who braved the wet, windy and chilly day ran laps around a track on the property.
Marie Freeman, who is on the nonprofit's Board of Directors, said the event was a lot of fun. She recalled little girls at the event searching for worms brought out by the rain.
Vincent Dyer, a senior at Saints Peter and Paul High School, said before the race that he didn't know if his parents — who were walking in the event — had umbrellas, but he hoped they did.
"I hope they brought their boots because the track's a little squishy," he added.
Dyer was the student chairman of the event this year. He helped design the flyers and registration forms as well as dinner tickets for another fundraiser the nonprofit holds.
Dyer co-chaired the event to honor the memory of his brother Benedict Dyer, who died in a car crash in June.
"I think it's a great experience," Dyer said about being student chairman. "I'm glad they chose me to help out because it's a great charity, and I know where the money's going towards."
Lifetime Wells International was started in 2004. Its mission is to improve the quality of life in the developing world through engaging with and empowering local partners to install and maintain reliable drinking water systems, according to its website.
Kenny Wood, a Denton resident and one of the nonprofit's founders, will soon embark on his 67th trip to Africa to help with the organization's mission. He is tentatively scheduled to leave for Tanzania in April.
Dyer and other student volunteers counted laps, took the time and cheered on folks as they ran through the rain Saturday.
Davis Kimminau counted laps with Dyer during the race.
"It's just fun being here, supporting all the runners," he said. "It shows the dedication that they're coming out here in the rain for a good cause."

title: MLB owners approve sale of Orioles
author: Bill Haufe
content:
MLB owners approve sale of Orioles

 March 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 561
 Words 

 Read News Document

 David Rubenstein's purchase of the Baltimore Orioles was approved Wednesday by Major League Baseball owners, clearing the way for the Angelos family to finalize the sale after over three decades running the team.Approval of 75% of all owners was required, and MLB said the vote was unanimous. It came the day before the team is scheduled to open the season at home against the Los Angeles Angels. Rubenstein and his investor group were expected to close the purchase later Wednesday.
"To own the Orioles is a great civic duty," Rubenstein, a Carlyle Group Inc. co-founder, said in a statement. "On behalf of my fellow owners, I want the Baltimore community and Orioles fans everywhere to know that we will work our hardest to deliver for you with professionalism, integrity, excellence, and a fierce desire to win games."
The Orioles scheduled a news conference for Thursday morning with Rubenstein and Maryland Gov. Wes Moore.
Angelos and his family took control of the Orioles in 1993, when Peter Angelos purchased the team for $173 million. Angelos' health took a turn for the worse in recent years — he died Saturday at age 94 — and his son John has been the team's chairman, CEO and control person since 2019.
"I thank John Angelos and his family for all they have done to bring us to this point," Rubenstein said. "John led a dramatic overhaul of the team's management, roster, recruitment strategy, and farm system in recent years. Our job is to build on these accomplishments to advance a world-class professional sports agenda — with eyes on returning a World Series trophy to Baltimore."
Rubenstein's group, which includes Cal Ripken Jr. and Grant Hill, reached an agreement in January to buy the Orioles for an evaluation worth $1.725 billion.
Rubenstein, a Baltimore native, formed Carlyle in 1987. Before that, he practiced law in Washington. From 1977-81, he was a deputy assistant for domestic policy to President Jimmy Carter.
The Orioles are coming off a 101-win season and their first AL East title since 2014. Hopes are high after the team acquired ace right-hander Corbin Burnes in a trade with Milwaukee. Young stars Adley Rutschman and Gunnar Henderson have performed like franchise cornerstones, and Baltimore has another top prospect still in the minors in Jackson Holliday.
With all of that cost-controlled talent, the team's payroll remains meager, and the question is whether Rubenstein will be a more aggressive spender as the Orioles try to make the most of their opportunity to win a World Series for the first time since 1983.
Before the sale, the big off-season story for the Orioles was securing a long-term lease to stay at Camden Yards. That happened in December with a deal extending the lease for 30 years, with an option to end it after 15 if the team does not receive approval from state officials for development plans next to the stadium.
"Capping our organizational turnaround with a championship in perhaps the toughest division in sports, while fulfilling my pledge that the O's would forever play ball in Charm City, dovetails perfectly with the privilege to now pass stewardship of Baltimore's iconic team to a Baltimore native, passionate American, and celebrated philanthropist in David Rubenstein," John Angelos said Wednesday. "The Orioles are in great hands, and the club, as well as the city and state that it calls home, are well positioned for success into the future."

title: Henderson, Orioles pound Angels again
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Henderson, Orioles pound Angels again

 March 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 495
 Words 

 Read News Document

 BALTIMORE — Gunnar Henderson homered leading off the bottom of the first inning, then added a two-run triple in Baltimore's nine-run sixth as the Orioles pounded the Los Angeles Angels for a second straight game, 13-4 on Saturday.After winning 11-3 on opening day, Baltimore jumped ahead quickly in this one when Henderson hit a drive to right-center. The reigning American League Rookie of the Year had three hits and ended up a double shy of the cycle.
"I felt like I stuck with my approach — didn't try to get too big," Henderson said. "Laid off some good pitches, and put a good swing on the good ones."
Anthony Santander hit a three-run homer in the sixth for the Orioles. The first nine Baltimore batters that inning — an entire trip through the batting order — had come in to score by the time the Angels got an out.
Grayson Rodriguez (1-0) allowed a run and four hits in six innings and struck out nine.
Taylor Ward went deep for the Angels in the fourth and added an RBI single during the team's three-run ninth. Griffin Canning (0-1) allowed five runs and seven hits in five-plus innings.
"All of us need to take a look at what we did tonight and learn from it," Ward said ."And then turn the page quickly."
The Orioles led 3-1 before breaking open the game in the sixth. Of the first nine hitters that inning, six had hits, two walked, and one reached on a fielder's choice when shortstop Zach Neto made an error. After Santander's three-run shot made it 12-1, the inning had included nine hitters, nine runs and no outs.
The previous team to have its first nine hitters in an inning all score was the Kansas City Royals in the first inning on Sept. 29, 2023, against the New York Yankees, according to Sportradar. Although in that game, the ninth run came home on a sacrifice fly that was the first out of the inning.
The previous time a team had its first nine batters cross the plate before the first out was Arizona's fifth inning at Colorado on Sept. 9, 2022.
The triple was Henderson's last plate appearance of the game. He was removed for a pinch-hitter in the eighth.
"It's early in the year. I get it," Henderson said. "I get the decision."
After Henderson put Baltimore ahead 1-0, Mountcastle added a one-out RBI double that just missed clearing the big wall in left field at Camden Yards.
In the third, Santander and Mountcastle hit consecutive doubles to make it 3-0.
TRAINER'S ROOMAngels: Manager Ron Washington said RHP Robert Stephenson (right shoulder inflammation) threw a bullpen of about 20-25 pitches and is throwing another one Monday.
Orioles: LHP Cionel Pérez left the game in the ninth with lower back discomfort. ... LHP John Means (left forearm strain) is set to begin a rehab assignment Sunday with Triple-A Norfolk.
UP NEXTThe Orioles try for an opening sweep when they send Tyler Wells to the mound Sunday against Reid Detmers.

title: UP FOR THE CHALLENGE
author: Bill Haufe
content:
UP FOR THE CHALLENGE

 March 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 2069
 Words 

 Read News Document

 North Dorchester High head softball coach Carol Hubbard's approach hasn't changed."We're going into this season exactly the same way we went into last season," Hubbard said.
Well, not exactly.
For the first time in school history, the Eagles will be playing with a significant tag attached to their name — defending state champion.
"I think that's always in the back of everybody's mind, especially the kids that are returners," said Hubbard of making a run at another state crown. "But we've talked. We want to play as many games as we can, and we approach each game one pitch at a time."
That mindset certainly worked last year, as North Dorchester compiled a school-record 22-2 slate that was capped with a 1-0 victory over Catoctin in the Class 1A state title game.
In addition to playing with that same approach, the Eagles will also be playing with a lot of the same players from a year ago, including senior ace and North Bayside pitcher of the year Emilee Cohee, who punctuated a 13-1 season in the circle with a complete-game three-hitter against Catoctin in the state final.
Rock-solid senior Maggie Hubbard is back at catcher, as is the fleet Mackenzie Lewis in center field, giving the Eagles one of the Bayside Conference's stronger defenses through the middle. Also returning are sophomore first baseman/pitcher Jewels Vroman, senior third baseman/pitcher Maddie Nagel, sophomore Emily Boyle, and juniors Averi Warfield and Brooke Outten.
"The potential is definitely there," Coach Hubbard said of a possible state-title repeat. "Like I say, we just try to go one pitch at a time and we'll see where it takes us. We're definitely in a tougher region this year having Mardela in our region."
The Warriors were the only team to defeat the Eagles a year, winning 4-3 in the regular season, then 4-2 in the Bayside Conference championship. Mardela, which fell to Catoctin in last year's state semifinals, has the potential to play North Dorchester three times this season — once in the regular season, a possible rematch in the Bayside championship, and a third clash now that North Dorchester has moved from Region II to I in the 1A East.
"I think this team is definitely up to the challenge," Hubbard said of pushing for a second straight state championship. "I've got a good core group coming back."
As do Queen Anne's, Colonel Richardson and Kent Island, who have opened the season a collective 9-0 and figure to be the Eagles' chief competition in the North.
"I don't take any games for granted," Coach Hubbard said. "Softball is kind of a fickle game. Softball luck can go one way or the other sometimes. So we just try to be as prepared as we can, tell the kids, their job is to know the situation, whether they're in the field or at the plate. And we just take it one pitch at a time.
Here's a look at this year's teams:
COLONEL RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Brett Ireland.
Who's Where: Makayla Newcomb (Sr., P); Kylie Rhinehardt (Jr., C); Eileen Johnson (Sr., 1B); Clarissa Peugh (Sr., 2B); Aubrey Taylor (So., SS); Tyla Dickerson (Sr., 3B); Kendall Sann (Sr., RF); Sadie Prettyman (Fr., CF); Montana Davis (Jr., LF); Ryleigh Porter (Jr., DH); Kayleigh Bradley (Fr., DH); Alaina Hall (Jr., OF); Kailey Cummings (Jr., OF).
Outlook: Not counting the cancelled 2020 season, Colonel has lost to the eventual 1A state champion in the regional finals by one run in three of the last five years — Bohemia Manor (2018), Patterson Mill (2021) and North Dorchester (2024).
"We got to find a way to get one run better," Ireland said.
The move from 1A East Region II — where North Dorchester and Mardela reside — to Region I could help those chances, though the Colonels look to have the goods to again be a serious contender in the North and region.
"It seems like we're going to an easier region, but you never know," Ireland said.
Newcomb, an all-North second-team pick a year ago, returns to the circle. The Colonels also return second-team first baseman Johnson, who batted over .500 last year, as well as Rhinehardt, Sann, Taylor and Dickerson, all honorable-mention picks a year ago.
The Colonels graduated the middle of their defense, but Ireland said Peugh and Taylor are making progress in the move from outfield to infield.
EASTON
Head Coach: Ryan Brice.
Who's Where: Lailah Janes (Jr., C); Lyla Roe (So., 1B/P); Gemma Vogel (So., 2B); Brynlee Buchkoski (So., SS); Olivia Orrell (Jr., 3B); Leigha Bosley (So., LF); Mayah Wilkins (Sr., CF); Kaylee Verley (Sr., RF); Sammy Townsend (So., P).
Outlook: Brice has one of the tougher challenges in front of him in trying to replace longtime head coach Jen Powell, who stepped down last summer after an outstanding career that included state titles in 2011 and 2013.
"The girls are familiar with me so we kind of have a good relationship," said Brice, an assistant on last year's 7-10 team. "But I'm not going to say I'm going to take over for Powell because she was a great coach for a long period of time. She took me under her wing. So I'm just trying to put what I learned over the years that I was under her and put that to good use this year."
The Warriors opened the season thumping Parkside, and were even with Kent Island through four innings before the Bucs ran away with a 20-6 victory.
"We're young," Brice said. "We're good. But I think with the right coaching staff that we have we can make some noise in the Bayside."
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Michelle Phillips.
Who's Where: Paige Miller (Jr., C); Kate Cannon (Jr., 1B/P); Anna Bitter (Sr., 2B); Talicia Wright (Fr., SS); Michelle Menequin (So., 3B/P); Asia Wilson (So., LF); Melissa Landon (Sr., CF); Madison Raleigh (Jr., RF/2B); Heather Bilborough (Jr., OF); Aaryona Wesley (Fr., OF); Ariyana Green (Fr., 2B); Laila Johnson (So., 1B).
Outlook: Cannon and Miller were honorable-mention picks a year ago and should again lead a team that finished 5-14 a year ago.
"If I can have all bodies healthy, and they're willing to go where they need to go, they're going to surprise some people," Phillips said. "But we have to eliminate errors, and we have to hit the ball. That's going to be the biggest key."
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Jeremy Black.
Who's Where: Mackenzie Mascetti (So., C); Emma Fleshman (Jr., 1B/P); Hayven Applefeld (Jr., 2B/P)); Abbie Mahaffey (So., SS); Ava Blum (Sr., 3B); Lizzie McConnell (Sr., LF); Avery Eaton (Jr., CF); Emily Saunders (So., RF); Bri Kurtz (Jr., P);
Outlook: The Bucs scored 20 runs or more once last year. They've already done that in their first two games this season.
"I wasn't sure what to expect," said Black, who in addition to graduating all-North Bayside Player of the Year Allison Corbin — now at UNC-Wilmington — also graduated all-North first-team picks Rilyn Heyliger and Erin Bowen off last year's 11-8 team. "I knew I had six returning starters that are a year older, a year better, and have some additional travel experience under their belts. The two kids that were freshmen last year, again, another year older, another year stronger, another year smarter. But I just didn't know how well that was going to translate yet. We're still pretty young. I only have two seniors. So it's been a very pleasant surprise to this point. They're all hitting."
If the Bucs are to challenge in the division or region, Black knows his team must continue to hit and play solid in the field."
"We're not going to shut anybody out," Black said. "We just don't have that (dominating pitcher) in the circle. So we have to play solid defense and we have to score. Fortunately for us, the first three games, the scoring hasn't been an issue. But that's going to be the key to success for us. We have to put runs on the board in order to succeed."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: Lee Hutchison.
Who's Where: Gracie Calloway (Sr., C); Hadley Eigenbrode (Jr., 1B); Maddie Porter (Jr., 2B/3B); Alyssa Garlick (Fr., 2B); Hatteras Ghrist (Jr., SS); Katie Tribbett (Sr., 3B/P); Jordyn Hunt (So., LF); Elizabeth Knott (Jr., CF); Natalie Newman (So., RF); Anna Hutchison (Sr., P); Brooklyn Spencer (So., OF); Emma Hansley (Fr., P); Lilly Carpenter (Fr., C).
Outlook: The defending 2A East Region II champions graduated all-North first-team pitcher Taylor Dawkins — now at Bowie State — and outfielder Lillian Williams, though fellow first-team choices Tribbett and Anna Hutchison return.
But Hutchison, who begins his first full year as skipper, knows if the Bulldogs are to go far, they must shore up their defense.
"What I said at the end of last year, this year we have the same Achilles' heel defensively," said Hutchison, whose team finished 13-8 last season. "We're going to go as far as our defense can take us. Two games and we've got 10 errors. We're going to be able to hit. We're going to score some runs. But we've got to be better defensively."
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Carol Hubbard.
Who's Where: Maggie Hubbard (Sr., C); Jewels Vroman (So., 1B/P); Emily Boyle (So., 2B); Kinsley Peters (Fr., SS); Maddie Nagel (Sr., 3B/P); Averi Warfield (Jr., LF); Mackenzie Lewis (Sr., CF); Lola Allen (Fr., RF); Journey Pearson (Fr., RF); Emilee Cohee (Sr., P/1B/3B); Brooke Outten (Jr., OF/DP); Abigail Sann (Fr., OF).
Outlook: With the return of first-team all-North picks Hubbard, Lewis and Cohee, the Eagles figure to again challenge at the division, conference, regional and — if they get that far — state levels.
And though she graduated her dynamic shortstop and leadoff hitter Anna Hopkins — now at Salisbury — Hubbard thinks this year's offense has the potential to be better.
"We lost a great offensive threat in Anna Hopkins," Hubbard said. "But I feel like some of the kids that we've picked up probably overall make us a little stronger offensively than we were last year."
QUEEN ANNE'S COUNTY
Head Coach: Andrew Stewart.
Who's Where: Emilie Smith (Sr., C); Morgan Gottleib (Sr., 1B); Emily Rendulic (Sr., 2B); Caroline Taylor (Sr., SS); Autumn Huber (Sr., 3B); Abbie Denes (Sr., LF); Cameryn Jacobi (Sr., CF); Abby Gunther (Sr., RF); Hannah Martin (So., P); Mikayla Livingston (Jr., C/RF); Nevaeh Truitt (Jr., OF/P); Kiera Corcoran (Jr., OF/C); Emily Hirschbock (So., P); Reese Brooks (So., OF).
Outlook: All-North second-team picks Huber, Denes and Taylor are back for a team that has a senior and experience at every position with the exception of sophomore pitcher Martin. Now, if the Lions can do what often escaped them last season and finish, they could challenge for a second 2A state title in four years.
"The big thing we have to do this year is finish," said Stewart, whose team finished 12-6 last year. "Something we couldn't do last year. We could not finish and I think this group, the leadership in the group, we're going to see that we're going to be able to finish games this year. Offensively and defensively.
"Defense looks extremely well right now," Stewart continued. "We're hitting the ball. We're seeing the ball. Couple miscues on the bases that got to clean up, but other than that, we're looking really good. As long as we hit the ball I think we're going to win. We're going to win a lot."
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: David Fisher.
Who's Where: Madi White (Sr., C); Ayla Gowe (Jr., 1B); Katie Jenkins (Sr., 2B); Myla Ramey (Sr., SS/P); Lola Browning (Jr., 3B); Bri Crow (Sr., LF); Brooke Reilly (Sr., CF); Haven Haddaway (Jr., RF); Angel Bock (Sr., P/SS/3B).
Outlook: The Saints went from getting humbled by Mardela in their season opener to routing Snow Hill. And with the rainy preseason — and more forecasted this week — Fisher said it's been hard to fix things.
Jenkins, White and Ramey earned all-North honorable-mention recognition a year ago, and Gowe and Browning return after missing last season due to injury. That combination could help in the effort to improve on last year's 8-10 record.
"We're experienced but inexperienced," Fisher said. "Having them adds a little more depth, a little more experience. Without them there we were going to be very inexperienced at the corners, which can be challenging."
Fisher said he's still trying to figure out his pitching, but if the Saints continue developing they could prove to be a sleeper in the second half of the season and the playoffs.
"We're slowing getting to where we want to be," Fisher said. "It's a work in progress. Everybody kind of knows their position, but getting everybody on the same page with each other is taking a little bit of time."

title: Sts. Peter & Paul pushes for fourth consecutive ESIAC title, while Queen Anne's bids for a third straight Bayside title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sts. Peter & Paul pushes for fourth consecutive ESIAC title, while Queen Anne's bids for a third straight Bayside title

 April 3, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1749
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Dynasty?Some might say that's a little strong, while others might reply, 'Why not?'
It's certainly applicable, though Alison Beyer never considered the subject when she took over as Saints Peter and Paul High's girls head lacrosse coach.
"I was just hopeful that we would win a couple games," Beyer said. "And then to win the championship one year. And then two years. And then three years. I never imagined. That was not even on my radar."
Now, four games deep into her sixth season at the helm, Beyer and the Sabres are riding a 21-game win streak against Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference competition and have their sights fixed on a fourth consecutive conference title. And with 16 of their 20 players either sophomores or freshmen, that streak may extend beyond this season.
"We're only going to lose only two seniors," Beyer said of Morgan Quade and Emmary Sweeney, who is out with an injury. "I'd say at least for the next two years we'll be successful."
Beyer admitted she was concerned about numbers after graduating seven from last year's 13-4 title team, including offensive stars Hattie Messick and Evelyn Murphy, and defensive stalwart Ashley Reinoehl, and goalie Katie Bryan. That concern has vanished with what appears to be another talented freshman class, leaving Beyer and assistants Hailey (Stauch) Richardson and Sarah Krocheski to focus on fundamentals.
"It's all about the fundamentals," Beyer said. "I can't stress that enough."
Fundamentals and patience has proved a winning combination for Queen Anne's County in Kesley Fitzgerald's three years as head coach, and year four figures to be no different. The two-time defending Bayside Conference champions again look to be the team to beat in the North, and have a roster deep on talent and skill to make a run at a second Class 2A state title in four years.
Here's a look at this year's teams:
EASTONHead Coach: Katie Lowman.
Who's Where: Haiden Hulliger (Sr., GK); Zelia Proa (Fr., GK); Grier Kegan (So., D); Hannah Dahlen (Fr., D); Anna Quidley (Jr., D); Abby Jobeck (Fr., D); Emily Currie (Sr., MF); Stella Kabler (So., MF); Addie Knox (Fr., MF); Elena Szwaja (Fr., MF); Myka Motovidlak (Jr., A); Anna Krist (So., A); Dakota Lhotsky (So., A); Miranda Stup (So., A); Stella Petrichenko (Fr., A).
Outlook: Eleven of the Easton's 15 players are either sophomores or freshmen, so improving on last year's 5-7 mark could be a challenge. Then again, Lowman thinks the returning cast of Currie, Motovidlak, Kabler, Lhotsky and Stup provides versatility that could help her team's development.
"We have some key returners who are also a little bit young, but I think that bodes really well for the next couple years," Lowman said. "Little bit of a work in progress because we have a lot of new personnel in starting spots. So I think the first couple games we're going to be trying different combinations and seeing what works the best."
KENT COUNTYHead Coach: Jessie Bonass.
Who's Where: Emma Morris (Sr., GK); Eliza Loller (Fr., D); Aubrey Baker (So., D); Savanna Reynolds (So., D); Havianna Puglisi (Sr., D); Larah Mackey (Jr., D); Abra Hynson (Sr., D); Mary Jane Joiner (So., MF); Hailey Myers (So., MF); Carly King (Sr., MF); Gillian Bonass (Sr., A); Drew Davis (Sr., A); Addisyn Litton (Sr., A); McKenna Messick (So., A); Taylor Strong (Fr., A); Tess Fuchs (Fr., A); Grace Gerstung (So., A); Jane Cleary (Fr., A).
Outlook: An assistant on last year's 2-9 team, Bonass takes over as head coach with an approach that's both optimistic and realistic.
"We won our first game against Bo (Manor), but then we got destroyed by Stephen Decatur," Bonass said. "I think that stung a little bit."
That sting may last a bit with Queen Anne's, Parkside and Kent Island up next on the schedule, but Bonass has liked what she's seen.
"We're definitely starting out the season in a better place than we ended last year," Bonass said. "We have some new girls that are huge assets to our team. It may take us the whole season but we will definitely see a huge improvement.
KENT ISLANDHead Coach: Kaitlin Paukovits.
Who's Where: Brianna Legg (So., GK); Ava Mason (Jr., GK); Lilli Mellinger (So., D); Rita Yost (So., D); Ellie Burnside (Jr., D); Rylie Lowe (Sr., D); Jo McGrath (Sr., MF); Cara Steele (Fr., MF); Lina Donoway (Sr., A); Parker Tengwell (Fr., A); Gabby Polk (Jr., A).
Outlook: The Bucs gritted out an overtime win against Leonardtown to open the season, then, despite winning multiple draws, struggled with their shooting percentage in a loss at Sussex Academy, Del. But Paukovits, who starts her second year as head coach, is encouraged.
"It's a very good, versatile group," said Paukovitz, who was 7-5 in her first year. "Lot of young ones out there and a lot of growth that needs to happen. But there's a lot of good, positive things going on so far. They're very promising."
NORTH CAROLINEHead Coach: Mandie Shockley.
Who's Where: Ashleigh Lawry (Sr. G); Amber Baiers (So., D); Kylie Ogden (So., D); Mackenzie Cahall (So., D); Jordyn Roberts (Jr., D); Irma Sanchez (So., D); Emma Davis (So., D); Mia Schreyer (Sr., D); Reece Bisesi (So., MF); Ashlynn Bisesi (Fr., MF); Claire Blue (Sr., MF); Ashley Kercheval (Jr., MF); Riley Walstrum (Sr., A); Calleigh Tribbett (Sr., A); Gracie Faulkner (So., A); Maddie McNinch (So., A); Maddie Nicholson (So., A).
Outlook: The Bulldogs ended last season with a heartbreaking 10-9 loss to Parkside in the 2A East Region II semifinals. And though they lost their season-opener to Sussex Academy, Shockley has already seen progress from a year ago.
"We were down 5-1 and came back and tied it 6-6 in the second quarter," Shockley said of the Sussex game. "It seems like they've broken through that mental struggle that we've had in the past, where when we get down, the girls just get defeated. So that's what I took away from that game. So as long as they keep practicing hard, keep showing up we should have a very successful season."
Though Caroline moves from Region II to Region I — joining the ranks of Queen Anne's, Kent Island and Easton — the talent is certainly there for another winning season.
Lawry, who's been in goal since her sophomore year, is headed to Wilmington (Del.) University. Blue is bound for Lindenwood (Missouri) University. And Walstrum is taking her game to Ashland (Ohio) College after graduation.
That trio mixes with a roster of 17 that features 10 sophomores, including Reese Bisesi, who returns from injury.
QUEEN ANNE'S COUNTYHead Coach: Kesley Fitzgerald.
Who's Where: Maddie George (Sr., GK); Emma Dulin (Jr., GK); Ava Fields (Jr., D); Elizabeth Oldfield (Sr., D); Emily Keppler (Sr., D); Taylor Brown (Fr., D); Bea Holthaus (Fr., D); RJ Ensor (Jr., MF); Faith Novak (Sr., MF); Olivia Ryan (Jr., MF); Haley Cole (Jr., MF); Baillie Pinder (Sr., A); Riley Klepper (Jr., A); Kaitlyn Horney (Jr., A); Madi Brown (Jr., A); Kaisa Hickson (Jr., A); Charlotte Schmidt (Fr., A).
Outlook: Despite being humbled 14-2 Delaware state runner-up Cape Henlopen in the season-opener, Fitzgerald likes what she has on this year's roster. She also likes knowing what needs to be worked from the beginning of the season.
"I've told them, I told everybody, I would schedule it again even if I knew the score ahead of time," Fitzgerald said of the Cape Henlopen game. "It was a great way to open up the season. You know you're always going to be playing great competition when you're playing Cape. And without having to wait a few weeks to get against some of our better Bayside competition, we know exactly what we need to work on and improve on."
There is plenty returning from last year's team that went 14-2 and lost 13-11 to C. Milton Wright in the 2A East Region I final, including George and Dulin.
"I still think I have the two best goalies in the Bayside," Fitzgerald said of George, who has signed with Delaware, and Dulin, who has verbally committed to Towson.
The offense is led by Pinder, who is headed for Florida Southern, Ensor (verbally committed to Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University) and Brown, who is bound for Rollins (Fla.) College. Novak, who helped guide the Lions to their first conference championship in field hockey last fall, is another offensive threat teams need to be concerned with.
"I think we're going to see improvement for sure from the first game," Fitzgerald said. "I have a lot of trust in these girls. I have three amazing captains (George, Pinder, Novak). This crew is really working hard."
SAINTS PETER & PAULHead Coach: Alison Beyer.
Who's Where: Morgan Quade (Sr., MF/A); Emmary Sweeney (Sr., MF); Kendall Kroniser (Jr., MF/A/D); Samantha Murphy (Jr., D/MF); Caroline Ewing (So., MF); Avery McCall (So., MF); Kylie Kroniser (So., GK); Eden Zimmerman (So., A); Annie Albright (So., D); Eryn Callahan (So., A); Kayla Davis (So., D); Ashley Handy (So., D); Morgan Tanner (So., A); Julia Spero (Fr., D/A); Kate Sweeney (Fr., D/A); Bridget Gilman (Fr., D); Emma Hainey (Fr., A); Kaylin Palmer (Fr., D); Veronica Pool (Fr., GK); Emery Zimmerman (Fr., MF).
Outlook: Beyer knows at some point all this success will end.
"It will happen," Beyer said. "That's just the nature of the game. But when it will happen? I don't know."
This doesn't appear to be the year the Sabres' dominance ends. Quade, who is headed to Loyola, is back to push for a fourth title in four years. She is surrounded by a talented cast that includes the Kroniser sisters, Murphy, Ewing and McCall, and figures to again outdistance its conference competition — and possibly any opponent for that matter — by wide margins.
GUNSTONHead Coach: Imani Black.
Who's Where: Sarah Porter (Fr., GK); Kate Zottarelli (Fr., D); Emily Steele (So., D); Olivia Blusk (Fr., D); Peri Overton (Fr., D); Leah Rhoades (Fr., D); Elena Edmonds (Fr., D); Emma Morris (So., MF); Genevieve Baughman (So., MF); Grace Shepherd (Jr., MF); Sophia Kent (Sr., A); Layla Kent (So., A); Emma Walker (Fr., A); Alexa Duncan (Jr., A); Ellie Hodge (Sr., GK).
Outlook: This may be Black's greatest coaching challenge, as well as the smallest team she's ever coached at Gunston.
Injuries have dropped the Herons' roster to 11, and with little on the bench, Black and her assistants have focused on conditioning.
"We're really pushing stick skills," said Black, who has seven freshmen on the team. "It's a lot of one drill that's going to hit multiple things at one time. It's a lot to try to get together in a short amount of time."
Having the Kent sisters on attack should help up top, but the lack of numbers may have Black rotating players into multiple positions throughout the season.

title: Final Four beckons Bueckers and Clark
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Final Four beckons Bueckers and Clark

 April 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1167
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CLEVELAND — Their memories are blurry.Of AAU tournaments and Team USA practices. Of gold medals and deep 3s. Of the girl with the brown ponytail with the unlimited range who always seemed to know what was coming next and the blonde who never got rattled with the ball in her hands, by opponents or the sea of eyes constantly transfixed on her.
Yet ask Iowa's Caitlin Clark and UConn's Paige Bueckers their earliest impression of the other and you get generalities, light on details if heavy on respect.
Maybe because those years shadowing each other on the travel circuit across the Midwest or teaming up for the occasional international competition seem so long ago. Maybe because in some ways — in the most meaningful of ways — they are.
The NCAA Tournament that Clark grew up watching in Iowa and Bueckers took in from the outskirts of Minneapolis doesn't exist anymore. Back then, the inequalities between the men's and women's versions of March Madness were massive, from facilities to swag to TV ratings, even the branding.
It's not that way anymore.
Not with Clark and Iowa selling out everywhere they go. Not with Bueckers finally healthy after spending the better part of two years recovering from knee injuries that left her fearful the generational skills that made her the first freshman to win the AP Player of the Year award would never return.
Only they have. Just in time for the two players who have helped propel interest in the women's tournament to an all-time high to take center stage.
When Clark and the top-seeded Hawkeyes face Bueckers and third-seeded UConn on Friday night in the Final Four, they'll do it not in some anonymous gym with nothing but parents, scouts and college coaches watching.
They will play in front of a packed arena with millions watching on television and millions more keeping track on social media, an ever-growing group that includes LeBron James and Steph Curry and Luka Doncic and aspiring ballers from all over.
It's not that women's basketball hasn't had stars before. It has. Just never quite as many as this who play quite like this.
And while Iowa coach Lisa Bluder made it a point on Thursday to say she didn't want the national semifinal to be pitted as "Caitlin vs. Paige," everyone else involved seems to be OK with the arrangement because of what it means for not just their respective teams, but the women's game in general.
"It's a star-driven society that we live in," UConn coach Geno Auriemma said. "It's a celebrity-driven, star-driven, influencer-driven world that's been created."
One in which both Clark and Bueckers are comfortable traveling, perhaps because it's the only world they've ever known.
BIRD VS. MAGIC 2.0? YES AND NOThe parallels to the rivalry between Magic Johnson and Larry Bird that began when Johnson and Michigan State faced Bird and Indiana State in the 1979 NCAA championship are obvious.
"All of a sudden those two particular players came on and it just lit everything up, and it just took off from there," Auriemma said. "So it needs some stars. It needs people that have the right personality, the right game. And we have that now."
Thing is, Bueckers and Clark don't view themselves as rivals. Not in a traditional sense. If anything, they believe they're simply riding the crest of a wave that's been building for years, long before they reached a first-name-only level of fame.
Ask Clark why interest in women's basketball has spiked and she doesn't point to her record-setting career or her "did she really shoot that" range or even her team's success but simple exposure.
To Clark, the women's game has always been great. It's just taken a while, a long while, for the world to catch up.
"It's the platforms that (we're able to have now) that should have been there for a really long time," Clark said. "We've had some amazing talents come through our game, over the last 10, 20 years."
Talents that haven't quite connected in the way that Clark and Bueckers have connected. The easing of rules surrounding name, image and likeness compensation has allowed them to market themselves and their game in ways once unimaginable.
FOLLOWING LEGENDSIt's a history not lost on either of them. They understand and embrace the responsibility of being a role model, knowing they were once on the other end, looking up to the likes of college and WNBA stars Maya Moore and Lindsay Whalen.
"They were everything that I wanted to be like," Bueckers said. "And they won."
A trait that has followed Bueckers seemingly from the first time she picked up a ball. It's telling that when asked about Bueckers' game, Clark didn't talk about her impeccable court vision or precise midrange jumper but what the scoreboard says after nearly every game in which she plays.
"She's always been dominant," Clark said. "Every team that she's ever been on, she's led them to great success. It's just what she does. She's a winner."
That hasn't changed, though the dynamics around the way Clark and Bueckers are perceived have flipped over the last three years.
ROLE REVERSALIt was Bueckers, not Clark, who was the top recruit in the Class of 2020. It was Bueckers, not Clark, who was recruited by the Huskies, though Auriemma did point out this week "if Caitlin really wanted to come to UConn, she would have called me." It was Bueckers, not Clark, who won that first meeting in 2021 and became the "media darling," as Bueckers put it Friday.
Clark is in that position now. Setting the NCAA Division I scoring record and playing with a fearlessness that is equal parts thrilling and accessible will do that.
Security people had to clear a path deep inside Rocket Mortgage Fieldhouse on Friday to make sure she could make it from one media opportunity to the next. When UConn and Bueckers came through an hour later, the throng was half the size.
Even for a player who says on the court she can see things before they happen, it's been a lot. The 22-year-old Clark welcomes the attention because she understands it has brought new people to her sport. Yet she's not here to be The Star, as much as people want to thrust that moniker on her.
Three years ago, it was Bueckers. The last two years, it's been her. Next spring it might be Bueckers during her redshirt senior season. Bueckers is leaning toward this year's blockbuster freshman class, a group that includes USC's JuJu Watkins or Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo. A decade from now, it might be some young woman who didn't pick up a ball until she watched Clark hoist it from deep and Bueckers weave through traffic in the lane.
In that way, Clark doesn't see herself or Bueckers as the end result of something, but simply the latest links in a chain growing ever stronger with each passing season.
"It doesn't need to be one end-all, be-all (star) just like I think there doesn't need to be one end-all, be-all team," Clark said. "The young talent, it's only going to get better."

title: Easton follows great loss with victory
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton follows great loss with victory

 April 6, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1245
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton High assistant baseball coach Matt Blue died Friday night after a 17-month battle with cancer.Less than 24 hours later, the Warriors were back on the field, having decided to go forward with Saturday's home game against Southern-Anne Arundel.
And Blue's son Dustin wanted the ball.
"He wanted to pitch," Easton head coach Albert Pritchett said of his sophomore right-hander. "We talked before the game. He wanted to pitch."
Dustin Blue pitched three-plus innings of two-hit ball before running into a jam in the fourth inning, but by then the Warriors had built a lead that was never in jeopardy en route to an emotional 11-2 victory.
"He wanted to play last night," Pritchett said of Dustin Blue. "As soon as we knew (of Matt's passing), the kids, the players and families wanted to play. We felt that was the best way to honor Matt. Matt would have wanted us to play. I think we showed it was the right decision."
Matt Blue was a three-sport athlete at Easton High before graduating in 2002. He went on to play goalkeeper for Salisbury University's soccer team before returning to teach in Talbot County. The former boys' head soccer coach at Easton High, he was diagnosed with cancer in December, 2022. Matt continued teaching at Easton Middle School, and remained an assistant on Easton's varsity baseball team until he passed Friday. Matt Blue was 40 years old.
"I thought the kids responded," Pritchett said. "They loved Matt Blue. They loved the coach. The community has a tremendous loss. It's going to be hard to replace him. I don't think we will.
"So I thought the kids, in the face of a lot of emotion, a lot of feelings, and a lot of loss, they did a good job," Pritchett continued. "They were here together playing the sport they love, supporting Dustin, the family. I'm very proud of them."
Matt Blue gave a speech prior to last year's St. Michaels at Easton game on April 13. Before Saturday's game, the public-address announcer reminded players, coaches and the large home crowd settled behind the backstop of one of Blue's main themes of recognizing the moment.
His son did just that on a wind-chilled afternoon of gray clouds and big patches of blue sky.
"It's incredible," Southern head coach Kyle Lynch said of Dustin. "The effort. Obviously the emotion. You don't know what's going through his head, but he threw tremendously. He was great. We have a lot respect for them and coach Pritchett. But what Dustin did was truly pretty special. Been around baseball for a long time and haven't seen anything like that."
Dustin's first pitch of the game was a strike to Thomas Martin. He got Martin on a grounder to short, then hit JC Wilson with a pitch. Easton catcher Colin Moody threw out Wilson trying to steal second then watched Dustin get a called strike three on Gavin Crandall to end the inning.
Easton's starting pitcher issued a one-out walk to Owen Meyers in the second, induced Andrew Cook into a fielder's choice, then zipped a pickoff throw to first that led to Cook getting caught in an inning-ending rundown.
Southern's Brendan Hinkle was hit by a pitch to lead off the third. But Nick Youmans grounded into a fielder's choice, struck out Dylan Clarke looking before Martin hit a deep fly that Warrior left fielder Carter Mooney made a nice play on.
Wilson lined Dustin's first offering of the fourth sharply through the middle for Southern's first hit. Wilson was erased on a fielder's choice. O'Brien was then hit by a pitch before Meyers dumped a singled into shallow left, loading the bases. Cook hit into a fielder's choice to plate the Bulldogs' first run before Pritchett came out to relieve Dustin with Garrett Fink.
"I thought he threw great," Pritchett said of Dustin (2-0), who remained in the game at shortstop. "I think (he threw) 60-something percent strikes. He commanded all three of his pitches. Again under a tremendous amount of pressure and emotion. Just showed a lot of character; lot of grit. It's a tremendous effort again in the face of tremendous loss and emotion. He's a tough kid. I'm proud of him."
Easton (3-1) scored all the runs it needed during a six-run second inning — all with two outs — against Bulldogs starter Crandall (1-1). Carter Mooney began the scoring, lining a stand-up RBI double down the left-field line. After Cullen Murphy walked, Dylan Cassell roped another run-producing double to left. Murphy scored on a wild pitch. Josh Dressler (2 for 4) singled to score Cassell for a 4-0 lead. Dressler eventually scored on a wild pitch before Dustin capped the scoring with an infield, RBI single.
The Warriors tacked on another five runs with two outs in the third for an 11-0 bulge. Murphy singled to center off reliever Rhett Dorval and was lifted for courtesy runner Mikey O'Connor. Cassell was hit by a pitch. Dressler singled into the hole at short, plating O'Connor. CJ Dugan (2 for 4) delivered the inning's big blow with a two-run single. Dustin (2 for 4) followed with an infield single.
Fink, who escaped a bases-loaded jam in the fourth, yielded a run in the fifth, but didn't give up a hit in two innings. He was relieved with two outs in the bottom of the sixth by O'Connor, who struck out three of the five batters he faced to close the win.
"I think it's a healthy distraction," Pritchett said of playing the game. "I think the kids needed it. They wanted it. And they proved it was a good decision for all of them. I thought their energy was high. They were positive despite the emotion."
After the game, Pritchett handed the game-ball to Dustin.
"Dustin looked fabulous," Pritchett said.
COLONEL 10, NORTH DORCHESTER 5
AMERICAN CORNER — Senior Daniel Hesson hurled a complete game Saturday morning, striking out nine, as the Colonels remained undefeated.
Derrick Mitchell hit a two-run homer for Colonel Richardson (5-0) and finished with three RBIs. Jordan Regulski and Johnny Beaven each had two hits.
SOFTBALL
NORTH DORCHESTER 7, COLONEL 2
AMERICAN CORNER — Emilee Cohee surrendered four hits, struck out 12 and issued one walk Saturday as the defending Class 1A state champions stayed unbeaten.
Cohee, Mackenzie Lewis, Maggie Hubbard and Maddie Nagel (two RBIs) each had two hits for the Eagles.
Makayla Newcomb suffered her first loss of the season as North Dorchester totaled 11 hits. Newcomb struck out six and walked two. Aubrey Taylor led Colonel with two hits, including a double.
QUEEN ANNE'S 8, CHESAPEAKE 5
CENTREVILLE — Abbie Denes blasted a three-run homer in the first inning and Autumn Huber was 3 for 4 with a four-inning homer Saturday to lead the Lions.
Caroline Taylor and Reece Brooks each had multiple-hit games for Queen Anne's. Hannah Martin earned the win, allowing just one run and four hits over six innings.
BOYS LACROSSE
EASTON 9, STEPHEN DECATUR 8
BERLIN — Drew Schmidt scored the game-winner in overtime Friday night as the Warriors edged the Seahawks in a rematch of last year's Bayside Conference championship.
Schmidt finished with a hat trick, Hudson Royer had four goals and an assist, and Tyler Rardin added two goals for Easton (1-1). Warrior goalie Jack Kilbourne made 11 saves.
GIRLS LACROSSE
NORTH CAROLINE 14, J.M. BENNETT 5
SALISBURY — Claire Blue scored four goals and Riley Walstrum had a hat trick to go with three assists Friday to pace the Bulldogs.
Reece Bisesi and Ashlynn Bisesi (assist) had two goals apiece for North Caroline. Calleigh Tribbett, Ashley Kercheval and Maddi Nicholson had one goal each.

title: Sabres deal Seahawks first loss of year
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres deal Seahawks first loss of year

 April 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1358
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Alison Beyer knows her talented sophomore class will likely stretch the success of Saints Peter and Paul High's girls lacrosse team over the next few years.Beyer also knows senior captain Morgan Quade has been a huge reason why the Sabres have won three consecutive Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference championships, and will push for a fourth this season.
Quade scooped ground balls that extended possessions and scored a season-high six goals, including a third-quarter strike that put the Sabres ahead to stay Monday on the way to a 13-10 victory over previously unbeaten Stephen Decatur.
"She's such a versatile player," Beyer, Sts. Peter & Paul's head coach, said of Quade, who is headed for Loyola University after graduation. "She's just so smart. She makes it happen on the field, and sometimes I just don't know how she does it. It's just her energy. Her lacrosse IQ is on point. I'm a stickler for fundamentals and she's got it."
In a clash that featured five ties and four lead changes, Quade made a slew of plays that returned possession, or kept the ball in the Sabres' offensive end throughout the game.
After four early saves by Decatur goalie Addison McDaniel (14 saves), sophomore standout Caroline Ewing (five goals, two assists) gave the Sabres (4-1) a 1-0 lead with 6:42 left in the first quarter. A little over a minute later, Quade scored her first goal before sophomore Avery McCall (goal, three assists) set up classmate Eryn Callahan's goal for a 3-0 lead.
But the Seahawks (5-1), who like the Sabres have a roster heavy with sophomores (11) and freshmen (three), and had never trailed this season entering Monday's game, netted four of the next six goals, as Sadie Kauffman (three goals) and Lily Carson scored 18 seconds apart near the end of the first quarter to knot the game at 4-4.
Kauffman nudged the Seahawks in front at 5-4 when she curved in from the right and snapped a shot into the left corner. About a minute later, Decatur's Jill Burton was injured after being struck inadvertently by a teammate's pass.
While the play rattled some Decatur players, the Seahawks maintained their slim lead until Quade converted a Ewing feed for the equalizer with 3:02 left in the second quarter, then scored to put the Sabres in front at 6-5 just 1:18 later. The Seahawks again pulled even at 6-6 with 11 seconds left in the half on Laila Pacucci's goal.
"Lot of emotions going on on the sideline and the game," Stephen Decatur head coach Lindsay Owens said of Burton's injury. "Trying to kind of come back from having one of your players down. I noticed a lot of girls were upset, but we were like, 'Hey, we're proud of you.' They were able to kind of put everything aside and also play, but also deal with all these emotions."
The Seahawks went back in front at 7-6 on Caitlin Shimko's goal 1:45 into the third quarter. But Ewing scored on a pair of free-position opportunities 1:14 apart, returning the lead to the Sabres at 8-7 with 7:15 left in the third. MB Morse slipped behind the defense and tucked a shot past Sts. Peter & Paul goalie Kylie Kroniser (eight saves) with 5:54 left to forge the game's fifth and final tie at 8-8.
The Sabres won the ensuing draw. Just 29 seconds later, Ewing got the ball on the left wing and flipped a pass to an open Quade, who quickly dumped a shot over McDaniel's left shoulder for her fifth goal and a 9-8 lead with 5:25 remaining in the third quarter.
"We really needed to get the draw controls," Owens said. "They got those draw controls, they got the possession, they were able to come down, and they have some amazing players. They are able to shoot and go from everywhere.
"We made stops," Owens continued. "Our goalie played amazing, had some great saves. But the second and third opportunities with a talented team like Saints Peter and Paul. ... If you keep giving them that, they're going to eventually score. And that's kind of the name of the game right there; possession and draw controls. And we just didn't get enough of them."
Addison made a huge stop on Quade from close range near the end of the third. But the Sabres controlled possession and played settled in the fourth, outscoring the Seahawks 4-2 over the final 12 minutes for their fourth consecutive victory.
"That's what I wanted them to do the whole time," said Beyer, who called a timeout less than 5 minutes into the game to tell her team to slow down. "That's what killed us in the beginning. Rushing. That was the negative aspect of what killed us in the beginning of the game. 'Slow it down,' I said. 'This is where the beginning starts now. We have possession. Here's where it begins.'"
Goals from Ewing and Quade fattened the Sabres lead to 11-8 before Kauffman completed her hat trick with 7 minutes remaining, drawing Decatur within 11-9. And though the Seahawks would get no closer, McCall hit Ewing in stride with a pinpoint pass and watched her teammate pop her fifth goal into the net for a touch of insurance with a little over 6 minutes remaining for a 12-9 lead.
"Just like a typical play we practice," Beyer said of the goal. "Beautiful. They've been playing together for years. Just your average, everyday play. It was beautiful transition down the field. Just like we talked about."
Morse also finished with a hat trick for Decatur.
"They have a ton of talent on that team," Owens said of the Sabres. "Some of our girls that are starting, have never really been in a game like this before at this level. So it was really cool to have them see this game now in our season. I'm very happy with where we're at. We just need to fix a few things and kind of clean up the possessions and score on the other end."
BASEBALLCOLONEL 9, MARDELA 4MARDELA SPRINGS — Jack Walls had three hits and earned the win Monday to lead unbeaten Colonel Richardson.
Manny Wallace also had three hits for the Colonels, and Jordan Regulski and Daniel Hesson added a pair of hits each. Kenton Robbins yielded one earned run in 4 1/3 innings for Colonel.

Connor Wheeler was 1 for 3 with two runs scored and two RBIs for St. Michaels. Jack Brennan (1 for 1) drove in two runs and scored once, and Jacob Bealfeld (1 for 2) scored two runs.

Boyle struck out nine while earning the win. Nate Swann had a three-run double and a two-run single for North Dorchester. Wes Windsor, freshman Brayden Phippen and sophomore Manny Reyes each had two hits.

title: Sabres stay hot, top Seahawks
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres stay hot, top Seahawks

 April 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 853
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Hank Wolters was comparing his team's defensive performance Tuesday afternoon to Monday's loss to Cape Henlopen of Delaware."Defensively I think today we just played better," said Saints Peter and Paul High's sophomore goalie. "We were more focused on slides. One-on-one defense was incredible. Midfield defense was fantastic. A lot better than Cape."
Wolters hadn't quite finished his final sentence when J.J. Rardin, knowing his goalie had left out one glaring detail, stepped in almost as fast as one the five goals he had scored on the day.
"Goalie also stood on his head," said Rardin, bringing a smile to he and Wolters' face. "Great day in the goal."
Hard to argue that considering Wolters and his defensive mates held Stephen Decatur 10 goals under its scoring average Tuesday during a 9-4 victory that gave Saints Peter & Paul its fourth win in five games.
"Defense was on key and Hank was on fire," Sabres head coach Todd Wolters said of his son's 10-save performance.
Sts. Peter and Paul's offense wasn't too shabby either, as it built a 3-1 halftime lead.
"We were just moving," Rardin said. "We seemed to play a lot faster."
The Sabres were also playing a lot crisper.
"We were catching and throwing," Coach Wolters said. "And we were clearing the ball. We still lost the ground-ball battle, especially on faceoffs. Again, it wasn't my faceoff man. We made it a 50-50 (ball) every single time. I don't have people that want to go in and truly come in and pick up ground balls."
Sts. Peter and Paul (4-3) does have people who can fill the net, and on this day, Rardin led that charge, starting 2:24 into the game. A little over 3 minutes later Noah Zimmerman found an open Andrew Steinhardt, who beat Seahawk goalie Declan Horan (six saves) one on one.
Hank Wolters and Horan each made big saves throughout the rest of the first half, but Rardin again found the back of the net with 4:16 left in the second quarter, breaking in from the right side of the goal and slipping one past Horan for a 3-0 lead.
The Seahawks (3-2), who came in averaging 14 goals a game — not including their 1-0 forfeit against Gunston — finally got on the board with 2:24 remaining before half on Ashton March's goal.
"He made some good saves," Decatur head coach Hoffy Hoffman said of Wolters and company who held the Seahawks to their lowest goal total of the season. "And not to take anything away from their defense, but I think it was more what our offense wasn't doing today than necessarily what their defense was doing. Hats off to them for keeping us to four. But if we're not executing what we've been practicing all week, if we're not executing the plays, if we're not getting in the right formations from the get-go we can't be successful.
"I think that was apparent," Hoffman continued. "They did step up on some big occasions and the goalie made some great saves. It was what it was today. It just didn't fall in our favor."
Liam Durnbaugh began working on his hat trick with 3:44 left in the third quarter, when he intercepted a Decatur clearing attempt and deposited a shot past Horan. March answered with just 14 seconds left in the quarter to get the Seahawks within 4-2.
Rardin and Durnbaugh then just started unloading darts into the corners as they steadily expanded the Sabres lead. Rardin scored 52 seconds into the fourth then moved Sts. Peter & Paul to a 6-2 lead with just under 9 minutes to play.
A Sabres defenseman inadvertently knocked the ball past Wolters while trying to scoop the ball from the crease with 7:34 to go, trimming the Seahawk deficit to 6-3. But Durnbaugh ripped a left-handed laser into the upper left corner a little over 2 minutes later. Rardin followed, weaving his way through 35 yards of traffic before parking his fourth goal into the net. Durnbaugh then sent yet another rocket into the upper left corner to make it 9-3 with 50 seconds left.
Graham Geiser scored Decatur's final goal with 43 seconds left.
"Very happy," Todd Wolters said. "It's the first four quarters we've put together in our first seven games. I thought we played four (quarters)."
BASEBALLST. MICHAELS 15 KENT COUNTY 4WORTON — Will Sherwood went 3 for 4 with two RBIs and Connor Wheeler jacked a two-run homer and finished with three RBIs as the Saints stayed undefeated.
Brock Grow earned the win, allowing one hit and striking out five over two scoreless innings. Jacob Bealfeld (three RBIs) and Pearson Greenwood each went 2 for 3.
SOFTBALLST. MICHAELS 12 KENT COUNTY 8WORTON — Angel Bock was 3 for 4 with a triple and three runs scored and Madi White went 2 for 4 with a pair of RBIs to lead the Saints on Tuesday.
Myla Ramey earned the win, giving up seven runs (five earned), six walks to go with six strikeouts over six innings. Bock pitched one inning of relief, allowing one hit, one run and one walk. She struck out one.

title: Carlson still playing big minutes for Capitals
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Carlson still playing big minutes for Capitals

 April 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 729
 Words 

 Read News Document

 John Carlson has played more hockey than anyone in the NHL this season not named Drew Doughty, and that volume has not gone unnoticed around the league."He's playing a lot of minutes," Detroit winger Patrick Kane said. "As time goes on, you don't get any younger, but he seems to be keeping his endurance and stamina up and obviously capability for the team, as well."
A decade since playing with Kane for the U.S. at the Sochi Olympics, Carlson recently passed the 1,000-games milestone and is still shouldering a heavy workload at age 34. While Washington's longtime No. 1 defenseman isn't quite sure how he has been able to log so many minutes for so long — "I don't know, I think you just do it" — more than a half-dozen of his teammates from the 2014 Games believe Carlson's durability and longevity are a credit to his smarts and the ability to do everything on the ice, from scoring and setting up goals to preventing them by opponents while not letting all the shifts take a toll.
"His brain is just elite at how he plays the game offensively, defensively, so I think he's able to be super efficient," said winger James van Riemsdyk, now with Boston. "His physical tools kind of speak for themselves, but you don't play that long and that high of a level, especially at this age, unless you have a really good hockey sense."
Carlson is averaging nearly 26 minutes of ice time a game for the Capitals, who lean on him in all situations as they're trying to return to the playoffs. Veteran Max Pacioretty, who got to know Carlson in Sochi and is teammates with him again, compared him to Hall of Famer and seven-time Norris Trophy winner Nicklas Lidstrom.
"He doesn't expend useless energy," Pacioretty said. "He knows when to use it, kind of when to be a little bit more reserved, and I think that's a skill that so few people have."
Retired defenseman Brooks Orpik knows all about needing to pace oneself throughout a long season, as Carlson has over his 15 years in the NHL, skating more than 26,600 shifts comprising 23,700 minutes of ice time. And Orpik thinks his 2018 Stanley Cup-winning teammate has gotten better about picking his spots.
"He has the ability to be physical when he has to be; he probably is a little bit more in the playoffs than he is regular season," Orpik said. "It's impossible to play that way with the minutes he's playing, so I think he's gotten smarter as he's gotten older, too, which is kind of learning when to kind of go at it a little bit harder and then when to maybe conserve his energy."
While Carlson is known more for his offense — 670 points in 1,005 regular-season games — his defensive acumen is often underappreciated, given how many tough matchups the Natick, Massachusetts, native by way of New Jersey has been tasked with throughout his career. Ryan Callahan felt more than a few shoves in front of the net from Carlson over the years, especially in Capitals-New York Rangers playoff series.
"He definitely had some snarl to his game," said Callahan, now an ESPN analyst. "As a teammate, when you see an offensive guy, a defenseman like that who puts up those points but also has that little bit of a bite to his game, it drags the rest of the guys to have that compete and have that bite."
With that bite, Callahan pointed out, also comes Carlson being a reliable player whose consistency makes him predictable and easy to work with. Watching some highlights recently, Bruins defenseman Kevin Shattenkirk notices his former teammate "making these typical big-time John Carlson plays" to keep the Caps in the playoff race.
"There's no moment too big for him," Shattenkirk said. "Nothing seems to faze him. That usually comes with experience, but he seemed to have that from the start."
T.J. Oshie, who has played with him since 2015 after sharing the Sochi Olympic experience, saw that from afar when he was with St. Louis in previous years and thought Carlson had the ability to be a "mainstay" in Washington. He has been, skating nearly 30 minutes — including the final 4:38 — in a crucial victory at Detroit on Tuesday.
"He doesn't seem like he's slowing down all that much," Orpik said, "even at this age."
