title: Saints top Eagles, stay unbeaten
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Saints top Eagles, stay unbeaten

 April 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 879
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — St. Michaels High head baseball coach Brian Femi has always been known for the small things.And the small things again helped produce a victory Wednesday afternoon.
But the Saints also got a big pitching performance from Will Sherwood and a huge throw from center fielder Connor Wheeler that cut down a run at plate while helping St. Michaels remain unbeaten with a 4-1 victory over North Dorchester.
"Anytime you don't walk anybody you're going to be in a ballgame," Femi said. "Their pitcher (Wes Windsor) held us in check and we made a couple errors. And because Will pitched so well, it just kept us in a good position to win the game."
A junior right-hander, Sherwood (2-0) was touched for seven hits, but did not walk a batter and struck out 12 over six innings, mixing fastballs and curves.
"Coach was calling a lot of curveballs," Sherwood said of assistant Zach Wallace. "I was getting 'em over and they were swinging and missing at the ones that were low that he called. And locating the fastball was really nice today."
North Dorchester (4-2 overall, 0-1 North Bayside) took a 1-0 lead in the second inning. Nate Swann reached on an error to lead off the frame. Sherwood got a called strike three on Vernon Price, but Manny Reyes singled Swann to third, and Chance Blake singled down the left-field line to plate Swann. Sherwood ended the rally there, striking out the next two batters.
"He's picked up a little more velocity, but I've noticed he's got a lot more poise to him now," Femi said of Sherwood. "And I think it comes with experience. And he doesn't get rattled."
Sherwood could have gotten rattled in the fourth, when the Eagles' first two hitters got on. Instead, he struck out the next two batters before getting an inning-ending groundout.
The Saints (6-0, 1-0) took a 2-1 lead in the home fourth, but North Dorchester pieced together a two-out rally in the fifth, when Nate Fraccaroli reached on an error and Windsor dumped a single into center field. Swann followed by lacing a single up the middle that Wheeler got to quickly before unloading a strike to catcher Henry Mullikin, who tagged out Fraccaroli trying to score from second.
"I thought North Dorchester actually had the momentum in the early parts of the game until that throw," Femi said. "I think it just changed the whole complexion of it; took the wind out of their sails. And I think it gave us a little bit of an offensive boost once that happened.
"That ball was a little bit in the gap," Femi continued. "It wasn't like it was right to him. So he had to cut it off and then just made a throw right on the money. And that's a hard play for a catcher to make. People don't know. You got a guy barreling down on you. He still has to slide, but that's as bang bang as you can get."
Vernon Price hit a leadoff single in the sixth but Sherwood retired the next three batters to end his day. Anthony Massaro came on to pitch the seventh, allowing one hit.
"Pitchers did a great job today," North Dorchester head coach Dave Morrissette said. "Both sides. Will did a great job. Kept us off balance with that curveball a little bit, early especially. We hit some balls hard, but we got to score some guys once we get 'em on too."
St. Michaels struggled for offense, totaling six hits against Windsor, but scratched two runs across in the fourth inning.
Jacob Bealefeld worked a leadoff walk. Mullikin singled to right field. Pearson Greenwood's groundout to second moved Bealefeld to third. Pinch-hitter Eli Wallace then dropped a bunt to score Bealefield with the tying run.
Windsor hit Ethan Royer with a pitch. Royer stole second, broke for third and got caught in a rundown, allowing Mullikin to score from third for a 2-1 St. Michaels lead.
The Saints tacked on a run in the fifth. Hunter Gottleib reached on a bunt single and stole second. Wheeler hit a hard comebacker that Windsor made a nice play on before throwing to first for the out. Gottleib moved to third on the play and looked like he might get stranded, as Windsor retired Sherwood, then walked Bealefield. But Bealefeld broke for second, drawing a throw from Windsor. Gottleib raced home for a 3-1 lead.
"We bunt the ball and just try to put some balls in play," Femi said. "We had a lot of at-bats where we were striking out and just didn't put balls in play. He (Windsor) competes. I can't say enough about him and his catcher (TJ Leonard). We just had to do what we had to do not so much because of us, but because of them. I thought they played a really good game."
St. Michaels added a run in the sixth. Greenwood singled off the glove of the leaping Fraccaroli at second. Bobby Fink moved Greenwood to second with a sacrifice bunt. Two batters later, Gottleib popped up a bunt that Windsor made a lunging attempt to catch, but couldn't come up with the ball, allowing Greenwood to score from third.
Notes: Wheeler hit a two-out triple in the third but was stranded when Windsor got an inning-ending groundout.

title: Colonel strikes early, hangs on late
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonel strikes early, hangs on late

 April 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1096
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Perhaps one of the biggest reasons behind Daniel Hesson's success on the mound the past three seasons has been his practical approach."I felt like I had decent stuff," Colonel Richardson High's senior left-hander said. "Missed a couple locations. But you know, that's baseball. Sometimes you miss a spot, sometimes you put one where you want to put it. And other stuff happens. There's not much you can do about it."
Hesson tried to do as much as he could Thursday afternoon, limiting Easton to four runs over six-plus innings before the Warriors pieced together a late rally that fell short in an 11-8 loss to the Colonels.
"We got a saying: 'Winners find a way,'" Colonel first-year head coach Garrett Nepert said after his team's fourth straight win. "We found a way. It wasn't pretty, but winners find a way. So that's what we're kind of going with to make ourselves feel better today."
The Colonels (8-1 overall, 2-0 North Bayside) were feeling pretty good about themselves after sending 13 batters to the plate in a nine-run first inning that featured eight walks, Jordan Regulski's three-run double, and Hesson's RBI two-bagger.
Hesson (2-1) yielded three runs and six hits over 6 1/3 innings, striking out five and walking two. And though he surrendered Dustin Blue's leadoff homer to left-center field in the second inning, and Mikey O'Connor's two-out, two-run double in the fourth, he avoided the big inning for the most part.
"I was hitting locations early," Hesson said. "Missed a couple spots early. But really just movement on the changeup and everything like that was working well today."
O'Connor (0-1), Easton's starting pitcher, didn't get out of the first inning and was relieved by Pax Echternach. The Warriors' first reliever faced two men, including Regulski (2 for 3) who hit his bases-clearing double. Echternach was relieved by Cullen Murphy, who quieted the Colonels until the fourth, when Gavin Whitby (2 for 2) hit an RBI single and courtesy runner EJ Jones scored on a pop-out to first.
Down 11-3, Easton (4-4, 0-1), playing its fifth game in six days, had a potential rally going in the fifth, when Finn McGuckin and Dylan Cassell (2 for 3, RBI) led off with back-to-back singles. That rally was squelched though, when Josh Dressler hit a rope to short that Regulski lunged forward to catch. Colonel's shortstop, who has verbally committed to Wake Forest, got to his feet, stepped on second and threw to first to complete a triple play.
But Easton wasn't quite finished.
"We felt very comfortable today and that kind of came back and bit us," Hesson said. "They made it close in the very end. We got too comfortable. We have stuff to work on as a team. Me as well. This isn't our final form. We just got to get better as a team."
Hesson was relieved after allowing a one-out single to Carter Mooney in the home seventh. Reliever Jack Walls walked the first three batters he faced before Kayden Webb stung a two-run single to center, drawing Easton within 11-6. CJ Dugan's sacrifice fly trimmed Colonel's lead to 11-7. Blue walked before Colin Mooney singled to score Webb to make it 11-8. But Walls extinguished the rally there, getting a called third strike on O'Connor to end the game.
"At the end we didn't play our best baseball," Nepert said. "We have to continue to coach no matter what the lead is. Early on we kind of stuck to a good approach. Kind of went away from that later on in the game. But when you get a nine-run lead you get a little bit of a cushion which is a great thing."
Though his team's pitching was thin, Easton head coach Albert Pritchett liked how his team battled despite the early deficit.
"We probably had a few too many walks," said Pritchett, whose team issued 13. "But like the team we've always had in Easton, we never gave up. We had a hole. Cullen Murphy and Al Rhodes came in and held down things, and our offense chipped away. We got Hesson out of the game and got to the next pitcher and scored a few runs to make it competitive. Had a couple extra errors I would have liked to have got ridden of. But we're hitting the ball. I don't think this team thinks it's ever over."
ST. MICHAELS 16 KENT ISLAND 8
STEVENSVILLE — Jacob Bealefeld (2 for 2) homered, Connor Wheeler (2 for 4) doubled, and Will Sherwood (2 for 4) stole three bases as the Saints remained undefeated.
Anthony Massaro earned the win, allowing four runs (two earned) and eight hits over four innings. Brock Grow pitched three innings for the save.
Grow also went 2 for 2 with a pair of walks, and Bobby Fink has an two-run double for St. Michaels (7-0).

Queen Anne's scored five runs on four hits in the bottom of the third inning, with Mikayla Livingston and Emilie Smith hitting RBI singles.

title: O.J. was among greatest before 'Trial of the Century'
author: Bill Haufe
content:
O.J. was among greatest before 'Trial of the Century'

 April 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 937
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Long before the Bronco chase gripped a national television audience and the "Trial of the Century" captivated the country, O.J. Simpson was making his mark on the football field.The Juice was the best running back of his era during an 11-year NFL career mostly played with the Buffalo Bills. He won a national championship and a Heisman Trophy in college and set records in the NFL. But Simpson's accomplishments on the field were overshadowed and his image was forever ruined by charges that he killed his former wife and her male friend in 1994. Though he was acquitted of murder, Simpson was later found liable for the deaths in a separate civil case.
Simpson's tarnished legacy resulted in a muted reaction to news of his death Thursday. He wasn't acknowledged publicly by the NFL, the Bills or the San Francisco 49ers, where he played his final two seasons.
The Pro Football Hall of Fame issued a statement attributed to its President Jim Porter that said: "O.J. Simpson was the first player to reach a rushing mark many thought could not be attained in a 14-game season when he topped 2,000 yards. His on-field contributions will be preserved in the Hall's archives in Canton, Ohio."
Simpson's name remains on the Bills' Wall of Fame, which rings the inside of Highmark Stadium, known as Rich Stadium during his playing days. That could change in a few years when the Bills move into a new stadium set to open across the street in 2026. Fans previously petitioned the team to remove Simpson's name from the wall.
Otherwise, there are very few reminders of Simpson's time playing in Buffalo. No statues. Many of his teammates and friends have moved away or died.
"He and I had a bumpy start and then we had a great relationship throughout," former Bills defensive back Booker Edgerson told the AP. "Because he was a celebrity. And in his ways, he just didn't understand. He was a young guy. He didn't understand the game of professional football and what all the guys went through. He just didn't react to the veterans as I thought he should have. Like, disrespect and everything. But once we got to know each other and everything, and then eventually when we became roommates for that one year, from that point on, he and I had a very good relationship."
After his success at USC, Simpson didn't initially live up to the hype and expectations of a No. 1 overall draft pick. He averaged 642 yards and four touchdowns in his first three seasons with the Bills and some thought he would be a bust.
Then the arrival of coach Lou Saban in 1972 changed the trajectory of Simpson's football career. Saban built Buffalo's offense around Simpson's skills. That led to his breakout.
The 6-foot-2, 212-pound Simpson ran more with grace than power, though he could push through defenders for that extra yard or two. He danced and juked, dodged and eluded tacklers, using his instincts to find open space that allowed him to use his speed to outrace the defense into the end zone.
Simpson rushed for 1,251 yards and six TDs in Saban's first year in Buffalo. He followed up with one of the greatest seasons in league history, rushing for 2,003 yards and 12 scores in 1973 while earning the NFL Most Valuable Player award.
Simpson accomplished that remarkable total in 14 games and his record of 143.1 yards rushing per game still stands. Simpson topped 1,000 yards in each of his next three seasons and 1975 was his best all-around effort.
He rushed for 1,817 yards and 16 TDs and had 426 yards receiving and seven more scores that year. A knee injury ended his season early in 1977 and Simpson finished his career in San Francisco, where he grew up.
The five-time All-Pro was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1985.
By then, he was already a fixture on television as an actor, pitchman and football analyst. Simpson first appeared in an ad for Hertz in 1975, and legions of sports fans knew him as the former player who dashed through airports wearing three-piece suits and holding a briefcase while hurdling railings on his way to the rental counter to secure his car.
Simpson began acting during his time at USC, appeared in various roles on television shows while in the NFL and co-starred in several movies after retiring. His promising on-screen career and everything else was halted following the murder allegations.
Hall of Fame guard Joe DeLamielleure was a rookie with the Bills during Simpson's record-breaking season and became an important member of an offensive line known as "The Electric Company" that paved the lane for Simpson to run free.
Simpson had matured as a teammate by the time DeLamielleure met him, aided by guidance he received from Edgerson and other veteran players who helped him find his way.
"He was like a star to us, even back then," DeLamielleure told the AP. "He was like an icon even back then. ... But I'll tell you what, he was never cocky. He worked hard in practice. ... He was just one of those guys who was bigger than all of us. But he hung with everybody. Very humble to football players and very respectful to the offensive line because he's a guy who shined a light on the offensive linemen throughout the league. He was a special person, a special player. ... I watched Pete Maravich play. I also saw Muhammad Ali box. ... Holy cow. But I was privileged to play with him."
In the end, however, Simpson is remembered more for the murder trial than his football accolades.

title: Easton gets in the zone, routs Rams
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton gets in the zone, routs Rams

 April 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 825
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — This is how last season started for Easton High's boys lacrosse team.The Warriors lost their season-opener to Salesianum of Delaware then proceeded to piece together a school-record 14-game winning streak that ended in the Class 2A state semifinals.
Easton head coach Dennis Keenan may have thought he was watching last season unfold all in one afternoon Friday, as the Warriors surrendered the game's first goal, started slow, then reeled off 12 consecutive goals en route to a convincing 14-2 win over Parkside for their third straight victory.
"We're starting slow so we got to work on that. It's my fault. I got to get them into a warmup or something. Or some kind of dance routine before the game," Keenan said with a smile. "Get 'em a boombox. Get Saturday Night Fever going or something just to get 'em going."
After Nate Pusey's goal staked the Rams (3-3) to a 1-0 lead with 1:41 elapsed, Easton (3-1) struggled against Parkside's zone defense. The Warriors finally broke through when Hudson Royer snapped a left-handed shot past Rams goalie Nicolas Pastusak with 3:50 remaining in the first quarter.
Easton's struggles continued, but its defense allowed Parkside little in offense, killing off two extra-man opportunities early in the second quarter. The Warriors nudged in front when Drew Schmidt got free in front of the goal and tucked a shot over Pastusak's shoulder for a 2-1 lead with 4:52 left before halftime. Ty Finlay then won the ensuing faceoff, sprinted downfield and scored 12 seconds later for a 3-1 lead Easton carried into the half.
"First time seeing the zone this year and the guys just had to work through it," Keenan said. "Once we saw the seams in the zone the guys were able to take advantage of it. They tried to dodge into the zone too much early. Once they were aware of it, they pulled it out and starting moving the ball more."
That was evident in the third quarter, as Easton, despite a brief, cold burst of rain and continuously strong gusting winds, began finding openings in Parkside's defense. Landon Chaney scored just 1:11 into the third quarter to make it 4-1. Only 37 seconds later, Tyler Rardin bulled through traffic and flicked the first of his game-high five goals into the net for a 5-1 lead.
"Defense played great all game," Rardin said. "Offense, we finally just started shooting the ball more and they started falling second half. I think it was just trying to figure out their zone on offense, trying to find open shots. I think we got a lot in the first half, but really started making them in the second."
Campbell Taliaferro set up Rardin's second strike with 4:21 left in the third. Less than a minute later, Blake Royer zipped a pass from behind the net to Charlie Kaminskas, who completed the nice give-and-score play for a 7-1 lead. Blake Royer capped the 5-0 third-quarter scoring spree with under 2 minutes remaining in the third, parking an overhand shot into the net for an 8-1 cushion.
"I think our offense is getting there," Warrior goalie Jack Kilbourne said. "They're starting to click."
The offense continued clicking and widening the lead in the fourth. Rardin sandwiched a pair of goals around a Schmidt score, and Taliaferro notched a goal, all within the first 5 minutes of the fourth for a 12-1 bulge.
Parkside ended a 39-minute, 25-second scoring drought with just under 7 minutes left in the game, when Tavian Dashiell slipped one past Kilbourne, who along with defensive mates Kyle Dyott, BT Todd and Edward Whelan held the Rams to their lowest scoring output of the season.
"I think we just kind of played as a whole unit," said Kilbourne, who finished with 11 saves. "And we really trusted our guys to push them in the right direction. I saw shots, I was able to make a save. They put me in a good position.
"I should have had it," Kilbourne said of Pusey's first-quarter goal. "But you can't have 'em all. I think we're moving in the right direction. And I think we're only going to get better from here."
Easton closed the scoring with goals from Jackson Wieland and Rardin in the final 6 minutes.
GIRLS LACROSSEEASTON 18, PARKSIDE 7EASTON — Myka Motovidlak scored four goals and set up three others Friday as the Warriors routed the Rams.
Stella Kabler, Dakota Lhotsky, Addie Knox and Emily Currie each recorded hat tricks for Easton, and Miranda Stup and Anna Crist added one goal apiece. Zelia Proa made five saves and Haiden Hulliger stopped eight shots.
BASEBALLQUEEN ANNE'S 13, ANNAPOLIS 12CENTREVILLE — Dalton Brown had three hits and drove in two runs, and Dulin Clark and Jacob Clough each had two hits and three RBIs Saturday as the Lions edged Annapolis.
Evan Dickey earned the win for Queen Anne's County.
Colin Siwald and Dickey each had a hit and one RBI for the Lions, and Travis Sutch and Bobby McCarthy finished with a hit apiece..

title: Calvert middle schooler gets chance to golf at Masters
author: Ted Black tblack@somdnews.com
content:
Calvert middle schooler gets chance to golf at Masters

 April 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Ted Black tblack@somdnews.com | Section: State News 
 
 527
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Golfers of all levels from across the country aspire to compete in the Masters Tournament each April in Augusta, Ga., and for one Calvert County middle school student the dream became a reality, at least to a certain extent.Chesapeake Beach resident Luke Gladfelter earned the unique opportunity to compete in a drive, chip and putt competition for male and female golfers ages 7 to 15 and divided by gender. The three-pronged event at the Masters tests the talents and levels of consistency of youngsters in the key aspects of the game.
The Windy Hill Middle School seventh grader finished seventh in the National Drive, Chip & Putt Competition at Augusta National Golf Club in Georgia on April 7. The Chesapeake Beach resident tied for second in the putting competition of the event, which was part of the Masters held last week, and placed seventh overall in his age group.
The competition conducted in conjunction with the USGA, the Masters Tournament and the PGA of America, included 80 golfers from 31 different U.S. states, Canada and Australia. It took place several days prior to the start of the 88th Masters Tournament at Augusta National in Georgia which ran from April 11-14.
"I've always dreamed of being able to play at Augusta," Gladfelter said. "Now I get the chance to live out my dream. When I started playing golf, I learned a lot from my dad [Mark Gladfelter] and then I started playing in the Calvert County league. I played other sports, too. But I stuck with golf."
Prior to competing in the opening leg of the drive, chip and putt event, Gladfelter honed his skills in the Junior Tour events in Southern Maryland that thrived in the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. Established high school golfers Shelby Herbert (La Plata High) and Aspen Bikowski (North Point High) also competed in those events, which were initially not divided by gender.
Gladfelter's climb to the national finals at Augusta began on June 14 when he captured the first local leg of the event at the University of Maryland as an alternate after three others defected. Two months later at River Bend in Great Falls, Virginia, Gladfelter finished second with 142 points in an event in which the top two finishers in each age group advanced to the next round.
On Sep. 16, 2023, in the Mid-Atlantic Regional Tournament at Aronimink Golf Club just outside of Philadelphia, Gladfelter scored 156 points and took first place in one of 10 regional events nationwide in which only the winner in each group would advance to the national finals.
"Luke had a really good day driving and chipping that day, and he also got points for his putting," said Mark Gladfelter, an assistant principal at Northern High School where his two oldest sons, Jack Gladfelter and Sean Gladfelter, are current students. "I was following along the scores and Luke was way out in front after most of the kids had played. So when I was waiting on the last couple of scores to come in I knew he was in good shape."
The National Drive, Chip & Putt Tournament was telecast live on the Golf Channel on Sunday, April 7.

title: Colonels upend unbeaten Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonels upend unbeaten Queen Anne's

 April 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 953
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Makayla Newcomb has pitched well this season.But Colonel Richardson High's softball team either couldn't deliver the big hit or make the big play defensively when it was needed.
Tuesday, the Colonels got both.
Aubrey Taylor ripped a two-run triple down the right-field line and Newcomb crafted a complete-game five-hitter, as the Colonels defeated Queen Anne's County, 4-1, dealing the Lions their first loss of the season.
"She's had a good year for us," Colonel Richardson head coach Brett Ireland said of Newcomb (7-4), who finished with 10 strikeouts and no walks. "All year we just couldn't make enough plays or one thing would go wrong and it sort of snowballed. But we got the clutch hit today. We've struggled with the runners in scoring position."
Colonel (7-4 overall, 2-2 North Bayside) took a 1-0 lead in the first inning, as Kylie Rhinehardt, Clarissa Peugh, Eileen Johnson and Tyla Dickerson each singled off Hannah Martin (6-1), with Dickerson's hit to center plating Rhinehardt.
Martin though prevented the big inning, retiring the next three batters to end the inning, then setting down the side in order in the second.
Martin issued her only walk of the game to Peugh to lead off the third. Johnson (2 for 3) singled to left. Peugh was forced at third when Dickerson bounced into a fielder's choice. Taylor (2 for 3) then laced a 1-0 offering down the right-field line, scoring Johnson and Dickerson. Taylor raced home on an overthrow to third.
"Mostly I was just looking for a hit to the right side because I knew it would score both the runs on first and second," Taylor said.
That's exactly what her coach was looking for as well.
"Aubrey stepped up today and gave us a big hit," Ireland said. "Runners on first and second, she hit a triple down the line. I was hoping someone would hit it down that far just because I could see the right fielder was in right-center a lot. That (right-field) line was open and once it got there both runs were able to score. And Aubrey made good hustle to third. And then there was an overthrow and (she) was able to get in there and score. That really gave us nice comfortable lead. I was wishing we could tack on more but we just couldn't do it."
Martin yielded only one more hit the rest of the way, retiring 13 of the final 15 batters she faced.
"I think Hannah pitched extremely well," Queen Anne's head coach Aaron Stewart said, whose pitcher allowed seven hits and struck out seven. "Four runs. Our average is eight, nine runs. We score eight, nine runs — we had that one bad inning — we win the game."
Newcomb held the Lions (9-1, 2-1) to their lowest run total of the season and retired the first nine batters she faced before Queen Anne's scored its lone run in the fourth.
"I had a little bit of pressure, but I just go on top of the hitters," Newcomb said. "Once I got three-up, three-down on the whole lineup the first time (I was good). My curveball was good. And just the fastball, spotting it."
Newcomb recorded five of her 10 strikeouts through the first three innings.
That streak ended in the fourth, when Cam Jacobi drove a leadoff double to the fence in left field. Caroline Taylor then hit a line drive that Peugh made a diving stop on at second base. Autumn Huber followed with another double to the left-field fence, scoring Jacobi to make it 4-1.
But Newcomb got Abbie Denes and Martin to fly out to end the inning.
"Makayla threw a great game today," Ireland said. "She hit her spots well. We know Queen Anne's has some good sticks and I thought she was able to throw her off-speed pitch for strikes and got a couple of big outs with that. I thought the second and third time through the lineup, the changeup was good enough to get us some outs. "
Queen Anne's threatened again in the fifth.
Emily Rendulic stroked a single just over the outstretched glove of Taylor at short. Newcomb got a called third strike on Morgan Gottleib. Emilie Smith then doubled into the left-field corner, moving Rendulic to third. But Newcomb stifled the rally there, notching a strikeout and before inducing an inning-ending pop-up.
"We couldn't hit the ball today," Stewart said. "That's what it pretty much came down to. We've hit the ball extremely, extremely well all year long and we just couldn't get the hit today. Looked like she (Newcomb) was throwing the good stuff and we couldn't hit the ball. We normally put up eight, nine runs every game and one run isn't going to win you games. But we move on."
NORTH DORCHESTER 4, EASTON 1EASTON — Emilee Cohee hurled a two-hitter, striking out 14 and walking none, as the Eagles took over sole possession of first place in the North Bayside.
Mackenzie Lewis and freshmen Kinsley Peters and Journey Pearson each had two hits for the Eagles (9-0, 3-0), who ended Easton's three-game win streak.
BASEBALLST. MICHAELS 10, CAMBRIDGE-SD 0CAMBRIDGE — Connor Wheeler went 3 for 3 with a double and a stolen base, and Jacob Bealefeld tossed a three-hitter, striking out six and walking one, as the Saints blanked the Vikings in five innings.
Bealefeld went 2 for 3 with a double and two runs scored, and Henry Mullikin (2 for 3) doubled and drove in two runs for St. Michaels (9-0, 4-0).
COLONEL 5, QUEEN ANNE'S 3CENTREVILLE — Daniel Hesson pitched a complete game, striking out six and yielding no earned runs as Colonel (10-1, 3-0) handed the Lions (7-2, 2-1) their first North Bayside loss.
Jack Walls and Hesson each had two hits for Colonel Richardson. Gavin Whitby added a hit.

title: Easton continues new approach, tops Saints
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton continues new approach, tops Saints

 April 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1079
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — The rough start to the season was one thing.Not making contact though may have troubled Ryan Brice even more. So Easton High's first-year head softball coach tried a different approach.
"I told them, 'We're not going to have any more double-digit strikeout games,'" Brice said. "I told them before each game we're going to line up in the on-deck circle and time the pitcher. I'm not sure, but I think today we only had one strikeout. So I'm going to keep on going with that approach."
That approach certainly worked Monday, as the Warriors churned out 17 hits, including four doubles, on the way to a 14-3 six-inning victory over St. Michaels that extended their win streak to three.
"It's very hard to beat a team like St. Michaels like this," Brice said of a Saints team that entered the game having won three of four, its lone loss coming to defending Class 1A state champion North Dorchester. "They are very well coached. They're very aggressive. They're a good team from top to bottom. So for us to come here and do what we did is huge."
Easton (4-3 overall, 3-0 North Bayside) pushed four runs across in the first inning. Mayah Wilkins (4 for 5) and Lyla Roe (3 for 5) reached on back-to-back singles. Olivia Orrell and Sammy Townsend followed with consecutive run-producing groundouts.
St. Michaels starting pitcher Angel Bock (2-3) looked like she might escape further damage when she worked the count to 1-2 on Laillah Janes. But Janes (2 for 5) singled to right and Gemma Vogel reached on an error before Brynlee Buchkoski (2 for 4) doubled down the left-field line to plate Janes and Vogel for a 4-0 lead.
Myla Ramey relieved Bock to start the second, but Easton stretched its lead to 6-0, scoring two runs on a throwing error.
"Just an off-day all around," St. Michaels head coach David Fisher said after his team slipped to 4-4, 1-2). "I really felt like we were focused and we were ready. We just didn't click. Couple mental errors. It wasn't even the Easton-St. Michaels hype. It was just lack of focus. And then all of a sudden pitching change and we got down early and just didn't pull ourself out."
Easton expanded its lead in the fourth, cranking out five runs on seven hits. Roe reached on an error and scored on Orrell's double down the left-field line to make it 7-0. After Townsend singled, Janes and Vogel delivered consecutive RBI singles for a 9-0 cushion. Isabelle Ludwig added an RBI single before Roe hit a ball deep in the hole at short for an RBI infield hit and an 11-0 lead.
Roe (2-1) had a shutout through four innings, but issued back-to-back walks to Bri Grow and Ramey to open the bottom of the fifth. Roe was relieved by Townsend, who got Katie Jenkins to bounce into a fielder's choice. But Madi White (2 for 3) singled to center, scoring Ramey. Bock followed with a single to right that plated Jenkins before White scored on Lola Browning's sacrifice fly to left, drawing the Saints within 11-3. Townsend stopped the threat there, inducing Brooke Reilly into an inning-ending groundout.
"She pitched a great game," Brice said of Roe, who allowed two runs, three hits, three walks and struck out three over four innings. "I call her a dog for a reason. She's a tough one. Lyla Roe did an amazing job today."
The Warriors regained their 11-run edge in the sixth. Leigha Bosley lined a leadoff double to left. After a Wilkins single, Roe singled to right, scoring Bosley. Wilkins scored on a wild pitch before Townsend's groundout to short plated Roe for a 14-3 lead.
Mercy Haddaway reached on an infield hit to open the Saints' sixth, but Townsend recorded a strikeout before getting a pair of groundouts to second to end the game.
COLONEL 6 CAMBRIDGE-SD 1AMERICAN CORNER — Makayla Newcomb pitched a one-hitter, striking out 11 and walking just one, as the Colonels ended a four-game skid.
Newcomb also had a two-run single for Colonel Richardson (6-4). Montana Davis hit a two-run triple, Sadie Prettyman belted an RBI triple, and Aubrey Taylor cracked a double.

 SHILOH — This was act one in a potential three-part series.If acts two and three do materialize, North Dorchester High head softball coach Carol Hubbard hopes they go a lot better than this one.
Mardela cranked out 14 hits and sophomore pitcher Hayden Adkins hurled a complete-game one-hitter for her sixth shutout of the season Thursday, as the Warriors rolled to a 10-0 victory over the Eagles in a battle of unbeatens.
"Definitely an off-day," Hubbard said after the Eagles committed an uncharacteristic six errors. "We knew going in we're both tough teams. We both have strong pitching. We both typically put the bat on the ball. Tonight they outplayed us. No other way to say it. We had errors in the field. We didn't put the bat on the ball nearly as well as we're capable of. It just wasn't our day."
Mardela (12-0) took a 2-0 lead in the first inning against Eagles ace Emilee Cohee (5-1). Lexie Guy led off by blooping a single into center field. Julia Wisk advanced her with a sacrifice bunt. Camryn Dorr reached on an error that pushed Guy to third. Ava Twilley hit a comebacker to the mound that Cohee fielded. Knowing she didn't have time to get Guy at the plate, Cohee wisely threw for first for the second out. Karsyn Shockley then smacked a 2-2 pitch to the right-field fence for a double, plating Dorr. Cohee got Elana Donalds to ground out to second, ending the inning.
Cohee retired the first two batters of the second inning. Samantha Witte then hit a towering pop-up that landed between second baseman Emily Boyle and right fielder Journey Pearson. Witte raced to second on the play, stole third and scored on Guy's single to left field for a 3-0 lead.
"Eight of our nine in the lineup are batting .390 or above," said Mardela head coach Kory Shiles, whose team defeated North Dorchester in last year's Bayside Conference championship — the last team to defeat the defending Class 1A state champion Eagles. "We have five" — Twilley, Wisk, Dorr, Donalds, Abby Campbell — "that are batting over .500. That to go with our phenomenal pitching ..."
Phenomenal indeed.
Coming into Thursday's game the Warriors had yielded just two runs in regular-season play — that to Colonel Richardson. Adkins (7-0) struck out eight and walked two. Then there's Twilley who has only given up one hit all season.
"Mardela played a great game," Hubbard said. "They made the plays when we put the ball in play. And Hayden pitched a great game."
North Dorchester got its only hit in the third, when Mackenzie Lewis beat out a spinning infield single up the third-base line. Cohee followed with a walk, but Adkins squelched the rally there, getting Kinsley Peters to ground out to short.
The closest the Eagles came to a second hit came in the fourth when Maggie Hubbard scorched a hard grounder went off first baseman Shockley that Shiles called an error. Adkins retired 11 of the final 12 batters she faced, surrendering a leadofff walk to Maddie Nagel in the seventh. Nagel, who was hit on the ankle with ball four, was lifted for a courtesy runner, who was thrown out trying to steal second.
Mardela extended its lead to 4-0 in the fourth. Guy and Wisk hit back-to-back two-out singles before Dorr singled to right, scoring Guy.
The Warriors put together another two-out rally in the fifth, but Cohee got a called third strike on Witte to end the inning.
"I thought Emilee pitched well," Hubbard said, whose starter gave up 11 hits, the last, an RBI double by Dorr that pushed Mardela's lead to 5-0 in the sixth and ended Cohee's day on the mound. "She gave up one walk. Not a bad performance. Can't ask a whole lot more out of your pitcher than that."
Twilley greeted reliever Jewels Vroman with an RBI single. The Warriors tacked on two more runs — both scoring on errors.
"I got a feeling we'll see them one more time, if not two more times," Shiles said of a potential rematch with the Eagles in the Bayside Conference championship and the Class 1A East Region I final.

title: Lions regain form with bounce-back win
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions regain form with bounce-back win

 April 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1468
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Yes, its opponent was different.But so was its execution on both ends of the field.
"I think we were more cohesive and we played a lot more calmly," Lions senior defender Faith Novak said. "Still intense. But more calm to the point where we could communicate, stay in our zones, and really just work more as a unit than individual defense."
That was apparent early Friday night, as Queen Anne's County High's girls lacrosse team — three days after losing to Stephen Decatur — held a red-hot North Caroline team to its lowest goal total of the season during a convincing 15-4 victory on senior night at Lions Stadium.
"It's Queen Anne's. They are a powerhouse," North Caroline head coach Mandie Shockley said after the two-time defending Bayside Conference champions had ended her team's five-game winning streak. "We knew what to expect. They just outplayed us."
It was the Lions who had their five-game win streak ended Tuesday night as Decatur earned a 10-7 victory over Queen Anne's. Head coach Kesley Fitzgerald's bunch certainly appeared to have shaken off that rare conference loss Friday, as they spotted the Bulldogs the game's first goal then proceeded to score the next 12.
"We take a lot of pride in our preparation and I feel at practice (Wednesday and Thursday) we were all working to fix our flaws," Novak said. "And I think that really showed how much we worked to fix what we needed to work on. Like our transition looked a lot better. We were more comfortable with it. We were more comfortable with taking pressure, and I feel that led us to the win."
The Bulldogs (5-2 overall, 1-1 North Bayside), who averaged 17.4 goals an outing during their five-game win streak, took a 1-0 lead 4:23 into the game, when Claire Blue scored on a free-position opportunity.
It would be almost another 32 minutes of play before North Caroline put another shot past Queen Anne's goalie Maddie George (five saves), as Reece Bisesi scored 30 seconds into the fourth quarter, ending the Lions' streak of 12 consecutive goals.
"The draw," Shockley said. "Every other game we've played we've dominated the draw and we just could not get it. I think we got five, maybe six. And Queen Anne's is a team, they don't drop the ball. They definitely dominated the draw (winning 13). It was hard for us to get it back. We had a few, but we just had a lot of trouble getting to the net. They played hard."
The Lions (6-2, 2-0) also played with a longtime trademark of Fitzgerald's teams — patience.
"More calm. More patience," Fitzgerald said. "There were a few times where we still looked for that first push on the shot or pass."
But those times were far outnumbered by Queen Anne's Baillie Pinder (four goals, four assists) and RJ Ensor (three goals, four assists) waiting and finding teammates either cutting toward the goal or finding a small opening in Caroline's defense.
"Off-ballers were working a lot better tonight seeing things," said Fitzgerald, whose team has now won six of seven. "More communication. More composure. I think a turning point was they realized, we take it in, get your cut, and if you don't like what you see, pull it back out and then find something else."
After being held to just one first-quarter goal — that coming with 3:20 left in the opening period when Riley Klepper (game-high five goals) converted a Pinder dish to tie the game at 1-1, Queen Anne's blew open the game, outscoring the Bulldogs 7-0 in the second quarter and 4-0 in the third.
"We went to practice and we knew we had work to do," Pinder said. "I think this time we had a lot more patience and trust in ourselves with the ball. And we just wanted to come out and prove ourselves after the last game. Especially in the second half on offense. I could feel us a lot more calm. And we knew what we were going to do. We weren't playing as frantic. We looked for the best thing and didn't force anything."
Ensor ignited the Lions' 8-0 second quarter when she set up the first of Pinder's four goals 31 seconds into the period. Less than 2 minutes later, Ensor juked defenders and beat North Caroline goalie Ashleigh Lawry (eight saves) for a 3-1 lead.
North Caroline called time. A little over a minute later, Pinder found space off the left post, waited, then flicked a pass to Klepper, who wasted little time dumping the ball into the back of the net. Queen Anne's intercepted a Bulldog clearing attempt, got the ball quickly to Pinder, who neatly tucked in her second goal for a 5-1 lead. Klepper converted a pair of passes from Pinder for goals and another off an Ensor feed for an 8-1 halftime lead.
Madi Brown scored on a free-position opportunity before Ensor sandwiched a pair of scores around another Pinder goal — the second off a Kaitlyn Horney pass.
North Caroline played even with the Lions in the fourth, as Bisesi scored twice and Riley Walstrum once. Pinder, Kaisa Hickson and Brown added goals for Queen Anne's.
"Obviously their goalie is a good goalie," Shockley said of Brown. "Maybe not our best day on that side, but it happens."
EASTON 10, J.M. BENNETT 7
EASTON — Dakota Lhotsky scored four goals and Miranda Stup had a hat trick as the Warriors won for the fourth time in five games.
Emily Currie scored twice for Easton (4-2) and Myka Motovidlak added a goal. Warrior goalies Haiden Hulliger and Zelia Proa each made four saves.
SSPP 23, GUNSTON 5
CENTREVILLE — Sophomore Caroline Ewing had five goals and set up three others, and senior Morgan Quade notched a hat trick and doled out seven assists Thursday as the Sabres extended their Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference win streak to 24.
Freshman Emery Zimmerman finished with three goals and three assists for Sts. Peter & Paul (8-1, 4-0). Sophomores Eryn Callahan (three assists) and Avery McCall, and freshmen Kate Sweeney (assist) and Julia Spero scored two goals apiece. Eden Zimmerman (three assists), Ashley Handy, Samantha Murphy and Emma Hainey each scored one goal.
BASEBALL
ST. MICHAELS 13 POCOMOKE 0
ST. MICHAELS — Bobby Fink tossed four innings of one-hit ball, striking out six and walking none Thursday as the Saints improved to 11-0.
St. Michaels' Jacob Bealefeld doubled, drove in three runs and was hit by a pitch three times. Brock Grow (1 for 1) scored three runs and was hit twice, and Ethan Royer was 1 for 1 with two runs and two RBIs. Eli Wallace pitched an inning of one-hit relief, fanning one.
QUEEN ANNE'S 14 J.M. BENNETT 4
SALISBURY — Evan Dickey pitched a complete-game four-hitter, striking out seven, and Colin Siwald went 3 for 4 with three RBIs Thursday to pace the Lions.
Jacob Clough was 3 for 4 with two RBIs, Noah Cramer collected three hits, and Bobby McCarthy drove in four runs for Queen Anne's County (9-2).
SOFTBALL
QUEEN ANNE'S 11 J.M. BENNETT 0
SALISBURY — Senior Autumn Huber knocked in four runs with three doubles as the Lions rebounded from their first loss of the season with a shutout of the Clippers.
Emily Hirschbock yielded four hits and no runs over five innings to earn the win for Queen Anne's (10-1), striking out six and walking just two. Caroline Taylor, Camaryn Jacobi and Hannah Martin each had multiple hits for the Lions.
EASTON 16, WICOMICO 2
SALISBURY — Sammy Townsend swatted a pair of home runs and also singled, driving in five, as the Warriors improved to 5-4 on Thursday.
Townsend also earned the win for Easton, allowing six hits and two runs over six innings. She struck out 11 and walked none. Leilani Brooks, Olivia Orrell and Gemma Vogel each smacked run-producing doubles, and Kaylee Verley drilled a two-run double. Isabelle Ludwig (double), Vogel and Brynlee Buchkoski each had multiple-hit games for the Warriors.
COL. RICHARDSON 17 WASHINGTON 0
AMERICAN CORNER — Eileen Johnson and Kylie Rhinehardt each had two hits, and Makayla Newcomb tossed three innings of no-hit ball, fanning five to lead the Colonels (8-4).
Rhinehardt pitched two scoreless innings of relief, striking out six, to complete the no-hitter.
Clarissa Peugh doubled for Colonel and Alaina Hall (RBI) and Tyla Dickerson each had a hit.
ST. MICHAELS 12 POCOMOKE 2
ST. MICHAELS — Lilly Haddaway went 4 for 4 with four RBIs and two runs as the Saints defeated the Warriors, raising their record to 5-6.
Myla Ramey earned the win, giving up two earned runs and four hits over three innings. Ramey struck out four and walked two. Mercy Haddaway worked two innings of scoreless relief, allowing one hit, a walk and striking out two.
Madi White was 2 for 3 with a double and two RBIs, Mercy Haddaway (double) and Gabby Pickens each went 2 for 3, and Katie Jenkins was 2 for 4 with a triple and double.

title: Seek, Saints outduel Palmer, Lions
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Seek, Saints outduel Palmer, Lions

 April 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1419
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Like many a game that shapes a division race, it was close.Each team turned an inning-ending double play.
Each team had a batter hit by a pitch and another intentionally walk.
Each team got outstanding performances from their big-name pitchers.
And each team finished with five hits.
But it was St. Michaels High's baseball team that produced the decisive — and what proved to be the last — hit. That hit came with two outs and the bases loaded in the bottom of the fifth inning Monday, when Jack Brennen chopped a slow bouncer down the third-base line for an infield hit that scored Pearson Greenwood with the winning run in a 3-2 Saints victory at Harold Baines Field.
St. Michaels (12-0 overall, 5-0 North Bayside) entered Tuesday tied atop the division with Colonel Richardson (12-1, 5-0) while Queen Anne's slipped to 9-3, 2-2.
"It was a very good high school baseball game," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said. "Both teams played well. It was an outstanding pitching duel. Both teams got timely hits. Both played good defense."
And both had scored two runs apiece heading into the bottom of the fifth.
That's when Will Sherwood lined a one-out single to center field. Queen Anne's right-hander Noah Palmer (3-1) walked Greenwood. Both runners advanced on a wild pitch before Palmer issued an intentional pass to Jacob Bealefeld, loading the bases. Henry Mullikin grounded to third baseman Jacob Clough, who threw home to force Sherwood at the plate for the second out.
Brennen then beat a grounder down the third-base line. Clough got to the ball, but didn't have time to make a throw to first as Greenwood raced home with the go-ahead run. Femi and Queen Anne's head coach Chris Fitzgerald agreed Brennen's bouncer was an infield hit — the last hit for either team the rest of the game.
"Heavyweight game for sure," Fitzgerald said. "They got the hit they needed and came away with the W."
Both pitchers were impressive, with St. Michaels senior left-hander Jacob Seek (4-0) striking out a season-high 13 in a complete-game victory. Seek allowed one earned run and walked two.
"This is what he's done all year," Femi said of Seek. "He just goes out and makes big pitches in big situations. The bigger the situation the bigger the pitcher. And he's a leader."
Queen Anne's Dalton Brown led off the game with a single, but Seek struck out the next three batters.
Down 2-0, the Lions had a rally working in the second, when Clough walked on four pitches and Colin Siwald singled to left. Seek fanned Bobby McCarthy, but Palmer reached with a bunt single up the third-base line, loading the bases. Gavin Leith grounded into a fielder's choice that plated Clough to make it 2-1. Seek ended the inning when Brown skied out to center.
"At moments it was little tight, but I think we did a good job of pulling out of it and being efficient," Seek said. "My curveball was on point today I felt like. I felt like I had a little mechanical issue that I had to (work the) kink out early. And I think when I figured that out in that second inning it kind of picked up for me and I was able to be more efficient with my pitches and hit my locations."
The Lions though pulled even in the top of the third. With one out, Seek struck out Dulin Clark. But the ball kicked away from Mullikin behind the plate. By the time St. Michaels' catcher located and retrieved the ball over by the St. Michaels dugout, Clark was on second. Evan Dickey then laced a 1-2 offering up the middle to score Clark with the tying run.
The closest Queen Anne's came to breaking the 2-2 tie was in the fourth. Leith reached on an infield hit and moved to second on a passed ball. After Brown was intentionally walk, Seek fanned Noah Cramer to end the inning.
Seek retired nine of the final 10 batters he faced. McCarthy reached with one out in the sixth when he was hit by a pitch before Palmer bounced to Bealefeld at third to a 5-4-3 inning-ending double play.
"That turned the game around I thought," Femi said. "Jake's played well for us all year. And that just swung the momentum our way."
Palmer delivered yet another quality performance for the Lions, striking out eight and walking four in 5 1/3 innings.
"I thought he was fantastic," Femi said of Palmer. "He beat us last year. We haven't hit him in two years. He competes. He changes speeds. He throws multiple pitches. I think he's one of the better pitchers in the Bayside."
But the Saints pushed two runs across in the home half of the first. Connor Wheeler was hit by a pitch and stole second base. Sherwood reached on an error, advancing Wheeler to third. Palmer looked like he might escape any damage when he struck out Greenwood and Bealefeld. But Mullikin drove a 1-1 pitch up the middle to score Wheeler and Sherwood for a 2-0 lead. Brennen followed with a single before Palmer fanned Bobby Fink to end the frame.
"After that first inning, it was rough," Palmer said. "But I came back and I feel like I was dialed in."
Blending his fastball and curve, Palmer wouldn't face more than four batters over the next three innings. Wheeler hit a two-out single in the second, stole second base and moved to third on a passed ball before Palmer got Sherwood to bounce out to third. The right-hander walked Bealefeld with one out in the third. Mullikin flew out to center fielder Brown, who fired a strike to first to double off Bealefield for the inning-ending double play.
Brock Grow got on via a two-out walk in the fourth and advanced to second on a passed ball. But Palmer got a called third strike on Ethan Royer to strand Grow. St. Michaels stranded seven baserunners, six in scoring position.
"He hasn't had a bad game," Fitzgerald said of Palmer. "We've put him up against all the big teams we got to go up against and we're proud the way he's handled himself all year. This wasn't surprising. Every game he's always performed like he did today. Just a stud for us. Proved it again today. Wish we could have gotten a couple more hits for him here and there and the game might have turned out different. But he did everything we asked of him today."
Palmer struck out Grow to open the sixth before reaching his pitch limit and being relieved by Brown, who struck out both batters he faced.
Queen Anne's stranded six, two in scoring position.

title: Lions closer to finish line
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions closer to finish line

 April 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 590
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — One word has been on the collective minds of Queen Anne's County High's softball team all season. Finish."Our motto has been finish all year long," Lions head coach Aaron Stewart said. "We didn't finish last year. Coming into the season this year, one of my coaches just came up to me and said, 'You know the word of the year has to be finish.' And we're finishing right now."
Queen Anne's took a big step in putting itself in a position to finish atop the North Bayside Tuesday afternoon, using a nine-hit attack to back the pitching of Emily Hirschbock in a 6-1 victory over defending division champion North Dorchester.
The Lions (12-1 overall) moved into first place in the North at 4-1 and now hold the tiebreaker over the Eagles (11-2, 4-1) after beating them in their only head-to-head meeting of the season. Colonel Richardson (10-4, 4-2), which defeated Kent County by forfeit Tuesday, North Dorchester and Easton (6-4, 4-1) remain in contention but need help to overtake the Lions.
"The bats definitely came back today," said Stewart, who was puzzled after his team was limited to just five hits in last Tuesday's 4-1 loss to Colonel Richardson. "We hit the ball well. Opposite field, which is even better. I like to see opposite-field hitting. We practice that over and over and over again, to take that outside pitch and drive it to right field. And we executed it today."
The Lions did just that in the third inning, breaking a scoreless tie with three consecutive two-out, opposite-field hits for a 3-0 lead.
Morgan Gottleib worked a one-out walk against North Dorchester ace Emilee Cohee (5-2) and was advanced to second on Emily Hirschbock's sacrifice bunt. Cam Jacobi lined a single into right field to score Gottleib. Caroline Taylor (3 for 4) drilled a 1-0 offering into the right field corner for a double. Autumn Huber then drove another Cohee delivery the other way for a two-run triple.
North Dorchester scratched a run across in the top of the fourth. Maggie Hubbard (2 for 3) hit a leadoff single and scored four batters later, when freshman Journey Pearson lined a shot to center that Jacobi just missed making a spectacular leaping catch on for the third out of the inning.
That would be the lone run allowed by Hirschbock (7-0) who finished with a complete-game five-hitter, striking out four and walking four.
"I was just kind of thinking to attack every pitch," said Hirschbock, who retired nine of the last 11 batters she faced. "It's been a big thing for me to attack specifically the first batter. I feel like I did that pretty well tonight. I'm proud of myself for that.
"It's always nice pitching with the lead," Hirschbock said with a big smile. "My hitters hit and it was awesome."
Queen Anne's extended its lead in the fifth. Jacobi reached on a one-out error. Taylor dropped a bunt that Cohee fielded, but had to hold onto with no one covering first. Huber walked to load the bases. Abbie Denes singled to left field to plate Jacobi for a 4-1 lead. Cohee notched her seventh and final strikeout before Emily Rendulic singled to score Taylor and Huber for a 6-1 cushion.
"Tough day," North Dorchester head coach Carol Hubbard said. "They out-hit us. We had a few unfortunate things on the base paths. Not making excuses. They made the plays they had to make."
Maddie Nagel relieved Cohee, got an inning-ending strikeout, then held the Lions scoreless in the sixth despite yielding singles to Jacobi and Taylor.

title: La Plata man selected as judge for Westminster dog show
author: Matt Wynn mwynn@somdnews.com
content:
La Plata man selected as judge for Westminster dog show

 April 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Matt Wynn mwynn@somdnews.com | Section: State News 
 
 484
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Westminster Kennel Club has selected a La Plata man as a judge for the 148th annual Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show."I've always had dogs. They developed into a huge part of my life and became a major hobby for me," Richard Todd Jackson, 54, told Southern Maryland News. "Everything kind of exploded while I was in college."
Jackson, like many freshmen, said he hated living in dorms and moved off-campus. His parents told him he would have to pay half the rent, so he found a job as a kennel assistant.
His work at the Tsang-Po Kennels kindled his lifelong passion for chow chows, leading him to achieve over 50 championships and grand championships.
"I've had chow chows ever since," Jackson said. "I left to go off to college with no dogs, and I came home with six dogs."
As he was from Miami, he had to make special accommodations so his chow chows, which are an arctic dog, would be comfortable in the climate. He formed a makeshift kennel on his air-conditioned patio to keep his dogs cool in the long, hot Florida summers.
"I started judging my own breed, which is chow chows, and I've had quite a bit of success. I still show my dogs," Jackson said. "I don't get a chance to do it as much as I would like to because of avoiding conflicts of interest as a judge."
Jackson said his claim to fame came from his smooth-coated chow chows, which have a rougher, shorter, more bristly coat.
The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show invited Jackson nearly a year and a half ago to serve on the panel, but he was sworn to secrecy until they made their announcement.
He is among 43 other judges for this year's show, being selected out of what he estimates to be at least 2,000 others.
He is listed on the Westminster Kennel Club's website as a toy breed judge for this year, examining affenpinschers, Biewer terriers and papillons.
"It's an honor to be invited to judge at what is one of the most revered dog shows in the world. The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show is second only to the Kentucky Derby as one of the oldest sporting events in the United States," Jackson said, reflecting on his appointment. "Being chosen to judge is a dream to which most dog show judges aspire. To do so as one of the few people of color ever to attain this role adds a profound sense of responsibility, pride, and history."
The show will return for the second year to the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows–Corona Park, N.Y., on May 11, 13 and 14.
Beyond his contributions to the dog sport, according to a release from the Westminster Kennel Club, Jackson has been involved in real estate development and asset management, focusing on providing affordable housing to seniors and military families in the Mid-Atlantic region for over 25 years.

title: RIGHT IN THE MIX
author: Bill Haufe
content:
RIGHT IN THE MIX

 April 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 925
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The North Bayside softball championship.Defending division and Class 1A state champion North Dorchester was certainly cast among the favorites at the beginning of this season. Queen Anne's County and Colonel Richardson also figured to be right at the top.
Easton?
After a 1-3 start, some may have brushed the Warriors to the side, thinking this was a season of rebuilding, or at least readjusting under first-year head coach Ryan Brice. Well, Brice's bunch showed again Thursday afternoon they have adjusted just fine, notching their seventh win in eight games via a 10-0 five-inning shutout of Cambridge-South Dorchester.
Easton (8-4 overall) improved to 5-1 in the North, tied with Queen Anne's (13-1, 5-1) and North Dorchester (12-2, 5-1) — though the Eagles hold the tiebreaker over the Warriors, having won the only meeting between the two teams. Queen Anne's plays Easton on Tuesday.
"We're on a roll," Brice said. "Hopefully we can keep this going until next week because we have three straight (Queen Anne's, James M. Bennett, North Caroline), Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday."
Brice is also hoping Sammy Townsend can keep it going. With Lyle Roe not pitching this week due to an injury, Townsend (7-2) started all three games in the circle for the Warriors. The sophomore punctuated her week by throwing Easton's first shutout of the season, a three-hit gem that including 11 strikeouts — eight swinging — and no walks.
"Sammy did an amazing job, not only today, but the past three games that we had," Brice said. "Three-and-oh. She pitched amazing today with a shutout. I can't say enough about her. She's one of the best pitchers I've ever had the pleasure of coaching."
Townsend gave up a game-opening single to Enazajah Young, who raced to second when the ball bounced and hit center fielder Leigha Bosley in the throat. Townsend promptly struck out the next three, leaving Young, who stole third, stranded at third.
Camryn Russum singled sharply to left field with one out in the second, but was thrown out stealing by Warrior catcher Laillah Janes. Townsend fanned Evelyn Windsor to end the inning.
"I felt like my spins were really tight today, and the past couple of games," Townsend said. "I felt like this week I've pitched the best that I've pitched all season."
Townsend set the Vikings (6-7, 1-5) down in order in the third before Laila Insley reached with a bunt single down the third-base line to open the fourth. Townsend got Emma Robinson to pop out to short, watched Lainey Jones move Insley to second with a sacrifice bunt before striking out M'Kya Molock to end the frame.
The right-hander fanned the first two batters she faced in the fifth before Keyth Rodriguez smacked a comebacker off Townsend's glove. But Townsend finished the mercy-shortened game with her fourth inning-ending strikeout of the game.
"I knew my defense had me," Townsend said. "I feel like we have a set infield and outfield now, because I know in the beginning of the year we were all wishy-washy with who we were going to put where."
The Warriors took a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first, when Mayah Wilkins (2 for 3) reached on an infield hit, dashed to third on a two-base throwing error on the play, and scored on a wild pitch.
Back-to-back, bases-loaded walks with two outs in the second extended that lead to 3-0.
Easton widened its advantage to 5-0 in the third. Townsend (2 for 3, two RBIs) roped a leadoff double into the left-field corner and scored on an error. Two batters later, Brynlee Buchkoski laced a triple to right that plated Janes. Buchkoski tried to score on a passed ball, but Viking catcher Lainey Jones threw to pitcher Robinson, who tagged out Buchkoski for the inning's final out.
The Warriors' lead ballooned to 10-0 in the fourth. After Bosley reached on an error, Wilkins doubled to left. Three batters later, Townsend lined a two-out, two-run single to right for a 7-0 lead. Janes and Gemma Vogel (2 for 3) followed with consecutive RBI singles. Robinson was relieved by Windsor, who gave up a bases-loaded walk to Isabelle Ludwig before getting two fly-ball outs to end the game.

title: Lions move closer to first North Bayside title in program history
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions move closer to first North Bayside title in program history

 April 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1285
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — The walls of Queen Anne's County High's gymnasium are plastered with banners celebrating past champions in just about every sport.But with the exception of the banner commemorating head coach Dee Fisher's 200th career victory last year, girls tennis is not represented on the gym walls.
"Girls tennis doesn't have anything," said Lucy Taylor, Queen Anne's No. 1 singles player. "Sometimes those posters are kind of behind (in being updated). And we joke that it's like a forgotten sport. But we're out here showing we can win stuff too."
The Lions have shown they can win quite often this year.
It started in the season-opener, when Queen Anne's ended Kent Island's impressive 102-match win streak against Bayside Conference competition. The Lions defeated the six-time defending Bayside champions again Friday by a 7-0 count, this one moving them within a victory of their first North Bayside title in school history.
"At the beginning of the season we had like an inter-squad scrimmage and that was like the best thing ever," Fisher said after his team improved to 11-1 overall, 9-0 North. "Because when I matched them up they were just pushing each other."
What has also helped is having players who have won conference or division titles in other sports this school year.
"I have volleyball players who had a great (Bayside title) team," Fisher said. "Basketball players who had a great (North Bayside title) team. Field hockey players that had a great (Bayside championship) team. Soccer (which won the North Bayside). So I have a team of winners basically. They win at every sport they play. So it kind of trickled over to tennis."
But Fisher admitted he did not see this coming after graduating nine seniors last year, most of which made up his starting lineup.
"We had a full team of juniors and sophomores," Fisher said. "So this was going to be my get-them-used-to-playing year. Next year would be the year.
"A lot of the players hadn't played doubles and singles," Fisher said of his team. "So this was a chance to get their feet wet. But our program has a lot of girls, so I always try to build that up through exhibition. I'm always encouraging exhibition matches, lot of practice, and just having fun."
In the process, Fisher's get-them-used-to-playing year has turned into the get-them-used-to-winning year."
Queen Anne's got an early start on that Friday, sweeping doubles play for a 3-0 lead. Lucy Taylor and sister Meg Taylor, who have lost only once this season, defeated Jamie Tranquill and Isabelle Gamez, 8-2 at No. 1. The No. 2 tandem of Hayden Legg and Marylee Kline put together a similar 8-2 result over Gianna Tamburo and Taylor Harding. Sydney Pinder and Kara Ringold completed the sweep with an 8-4 win over Grace Turner and Jasleen Paquer.
"Last year we lost, what, nine seniors?" Lucy Taylor asked. "Most of which were in the lineup. This year, Hayden and Marylee have both come so far, and they have been able to pick up big wins for us. The same with Sydney and Kara. I think it's just like, keep building on those skills we learned freshman year. It's just amazing how much everyone has grown."
Queen Anne's lead continued to grow through singles play.
Meg Taylor defeated Gamez, 8-4, at No. 2. Legg was an 8-4 winner over Tamburo, and Kline earned an 8-2 win over Harding.
In the marathon match of the afternoon, Lucy Taylor, who lost both her singles matches earlier in the week, fell behind 3-0 to Tranquill. This wasn't exactly anything new for the Lions' No. 1, who rallied from a 4-0 deficit to win when her and Tranquill met in the season-opener.
"I was just thinking, 'I've done this before. I can get it back,'" Lucy Taylor said. "I used the same mentality I did last time which is just like, one point at a time, one game at a time. And then I was able to build off of that."
Taylor rallied to take an 8-7 lead, but Tranquill showed she too could battle back, pulling even at 8-8 to force a tiebreaker.
"This time was a little harder because we went back and forth so many times," said Taylor, who won the tiebreaker 9-7. "This one really felt good."
A win over visiting Easton on Tuesday or against Cambridge-South Dorchester on Wednesday clinches the division title for Queen Anne's.
Do the Lions feel any pressure one victory shy of history?
"I think they don't think about it," Fisher said smiling. "I think they just go out and just play hard and have fun. No. We really don't talk about it.
"This is our throw-away year," Fisher said, referring back to this being a season of preparation for next year. "I don't know how to explain it. We just go with the flow."
Primarily an exhibition player, junior captain Sydnee Carr said it's been a joy to be on the ride toward a potential first division title.
"It's hard for me to speak on it because I'm typically an exhibition player," said Carr, who has won all her doubles matches when Fisher has inserted into the starting lineup. "But it has been fun to watch everybody improve. Definitely Hayden and Lucy and Marylee. Just seeing them come out the past two years and improve in so many ways, and then be able to be in the starting lineup and excel is really fun to watch.
"Being on the field hockey team and being on the swim team, our teams have a lot of banners," Carr continued. "So it will be fun to see my third sport be represented up on the wall."
GIRLS LACROSSE
SSPP 21, SALISBURY SCHOOL 3
SALISBURY — Sophomore Caroline Ewing scored five goals and set up another, and senior Morgan Quade distributed nine assists and scored twice Friday, as Saints Peter and Paul won its 10th straight.
Eden Zimmerman had four goals and Kendall Kroniser (assist), Avery McCall (two assists) and Eryn Callahan (assist) each recorded hat tricks for the Sabres (10-1, 6-0 Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference). Kate Sweeney (goal) and Emery Zimmerman had two assists apiece.
NORTH CAROLINE 18, CAMBRIDGE-SD 2
CAMBRIDGE — Calleigh Tribbett and Ashlynn Bisesi (assist) each notched hat tricks Friday to pace the Bulldogs to their second straight victory.
Riley Walstrum (two assists), Ashley Kercheval (three assists), Maddie Mcninch, Reece Bisesi and Mia Schreyer had two goals apiece for North Caroline (7-3), and Claire Blue and Gracie Faulkner had one each.
SOFTBALL
QUEEN ANNE'S 6, KENT ISLAND 1
CENTREVILLE — Hannah Martin pitched a complete-game three-hitter Thursday, striking out 12 and walking just one as the Lions remained atop the North Bayside with North Dorchester and Easton.
Autumn Huber had one hit and three RBIs for Queen Anne's (13-1, 5-1) and Morgan Gottleib, Caroline Taylor, Camaryn Jacobi, Emily Rendulic and Reese Brooks each had one hit.
Bri Kurtz, Abbie Mahaffey (RBI) and Sena Koch had one hit apiece for Kent Island
ST. MICHAELS 22, KENT COUNTY 6
ST. MICHAELS — Madi White was 3 for 3 with a double, three RBIs and three runs, and Myla Ramey was 3 for 4 with three runs Thursday as the Saints (6-9, 2-5) ended a three-game skid.
Mercy Haddaway earned the win, striking out three and walking five.
St. Michaels' Brooke Reilly was 2 for 4 with three runs scored, Lily Haddaway was 2 for 3, scoring two runs, Brianna Crow went 2 for 4 with three runs scored, Lola Browning was 3 for 5 with two RBIs, and Katie Jenkins was 2 for 5 with a triple and a run scored.
BASEBALL
QUEEN ANNE'S 4, KENT ISLAND 3
CENTREVILLE — Evan Dickey was 4 for 4 with two RBIs, and Dalton Brown went 1 for 2, knocking in two runs as the Lions outlasted their county rival in nine innings.
Brown earned the win, going 3 2/3 innings. Dickey pitched 5 1/3 innings.

title: Franklin gets call from Ravens
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Franklin gets call from Ravens

 April 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 768
 Words 

 Read News Document

 For three days, Ja'Mion Franklin waited for his name to be called during the NFL draft.It never was.
But Franklin kept coming back to something his Aunt Ty Bolden, told him during a pre-draft party.
"She was like, 'It doesn't matter when the phone rings, as long as it rings,'" Franklin said. "Low and behold, I got a ring. Literally as soon as the draft ended I got a call."
That call Saturday was from Franklin's agent, John Apple, who told the 2018 North Caroline High graduate, the Baltimore Ravens were going to give him a chance as an undrafted free agent.
"I was shocked," Franklin said of his selection during a phone interview Monday afternoon. "It's crazy. You can't write a better story. To go through all I've been through, and then to finally get an opportunity to not only chase my dream as being an NFL player, but to do it at home, for the home team that I always rooted for. I was ecstatic. He (Apple) said, 'I know this has been a stressful day but we're going to send you to Baltimore.' And I was like, 'I'm ready. Let's do it.'"
A 6-foot-1, 313-pound defensive tackle/nose guard who graduated from Duke University last May, the 24-year-old Franklin reports to the Ravens' training facility in Owings Mills this Thursday to begin a four-day mini-camp. He will be given a physical, sign his contract, and begin meetings and learning the playbook.
"I'm excited," said Franklin, a Ridgely native. "I'm obviously anxious but this entire process has been stressful, and not really a lot of football. But now I get to do what I love to do."
Franklin played three years at Notre Dame before transferring to Duke in December 2020. He made 16 tackles his first season in Durham, and improved those numbers the following year, logging 26 tackles, including three sacks. He was a captain this past season, totaling 31 tackles and a sack for the Blue Devils, who capped an 8-5 season with a 17-10 victory over Troy in the Birmingham Bowl.
It was over the past two seasons Franklin began adding fuel to his hopes of someday playing in the NFL.
"I always had the aspirations of playing in the league," Franklin said. "But the last two years at Duke really showed me I could do it. It was attainable. Starting every game the last two seasons and producing the way that I did, and being around the people I was around. I just took it and ran with it, and here we are."
Two people who further stoked that dream were Franklin's strength coach, David Feeley, and former Duke defensive tackle coach Jess Simpson, who coached previously in the NFL, and is now an assistant at Georgia Tech.
"Those are the two guys that told me really this is possible," Franklin said of Feeley and Simpson, "to keep doing the things that I was doing, and everything will take care of itself. And that's what I was doing.
"He was like, 'I've coached guys just like you in the league so I think you should pursue it,'" Franklin said of Simpson. "I just started thinking about it a lot more serious. Being a captain this past season got me a lot more attention. And being a leader and being up for the national awards for community service. Just getting my name out there in positive ways as much as I can."
Franklin, who has been training at Grosetti Performance in New Castle, Pennsylvania outside Pittsburgh prior to the draft, did not attend this year's NFL combine, but thought he impressed during Duke's Pro Day on March 28.
"I knew I was going to get an opportunity," said Franklin, who spoke with scouts from Baltimore, Houston, Miami, Minnesota, Denver and Chicago. "There's been too much invested, and I absolutely killed my pro day. I walked away confident. And I walked away knowing somebody was going to give me an opportunity to do what I do."
Franklin thought he might hear his named called during Saturday's fifth or sixth round, but it didn't happen.
"There was definitely the possibility," Franklin said of being drafted. "I think it just shook out different because the way the draft started. A lot of the guys that were ranked ahead of me went a lot later than they were supposed to.
"I knew that there was a chance, but it was definitely nerve wracking, man," Franklin added. "It's a stressful situation. Putting in all the work and controlling all you can control is all you can do. But it's all good. And you know the Baltimore Ravens took a chance on a hometown kid."
