title: TOUGH ACT TO FOLLOW
author: Bill Haufe
content:
TOUGH ACT TO FOLLOW

 August 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1769
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Queen Anne's County High head field hockey coach Shana Corder already knows there will be no topping last year's near perfect run.All the Lions did in 2023 was win their first Bayside Conference championship in school history, and notch a program record 14 shutouts while yielding just two goals during a magical 15-1 season that ended with a 1-0 loss to Hereford in the Class 2A state semifinals.
"No topping that," Corder said. "The numbers were amazing."
And though Queen Anne's may not be as strong after graduating its entire starting defense from a year ago with the exception of goalie Cassidy Alexander, the Lions aren't likely ready to fall off the map.
"New team, new dream," Corder said. "They know we lost our entire defense, so it's the next man up; fighting for your spots. It's pretty much what we've been telling them. 'Be ready to be a team player. And this might have been your position last year but we need help in this position and you're good here and you're going to go there.'"
Kent Island again looks to be in a position to challenge for its 11th North Bayside title in 14 seasons — excluding the COVID-canceled 2020 championship game.
"It's the most balanced team I've had in my four years as head coach," Kent Island's Laura Harding said.
And should the Bucs stumble, Easton may be in line for its first division crown since 2010.
"This is probably the most athletic group of girls I've had the pleasure of coaching as a whole," Warrior head coach Kim Neff said.
While Kent Island, Easton and Queen Anne's figure to duke it out for top billing in the North Bayside, Debbie McQuaid will look to steer Saints Peter and Paul to a fourth Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference championship in five years.
"I'm excited about the energy that the younger kids are bringing," said McQuaid, whose chief conference rival could again be Gunston, which has reached the ESIAC final the past two years. "We've got some versatility so we'll be able to switch lines. That makes the coach happy."
Here's a look at this year's Mid-Shore teams.
EASTON
Head Coach: Kim Neff.
Who's Where: Goalie: Alli Newman (Sr.); Taylor Bowen (Fr.); Defense: Lea Boutte (Sr.); Kadence McGuckin (Jr.); Sammy Townsend (Jr.); Macy Graves (Fr.); Alden Gibbons-Neff (Fr.); Adeline Moore (So.); Midfield: Bis Johnson (Jr.); Myka Motovidlak (Sr.); Addison Knox (So.); Hannah Dahlen (So.); Stella Kabler (Jr.); Forwards: Maedy Leitzer (Sr.); Olivia Orrell (Sr.); Georgia Spies (So.); Ryann Quicke (So.); McKenna Clow (So.); Sutherland Chandler (Fr.).
Outlook: Neff would like to avoid a repeat of a year ago, when the Warriors opened with four consecutive overtime games. She also hopes to find replacements for graduated all-North Bayside first-team picks Emily Branic, Sydney Johnson and Jordan Reagan, but has been encouraged by what she's seen this preseason, which included a play-day win over perennial 1A power Pocomoke.
"This is not a rebuild," said Neff, who returns first-team picks Orrell and McGuckin. "They're just very fast, and they have really good foundational skills. I have high expectations for them, and a lot of them have played together because of travel ball. They really are a cohesive group. We're kind of moving forward from where we left off last year."
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Suzie Wright-Taylor.
Who's Where: Goalie: Abigail Strayer (Fr.); Defense: Taylor Strong (So.); Hailey Myers (Jr.); Tess Fuchs (Jr.); Midfield: Abby Gallo (Fr.); Liza Loller (So.); Mali Wirth (Fr.); Forwards: Kate Cannon (Sr.); Grace Gerstung (Jr.); Clare Gerstung (Fr.); McKenna Messik (Jr.); Amaya Spicer (Sr.); Nevaeh Blackiston (Fr.); Mackenzie Walker (Fr.).
Outlook: The Trojans were winless a year ago with one of the smallest teams Wright-Taylor has ever had under her direction, but there have been positive signs this preseason.
"The freshmen that have come in have played rec," said Wright-Taylor, who has often watched players coming through the county's youth program go to other schools. "They have some experience at least, so we're not starting totally from ground zero.
"For the most part that group played together at rec with that goalie," Wright-Taylor said of her six freshmen, which are led by Gallo.
Bolstering hopes are the return of Cannon, Fuchs, Strong, Loller, Grace Gerstung and Messik. And there was Thursday's scrimmage against Bohemia Manor and North East.
"We scored more goals today than we did all last season," Wright-Taylor said.
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Laura Harding.
Who's Where: Goalie: Brynja Petursson (So.); Parissa Butler (Jr.); Defense: Sydney Riska (Sr.); Emma Wackowski (Jr.); Laura Peck (Jr.); Kai Moore (So.); Emma Fleshman (Sr.); Makenzie Guidry (Sr.); Midfield: Ella Napier (Jr.); Lilly Snyder (So.); Rita Yost (Jr.); Sadie Latchaw (Sr.); Sydney Cox (Sr.); Lyla Baily (Jr.); Caelan Green (Jr.); Elizabeth Talbott (Sr.); Forwards: Ellie Burnside (Sr.); Audrey Fleshman (So.); Caroline Levin (Sr.); Willow Yost (Jr.); Parker Tengwall (So.); Anna Fronczek (Jr.); Madison Jordan (Sr.).
Outlook: The Bucs went 8-6 a year ago, which included three straight one-goal losses to open the season and another against Queen Anne's in the 2A East Regional playoffs that ended it.
But Harding is excited by what she has seen this preseason.
"I don't have like a Megan Carpenter," Harding said of her former standout now playing at the University of Massachusetts. "I just have a full squad of girls that play field hockey year round. It's fun to watch."
The return of Riska, who did not play last year, strengthens the defense, while Burnside and the Yosts — all first-team North Bayside picks — provide a solid foundation which could be set for a series of title challenges.
"Talent across the board," Harding said. "I think we have a lot of depth. The kids coming off the bench are almost as strong as the kids starting on the field."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: Molly Elliott.
Who's Where: Goalie: Selena Lopez (Jr.); Alyssa Hand (Fr.); Defense: Brooklyn Spencer (Jr.); Abby Jones (Jr.); Emily Kimble (Sr.); Midfield: Morgan Knott (Sr.); Kylie Ogden (Jr.); Ashlynn Bisesi (So.); Reece Bisesi (Jr.); Forwards: Gracie Faulkner (Jr.); Jamie Robey (Fr.); Julia White (Fr.); Reagan Rizer (Jr.).
Outlook: After five years as Easton's junior varsity head coach, Elliott begins her third year with the Bulldogs, the last two as head coach.
And though North Caroline doesn't figure to challenge for a division title, Elliott has three players with club experience, including Knott, who has verbally committed to play at Central Michigan.
"We have a lot more experience on the field than we have had in seasons past," Elliott said. "We've been plagued the last few seasons by some major injuries So having Morgan and Ashlynn and Reece on the field at the same time isn't something we've been able to do in seasons past, and so I'm very excited that we have a very healthy starting midfield line.
QUEEN ANNE'S
Head Coach: Shana Corder.
Who's Where: Goalie: Cassidy Alexander (Sr.); Caroline Kimball (Jr.); Defense: Melanie Gill (Fr.); Midfield: Ava Fields (Sr.); Ellee McLean (Sr.); Haley Cole (Jr.); Jordan Bilbo (Jr.); Taylor Brown (So.); Ella Rebstock (So.); Forwards: Aly Edwards (Sr.); Jolie Leager (Sr.); Jamie Baldwin (Sr.).
Outlook: Like a number of coaches, Corder will shift players between lines, especially at midfield and forward.
But whereas the defense was last year's anchor, this season it will be the offense that needs to shoulder the load
"My defense carried us last year," said Corder, whose team didn't yield a goal until the final regular-season game against Stephen Decatur. "This year my message is offense needs to do the same until they can figure out their way and our strategy on defense."
While Corder is mixing a new lineup to replace first-team all-North defenders Abbie Denes — now at St. Mary's — Julia Reburn and Molly Holthaus, and well as North Bayside player of the year Faith Novak and first-team forward Gabrielle Scully, there is talent up front.
Corder said she will lean on Cole, who is headed to James Madison at the midfield. Bilbo, who had a knack for big goals a year ago, is also back. Fields and McLean have started four years, giving Queen Anne's one of the strongest midfields in the Bayside.
"It's going to be a different year this year for Queen Anne's field hockey," Corder said. "We're going to rebuild, but it's totally fine."
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: Karen Hopkins.
Who's Where: Goalie: Olivia Patrick (Jr.); Defense: Brynn Lizewski (Sr.); Phoebe Cole (Sr.); Regan Wibberley (Jr.); Rebeca Martinez (Jr.); Midfield: Jordyn Beckett (So.); Stella Wibberley (Fr.); Kim Montoya-Guzman (Fr.); Midfield: Molly Genrich (Sr.); Maddie Dunker (Sr.); Tess Weller (Jr.); Forwards: Karina Mazur (Sr.); Abbie Fisher (So.); Ella Marr (Fr.); Penny Turner (Fr.); Zoe Cerrato (Fr.); Kayla Montoya-Guzman (Jr.).
Outlook: Returning first-team midfielders Dunker and Genrich, and forward Mazur give the Saints a nice base to work off. The defense returns plenty of experience, and generating more offense will be among the top priorities.
"The leadership we have through our five seniors is very apparent," Hopkins said. "They've been helping the younger girls as well as leveling up their play. We have such positive energy on the field. We're striving for the intensity. We are striving for better plays and more strategy and more consistency."
SAINTS PETER & PAUL
Head Coach: Debbie McQuaid.
Who's Where: Goalie: Pyper Mister (Fr.); Rynn Morgan (So.); Defense: Kat Murphy (Sr.); Reagan Wolters (Fr.); McKenzie Foster (So.); Lucy Rankin (Jr.); Midfield: Claire Beiber (Sr.); Sadie Jacobs (Fr.); Angie Webb (So.); Forwards: Jules Stepp (Jr.); CC O'Connor (Sr.).
Outlook: The Sabres lost a number of key players from last year's 14-2 title-winning team, including ESIAC player of the year Gennie Webb — now at Virginia Commonwealth — Morgan Quade, Emmary Sweeney, Cadence Kelley and Schuyler Gary.
The cupboard is hardly bare though.
Angie Webb returns at the midfield and is joined by St. Michaels transfer Beiber, who is headed to VCU. The front line also looks strong with Stepp and O'Connor returning.
"I usually get some really good athletes, but they're not always field hockey players," McQuaid said. "This year I've got a good bunch of athletes who are actually field hockey players."
GUNSTON
Head Coach: Yvonne Gazelle.
Who's Where: Goalie: Lorelei DeGour (Fr.); Defense: Izzy Labrador (Fr.); Victoria MacGlashan (Sr.); Lila McDermott (Fr.); Midfield: Layla Kent (Jr.); Genevieve Baughman (Jr.); Camilla Nonemaker (So.); Forwards: Grace Shepherd (Sr.); Gabi Shepherd (So.); Kate Zottarelli (So.); Tori Nessly (Sr.).
Outlook: Sophia Kent, a four-year fixture in goal, has graduated and is now at St. Mary's. The Herons have made it to the ESIAC championship the past two years, but Gazelle thinks it will be a year of trying to find the right combinations in hopes of making a third straight conference final.
"It's going to be a building year," Gazelle said. "We're all pretty new. We have some brand new ones to the sport, but there's a lot of promise."
Layla Kent provides a building block at midfield, while Grace Shepherd figures to be a force up front.

title: ON THE REBOUND
author: Bill Haufe
content:
ON THE REBOUND

 September 3, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 834
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — If.That's how Matt Griffith started his preseason commentary entering his 10th year as Easton High's head football coach.
Griffith's first word is certainly understandable considering starting quarterback Mikey O'Connor suffered a season-ending injury in Week 2 of last year, which played a huge role in the Warriors going 1-8.
"If we can healthy, 'cause we got low numbers, and continue to improve we should be able to put a good product out on the field," said Griffith, who also lost his starting quarterback, Mason Ledford, in Week 2 of the 2017 season.
A 6-foot-3, 195-pound senior, the left-handed throwing O'Connor returns as the starter behind center, and is backed by 6-3, 220-pound sophomore Brady Walls, a transfer from St. Mary's.
"Mikey looks really good," said Griffith, of the third O'Connor brother to start at quarterback for the Warriors. "The transfer kid (Walls) is pretty good, too."
Easton's backfield not only looks pretty good, but appears plenty deep. Junior Dustin Blue (5-11, 212) and sophomore Jordan Horsey form a nice, physical one-two punch. Freshman Jamier Copper (5-9, 195), juniors JaSere Molina (5-7, 160) and Tayshaun Roberts (5-8, 180), and senior Najhay Smith (5-9, 175) are also expected to get rotated into the ground game.
"Really deep at running back," Griffith said. "We've got five kids that I think we can hand the ball off to and we're not missing much of anything. The first two are bruisers with Dustin and Jordan. They're a load to tackle. And JaSere gives us a nice change of pace with a different type speed. He's pretty quick."
Quickness is also found in a receiving corps that welcomes the return of senior standout Chase Raab (5-11, 180), who never got on the field a year ago after an injury in 7-on-7 summer play wiped out his entire season.
"That's a big, big lift for us, getting him back," Griffith said of Raab. "And he's 100 percent, which is good."
The rest of the receiving cast doesn't look too shabby either, with junior wideouts Carter Mooney (5-11, 180) and Logan Friend (5-10, 160), and seniors Jaden Prestwood (6-3, 215) and Finn Gunshenan (5-10, 170). The Warriors' biggest threats though may be at slot. Senior Colin Mooney (5-7, 170) returns and is joined by juniors Diontaye Copper (5-10, 185), Kyree Acree (5-11, 175) and Zach Barnhart (5-8, 180).
"We have a good core that we can cycle through and get breaks on offense, and not have any drop-offs because some of these guys are going to be playing on the defensive side of the ball as well," Griffith said. "It's going to be nice to be able to go, 'Kyree you're going in for Diontaye, and Zach,' and vice versa to be able to get them some breaks."
Easton lost four starters from the offensive line, with junior right tackle Tymiere Thomas (5-10, 240) the lone returner. But Griffith has liked his young group's development and praised the work of assistants Drew Griffith — his son — and Dave Perillo, the longtime line coach at Queen Anne's County.
Junior Trushun Truxon Jr. (5-11, 190) starts at center, with freshman guard Brady Gilliece (6-3, 225) and sophomore tackle Xavier Stowers (6-3, 230) lining up on his left, and junior guard Jack Chapple (6-4, 220) joining Thomas on the right side. Senior Nathaniel Lapp (6-7, 225) and juniors Paul Whitlock (5-10, 210) and Tracey Gore (6-0, 285) could also be moved in and out of the lineup.
"Young. Inexperienced. But a very good work in progress," Griffith said of his offensive front. "They're improving every day. It's good sized and most of those kids spent time in the weight room."
The defense has many of the same faces, with a few different ones sprinkled through.
Sophomore Elias Leonard (5-10, 305) is at nose guard, where Groce and Truxon could also get time. Thomas is back at one tackle and has looked great in the preseason, according to his head coach. Teaming with him up front will be a rotation of Stowers, Lapp, Gilliece, Whitlock and Chapple.
Inside linebacker should be a strength, with Blue and Horsey starting, and Copper, Gunshenan and junior Alex Rhodes (5-10, 180) in reserve. Prestwood and Roberts start outside, but Griffith noted sophomores Nevin Whitaker (5-9, 190) and Teddy Antal (6-0, 175) could see time.
The secondary is athletic and fast, with Acree, Copper, Friend, Molina and Carter Mooney at the corners. Raab starts at free safety, while Colin Mooney and Barnhart are at strong safety.
"They're learning the new system under coach (Al) Waters," Griffith said of his new defensive coordinator, who has coached at Queen Anne's and Cambridge-South Dorchester. "They're enjoying it. It's not a lot different from what we're used to. We're starting to do less thinking and play a little faster."
Senior Dominic Stanco, who also plays soccer, handles the place-kicking chores. Horsey and Walls will punt.
"Very excited to see how they continue to improve," Griffith said of his team.
Easton opens Friday when its hosts North East of Cecil County, coached by Warrior alum Taylor Slaughenhoupt. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m.

title: 6th annual Casey Cares Foundation clay tournament to benefit ill children
author: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com
content:
6th annual Casey Cares Foundation clay tournament to benefit ill children

 September 3, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com | Section: News 
 
 349
 Words 

 Read News Document

 QUEENSTOWN — The Casey Cares Foundation will host its sixth annual Sporting Clay Tournament at the Point at Pintail in Queenstown Sept. 13.All proceeds from the tournament event will benefit programs of the Casey Cares Foundation that provide ongoing support and uplifting activities for critically ill children and their families in eight states and Washington, D.C.
The Point at Pintail is nationally recognized as a premier location for sporting clay tournaments and outings. Novice and experienced shooters alike can appreciate the target presentation and picturesque setting.
According to Dawn Weissman, director of corporate engagement, the annual torment brings in between 30 and 50 participants and raises thousands of dollars for Casey Cares seasonal activities, including pumpkin patch trips, apple picking and Christmas events.
The idea for the fundraiser came about through board member and Director of Ellin & Tucker Steven Manekin, a passionate clay shooter who serves as lead event organizer.
Year after year, the event draws in teams eager to give back to the community in a relaxed atmosphere, particularly as an informal corporate team-building day, Weissman said.
"It's been going strong for all six years we've been doing it," she said, noting even through COVID the outdoor event was met with great success.
Awards are presented at the end of the tournament for the top team, top individual and a "Clay Conservation Award."
"Basically the one with the lowest number of clay shots," she said with a laugh.
Casey Baynes, founder and executive director of Casey Cares, said, "Not once-a-lifetime or once-a-year, Casey Cares knows that the best palliative care comes from continuous, ongoing support. Thanks to fundraisers like this tournament, our sponsors participation and contributions made our event successful which helps provide additional activities for critically ill kids and their families this fall. Our shared commitment to make a positive impact on lives of critically ill children is invaluable."
Ryan Webb, vice president of Delmarva Site Development and tournament participant said, "My company has supported this great event for sick kids for four years. It's a perfect opportunity to get our people out for this cause."
More information and tournament registration is available at caseycares.org.

title: Florida St. drops out of AP Top 25
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Florida St. drops out of AP Top 25

 September 3, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 839
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Florida State fell out of The Associated Press college football poll on Tuesday after starting the season 0-2, becoming just the third team to go from preseason top 10 to unranked in the first regular-season poll since the rankings expanded to 25 in 1989.Georgia remained No. 1, receiving 57 first-place votes after starting the season with a blowout of then-No. 14 Clemson. The Tigers hung on at No. 25, but it was the second straight year they dropped at least 10 spots after losing their season opener.
Ohio State was No. 2 with five first-place votes. No. 3 Texas and No. 4 Alabama each moved up a spot, putting three Southeastern Conference teams in the top four along with Georgia. The last time the SEC did that in a non-pandemic season was Sept. 22, 2019.
No. 5 Notre Dame jumped two spots after opening the season with a victory at then-No. 20 Texas A&M, which fell out of the rankings.
Florida State has been the early season's major disappointment. The defending Atlantic Coast Conference champion lost in Dublin, Ireland, to ACC rival Georgia Tech and then dropped another league game Monday night at home to Boston College.
No other preseason Top 25 team this year lost to an unranked opponent to open the season. Florida State did it twice as a double-digit favorite and did not receive a single vote from the AP poll panel.
The other preseason top-10 teams to fall all the way out of the Top 25 after Week 1 in the past 35 years were Michigan in 2007 after famously losing to Appalachian State as No. 5 and Clemson in 2008. The Tigers were No. 9 but opened with a blowout loss to Alabama and tumbled out of the rankings.
Mississippi remained at No. 6. Oregon slipped four spots to No. 7 after winning a close game with Idaho. Penn State stayed at No. 8. Missouri moved up two spots to No. 9 to give the SEC five teams in the top 10. Michigan dropped one spot to No. 10.
Georgia Tech's 2-0 start has the No. 23 Yellow Jackets ranked for the first time since 2015.
Poll points
Because Florida State started its season a week before most of the country, it moves into an exclusive club of teams that began their seasons 0-2 with each loss coming while ranked in the top 10.
Notre Dame was the last to do it in 2022, when the Fighting Irish began the season No. 5, lost at No. 2 Ohio State in their opener, and then were beaten at home the next week by Marshall while ranked eighth. The Irish went to on finish 9-4.
Ohio State opened the 1986 season ranked ninth and lost back-to-back games to ranked opponents, No. 5 Alabama and No. 17 Washington. The Buckeyes were No. 10 when they played the Huskies. Ohio State finished 10-3.
The 1967 Texas team and TCU from 1952 also started 0-2 while ranked in the top 10 in both games.
Florida State is only the second ranked team to lose twice before the first regular-season poll was released, joining Kentucky in 1951. The Wildcats went from No. 6 to No. 17 while going 1-2 to start the season, losing at No. 11 Texas and at Mississippi.
Florida State gets a weekend off before resuming its schedule with home games against Memphis and new ACC member California before a trip to SMU followed by a home game against Clemson.
"You've got a football team that nobody envisioned ever being where we are and having disappointment, having failure, but I do believe in what this team can do," coach Mike Norvell said after the BC loss. "I believe in what this team can accomplish."
Moving up
The big movers upward in the Top 25 were Miami and Southern California.
The Hurricanes jumped seven spots to No. 12 after routing Florida at The Swamp and have their best ranking since cracking the top 10 late in the 2020 season.
No. 13 USC moved up 10 places after beating LSU with a late touchdown Sunday night in Las Vegas. LSU dropped to No. 18.
The Trojans started last season at No. 6, but ended up unranked after a disappointing 8-5 season with 2022 Heisman Trophy winner Caleb Williams.
In and out
The only other team to move into the rankings this week, along with Georgia Tech, was fellow ACC school Louisville. The Cardinals were among the top unranked voter-getters in the preseason and now sit at No. 22.
Conference call
Despite Florida State and Clemson starting the season 0-3, the ACC has one more team in this week's rankings than it did last time:
SEC — 8 (Nos. 1, 3, 4, 6, 9, 14, 16, 18).
Big Ten — 6 (Nos. 2, 7, 8, 10, 13, 21).
ACC — 5 (Nos. 12, 22, 23, 24, 25).
Big 12 — 5 (Nos. 11, 16, 17, 19, 20).
Independent — 1 (No. 5).
Ranked vs. ranked
No. 3 Texas at No. 10 Michigan. The first regular-season meeting ever is a top-10 matchup at the Big House.
No. 14 Tennessee vs. No. 24 N.C. State in Charlotte, North Carolina. Interesting SEC-ACC ranked matchup.

title: WELL GROUNDED
author: Bill Haufe
content:
WELL GROUNDED

 September 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 866
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — He's been running offenses for 20 years, including the last four seasons at Cambridge-South Dorchester High.But Rob Burnham, who took over as Vikings head coach in July, knows a thing or two about defense.
"For the last 13 years I've just been an offensive guy," said Burnham, who during that span was an assistant to former Vikings head coach Toby Peer, first at South Hagerstown, then at Cambridge-SD. "But I've coached defense previously for a dozen years so it's not new. Just having to oversee everything is a little bit different. But I like doing it."
Burnham has liked what he's seen on both sides of the ball this preseason from a team that returns 18 starters from last year's 9-3 Class 1A East Region championship outfit that reached the state semifinals, where it lost to eventual state champ Fort Hill.
The graduation of Class 1A first-team all-state quarterback Blake LaBelle — now at Frostburg State University — may affect the passing game, but Burnham thinks 6-foot-2, 190-pound senior Anthony Hughes can run the offense just fine.
"We lose the all-state quarterback and that stings a little bit," Burnham said. "But we can find other ways to make up for the great things he did for us, and do the best that we can with the kids that we have and find a way to make them successful.
"We don't have an all-state quarterback this year I don't believe, unless he just cranks it up and starts throwing it a whole lot better," Burnham said of Hughes, who is backed up by freshman Nate Twilley (5-11, 200). "But Anthony's strength is not his arm, it's his legs. He has the ability to throw, but he's a better runner than he is a thrower."
The Vikings could again have one of the Bayside Conference's better running attacks, led by returning starter Sterling Perkins, a 5-8, 180-pound junior, who along with Hughes helped the Vikings reach the Class 1A state basketball championship game back in March. Senior Will Jackson (5-10, 170) and juniors Ra'Qwan Cornish (5-11, 150) and Jayden Hollowel (5-10, 175) all have the potential to bust the big play every time they touch the ball.
"I think our run game is certainly going to drive the bus," Burnham said.
Covering Cambridge-SD's fleet of receivers could drive opposing defensive coordinators crazy. Heading that cast is senior Antonio Blueford (6-4, 190), a four-year starter, and junior Magestic Jones (5-11, 180) a three-year returning starter. They are joined by juniors Tamyron Evans (5-10, 160), TJ Wilson (6-2, 175) and Leonbre Chester (6-1, 180), and senior Kimir Lake (6-0, 160).
"We've got some kids that run fast and jump high," Burnham said. "The plan is to try to find the best things that we can execute and get the ball in our playmakers' hands in space and let them do their thing. We try to maximize their ability."
Senior left guard Omarian Travers (6-4, 255) is the lone returning starter on the offensive line. He starts between freshman center Telorian Williams Jr. (6-4, 265) and sophomore left tackle K'Marion Hall (6-2, 240). The right side of the line has sophomore Jeffrey Sellman (5-11, 240) at guard and junior Russell Johnson (6-2, 200) at tackle. Senior KaMarii Stanley (6-2, 190), who's been on varsity all four years, is at tight end.
"I think we've done well up front blocking," Burnham said. "We've had a tremendous amount of improvement that we've done over the course of the last year or so in offensive line play. Our group of kids that we have are picking up things pretty quickly, and I think we did well with our run game."
Cambridge-SD has done a solid job against the run in preseason, with sophomore JaKuez Sneed (5-9, 210) starting at nose guard flanked by senior tackles Jairyn Lewis (6-2, 195) and Stanley.
The tall, rangy Blueford has the potential to be a wrecking machine at outside linebacker, a unit that includes Hughes, Wilson and Chester. Senior Christen Dockins (5-11, 175), who led the team in tackles a year ago, returns at inside linebacker, teaming with senior Donnell Cephas (5-10, 190), Perkins and Hollowell.
"Defense will be the backbone of our team," Burnham said. "We're pretty stout against the run and we're fast everywhere. I don't want to sound conceited, but we don't have slow kids on defense. Every position is fast."
That's especially true in the secondary where Lake will start at corner with either Jones or Cornish, while Jackson and Evans start as safeties.
"I've been pretty impressed by our ability to tackle," Burnham said. "We've only missed a handful of open-field tackles in our scrimmages but we've had a couple of mishaps in coverage. But it's to be expected when you go out and scrimmage. You try to teach from that stuff. It's a learning experience, and you get better and you don't make that mistake again. If we get good film and we teach from it the scrimmage is successful."
Junior Collin Bair handles the kicking duties.
"I can't wait to get on the field Friday night and see what our kids can do," said Burnham of the Vikings' season opener at North Caroline. "And I think our kids are excited too. That's ultimately the important part."

title: A FINE BLEND
author: Bill Haufe
content:
A FINE BLEND

 September 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 846
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Brian Mooney likes the blend Queen Anne's County High's football team has going this preseason.The Lions' second-year head coach likes how his offensive spread game is mixing with the return of former head coach Donny Graef's double-wing approach.
Mooney likes that his offense returns rock-solid 1,000-plus yard rusher John Connolly and sophomore sensation Ja'Dereon Thompson. He likes how his almost new offensive line is coming together under Graef's tutelage.
Mooney also likes his defensive blend, where he and Graef have been molding ends Amari Baynard and Conlan Nagle, where the electric Thompson and two-time all-Bayside Conference corner Carter Dickey are again roaming the secondary, and where Parker Whiteford — after a year at DeMatha — has returned in an alpha role at inside linebacker.
"It's a work in progress," said Mooney, who went 6-5 a year ago. "We're transitioning."
Perhaps the biggest transition is on offense, where Graef, the school's winningest head coach — compiling a 176-95 record over 25 years — returns as an assistant. Among Graef's duties will be coaching the offensive line, which was the longtime domain of another Lions' coaching great, Dave Perillo, now at Easton.
"We have a brand new line," said Mooney, noting senior Nate Mayoral did get a couple spot starts last season. "He's the only one with varsity starting experience. All those guys are cutting their teeth under coach Graef which is awesome.
Centering that line will be 5-foot-11, 225-pound junior Drew Sutton. Juniors Brian Maleski (5-10, 185) and Mac Windsor (6-foot, 210) line up at guard, though senior Ethan Wheaton (5-10, 195) figures to be worked in. Junior Elijah Goldsborough (6-4, 280) is at right tackle and Mayoral (6-3, 260) is on the left side.
"To learn from a Hall of Famer is an awesome opportunity for those guys," Mooney said of his offensive front which includes senior tight ends Christian St. Germain (5-11, 190) and Whiteford (6-1, 215). "They're really soaking it in. Coach Graef, he has high expectations, and when they don't meet those expectations he holds them to it. It's really cool to watch that blend with the skills we have."
The Lions' skill group looks strong. Junior Lance Arnold (5-10, 180), who started the last six games a year ago, returns at quarterback, with sophomore Carter Hercher (6-0, 190) at backup.
A first-time all-conference pick a year ago, Connolly (6-0, 210), a senior, returns to lead a backfield that includes juniors Dorrin Phillips (5-9, 195) and Dickey (5-8, 155), and sophomore Hunter Kelly (5-9, 170).
"We have some skill guys that are going to make any offensive line look good," Mooney said. "John Connolly, we expect to lean on him very heavily."
But as far as play calling goes, Mooney plans to balance his spread philosophy with Graef's old-school style.
"We're kind of working on doing some things Coach Graef is more familiar with," Mooney said. "Bringing him in as offensive line coach makes sense to go back to doing a lot of the things we were successful doing before. It's been a good blend."
Adding to that blend is a receiving corps that includes juniors Baynard (6-4, 190) and Brooks Blodgett (6-0, 175), and senior Nagle (6-2, 190). But the biggest threat is Thompson.
"Ja'Dereon obviously is a human highlight reel," Mooney said.
Thompson is also a threat to blaze into the end zone every time he handles a kick. Last year as a freshman he averaged 41 yards on kickoff returns, taking three in for touchdowns, and 25 yards on punt returns, which included one touchdown.
"He's a blessing to have," Mooney said of Thompson. "And the way he practice and carries himself. I mean some of the stuff you see. ... I always tell the college coaches I talk to, if you could see his practice tape you'd offer him right now."
The Lions look to have more experience on defense, where Thompson returns at deep safety in a secondary that features Dickey and Kelly at strong safety, Blodgett and junior Wyatt Wilhoit (5-8, 155) at corner, and Hercher, who can be inserted at corner or safety.
Wheaton returns at starting tackle and is joined by Sutton, who had spot starts last year, and Goldsborough, who can give either a break when needed. Bookending that trio are ends Baynard and Nagle.
The biggest boost to the defense though figures to be the return of Whiteford at inside linebacker, where he plays along side senior Frank Constantino (5-9, 210) and Maleski.
"The linebacker core, Parker being an alpha, being that coach on the field, he always has them in the right spots, and he makes up if they mess up," Mooney said. "He's just a downhill dynamo. We're excited about having a kid like that patrolling the middle of our defense."
Nagle will kick and punt, though Mooney said Ethan Kepler, a goalie on the soccer team, could also do some place-kicking throughout the season. The Lions also have Michaels Simmons, who goes from being team manager a year ago, to this year's long snapper on punts and kicks.
"We expect to have some bumps and bruises along the way," Mooney said. "But it's going to be fun to see."

title: PUTTING IT TOGETHER
author: Bill Haufe
content:
PUTTING IT TOGETHER

 September 5, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 873
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Ja'Mion Franklin has graduated from Duke University.Kendron Wayman is one game deep into his senior season at Wake Forest. And Nasai Bell is on West Virginia University's roster at safety.
Zymear Smith appears to be the next football standout from North Caroline High headed for the Division I ranks, having verbally committed to the University of Maryland.
And while the talented 6-foot, 175-pound senior halfback figures to draw plenty of attention this season from opponents, Smith knows he's just one part of the Bulldogs' offense and its all-senior backfield.
"He's a solid team player for us," North Caroline second-year head coach Nic McMorris said of Smith, who was the team's third leading rusher a year ago on the way to earning first-team all-Bayside Conference honors. "He wants everybody to kind of lift their game, himself included. He doesn't think he's above the program or anything like that. He's taking a lot of pride this season, especially in his blocking. He's a solid leader for us."
He's also part of what again should be one of the Bayside Conference's more solid backfields with the return of fellow seniors Tyson Weber and Justice Hall.
"Tyson is a very hard-nosed runner," McMorris said of the 5-10, 180-pound halfback. "And honestly, he has the ability to be our top receiver. It's saying a lot, but he runs a very good route, and he's got 10½-inch hands. His agility is through the roof, and he's a hard enough runner who prides himself in running between the tackles."
Then there's the 6-foot, 205-pound Hall, who can fill the role of battering ram quite nicely.
"Justice is a very hard-nosed runner that I'm looking to lean on a lot," McMorris said. "There's not a lot that's flashy, but he kind of prides himself on being a throwback football player. Exactly how the fullback should be."
Add to that mix Bell's successor at quarterback, senior Corey Bunce (6-foot, 170), who also hopes to show his running abilities when given the opportunity.
"We're putting it together," said McMorris, who will have junior Owen Walstrum (5-11, 165) backing up Bunce, and senior Tannor Wood (5-9 140) and junior Darrian Somerville (5-7, 140) coming in to give the starters a breather when needed. "I'm real happy with our run game. And it's not just my starting guys. I know Tannor and Darrian can get it done with the run game and the pass game."
The pass game includes a four-man rotation at wide receiver — seniors Jackson Conn (5-8, 145), Shelton Nichols (6-0, 160) and Derek Jones (6-1, 160), and junior Glother Gabriel (5-10, 180) — as well as junior tight end Declan Egan (6-2, 205).
There is experience on the offensive line, with the return of junior center Grayson Martin (6-1, 250), senior left tackle Owen Piavis (6-1, 210), and senior Cam King (6-4, 240), who moves from tight end to starting right tackle. Joining that group are sophomore left guard Demarcus Forsyth (6-5, 320) and junior right guard David Kusyk (5-10, 195). McMorris said junior Wyatt Eaton (6-2, 210), one of the team's best offensive linemen, figures to work his way into that starting group as he returns from injury.
"We still need to clean some things up just in terms of kids' specific jobs," McMorris said of his offense. "I think some kids are worrying about other kids' jobs. It's affecting the play because they're so worried about another block. It's just a matter of everybody jelling together and having faith in each other to get the job done. Once we get that we should have a really solid running game."
The defense also looks solid.
McMorris plans to go with a four-man rotation at the tackles, with Martin and King starting, and sophomore Xavier Comacho (5-10, 255) and freshman Desmeir Duckery (6-0, 210) stepping in when needed. Piavis, a first-team all-conference pick, returns at defensive end along with Egan and junior Caden Deavers (5-10, 205). All-Bayside linebacker Tommy Morris graduated, but the Bulldogs looked to be in good shape, with Gabriel and Somerville starting inside, and senior David Aviles (6-0, 195) and Hall staring on the outside.
Smith and Weber figure to form one of the conference's more formidable cornerback combinations. Wood starts at safety, with Walstrum also seeing time in the secondary.
"I think we're still putting it together," McMorris said of his defense. "We have a lot of guys that are kind of playing in new positions. We're getting there."
McMorris knows there may be pressure after going 9-2 in his first season as head coach, but that pressure may not necessarily translate into a repeat of, or improving on last season.
"It's more knowing that we have a good team and we should do well; more of just living up to the expectations that we've laid out for ourselves," said McMorris, who will have Mason Shilling handling the kicking duties.
"We often tell them, it's a thing we've said for years, 'You're never as good as you think you are. You're never as bad as you think you are,'" McMorris added. "And it comes down to, you don't read into the outside hype of what's going on. Like our film is going to tell us how we played and we need to be our number one critics of ourselves. Anybody else's opinion is rat poison."

title: New-look Buccameers begin Davis era
author: Bill Haufe
content:
New-look Buccameers begin Davis era

 September 5, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 577
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The head coach is new, and so are many of the faces in starting roles on both sides of the ball.But not everything has changed with Kent Island High's football program, which is set to begin the Zach Davis era Friday when the Bucs host Parkside at Andy Schipul Stadium at 6 p.m.
"We kept a lot of things very similar to how things have been done. I think that's helped," said Davis, who begins his 10th season as a head coach, but his first in Stevensville as the successor to Bryon Sofinowski, who retired after last year. "Even though there's a whole bunch of new guys, it's not like it's brand new to the coaches and players. It's pretty similar."
One thing that has remained the same is senior quarterback Gavan Henry, who returns after helping the Buccaneers to a 9-3 season a year ago, which included upending North Caroline in the second round of the Class 2A East Region playoffs.
"He's throwing the ball really well," Davis said of Henry, who will be backed up by junior Ryan Brestensky. "Good arm, good command of the offense. He's a good player for us."
Though last year's starting backfield graduated, starters Nate Green (senior wingback) and Jaxson Hess (junior single back) did get playing time in reserve roles last season. Junior wingbacks Connor Byrne and Kerry O'Brien figure to also get plenty of touches.
"We're going to come downhill at you," Davis said. "We're going to run zone, power schemes, counter schemes, some buck-sweep schemes. Our passing game comes off our run game. And then we have a spread package, where we can throw it some."
When Henry does throw, his targets will include senior Richie Guthrie and juniors Luke Umstot and Isaiah Diaz at wideout, and senior tight end Jackson Towers.
The Bucs graduated their entire offensive line from last year, so Davis, who coaches the offensive line, has been busy rebuilding. Senior James Prince starts at center between junior guards Mike Luttrell and Gerson Chevez. Senior Joe Guida is at right tackle, while Jeremiah Bounds starts on the right side.
"They're a really good group and they're working hard," Davis said of the offensive front. "But I'm their position coach so I'm partial. I think they're coachable, and I think if someone's coachable they can play pretty quickly, as long as they have the physical tools."
Perhaps the biggest returner for the Bucs is longtime defensive coordinator Tim Goodrich, who watched his unit notch three shutouts last season, and limit two other opponents to just seven points.
"He tells me all the time if I can score 14 points we'll win a lot of games," Davis said of Goodrich, who looks to replace three all-Bayside Conference first-team selections in lineman Brady O'Neal, defensive back Tucker Claxton, and linebacker Giuseppe Mellinger, the conference defensive player of the year.
Junior Greg Coffey, Bounds and Guida start up front, with senior Keegan Green and Towers at ends. Junior Roy Scott and O'Brien are at inside linebacker, with Green and Hess manning the outside backer spots. The secondary includes a combination between junior Taray Wright, Andy Bennett, Umstot, and Byrne.
Spencer Chappell kicks for the Bucs and Keegan Green punts.
"I think you feel excitement before every game," said Davis when asked about heading into his 10th season opener, the first nine of which were as a head coach in West Virginia. "That's good though. That means it means something. It's coming quickly. Then we'll move on to the next one."

title: O'Connor, Easton roll in opener
author: Bill Haufe
content:
O'Connor, Easton roll in opener

 September 6, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 755
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Mikey O'Connor may have been the happiest player on the field. And Chase Raab wasn't too far behind.O'Connor, who suffered a season-ending injury in last year's second game, ran for a pair of touchdowns and threw for two more Friday night, as Easton High's football team opened its season with a dominating 43-0 victory over North East of Cecil County.
"He's a great athlete," North East head coach Taylor Slaughenhoupt said of O'Connor, Easton's senior quarterback. "And we knew it coming in. Fantastic athlete and he did what he does. There's a reason why … he's missed pretty much two years and he still has college offers. That kid can play flat out. Just like his brothers (former Easton quarterbacks Ryan and Kevin)."
The Warriors scored on their first possession, junior running back Dustin Blue's 8-yard touchdown run capping an eight-play, 66-yard scoring drive with 8 minutes, 21 seconds left in the first quarter. Dominic Stanco drilled the first of his five point-after kicks to make it 7-0.
North East senior quarterback Garrette Kirby ran for 13 yards and a first down on the first play of the Indians' next possession. But North East went nowhere with a fresh set of downs, as Easton's Tymiere Thomas sacked Kirby on third down, forcing a punt.
One play later, O'Connor found space around right end and raced 34 yards for a touchdown. Stanco's second PAT made it 14-0 with 5:06 left in the first quarter.
"Feels great to be back out here playing again, and to get a good win like this," said O'Connor, who carried four times for 84 yards. "Definitely feels great."
Easton extended its lead to 22-0 on its next possession, as O'Connor (7 of 14, 121 yards, one interception) hit Raab in stride for a 52-yard scoring play, then found Diontaye Copper for the two-point conversion. A senior wide receiver, Raab missed all of last year because of an injury suffered during summer 7-on-7 play.
"Mikey did a good job," Easton head coach Matt Griffith said. "He managed the offense and took what the defense gave him all night long. He made some big plays with his arm and his legs tonight. And that's what we expect out of him."
Easton looked ready to take a 22-0 lead into the break. But a snap from center sailed over the head of North East punter Craig Aubrey, giving the Warriors the ball on the Indians' 5-yard line. On the next play, O'Connor raced virtually untouched around right end for a 5-yard touchdown that helped Easton to a 29-0 halftime cushion.
"They had a ton of great plays tonight," O'Connor said of his young offensive line. "And they really showed how good they can be. A lot of our touchdowns and big plays, give credit to them for that, especially on my runs."
The Warrior set the running clock in motion with 10:09 left in the third quarter as O'Connor rolled left and hit Copper for a 35-yard scoring strike. Stanco's kick made it 36-0.
Easton padded its lead with 4:30 remaining when backup quarterback Brady Walls connected with Colin Mooney for a 52-yard touchdown play.
"It was a good night," Griffith said. "We still have a lot of things to clean up on. I thought we did enough things well to put a good product on the field tonight."
Easton, which notched its first shutout since Week 2 of the 2021 season, held North East to just 39 yards rushing on 22 carries, dropping the Indians for losses seven times. Kirby, who was harassed seemingly from start to finish, completed 5 of 18 passes for 65 yards and was intercepted by Zach Barnhart.
"He was running for his life," Slaughenhoupt said of his quarterback. "We weren't protecting him. I mean we couldn't stop a leak up front.
"I thought we'd be able to run the ball on them," continued Slaughenhoupt, who graduated from Easton. "I thought it would be a competitive game and it kills me. We just did a lot of things tonight that were not us. We had a really good week (of practice) and a really good (preseason) camp, and it just wasn't there tonight."
Notes: Blue carried 8 times for 87 yards. ... Raab had two receptions for 64 yards, Copper caught three passes for 44 yards, and Colin Mooney had a pair of catches for 52 yards. ... North East wide receiver Deyshawn Henderson had two receptions for 41 yards. ... O'Connor was intercepted in the second quarter by Nathan Tesch, who caught a ball that deflected off Warrior receiver Carter Mooney.

title: Ensminger, Monroy each score twice as Warriors romp in opener for new head coach
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Ensminger, Monroy each score twice as Warriors romp in opener for new head coach

 September 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 600
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — He knows there will be tougher games and stiffer competition.But, man, did this first one feel good.
Kyle Ensminger scored a pair of goals in the opening 14 minutes, and Ale Monroy scored in each half Tuesday, as Easton High's boys soccer team rolled to an 8-0 victory over Wicomico in the head coaching debut of Avery Brice.
"Feels great," said Brice, who played on the Warriors' 2014 team that reached the Class 2A state championship game. "I told the guys in the group, everything I asked of them they delivered. I think that means a lot for me. It means they're balled in. They got the same mindset as me. That means everything. First game, 8-0. But it doesn't stop today. And we don't be complacent."
Ensminger collected a pass from Kai Ferraris, slipped past a defender, and deposited Easton's first goal of the season into the net just 4:14 into the game.
Wicomico keeper Matthew Bier stopped a point-blank bid by Ensminger a little over two minutes later. But in the 14th minute, Ensminger gathered a lead pass from Dominic Stanco, calmly pushed downfield with a pair of defenders closing on his right hip, drew Bier off his line, and neatly tucked a left-footed shot into the right side of the net for a 2-0 lead.
The Warriors continued to extend their advantage.
Mario Medina fed Monroy, who unloaded a low, hard drive off Bier's hands for a 3-0 cushion with 25:30 left in the first half. CJ Chaconas settled a ball from Ensminger and hammered a shot off the keeper's hands to make it 4-0. Landon Chaney capped the first-half scoring with a drive from near the left post for a 5-0 Warrior lead.
"We continue to go," said Brice of his team's not getting complacent despite its comfortable halftime lead. "And I know when we get really tested, opportunities won't come like they did today. I told the guys that. So we do got to work on finishing, things of that nature, taking our chances and making them count when they are presented upon us."
Easton junior keeper Sam Hutchison was never seriously challenged, as the Warriors' backline and midfield controlled play.
"Love our defense. Love our possession game," Brice said. "The guys know that we got to play a little bit simpler. And I told the guys from the get (go), like we do the simple things correct, we'll be the best team."
Medina broke in from left wing in the 8th minute of the second half and was taken down, setting up his penalty-kick goal that pushed the lead to 6-0. Monroy netted his second goal with an innocent-looking chip less than two minutes later. Elmer Pineda completed with scoring with 24:08 remaining when he put one past Indians backup keeper Sam Fleuriot, making it 8-0.
A new rule instituted this season stops play in the 60th minute if a team has an eight-goal lead.
"It was the first thing I was thinking when I woke up this morning," Brice said of his first game as head coach. "So proud of these guys. Talented team. I just want them to continue to know that. One game at a time. We move on. OK, it's not a celebration. We did what we were supposed to and we move on."
QUEEN ANNE'S 2, PARKSIDE 2
CENTREVILLE — Ryan Lee and James Rath each scored once, and Gage Jordan notched an assist as the Lions battled the Rams to a draw in double overtime.
J.M. BENNETT 10, N. CAROLINE 2

title: Webb's four goals pace Sabres in shutout of ESIAC newcomer Tome School
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Webb's four goals pace Sabres in shutout of ESIAC newcomer Tome School

 September 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 650
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — It could have easily been deemed a reenactment of David and Goliath."It's the equivalent of my son's rec team going up against a college team," Tome School head field hockey coach Jenn Waldron said after her team's visit to Saints Peter and Paul High.
Of course don't expect Sabres head coach Debbie McQuaid to ever call her team Goliath. The defending Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference champions? Yes. Goliath? No.
Yet McQuaid's bunch looked very much the part Wednesday, as Angie Webb scored four goals to lead seven different scorers during a 13-0 victory over the the Titans.
"I told one of the players, she's in my Spanish One class, I'm like, 'You're in Spanish One. Could you walk into Spanish Four and hold your own?'" said Waldron, whose team is in the ESIAC for the first time. 'Does it mean you're not as smart? No. You're just not there yet.' So they are a solid team. They've got the resources. They got the coaching staff. That's what showed on the field."
And it didn't take the Sabres (2-1 overall, 1-0 ESIAC) long to show their stuff.
The contest was all of 46 seconds old, when Webb converted a Caroline Corson feed into the game's first goal. Tome (1-2) and first-year goalie Steph Cingle held Sts. Peter & Paul scoreless for a stretch despite the Sabres racking up a slew of early penalty-corner opportunities.
But with just under 7 minutes left in the first quarter, Webb scored to spark a four-goal surge. Kate Sweeney (two goals) scored off a dish from Jules Stepp (two goals, two assists) with less than 5 minutes remaining in the opening quarter. Webb added her third goal with 2 minutes to go before Kat Murphy netted the first of her two goals for a 5-0 lead heading into the second quarter.
"I think we're jelling more than we did the first (scrimmage) because we played Stephen Decatur and we lost," Stepp said. "But after that we built together as a team. We practiced hard and we're jelling now. We're looking for our back passes. We're looking up for each other. And we're looking for our open teammates."
Claire Bieber, who transferred in from St. Michaels this season, touched on another Sabres' staple — speed.
"We have a very fast team," Bieber said. "We have a lot of speed, and we've been working on quick release and transfers."
The Sabres stretched the lead to 9-0 at halftime as Sweeney, Kiera Crossed, Webb and Corson each scored during a second quarter that was played with a running clock.
Bieber scored the lone goal of the third, then watched Stepp score twice and Murphy once in the fourth quarter.
"We are learning from what we are missing," Stepp said in reference to a graduated crowd that included Gennie Webb, Morgan Quade and Emmary Sweeney from last year's 14-2 team. "And we're trying to fill that void together and add more people in, and work together as a team."
McQuaid agreed, saying since preseason she has liked the influx of youth to this year's team.
"The younger kids' energy and enthusiasm, and how quickly they're picking up our system, has been very good," McQuaid said. "Bridget Gilman and Tara Foley in the back, they got good minutes and did what they were supposed to do; passed and share the ball. They don't always get into the tighter games, but today they were ready.
"Tried to play everybody," McQuaid added. "Had seven different people score. So that was good."
Corson finished with two assists and CC O'Connor had one assist. Sts. Peter & Paul finished with 13 corners to Tome's four.
KENT ISLAND 4, WASHINGTON 0
PRINCESS ANNE — Willow Yost scored a pair of goals and Ellie Burnside totaled three assists the lead the Buccaneers.
Sydney Riska and Lyla Bailey each had one goal for Kent Island (1-0) and Sadie Latchaw had an assist. Brynja Petursson finished with four saves. The Bucs had six corners.

title: Vikings rush past Knights
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings rush past Knights

 September 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 603
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — Rob Burnham is among the football coaching crowd who stresses the importance of the second half's first possession.The last possession of the first half proved pretty important as well for Burnham's Cambridge-South Dorchester High team Friday night.
Sterling Perkins hauled in a 14-yard touchdown pass just before the end of the first half, then scored on a 3-yard run to open the second half, to help give the Vikings separation on the way to a 49-21 victory over Century.
"I tell our kids all the time when we get in the locker room that the first possession of the second half is the biggest possession of the game," said Cambridge-SD's first-year head coach after his team improved to 2-0. "And I believe that. You open the game and score, that's OK because there's a lot of ballgame left. But when you open the second half (and score). ... And I thought it was big that we scored right before halftime and then we got the possession again. So that gives us the two-score lead. That's huge. Huge."
After a scoreless first quarter, Cambridge-SD senior quarterback Anthony Hughes scored on runs of 20 and 55 yards to help stake the Vikings to a 14-0 lead with 9 minutes, 18 seconds left in the second quarter. Collin Bair drilled both point-after kicks.
The Knights (0-2) rallied though. Jonathan Ferguson scored on a 1-yard run up the middle, but the point-after boot sailed wide left, leaving Century trailing 14-6.
Cambridge-SD drove from its 40 to the Knights' 20, where Dylan Vroom intercepted Vikings backup quarterback Nathan Twilley and raced 80 yards up the sideline for a touchdown. Ferguson's two-point conversion run tied the game at 14-all with 3:02 left before halftime.
The Vikings came right back, as Hughes lofted a pass toward the end zone that Perkins made a nice over-the-shoulder grab on for a 14-yard touchdown and a 20-14 lead with 7.6 remaining in the first half. Cambridge-SD bobbled the snap from center on the extra-point attempt, and settled for a six-point lead entering the break.
The Vikings needed just three plays to expand that lead on the first possession of the second half. Perkins ran for gains of 17 and 27 yards before he took a handoff and made a quick juke into the end zone for a 3-yard touchdown. Hughes hit Antonio Blueford with a two-point conversion pass for a 28-14 lead just 42 seconds into the third.
On its next possession, Century tried to convert a fourth-and-four from its own 31. But quarterback Jacob Dexter fired incomplete, turning the ball over to the Vikings. On the next play, William Jackson swept right and blazed into the end zone for a 31-yard touchdown. Bair added the PAT for a 35-14 lead with 9:08 to go in the third.
Century pulled within 35-21 with 4:50 left in the third, as Ferguson bulled his way into the end zone from 2 yards out, then booted the point-after.
The Knights though could not stop Cambridge-SD's big plays.
On its ensuing possession, Hughes broke free for his third touchdown run, this one covering 42 yards for a 41-21 cushion with 3:34 left in the third.
Cambridge-SD again stopped the Knights on fourth down, but penalties from the Vikings back to their own 6-yard line. It didn't matter, as Perkins took a handoff, found a seam up the middle, and bolted 94 yards for a touchdown. Blueford made a diving grab on Hughes' two-point pass for a 49-21 lead.
"We're going to get better," Burnham said. "The things we struggled with today we'll make improvements on. We have to be better than we were tonight that's for sure."

title: Defending North Bayside champion Queen Anne’s County among teams trying to fill graduation holes in an attempt for another deep playoff
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Defending North Bayside champion Queen Anne’s County among teams trying to fill graduation holes in an attempt for another deep playoff

 September 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1620
 Words 

 Read News Document

 North Bayside boys soccer coaches have been busy this preseason — and during the early weeks of the regular season — mending holes in their lineups.Defending division champion Queen Anne's County High, which went 13-3-1 and reached the Class 2A state semifinals a year ago, graduated eight, including six starters.
"The guys that we lost were huge parts," Lions head coach Wade Hosler said.
North Caroline head coach John Austin can sympathize after graduating seven, including 2023 North Bayside Player of the Year Logan Harned.
"I feel as a conference we lost a lot of really good players," Austin said. "Last year's conference was very, very senior heavy."
A handful of those graduates are now playing in the collegiate ranks, with North Caroline's Harned at Neumann (Pa.) University and goalie Gavin O'Brien at Frostburg State, while Queen Anne's has Billy Schindler at Washington College.
The Class 1A ranks also felt graduation's sting. North Dorchester lost 10, while Cambridge-South Dorchester first-year head coach Josh Dohoney is trying to patch holes created by almost half of dozen losses.
In addition to the Vikings, Easton welcomes former standout Avery Brice as its new head coach, while Kent County begins the Dennis Hickman era.
Queen Anne's shared the conference title with James M. Bennett in 2021, but the last North team to win the Bayside championship outright was Kent Island in 2016, when the Bucs topped Stephen Decatur in penalty kicks. The Bucs and Lions look to be on another collision course to decide the North when they meet in Stevensville on Oct. 18, though North Caroline and Easton figure to also be atop the division ranks.
The South's dominance of the conference crown could be extended this year, as Bennett, which lost to eventual Class 3A state champion South River in last year's postseason, returns the bulk of its team from a season ago.
Here's a look at this year's North Bayside teams.
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Josh Dohoney.
Who's Where: Goalie: Nate Huber (Sr.); Backs: Osvaldo Hernandez (Jr.); Evan Kozak (Sr.); Colton Phillips (So.); Gibby Robinson (So.); Midfield: Lucas Harper (So.); Gavin Weber (So.); Ryan Harris (Sr.); Forwards: Will Banks (Jr.); Wyatt Abbott (So.); Marcos Hernandez (Fr.).
Outlook: After one year as an assistant, Dohoney begins his first head coaching job in soccer knowing he'll need to be patient.
"We're very young. Very much a rebuilding squad," said Dohoney, who played at Delmar, Del.
The Vikings graduated more than half a dozen from last year, including center midfielder Randall Johnson. The midfield looks technically sound, but with five sophomores and one freshman starting, Dohoney hopes this will be a season of growth.
COL. RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Dillon Shaheen.
Who's Where: Goalie: Cohen Carels (Sr.); Backs: Cameron Todd (Sr.); Jacklin Novembre (Jr.); Jackson Jean Jr. (Jr.); Caleb Rouser (So.); Midfield: John Beaven (So.); Jack Walls (Jr.); Preston Rickwood (Sr.); Ludver Vasquez (Jr.); Aydan Downie (Sr.); Forwards: Morgan Demir (Sr.); Angel Castro-Rios (Sr.); Skyler Endzel (Fr.); Brody Omohundro (Fr.).
Outlook: Shaheen begins his third year as head coach with his most experienced team he's had. That has translated into victories over Pocomoke and North Dorchester for starters.
"It's been pretty good so far," said Shaheen, who lost three seniors from last year. "Obviously we have a lot of seniors and juniors, and most have been playing at the varsity level for three or four years. I'm pretty confident in our squad this year."
EASTON
Head Coach: Avery Brice.
Who's Where: Goalie: Sam Hutchison (Jr.); Backs: Mario Medina (Sr.); Felix Valentine (Jr.); Brody Byrnes (Sr.); Kai Ferraris (Jr.); Landon Chaney (Sr.); Midfield: Clay Nagle (Sr.); Luke Stanco (Jr.); CJ Chaconas (Sr.); Blake Royer (So.); Ale Monroy (So.); Dominic Stanco (Sr.); Otto Perez-Arreaga (Fr.); Logan Sundt (Jr.); Liam Edgell (Sr.); Forwards: Kyle Ensminger (Jr.); Rodi Fresco Rubio (Jr.).
Outlook: Brice was a center midfielder on Easton's last two teams to win Bayside titles (2013, '14) and helped the Warriors reach the 2A state final in '14 before continuing his playing career at Wesley (Del.) College.
Now, he steps into his first head coaching job.
"Things are shaping up nicely," Brice said. "Could things be better? Yes. That's kind of one thing that we just hope to do every day in the season; just be better than the day before."
While the Warriors have been receptive to their new coach's ideas and style, Brice stressed they must strive for consistency.
"The mindset is you can be really good, but every game you've got to bring it," Brice said.
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Dennis Hickman.
Who's Where: Goalie: Leyder Cruz (Sr.); Backs: Noah Iacona (Jr.); Jayden Miller (So.); Stewart Hickman (Jr.); Bryce Jacobs (So.); Midfield: Nick Stead (Sr.); Colbyn Lopez (Jr.); Ethan Clark (Sr.); Forwards: Gabe Parr (So.); Dylan Peralta (Fr.); Sebastian Cousineau (So.).
Outlook: A 1993 graduate of Kent County, Hickman, who played soccer, baseball and wrestled for the Trojans, takes over as head coach after spending the last two years as an assistant.
In an attempt to build a program, Hickman has already achieved one goal in fielding a junior varsity for the first time since 2019.
"We think by having a jayvee, getting them out there on practice, getting them those reps and having some game-time situations and play, that we're only going to be able to build on that moving forward," Hickman said. "It's just the best thing for the program."
That coupled with a varsity roster that includes nine juniors and nine sophomores, could bode well for the future.
As for this year's team, there isn't a lot of experience, though Stewart Hickman has plenty of travel ball experience, as has recruited players over the summer to come out for the team.
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Lin Outten.
Who's Where: Goalie: Quinn Burns (Fr.); Backs: Davis Miller (Sr.); Noah Scopp (Sr.); Gavin Neboshynsky (Sr.); Mark Rees (Sr.); Spencer Chappell (Jr.); Elijah James (So.); Midfield: Simon Vujinovic (Sr.); Brendan Thomas (Jr.); Cooper Liebel (So.); Landon Pecor (Jr.); Forwards: AJ Miller (Jr.); Eric Hoffman (Sr.); Ethan Schriver (Sr.); Robert Simkins (Jr.).
Outlook: The Bucs have a lot of experience moving from the midfield into the attack, but are not as experienced in the back. Though seniors Davis Miller, Scopp and Rees return, Outten hopes shifting Neboshynsky and Chappell from midfield to the back bolsters his defense.
AJ Miller netted 10 goals a year ago, and Outten thinks that number will go up, especially with the return of Hoffman, who missed the bulk of last year with an early season injury.
"But really what makes the engine go is the three guys in the middle — Thomas, Vujinovic and Liebel," Outten said.
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: John Austin.
Who's Where: Goalie: Mason Shilling (Jr.); Backs: Lewis Higgs (Jr.); Brayden Boarts (Sr.); Jimmy Cohoon (Jr.); Midfield: Ayden Russell (Jr.); Tyler Gutierrez (Jr.); Omar Marroquin (Sr.); Jonnathan Luna Feliciano (Jr.); Diego Castro (So.); Landyn Harned (So.); Kyle Reed (Jr.); Forwards: Heath Frantum (Jr.); Issac Bautista (Jr.); Luke Raga (So.).
Outlook: The Bulldogs graduated seven from a year ago, including Harned, O'Brien, and also lost leading scorer Kevin Godinez.
Austin thinks his team will be more defensive-minded this season. The defense is led by Shilling, who Austin thinks has college potential. Shilling and company figure to be tested early, as the Bulldogs open with defending conference champion James M. Bennett, Class 2A state semifinalist Queen Anne's, and perennial conference heavyweight Stephen Decatur.
"We have a lot of holes to fill," Austin said. "I think we are where we need to be right now. But the goal is can we just keep getting better as the year goes on, and then when October rolls around, play our best soccer?"
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Gabe Guzman.
Who's Where: Goalie: Jayden Coleman (Jr.); Backs: Chris Sanchez (Jr.); Tahjere Pritchett (Jr.); Alex Fonseca-Gonzalez (So.); Martin Chirino Fernandez (Jr.); Midfield: Christian Chase (Jr.); Peyton Bleyer (So.); Daniel Mejia (Sr.); Kegan Henry (Jr.); Forwards: Volcy Nerat (Fr.); Dagoberto Chirino Fernandez.
Outlook: The Eagles graduated 10, including seven starters. Among Guzman's top priorities is getting his freshman to buy into his system and get acclimated to the high school varsity format.
"We're working on trust," Guzman said.
QUEEN ANNE'S
Head Coach: Wade Hosler.
Who's Where: Goalie: Ethan Keppler (Sr.); Backs: Christian Coppage (Sr.); Conner Cheezum (Sr.); Hayden Albright (Sr.); Brody Nordvik (Jr.); Midfield: James Rath (Jr.); Gage Jordan (Sr.); Nathan Kostka (Jr.); Mason Albright (Sr.); Boden Blodgett (So.); Josiah Hegarty (So.); Forwards: Ryan Lee (Sr.).
Outlook: "The preseason seemed awfully short this year, and our chemistry wasn't quite where I'd like it this time of year," Hosler said. "But I think it's coming, so I'm optimistic that we can do good things. We've had good moments and we've had mistakes. But I like the direction we're heading in."
Hosler has also liked his team's 3-0-1 start, which included Monday's 3-0 shutout of North Caroline.
Despite its big graduation losses, the Lions do have a solid core of returners. Outside backs Coppage and Cheezum return along with Keppler in goal. Jordan is back in the midfield while Lee returns at striker.
"We have some big pieces, but we still have some big holes to fill," said Hosler, who graduation losses included Schindler, center back William Nagle and leading scorer Nick Esper. "If we can have some guys step up I think we'll be OK."
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: Pat Hambleton.
Who's Where: Goalie: Will Sherwood (Sr.); Backs: Tyler Murphy (Jr.); Jack Brennan (Sr.); Sherwin Mendez (Sr.); Brennan Dean (Jr.); Midfield: Ethan Royer (Jr.); Gavin Bieber (Fr.); Johnny Mautz (Jr.); Abel Delgaudio (So.); Forwards: Connor Wheeler (Jr.); Miles Fox (Jr.); Haven Haddaway (Sr.).
Outlook: Having Sherwood — first-team all-North Bayside goalie the past two years — and an experienced returning defensive unit should make the Saints plenty tough.
While that provides Hambleton comfort, he also liked what he has seen on the offensive end.
"Finally creative," Hambleton said of his attack. "We're going to be an enjoyment to watch. Still have an older group to support our creative offensive style. I have players to make it a pretty game finally. And they get it."

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 848
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Two-time Super Bowl MVP Eli Manning, former Defensive Players of the Year Luke Kuechly and Terrell Suggs, and postseason kicking hero Adam Vinatieri are among the players nominated for the 2025 Pro Football Hall of Fame class in their first year of eligibility.The Hall announced 167 modern era candidates for the class on Wednesday that included 16 players who became eligible this year, including two-time All-Pro guard Marshal Yanda.
A screening committee will reduce the list of nominees to 50 players next month. Then the full 50-person selection committee will cut the list down to 25 semifinalists and then 15 finalists for the annual meeting before the Super Bowl that will produce the new class. Players must get 80% of votes to get in with between three and five players getting in as modern era candidates.
There will also be three senior candidates, grouped with one coach and contributor with at least one and no more than three of those finalists getting in based on voting.
The other first-year candidates are offensive linemen Travis Frederick, Ryan Kalil and Joe Staley; running backs Darren Sproles and Marshawn Lynch; receiver Demaryius Thomas; tight ends Vernon Davis and Delanie Walker; and defensive backs Antoine Bethea, Aqib Talib and Earl Thomas.
There are also 10 players back under consideration who were finalists a year ago with tight end Antonio Gates, receivers Torry Holt and Reggie Wayne; offensive linemen Willie Anderson and Jahri Evans; defensive backs Darren Woodson, Eric Allen and Rodney Harrison; defensive lineman Jared Allen; and running back Fred Taylor back on the list.
Manning will look to follow his brother Peyton into the Hall following a standout career with the New York Giants. Manning was picked first overall in the 2004 draft and spent his entire career in New York. He led the Giants to an upset win over the undefeated New England Patriots in the Super Bowl following the 2007 season, throwing a game-winning TD pass to Plaxico Burress in the final minute.
He led another late TD drive to upset Tom Brady and the Patriots four years later. Manning is one of 13 QBs to win multiple Super Bowls with eight of the nine who are eligible for the Hall getting inducted.
Only Jim Plunkett has not been inducted along with more recent players such as Brady, Ben Roethlisberger and Patrick Mahomes, who aren't eligible.
Manning was a four-time Pro Bowler but never made All-Pro or led the league in a major statistical category in a season but finished his career with 57,023 yards passing and 366 TDs.
His best moments were in those two postseason runs. Manning joined Brady (five), Mahomes (three), Joe Montana (three), Bart Starr (two) and Terry Bradshaw (two) as the only multiple winners of Super Bowl MVP awards.
Kuechly and Suggs were among the top defensive players of their era with Kuechly selected as the top defensive player in 2013 and Suggs in 2011.
Kuechly's career was brief but impactful. The first-round pick by Carolina in 2012 was an All-Pro five times in his eight-year career with seven Pro Bowl nods and a Defensive Rookie of the Year award.
Over his eight-year career, Kuechly led all linebackers in the NFL in tackles (1,090), takeaways (26), interceptions (18) and passes defensed (66).
Suggs was one of the top pass rushers in the league over his 17-year career, with his 139 sacks ranking eighth best since they became an official stat in 1982.
Suggs had seven double-digit sack seasons in his 16 seasons with Baltimore, including 14 in 2011 when he was selected as the top defensive player in the league and led the NFL with seven forced fumbles.
He won Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2003 and helped the Ravens win the Super Bowl in the 2012 season. He finished his career in Kansas City where he helped the Chiefs win the Super Bowl in the 2019 season.
Vinatieri was one of the most clutch kickers in NFL history, making the game-winning field goals in the first two Super Bowl titles during New England's dynasty.
He helped launch the run with one of the game's greatest kicks — a 45-yarder in the snow to force overtime in the "Tuck Rule" game against the Raiders in the 2001 divisional round. He made the game-winning kick in OT to win that game and then hit a 48-yarder on the final play of a 20-17 win in the Super Bowl against the Rams.
He then made a 41-yarder two years later to give the Patriots a 32-29 win in the Super Bowl against Carolina. Vinatieri also won Super Bowls in 2004 with New England and in the 2006 season with Indianapolis.
Vinatieri is the NFL's all-time leader in points (2,673) and made field goals (599) over a 24-year career with New England and Indianapolis. He also leads all players with 56 field goals and 238 points in the postseason.
Yanda was a member of the 2010s all-decade team as a key of Baltimore's success. He also was selected second-team All-Pro five times and made the Pro Bowl in eight of his final seasons, missing in 2017 when he played only two games of an injury.

title: Caps may lose Oshie for season
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Caps may lose Oshie for season

 September 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 440
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Washington Capitals winger T.J. Oshie is expected to go on long-term injured reserve this season because of chronic back problems.The team announced Wednesday that Oshie will be listed as injured at the start of training camp after undergoing his medical exam. He and the Capitals left the door open for a possible return, even though it may be unlikely.
"I have used the offseason to explore and pursue long-term solutions for my injury," Oshie said in a statement. "I remain committed to the process and am working and doing my best to regain total health. In the meantime, I will continue to help and support my teammates and the organization in any way I can."
Oshie, 37, said in late April he hoped to continue playing but only if he and doctors could find a permanent solution with his back that would keep him from being in and out of the lineup. Injuries, though not just to his back, limited Oshie to 52 of 82 games last season, 58 in 2022-23 and 44 in '21-22.
"We will support and assist T.J. as he seeks a lasting solution for his recurring injury," general manager Chris Patrick said. "T.J. is a vital member of our team and continues to be an indispensable member of the organization and leadership group. Our organization fully backs him as he assesses his current health challenges."
Oshie is in the last year of his contract, and the Capitals will get LTIR relief for Oshie's $5.75 million salary cap hit, just as they are with center Nicklas Backstrom, who stepped away early last season because of a nagging hip injury.
The front office planned this past offseason for the possibility of not having Oshie, acquiring winger Andrew Mangiapane from Calgary among several moves to revamp the roster following a first-round sweep at the hands of the New York Rangers. Before handing the day-to-day responsibilities over to Patrick, longtime GM Brian MacLellan put together a team that would be cap compliant with Oshie and Backstrom on LTIR but with the flexibility to adjust if the situation changed.
Oshie, who grew up in Everett, Washington, and moved to Warroad, Minnesota, as a teenager, played his first seven seasons in the league with St. Louis. He's best known for his shootout heroics for the U.S. against host Russia at the 2014 Olympics, where he scored on four of six attempts to clinch a victory and earned national fame beyond hockey as "T.J. Sochi."
Traded to Washington in 2015, he had 21 points on the 2018 Stanley Cup run and famously chugged a beer through his jersey at the rally following the first championship parade in franchise history.
