title: Queen Anne's takes aim at fifth straight North Bayside title and more
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's takes aim at fifth straight North Bayside title and more

 September 19, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1297
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Queen Anne's County High's girls soccer program has compiled an impressive resume during Mike Kern's 23 seasons as head coach.The Lions have won 14 North Bayside titles and two Bayside Conference championships. They've reached 11 regional finals, winning twice, and have advanced to the state finals once.
But as Queen Anne's has worked through preseason tryouts, scrimmages and into the regular season's early weeks, Kern sees a team that could be among his finest from front to back.
"This might be our most talented team we've ever had in my opinion," said Kern, who has never had a losing record as he enters his 24th season as head coach. "Every single one of them has played travel for years. There's a lot of times we'd get good athletes that played lacrosse or something else, and just played soccer to stay in shape. But this year we have soccer players. And for most of the girls, their first sport is soccer. I think that's the difference from years past."
Despite that talent, which includes all-state first-team selection and returning North Bayside Player of the Year Olivia Ryan, Kern knows there is one main obstacle in his team's path to a fifth consecutive North title — the 2020 COVID-shortened season excluded — and a potential regional title — Kent Island.
Though Queen Anne's shut out the Bucs 3-0 during the regular season last year, it lost 3-2 in double overtime in the Class 2A East Region II title game.
The Lions blanked Kent Island, 1-0, already this season, but have a second date with their county rival Oct. 16 which will likely decided the division crown, and then could have a third encounter come the postseason.
"I'm excited. I really am," Kern said of the season. "We should go far. But we've got to get through Kent Island."
Here's a look at this year's teams.
CAMBRIDGE-SDHead Coach: Sarah Alpaugh.
Who's Where: Goalie: Akizhae Hammond (Jr.); Backs: Monti Jackson (So.); Skyla Ali (So.); Mimi Exume (So.); Sophia Diaz (Fr.); Midfield: Lainey Jones (Sr.); Olivia Fischer (Fr.); Kamryn Bourne (So.); Lilly Moxey (Fr.); Forwards: Laila Insley (Sr.); Madalyn Spicer (Jr.); Jade Bryant (Jr.); Kennedy Bourne (So.).
Outlook: The Vikings graduated their entire defensive unit from a year ago, so one of Alpaugh's focuses will be hoping a young cast of replacements can stick together and gain experience to form a strong foundation for the future.
Jones is a four-year starter that anchors a midfield, which hopes to regain the services of returning starter Kamryn Bourne, who was injured in the season's second game. Alpaugh, who begins her third year, calls Insley a key component, and coupled with the speedy Bryant, could provide a nice one-two punch at the top.
COL. RICHARDSONHead Coach: Beth Carmen.
Who's Where: Goalie: Cloee Welzel (So.); Backs: Olivia McGregor (So.); Kallie Peele (Sr.); Violet Cheezum (Jr.); Adan Alvi (Sr.); Agatha Divjak (Fr.); Lila Schriefer (Jr.); Vanessa Odidika (Sr.); Midfield: Brynne Harper (So.); Doranelli Tomas-Ortiz (So.); Forwards: Ryleigh Hall (So.); Sadie Prettyman (So.).
Outlook: The Colonels got clobbered by Snow Hill a year ago, 8-0. They met the Eagles in this year's opener and scored the game's first goal in an eventual 4-2 loss.
"I have really seen a lot of improvement from last year," said Carmen, who is in her second year as head coach. "I've actually had one of the refs come over to me and say this is one of the best looking Colonel girls soccer teams that he's seen in a long time."
Carmen will rotate players between defense and midfield, and attack and midfield in hopes of finding a consistent combination. After falling to the Eagles in the opener, Colonel bounced back with wins over Cambridge-SD and North Dorchester.
"This is a really great group of kids," Carmen said. "They work well together and they communicate well."
EASTONHead Coach: Ellie Kilmon.
Who's Where: Goalie Zelia Proa (So.); Backs: Dakota Lhotsky (Jr.); Sam Murphy (Sr.); Bella Swann (Sr.); Finley Golden (So.); Stella Petrichenko (So.); Midfield: Addie Schindler (Fr.); Laillah Janes (Sr.); Addie Chandler (Sr.); Anna Quidley (Sr.); Megan Wright (Fr.); Angie Martinez (Jr.); Forward: Miranda Stup (Jr.).
Outlook: Kilmon isn't making any predictions whether the Warriors can battle Queen Anne's and Kent Island for division supremacy.
"I never know until we play," Kilmon said. "It really depends on how the girls show up and play."
Center backs Lhotsky and Murphy look to provide a solid defensive core.
"I'm excited for the year," Kilmon said. "I think we have a good amount of returners and we just have a nice team dynamics that's building so I'm excited to seem them grow together."
KENT COUNTYHead Coach: Ben Joiner.
Who's Where: Goalie: Sophia Cousineau (So.); Backs: Mary Jane Joiner (Jr.); Paige Miller (Sr.); Savanna Reynolds (Jr.); Reese Strong (Fr.); Midfield: Delilah Markovic (Jr.); Jane Cleary (So.); Emy Karlik (Fr.); Bella Hinefelt (So.); Forwards: Zuleika Nava (Jr.); Sabrina Tee (Fr.); Madison Garcia (Fr.); Morgan Kendall (Sr.); Kayla Aguilar (Fr.); Ashlynn Elborn (Fr.); Amelia Plummer (Fr.).
Outlook: A 1995 Kent County graduate, Joiner takes over as head coach and has watched his young team get off to a 2-1 start.
"We really got a lot of positive momentum going with the number of girls that have joined the team this year," said Joiner, who praised the work of assistant Joel Tolbert in helping develop the team. "We're super young. We're really relying on the leadership of our seniors and juniors to elevate the team."
Joiner said an emphasis has been placed on defense in preparation for the 2A schools on the schedule, but has been encouraged by his team's play against 1A rivals.
NORTH CAROLINEHead Coach: Jenna Riordan.
Who's Where: Goalie: Rylee Gowen (Jr.); Amber Biars (Jr.); Backs: Sarah Brown (Sr.); Natalie Newman (Jr.); Izzy Knott (Sr.); Midfield: Emma Hansley (So.); Megan Rogers (Sr.); Madison McNinch (Jr.); Paisley Garland (Jr.); Linda Ridgell (Jr.); Forwards: Irma Sanchez (Jr.); Seanna Rupp (Sr.).
Outlook: The Bulldogs opened the season by defeating Parkside — gaining a measure of revenge on the Rams, who knocked them out of the playoffs in last year's 2A East Region I title game — but then lost by a goal to Easton before getting humbled by Stephen Decatur.
"We have had a rough start to our season so far, but I'm hoping to get a couple wins under our belts the next two weeks," Riordan said. "That ought to help our record."
Riordan also hopes a few wins help her team's confidence as it transitions from a 4-4-2 scheme to a 3-5-2 alignment.
"We're still adjusting and learning our positions," said Riordan, who begins her sixth season. "I've always said that we play up to the teams that are above us, so I do think we'll play (Queen Anne's and Kent Island) a really good game."
QUEEN ANNE'SHead Coach: Mike Kern.
Who's Where: Goalie: Bea Holthaus (So.); Backs: Shannon Rath (Jr.); Hayden Legg (Sr.); Finley Patchett (So.); Kathryn Baer (Sr.); Abby Robinson (So.); Midfield: Chloe Sharp (Sr.); Olivia Ryan (Sr.); Morgan Scott (Sr.); Kara Ringold (Jr.); Forwards: Madi Horney (So.); Riley Klepper (Sr.); Taylor Napier (So.).
Outlook: The most notable graduation loss for the Lions was back Elizabeth Oldfield. But this could be one of the best defensive units Kern and longtime assistant Jeff Anthony have ever had in Centreville.
Kern also noted Scott and Ringold may be the two best outside midfielders Queen Anne's has had since the days of former standout Kesley Dean. Add to the mix Ryan, the all-state pick and the Lions' leading scorer from last year is back, along with a group of nine sophomores, several of which played together on a travel team coached by Kern.
Despite all that, Kent Island remains the primary hurdle in the North, while James M. Bennett or Stephen Decatur — which defeated the Lions in overtime to open the season — are angling toward the South Bayside crown and a possible conference championship showdown.

title: Warriors survive Bulldogs' rally
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors survive Bulldogs' rally

 September 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 836
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — It didn't matter that North Caroline High's football team had lost its first two games this season.The Bulldogs just scared Easton head coach Matt Griffith. And in a furious fourth-quarter span of just over four minutes they showed why, shaving a 28-point Warrior lead to just seven.
That's when Mikey O'Connor took over. Easton's senior quarterback ran for a pair of first downs and threw for another in the final 2:52 Friday night to finally secure a 28-21 victory that pushed the Warriors' record to 3-0.
"They got great athletes all over the field," Griffith said of North Caroline. "They've struggled early on, but you saw exactly how explosive they can be, and how quick they can be explosive. That's what I was worried about. Sometimes you can do all the right things, but sometimes really good athletes can make plays. And that's a lot of what happened in the last five minutes of the twilight zone that we're calling it."
O'Connor hit Diontaye Copper for a 35-yard touchdown pass 1:41 into the third quarter, and Dominic Stanco tacked on the point-after kick for a 28-0 Easton lead.
The Warriors had not allowed a point all season until North Caroline's Tyson Weber scored on a 16-yard run with just under seven minutes left in the game, drawing the Bulldogs (0-3) within 28-7. Mason Shilling added the extra point.
Easton went three-and-out on its next possession, with O'Connor booting a quick kick to North Caroline's 27. Bulldog senior quarterback Corey Bunce hit Derek Jones for 13 yards, then connected with Zymear Smith for a 33-yard pickup. Weber scored on a 27-yard touchdown run on the next play and Shilling again converted the PAT, narrowing Easton's lead to 28-14 with 3:57 left.
North Caroline recovered the ensuing onsides kick at the Warrior 47. Bunce hit Jones for a 20-yard gain. Easton's Tymiere Thomas sacked Bunce for a 5-yard loss. But the Bulldogs' quarterback fired toward the end zone on the next play, and watched the ball deflect into the hands of Jones for a 33-yard touchdown. Shilling's point-after kick made it 28-21 with 2:52 remaining.
"Hell of a comeback," North Caroline head coach Nic McMorris said. "I'm so proud of the resilience of our guys. It was the first time that we recognized this team.
"They're a great team," McMorris added of Easton. "They have such a dynamic offense. But we were moving the ball and just kept shooting ourselves in the foot. And then we just started playing inspired football."
North Caroline drove from its 38 to the Easton 12 when it fumbled the ball away late in the first quarter. But the Bulldogs regained possession four plays later when O'Connor's pass was deflected and intercepted by Smith. Again Caroline moved the ball, marching 32 yards to the Warrior 8. But the Bulldogs again fumbled, with Easton recovering at the 1.
Easton's next drive ended with a fumble, giving North Caroline possession at the Warrior 25. But North Caroline went no where on three plays. Shilling came on to attempt a 40-yard field goal, but slipped on his approach, the kick falling well short.
The Warriors, who took a 7-0 lead on O'Connor's 3-yard touchdown run and Stanco's PAT with 3:54 left in the first quarter, stretched their lead to 14-0 with 2:11 left in the first half, when Jordan Horsey slammed in from five yards out. Stanco again made the extra point.
Easton took advantage of a short Caroline punt, as O'Connor hit Carter Mooney for 18 yards, and Copper for 17 yards before scoring on a 2-yard run for a 21-0 halftime lead.
"We came out with a game plan and we executed very well," Griffith said. "I think we did a lot of really good things early, even with two turnovers. Those are our first two turnovers of the year. We were able to bounce back."
So was North Caroline.
"No excuses," Griffith said. "Caroline's a good football team. They're a very good football team for being 0-3."
It's one-time 28-point cushion reduced to just seven, Dustin Blue recovered the onsides kick for Easton after North Caroline had gotten within 28-21.
O'Connor ran for three yards before Caroline called time. O'Connor then ran for eight yards and a first down. North Caroline stuffed Easton's quarterback for no gain on the next play and again burned a timeout. O'Connor then fired an 11-yard dart to Carter Mooney for a first down, then found room around left end for a 22-yard pickup and a first down that clinched the win. O'Connor took a knee on the next two plays to bleed the final minute.
'We got up and then we just kind of let off," O'Connor said. "And we just can't do that against a great team like this. Great first half. Then the second half we slipped off. But we need to play two halves of football."
Griffith agreed but applauded his quarterback.
"He did a phenomenal job," Griffith said of O'Connor. "And he took control at the end of the game to make sure we were able to seal the victory."

title: Ironman Maryland brings athletes back to Cambridge for 2024 race
author: Maggie Trovato
content:
Ironman Maryland brings athletes back to Cambridge for 2024 race

 September 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Maggie Trovato | Section: Local News 
 
 672
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — As the overall second place finisher of the 2024 Ironman Maryland Emmanuel Lopez walked from the finish line toward a 12-pack of beers, athletes running in the race shouted their congratulations to him."You came flying by me, and I was like, I want to be you," one runner said to him while she was in the midst of the final leg of the race, a 26.2-mile journey.
"See, that's what I mean by inspiring," Lopez said as athletes congratulated him. "It makes you want to do more."
On Saturday, a sea of athletes, along with their family and friends, descended on Cambridge for the annual Ironman event. Participants completed a 2.4-mile swim in the Choptank River, a 112-mile bike ride through Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge and a marathon that ended at Long Wharf Park.
In the overall men's category, Matthew Tatum came in first place at 8 hours, 38 minutes and 12 seconds. Lopez and Hugues Abram finished in second and third place, respectively. In the overall women's category, Jill Jacinth placed first in 9 hours, 55 minutes and 43 seconds. Carly Zanatta and Dana Glodek placed second and third, respectively.
For Lopez — who finished the race in 8 hours, 46 minutes and 23 seconds, landing him first place in the men's age 35 to 29 category — its the hard work that goes into an Ironman that creates a real camaraderie among racers.
"I mean you appreciate the hard work that everybody out here is putting in," he said. "So that kind of brings us together."
This was Lopez's 19th Ironman, but his first in Cambridge. He said he had never placed first in his age group or finished second overall in a full Ironman before this race. The Mission, Texas native will be traveling to Kailua-Kona, Hawaii for the Ironman World Championship.
Lopez called the Cambridge course beautiful, admiring the cooler weather and greenery.
"In south Texas we don't have a lot of trees and green," he said.
Matthew Tatum, who was the first place finisher of the race and placed first in the mens 40-44 age category, said with something like 24 full Ironmans under his belt, the Cambridge course is his favorite.
"This community is incredible," he said.
After finishing the race, Tatum talked about a recent bike accident that resulted in multiple broken bones and a punctured lung. His word of the day was "phoenix," the mythological bird that rises to life from its own ashes.
"Persistence and 'anything is possible' really pays off," he said.
Easton residents Ryan Levin and Casey Brasington, who volunteered in the race, watched Tatum cross the finish line. This was the couple's first year volunteering, but they have watched the race from the sidelines before. Both of them enjoy the atmosphere.
"Every family member that's out here makes me cry almost," Brasington said before Levin recalled a family of about 40 coming out last year to support a racer who was running for family members they had lost the year before.
"There's so many emotions," Levin said.
Levin hopes to compete in the Ironman within the next two years. He said he has run a marathon and has biked a century, which is 100 miles.
Jaime Ferns and her mother-in-law-to-be Mary Pat Kiessling were two of the many supporters cheering from the sidelines of the race on Saturday. Ferns' fiancé Joseph Kiessling, Mary Pat's son, participated in the race with his father Brian Kiessling.
This is the father-son duo's second full Ironman, Ferns said.
"They started doing it 2019 when an Ironman came to their hometown in Michigan, where Joseph is originally from and Brian lives," said Ferns, who is from the Washington, D.C., area.
Ferns said she loves seeing all the people and the excitement at the races. She said she's "in awe" of the athletes.
"Tomorrow's going to be rough, I think," she said about recovery for Joseph. "But it's worth it."
Marci Goldberg, who has finished three Ironmans herself, came out to Cambridge to cheer on friends.
"Because no matter how many times you've done it, it's a tough day and you need that encouragement," she said.

title: Mautz' first goal proves to be game-winner for Saints
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Mautz' first goal proves to be game-winner for Saints

 September 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 708
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Johnny Mautz hadn't played high school soccer before this season.Judging by the celebration he triggered midway through Tuesday night's second half, his St. Michaels High teammates are elated he decided to give the game a go this season.
Ethan Royer crossed a ball that Mautz converted into what proved to be the game-winning goal, as the Saints rallied from a halftime deficit to notch a 3-2 victory over Class 1A rival and previously unbeaten Colonel Richardson.
"I was playing baseball for awhile but I just stopped playing last year," said Mautz, a standout on the Saints' basketball team. "I never played soccer 'cause I didn't want to play three sports. But I said I might as well come out because I was only playing one sport (basketball). And then the rest is history."
There was also a touch of history attached to Mautz' score.
"That was his first goal of the year," St. Michaels head coach Pat Hambleton said of Mautz. "He's hit the post six times."
That strike with 21 minutes, 9 seconds remaining not only capped a three-goal, second-half surge, giving St. Michaels a 3-1 lead, but it also afforded the Saints (3-2 overall, 2-1 North Bayside) the breathing room they needed to weather Colonels' late-game push.
Not quite 4 minutes after having a goal erased by an offsides call, Colonel (4-1, 2-1) took a 1-0 lead on Aydan Downie's unassisted tally with 9:42 left in the first half.
St. Michaels' best chance to pull even came with just under 2 minutes to go in the first half, when Miles Fox put a shot right on Colonel keeper Cohen Carels, who made a midsection stop.
The Saints pulled even though just 1:26 into the second half, when Sherwin Mendez parked a direct kick into the back of the net for a 1-all tie.
"I think their free kick a minute and a half into the second half definitely gave them some momentum," Colonel head coach Dillon Shaheen said. "And they took that and ran with it."
Not quite 10 minutes later, Fox got deep on the left wing and steered a crossing pass that Connor Wheeler banged into the net for a 2-1 St. Michaels lead.
"Their sweeper was playing a little too far back I noticed," Hambleton said. "He was solely intercepting through balls, so I just made a small adjustment, where once he left for that through ball, I had a forward there, and it happened to be Connor. So he left, peeled off to Miles. Miles received and played that ball across, and it was wide open in the front of the net. It was just a good momentum boost that we needed to start the half."
Less than 8 minutes later, Royer slid a pass from the left side through the crease to the right post and a waiting Mautz for a 3-1 lead.
"I've been working on staying back post so that I can get whatever comes my way," Mautz said. "And Ethan played me a beautiful ball and I was just right there for the lefty finish."
Colonel wasn't quite finished though.
With 15:06 remaining, St. Michaels was called for a handball in the box. Colonel's Angel Castro Rios calmly deposited the penalty kick to the left of St. Michaels keeper Lucas Greenwood to make it a one-goal difference.
With Colonel continuing to push into the Saints' end, Hambleton dropped his team into defensive mode. St. Michaels foiled rushes and generally got in the way over the final 12 minutes, with Colonel's best chance for the equalizer coming with 6:37 left, when Greenwood smothered a loose ball near the left post in front of a charging Downie.
"Energy. They definitely came out a little more ready than we were, and we talked to them about that at halftime," Shaheen said. "I think they wanted the ball more it seemed. We match up pretty well with them, and they know they match up well with us. What it usually comes down to is which ever team plays harder, and they were definitely that team."
NORTH CAROLINE 8 CAMBRIDGE-SD 0
CAMBRIDGE — Omar Marroquin had a hat trick as the Bulldogs earned their first win of the season.
North Caroline (1-4, 1-2) also got goals from Mason Shilling, Adrian Lopez Rivera, Brayden Boarts, Karson Hollingworth and Jimmy Cohoon.

title: Yost's hat trick paces Bucs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Yost's hat trick paces Bucs

 September 26, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 700
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — It took Kent Island High's field hockey team some time to adjust to life without graduated standout Megan Carpenter last year.Without Carpenter — who was seemingly everywhere on the field — the Bucs dropped their first three games, and were outscored 8-7 through their opening five games.
That has not been the case this season.
Kent Island showed its strength on offense, defense and at the midfield Thursday, as Willow Yost notched her first hat trick of the season and Ellie Burnside totaled three assists to fuel a 4-1 victory over Crisfield at Andy Schipul Stadium.
"We don't really have a superstar," Bucs head coach Laura Harding said after her team improved to 4-1. "We are a very, very balanced team. And I think last year we lost Megan and it took us a little while to figure it out because she did everything for us. She was on defense. She was on offense. She was distributing the ball all over the field. Everywhere.
"So it just took us a little while last year to figure it out, which is why I think we were way stronger at the end of the year," added Harding of a team that won eight of its last 11 games. "And we have a lot of girls on this team that play year round."
Harding may have felt she was watching last year's slow start during Thursday's first half, as the Buccaneers and Crabbers (3-2) were tied at 1-1.
"I just felt like we were a little flat in the first half and it just took us a while to get going," Harding said. "Yes, we have a very strong mid(field) and a very strong D. So that's nice. But then we just have to work on getting it in the cage, which we did the rest of the game. We were just flat in the beginning."
Yost gave Kent Island a 1-0 lead with 55 seconds remaining in the first quarter, when she scored off Sadie Latchaw's assist. Crisfield struggled to get the ball past Kent Island's midfield through the first quarter and into the second. But with 3:43 left in the half, Emily Engle set up Mya Pendry's tying goal off a corner.
"That was a beautiful goal that Crisfield had on that corner," Harding said. "The passing was gorgeous. So kudos to them."
Just a 1:20 later though, Parker Tengwall scored off the first of Burnside's three assists. Tengwall just missed giving Kent Island a two-goal halftime lead when she clanged a shot off the left post with less than a minute left in the half.
The Bucs had three corner opportunities to the Crabbers' two in the third quarter, before Burnside set up Yost's second goal for a 3-1 lead with 5:08 to go in the third.
"We kept turning over the ball and we kept passing it to the other team," Yost said of Kent Island's early struggles. "But then after the first half we definitely connected better."
The Burnside-to-Yost combination connected again with a little over 9 minutes remaining off a corner that widened Kent Island's cushion to 4-1.
"I definitely think her being in an offensive mid and me in the center, it works really well together," Yost said of her scoring connection with Burnside.
Yost thought there was a tendency for the Bucs to crowd one side of the field last season instead of spreading out. That appears to have been fixed this early season, as the Bucs have outscored their first five opponents, 13-3.
"I think we have a couple things to clean up," Harding said. "We've been working on both circles. Like I don't think that goal should have happened. And I don't the one against Parkside should have happened. So we have to work.
"But the middle of our field is solid," Harding continued. "We just have to work on finishing on the offensive end and not letting those goals in. But way better start than last year."
QUEEN ANNE'S 4 J.M. BENNETT 1CENTREVILLE — Aly Edwards had one goal and an assist, and goalie Cassidy Alexander stopped two shots as the Lions won their fourth straight.
Haley Cole, Jamie Baldwin and Jolie Leager had one goal apiece for Queen Anne's (4-1) and Ava Fields had an assist.

title: O'Connor's big day leads Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
O'Connor's big day leads Easton

 September 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 723
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The message didn't surface until after the game.Easton High head football coach Matt Griffith brought up that little note, saying how some Kent Island players had sent an Instagram screen shot to Warrior quarterback Mikey O'Connor earlier this week.
"They sent it to us," Griffith said. "It said, 'Come out and support Kent Island. It's Gavan (Henry), their quarterback, against Kevin's brother.'"
Well, Kevin O'Connor's younger brother had quite the night.
Mikey O'Connor rushed for a career-high 250 yards, including three touchdowns, and threw for 146 yards and a pair of TDs Friday, as Easton defeated Kent Island, 43-24, in a battle of Bayside Conference unbeatens.
"He's a really good player," Kent Island head coach Zach Davis said of Mikey O'Connor, the third O'Connor brother to play quarterback at Easton. "And they use him well; running and passing. He's a load."
O'Connor proved to be just that, scoring on runs of 5, 1 and 4 yards to help the Warriors (4-0) build a 21-10 halftime lead.
That lead stood until late in the third quarter, when Kent Island's Jaxon Hess raced 25 yards around right end for an apparent touchdown. But that score was erased when the Buccaneers (3-1) were called for holding. Four plays later, Kent Island punted the ball to the Easton 1.
The Warriors pieced together a 10-play, 99-yard drive that ended with O'Connor hitting Chase Raab for a 24-yard touchdown. Dominic Stanco's point-after boot made it 28-10 with 8:49 remaining in the game.
"That was huge," said Griffith of Kent Island having a score taken away before the Warriors lengthened their advantage to 18. "We talked about trying to finish. And I think that's the biggest thing. We've focused all week long on execution and finishing the game. And I thought tonight we did."
Kent Island came right back, as Henry hit Jackson Towers for a 64-yard touchdown pass that — together with Spencer Chappell's PAT — pulled the Bucs within 28-17 with 6 minutes left.
But Easton sealed the win when it scored two touchdowns in 58 seconds.
O'Connor found a wide-open Diontaye Copper for a 16-yard touchdown pass, then snagged a high snap from center and hit Raab with a two-point conversion pass for a 36-17 lead with 3:31 to go in the game. Kent Island fumbled on its next play from scrimmage, giving the Warriors possession at the Bucs' 27. Three plays later, Jordan Horsey bulled through the middle for an 11-yard touchdown with 2:23 remaining. Stanco's PAT made it 43-17.
"We gave up a late touchdown, but besides that, they only gave up three points in the first half," Griffith said of his defense. "The defense responded late in the second. That was key. Coming out in the third quarter and stopping them. Then we stalled and it was a defensive game most of the (scoreless) third quarter. Then we got back on track offensively and that's was good to see."
Easton drove 87 yards on its first possession to take a 7-0 lead on O'Connor's 5-yard touchdown run around left end.
The Warriors forced a Bucs' three-and-out, and had moved back into Kent Island territory, when Hess intercepted O'Connor in the left flat and sprinted 55 yards for a touchdown. Chappell's PAT forged a 7-7 tie with 5:40 left in the first quarter.
The game remained close. O'Connor scored on a 1-yard run, but Stanco's extra-point attempt was blocked, giving the Warriors a 13-7 lead with under 3 minutes left in the first quarter.
Kent Island shaved that lead to 13-10 just 53 seconds into the second quarter, when Chappell hammered a 38-yard field goal.
Easton responded with O'Connor's 4-yard touchdown run and a two-point pass to Colin Mooney for a 21-10 halftime lead.
"Good football team," Davis said of Easton. "Definitely a physical football team. We weren't as physical as we needed to be tonight. And we had some big plays taken away by penalties."
Henry fired his second touchdown pass with 43.2 seconds left in the game when he hit Isaiah Diaz for a 29-yard score.
"We've got work to do obviously," Davis said.
O'Connor said the same thing of Easton.
"I thought this win was big for us. Kind of a like statement," said O'Connor, who leads Easton into another battle of unbeatens next Friday at defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur. "I feel like I played all right. But I could have done a lot of things better."

title: Talbot Mentors' Golf Classic takes its cause to the field
author: Veronica Fernandez-Alvarado
content:
Talbot Mentors' Golf Classic takes its cause to the field

 September 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Veronica Fernandez-Alvarado | Section: News

 EASTON — On Monday morning, dozens of people made their way to the golf field with excitement to support Talbot Mentors through competitive spirit and good sportsmanship.The Talbot Mentors Golf Classic, hosted at Links Perry Cabin in St. Michaels, aimed to raise funds, introduce sponsors and attract potential mentors for the organization, which seeks to empower young people through mentorship.
Kentavius Jones, executive director for Talbot Mentors, said the event aimed to recruit 18 foursomes, golfers competing in teams of two using only one ball per team. To his excitement, the event had rallied about 30 foursomes, far exceeding his initial expectation.
"We were successful in not only bringing folks out to go enjoy themselves for a day, but they got to learn about Talbot Mentors, what we do and other ways to get involved with our organization," Jones said.
According to Jones, the event was a major learning experience for him. Jones, who had never put on an event like this before, is not an experienced golfer, but he saw an opportunity to provide a fun experience to people who were looking for ways to support the organization.
Dan Morris, an attendee of the event and local golfer, said he had a great time and appreciated the opportunity to support a cause while playing a game he enjoys. Additionally, he had fun networking with other professionals in the area.
"I got to support a great cause and got a chance to play on the renovated course that a lot of local golfers don't get to play on," Morris said. "So I know that was a shared sentiment amongst a lot of the people that were playing there."
According to Jones, the atmosphere of the event was electric. He was happy for the success of the event and the help of the staff and team from the Links Perry Cabin.
Sponsors for the event included Al and Eleanor Smith, Shoregate Partners, Kelly Benefits and Doc's Sunset Grille, among others.
"At the end of the day, all the work, all the planning, all the energy put into the event was to yield some funding to help continue the work of just cultivating meaningful relationships between adults and youth," Jones said.

title: Lions show grit; Vikings off to fast start
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions show grit; Vikings off to fast start

 October 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 623
 Words

 Queen Anne's County High isn't the fastest or strongest football team in the Bayside Conference.But four games into the season, the Lions are playing with a longtime program staple — grit.
"They're gritty," head coach Brian Mooney said after Queen Anne's — playing its first home game of the season — evened its record last Friday night with a 20-15 victory over James M. Bennett. "There's no quit on this team. We're not going to quit at any point. Adversity struck and they smiled back and we ended up pulling it out."
Adversity has been stalking the Lions since the beginning of the season.
Starting right tackle Elijah Goldsborough went down during a Week 1 loss at Stephen Decatur. Starting quarterback Lance Arnold suffered a season-ending injury on the final drive of a Week 2 setback at Chesapeake-Anne Arundel.
Despite those two injuries, Queen Anne's notched its first win of the season Sept. 19 with a 24-0 shutout of Wicomico.
But the Lions lost two more starting pieces on offense. Starting left tackle and team captain Nathan Mayoral got injured last week in practice. Then Drew Sutton, who starts at center and defensive tackle, got injured during Friday's win over the Clippers.
"We're shuffling some guys around for sure," Mooney said.
Junior Gannon Brown, who was getting limited playing time, has taken over for Goldsborough at right tackle. Levi Frank has stepped into Mayoral's spot on the left side. And Ethan Wheaton is at center.
"We're getting back to playing Queen Anne's football," Mooney said. "We're going to line up and punch you in the teeth. It's a next-man-up philosophy and hats off to (assistant) coach (Donny) Graef doing his job on the offensive line. We've had four different starting combinations on our line now in the last four weeks. We're just trying to get some consistency there."
Then there is sophomore quarterback Carter Hercher, who on Friday carried nine times for 58 yards that included a 3-yard touchdown run and a QB sneak for the two-point conversion.
"He was a DB (defensive back) at the beginning of the season and we flipped him into the quarterback role," Mooney said of Hercher.
The Lions got a huge performance from running back John Connolly, who carried 27 times for 147 yards, including touchdowns runs of 18 and 8 yards. Hunter Kelly had 56 yards rushing on six touches, and Parker Whiteford logged eight tackles.
UNBEATEN VIKINGSCambridge-South Dorchester on Friday pushed its record to 4-0 for the first time since 2014 with a 23-0 shutout of Colonel Richardson.
"To be fully honest I didn't expect us to shut 'em out," Vikings first-year head coach Rob Burnham said. "I hoped to slow them down. I was very pleased with our defensive performance. I know the weather played a role in that, but our kids responded to the challenge that was laid before them, and I'm very pleased with the result."
The second half was played in a heavy rain, but Cambridge-SD had already built a big enough lead at that point.
Sterling Perkins racked up 175 yards rushing on 14 carries that included first-quarter 73-yard touchdown romp. The Vikings fattened their lead in the second quarter, as senior quarterback Anthony Hughes hit Antonio Blueford with a 44-yard touchdown pass. Hughes later scooped a fumble and returned it for a touchdown, then ran in the two-point conversion on a bobbled snap from center. Taybrion Watts had a safety for the Vikings' other points.
"Our kids are playing really hard," Burnham said of his team's 4-0 start. "They bought into what I asked them to do. They're very coachable. They're doing the little things right for the most part, and they recognize where we have deficiencies and we've made improvements. We've tried to get better each and every time we touch the field."

title: Queen Anne's outlasts Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's outlasts Easton

 October 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 897
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Queen Anne's County High's field hockey team doesn't have a goalie competition.It has a goalie luxury.
Longtime head coach Shana Corder can rotate senior Cassidy Alexander and junior Caroline Kimball throughout regulation play. But when it comes to defending a penalty stroke, Alexander draws the assignment. And when the game pushes into one vs. one play, Kimball knows it's her turn to step into the cage.
Ellee McLean and Jordan Bilbo each scored on their one vs. one chances, and Kimball allowed Easton nothing on four opportunities Tuesday afternoon, boosting Queen Anne's to a 1-0 victory over the Warriors in a game that felt more like a Class 2A regional playoff clash.
"It was a great game," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, after her team slipped to 4-3 overall, 1-1 North Bayside.
It was a game that featured strong defensive play by both teams, and huge stops by goalies on both sides.
Queen Anne's (6-1, 3-0), which hasn't lost since losing a one vs. one showdown at Pocomoke to open the season, rotated their goalies during regulation play, with Alexander playing the first and third quarters, and Kimball the second and fourth.
Alexander, registered her 100th career save with 7 minutes, 25 seconds remaining in the third quarter, when she dove to her left to smother a shot on an Easton penalty corner. Just 33 seconds later, Alexander laid flat out to foil another Warrior scoring bid, to keep the game a scoreless stalemate.
"I just thought about my team," said Alexander, when asked if save No. 100 was weighing on her mind. "We have an extremely intense team and they always are willing to give 110 percent. So when it comes to my end, it's just my job to pick up the scraps and do my job to help us win that game. And I think I definitely played a part in that."
Alexander, who finished with eight saves, played both 10-minute overtime periods, and foiled Easton's Addie Knox on the doorstep 1:38 into the first OT.
Just a freshman, Easton goalie Taylor Bowen turned away everything that came her way, and produced her biggest save at the end of the second overtime, when she denied McLean in the closing seconds.
"She is incredible," Neff said of Bowen, who finished with four saves. "Her footwork. She's really fast. She can see the field. She's great at communicating with her defense. And for a freshman who just came into the position, we're very impressed."
The game remained scoreless after two overtimes, pushing the game into one vs. one play. Each team selected five players, with each one having 10 seconds to try and score.
Kimball, who did not register a save in regulation, made three one vs. one stops, charging from the cage, flopping onto the ground while waving her stick to make deflections and foil every Easton attempt.
"She's more dynamic that me," Alexander said of Kimball when it comes to one vs. ones. "She's really good at just staying with the girl. She's incredible. She's like my little sister. I always had trust in her."
The first shooter in the game's deciding segment, McLean moved toward Bowen, stopped and made a quick circle before sending a shot into the right corner of the cage for the game's first goal.
Olivia Orrell's was Easton's first shooter, but with Kimball coming out to challenge her, never got a shot off in the 10-second limit.
Jordan Bilbo gave Queen Anne's a 2-0 lead when she steered another ball into the right side of the cage.
Kimball again came out to cut down the angle on Easton's No. 2 shooter, Maedy Leitzer, who could not find the cage.
"Definitely not my first shootout," Kimball said. "Whenever I do go into something like that I really just try to focus on what's happening in front of me. And just like, try and see what I can do to like counteract what they're trying to do. Fortunately, they had a couple of balls come at me, and that's when I swiped it away or kicked it. That was me counteracting. Most of the time I just trying to run down the time so that they have less time to score."
Queen Anne's last two shooters, Haley Cole and Ava Fields, were unable to cushion the Lions' advantage. But Kimball dove to her left to deflect Myka Motovidlak's bid, then flopped to her left again to get a piece of Addie Knox's shot, that skidded left of the cage, bringing Queen Anne's players onto the field to mob Kimball.
"Caroline knows she's our shootout goalie," Corder said. "Cassidy is better at saving strokes and Caroline is better at one v. ones. And these two girls work so well together. So Cassidy's like, 'Yes, put her in (in one v. ones). She's better at that.' So if I get a stroke call and Cassidy's on the sideline, I sub my goalie in because Cassidy's better. I'm so blessed that I have the ability to do that off the bench. In my career, that's never happened.
"And it makes the girls believe in both of them," Corder continued. "So they're confident no matter who's back there. Whether it's Cassidy the first half and then Caroline, they're totally confident with their goalies. Both are excellent leaders back there. I just couldn't be more proud of them because honestly they're literally keeping us in it."
Queen Anne's finished with 11 corners to Easton's 10.

title: Bennett blanks Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bennett blanks Queen Anne's

 October 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 751
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Mike Kern tried stopping them before they started."Don't hang your heads," Queen Anne's County High's girls head soccer coach instructed his players after Monday night's 3-0 loss to James M. Bennett.
Though the defending Bayside Conference-champion Clippers had ended the Lions' five-game winning streak, Kern was encouraged by what he saw.
"It's great playing against good competition," said Kern, whose team had outscored its last five opponents 29-0. "I thought we played well."
Queen Anne's (5-2) had also come within inches of playing even with Bennett (7-0) until late in the second half.
Chloe Sharp sent a header wide right midway through the first half. Shannon Rath unloaded a rocket into the left side of the net less than a minute later, but it was waved off because it came on an indirect kick.
"We had our chances," Kern said.
And the Lions would create more chances.
But it was the Clippers who were able to finish their opportunities.
The first of those came with 15 minutes, 41 seconds left in the first half, when a Bennett corner kick slipped behind Queen Anne's keeper Bea Holthaus. Queen Anne's Ava Bouch converged on the ball between Bennett's Gracie Core and Isabella Wieland. But Core, a freshman striker, arrived at the ball first, and poked the game's first score in with her left foot.
"We had two breakdowns," Kern said. "One on the corner kick; we really didn't go to the ball well. The ball bounced around the middle and they snuck it in. It was unfortunate, but we've got to do a better job of winning the ball there."
Bennett widened its lead to 2-0 with 4:43 left in the first half, as Riley Matthews gained possession, came down left wing, and angled a hard shot that eluded Holthaus' lunge before settling into the right side of the goal.
"We shoot on sight," Bennett head coach Ed O'Leary said. "When we get in front of the goal, when we get a chance, we get on target a lot. And that's what I think the difference was."
The Lions just missed trimming that two-goal deficit with 3:10 remaining in the first half, when Sharp unloaded a drive that banged off the crossbar, but fell just in front of the goal line.
Sharp rang yet another ball off the crossbar 50 seconds into the second half.
Holthaus kept it a two-goal game, stopping a Matthews' shot from left wing 3 minutes into the second half, then tracking a 30-yard direct kick for another save less than 2 minutes later.
Madi Horny had Queen Anne's two last scoring chances, angling a ball from right wing toward the left post that Valenzano smothered with 18:20 left. Valenzano stopped yet another Horney chance a little more than 3 minutes later.
"We got to score against good teams," Kern said. "We've got to get the ball in the back of the net. We were creating some opportunities, but we got to finish."
Matthews finished yet another chance with 6:28 remaining, when she got a thru pass from Core, broke down the left side alone against Holthaus and parked a shot into the left side for a 3-0 lead.
"That's what we can't have," Kern said of Matthews' breakaway. "We've got to keep them in front, and that's kind of what we stress. We did a good job with that most of the game except for that one play.
"But at the end there we pushed Shannon (Rath) up," Kern said. "We had some opportunities. We were attacking and had a lot of momentum going. And then they got that one little breakaway that sealed the game for them."
The three-goal victory was the Clippers' narrowest margin of victory this season, matching their 4-1 win over Kent Island on Sept. 16. Bennett had outscored its other five opponents, 40-1.
"We've kind of had an easy start," O'Leary said. "Kent Island was a tough game for us, but this was our big test. We were looking forward to it. Teams coached by coach Kern, they're always physical and they're always skillful and they're motivated. So for us to come out here and win this. ... I think 3-0 is a bit flattering, but it was a good tough game and we needed it.
"It's going to do us a world of good going forward," O'Leary added. "Just proud. They pinned us back into our half a few times and we stood tall and we played hard and we didn't concede a goal and got through. Some days it's your day, and some days it's not. Today was our day."

title: Jousting championship held at Tuckahoe
author: Tom McCall
content:
Jousting championship held at Tuckahoe

 October 2, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Tom McCall | Section: Local News 
 
 514
 Words 

 Read News Document

 QUEEN ANNE — The announcer called into the microphone, "charge fair maiden" as John Philip Sousa's rousing military march "Stars and Stripes Forever" echoes across the track.Maidens and knights charged on their steeds at Eastern Shore Jousting Association's 55th Annual Championship Tournament on Sept. 29. The competition took place at the the Tuckahoe Equestrian Center.
The event began with the American Flag waving above a rider's head as she circled the track. When she stopped, everyone young and old took off their hats and placed their hands over their hearts for the National Anthem.
Riders then competed, spearing tiny white rings with a lance while riding on galloping horses. Competition and skill levels included leadline, novice, amateur, semi-pro and professional classes. With each advancing class, the rings get smaller. The big ones are 1 ¾ inches and the small ones are ¾ inch in diameter.
The victorious jousters were Karen A. Callahan for leadline, Kaja Lyons for novice and Michaella Patrick for semi-pro.
This sport is just as much about the horse's training as it is about the skill of the rider.
"I ride on an inch and quarter ring for my class, but I ride with the professional class a lot, which is an inch. Last weekend I rode off a professional rider all the way down to the size of an inch and won," said Patrick, a fourth generation rider is from Port Deposit.
She travels with her horse Sally in a trailer all over the place for her sport. At her level, the horses are at a full gallop, but the leadliners are much slower. They are walked through the course on a rope by a helper. These participants tend to be younger and are the future of Maryland's oldest sport.
Although Patrick is a fierce competitor, she lends her horse to the six year olds so they try to get a ring or two.
"We have limited membership because of age. Those that have kids are involved with other sports. Right now it is hard to have a horse. Economy-wise it is expensive. It is expensive to do jousting," Callahan said.
The sport tends to be generational. One of the founding members, Dorsey Wooters, now has the pleasure of watching his grandkids compete.
"Its tradition. Some of my family members have jousted. I was a member of St. Joseph's Church in Cordova and the first Wednesday of August every year, we were at church for jousting. It is truly a family sport," Callahan said.
The competitors Sunday had to earn their spots in the championship tournament.
"They have to qualify. They have to provide a certain amount of tournaments to ride and be a member. Everybody is tickled to win, but we kind of wrap the season up with a covered dish. I made lasagna and ham, and we will get some Royal Farms chicken. You can't lose with that," said Diane Sherwood, president of the Eastern Shore Jousting Association.
When the riding was complete, everybody gathered around the announcer's hut. There were medals, trophies and flower wreaths given out with a formal, knightly bow. Then, the competitiors gathered to feast together.

title: Queen Anne's sweeps past Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's sweeps past Easton

 October 2, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 616
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The view from college to the high school game has been somewhat of a transition for Jamie Leventry."The growth of the players at the high school level is fun to see. We can really see it," said Leventry, Queen Anne's County High's first-year head volleyball coach, who last year was coaching at Washington College. "When I was in college, you really had to grind hard on some players to get them to have basically incremental improvements, whereas here, every week we get better. And it's a lot of fun to be back doing that."
Two nights after an emotional victory over Kent Island, the Lions registered their seventh sweep of the season Wednesday, grinding their way past Easton, 25-23, 25-20, 25-15 to remain unbeaten.
"We played so hard on Monday and it really took a lot out of us," Leventry said of Queen Anne's 3-1 victory over Kent Island, leaving the Lions (8-0 overall) alone in first place atop the North Bayside Division at 7-0. "Even at practice (Tuesday) we were a little sluggish. But we pushed through. It wasn't pretty but we pushed through."
Queen Anne's appeared ready to answer their coaches plea for a fast start when it built a 6-2 lead in Game 1. But a kill by Easton's Sofia Stecher-Roberts pulled the Warriors (3-5, 2-5) even at 9-9. Stecher-Roberts tapped down a kill and converted two service points to give Easton a 15-11 lead. Three times Queen Anne's rallied to tie before a block by Elizabeth Darling pushed the Lions in front at 21-20.
The Warriors took a 23-22 lead on a Lions' mishit. But a Bianca Baker kill and two errant Easton returns sealed Game 1 for the Lions.
Easton took an early lead in Game 2 behind Sacoya Williams' four-point service run, which included an ace. But Marylee Kline's six-point run from the service line nudged Queen Anne's to an 8-6 lead. The match would be tied five times before Baker hammered a winner that gave the Lions a lead they never surrendered at 17-16. And though Alli Dill's back-to-back winners clinched the 25-20 victory for Queen Anne's in the second game, Easton first-year head coach Scott Walstrum was pleased with his team's play.
"My big concern was that we'd lose focus mid-set and they didn't," Walstrum said. "We've been getting to mid-set and the bottom has been falling out. But tonight the girls played all the way through.
"Queen Anne's is a great team, and a lot of teams can be intimidated by that," Walstrum added. "But our girls had nothing to lose and they put everything out there, and I couldn't be more proud. They played all the way to 25."
Game 3 featured only one tie — that coming at 1-1 — as Queen Anne's steadily built a lead before the Warriors sent a return into the net to complete the 10-point, third-set victory for the defending Bayside Conference champions.
"I think our volleyball IQ is getting higher, and we're serving and passing well," Leventry said of a team that again features heavy hitters Sydney Pinder and Baker. "Then the others can contribute as well. Libs (Liberty Ott) has had some big games for us. We've got some depth."
The Lions have the type of poise they showed last year on the way to winning the Bayside and regional titles.
"That's kind of our goal this year was really just stay at a high level; not to get too up or down," Leventry said. "Just play at a good level. And we've had some opportunities this year where we were down a little bit but still started playing at a high level and were able to come back and win. It's nice that we're there."

title: Vikings continue going back in time
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings continue going back in time

 October 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 404
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It took until the middle of the third quarter Thursday night for Cambridge-South Dorchester High's football team to get going.It's taken the Vikings a great deal longer though to reach the midway point of a season with a 5-0 record.
Down by a point with 9 minutes, 22 seconds remaining in the third quarter, Cambridge-SD closed with a flourish, scoring the game's last 39 points en route to a 46-8 victory over Kent County in Worton, giving the Vikings a 5-0 record for the first time since 2000.
"I guess our kids fell asleep on the bus and didn't wake up," Cambridge-SD head coach Rob Burnham said of his team's slow start. "We tried to get there early enough to get them ready to go. It took us being down by a point before they decided, 'Oh, maybe we should go and actually play.' And that was really frustrating for me."
Cambridge-SD led 7-0 and was driving early in the third quarter, when Kent County's Jonah Somerville intercepted Viking quarterback Anthony Hughes' pass and returned it for a touchdown. Tyrell Fennell ran in the two-point conversion, nudging the Trojans (1-4) to an 8-7 lead.
That seemed to only arouse the Vikings, who got their running game cranked up and took control.
"It took awhile," Burnham said of his offense finding its groove. "I'm not sure why, but they figured it out, and then we were able to move the ball, both passing and running. And it didn't really matter who was doing it."
Cambridge-SD amassed 379 yards rushing on 35 carries. Leading the way was Hughes, who carried 10 times for a game-high 152 yards, including touchdowns runs of 34 and 20 yards. Running back Sterling Perkins Jr. had touchdown runs of 16, 2 and 25 yards as part of his 13-carry, 132-yard effort.
William Jackson added a 36-yard touchdown run, and finished with 75 yards on eight carries. And freshman backup quarterback Nate Twilley had a 13-yard touchdown run.
"The strength of our team right now is running the football," Burnham said. "So we want to make sure that we can establish the strength of our team and continue to move forward, and do the things that we do."
Hughes was 4 of 9 passing for 32 yards, and Twilley completed both his attempts for 33 yards.
The 2000 Vikings went 10-0 during the regular season under then head coach David Bromwell before losing to Southern Garrett in the Class 1A quarterfinals.

title: Colonel ends skid in a rush
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonel ends skid in a rush

 October 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 648
 Words 

 Read News Document

 AMERICAN CORNER — James Jackson did a lot of preaching in practice this week.A whole lot of preaching.
"We've been preaching all week, the backs hitting the holes," Colonel Richardson High's head football coach said. "They've been running past the holes, or cutting out too early. So tonight they actually hit the holes and stayed in the holes, and they found green. They found a lot of green."
Ja'Zir Dickerson returned the opening kickoff 75 yards for a touchdown and Derrick Mitchell ran for three touchdowns Friday night, as the Colonels celebrated homecoming with a 56-0 shellacking of Lancaster, Virginia.
"Coach James preached to me at practice, 'You stay in the wedge on the kick return,'" Dickerson said. "He was like, 'It's going to open up.' We watched film, seen they didn't tackle very well. So they kicked it to me and I just knew I had to get in the wedge and take one home and bring the energy."
Dickerson grabbed the opening kickoff, moved upfield, then broke left and down the home sideline to give Colonel (2-3) a 6-0 lead with only 13 seconds off the clock. Morgan Demir drilled the first of his four point-after kicks.
"That's big," Jackson said of Dickerson's game-opening score. "Anytime you come out and you score right off the jump then you make a team a little nervous. Then you don't know what's coming at you.
"We set that up all week," Jackson continued. "I was watching their special teams on film and I told our guys that 'They don't stay in their lanes, and if we set it up, we can return the opening kickoff.' And we did. That definitely set the tone for the rest of the night. That brought the energy."
Colonel, which snapped a three-game losing streak, scored on all six of its first-half possessions in addition to Dickerson's opening romp.
Mitchell, who carried five times for 113 yards, scored his first touchdown from 3 yards out with 6:17 left in the first quarter. Quarterback Tarron Hammond ran in the two-point conversion for a 15-0 lead.
Hammond squeezed into the end zone on the Colonels' next possession and watched Demir convert his second PAT for a 22-0 lead after one quarter.
"They had to bring back the intensity they had in Week 1," Jackson said in reference to Colonel's 55-0 win over Washington. "And I needed the team that played Kent Island (a 38-33 loss) to play the same way tonight, but come out with a win. I think they listened. They answered the call."
Dickerson, who also finished with 113 yards rushing on just three carries, and who had a first-quarter punt return for a touchdown erased by a penalty, was sprung for a 64-yard touchdown run with 9:46 left in the second quarter. Collin Brewer bulled in for the two-point conversion and a 30-0 lead.
Colonel scored three more touchdowns in a little over 5 minutes to close the first half. Hammond hit Carter Turbitt with a 30-yard touchdown pass, Mitchell scored on a 31-yard burst around right end, and Chatydrick Pickrom seemingly moved the bulk of Lancaster's defense during an 11-yard touchdown run up the middle that gave Colonel a 50-0 halftime lead.
Mitchell scored the only touchdown of the second half when he broke loose for a 37-yard touchdown jaunt in the third quarter.
"We came out with a lot more energy and we played as a team," Mitchell said. "We blocked for each other. We did everything we were supposed to do. Great blocking."
Jackson agreed.
"They did a tremendous job tonight," Jackson said of his offensive line. "I've been looking for the o line all year. Tonight we were running as one unit. It wasn't one side here and one side there. It was everybody working for us tonight with our o line."
Colonel stopped Lancaster (2-4) six times of fourth down and forced two punts. Lancaster's other possession ended with the first-half clock running down.

 CHESTER — Owners of RS Shooting Sports Scott Gray and Robbie Frey invited the community to celebrate the business's three year anniversary and get a glimpse of the future.Joining the celebration at 110 D Country Day Rd. in Chester were coaches and student athletes from three area high schools that Gray and Frey are sponsoring as they compete in the Maryland State High School Clay Target League.
Gray and Frey set out to establish a different kind of gun shop, focused on establishing a community for the shooting sports enthusiasts in the area, and have succeeded in building a thriving business, growing steadily the past three years. Now entering its fourth year at this location, RSSS has expanded, adding a training facility for a myriad of courses.
In addition to the classes offered at the store, the shop also offers engraving services, full-service gunsmithing, on-site Cerakote services and Custom Kydex Holsters to fit any firearm. They are now running monthly classes for a number of firearms permits including the Maryland Handgun Wear and Carry Permit.
The two owners were happy to help the first Eastern Shore high school clay team — the Kent Island team is recognized as being the first public school in Maryland to join the USA High School Clay Target League and was followed soon after with the establishment of the club at Queen Anne's County High. They helped the team get established, and their commitment to the local shooting community has expanded with the introduction of a clay targets team at Easton High School.
Speaking with volunteer coach Joe Cap, he said, "we have stressed to our team that this is not just about shooting. They are required to attend and participate in community functions." Cap continued, "Just last week they attended the school board meeting, and the students provided them with an update."
In an email chat with QACHS coach Nathan Powell, he spelled out the underlying strategy, saying, "The continual development and evolution of our program is building young adults who are active in our communities and developing critical leadership skills to continue to grow and contribute beyond the high school environment."
"Additionally, we have tapped into a population of student athletes who do not always fit the traditional sports model or mold," Powell continued. "Our program has given them purpose, focus and direction that extends away from the sports environment, into the classroom, the home and the community."
Also joining in the festivities was Marine Corp recruiter Mark Winkles, who challenged guests with a chin-up challenge. Pupuseria Kent Island was on hand to feed the masses, along with tasty treats from AB Made Sweets and Treats.

title: Next-man-up approach still working for QA's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Next-man-up approach still working for QA's

 October 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 837
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It was just another weekend for Queen Anne's County High's football team.It was another game tainted by injury. Wait, make that injuries.
And yet despite losing two defensive starters and their starting quarterback, the Lions again found a way to log another victory last Friday, stretching their win streak to three with a convincing 43-6 rout of North Caroline.
"Hats off to our defensive coordinator, coach Jude Mandes," Queen Anne's head coach Brian Mooney said after the Lions registered their most lopsided victory of the season while holding North Caroline to a season-low six points. "He does a great job of mixing up his coverages and the looks that he gives defenses. He's been really dialed in with his blitz packages as of late. He's continuing to grow just like our defense."
Also continuing to grow is the Lions' injury list.
On the first play of the game Friday, starting defensive end Conlan Nagle got rolled up on, suffering a leg injury. Amari Baynard stepped in for Nagle.
All-Bayside Conference starting safety Carter Dickey injured his arm during the second defensive series. Sophomore Alex McDonald went in for Dickey and got his first playing time of the year, and "played really well," Mooney said.
The defense got another outstanding effort from inside linebacker Parker Whiteford (10 tackles).
"They moved the ball on us pretty good that first drive, but he's just an alpha," Mooney said of Whiteford. "He's just a man-child. I don't know what else to say about the kid. It's an awesome treat to have. Him and coach Jude have a great unison and between the two of them, he's kind of like another Jude out on the field."
Mooney also praised the play of junior cornerback Wyatt Wilhoit, who finished with six tackles, including a sack, and a forced fumble.
"Kind of getting his first varsity experience, he had a great night," Mooney said of Wilhoit. "Had a forced fumble inside the 20 on one of their first drives, and then I think he had the game-changing play. Right before halftime they were driving (to Queen Anne's 30) and he came off the edge on one of coach's blitzes and just cracked the quarterback for about a 10-yard loss. It just kind of changed the whole momentum of the game I felt."
Queen Anne's then lost starting quarterback Carter Hercher, who got hurt while attempting a pass in the third quarter.
Before getting injured, Hercher had completed 6 of 7 passes for 104 yards, and carried three times for 11 yards.
The Lions didn't stall though, moving sophomore Ja'Dereon Thompson behind center in the wildcat formation. Thompson finished the game with touchdown runs of 25 and 40 yards as part of a six-carry, 92-yard rushing effort, and caught two passes for 62 yards.
"We call it the flashback with Ja'Dereon, and we've been practicing that just in case something like that happened," Mooney said. "And he went in and we didn't miss a beat."
Senior running back John Connolly also didn't miss a beat, as he carried 16 times for 190 yards, with touchdown runs of 1, 10 and 11 yards.
"We've been really working on his technique, some of his footwork stuff in the week leading up, and he just hit it on a tee," Mooney said of Connolly. "He was cutting really well behind the guards on power and finding that groove. He was averaging 11 yards a carry. We're going to ride our guy."
Queen Anne's hosts Kent County (1-4) for homecoming on Saturday at noon.
NO PANICDespite Friday's 38-0 loss at defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur, Easton head coach Matt Griffith doesn't see his team unraveling.
"Obviously it was not what we expected," Griffith said after the Warriors slipped to 4-1. "We expected to give them a game at least. We did early."
The Seahawks (5-0) were up 7-0, scored early in the second quarter, then erupted for three more touchdowns in the final 5:02 before halftime.
"There was a tipped ball that goes off a receiver's hands, and we had some debacles up front driving," Griffith said. "Again, good football team. They've got some great athletes. We just didn't execute our part. If we want a chance to redeem ourselves we have to play really good and redeem ourselves against them maybe in the postseason."
Easton was held to 12 rushing yards on 11 attempts, and senior quarterback Mikey O'Connor completed 7 of 20 passes or a season-low 27 yards.
"We didn't respond in a big game, big atmosphere," Griffith said. "And while Decatur's a very good football team we did not play our best football. And this game does not dictate the season. You get to dictate the rest of the season and that starts (last) Saturday morning.
Easton hosts Parkside (2-3) on Friday at 6:30 p.m.
BUCS STOPPEDThe surprise from last weekend may have been Wicomico's 21-14 upset of Kent Island on Saturday in Stevensville. Bucs quarterback Gavan Henry completed 10 of 25 passes for 122 yards and a touchdown to Jackson Towers, and running back Jaxson Hess finished with 12 carries for 44 yards and a touchdown.

title: Warriors battle but can’t extend win streak against undefeated Bennett
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors battle but can’t extend win streak against undefeated Bennett

 October 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 714
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Avery Brice was eager for Monday night."I was very excited about this game tonight just to see where we were at as far as playing against top competition," Easton High's first-year boys head soccer coach said of facing undefeated and defending Bayside Conference champion James M. Bennett.
After 80 minutes, the Warriors were where everyone else has been this season after playing the Clippers — behind on the scoreboard.
And yet despite watching Easton's four-game win streak come to a halt in a 3-0 loss, Brice was largely encouraged by what he saw from his team.
"Goals change momentum," said Brice, who watched the Clippers take a 1-0 lead, when star Noah Blankensop gained possession on left wing, and, with Easton keeper Sam Hutchison far from his goal, sent a ball drifting over everyone before settling into the right side of the net with 15 minutes, 27 seconds left in the first half. "I loved how we responded. Going down a goal sucks. Guys responded great. Better than we have previously. We get scored on and it's like, 'Wow.' You just see everyone drop. But tonight you saw guys, 'Hey come on. Next play. Let's go again.' I was really proud of them for that."
Brice was also proud of Hutchison's play in goal. The junior keeper stopped a hard shot by Blankensop in the 9th minute and made a save on Sebastien Dorvelus just a moment later to keep the game scoreless. Hutchison then made perhaps his stop of the game, when he punched away a shot that banged off the left post with 7 minutes left in the first half, keeping it a one-goal game.
"Goalie had a huge night," Brice said of Hutchison, who finished with 11 saves. "Crazy saves. One of the best games I've seen him play."
Bennett (8-0), which has beaten six of its eight opponents this season by six or more goals — the exceptions, Queen Anne's (3-0 on Sept. 19) and now Easton — looked ready to take a 1-0 lead halftime. But with just over 10 seconds remaining, Grant Ziervogel served a ball that Easton's Felix Valentin attempted to head away, only to watch it go into the net for a 2-0 Clippers lead.
"The own goal, miscommunication," Brice said. "We learn from it. Felix, he is an amazing defender and I told him, he's saved games prior to this. 'Don't even worry about it. It happens. It's part of the game.'"
The Warriors (6-2) thought they cut their deficit in half with 20:20 left in the game, when Clay Nagel, with Bennett keeper Jake Ziervogel away from the goal and two defenders on his back, caught up to a ball and touched it into the net. But the goal was waved off, when Nagel was ruled offsides.
"First competitive (game)," Bennett head coach Gabe Kane said. "First one that wasn't decided by halftime.
"We don't want 12 strolls," said Kane in reference to the Clippers outscoring their opponents, 53-2 this season. "We want to be battle tested, and Easton came at us for 80 minutes today. There was no quit in them. They seemed to play harder after the third goal. I think they had more chances at the end of the game when I know they were tired. But they kept battling."
Bennett bumped its lead to 3-0 as Grason Adkins scored from the right side of the box with 7:26 left.
Jake Ziervogel, who according to Kane has not had more than one save in a game this season prior to Monday, made a leaping stop on Ale Monroy with 6:45 left. Blankensop, who was recruited by a number of Division I schools but is headed to Salisbury University, just missed pushing the lead to 4-0 in the waning moments when he blasted a shot off the crossbar.
"I knew they were going to be our best opponent we'd play to date," Brice said. "I think we made some silly mistakes and we paid for them. But they are just minor ones. We switched off for a moment, not marking in the box, not getting and winning the second ball in the box.
"The score does not reflect how we played," Brice continued. "I think going forward, we work on finishing our chances and then just being a little more creative up top."

title: North Caroline fires head football coach
author: Bill Haufe
content:
North Caroline fires head football coach

 October 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 482
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Nic McMorris was fired Monday morning as North Caroline High's head football coach midway through his second season.The Bulldogs went 9-2 and reached the second round of the Class 2A East Region playoffs last year in McMorris' first season as head coach. The team was expected to have another strong season this year, with running backs Zymear Smith and Tyson Weber, and all-Bayside Conference defensive end Owen Piavis returning.
But the Bulldogs have struggled, falling to 0-5 after last Friday night's 43-6 loss at Queen Anne's, their most lopsided loss of the season.
McMorris said he received a phone call Monday morning from North Caroline principal Matt Spiker, who wanted to schedule a face-to-face meeting with the head coach.
"I will say he tried to have me in the office. He tried to have a face-to-face conversation," McMorris said Wednesday morning during a phone interview. "I wanted to have a conversation right then and there, so we talked on the phone. I was in St. Michaels, and I was like, 'I don't want to be thinking about this for an hour and a half.'"
McMorris said Spiker told him he was being let go as head football coach. McMorris did not say why he was let go.
Reached by phone Wednesday morning, Spiker declined to comment, referring the matter to Caroline County Public Schools public information officer Sandi Barry.
"Mr. McMorris is no longer employed by CCPS (Caroline County Public Schools), however we wish him success in future endeavors," Barry said, reading from a statement. "As with all personnel matters, we cannot provide any further information."
McMorris, 34, who is not a teacher, was North Caroline's junior varsity head coach before being named offensive coordinator for the varsity for the 2022 season. When then-head coach James McCormick stepped down after 22 seasons, McMorris was named the school's head varsity coach.
"I'm obviously disheartened and pretty upset about it," McMorris said of the decision. "But I want the kids to go out and win on (Thursday) despite me not being there."
McMorris said junior varsity head coach Heath Wilkins has been promoted to varsity head coach and will be on the sideline Thursday when North Caroline travels to play at James M. Bennett in Salisbury.
"I am genuinely happy for Heath Wilkins, who's taking over," McMorris said. "He's a fantastic coach and literally my number two. He supported me the whole time."
McMorris finishes with a 9-7 career record at North Caroline.
Wilkins, 49, who's been with North Caroline's program for more than five years, was in his third season as junior varsity head coach before his promotion. He played football at Howard High School and then played semi-pro ball for 10 years.
"It's bittersweet," Wilkins said of being named McMorris' successor. "I consider Nic a friend. It's just a bad situation, but I am excited.
"It's a high profile position, and who wouldn't be nervous," Wilkins said of beginning his first varsity head coach job.

title: SSPP defeats Herons to strengthen hold on top seed for ESIAC playoffs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
SSPP defeats Herons to strengthen hold on top seed for ESIAC playoffs

 October 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 587
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — With no seniors on her team, Saints Peter and Paul High girls head soccer coach Nicole Edsall called last season a bit of a growing year.Edsall called the beginning of this season, "a bit of a rough start" after the Sabres went 2-2 over their first four games.
Now, with just one regular-season game remaining, Edsall has seen her team grow into the No. 1 seed for the approaching Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference playoffs. Buoyed by a dominating midfield, the Sabres tightened their grip on that top spot Tuesday afternoon with a 3-1 victory over Gunston for their fourth straight win, and fifth victory in six games.
"Saints Peter and Paul has a great team," said Gunston head coach Tony D'Antonio after losing to the Sabres for the second time in five days. "They're best in the conference for sure. Saints Peter and Paul's midfield was just dominant."
Edsall has literally watched that midfield grow, especially center mids Avery McCall and Annie Albright, who she has coached since fifth grade.
"Avery is just extremely athletic, can control the field," Edsall said. "And Annie's got a ton of grit and never stops running. So Annie's usually on an offensive side and Avery really controls the back and the defensive side."
Completing that midfield are seniors Gracie Galdieri and Keely Morgan.
"For the past three years they've been kind of bouncing around," Edsall said of Galdieri and Morgan. "They found homes in the outside, running the flanks. They've done a really good job doing that. They've all grown into the positions."
That group helped keep the Sabres (7-3 overall, 7-0 ESIAC) control possession, keep play largely in the Herons' end, and limited Gunston's chances on the offensive end. Adding to Sts. Peter & Paul's midfield dominance was the fact D'Antonio had his best midfielder, senior Vee McCluskey, playing goalie.
"We need her in goal," said D'Antonio, whose team lost to the Sabres 4-0 last Friday in Centreville. "Our game plan was to kind of pack things in a bit and try to attack on the transition."
That transition game materialized only a few times compared to the Sabres' attack, which struck in the 18th minute, when Kendall Kroniser crossed a ball that Albright put away in the left side of the net. Sts. Peter & Paul scored again not quite 2 minutes later, as Eden Zimmerman sent a pass across the goalmouth to Kroniser, who tapped it in for a 2-0 lead.
Gunston (5-4-1, 5-3) came close to scoring in the fourth minute of the second half on a direct kick. But Sabres keeper Kaylin Palmer tracked the ball coming in from her right side, watched it bounce through the crease, before smothering it.
Sts. Peter & Paul, which has outscored its ESIAC competition 29-4 this season, was pushing for its fourth shutout in conference play. But with 1:27 left, Gunston's Abby Philippon unloaded a 20-yard rocket from just outside the box that found the upper right corner to make it 2-1.
"That's her thing," D'Antonio said of Philippon. "She did not get a whole lot of chances today. They did a nice job. They defended very well."
The Sabres answered quickly as Eden Zimmerman converted a pass from her sister Emery Zimmerman for a goal and a 3-1 lead just 45 seconds later.
"We had a rough start to the season, but we had a tough schedule," Edsall said. "It seemed like we were losing game after game but as soon as we started the conference it clicked. So I'm thankful for the tough start to the season."
