title: Queen Anne's extends North shutout streak
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's extends North shutout streak

 October 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 748
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton High's Dafny Vasquez is one of the North Bayside's more dynamic female soccer players.And Queen Anne's County junior center back Shannon Rath is well aware of those talents.
"I've played with Dafny most of my childhood, so I'm really close with her," said Rath, who used to play on the same club team with Vasquez. "I think because of that, I know just to contain and keep her in front of me, and don't let her get behind. Because if she gets behind you she's very dangerous."
Rath and her teammates kept a close eye on Vasquez Wednesday night, limiting the junior striker to just two shots, as the Lions, paced by Madi Horney's second hat trick of the season, shut out the Warriors, 6-0, for their eighth win in nine games.
"We just got done playing Colonel (Richardson) and they have Sadie Prettyman, who in my opinion is a very, very good soccer player, that we knew we had to be aware of her at all times," Queen Anne's head coach Mike Kern said. "So that's kind of what we did tonight.
"We didn't mark her up or anything," continued Kern, who had no specially designed defensive package just for Vasquez. "We just made sure we were aware of her when she did get the ball. We looked to double her, just contain her to keep her in front of us. And I think we did a good job doing that tonight because she is a very good player."
Two days after netting a hat trick against Cambridge-South Dorchester, Vazquez was limited to just two shots on goal. The first of those came in the 15th minute when she fired a strong shot from left wing that Queen Anne's keeper Bea Holthaus stopped. The Warrior standout wouldn't get another shot off until 15:21 remained in the game, when she booted a ball well over the crossbar.
"I think they always expect Dafny so they look for that double team on her," Easton head coach Ellie Kilmon said. "I think they did contain her pretty well. But we always expect it. It's just how they (Queen Anne's) work together as a team."
While the Lions (8-2 overall, 6-0 North Bayside) stifled Vasquez and Easton (6-4, 4-2), they also maintained their season-long shutout streak against division competition, blanking their seventh North opponent. Though Queen Anne's shut out Kent Island early in the season, it's next Wednesday's home game against the Buccaneers that counts toward in the division, and will determine the regular-season champion.
"Our defense has been great all year," said Kern, whose team has outscored its division opponents 49-0. "Bea in the goal has been great. Our defense is very, very good. We probably could score more goals if we didn't put so much effort in the defense."
The Lions put plenty of effort trying to score in the first half, but were either foiled by Warrior goalie Zelia Proa (10 saves), or launched shots over the crossbar.
"The first half we just couldn't get it in the net," Kern said. "So in the second half we did a better job of finishing."
Queen Anne's managed to get two in the net in the first half, the first coming with 6:48 remaining, when Horney set up Olivia Ryan's goal. The Lions made it 2-0 with 3:40 left, after Kara Ringold was taken down inside the box, setting up a penalty kick by Horney, whose shot glanced off Proa's fingertips and into the left side of the net.
Queen Anne's began widening its lead with 23:50 left in the game, when Rath's corner kick landed right at the feet of Horney, who tapped in her second goal.
Addison Chandler had a chance to put Easton on the board less than 3 minutes later, but her shot went over the crossbar.
Proa made two more saves midway through the second half before Rath struck a ball that was headed into the net by Horney, completing her hat trick for a 4-0 lead.
"I let the play come to me," Horney said. "I don't come into it cocky. I just do it."
The Lions tacked on two more goals, Ryan setting up Lexi Kern, who hit a beautiful chip from about 20 yards out that sailed over Proa and into the net with 10:31 to go, and Mia Bennett scoring with 6:30 left.
"I think we definitely have our ups and downs," Horney said. "But as of right now we're having our ups, and hopefully it keeps going coming into Kent Island next week."

title: Knox's penalty stroke in overtime boosts Easton past Pocomoke for first time since 2019
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Knox's penalty stroke in overtime boosts Easton past Pocomoke for first time since 2019

 October 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 684
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Addie Knox's mind went blank.And then a thought that brought clarity and fright together came crashing in.
"I don't even know what was going through my head," said Knox, who was awarded a penalty stroke after a collision with Pocomoke goalie Madison Castaneda with two minutes remaining in overtime Thursday. "It was just like, 'If I don't get this stroke and we lose to Pocomoke. ….'"
Knox converted that stroke, lifting a shot into the upper left corner of the cage before turning and running headlong into a swarm of ecstatic teammates to celebrate a 3-2 victory — Easton's first over the perennial Bayside Conference power since 2019, when Knox's older sister Kat was on the team.
"Amazing," Knox said still trying to catch her breath. "Beating Pocomoke is insane. I was just so excited and when my team piled on me it was just insane the adrenaline rush."
One week after losing in a heartbreaking shootout against Queen Anne's, Easton fell behind twice to Pocomoke in regulation.
Pocomoke (6-3) took a 1-0 lead with 3 minutes, 48 seconds remaining in the first quarter, when Audrey Pham slipped a shot past Easton goalie Taylor Bowen off a penalty corner.
Easton (6-3) pulled even as Maedy Leitzer set up Sunny Chandler's goal with 2:37 left in the second quarter.
Pocomoke sent three shots wide early in the third quarter, earned two corners, then converted on its third corner, with Chloe Holland finding the back of the cage with 3:53 to go in the period.
Easton's Olivia Orrell delivered the equalizer just 35 seconds into the fourth quarter, when she came down the right side and unloaded a tough angled shot near the end line that squeaked past Castaneda and slammed into the far side of the cage for a 2-2 tie.
"I was very, very surprised," Orrell said. "A couple plays before I tried to do the same thing and it went out of bounds. I just really like focused on my drives and staying low to the ground. I looked back at the ref and he called it and I was just like, 'Oh my God. No way.'"
Easton got three corner opportunities between the 10- and 8-minute mark of the fourth but couldn't get anything past Castaneda.
Easton had a man-advantage opportunity in the final minute of regulation, and held that advantage in the first minute of the 10-minute overtime.
Easton earned a corner early in OT, but Knox's shot was stopped by Pocomoke's Madeline Cornwell. Pocomoke couldn't capitalize on two corner opportunities.
Then with the game approaching the final two minutes of overtime, Knox carried the ball in from the left side. Castaneda came away from her crease, and in a bid to reach the ball, was ruled to have fouled Knox, setting up the penalty stroke.
"I couldn't even catch my breath when I was taking the stroke," Knox said. "I knew I was going to go where the goalie's stick was. I always lift the ball."
As Knox prepared to shoot, Castaneda raised both her arms to cover as much of the cage as possible. Knox snapped a shot that slipped under the crossbar and banged into the upper corner."
"I did not think it was going to go that high," Knox admitted. I was really scared."
Easton head coach Kim Neff wasn't.
"It was a perfect stroke," Neff said. "And we knew that she could do it. She has a great lift on the ball. So I had all the confidence in the world in her to do it. And she executed so well. I wanted to have those girls to have that feeling after that Queen Anne's loss."
Though Pocomoke still figures to be a fmajor orce in the approaching Class 1A playoffs, head coach Brandi Castaneda said her team has some work to do.
"I think our second effort definitely needs some work," Coach Castaneda said. "I was telling the girls, 'Everybody has go hard and everybody has go wrong. We can always fix the go wrongs. But the go hards are on the independent player.' I think today we felt short of a little bit of that extra tank energy that we needed."

title: Clippers rally to spoil Wilkins head coaching debut
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Clippers rally to spoil Wilkins head coaching debut

 October 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 491
 Words 

 Read News Document

 North Caroline High's football team hadn't had a start like this all season.Now, the Bulldogs have to work on finishing.
Senior wide receiver Zakai Smullen ran for two touchdowns, caught a TD pass, then threw a game-winning touchdown pass to Ja'Mareon Stevens with a little over a minute remaining Thursday night, as James M. Bennett rallied from a 15-point halftime deficit to defeat visiting North Caroline, 27-21, spoiling the head coaching debut of North Caroline's Heath Wilkins.
"There was a really good feeling out there for that first half," said Wilkins, who was named head coach after North Caroline fired Nic McMorris this past Monday. "We felt good going into the game. We knew we'd be able to compete."
The Bulldogs (0-6) weren't only competing, but leading the Clippers, 21-6, at halftime — matching the most points they had scored in an entire game all season when they lost at Easton, 28-21, in Week 3.
North Caroline's Owen Walstrum returned the opening kickoff for a touchdown. Senior quarterback Corey Bunce then threw a pair of touchdown passes to Derek Jones off play-action to help the Bulldogs to a 21-6 halftime lead.
But the Clippers rallied behind Smullen.
"We have a package of plays where we just try to get him the ball anyway we can," Bennett head coach Greg Lasinski said of Smullen. "Heckuva player. I think he's the most under recruited player in the Bayside (Conference) right now. Whatever we ask him to do he can do it. He's explosive. He's just one of those kids you're lucky to have on your team because he can flip the game in your favor in a hurry."
Smullen did just that in the second half, scoring his second rushing touchdown before hauling in a touchdown pass from Liam Nelson that pulled the Clippers within 21-19.
Smullen, who was Bennett's starting quarterback the past two years before being moved to wideout at the beginning of this season, then hit Stevens with a 15-yard touchdown pass and ran in the two-point conversion to complete the Clippers' comeback.
"I was proud of the effort in the second half," said Lasinski, his team now 3-3. "It was a resilient effort. This is my third year at Bennett, and in previous years maybe we don't come back and win that game. This group, they work hard. They came out focused in the second half and they kept fighting all the way to the end."
Despite the tough loss, Wilkins was optimistic during a Friday morning phone call.
"They haven't quit and that's all I can ask at this point," Wilkins said. "We're going to do film (Friday) and this will be my first chance to do film with these guys ,and we'll be able to see where the mistakes were and make the corrections. This is going to be a totally different team in two weeks."
North Caroline hosts defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur (6-0) next Thursday before traveling to Kent Island (3-3) on Oct. 25.

title: Bratten, Rams race past Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bratten, Rams race past Warriors

 October 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 662
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton High's football team still has a chance to earn the No. 2 seed for the Class 2A East Region playoffs.But head coach Matt Griffith knows his team has to do better than this.
Parkside running back Karontez Bratten returned the opening kickoff 80 yards for a touchdown, then ran for four more TDs Friday night, leading the Rams to a 37-30 upset of the turnover-plagued Warriors on homecoming.
"Not good," Griffith said of his team's tackling. "They've got good athletes, good running backs. We knew that coming in. You can only rep it so much in practice. It's hard when you don't have someone that's like number one (Bratten), number two (Tavian Dashiell), number zero (Canaan Mapp). They're very athletic.
"But we hurt ourself tonight," Griffith continued. "Four turnovers; three interceptions, one fumble. Missed field goal. So there's seven to eight extra possessions that we're giving a really good athletic football team. And we can't do that."
Bratten took the opening kickoff, veered right and bolted down the visiting sideline to give Parkside (3-3) a 6-0 lead with only 18 seconds off the clock. The point-after kick was blocked.
Parkside's Nazere Sturgis intercepted Easton quarterback Mikey O'Connor (13 of 27, 211 yards, two touchdowns, three interceptions) less than 2 minutes into the second quarter. Three plays later, Bratten found room around right end and was off on a 58-yard touchdown romp to make it 12-0 with 8:44 to go in the second quarter. Easton stopped the two-point conversion attempt.
The Warriors (4-2) got on the scoreboard with 4:34 left in the half, when O'Connor hit Zach Barnhart with an 18-yard touchdown pass. Dom Stanco's extra-point made it 12-7.
Bratten returned the ensuing kickoff to Easton's 27. Six plays later, Matt Kramer booted a 25-yard field goal for a 15-7 Rams lead.
Stanco missed a 25-yard attempt with 43.9 seconds left in the half. But on the next play, Easton's Jordan Horsey intercepted Parkside quarterback Chris Morandi and returned the ball 30 yards for a touchdown. O'Connor hit Colin Mooney in the left corner of the end zone for the two-point conversion and a 15-15 tie with 15.6 seconds left before the break.
But Bratten (23 carries, 248 yards) again stung the Warriors, finding a seam on the right side and blazing 74 yards for a TD and a 21-15 Rams lead at halftime.
"He's getting better every week," Parkside head coach Brendan Riley said of Bratten. "He doesn't need much room, man, and he can frickin find it and he rolls."
Parkside recovered an Easton fumble on the first play of the second half, setting up Bratten's 1-yard touchdown run. Harmon ran in the two-point conversion for a 29-15 lead with just under 10 minutes remaining in the third quarter.
The Warriors narrowed their deficit to 29-21 with 5 seconds left in the third quarter, when O'Connor swept right and slammed into the end zone with a 2-yard touchdown run. Stanco's PAT pulled Easton within 29-22.
Bratten was sprung for his fifth touchdown of the game, a 37-yard jaunt around the right side with 10:13 left in the game. Harmon handled a bad snap from center and hit Austin Townsend with a two-point conversion pass to make it 37-22.
Easton closed its deficit again, as O'Connor hit Diontaye Copper on a slant down the middle for a 38-yard touchdown play. O'Connor then connected with Carter Mooney on the two-point conversion pass, drawing Easton with 37-30 with 9:19 to go.
Parkside's running game chewed up almost 6 minutes of clock before a bad snap from center got past Morandi. Barnhart recovered for Easton at the Rams 40. But two plays later, Harmon intercepted O'Connor. The Rams picked up three first downs on the ground to bleed the game's final 3:19.
"We've got a really solid core of backs and Karontez ran his tail off. James (Harmon) ran his tail off tonight. Offensive line had a great night up front."
Notes: Parkside finished with 492 yards rushing. ... Parkside's James Harmon carried 11 times for 124 yards.

title: Thompson flirts with history as Lions roll
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Thompson flirts with history as Lions roll

 October 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1051
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Ja'Dereon Thompson knows a little about Queen Anne's County High's football history."When I was in eighth grade, KJ Smothers scored five touchdowns against Parkside one homecoming," Thompson said of the former Lions rushing standout.
After rushing for three touchdowns and passing for a fourth — all in the first half — Thompson was lobbying to get back on the field during homecoming Saturday afternoon at Lions Stadium. But with three regular-season games and at least one playoff contest still on the docket, Queen Anne's head coach Brian Mooney opted to keep his electric sophomore on the sideline.
"We told him 'We just want to get out of here healthy,'" Mooney said. "We haven't had a game yet where we've had no injuries. This was the first one that we got out of with no injuries."
The Lions not only got away injury free Saturday, but notched their second shutout of the season while extending their winning streak to four via a 45-0 victory over Kent County before a large homecoming crowd.
"He's special," Mooney said of Thompson, who started his first game at quarterback after the Lions lost starter Lance Arnold to injury in Week 2 and backup Carter Hercher to injury last week. "Four touchdowns in the first half. He wanted more, but I told him, 'Look man, we got to save you for the next game as we keep going."
Mooney's reasoning was understandable, considering the Lions (4-2) prior to Saturday had lost two quarterbacks, both starting offensive tackles, their starting center — who also started at defensive tackle — a defensive end and a cornerback all to injury.
Queen Anne's second-year head coach had most of his starters on the sideline during the second half after the Lions got off to their best start of the season, taking a 38-0 lead into the locker room.
"We talked about kind of starting fast, Mooney said. "It was something we haven't done all year. Most of the time we're like a second-half team. This time we came out in the first half and executed, and that first drive was a real long drive; took about seven or eight minutes off the clock. We pounded it down, got a touchdown out of it."
After receiving the opening kickoff, Queen Anne's ran 14 running plays covering 73 yards and eating close to 8 minutes of clock before senior John Connolly (9 carries, game-high 76 yards rushing) scored on a 2-yard run. Thompson ran in the two-point conversion for an 8-0 lead with 3:38 left in the first quarter.
Connolly gave the ball back to Queen Anne's, when he intercepted Kent quarterback Dwan Harris on the Trojans' first drive. Thompson (9 carries, 70 yards) dashed 16 yards around right end for a touchdown and Levi Frank added the point-after for a 15-0 lead with 13.2 seconds left in the first quarter.
Queen Anne's next points were set up by punter Ethan Keppler, who booted a 55-yard punt to the Trojans' 1-yard line. Two plays later, Kent's Jysir Valentine was stacked up and dropped for a safety and a 17-0 lead.
Thompson showed why he's nicknamed "Flash" on the ensuing kick, darting through traffic before getting knocked out of bounds at the Kent 16. The Trojans (1-5) looked like they might avoid a deeper deficit, but on a fourth-and-nine, Thompson, weaved his way to a 15-yard touchdown before Frank again hammered the PAT through for a 24-0 lead with 4:47 remaining in the first half.
"I think we're playing amazing," Thompson said. "With me at quarterback, it's like Lamar Jackson, and Derrick Henry with John Connolly. And then you've got the blockers. They're stepping up to play. It feels great right now. We're rolling right now."
Queen Anne's continued rolling, scoring on its next two possessions. Chance Hegedus wrestled a ball away from a defender for an 18-yard pass reception from Thompson with 3:07 left in the first half. Thompson added his third rushing touchdown with 26.4 seconds to go in the half, racing untouched around left end for a 10-yard score before another Frank PAT gave the Lions a 38-0 halftime cushion.
Parker Whiteford's 7-yard touchdown run and Frank's fifth extra-point kick pushed Queen Anne's to a 45-0 with 1:15 remaining on a running third-quarter clock.
Whiteford had a greater impact at inside linebacker, though, leading a defense that held Kent County to 49 yards rushing and 13 yards passing. Queen Anne's stopped seven of the Trojans' eight third-down attempts, forced three punts and one quick kick, had two interceptions, recovered a fumble, and foiled Kent's one fourth-down attempt.
"Defensively, I think we've been locked in all year long," Whiteford said of a unit that since giving up 35 points in a season-opening loss to defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur — the Seahawks' lowest point total of the season so far — has yielded an average of just 7.4 points a game and notched two shutouts. "We're going out there doing our jobs. Coach Jude (Mandes) puts us in a good spot to keep growing and be good."
Whiteford attended DeMatha last year, where he played early in the season but saw limited duty after the starting linebacker he replaced returned.
"I'm real happy to be back," said Whiteford, who finished with nine tackles, three for losses against the Trojans. "This is the most fun I've had ever playing football. I love playing in front of my home crowd. It's amazing."
Notes: Alex McDonald had Queen Anne's second interception, picking off Harris in the third quarter. … Tyrel Fennel led Kent County with 54 yards on eight carries. … Queen Anne's hosts Easton (4-2) on Thursday at 6 p.m., while Kent County welcomes Washington (0-6).

title: Orrell's overtime goal lifts Warriors over Kent Island in thriller
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Orrell's overtime goal lifts Warriors over Kent Island in thriller

 October 15, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 730
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — Addie Knox paused.Easton High's sophomore midfielder stood on the end line 4 minutes deep into overtime preparing to deliver an entry pass on a penalty corner, when she asked her teammates aligned inside the circle's fringe, "What are we doing?"
Less than a moment later, Knox had her answer: scoring.
Olivia Orrell scored from just inside the circle Monday night, lifting Easton High's field hockey team to a 1-0 victory over Kent Island at Andy Schipul Stadium — the Warriors' second overtime win in four days.
After Tuesday's games, Queen Anne's (9-1 overall, 4-0 North Bayside) sits atop the division alone in first with Easton (7-3, 3-1) in second and Kent Island (8-3, 3-1) in third. Kent Island could forge a three-way tie atop the North when it hosts Queen Anne's Saturday. But the Lions would likely win the tiebreaker based on a better overall winning percentage.
Four days after defeating Pocomoke in overtime, Easton and the Bucs needed extra time to settle things, courtesy of some outstanding defense and fine goalie play. Warrior goalie Taylor Bowen (seven saves) faced her heaviest pressure in the first half but let nothing get by her. Easton dominated play in the second half, but couldn't beat Bucs goalie Brynja Petursson (11 saves), who stopped shots sitting and laying down, sending the scoreless stalemate into overtime.
"She's a great goalie," Kent Island head coach Laura Harding said of Petursson. "I thought the defense played well. Emma Fleshman stepped up; she was the one playing over Sydney Riska (who was out of town) and did a good job.
"We had many opportunities to put it in in the first half," Harding continued. "That's when we had the momentum and couldn't finish. You've got to finish to win."
Easton controlled the second half, and was inches from taking the lead on a corner with 7 minutes left in the third period. But Petursson, with the Warriors poking and trying to jam the ball past her, first made stops while seated, then stretched her body across the goalmouth to keep the game scoreless.
"First quarter when they came out I told them we're playing as individuals," Easton head coach Kim Neff said of her team. "And then they started communicating better and playing as a unit. That's when we kind of took over and dominated. But I have to give it to their defense and their goalie because they played a heckuva game. They are hard to get through."
Easton also got some big defensive plays. Stella Kabler poke checked the ball away from Kent Island's Rita Yost on a breakaway, and Myka Motovidlak twice spoiled threats.
Kent Island earned two late corners in the final 2 minutes of regulation, but fired wide of the cage, then watched Easton clear the second attempt, sending the game into the 7-on-7 overtime.
"I think we were really determined to get the corner, or at least get the shot off," Orrell said. "We just kept pounding the goal and I got the corner."
Knox set up on the end line to the left of Petursson and directed a pass to Orrell, who took possession, stepped out of the circle, then back in, and smacked a low, hard shot that slid past the right leg of the Bucs' goalie for the game-winner.
"I'm like, 'I can do this,'" Orrell said of the corner. "I knew it was a good shot. It was a hard hit. And then it went in and made the best sound ever. And then when the ref called it I looked at Addie and the whole team and I was so excited."
Within seconds, Orrell swarmed on by her jubilant teammates.
"It was a great game," Harding said. "Great reffed game. Great played game. Easton ended up wanting it a little more than us in the end. It was clear."
KENT ISLAND 3 KENT COUNTY 1
WORTON — Rita Yost, Caroline Levin and Audrey Fleshman each scored one goal Tuesday, as the Bucs topped the Trojans.
Ellie Burnside had an assist for Kent Island and Brynja Petursson had three saves.
QUEEN ANNE'S 7 ST. MICHAELS 0
CENTREVILLE — Ella Rebstock and Jamie Baldwin netted two goals apiece as the Lions won their ninth straight.
Jordan Bilbo and Haley Cole each had a goal and an assist for Queen Anne's. Aly Edwards added a goal and Ellee McLean an assist. The Lions didn't allow a shot on goal in posting their sixth shutout of the season.

title: Corcoran wins playoff, girls
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Corcoran wins playoff, girls

 October 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 764
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GRASONVILLE — She had not placed in the top three in any regular-season event.She didn't have the leader board up on her phone because she didn't want to stress herself out.
Then, after 18 holes Tuesday, Queen Anne's County High's Keira Corcoran walked to the Prospect Bay Country Club scoreboard and was greeted by a group of team family members.
"They told me I was about to go into a playoff because I was tied for first," Corcoran said. "I did not believe them. I had to go up to the scoreboard myself."
Corcoran was surprised when she saw she was indeed tied for first and headed for a playoff with North Caroline's Taryn Brandt. She was even more surprised two playoff holes later, when she made par on No. 18 to win the girls individual championship at the District 8 tournament.
"It was absolutely unbelievable," Queen Anne's County head coach Brad Niesz said of Corcoran's victory that gave the Lions a sweep of all three titles — Nate Smith winning his third straight boys individual crown while helping Queen Anne's win the team championship. "I would say that it was something that we knew was within her, but also surprising in that we do have a very talented field of female golfers. And when you combine the North females with the South females, what she accomplished was pretty incredible."
Playing in separate groups, Brandt fired a 42 over her first nine holes while Corcoran recorded a 43. The Queen Anne's senior then birdied her 17th hole, drawing her even the North Caroline senior. Both then bogeyed their final hole, finishing tied at 85 and creating a playoff.
"Through the first nine holes that I played I felt I was playing really good," Corcoran said. "And then I started to get a little bit tired I guess. I felt like I played well, but I didn't feel like I play outstanding."
Then came the discovery there was still more golf to play.
"I kind of started getting really nervous," Corcoran said. "I had to go by myself a little bit and I started just chipping and putting to kind of keep myself warm I guess."
Corcoran was still wrestling with her nerves the first playoff hole, the par-4 17.
"I was extremely nervous," she said. "I was shaking the entire time. Putting. Everything. When I would put my ball down I was shaking. I just had to contain myself and try to make a decent shot."
Both players made decent shots to earn par and remain deadlock, forcing the playoff to a second hole, the par-5 18.
Admittedly calmer on 18, Corcoran hit a beautiful drive down the middle of the fairway, then drove her second shot 130 yards, putting her 10 yards in front of the water hazard.
"I knew that I just didn't want to get into the water," Corcoran said. "I was focusing on the green. The flag was in the back of the green and there's a bunker behind (the flag) so I don't want to go long. I was just focusing on getting it up there. I didn't care if I had to chip. I just wanted it to be there."
Corcoran's third shot traveled about 100 yards, leaving her with a putt in the neighborhood of 20 feet.
Brandt's third shot caught a piece of a tree and fell into the water's marshy bank, virtually knocking her out of title contention.
Corcoran's first put stopped three feet shy of the cup.
"I knew I could miss this putt, but I knew I could definitely make it," Corcoran said. "Not quite a tap-in, but it was pretty close. I just knew I had to get it into the center of the cup. There was no break. I just needed to aim for the center of the cup."
Corcoran found the center to complete her title run.
"I tried to contain myself because I knew that it was a big deal for her as well," Corcoran said of Brandt. "I was extremely excited and I went up and shook her hand and told her she did a great job. And then I wanted to go to coach (Niesz) right away because I knew how excited and nervous he was for me."
Corcoran and Brandt each qualified for the state tournament at the University of Maryland in College Park. The state qualifying cut was 94 for the girls. Also qualifying were Parkside's Addison Apolenis (3rd, 86); Stephen Decatur's Samantha Boger (4th, 87); St. Michaels' Lexi Rockwell (5th, 89); defending champion Brianna Kurtz (6th, 91) from Kent Island; St. Michaels' Lola Browning (6th, 91); and Kent Island's Noelle Agee (8th, 92).

title: Smith leads Queen Anne's sweep
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Smith leads Queen Anne's sweep

 October 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 780
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GRASONVILLE — Despite being the two-time defending champion, Nate Smith admitted he's never played his best golf during the annual District 8 championship tournament.The Queen Anne's County High senior continued that trend Tuesday, and even poked fun at himself, noting his strength on this blustery autumn day at Prospect Bay Country Club was hitting his way out of the trees.
"I've had a lot of practice," Smith said with a slight grin. "I was basically in the trees every hole so I was pretty used to it. That's the best part of my game."
Smith's mental toughness though may be a notch above his knack for escaping the trees. He certainly showed that quality, as he rallied over the back nine before taking the lead on the second-to-last hole en route to carding a 3-over 75 to win his third consecutive boys individual title by two strokes over Kent County freshman standout Quinten Joiner.
Smith's third crown also helped Queen Anne's win the district championship for the first time under head coach Brad Niesz, and qualified the Lions team of Smith, Sam Yetman (85), George Cook (92), and girls champion Keira Corcoran (85) for the state tournament. Queen Anne's finished with a 337, two strokes better than runner-up Stephen Decatur.
"Just an incredible group of kids that are driven," Niesz said. "Love the game and love to compete."
Leading that group was Smith.
"Over the last year the mental part of his game has matured exponentially," Queen Anne's head coach Brad Niesz said of Smith. "He's always been a strong mental player. He's always had all the tools. But his ability to handle adversity on the golf course has been unparalleled.
"Golf's a funny game," Niesz continued. "It's basically divided into three parts: off the tee, your approach, and on the green. If you can get all three of those parts clicking you're in business. But it's very rare that that happens."
It didn't seem to happen for anyone on a course that many think is perhaps the toughest on at least the North Bayside Conference circuit.
Then there was Joiner, who dropped three birdies on the front nine for a 1-under 35 that gave him a three-stroke lead on Smith at the turn.
"Early I was just scrambling for pars," said Smith, who had seven pars and two bogeys over the first nine holes. "I couldn't get anything going. I was putting well, but off the tee I couldn't hit much of anything, or any fairways."
And yet the defending champion parred the first three holes on the back nine while Joiner bogeyed two of three, reducing his lead to one. Joiner restored his 3-shot cushion when he birdied 13 as Smith carded a bogey.
But back-to-back bogeys by Kent's outstanding freshman allowed Smith to pull even with a par on 14 and his lone birdie of the day on 15. Both made par on 16. Smith took his first lead on the 408-yard, par-4 17th with a par while Joiner had a double bogey.
"I kind of got ahead of myself, just got out of my game," said Joiner, who was praised for his play and maturity by Niesz. "That's what happens. You start thinking results, not process.
"Putter let me down pretty much the whole way around," Joiner added. "Just struggling on the greens; couldn't really find it. I made a couple good ones. There's just a few … man, it got away out there."
Smith and Joiner both found the trees off the tee on 18. Smith lined his second shot to the left of the water fronting the green. Joiner also delivered an impressive second shot, blasting a ball that was right up against a root, leaving his hands stinging.
Smith chipped within 8 feet of the cup with his fourth shot, missed a putt that made him wince, before tapping in for bogey and watching Joiner suffer a similar fate, with a miss on a short putt before settling for bogey.
"He's a great player," Joiner said of Smith. "He deserves it."
Smith said he was battling nerves, but not just because he was bidding for a third championship.
"I was very nervous because I was also playing for my team to go to states," Smith said. "It was very nerve racking.
"I just kept grinding," Smith said of the back nine. "Some putts started to fall and my chipping got a little better. I feel like I've got a lot of work to do. I've got to tighten somethings up. Like hitting it straight."
Kent Island's Josh David finished third with a 78 to qualify for states, and James M. Bennett's Colton Thomas carded an 83 to finish tied for fifth with Decatur's Jasper Davis. The qualifying cutoff for the boys was 83.

title: 'The love of football keeps me going': Ed Ginder celebrates 50 years leading Delaware football's 'chain gang'
author: Jon Buzby For the Cecil Whig
content:
'The love of football keeps me going': Ed Ginder celebrates 50 years leading Delaware football's 'chain gang'

 October 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Jon Buzby For the Cecil Whig | Section: News 
 
 1258
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Half a century is a long time no matter how you look at it. In Ed Ginder's case, he looks at it as time well spent.The longtime Elkton resident has been on the sideline as part of the "chain gang" for University of Delaware football games for five decades.
"As I tell people, I've been there longer than Tubby Raymond was head coach," Ginder, 79, said with a chuckle.
What started out in 1974 as a happenchance opportunity has turned into 50 years of reporting for duty on Delaware football game days as the supervisor of one of the most respected chain crew units in the region. Responsible for holding and moving the orange markers that designate the line of scrimmage and first down line, the crew is made up of 11 members, 13 when it's raining so that there are extras to keep the balls dry.
It's that type of attention to detail that has earned the UD chain crew, and its supervisor, Ginder, an exceptional reputation.
"Ed Ginder and his numerous chain crew members have done, and continue to do, a great job helping to manage the flow of our football contests," said Jerry Oravitz, senior associate athletics director for football. "Over the years, numerous officiating crews from the Yankee Conference, the A-10 Conference, and now the CAA have asked if they could bring Ed and his crew on the road to work games. That is certainly a credit to those guys. We recognize and appreciate the professionalism, dedication and commitment that Ed and his crew team members have demonstrated over a long period of time for Delaware football."
The current crew members and their years of service are Earle Miller (47), Dave Browne (42), Ken McCoy (39), Frank Wiggins Jr. (30), Steve Burke (26), Rob Alt (24), Jeremy Browne (24), Josh Browne (24), Dave Wiseman, (24), Joe Buckley (10), Matt Wharton (10), Glen Beechy (4), Ray Dudkewitz (4), Jay Hodge (4), Eli Scott (4), Ken Scott (4) and George Williams (4).
"Without the crew that I have, we wouldn't have the reputation that we have," said Ginder, who has supervised the crew since its inception. "They are very dependable."
One of the dependable crew members was quick to point out why he feels they are so successful.
"It's always been that way with Ed in charge because he has always paid attention to detail in terms of our equipment on the field and the job that we do," Wiggins said. "Before every game, we have to meet with the officials, and once they see our crew and who is on it, they always comment that there won't be any problems today. That all starts with Ed."
The chain gang's inceptionSo how did it all begin?
Ginder was employed by New Castle County Parks and Recreation as the supervisor of lifetime sports when one of his employees, who was a member of Coach Raymond's staff, asked if he could supply men for a chain crew. He was told it was becoming a new concept in college football to have people who were actually trained in keeping track of downs, yardage gained and distanced needed for a first down.
"Student-athletes did it before I did here at Delaware," Ginder said. "Other colleges would call people out of the stands to do it."
The late Scotty Duncan, who was UD's assistant athletic director at the time, promised Ginder and his crew uniforms, a locker room to change in, and season tickets and parking passes if they were willing to cover the home games.
"He gave us some leftover XXXL pants and shirts," Ginder recalled, grinning ear to ear. "If a gust of wind had come and you tied ropes to our arms and legs we would have been like floats in the Macy's parade."
Ginder shared that back in the early days, the crew originally used golf tees to mark the line of scrimmage and where the yard to gain a first down was located.
"That worked fine until it got cold and the ground froze," he recalled. "Then someone suggested banging a steel spike into the ground. I knew that wasn't going to be a good idea, and sure enough, a West Chester player landed on it and it got stuck in his shoulder."
Ginder eventually bought knickers and striped shirts for his workers, making them one of the first chain crews in the region to have a full uniform. He also designed a chart so that someone on the crew could keep track of every down and distance on paper, in case it was needed. It turned out to become a method other crews, and even referees, adopted.
"I developed this sheet of paper to track the spot of the ball and write down the yardage needed for a first down, before refs had their own," he explained while pointing at the chart he still uses to this day. The first year I used it, an official asked to have a copy. Two years later, the same ref came back and he handed it to me and said, 'I came up with this.' He stole my idea."
50 years of memoriesGinder has missed just two games, one for a funeral and one for his sister's wedding, and therefore has a multitude of favorite memories.
His most memorable moment during a game was when Delaware played Navy back in the late 1980s and the Midshipmen's star running back, Admiral Sydnor, was stopped mid-air on a fourth-and-1 by UD linebacker Darrell Booker to seal the upset.
Ginder also proudly mentioned that he and a few men from his crew were out shoveling snow on the sideline before the 2003 semifinal game played the day after a snowstorm turned the county into a winter wonderland.
"Someone from UD called me and asked if I could help shovel snow," Ginder recalled. "So, I called a few guys who I knew had vehicles that could get through the snow and get to the stadium, and we helped get it done."
'You just can't beat it'Ginder takes great pride in his role as supervisor on the crew and reiterated that the job is more important than the casual fan might think. He pointed out that it was a different chain gang's error late in the 2010 national championship game that might have cost UD the title.
"The yardage clip was removed before it should have been," he explained of the very controversial ending to that game. "And because of that, it was a bad mark made by the head linesman before measuring for the first down. If UD had gotten the first down, they would have run the clock out and won the championship."
Ginder pointed out that the most significant equipment modification was the electronic box on the stick that now changes the down with a press of the button, which then automatically displays the yardage to gain a first down on the box that sits atop the other stick.
"There's no more flipping numbers," he said, smiling.
Ginder's love of what he does is on display at his house in the form of one national championship and two runner-up rings that he purchased himself. All three have already been designated to be handed down to members of his family so the next generations have a way to remember the amount of time Ginder spent on the UD sideline, and more importantly, the reason he spent well over half his lifetime doing it.
"The love of football keeps me going," he said with a hint of emotion in his voice. "It's a whole different world down on that field. College football … you just can't beat it."

title: Lions win North despite tie with Bucs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions win North despite tie with Bucs

 October 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 694
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Queen Anne's County High girls head soccer coach Mike Kern didn't pop out of gear or launch into a tirade.But with his team trailing and doing everything but sticking the ball in the net Wednesday night against Kent Island, Kern was a bit more animated than usual as he pleaded for more.
"I just told them we had to play harder," Kern said. "We were knocking on the doorstep the entire first half. I thought we dominated the game. We had more opportunities to score and we just couldn't get it in the net. I just told them they had to play with a little more heart."
In another physical battle that has become commonplace in this rivalry, Queen Anne's got the equalizing goal it needed, when Shannon Rath buried a penalty kick into the right side of the net in the third minute of the second half in an eventual 1-1 double-overtime tie.
While the Lions and Buccaneers each finished the regular season with identical records — 9-2-1 overall, 6-0-1 North Bayside — Queen Anne's wins the tiebreaker between the two schools based on its 1-0 victory over Kent Island on Sept. 11. Though that first meeting did not count toward the North division, it was the deciding factor since head-to-head competition is the first tiebreaker.
Queen Anne's faces two-time defending conference champion James M. Bennett (12-0) for the Bayside championship on Monday at Snow Hill High School at 6:45 p.m. It will be the fourth consecutive year the Lions and Clippers decide the conference championship. Bennett beat Queen Anne's, 3-0, on Sept. 30 in Centreville.
"I thought Olivia (Ryan) played her best game of the season," Kern said of Wednesday's clash with Kent Island. "So I think we're starting to peak a little bit. We're pretty confident. I think going against (head coach) Ed O'Leary's (Bennett) team, they know us well, we know them well. I think it's going to be a good battle.
"I think this is one of the more talented teams we've ever had," Kern continued. "I mean we can play with anybody as far from 18 to 18. We've struggled to get the ball in the back of the net against these tougher teams. But we can defend. Bennett when we played them last time, we lost 3-0, but the score didn't depict the game. We lost on the scoreboard. But we got to get the ball in the back of the net."
Queen Anne's had three direct kicks and three corner kicks in the first 17 minutes against the Bucs, but could not beat Kent Island keeper Taylor Ritz. Then with 15 minutes left in the half, Buccaneers speedster Abbie Mahaffey — with Queen Anne's Rath trying to shield her from the ball and Lions keeper Bea Holthaus moving toward the ball from the opposite direction — managed to chip a shot that floated over Holthaus for a 1-0 Kent Island lead.
"I think it was just a miscommunication," Kern said of the play. "Shannon running toward her shielding the ball, and Bea coming out. And I think Abbie just made a good play to poke a foot in there and poke it around her. It was just communication."
Kent Island, which stretched its unbeaten streak to nine games after a 1-2 start to the season, held that lead into halftime, despite the Lions swarming near the goal with less than 2 minutes left in the first half in a bid for the tying goal and Ritz away from the net. But the Bucs defense denied Queen Anne's, carrying the 1-0 lead into the break.
The Lions put immediate pressure on Kent Island early in the second half, sending a header over the crossbar. Then with almost 3 minutes elapsed, Kara Ringold was fouled just inside the box, setting up Rath, who roped a shot into the right side past Ritz's dive.
Two yellow cards against the Bucs gave Queen Anne's two more direct-kick chances, but the first sailed wide right and the second was stopped by Ritz.
The Lions came within inches of taking the lead when a shot hit under the crossbar and fell in front of the goal with 9:20 remaining in regulation.

title: Webb, Stepp score late, lift Sabres over Herons for third straight title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Webb, Stepp score late, lift Sabres over Herons for third straight title

 October 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 824
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — It had gone undefeated in conference play this season, outscoring its six opponents by a 58-1 margin.So it was easy to think Thursday's Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference title game was a mere gimme for Saints Peter and Paul High's field hockey team.
It was anything but.
The two-time defending champ was in a scoreless stalemate at halftime. It nudged ahead in the third, only to be tied 55 seconds into the fourth quarter. But Angie Webb and Jules Stepp scored a little more than 2 minutes apart down the stretch to give the Sabres a 3-1 victory over a stubborn Gunston squad for its third consecutive ESIAC championship.
"They came to play," Sts. Peter & Paul head coach Debbie McQuaid said of the Herons, who lost both regular-season games to the Sabres by a combined 11-1 score. "We knew it was going to be hard. Gunston's gotten better. We've gotten better. Both teams have been playing some out-of-conference strong teams. So I expected them to come at me with all they had. And they did."
Despite having a 5-1 advantage in penalty corners in the first half, Sts. Peter & Paul (11-5) was held scoreless in the first half by a conference opponent for the first time all year, as Gunston junior standout Layla Kent seemed to be everywhere at once.
"The stress was really high," Stepp said. "We do a prayer before every single game. Then we came together (at halftime) and we prayed again."
The Sabres earned three more corners in the first seven minutes of the third quarter, but couldn't dent the scoreboard. But SSPP made its fourth corner of the period count, as Webb unloaded a sweeping drive that buzzed by Herons goalie Loreli deGour with 6:52 remaining in the third period for a 1-0 lead.
"It was a reverse chip," Webb said. "I saw the (defender) where she was, and I knew I had to pull around her. So I just pulled it to the left and just took the shot. I was aiming for the corner. I was just happy to get the corner in."
Just 55 seconds into the fourth quarter though, Gunston (9-4) pieced together a concerted push that got behind SSPP goalie Pyper Mister and finished with Kate Zottarelli's goal into the left side of the cage.
"We've been working so much more on our mental game this season, and we've had so many more games," Gunston assistant Jen Matthews said. "It's just given us a lot more opportunities to connect as a team, work as a team. We really peaked at the right time of the season."
Webb though struck again with 5:18 remaining.
"I knew we needed a goal," Webb said. "I didn't want to go into overtime. I knew we needed to get a goal and I just felt the adrenaline rush of wanting to score. Just took a shot when I needed to. We worked well as a team to get it off."
Gunston got tagged with a 2-minute card with just under 4 minutes remaining, and the Sabres capitalized, as Webb sent a smash toward the goal that Stepp — in a move that looked like an act of self defense — made a beautiful deflection for a 3-1 lead.
"I was so surreal, because Angie cranked a shot off from the top and it was up in the air," Stepp said. "I didn't hear a whistle so at first I thought it was a corner. But she ripped the shot off and it was coming at me so my initial reaction was hit at the ball in some way, shape of form. And it just deflected off right into the goal. It was amazing. I've never done that in my whole career, and it was just perfect to have it happen in our championship game."
Despite losing to the Sabres for a third straight year, Matthews and Gunston head coach Yvonne Gazelle gushed over their team's play.
"They did amazing," said Gazelle, who in addition to Kent's outstanding all-around play, got a big effort from Grace Shepherd, who is bound for Central Michigan University. "I'm super proud of these girls."
It was Sts. Peter & Paul's fourth championship in five years.
"The last two goals were simply amazing," McQuaid said. "Happy for Jules and Angie; the finish."
McQuaid acknowledged her past two championship teams had a tendency to lean heavily on Webb's older sister, Gennie Webb, now playing for Virginia Commonwealth University.
"It was not just one person; we relied on her a lot," McQuaid said of Gennie Webb. "This year I have a group of girls, who played as a unit and supported each other. And they were fabulous."
Notes: Kent was named the ESIAC player of the year, and along with teammates Grace Shepherd, Gabi Shepherd and Izzy Labrador, was named to the all-ESIAC first-team. … Sts. Peter & Paul's Webb, Stepp, Reagan Wolters, Lucy Rankin, Kat Murphy, and Claire Bieber all earned first-team honors. SSPP's Caroline Corson was an honorable mention pick.

title: Warriors rally three times before edging Lions
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors rally three times before edging Lions

 October 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 592
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It may not have matched the significance of the 2014 playoff between the two schools, but on an emotional level it came close.Mikey O'Connor hit Chase Raab with a 10-yard touchdown pass with 1 minute, 21 seconds remaining, and Zach Barnhart made his second interception with 53 seconds left Thursday night, as Easton High's football team rallied for a 27-26 victory over Queen Anne's County at Lions Stadium in Centreville.
The victory strengthened Easton's No. 2 seeding in the approaching Class 2A East Region playoffs behind undefeated and defending 2A state champion Stephen Decatur.
"For coach (Al) Waters and the rest of the guys that joined the staff it meant a lot for us to get a win there," Easton head coach Matt Griffith said Friday of Waters, his defensive coordinator who was a one-time head coach at Queen Anne's.
"But more importantly with that, we had a little bump in the road; two-game losing streak," Griffith continued. "And a young group of kids who are still trying to figure out to be mature on the football field and learn how to win. And they learned how to win last night. We could have folded the tent a few times."
Winners of four straight, Queen Anne's (4-3) jumped to a 14-0 first-quarter lead. DeRodney Smith (15 carries, 101 yards) scored on a 21-yard touchdown run, but Easton's Logan Friend blocked the extra point. Ja'Dereon Thompson then intercepted O'Connor and made an 84-yard touchdown return. Harris ran in the two-point conversion for a two-touchdown lead.
Easton (5-2) trimmed its deficit to 14-7, when O'Connor (12 of 20, 178 yards, three touchdowns, interception) connected with Colin Mooney for a 27-yard touchdown pass with 4:27 left in the first quarter. Dominic Stanco tacked on the extra point.
O'Connor's 1-yard touchdown run around left end and Stanco's second point-after kick pulled the Warriors even at 14-14 just 55 seconds into the second quarter.
But Queen Anne's responded, as John Connolly (12 carries, 101 yards) scored on an 8-yard run with 3:25 left in the first half for a 20-14 lead. Easton's Nathan Lapp blocked the extra point.
Barnhart intercepted Lions quarterback Carter Hercher with 30 seconds left in the first half, setting up O'Connor's touchdown pass to Diontaye Copper with 10 seconds to go before halftime. Stanco's PAT gave Easton a 21-20 lead.
The Warriors took the opening kickoff and drove 77 yards to the Queen Anne's 1, where they fumbled, the ball recovered by the Lions' Amari Baynard.
Queen Anne's put together a 97-yard drive that ended with Connolly's 3-yard touchdown run for a 26-21 lead. The Lions' two-point bid was stopped.
Easton regained the lead at 27-26, when O'Connor hit Raab with a 10-yard touchdown pass in the left side of the end zone with 1:25 left.
Barnhart then intercepted Hercher a second time with 46 seconds remaining to cement the Warriors' win.
"They were poised," Griffith said of his team. "Mikey made some plays. All the receivers made some plays. Dustin Blue was unbelievable (16 carries, season-high 101 yards)."
Then there was Barnhart.
"He's probably got one of our best football IQs on the team, and defensively makes a big difference out there for us," Griffith said of Barnhart. "The last two weeks he's been playing lights out. He's just going to keep getting better each week."

Easton defeated Queen Anne's 21-14 in the Class 2A East Region semifinals in 2014, when Jaelon Moaney hit Dre' Stevens with a 41-yard touchdown pass with 2 minutes left.

title: Sabres finish strong on way to crown
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres finish strong on way to crown

 October 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 767
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Keely Morgan's goal just 2 seconds before halftime put the home team in front.But it was Eden Zimmerman's goal off Avery McCall's beautiful corner kick that put Saints Peter and Paul High's girls soccer team finally in control.
That score gave the top-seeded Sabres an infusion of confidence Friday en route to a 4-1 victory over Gunston in the Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference championship.
"It feels amazing," said McCall, a junior midfielder, who has now been a part of conference title teams in soccer, basketball and lacrosse. "This is a very special team."
A team that had been bounced in the first round of the ESIAC postseason the past two years. A team that went undefeated in conference play this season and came in as the No. 1 seed. And a team that won its first ESIAC championship since 2019.
But the Sabres (10-3) were consistently beaten to the ball by the Herons (6-5-1) in the first half, and halfway through the second half.
"We were definitely dominant in the first half and the first 20 minutes of the second half," Gunston head coach Tony D'Antonio said. "And then it was pretty even after that. They found the net and we didn't."
Sts. Peter & Paul found the net in the 8th minute, when Emery Zimmerman parked a direct kick into the right side of the net for a 1-0 lead.
Gunston got a pair of corner kicks in the 18th minute, the first skidding through the crease but finding no one on the other end. Sabres keeper Kaylin Palmer made a save on a direct kick with 13:30 left in the first half.
The Herons then put together a flurry off a corner with 5 minutes remaining before the break. A corner kick sailed over the Palmer's outstretched fingers and through the crease. Gunston kept possession, striking a ball that hit one of its own players before sending a shot over the crossbar.
Then with 2:04 left before halftime, Ellie Roberts sent a drive from about 25 yards out that nestled into the far right corner for a 1-1 tie.
"It's hard to beat a team three times," McCall said of the Sabres' two regular-season wins over Gunston. "But I think we were mostly in panic mode. They (Gunston) always come out really fast and we're normally a second-half team. So we were very defensive and I think that's what saved us. And then eventually we got the offense together and it all came together."
Sts. Peter & Paul got a huge boost just 2 seconds before halftime when Morgan got a ball and tucked it inside the left post for a 2-1 halftime lead.
"It was absolutely huge," Sabres head coach Nicole Edsall said of Morgan's goal.
Sophomore Emery Zimmerman agreed.
"I think that was essential because it really just got us going," Emery Zimmerman said. "It (made us) realize, 'OK, we need to win this. We want to win this. This is ours. We came all this way undefeated (in conference play). This is the time that we need to come out and score.
"When they caught up to us and we got back up one more like right off the bat, it really got us going," Emery Zimmerman continued. "Gave us a lot of enthusiasm and momentum."
But not right away.
"They definitely had jitters in the first half," Edsall said of her team. "And when we talked at halftime I said, 'I know this isn't the team that we are. So just kind of brush it off. Let it go. Start the half over and let's play our game.'"
Play evened out midway through the second half. Then with 8:42 left, McCall bent a corner that plopped right in front of Eden Zimmerman, who tapped it in for a 3-1 lead.
"I've been struggling on my corners all season," McCall said. "I usually just boot it and hope. Eden is always everywhere and she just found it. It got the curve that it needed and she was just there for it. We've always been a team that struggles to like get it in (on corners). It's always gone right through. But she was just right there where she needed to be."
Less than 2 minutes later, the Sabres spilled into the box before Kendall Kroniser gained possession, spun away from a defender and drilled in a fourth goal.
"I'm sure it's great for the seniors," Emery Zimmerman said. "I'm happy for them. I feel over the last year nobody leaving (through graduation) and through this year, we really built up on our skills and built great team chemistry. And this is what happens when you work hard at practice."

title: Core's late goal lifts Bennett to third straight title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Core's late goal lifts Bennett to third straight title

 October 22, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 682
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SNOW HILL — James M. Bennett High girls head soccer coach Ed O'Leary knew the final of the regular-season match was deceiving."When we beat them three-nil in Queen Anne's, we knew it wasn't a three-nil game," O'Leary said of the Clippers' Sept. 30 game with Queen Anne's County.
Monday's rematch was much different, but still the Clippers came out on the winning end, as freshman Gracie Core's goal with 3 minutes, 8 seconds remaining lifted Bennett to its third consecutive Bayside Conference championship via a 3-2 victory over the Lions at Snow Hill High's Kelly Shumate Stadium.
"We expected that from Mike (Kern) and Jeff (Anthony)," O'Leary said of Queen Anne's head coach and assistant. "First minute they just were on top, and they were so aggressive. And we like that. And they made us fight for everything. You know what? That's the way it should be."
The first half ended with Bennett (13-0) in a place it had never been all year — trailing.
With not quite 2 minutes remaining, Queen Anne's Shannon Rath drove a direct kick that Clippers keeper Sophia Valenzano (six saves) dove to her left to make an initial save on. But the ball trickled to the right of Valenzano who was still on the ground when the Lions' Kara Ringold rushed in to knock in the game's first goal.
"We came out and we ended up getting that first goal in the first half," Kern said. "It's what we needed. It was very important because we've struggled scoring against the good teams this year. We've scored a lot of goals for the season, but (in) these big games we're having a tough time putting the ball in the back of the net. So getting that first goal was huge."
Queen Anne's goalie Bea Holthaus (seven saves) kept the Lions (9-3-1) in front early in the second half when she came out to intercept a corner kick headed near her goal line. But less than 3 minutes later, Holthaus made a sliding stop on Core, who quickly possessed the rebound and dished a short pass to Rilynn East for the tying goal.
Holthaus and Valenzano each made saves on corner kick 3 minutes apart.
Bennett transitioned downfield. Core came down the right side, was bumped by Queen Anne's Hayden Legg, managed to stay on her feet, and steered a shot past Holthaus into the left side for a 2-1 Bennett lead with 20:41 remaining in the game.
"Bennett's a strong team and we defended them well for most of the game," said Kern of a Clippers team that had outscored the opposition 82-3 this season.
Queen Anne's wasn't quite through though.
With 11:10 left, Madison Horney carried into the box, stumbled slightly through a tackle by Bennett's Taylor Matthews, then while falling, managed to get enough of her right foot on the ball to get it past Valenzano for a 2-2 tie. It was the first time Bennett had allowed two goals in game all season.
"We came back, hung tough," Kern said.
Queen Anne's came within inches of taking a lead when it banged shot off a corner went off the crossbar with 6:22 remaining.
The game appeared headed for overtime. But with the clock approaching the 3-minute mark, Core collected a ball that glanced off a defender, and from right wing, drove a left-footed shot into the left side of the net for the winning goal.
"I hope the crowd enjoyed it because it was a wonderful game," O'Leary said. "We got a little bit lucky in the end. They could have scored but the crossbar. But our super freshman (Core) went and scored a cracking goal at the end."
It was the Lions third straight loss to the Clippers in the championship game, yet Kern — who told his team afterwards "This was better than any practice we could have had," came away encouraged.
"Hit the crossbar on a corner kick and we had bad clear in the back and they capitalized on it," Kern said. "Proud of the girls. Proud how they played. The effort was there. And I think we can build from it moving into the playoffs."

title: Marks, Queen Anne's run into record book
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Marks, Queen Anne's run into record book

 October 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 925
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — Queen Anne's County High's Ben Marks wasn't thrilled with his time, yet still ran into the school record book.So did Queen Anne's County's girls team and Parkside's Logan Newton.
And then there was Kent Island's boys, who added to their historic run Wednesday by winning their 15th team championship in 18 years during the annual Bayside Conference cross country championships at Cambridge-South Dorchester's jungle course.
"It's definitely really cool," said Marks after becoming the first Queen Anne's runner — male or female — to win back-to-back individual titles in school history. "I'm extremely blessed and honored to be the Bayside record-holder and all that stuff. I wanted to do something special today, but it just was not the plan for the day."
Marks set a course and meet record last year here, when he clocked a winning time of 15 minutes, 17.94 seconds in his first season running cross country.
The senior moved to the front of the pack early yesterday on an unseasonable warm afternoon, broke from the first section of trees with the lead, and never relinquished it en route to covering the 3-mile course in a winning time of 16:06.51 — 45 seconds ahead of runner-up Tekai Drummond of Cambridge-SD.
But the defending champion was far from pleased.
"Today was not necessarily my best day to say the least," Marks said. "I went out with intention and it just didn't go the way I wanted it to.
"Good start, but it didn't feel amazing," Marks continued. "I don't have excuses. I guess the woods slowed me up a little bit today; nobody there with me pushing. So after a certain point in the race I was like, 'OK, this is not going right at all. Let's check the box and focus on a little more training before I head into the more important (regional and state) races.'"
The race for second may have been the best duel of the meet, as Cambridge-SD's Drummond and Mardela's Connor McIntyre charged down the stretch side by side, with Drummond (16:51.28) crossing the finish line just ahead of McIntyre (16:51.64).
Kent Island won its third straight boys crown, totaling 51 points to second-place Stephen Decatur's 82. But with Bucs' No. 1 runner Gunner Hansard unsure if he was going to run because of an ankle injury, second-year head coach Andrew McIntire stressed the importance of a pack mentality to his team prior to taking its place on the starting line.
"It was a last-minute decision and he decided to run," McIntire said of Hansard, who was Kent Island's second runner to finish, placing ninth in 17:39.94. "I told them before the race, 'We're going to need a close gap between one and five today.'"
The Bucs did just that, as its top five runners finished within 47 seconds of each other.
"That's about as good as it's going to get," McIntire said. "We've always run in a bunch. We have a lot of great runners and they like to run together, and it paid off. And it's paid off all season long."
Leading the way was senior Giovanni Aguirre, who was approached by Hansard before the race.
"When he looked at me and he was like, 'Hey my ankle's really bad. I need you to be able to take my spot," Aguirre said of Hansard. "And I managed to get up there. It was pretty fulfilling knowing I didn't let my team down. I had to beat one runner, and he almost got me at the end."
Aguirre finished fifth (17:19.20) edging Decatur's Braydon Bell (17:19.36). Following Aguirre and Hansard across the finish line for Kent Island were Caleb Heater (10th, 17:41.42), Cole Fury (12th, 17:52.58) and Jacob Keever (15th, 18:06.70).
Though its top five runners were separated by less than 4 minutes, Queen Anne's girls finished in a tight enough bunch to win their first team title since 2007 with 51 points, edging Decatur by one.
"This group of girls have worked so hard," Queen Anne's head coach Kim Agee said. "And when they get in a race we talk about what they need to do beforehand, and they get out there and just fight for it. It's been so impressive. I've loved watching them."
Leading the charge was junior Faith Gordon, who was among the leaders for a good portion of the race before Parkside's Newton and Snow Hill's Allie Suarezapecheche pulled away to finish first and second, respectively.
"Usually before my races I kind of dread them," Gordon said. "And then after them I'm like, 'That was really fun.' Today I felt really excited. I was like, 'I have a good feeling about this today.' I'm kind of beating myself up that I didn't get first place, but I know I did my best. I think I could have run faster."
Gordon finished third in 20:31.03, almost a full 30 seconds behind Newton (20:01.04), who became the first runner in Parkside's history — male or female — to win back-to-back individual titles at Baysides. Suarezapecheche was second in 20:20.37.
Helping Queen Anne's to the championship were Addison Holden (8th, 21:12.82), Riley Coleman (13th, 23:07.67); RJ Ensor (23:16.67) and Emmalyn Dutton (21st, 24:12.90).
Placing in the top 10 were Cambridge-SD's Camryn Russum (5th, 20:50.76) and North Caroline's Brooke Sullivan (7th, 21:11.36).
Finishing in the top 10 on the boys side were Cambridge-SD's Josiah Harris (4th, 17:11.27) and North Caroline's Darly Ortega-Miguel (8th, 17:31.14). Cambridge-SD (97 points) was third in the boys field followed by North Caroline (4th, 114), Queen Anne's (5th, 129), and Easton (6th, 149).
North Caroline (81) was third in the girls competition followed by Kent Island (97), Parkside (108) and Cambridge-SD (119).

title: Orrell nets equalizer, game-winner to lift Easton over Rams in double overtime
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Orrell nets equalizer, game-winner to lift Easton over Rams in double overtime

 October 24, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 614
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — It was a Warrior's cry."The story's not done," declared a member of Easton High's field hockey team before breaking the pregame huddle.
The Warriors did indeed extend their 2024 story Thursday afternoon. And as usual — at least when it comes to chapters with big games — they needed more than the usual amount of time to finish and deliver a happy ending.
Olivia Orrell scored the equalizer late in the fourth period, then knocked in the game-winner 1 minute, 52 seconds into the second overtime yesterday, lifting Easton to a 2-1 victory over No. 2 seed Parkside in a Class 2A East II semifinal.
Winners of six straight, the third-seeded Warriors (10-3) advance to Tuesday's 2A East II final at top-seeded Stephen Decatur (11-3).
"These girls never give up," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, whose team has played beyond regulation four times this season, losing a shootout to two-time Bayside champion Queen Anne's and beating perennial conference heavyweights Pocomoke and Kent Island in OT before yesterday's double-overtime thriller. "And as exhausted as they were, they never ever give up."
But Easton could have.
After a scoreless first half, the Warriors earned four penalty corners in the third period but couldn't beat Rams goalie Eden Hirsch. Easton continued applying pressure.
Then with 7:20 left in regulation, Parkside's Ava Holland converted a pass from Mady Bleile for a 1-0 Rams lead.
Neff immediately called time.
"I called time because I knew they were going to get in their own heads with that goal," Neff said of her team. "I knew I had to bring them back together as as unit and tell them we had seven minutes (in regulation). That's plenty of time to score and get ahead. And sure enough, they took that and within three minutes they were able to put one in the goal."
Easton surged into the circle and earned another corner. Hirsch made an initial save on the play. But Ryan Quicke gained possession and got the ball to Orrell, who tucked into the right corner of the cage with 3:52 remaining in regulation.
"When they scored the first goal, it put a drive in us to like dig deep," Orrell said. "Coach said we had it and she knew we had the energy. We just had the discipline. And the discipline I think as a team really got us through the game."
Easton's defense kept it a 1-1 tie through the first 10-minute overtime.
Freshman goalie Taylor Bowen (five saves) kicked away a sweeping backhand from Bleile 1:05 into the extra session. The Rams earned back-to-back corners but were denied, with Addie Knox making a clear on the second corner. Easton's Bis Johnson then swept away a ball inches from the goal line with 2 minutes remaining.
Hirsch answered, making a big save just 15 seconds later, forcing the game into a second OT.
The Warriors got two corners early, and capitalized on the second, as Orrell continuously hit at the ball before sneaking it into the back of the cage for the winner.
"Too many," Orrell answered when asked how many times she hit the ball before scoring. "We were really determined. We just got it in. It was great."
The Rams, who shut out Easton earlier in the season, finish 9-4.
"I think it was a great game from both sides," Parkside head coach Stephanie Cason said. "It just didn't fall in our favor."

STEVENSVILLE — Willow Yost scored two goals and set up a third as second-seeded Kent Island blanked the No. 3 seed Bulldogs.
The second-seeded Buccaneers (9-3-1) played at top-seed Queen Anne's (11-1-1) in the region final on Tuesday.
Ellie Burnside and Parker Tengwall each scored once for Kent Island. Goalie Brynja Petursson made seven saves.

title: Easton's fast start too much for Bennett
author: Bill Haufe

 EASTON — It may have been the most efficient offensive performance produced by Easton High's football team this season.The Warriors scored on all six of their first-half possessions, then scored the first time they had the ball in the second half Friday night en route to a 49-31 victory over James M. Bennett.
Easton improved to 6-2, strengthening its hold on the No. 2 seed in the approaching Class 2A East playoffs behind undefeated and defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur (8-0).
"We did very well in the first half," Warrior head coach Matt Griffith said. "We came out and I thought we did well in the second half, too. I think we went down and scored pretty quickly. Senior night, try to get a lot of players in and do some different things. But no matter who's in the game, we've got to learn to finish."
Senior quarterback Mikey O'Connor's 6-yard touchdown run around left end and Dom Stanco's point-after kick moved Easton to a 49-10 lead with 9 minutes, 20 seconds remaining in the third quarter, setting the running clock in motion.
The Warriors carried that 39-point cushion into the fourth quarter before the Clippers (3-5) got a pair of touchdown passes from Liam Nelson as part of a 21-point closing surge. But Easton's opening onslaught proved too much for Bennett to overcome.
Dustin Blue carried 17 times for 115 yards and scored on touchdown runs of 1, 1 and 11 yards in the first quarter to help Easton build a 21-3 lead.
"Dustin ran great tonight," Griffith said. "Awesome. Dustin dictated the tempo and how we were going to play physical up front tonight."
Easton's passing game took over from there, as O'Connor connected with Colin Mooney down the center of the field for a 37-yard touchdown strike that extended the Warriors lead to 28-3 just 33 seconds into the second quarter.
O'Connor, who had 14 carries for a game-high 129 yards and a touchdown, completed 9 of 13 for 120 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.
"Just kind of taking what they gave us in how they tried to defend us," Griffith said.
Chase Raab hauled in a 17-yard touchdown pass with 8:44 still to go in the second quarter, widening Easton's lead to 35-3.
Bennett stopped Easton's scoring spree, when Zakai Smullen hit Jamareon Stevens for a 1-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-goal with 4:25 left in the first half.
But Easton answered, as O'Connor hit Mooney for an 18-yard scoring play, pushing Easton's lead to 42-10 with 1:28 left in the first half.

title: Burnham has Vikings seemingly in all the right places
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Burnham has Vikings seemingly in all the right places

 October 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Rob Burnham deflects praise quite nicely."We got great kids. I'm not a good coach," Cambridge-South Dorchester High's first-year head football coach said. "All I've done is put people in places to be successful. I haven't done anything fancy."
Well, after Thursday night's 42-0 road victory at Washington, the Vikings have a fancy 8-0 record — the first time they've been unbeaten this deep into a season since 2000.
Despite his self evaluation, Burnham has proven to be a pretty good head coach, and has certainly put his personnel in the right spots offensively, as Cambridge-SD has outscored its last five opponents, 187-14.
Leading that charge has been junior running back Sterling Perkins, who has rushed for 902 yards and 10 touchdowns, and senior quarterback Anthony Hughes, who has 733 yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns on the ground, and has completed over 50% of his passes for 355 yards and seven touchdowns — two of those coming Thursday against the Jaguars.
But the Vikings have been equally, if not more impressive, on defense.
"The defense is definitely the strength of our team without question," Burnham said of a unit that has four players — KaMarii Stanley, Christen Dockins, Antonio Blueford and Tabrion Watts — with over 40 tackles apiece.
Hard to argue that considering Cambridge-SD has surrendered just one offensive touchdown over its last five games — that coming on an 8-yard run by Wicomico — and has shut out three of its last five opponents, including its last two.
"We've done pretty well defensively holding people," Burnham said. "Our kids play fast. We tackle well and drive the pile backwards. And we run fast to it."
That unit figures to face its stiffest test of the season next Friday when longtime rival Easton (5-2) comes to Cambridge for the regular-season finale for both teams.
"Easton brings a quality opponent to Cambridge next week," Burnham said. "They have some talent on offense that's pretty special and we have to be able to contain that. Our kids are going to be ready to play."
Burnham liked the way his team started for the most part against winless Washington. The Vikings scored on their first possession, committed a turnover, then scored the next three times they had the ball while building a 35-0 halftime lead.
Hughes was an efficient 4 of 5 passing for 65 yards and two touchdowns before being relieved by Nathan Twilley, who also had a scoring toss. Blueford, Ra'Quan Cornish and Tamyron Evans each had touchdown receptions, and William Jackson and Watts had one rushing touchdown apiece.
Still, Burnham said there's work to be done offensively.
"We have things we need to clean up offensively," Burnham said. "We're not anywhere near where I want to be offensively.
"Overall we blocked well. We finished well," Burnham said of Thursday's win. "But we have not played a complete game yet."
