title: Local young equestrian places high at All-American QH Congress
author: DOUG BISHOP Special to the Star Democrat
content:
Local young equestrian places high at All-American QH Congress

 October 26, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: DOUG BISHOP Special to the Star Democrat | Section: News 
 
 425
 Words

 COLUMBUS, OHIO — Equestrian Levi Marx, 8, of Centreville, competed at his first-ever national horse show, Oct. 12 to 14.The 56th All-American Quarter Horse Congress, horse show, was held in Columbus, Ohio. The QH Congress is the largest horse show in the world. Beginning originally in 1967 as a three-day show, and has grown over the years to a show now covering nearly four-weeks, this year starting Sunday, Sept. 29, ending Sunday, Oct. 27.
The show attracts over one million people and over 4,000 horses from around the world. The total show has over 26,000 entries on a wide range of equestrian categories.
Marx, a member of the local Dream Riders 4-H Club, has also been showing at horse shows since he was 4 years old, being trained primarily by his mother, Karen Marx, who also showed during her late teen years at the QH Congress.
Levi Marx competed in the youngest group, "Small Fry" equestrians, for ages 9 and under. He competed in six events over three days; SF Fitting & Showmanship, SF Horsemanship, SF Trail, SF Western Pleasure, SF Hunter Under Saddle, and SF Equitation.
Among the six classes, Marx qualified for the finals in three; Trail, Western Pleasure and Hunter Under Saddle. He placed 10th overall in Trail, and ninth overall in Hunter Under Saddle. The largest class had 49 competitors. Each class was judged by four different judges, who's scores were combined to determine the overall placings.
Marx has one more year of eligibility to compete in the Small Fry division as a 9-year-old. He will then move up to the next appropriate aged youth classes.
Of his first national competitive experience, marx said, "It was a lot of fun. I've been going to shows in New Jersey, thinking those were big shows. The QH Congress is really big. It was a different experience."
Levi's mom said, "We were thrilled at how well Levi did. He certainly learned a lot! I want to thank those who have helped Levi develop into the equestrian his has become."
Levi had his picture taken with longtime QH Congress Honorary Director Don Recchiuti and his wife, Leah, of Mineral City, Ohio following his placing in the SF Hunter Under Saddle class.
Recchiuti said, "It's obvious to me that Levi will continue to improve if he continues to work hard and practice riding his horse."
Don Recchuiti has been involved in volunteering at the QH Congress for 33 years. Leah Recchuiti worked 15 years in the NYATT office as a volunteer checking that all the entries were filed correctly.
More information can be found at quaterhorsecongress.com.

title: Lions serve up 3rd straight title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions serve up 3rd straight title

 October 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 630
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — Queen Anne's County High's volleyball team spent time during the first week of practice in August getting to know new head coach Jamie Leventry.But it was on the first day of practice that Leventry defined the importance of serving.
"We talked about it starting Day 1," Leventry said. "'We're going to serve tough. It's what we're going to do.'"
The Lions proved extremely tough from the serving line Monday night, as Emerson Stewart reeled off the team's longest service run of the season during a dominating 25-10, 25-9, 25-5 victory over Parkside that gave Queen Anne's its third consecutive Bayside Conference championship.
"There's a reason why their record is what it is," Parkside head coach Roy Geiser said after the Lions improved to 15-0. "Great serving team. Great passing team. And frankly we didn't play our best game. But they put a lot of pressure on us and we weren't prepared."
The Rams (14-4) got an idea of things to come in Game 1, when Sydney Pinder (eight kills) served four straight points, turning a 5-4 Lions lead into a 9-4 edge.
"I feel it gives us such an advantage and I think it helps build up our team's momentum," Pinder said of her team's service game. "It just keeps us up as a team."
Queen Anne's maintained that five-point edge before Kaisa Hickson started a five-point serving spree with one of the Lions' 22 aces, extending the lead to 19-9.
Parkside put down a winner to stop that run before Bianca Baker (team-high 13 kills) closed the first game with a six-point roll from the line to cap Game 1.
"It's just a matter of putting a lot of pressure on the other team, and kind of getting them out of system," Leventry said. "Whenever we're back there putting good, tough serves on them and they're struggling to pass those, then that puts us in a really good spot."
Jensen Nutley put the Lions in a really good spot, when she strung together eight service points for an 8-0 Queen Anne's lead to start Game 2.
"I think that was really important because when you're up by so much, I feel like you don't think about making mistakes so much," Nutley said. "When you're in a neck-to-neck game, like when we play a team like Kent Island, where it's serve and serve back and forth, that takes a lot of effort from us not to make mistakes and think about it a lot. When we're up by that much I feel like it lets us loose and play our game."
A Baker kill and three consecutive service points from Stewart pushed the Lions' lead to 11 at 12-1. Queen Anne's lead remained around 11 points until 20-9, when Stewart again stepped to the line and wedged two more aces into a game-sealing, five-point run.
"Climbing back on a team like that you just can't do," Geiser said. "We got to play at our very best and that's not what we did tonight."
Parkside's Brylie Geiser served to open Game 3, but Baker unloaded another kill for a 1-0 Lions lead. Stewart moved back to the service line and wouldn't leave until Queen Anne's lead was at 19-0.
"My main goal is to keep it in; keep a nice, clean flow at serve," said Stewart, whose previous best service run was 13. "I think it's definitely intimidating when there's a long serving streak, especially with a big game on the line."
Queen Anne's completed its 12th sweep of the season with a kill from Nutley and a Marylee Kline serve that was not returned.
"Feels great," Leventry said. "It's been a fun season so far. And like I said, we're not done yet. A state championship is our goal."
It was the first time Queen Anne's has won three straight conference titles in volleyball.

title: Rival clashes feature various degrees of confidence
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Rival clashes feature various degrees of confidence

 October 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 784
 Words 

 Read News Document

 They each come into rivalry week with varying degrees of confidence.After getting shutout by defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur on Oct. 11, Kent Island High's football team rides a two-game win streak into Friday's annual clash with county rival Queen Anne's.
The Lions come into Friday having won five of six, their latest, a 21-20 victory over Parkside eight days after losing a one-point heartbreaker to Easton.
Streaking Colonel Richardson readies for its annual duel with North Caroline having outscored its last four opponents, 203-20.
And though they are still searching for their first win of the season, the Bulldogs fell just two points shy of Kent Island but have senior star Zymear Smith back and running.
"I can see some progress that we've made," said Heath Wilkins, who became North Caroline's head coach just four weeks ago. "I wish I had the team for more time, but I don't, so this is what we've got."
For the second time in Wilkins' three games as head coach, the Bulldogs (0-8) held a halftime lead last Friday. Corey Bunce's 4-yard touchdown run and Caden Deavers' two-point conversion run gave North Caroline an 8-0 lead on Kent Island, which had a field-goal attempt blocked before the half.
But the Bucs (5-3) rebounded in the second half, as Nathan Green scored on runs of 14 and 38 yards to help push Kent Island to a 16-8 lead.
Caroline pulled within 16-14, when Bunce connected with tight end Declan Egan for a short touchdown pass in the fourth quarter. But the Bucs stopped North Caroline short on the two-point try, then picked up a couple of first downs over the final 4 minutes to melt the clock and seal the win.
"I think we've taken some steps," said Kent Island first-year head coach Zach Davis, who got a 16-carry, 123-yard rushing effort from Jaxson Hess against the Bulldogs. "We've been a streaky team; win three, lose three, and then we've won two.
"This team has been a work in progress, figuring out how do we have success because a lot of these guys are new starters," Davis added. "We bring back a ton of starters next year. But we're a young football team. Those growing pains showed in the middle of the season. We're getting better and that's what you want to see."
Queen Anne's head coach Brian Mooney has learned a lot about pain this season after losing a slew of starters to injuries, and then falling to Easton, 27-26, when Mikey O'Connor hit Chase Raab with a late touchdown pass on a fourth-and-five.
"The Easton game was a gut punch," Mooney said.
But it was the Lions delivering the gut punch last Friday by way of a 21-20 victory over Parkside.
Down 7-0, Queen Anne's (5-3) pulled even on John Connolly's 28-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. The Rams moved back in front in the third quarter, but again Connolly (season-high 27 carries, 156 yards rushing) answered, scoring on a 3-yard run. But Parkside maintained a slim lead when the Lions missed the point-after attempt.
Parkside extended its lead to 20-13 on a 70-yard touchdown pass. The Lions again looked poised to respond, only to fumble the ball away inside the Rams' 5-yard line. But Queen Anne's senior linebacker Parker Whiteford came through with one of the season's biggest plays when he made a tackle for a safety, drawing the Lions with 20-15.
Aided by Ja'Dereon Thompson's 33-yard completion to Jamison Woodward, Queen Anne's drove 60 yards, with Thompson scoring on a 4-yard run with a little over a minute to play giving the Lions a 21-20 victory.
"It was a nail-biter for sure," Mooney said. "It's huge. A confidence booster. Just again the resiliency. But we're going to scratch and claw just like we have all year."
Though is took a little while, Colonel Richardson appears to have found its groove.
Ja'Zir Dickerson carried 10 times for 175 yards and three touchdowns, and Derrick Mitchell had 100 yards on 11 touches during last Friday's 44-0 rout of Kent County, the Colonels' fourth straight win.
"We coach them each week to stay true to themselves and follow the system that we run," said Colonel head coach James Jackson, his team now 5-3. "Our backs I feel like are finally starting to follow our linemen, not trying to kick out too soon, or over-run the hole."
While the Colonel's running attack has impressed over the past four weeks, so has its defense, notching a pair of shutouts.
"Can we be better? Yes," Jackson said. "I think we need better play from our two d-tackles. Our d-ends have to contain a little better. Our linebackers, we've got to flow a little better. But the last four weeks they've been bent but they haven't been broken."

title: Warriors beat clock, Seahawks
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors beat clock, Seahawks

 October 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 675
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It's won on a penalty stroke in overtime.It's also won on penalty corners — once in overtime, once in double OT.
Tuesday evening, Easton High's field hockey team found yet another way to win — and fray their coaches nerves — scoring just before the clock ran dry.
Addie Knox scored on a corner with 11 seconds remaining in regulation, boosting the Warriors to a 2-1 victory over top-seeded Stephen Decatur in the Class 2A East Region II championship in Berlin.
Easton (11-3), which has won seven straight, is seeded fourth in the Class 2A state tournament and will host fifth-seeded Hereford (11-3) on Thursday at 3 p.m. in a quarterfinal match.
"They never give up," Easton head coach Kim Neff said of her team during a phone interview Wednesday. "They never come off the field thinking like, 'We're done.'"
Decatur (11-4) took a 1-0 lead in the second quarter on Jill Burton's goal, and carried that lead into halftime. But the Warriors didn't panic.
"I feel like this is our MO really," Neff said. "We're used to coming from behind. We don't stress too much about it. We knew we had plenty of time to get back in that game. And I told them, 'Just go put a goal in right now and score and tie it up.' And sure enough they went and tied it up."
Less than 2 minutes into the second half, Easton's Myka Motovidlak smacked a drive toward the goal that was knocked into the cage by Georgia Spies for a 1-1 tie.
"We have faced a lot of challenges this season," Neff said. "Not a lot of teams have. Some teams it comes a little easier to win. I feel running into the playoffs that's an advantage for us. We know we can come from behind. We know we can go to double overtime and win. We've experienced that. I feel like that's an advantage for us."
Play evened out through the rest of the third quarter. The Seahawks then got a string of corners in the fourth quarter, but could not get anything else past Easton's defense of Bis Johnson, Kadence McGuckin, Lea Boutte and freshman goalie Taylor Bowen (12 saves).
"Our goalie saved the day," Neff said of Bowen, whose only experience in goal prior to this season was in rec league play. "Taylor just did a phenomenal job. She's so coachable and she sees the field. And she's so athletic. She just impressed all of us."
Easton survived Decatur's flurry of corners and worked the ball back into the Seahawks end with about 2 minutes remaining. It was then that Neff turned to assistant Katie Spies and said they needed to start thinking about who they were going to put on the field for the first overtime period.
But with a little under a minute to play, Easton's Ryan Quicke drew a foul, setting up a corner.
"We got in a little huddle right before we got the corner and Stella (Kabler) was like, 'This is it guys,'" Knox said. "Then I looked up at the scoreboard and it said 50 seconds left. And when (Neff) called that Liv (Olivia Orrell) was taking the direct shot, I was like, 'This is it.' Because Liv always gets it in there."
Knox inserted the ball off the end line, then moved to the left post. Orrell sent a drive that was stopped by Decatur's goalie. But the ball bounced upward toward Knox, who batted the ball into the cage for a 2-1 Warriors lead.
"It was great," Knox said. "Everybody just jumped up. I couldn't even breath."
But while Easton's players were celebrating, Neff was pleading.
"Everybody was losing their mind except me who was saying, 'We still have 11 seconds left,'" Neff said. "'Do not let them go down and get in the circle.'"
Decatur rushed downfield and got close to the circle before Johnson swept the ball out of bounds, leaving the Seahawks not enough time to retrieve the ball and mount one last threat.
"They believe in themselves and they believe in their teammates," Neff said. "It's really an awesome group of girls."

title: One is enough for Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
One is enough for Queen Anne's

 October 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 711
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Neither one needed a lesson on the importance of scoring first."The first team that scores is more likely to win than the second," Kent Island High head field hockey coach Laura Harding said.
"Getting that early goal, it sets the tone," Queen Anne's County head coach Shana Corder said. "And I knew going into this game, I knew both teams were going to come out to win it in regulation."
Queen Anne's and Kent Island played to a scoreless, double-overtime tie Oct. 19 before each team scored twice in a shootout in their regular-season finale.
It didn't take that long Tuesday afternoon.
Haley Cole's goal on a corner just 7 minutes in proved enough, as the Lions blanked Kent Island, 1-0, for their second straight Class 2A East Region I championship.
Queen Anne's (12-1-1) is seeded third in the 2A state tournament and will host No. 6 seed Centenniel (11-3) on Thursday at 4 p.m. in a quarterfinal.
"We're successful on our corners because our defense is so amazing," said Corder, whose team has won back-to-back Bayside Conference and regional titles for the first time in the program's history. "And it pays off for us. And all you need is one to go in. And honestly going forward, this is how the state tournament's going to go. One goal is going to get it."
One goal was all that was needed on this beautiful autumn afternoon.
Queen Anne's earned two corners in the game's first 5 minutes, then got a third with 7:20 remaining in the first quarter. Jordan Bilbo sent an entry pass to Ellee McLean, who quickly sent the ball back Bilbo. Positioned to the right of the goal, Bilbo centered a pass to an unmarked Cole about five yards from the cage. Cole didn't hesitate, quickly sweeping shot under the lunge of Bucs goalie Brynja Petursson and into the left side of the cage for a 1-0 lead.
"We've been working really hard on corner execution, and every practice it's been getting better and better," Cole said. "And I got the perfect pass from Jordan and happened to be the one. It was really a team effort. We were all in there to get it done and earn the corner. I just happened to be the one lucky to tap it in."
That was plenty for Queen Anne's defense.
Since yielding a goal to Crisfield on Oct. 7, the Lions haven't surrendered a goal over their last six games — not counting the 1 vs. 1 against the Bucs in the regular-season finale. Corder again played Cassidy Alexander (four saves) and Caroline Kimball (two saves) two quarters each Tuesday. And even though Sydnie Harris — one of the new mainstays on a rebuilt defense — was not 100%, she played tough minutes along with linemates Sydnee Carr and Mel Gill. Corder dropped forward Aly Edwards back on defense when Harris needed a breather.
"I just knew if we scored first I knew we could do it because my defense is amazing, and they're peaking," Corder said of a unit that has now logged 10 shutouts this season. "They are peaking right now. They've done well all season.
"I had to put one of my forwards back to defense," Corder said of Edwards. "But the kids listen to what we tell them in practice and they know everybody's role. So we're just able to be successful even being sick. I'm super proud of the girls."
Harding was also proud of her defense, which limited an opponent to one goal or less for the 11th time this season. Petursson made seven saves, including a stop McLean's penalty stroke with 7:45 left in the second quarter, and made another save when the Bucs were down a man for 2 minutes in the third quarter.
"We made the save and we battled back on all the corners down here in the first half," said Harding, whose team stopped Queen Anne's on 10 of its 11 corners.
Kent Island (9-4-1) almost pulled even with 2:50 remaining, when a drive in the circle missed connecting with Ellie Burnside at the post.
"They have a good defense," Harding said of Queen Anne's. "And they've got a great goalie. It's going to be a big battle again next year, too. I think we'll be right back here again next year."

title: Warriors use stops from Bowen, and goals from Knox, Motovidlak and Quicke in shootout to reach state final four
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors use stops from Bowen, and goals from Knox, Motovidlak and Quicke in shootout to reach state final four

 October 31, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 647
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton High head field hockey coach Kim Neff started coaching Taylor Bowen when she was five."I always knew she had the potential," Neff said of Bowen. "She's so athletic. And she's got such a high IQ of the game, that I knew she would be a good goalie. And I used to beg her all the time, 'When you get to high school, will you be my goalie?' And finally in seventh grade she turned to me at a rec game and said, 'I'm going to be your goalie in high school.' And I was like, 'Awesome.'"
That described Bowen's performance beautifully Thursday afternoon. Easton's freshman goalie stopped three of the four Hereford players she faced in the 1v1 shootout, and watched teammates Addie Knox, Myka Motovidlak and Ryann Quicke each score goals, propelling the Warriors to a 1-0 victory over the fifth-seeded Bulls in a Class 2A state quarterfinal.
Fourth-seeded Easton (12-3) advances to next Wednesday's 2A state semifinals, where it will meet top-seeded Manchester Valley (15-0) at Glen Burnie High School at a time yet to be determined.
"I don't have enough words to say about her," Neff said of Bowen. "I have believed in her from Day 1. And she believes in herself. She has confidence. And her skills are just growing and growing. She is determined to get better and better, and she has this year. She's just phenomenal."
On an unseasonably warm Halloween day that took a toll on several players, the Warriors and Bulls (11-4) were scoreless after 60 minutes of regulation and two 10-minute overtimes, pushing the duel into a shootout.
Hereford's Gracie Berquist went first in the shootout, but with Bowen moving toward her, fired a shot wide.
Knox went first for Easton, stepped to the right of Bulls goalie Julia Pfitzinger, and sent a shot into the far left corner for a 1-0 Warriors lead.
Caitlin Meeker beat Bowen on Hereford's second attempt to tie the shootout at 1-all. Motovidlak nudged Easton back in front, dodging left and scoring to make it 2-1.
Kayla Owings pushed the ball to the left post on the Bulls' third attempt, but was denied by a diving Bowen.
"Me and my other goalie Alli (Newnam) have trained all season for the shootouts," Bowen said. "And we both hate diving. So we just want to say thank you to (goalie) coach Claire (Spurry), who has been pushing us all season to dive and it worked out perfect. Couldn't ask for a better time."
Quicke was Easton's next shooter.
"I really was down on myself throughout the whole game," Quicke said. "I was getting really frustrated. And my team had told me that this is our only chance right here. 'Why not us?'"
Pfitzinger knocked the ball away from Quicke initially. But the sophomore quickly regained possession and drove the ball into the back of the goal for a 3-1 Easton edge.
"I got a little scared when she cleared it," Quicke said. "But I turned around, and I shot and hoped for it to go in."
Bowen then made a leg save on a shot by Hereford's last hope, Lauren Mathews, then watched the rebound roll out of bounds.
"That was very exciting," Bowen said of her final stop. "I was off my angle, but it all works out. So exciting. Final four."
But before the Warriors launched into a full-blown celebration, they waited for game officials to confirm the game was complete, with Hereford having shot four times and with no chance to tie. Once Easton players got the official stamp on their victory, they stampeded toward their goalie. Leading the charge was Motovidlak, who caught and embraced Bowen in midair. Bowen and Motovidlak were soon taken to ground by an avalanche of teammates.
"Definitely wasn't our best game," Neff said. "I was a little frustrated with them in the first couple quarters. We just weren't playing as a team. But somehow they pulled it off."

title: Hughes, Vikings rally past Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Hughes, Vikings rally past Warriors

 November 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 885
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — His first touchdown run evened the score in the second quarter.His second TD trimmed the home team's deficit in the third.
But it was Anthony Hughes' final touchdown run — a 11-yard sweep around right end with 4 minutes, 23 seconds remaining — that put Cambridge-South Dorchester High's football team ahead to stay Friday night, as the Vikings rallied for a 27-24 victory over longtime rival Easton to cap an undefeated regular season.
Cambridge-SD (9-0) will be the No. 1 seed in the Class 1A East Region playoffs and have a first-round bye. Easton (6-3) slipped to the No. 3 seed in the Class 2A East postseason, and will host No. 6 Parkside on Thursday night in the first round.
"Anthony is an absolute dog," Viking first-year head coach Rob Burnham said in praise of his senior quarterback. "He is so physical. He plays outside linebacker and quarterback for crying out loud. I think he tapped out on me for two snaps because he was tired.
"I'm so proud of him," Burnham continued of Hughes. "His growth as a player from a ninth grader when he came up to play for us as as young kid to now is absolutely tremendous."
Burnham's stress level may have been reaching the tremendous range in the first half, when the Vikings committed three fumbles — two leading to Easton touchdowns.
The Warriors recovered a third fumble when Jordan Horsey stripped the ball from Sterling Perkins at Easton's 2-yard line late in the second quarter. Easton could not convert that miscue into points.
The Warriors led 21-14 at halftime, and had a chance to widen that lead when it recovered a fourth Vikings' fumble on the second-half kickoff. Easton drove to the Cambridge-SD 7. But on third-and-goal, Cambridge-SD's Majestic Jones stepped in front of Warrior receiver Chase Raab and intercepted Easton quarterback Mikey O'Connor's pass in the end zone, keeping it a seven-point game.
On the very next play, the Vikings lost their fifth fumble on their 20-yard line. The Warriors pushed to the Cambridge-SD 9, where they settled for Dominic Stanco's 26-yard field goal and a 24-14 lead with 8:55 left in the third quarter.
But Easton wouldn't score the rest of the game.
"We had opportunities to put them away, to increase the gap," Easton head coach Matt Griffith said. "We failed to do that. When you do that against a good team this is what happens. It comes back and bites you."
Easton got the ball back after a Vikings' three-and-out. But on second down, Jayden Hollowell intercepted O'Connor, giving the Vikings possession on their 44.
Back-to-back false starts pushed Cambridge-SD back to its 34, where on first-and-20, Hughes found a seam and trucked 66 yards for a touchdown, drawing the Vikings within 24-20 with 6:28 left in the third quarter. Cambridge-SD bobbled the snap on the point-after attempt, and tried a pass, but was called for intentional grounding.
Kimir Lake picked off O'Connor to end Easton's next possession, but the Warriors forced a punt and carried their four-point lead into the fourth quarter.
Easton looked ready to potentially add to its lead driving from its 25 to the Vikings 26. But on second-and-10 Lake intercepted O'Connor again and returned the ball to the Warrior 40. Hughes had runs of 8, 7 and 17 yards before turning the corner for an 11-yard touchdown run with 4:23 left. Collin Bair's point-after kick made it 27-24.
"I got to get it," said Hughes when asked what he was thinking on his final scoring run. "I've got to do it for my coach, my line. My teammates trust me so I got to go do it for them."
Easton punted on its next drive. Cambridge-SD kept the ball in Hughes' hands for the better part of the final minutes before punting the ball back to Easton with 34.7 seconds left. But the Warriors couldn't mount a last threat, as Brady Walls' fourth-down heave was intercepted by Lake. Hughes took a knee to end the game.
Easton took a 7-0 lead when O'Connor hit Raab with a 27-yard touchdown pass and Stanco hit the PAT with 9:56 left in the first quarter.
Cambridge-SD answered, as Perkins was sprung for a 55-yard touchdown run. Bair's extra point tied the game 7-all with 8:53 to go in the first.
The Warriors capitalized on a Vikings fumble, as O'Connor scored on a 2-yard run for a 14-7 lead with 38.2 second left in the first quarter.
Hughes responded with a 58-yard touchdown run just 52 seconds into the second quarter to tie the game at 14-14.
"He's good," Griffith said of Hughes. "We knew coming in he's good. (Number) One and two (Perkins), very, very good. They're a load to tackle. Two is very shifty. One is just a man."
Easton moved back in front with 7:17 left in the second quarter on O'Connor's 8-yard touchdown run.
"Our defense is pretty stout," Burnham said. "I think that's the most offensive points we've given up on the season. The O'Connor kid, he's a tremendous football player. Coach Griffith had a great game plan. They did a lot of really good things in the box, attacking downfield with switch routes and different combinations. And I would not want to play them again. I'm glad they're in the 2A and we're in the 1A because I don't want any part of the Easton Warriors right now."

title: QA's Marks runs off with 2nd straight regional crown
author: Bill Haufe
content:
QA's Marks runs off with 2nd straight regional crown

 November 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 615
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Ben Marks has been in races this cross country season where he's been challenged.The Queen Anne's County High senior has also been in races this autumn where half a mile in, the only one pushing him was himself.
Thursday at the Fair Hill Race Track in Elkton, Marks separated himself from the field early on the way to winning his second straight Class 2A East Region boys individual title in 17 minutes, 01.04 seconds.
"He's very strong," Queen Anne's head coach Kim Agee said of Marks during a phone interview Friday. "He's looking good. His biggest goal is obviously states. So he's just focused on that. He knows he has some really big competition there, and he knows that he can run with them. So he has just been really focused and training for that moment; for those hills."
Marks will bid to become the school's first state cross country champion next Saturday, when he competes in the 2A state championship at Hereford High in Parkton at 1:30 p.m. Marks ran a 15.48.90 at last year's state meet, finishing second to Arundel's Eric Penkala, who won in 15:47.80.
Marks was in control early Thursday and finished over a full minute ahead of Fallston's Nicholas Spangler, who was runner-up in 18:01.16.
"A few times he uses a (regular season) dual meet as a speed practice," Agee said when Marks isn't challenged. "Sometimes he will pace himself for a bit with the group and then he'll move out and move ahead. He is super aware that he needs that competition there. So he often in the race tries to get into a mental place to push himself."
Kent Island was the only boys team to qualify for states, finishing third with 91 points behind champion C. Milton Wright (83) and Fallston (85).
Pacing the Bucs was Gunner Hansard, who placed fifth overall in 18:16.16. Rounding out Kent Island's top five were Gio Aguirre (13th, 18:57.87), Caleb Heater (16th, 19:14.01), Hudson Scarlett (24th, 19:39.31) and Jacob Keever (33rd, 20 06.24).
The top six teams in 2A qualified for states. North Caroline (7th, 180) finished seven points behind North Harford. Queen Anne's (183) was eighth and Easton (184) ninth. Easton's Will Orndoff (9th, 18:28.77) and North Caroline's Darly Ortega-Miguel (13th, 18:52.51) qualified as individuals, cracking the top 20.

title: Lions prepare for first state semifinal since 2004
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions prepare for first state semifinal since 2004

 November 5, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 618
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Lexi Kern was going to get a turn regardless."The whole team knows Lexi does well with PKs," Queen Anne's County High girls head soccer coach Mike Kern said of his daughter.
Coach Kern sent his 11 players onto the field for a shootout to decide last Friday's Class 2A state quarterfinal against Wilde Lake, but noticed his third and fourth shooters had bumped themselves further back in the lineup. After Shannon Rath and Morgan Scott each buried their PKs, Kern watched his daughter move into the third spot and step behind the ball.
"She said, 'OK, I'll go,'" the coach said.
Like Rath and Scott, Lexi Kern parked her PK in the right corner, then watched Wilde Lake's third attempt miss the mark, sealing a 1-0 victory that gave the Lions their first state semifinal berth since 2004.
Second-seeded Queen Anne's (12-3-1) advances to Saturday's 2A state semifinals, where it will meet No. 3 seed Century (12-2-1) at 2:30 p.m. at Kent Island High School in Stevensville.
"That was kind of a cool moment for me," Mike Kern said of Lexi's PK. "Nobody else wanted it, which is the crazy part. Lexi is usually four or five or six (in the PK lineup). They just did not want to take it."
The Lions followed a familiar pattern against the seventh-seeded Wildecats (7-6-3), dominating play without benefit of a goal — though one score was negated by a questionable offsides call.
After two overtime periods, the game moved into penalty kicks.
"I was surprised how calm I was," said Mike Kern, who noted an eerie quiet fell over Lions Stadium during the shootout. "It was like golf. You could hear a pin drop. Both teams. After they made them they cheered. But it was quiet as could be. I had never experienced anything like that."
Queen Anne's went first, with Rath driving a shot into the right side of the net. Wilde Lake's first PK sailed over the crossbar.
Celebrating her 18th birthday, Scott deposited her PK in nearly the exact same spot at Rath's shot. The Wildecats' second attempt went wide. Lexi Kern promptly booted her shot into the right corner for a 3-0 lead. Wilde Lake's third — and final chance — again went well over the head of Lions keeper Bea Holthaus and the crossbar, clinching the victory.
This is the Lions' third trip to the state semifinals under their 24-year head coach. Queen Anne's last reached the state semis as a 1A school in 2004, when it lost in the closing minute of double overtime to Tuscarora. Queen Anne's also reached the state semifinals in 2003, outlasting Oakland Mills in an 11-man shootout before falling in the state final.
Kern and longtime assistant Jeff Anthony have built solid teams in the past, but often were eliminated by 2A powers Fallston and Bel Air.
But this season, Kern thought he had the goods to make a return trip to the final four.
"I really thought this team had the chance to get there," Kern said. "I think they're competitors. They love to compete. Even at practice with each other, they don't like to lose. And I think they accept challenges. They've been together for so long and played together for a long time. And I think they feed off each other. I think that they're competitors is the biggest thing."
Queen Anne's has posted 10 shutouts this season, and now faces a Century program that won the state title just two years ago. Since losing their first two games of the season by a combined score of 7-0, the Knights have gone 12-0-1 and logged 11 shutouts, including 10 straight.
"They very defensive," Kern said of the Knights. "They are very similar to us. I think we've got a legitimate shot."

title: QA’s, Easton hoping for a Shore thing
author: Bill Haufe
content:
QA’s, Easton hoping for a Shore thing

 November 5, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 841
 Words 

 Read News Document

 They battled each other in one of the season's more memorable duels, playing 80 scoreless minutes before settling things in 1v1s.That was Oct. 1, when Queen Anne's County High's field hockey team outlasted Easton in a shootout, part of a 14-game Lions' unbeaten streak.
The Warriors have not lost since that clash, reeling off eight straight victories.
Wednesday, 36 days later after that marathon, Queen Anne's and Easton prepare to play in the Class 2A state semifinals at Glen Burnie High School, not against each other, but hoping to possibly create the first all-Eastern Shore state final since 1997.
"How great would it be?" Queen Anne's longtime head coach Shana Corder asked rhetorically. "I am rooting for Easton and Queen Anne's to win this one. I think that would be an awesome setup."
Warrior head coach Kim Neff seconded that notion.
"That would be so wild," Neff said of an all-Shore final that hasn't happened since Pocomoke defeated Kent County in the 1997 Class 1A championship. "That would be so cool."
Of course, Corder and Neff each know that dream match doesn't happen unless their respective teams get past a pair of unbeatens tonight.
Third-seeded Queen Anne's (13-1-1) goes first, when it plays three-time defending state champion and No. 2 seed Glenelg (15-0) at 5:30 p.m. Fourth-seeded Easton (12-3) follows in a meeting with No. 1 seed Manchester Valley (15-0) at 7:30 p.m.
"OK. So we're not undefeated," Corder said. "We're the underdog."
The Lions may have thought they would be wearing that underdog tag through at least part of this season after graduating a number of standouts off last year's 15-1 team that posted 14 shutouts and reached the state semifinals. Corder honestly thought this would be a rebuild season, since the entire defense from a year ago — with the exception of goalie Cassidy Alexander — was gone.
But after a season-opening loss at Pocomoke, Corder changed her position.
"I think they felt, 'Oh, we're not going to be as good,'" Corder said. "'We are not as good as this team.' But I was like, 'We are as good. You can't set yourself up to think you're a failure.' I think losing that game was the best blessing we've gotten all year.
"I saw their faces and they weren't used to losing, all my returners," Corder continued. "And I felt like they didn't like to lose. So I thought that gave them the drive to want to win. I felt that was our turning point."
Since then the Lions, behind their one-two goalie punch of Caroline Kimball and Alexander, and a rebuilt defense, have gone unbeaten, which included winning their second straight Bayside Conference and regional championships — a first in program history — and recording 11 shutouts.
"I feel every team we play has given us their best game because we did so well (last year)," Corder said. "They understand pressure. They've been here before. All the returners know what this feels like. Hopefully they already felt the pressure. We've had 1v1 games, overtime, blah, blah, blah. I'm just hoping they are able to rise to the occasion Wednesday."
Though Easton didn't have a 2023 season that compared to Queen Anne's, Neff was filled with optimism at the outset of this season.
"I knew we were capable of getting this far," Neff said. "A lot of these girls I've coached since they were in kindergarten, and I know their potential. It was the most athletic group that I have seen (during preseason tryouts). I think them playing some travel ball together and being on rec teams together, they know each other well, which helps."
But Easton's record was sitting at 4-3 after the 1v1 loss to Queen Anne's. The Warriors moved to 5-3 with a shutout of Kent County.
Then came a 3-2 overtime victory over Pocomoke.
"We have a long history with Pocomoke," Neff said. "And Pocomoke tends to get the victories. So I think that game, and going into overtime, and doing what they did really solidified them. Like I knew and I had the confidence in them. But I think it solidified the confidence in them, like, 'We can do this.'"
Since that victory, Easton has defeated perennial Bayside heavyweight Kent Island 1-0 in overtime. The Warriors defeated Parkside 2-1 in overtime in a 2A East Region II semifinal, then beat Stephen Decatur 2-1 with 11 seconds remaining in regulation in the region final. Easton continued its trend for the dramatic last Thursday, defeating Hereford in a 1v1 in a state quarterfinal, placing the Warriors in the state semifinals for the first time since 2021.
"I told them, 'You've earned your spot there,'" Neff said. "'We're all good teams. We made it to the top four. We're not looking at records because every day's a clean slate for every team. We haven't seen them (Manchester Valley). They haven't seen us. And so we're going in and we're playing our game. They're ready."
Notes: Wednesday's winners will meet for the state final on Saturday at Stevenson University at 11 a.m.. … Third-seeded Pocomoke plays No. 2 seed Fallston Wednesday in a 1A state semifinal at Crofton High.

title: Lions, Warriors fall shy in final bids
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions, Warriors fall shy in final bids

 November 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 807
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GLEN BURNIE — Glenelg High head field hockey coach Martie Dyer didn't panic when her team fell behind for the first time all year."I was disappointed obviously," Dyer said when Queen Anne's County took a lead less than 5 minutes into Wednesday's Class 2A state semifinal. "But I didn't go, 'Oh, no. This is going to be terrible.'"
Dyer admitted she was worried though with the Gladiators holding just a one-goal lead midway through the fourth quarter.
"I kept telling the girls, 'I need an insurance goal,'" Dyer said. "'I can't have the game be 2-1 and then risk a breakaway and tie game.' I got a little emotional at the fourth quarter and said, 'You can't lose this game.' I just started to choke up. And they said, 'We got you coach Marti.'"
It took a few minutes to ease Dyer's tension, but Brinkley Eyre's penalty stroke with 4:15 remaining provided the cushion the Gladiators' head coach was looking for in an eventual 4-1 victory over the Lions at Glen Burnie High School's Pop Whayland Stadium.
Second-seeded Glenelg (16-0) will bid for a fourth consecutive Class 2A state title Saturday at 11 a.m., when it faces top-seeded Manchester Valley (16-0) in the championship game at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium.
"I felt we played a great 50 minutes of field hockey," said Queen Anne's head coach Shana Corder, whose team had not given up multiple goals in a game since 2022. "We had 'em 2-1. We scored first, got the momentum going. They answered back a little bit later and scored. I mean they are a fabulous team. And they are so fast. I just thought my team rose to the occasion."
Queen Anne's Aly Edwards may have shaken the Gladiator faithful when she knocked the ball past Glenelg goalie Trinity Shackelford (seven saves) 4:15 into the game for a 1-0 Lions lead.
"I saw how much we were dominating and they just happened to get us on a fastbreak," Dyer said. "And that happens. And then we put that other goal in and I thought, 'OK, it's back to zero-zero.' I purposely don't try to make a big deal about that so they don't get it in their head like, 'Oh, my gosh.'"
A little over 3 minutes later, Queen Anne's goalie Cassidy Alexander was guarding the right post on a corner when Glenelg's Meghan Walker got behind her and tapped in the equalizer for a 1-1 tie.
The Gladiators then took a lead they never relinquished at 2-1 when Eyre — the talented senior center midfielder who has netted 57 goals and 21 assists this season and his headed to the University of Maryland — set up Lexi Winters' goal with 10:50 left in the first half.
But Glenelg could not extend that lead despite earning three more penalty corners over the final 3:42 of the first half against Queen Anne's Caroline Kimball, who played the second and fourth quarters, and together with Alexander made 14 saves.
"I thought they did a nice job," Dyer said of the Lions' penalty-corner defense. "They came out very fast on corners. Their fly, as it's called, came out very fast on Brinkley. Yeah, that was somewhat of a factor."
Kimball made a save 34 seconds before halftime on the Gladiators' seventh corner of the first half. Glenelg crossed a pass through the crease with 7:30 left in the third quarter but had no one positioned at the far post.
Queen Anne's (13-2-1) fired wide on a corner with 5:48 left in the third, then had another shot stopped by Shackelford a few seconds later.
Alexander made a diving stop to keep the Lions' deficit at one with 1:49 to go in the third. Queen Anne's Haley Cole then sent a hard drive from the right side that missed connecting with two teammates stationed at the far post with under a minute remaining in the third.
Kimball made a save on another Glenelg corner early in the fourth, then stopped a sweeping backhand from Eyre with 7:44 remaining.
"They did amazing," Corder said of Alexander and Kimball. "They're two phenomenal goalies."
Eyre was then fouled with 4:15 remaining setting up her stroke. Alexander returned for the stroke and watched as Eyre snapped a shot into the upper left corner for a 3-1 edge.
"We were in the game until the stroke call," Corder said. "That happens. Nothing you can really do about that. And then that put it at 3-1 and kind of seals the deal."
Glenelg, which had won its region final and state quarterfinal by a combined score of 20-1, padded its lead with under 2 minutes left, when Kimball made another big save on Eyre, only to have Lakshmi Almili feed Walker for her second goal and a 4-1 final.
"They got that late goal with two minutes to go or whatever, but I'm super proud," Corder said. "I thought my girls played really well."

title: Top-sdded Mavs oust Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Top-sdded Mavs oust Easton

 November 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 650
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GLEN BURNIE — It had found multiple ways to win since early October.Easton High's field hockey team had won in overtime and double overtime. It had won with 11 seconds remaining in regulation. It had won on a penalty stroke and in a 1v1. And it continued to find paths to victory no matter how big the game.
But Wednesday night against top-seeded Manchester Valley, the Warrior offense rarely found its way into the circle and had its storybook season ended in a 3-0 loss to the Mavericks in a Class 2A state semifinal at Glen Burnie High School's Pop Whayland Stadium.
Manchester Valley (16-0) advances to Saturday's 11 a.m. Class 2A state championship game where it will meet three-time defending state champion Glenelg (16-0) at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium.
"I'm so proud of them," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, whose team had its eight-game win streak ended, finishing the year at 12-4. "Taylor Bowen again had so many shots on her that she was able to save. They battled many corners clear. It was a defensive-heavy game and they handled it very well."
Indeed, the Mavericks, who had blanked their previous three playoff opponents by a combined 27-0, were held to their lowest goal total of the postseason.
"Their whole team, they played hard," Manchester Valley head coach Denean Koontz said. "They did a very nice job of doubling us. They took us out of our game plan a little bit. They stepped to the ball very well. Defensively, they were on us everywhere. They did a very nice job of smothering the ball and smothering our players."
The Mavericks finished with 11 corners before Easton earned its first with only 1 minute, 26 seconds remaining in the game.
By then the No. 1 seed had already built a three-goal cushion that was started off a pair of first-quarter corners.
Bowen, Easton's freshman goalie, and her defense weathered Manchester Valley's first two corners in the opening 5 minutes. The Mavericks were awarded their third corner less than 3 minutes later and converted, as Lily Brookhart scored off Shelby Wurzburger's assist for a 1-0 lead.
Manchester Valley earned its fifth corner with 13 seconds remaining in the first quarter, and again capitalized, with Allie Largent setting up Brookhart's second goal with no time showing on the clock.
"They were aggressive," Neff said of Manchester Valley, which held Easton scoreless for the first time since a 1v1 loss to Queen Anne's on Oct. 1. "And their stick skills were incredible."
Bowen made a save on the Mavs' first corner of the second period, and watched her teammates foil a second corner near the end of the period.
But Easton generated little offense, the long rushes downfield by Olivia Orrell and Addie Knox were often and quickly stopped well short of the circle.
"I do feel like my girls held their own," Neff said. "And I think this is where it really comes into play not having a turf field, and not being able to practice on a turf field, and play on a turf field. It's hard to keep up with the competition. Their whole team was just fast."
Manchester Valley picked up three more corner chances in the third, but could not add to its lead as Bowen registered two more saves on corners.
"Our defense, our middies, they all stepped up," Neff said. "I will say I feel like each quarter we came out a little more aggressive cutting to the ball better. I feel if we had one more quarter you might have seen maybe a goal."
Manchester Valley put away one more goal with only 4 seconds left on the third-quarter clock, when Carroll County scoring leader Amanda Herrold scored on a breakaway.
Though they continued battling, the Warriors mounted few threats and got their first corners in succession with 1:26 left, when Mavericks' goalie Makayla Shoaf registered her lone save.
"They played hard," Koontz said of Easton. "They did a great job."

title: Blue, O'Connor lead Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Blue, O'Connor lead Easton

 November 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 978
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Matt Griffith delivered a familiar coaching lament."We still haven't played a full game," Easton High's head football coach said. "And if we can ever figure that out before the season ends we're going to be OK."
Well, the Warriors figured out one thing Thursday night — how to win a home playoff game.
Dustin Blue and Mikey O'Connor each rushed for three touchdowns, and Jordan Horsey had an interception and returned a second takeaway for a touchdown, as Easton won a playoff game on its home turf for the first time since 1993 with a 62-36 victory over Parkside in a Class 2A East Region first-round game.
The third-seeded Warriors (7-3) advance to the second round, where they will play at No. 2 seed Kent Island (7-3) at a date yet to be determined.
"We had more turnovers than they did," said Parkside head coach Brendan Riley, whose team committed three turnovers and had a punt blocked, leading to 24 Easton points.
The Warriors had four turnovers in a 37-30 loss to the Rams on Oct. 11. Thursday they had none.
"They came into our house and beat us," O'Connor said of the Oct. 11 loss. "So we had like a chip on our shoulder. And the fact that we haven't won a home playoff game in a long time."
There were plenty of other reasons why Easton notched its first home playoff win since a 35-15 victory over Smithsburg in a 1993 Class 1A quarterfinal.
Blue was a battering ram, carrying 24 times for 125 yards — both season highs — and three touchdowns, and also caught four passes for 33 yards and another TD.
"Dustin and the o-line. I believe that group and Dustin really controlled the game," O'Connor said. "They carried us."
O'Connor wasn't too shabby either. The senior quarterback carried 18 times for 92 yards and three touchdowns, and completed 13 of 19 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown.
"Everything is centered on Mikey," Riley said. "I think he does a good job of commanding what they do."
Horsey intercepted Parkside quarterback Chris Morandi on the fourth play from scrimmage, setting the Warriors up at the Rams' 5-yard line. Four plays later, Blue crashed through the middle for a 1-yard touchdown. Dominic Stanco, who was 8 for 8 on extra-point attempts, and booted field goals of 24 and 36 yards, tacked on the PAT for a 7-0 Easton lead with 8:39 left in the first quarter.
The sixth-seeded Rams (3-7), who had not won since their win at Easton, pulled within 7-6, when Morandi connected with Tavian Dashiell for a 79-yard touchdown pass with 3:47 to go in the first quarter. The Warriors maintained the lead though, when Logan Friend blocked the extra point.
Easton answered with an 11-play, 65-yard march that ended with Blue blasting in from the 1 with 25 seconds remaining in the first quarter.
"He ran the ball unbelievable tonight," Griffith said of Blue. "Very hard. Very committed. We knew coming in we wanted to pound the rock with him. He did exactly what we asked him to do: ball security. He was able to pick us up short yards and stuff. And he extended some big runs in the middle, taking advantage of some of the alignments they gave us."
Less than 4 minutes into the second quarter, Rams senior running back Karontez Bratten (24 carries, 240 yards) scored on a 2-yard run. James Harmon's two-point run tied the game at 14-all.
But Friend gave the Warriors another short field when he blocked a punt. Parkside's punter kicked the ball out of bounds, giving Easton a safety. But Griffith opted to give up the points in favor of getting the ball at the Rams' 2-yard line. O'Connor scored on a 2-yard run with 5:20 left, then watched Stanco drill a 24-yard field goal as time ran out in the first half with Easton up 24-14.
The Warriors widened their lead to 31-14 on their first possession of the second half, as O'Connor rolled left and dumped a short pass to Blue for a 12-yard touchdown.
But Bratten, who had five touchdowns and rushed for 248 yards on 23 touches in the first meeting, broke free for a 59-yard touchdown jaunt and ran in the two-point conversion, shaving Easton's lead to 31-22 with 6:45 to go in the third.
"Is he a senior," Griffith asked of Bratten. "I hope he is. I hope he's graduating and moving out of the country or something. He's a dude. He's good. We were in a lot of the right places and he just made us miss. We'd hit him and he'd bounce off. Unbelievable."
Easton came right back though, as Blue, who bounced off defenders all game, scored on an 18-yard run around the right side, extending the Warrior lead to 38-22 with 4:12 still left in the third.
"Before the game, I expected the ball 30 times," Blue said. "But just doing it for the seniors. I just love 'em so much, and I just want to keep playing with them on and on. So I'm just going to put it all on the field every single week."
Parkside wouldn't go away, as Harmon's 6-yard touchdown run and two-pointer trimmed the Rams' deficit to 38-30 with 2:50 left in the third.
The Warriors though took control from there, scoring the next 24 points.
O'Connor's 1-yard touchdown run made it 45-30 with 1:17 left in the third. Kyree Acree intercepted Morandi on the first play of the fourth quarter, setting up Stanco's 36-yard field goal for an 18-point cushion. O'Connor was sprung for a 17-yard touchdown run, moving Easton to a 55-30 lead.
Horsey then ended Parkside's next possession, when he stripped the ball from Bratten and raced 41 yards for a touchdown and a 62-30 lead.
Bratten added a 40-yard touchdown run with 2:12 left for the final score.
Easton's 62 points were the most it scored in a playoff game in at least 46 years.

title: Thomas, Colonels romp into second round
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Thomas, Colonels romp into second round

 November 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 718
 Words 

 Read News Document

 AMERICAN CORNER — James Jackson had no explanation."This is new to me," Colonel Richardson High's head football coach said of the seemingly new-found speed of Bradley Thomas.
Thomas also struggled to provide any further insight.
"I don't know," Thomas said of his surprising higher gear. "All my brothers are linemen so I have no clue where it came from. I guess I was gifted differently."
Thomas ran for a pair of touchdowns, including a 75-yard sprint late in the first half, and also returned a fumble for a touchdown Friday night to help the Colonels rout Snow Hill, 51-6, in the first round of the Class 1A East Region playoffs.
Fourth-seeded Colonel Richardson (6-4) advances to next week's second round, where it will travel to unbeaten No. 1 seed Cambridge-South Dorchester (9-0).
"I told them in the locker room, 'It's hard beating a team twice,'" said Jackson, whose team defeated the Eagles 43-6 in Snow Hill on Oct. 11. "'We got to go out, we got to score quickly. And then don't let up.' When we scored on that first drive I reminded the offensive linemen, 'Hey, we're not done, so don't go out on our next drive and lay an egg.'"
The Colonels didn't, scoring on all four of their first-half possessions for a 32-0 halftime cushion. Colonel also scored the only two times it had the ball in the second half before Thomas' 9-yard fumble return for a touchdown made it 51-0 with with 5 minutes remaining.
Fifth-seeded Snow Hill (5-5) avoided a shutout, when Justin Shipley returned a kickoff 95 yards down the visitors' sideline for a touchdown in the closing minutes.
Winners of five of their last six games, Colonel pieced together a 13-play, 70-yard scoring drive to open the game that included an 18-yard burst on fourth down by Thomas, and ended with quarterback Tarron Hammond's 5-yard touchdown run. Thomas ran in the two-point conversion for an 8-0 lead with 4 minutes, 44 seconds left in the first half.
The Colonels blew the game open with a 24-point second quarter. Derrick Mitchell scored on a 16-yard run and ran in the two-point try for a 16-0 lead on the first play of the quarter. Thomas bulled in from a yard out and Collin Brewer powered in the two-point run to make it 24-0 with 7:13 left before halftime.
"He started the year as a backup quarterback and fullback," Jackson said of Thomas. "And then we were like, 'You know what? Maybe we should try Bradley at some wing.' He's a bruiser. We got two finesse running backs so we decided we need a pounder and he became that pounding back. Brings back that (Camron) Gondeck that we used to have (at running back)."
Snow Hill drove to the Colonel 11 on its next drive, but fumbled on a fourth-and-one. Three plays later, Thomas found open space on the left side and romped 75 yards for a touchdown with his jubilant head coach chasing him down the sideline.
"I was excited for him," Jackson said smiling. "This is something you don't see with him. Usually he'll give you 10 to 15 yards, but when he breaks a long one it's exciting. I thought he really ran out of gas the last five yards, but he made it in.
"Tonight the way he ran the football, it was good to see," Jackson continued. "The long runs he had tonight were impressive. He's not a speed guy. When I get in the locker room I'm going to ask him was he running scared, or has he found some speed somewhere."
Thomas finished with 168 yards on 10 carries.
"I just saw green," Thomas said of his 75-yard scoring dash. "I was like, 'Just keep going. Don't fumble the ball. Just keep going.' And I kept going."
Hammond's 26-yard touchdown pass to Carter Tubitt, and Morgan Demir's point-after kick with 5:30 remaining in the third quarter pushed Colonel's lead to 39-0, and started the running clock.
Thomas then intercepted quarterback Dominic Kuipers on Snow Hill's next play from scrimmage, stirring Colonel's biggest sideline celebration of the night. The Colonels were back in the end zone two plays later, with Dominque Caven sweeping 28 yards around right end ffor a 45-0 lead.
Thomas capped Colonel's scoring two plays later when he grabbed a fumble and ran nine yards for his third touchdown of the game.

title: Bucs can't sustain momentum against Wildcats
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bucs can't sustain momentum against Wildcats

 November 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 693
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — It had cut its deficit in half, rallying and grinding to a Game 3 victory.Playing on its home floor, Kent Island High's volleyball team had momentum, and may have even felt it had gained a bit of traction. But that momentum was quickly extinguished Saturday, as Williamsport built an early Game 4 lead it steadily expanded on the way to sealing a 25-16, 25-15, 23-25, 25-9 victory over the Buccaneers in a Class 2A state quarterfinal.
No. 7 Williamsport (12-5) advances to Tuesday's 2A state semifinals at Watkins Mill High School in Gaithersburg, where it will face third-seeded Calvert (15-2) at 5 p.m.
"That third set, just getting that little bit of momentum, and placing the ball and playing a little bit smarter, that's what won us the victory there," Kent Island first-year head coach Brittney Guy said.
Despite pulling within 2-1, Guy reminded her team, "That set's over with. You've got to move on. We've got to play composed and play our game."
But the Wildcats recaptured momentum early in the fourth set, getting a side out before Kennedi Lawhorne reeled off three consecutive service points for a 4-0 lead.
"We kind of got stump on our serve-receive," Williamsport head coach Karen Hampton said of the Game 3 loss. "They were serving us really tough. So once we were able to kind of fix that we kind of got back on track.
"We definitely wanted to start out with a lead," Hampton said of Game 4. "We were receiving serve, so our goal was to side out on that very first ball so we could get it and try to get the momentum early. And we were able to do that."
The second-seeded Bucs (15-3) stopped that early run via Macayla Kirk's kill to make it 4-1. An errant Kent Island return made it 8-3, bringing Skylar Norris to the service line, where she remained until delivering an ace that punctuated a 10-point service streak for an 18-3 Williamsport lead.
"Coming into the fourth set, energy was low," Guy said. "Communication was low on the court. We came back a little bit. They dug deep, but it was just a little too late in that fourth set."
Kent Island never had back-to-back service points in Game 4, as Norris' kill on the final point sealed the 25-9 victory and the Wildcats' 26th trip to the state semifinals.
"We had a bus ride; a long ride," Hampton said of her team's trip from Washington County. "So we had to kind of get loose a little bit. But once we found our groove and we found our rhythm, I felt like we were able to execute what we needed to."
That was apparent in Game 1, as a game-opening side out, coupled with Alaina Dlabich's four-point service run, staked Kent Island to 5-0 lead. The Bucs clung to their lead until a net return on a serve by Williamsport's Elizabeth Warren forged the game's first tie at 14-all. It remained tight until the Bucs struggled returning Norris' serve, helping the Wildcats score the final nine points of Game 1 for a 1-0 lead.
Game 2 was also tight early, but again Williamsport closed strong, netting the last 10 points for a 25-15 win.
"We missed a few more serves than we normally do," Guy said. "Just the technique-wise, when you come into games like this with teams like this, everything technically has to be right. You got to be ready in the right defensive spot. I don't think we completely gave it to them, but we could have played a little bit more diligent ball. The opposing team, they played very smart."
Warren's five-point service run helped the Wildcats to a 7-2 lead in Game 3. But in a game that included seven ties — the last at 20-20 — Kent Island took a 21-20 lead on Dlabich's block. Williamsport hit an errant return on a Gianna King serve to make it 22-20. Kirk's block and a returning error moved the Bucs to a 24-21 lead. Williamsport pulled within 24-23 before Kirk drove a winner into a vacant left corner for a 25-23 Bucs win — giving Williamsport its first loss in three postseason matches.

title: Stakes raised in 2nd meeting between CSD, Colonel
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Stakes raised in 2nd meeting between CSD, Colonel

 November 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 772
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It was more of an announcement than analysis."That just wasn't us," Colonel Richardson High head football coach James Jackson said of his team's 23-0 loss at Cambridge-South Dorchester on Sept. 27.
Jackson wasn't disrespecting or discrediting the Vikings, though his reaction was certainly understandable considering a week earlier, the Colonels put up 33 points while flirting with an upset of Kent Island. Since that loss to the Vikings — the only time they've been shut out all year — the Colonels have won five of six in lopsided fashion.
The latest of those romps came last week during a 51-6 rout of Snow Hill, which propelled the fourth-seeded Colonels (6-4) into Friday's 6 p.m. rematch at top-seeded Cambridge-SD (9-0) in a Class 1A East second-round playoff game.
"It's always tough to beat a team twice in the same season," Vikings first-year head coach Rob Burnham said. "I expect coach Jackson to have a solid game plan. I expect his kids to come out and play hard. And I expect the game to be more competitive than it was last time. And it's our job to make sure that it's not as competitive."
Colonel had one turnover and about half a dozen fumbled snaps from center in that Week 4 loss. But Jackson noted his team's biggest problem that first meeting was "from our (offensive) line not knowing who to block. So correcting them, that changed a lot."
Those changes have helped running back Derrick Mitchell gain a team-high 800 yards and score five touchdowns on 94 carries. Ja'Zir Dickerson, back after missing the last two games, has rushed for 774 yards and 11 touchdowns on 72 touches.
"After the Cambridge game, the running backs got a better understanding of hitting the holes," Jackson said. "You can't overrun the holes and you can't assume just because you see the flash of a jersey that the hole is clogged. You've got to stay patient and run behind your linemen."
There has also been the emergence of Bradley Thomas (41-425, 3 TDs), who carried 10 times for 168 yards and two touchdowns during last week's first-round playoff against Snow Hill.
"We didn't use Bradley much at wing when we played them last time," Jackson said. "I think having Bradley this game will give us a little more power."
Colonel also has quarterback Tarron Hammond, who has run for six touchdowns, and completed 19 of 37 passes for 662 yards, nine TDs and no interceptions.
And while Colonel has improved, it still faces one of the Bayside Conference's most athletic and fastest defenses.
"I'm glad we don't have to block ourselves," Burnham said of his defense, which like Colonel logged three shutouts this season. "Our kids run fast across the board and they pursue to the football. And we preach it in practice and we drill it. And we try to be technicians and do the little things well."
Sophomore K'Marion Hall, who was injured in the first Colonel game, returns to the defensive line, and will play tight end for an offense that has the potential to score on any down from anywhere.
"Well, those kids that run fast for us on defense also run fast for us on offense," Burnham said.
Leading the offense is Anthony Hughes, who has been a problem for everyone he's faced this season. The senior quarterback, who also plays outside linebacker, has carried 108 times for 957 yards and 15 touchdowns, and completed 34 of 64 passes for 413 yards and seven touchdowns. Then there is Sterling Perkins Jr., who has rushed for 1,047 yards and 11 touchdowns on 105 touches.
"The first thing we've got to do is limit their explosive plays," Jackson said. "We can't give up the big runs. You can't let a kid catch a 7-yard slant and turn it into a 50-yard run."
Jackson is also well aware of how Hughes and Perkins can shed and break tackles in an instant.
"You got to wrap up," Jackson said. "And if you got him wrapped up, we can't assume that one person is going to bring either one of them down. We talk about that all the time: gang tackling. And don't assume someone's down. Somebody's got to come in and clean up."
Burnham, who's never coached a team that had a first-round bye in the playoffs, said his team is healthy and doesn't expect the Vikings to be rusty.
"We want to score as fast as we can," Burnham said. "But they are not going to roll over for us. They have a bunch of seniors and they don't want it to be their last game. And we have a bunch of seniors that don't want it to be their last game."

title: North Dorchester's deepest run ends
author: Bill Haufe
content:
North Dorchester's deepest run ends

 November 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 557
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GAMBRILLS — Carol Hubbard knows it takes time to build programs.In the spring of 2023, Hubbard guided North Dorchester High's softball team to its first Class 1A state championship.
Hubbard guided the Eagles to yet another first this year, leading the volleyball team to a Class 1A state semifinal berth for the first time in the program's 11-year history.
That bid for a state crown ended though Tuesday night at Arundel High School, as second-seeded Boonsboro swept No. 6 seed North Dorchester, 25-12, 25-6, 25-13 in that 1A state semifinal.
The Warriors (16-3) will play fifth-seeded Clear Spring (14-5) at noon on Saturday for the 1A state championship at Harford Community College's APG Federal Credit Union Arena.
"It was a huge accomplishment for them to get to this point," said Hubbard, whose team had a five-match win streak ended, finishing the year 12-7. "This is the farthest that any team has gone in our program."
North Dorchester scored the first point of the night, and stayed within two to three points of the Warriors early. But a four-point service run from Larissa Blair, that included a pair of kills from Rosslyn Briggs, helped give Boonsboro separation in Game 1 at 15-6. Another Briggs kill and an ace from Aly Phillips extended the Warriors lead to 19-8. Back-to-back errant returns by the Eagles closed the 25-12 set.
"Our game plan coming in is to always serve tough," Boonsboro seven-year head coach Shelby Wallace said. "But we had a few select styles of serve that we wanted to execute today and I think we did that. Mostly the deep float and some short serves where appropriate."
Those service combinations fueled Boonsboro's most dominant set of the match, as Devin Glines served 10 straight points before Blair reeled off a five-point run in Game 2.
"Serve-receive struggled," Hubbard said of her team. "And then when we did get a decent pass we weren't able to capitalize on it on the front row. So it was just kind of a snowball. I think the front row was getting frustrated with the back row some, and then the back row would finally get (the ball) up and they were getting frustrated with the front row."
A service error and back-to-back points off Katelyn Hopkins' serve gave North Dorchester a 4-3 edge in Game 3. Boonsboro rallied to a 9-5 lead. Brooke Outten answered, coupling a kill with consecutive aces to draw the Eagles within 9-8.
But Boonsboro steadily began widening its lead. A Warrior kill and two return errors bumped the gap to 13-8. Brooke Iager then delivered back-to-back aces to open a five-point service spree that gave Boonsboro a 19-9 lead. North Dorchester kept its deficit under 10 before Anna Jackson's kill and two errant returns capped the 25-13 Game 3 win.
"The third set early on we had a little run there and evened it up," Hubbard said. "I tip my hat to them. They are a strong team.
"As far as an all-around balanced team, I would say they're the best that we've seen," Hubbard added of Boonsboro, which advanced to its first state final since 2007. "They didn't have a weak spot. They were strong all the way around. You play some teams and they have a really strong outside hitter, or a really strong middle hitter. I would say they were as well-rounded a team as we've faced."

title: Warriors, Bucs set for round two
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors, Bucs set for round two

 November 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 994
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Last Friday's 41-0 rout of James M. Bennett, was the first time Kent Island High head football coach Zach Davis had played an opponent twice in one season.Matt Griffith has seen the same team a handful of times during his two stints as Easton High's head coach. During that span, Griffith has watched his team lose to a 2A rival in the regular season then beat that same team in the postseason. He's also been on the flip side of that scenario.
So it's no surprise heading into Friday's 6 p.m. Class 2A East Region second-round playoff clash with the Buccaneers at Andy Schipul Stadium, that Griffith hasn't placed much stock in the Warriors' 43-24 victory over Kent Island on Sept. 27.
"Game one doesn't mean anything except they know a little bit about us, and we know a little bit about them," Griffith said. "That's it."
Second-seeded Kent Island (7-3) enters the game on a four-game win streak. The third-seeded Warriors (7-3) opened the season with a four-game win streak, and arrive for this second encounter having won three of their last four.
"I think myself and my coaches have done a nice job of keeping them level, knowing that we're playing a really good football team that's coached very well, and that there's going to be adjustments and changes," Griffith said. "We have to be able to respond to that and be able to play our brand of football. And hopefully we have a better night than they do."
Adjustments figure to be coming from both sides.
Kent Island will look to contain Easton quarterback Mikey O'Connor, who rushed for 250 yards and three touchdowns, and passed for 146 yards and two touchdowns in the first game. The Warriors will again hope to limit the Bucs' two-pronged running attack of Jaxson Hess, who has carried 157 times this season for 987 yards and nine touchdowns, and Nate Green (101-825-9).
As far as wholesale changes?
"You have some wrinkles, but you can't change who you are," said Davis, who spent nine seasons coaching in West Virginia before taking over at Kent Island this year. "You can't put in a whole new playbook. But you have some things that they haven't seen on tape and just hope your guys play well, get them ready to play."
After losing 52-0 to defending 2A state champion Stephen Decatur, Kent Island has reeled off four straight wins, outscoring its opponents 122-35, which has led Davis to think his team has found its identity.
"We've embraced what kind of football works for us," Davis said. "We are blue collar. We play old-school football. That's the style of football I prefer to play; I think our staff prefers to play. That's what we want to do. We want to be hard-nosed, have a hard edge. And we want to get the game to the fourth quarter because that's where we feel we are the best."
Offensively, that means running the ball with Hess and Green.
"Kent Island has some really good running backs," Griffith said. "Number 11 (Green) is fast and very strong and athletic. Twenty-two (Hess) is what I consider one of the better running backs in the Bayside (Conference) as well. He hits the hole hard. He's a powerful runner.
"What they do they do very well," Griffith added. "We're going to be challenged and have to tackle well, and do our jobs up front to give our skill guys opportunities to make plays for us."
Easton also has to be concerned with quarterback Gavan Henry (38 carries, 142 yards, 7 touchdowns), who completed 35 of 94 for 607 yards and seven touchdowns — two coming against the Warriors — and his top target Jackson Towers (8 receptions, 207 yards, 2 touchdowns).
O'Connor figures to again be the focal point for the Bucs' defense. The senior has thrown for 1,761 yards and 19 touchdowns, and rushed for 1,005 yards and 16 TDs. He also has an array of targets with Chase Raab (519 yards, 8 touchdowns), Colin Mooney (388-4), Diontaye Copper (339-5), Carter Mooney (304-1) and Zach Barnhart.
But the Warriors were aided greatly in last Thursday's 62-36 first-round win over Parkside by junior running back Dustin Blue (579 yards), who last week ran for 125 yards and three touchdowns, and also had a touchdown reception.
"I think Mikey and Dustin, they offset each other and complement each other very well," Griffith said. "And I think that's part of what's taken place now. Mikey might have done some things earlier in the season that people want to take away now, and that allows Dustin to be able to showcase his ability. He's always been a very good running back for us and he's going to get some more opportunities based on what teams do against us."
Griffith has called his offensive line a work in progress throughout the season, but has seen improvement. He knows that unit will again have to play well in Friday's round two.
"We're going up against a really good defensive front," Griffith said. "They're going to have to have a really good game if we're going to be successful. Defensively, they're going to give us multiple looks, they're going to bring pressure. We've got to control the football. And we've got to take what they give us and not force things. One of the things that we had a lot of success with the first time is we didn't get silly trying to force things."
Execution and limiting turnovers and penalties have been stressed by both coaching staffs since the preseason. But Davis thinks if he and the Bucs are to even the slate against Easton they will have to stay true to their identity.
"We got to be able to run the football and stop the run," Davis said. "We rush for over 200 yards and we win. That's what we're going to try to do on offense. On defense, if we can hold them to 100 yards or less rushing, we're going to win. That's what we want to do."
