title: QA's Marks wins three region titles
author: Bill Haufe
content:
QA's Marks wins three region titles

 February 5, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 832
 Words 

 Read News Document

 LANDOVER — Ben Marks just wanted to get ahead of the traffic.He did and never allowed it catch him.
Queen Anne's County High's senior standout surged off the starting line through the first turn for a lead he never relinquished early Monday evening en route to winning the boys 800 meters for his third title during the Class 2A East Regional indoor track and field championships at the Prince George's Sports and Learning Complex.
"I chilled a little bit on my first two events so I was going to use the remaining energy I had to see what I could throw down in the 800," said Marks, who also won the 1,600 and 3,200 meters in convincing fashion before the 800. "I wanted to go out, race with integrity."
Seeded seventh, Marks started on the outside and drove immediately for the inside lane to get ahead of the pack and grab a lead coming off the opening curve. Shadowed by top seed Andrew Stein of Huntingtown through the bulk of the race, Marks never surrendered his lead, and never looked close to fading, crossing the finish line in a personal-record 1 minute, 57.60 seconds — 7 seconds ahead of Kent Island senior Giovanni Aguirre, who ran a PR of 2:04.29.
"I'm finally getting the speed under me," said Marks, who has clocked faster times in the 800 this season while running unattached in other meets. "I opened up pretty fast in this 800. I just wanted to get free of traffic because I knew my positioning wasn't ideal."
Marks admitted his legs weren't exactly feeling ideal after putting himself through in a tough workout just two days before.
"I knew going into today that my legs weren't going to be 100 percent fresh," Marks said. "That was OK because today is not the end-all, be-all. Obviously the main goal is outdoor, dropping down speed. My legs are a little heavy so me running that time, I'm not mad about it."
Marks, who won the same three events at last week's Bayside Conference championships, again began his string of title runs with victory in the 1,600 meters, where he ran a 4:35.27, finishing more than 7 full seconds ahead of second-place Trevor Thompson of La Plata.
Marks eased to the front as the lead pack thinned in the 3,200, settled into a comfortable pace, and again was never seriously challenged after moving into first, winning in 9:56.66 — 16 seconds ahead of runner-up Brendan Bischof of Huntingtown.
"Three wins today and we're moving on," said Marks, who will bid for his first state title at the 2A state championships on Feb. 19 at the Prince George's Sports & Learning Complex.
North Caroline's Brooke Sullivan, Autumn Vallee, Linda Ridgell and Seanna Rupp won the girls 4x800-meter relay in 10:40.48, edging second-place Patuxent (10:41.54).
Like Marks, Ridgell navigated her way through a crowded start in the girls 3,200 meters, found a steady a groove and remained in front while Calvert's Madison McCurry and the rest of the field gave chase for 16 laps.
"I just wanted to get a good start and increase my chances of getting first," said Ridgell, who won in 12:03.02 — 6 seconds ahead of McCurry.
The Caroline junior admitted she began to feel tired and sore, but felt confident she could win as the race reached the 11th lap.
Five days after clearing 7 feet, 6 inches to finish fourth at Baysides, Kent Island junior Siena Koch curled over the bar with personal-record 9 feet to win the girls pole vault. Koch was also part of the Bucs' 4x200 relay along with Grace Mathews, Naiya Grossman and Ava Tippett, who finished third in 1:53.61.
The top three finishers in each event qualified for states, or hit the standard time, height or distance.
Westlake (94 points) easily won the boys championship, but Kent Island took runner-up honors with 62 points, one point ahead of third-place La Plata.
In addition to his second place in the 800, Aguirre delivered another PR in the 500, finishing third in 1:07.48, and ran a leg on Kent Island's third-place 4x800 relay, joining Gunner Hansard, Hudson Scarlett and Caleb Heater to finish in 8:42.89.
Jack Morey cleared 13-6 to lead a 2-3-4 finish in the boys pole vault for Kent Island. Desmond Abbate placed third at 11 feet, and Qualib Carter was fourth at 10 feet. The Bucs also got big points from Jack Middleton, third in the high jump (6 feet) and Josh Fuller, who was fourth in the shot put with a personal-record 46-9.
North Caroline's Amir Long-Brown earned his way to states with a runner-up time of 8.47 in the boys 55-meter hurdles.
Ridgell led North Caroline to a third-place total of 48 points in the girls competition, which was won by Lackey (85). The Bulldogs also got points from multiple sources, with Amanda Snyder taking second in the high jump (4-10), Rupp placing third in the 500 (1:27.66), and Charlotte Stuetzle running a personal-record 2:40.64 for third in the 800.
Easton's Olivia Orrell placed fourth in the 1,600 with a personal-record 5:54.16.

title: Wizards acquire Middleton from Milwaukee
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Wizards acquire Middleton from Milwaukee

 February 5, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 629
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Milwaukee Bucks are trading NBA champion and Olympic gold medalist Khris Middleton to the Washington Wizards and getting Kyle Kuzma back in the deal, a person with knowledge of the agreement told The Associated Press on Wednesday.Also involved in the trade: A.J. Johnson goes from the Bucks to the Wizards and Patrick Baldwin goes from the Wizards to the Bucks, along with a future pick swap and some second-round draft capital, said the person, who spoke to the AP on condition of anonymity because the trade had yet to receive league approval.
The move, first reported by ESPN, came one day before Thursday's 3 p.m. Eastern trade deadline.
The 33-year-old Middleton, who has struggled with injuries, leaves the Bucks after spending all but one of his 13 NBA seasons in Milwaukee. The three-time All-Star has been limited to 23 games this season, 16 of those coming off the bench, but was shooting a career-best 51% in those appearances.
Middleton helped the Bucks win the NBA title in 2021, helped the United States win gold at the Tokyo Games later that year and was someone Bucks star Giannis Antetokounmpo has raved about for years.
"It's definitely a plus having Khris back," Antetokounmpo said earlier this season when Middleton was available again following ankle issues. "Man, he takes us to the next level with his IQ, decision-making, shot ability, defense."
Milwaukee will become Kuzma's third team, after four years with the Los Angeles Lakers and parts of four years with the Wizards. The 29-year-old has averaged 17.2 points per game for his career, 15.2 points per game this season.
The move gives the Bucks some financial flexibility in that it gets them below the second apron — meaning, in the short term, some other trade options may be available to them before the deadline.
Being over the second apron had limited the moves the Bucks could make as they tried to upgrade an aging roster. The Bucks (26-22) are in fifth place in the Eastern Conference after exiting in the first round of the playoffs each of the last two seasons.
They ended up trading a player whose No. 22 jersey could hang from the Fiserv Forum rafters at some point.
Middleton owns the Bucks franchise record for career 3-pointers with 1,382. He had 12,586 points with Milwaukee to rank as the franchise's third-leading scorer, behind Antetokounmpo and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.
He ranks second in team history in games played (735) and minutes played (23,039) — behind Antetokounmpo — and third in assists (2,990).
Middleton had 24 points, 6.3 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game during the 2021 NBA Finals as the Bucks beat Phoenix in six games. He averaged 20.6 points, 6.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists in 80 career playoff games with Milwaukee. He earned All-Star Game selections in 2019, 2020 and 2022.
But injuries limited him over the last few seasons.
He was unavailable for the Bucks' seven-game loss to Boston in the 2022 Eastern Conference semifinals and played in just 33 games in 2022-23 and 55 in 2023-24. Middleton didn't make his 2024-25 debut until Dec. 6 as he recovered from offseason surgery to each of his ankles. He went scoreless in two games in late January.
Kuzma has dealt with his own issues this season. He is shooting 42% from the floor, 28.1% on 3-point attempts and 60.2% on free throws — all career lows. He scored 31 points and 22 points in his last two games.
The Bucks selected Johnson with the 23rd overall pick in the 2024 draft. The 20-year-old guard averaged 2.9 points in seven games with Milwaukee.
Baldwin, who went to high school in the Milwaukee area and played his lone college season at Milwaukee, was the 28th overall pick in the 2022 draft. The 22-year-old forward averaged 2.1 points and 4.6 minutes in 22 games this season.

title: Warriors look to extend hot streak
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors look to extend hot streak

 February 6, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1223
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Dave Finlay didn't have any real expectations."I just wanted to kind of fill that gap," Finlay said of stepping in as Easton High's head ice hockey coach this season after Tim Nowak relinquished the reins in August to accept a job with the East Coast Hockey League. "I wanted kids to play hockey."
That didn't mean Pastor Dave lacked a dream.
"I knew we lost some players from last year that were pretty strong," Finlay said. "And knowing this (Maryland Student Hockey League) has always been a pretty competitive league, and Easton's kind of been in the middle of the pack — second, third, fourth, fifth — I thought, 'OK, hopefully we can make the playoffs; finish top six.' That's my dream. And then we kind of clicked."
"Clicked" is perhaps a mild understatement, considering the Warriors carry a 9-0-1 record into Friday's Eastern Conference showdown for first-place against South River (8-1) at the Bowie Ice Rink starting at 9 p.m.
"Honestly, we've exceeded our expectations," said senior goalie Charlie Beaufait, who logged a season-high 41 saves in last Friday's 3-1 victory over Broadneck, pushing his mark between the posts this season to 6-0-1. "I thought coming in we'd lose a couple games. But we're undefeated and that's just credit to everybody on the team stepping up and filling in the absence of the players that left last year."
The Warriors graduated eight off last season's 5-4 team, including captain Sabin Long, assistant captain Ty Finlay — Dave's son — as well as two of their leading scorers, Kaleb Fluharty and Bradyn Speakman. Nowak, an NHL official for 26 years, then took a promotion over the summer as Director of Officiating Development of the ECHL and moved.
Easton athletic director Kurisha Hoffman's coaching search led her to Finlay, lead pastor of the Anchor Church in Easton. Finlay, who grew up playing hockey in Canada, had coached in the Eastern Shore Hockey Association for 10 years and was familiar with the high school roster.
"I've coached most if not all these kids at some point," said Finlay, whose son Ethan, a senior, is the Warriors' leading scorer this season. "I've coached with the Easton Ice Hawks from U8 (under 8) to U18. So I knew them going in, and they knew who I was."
Finlay acknowledged coaching club — where players usually play at one level for two years before moving to the next tier — was different than coaching a player through four years of high school, but had few reservations about accepting his first high school post.
"I wasn't super nervous being that I had Cory (Siegmann) and Tucker (Rooney) that had been with the program longer than even Tim has been," Finlay said of the two longtime assistants. "Having that foundation of those guys, I've leaned on them heavily because they've been here, they've been through this whole process. It clicked from day one."
As did former Warrior standout Brady Barnes, who after playing four years at Coastal Carolina University — the last two as assistant captain — joined Easton's coaching staff this season.
"Brady has a lot of experience playing college hockey and he's brought a lot of that stuff with him," Coach Finlay said. "We do a lot of power skating, edge work, and we've seen our kids grow a lot the last six to eight weeks."
That growth has been evident since a 6-4 season-opening victory over Dulaney in late November.
"The first game was kind of rough; we let in four goals," Beaufait said. "After that we kind of regrouped."
Whatever Beaufait and company did worked, as the senior goalie stopped all 31 shots he faced in a 1-0 shutout of Harford County in the season's second game.
"We just do a really good job of forcing the other team to go out wide," Beaufait said of a defensive unit anchored by Blake Newton and Spencer Gunshenan. "And my defense has really made it easy this year to stop pucks from outside instead of the middle. So it's a credit to everybody that's in front of me for playing their role and pushing them to the outside."
As solid as that defense has been — which has featured backup goalie James Shaw (2-0 record, 43 saves over three games), the Finlays, both father and son, agreed a big part of this season's success has been Beaufait's play in net.
"He's just been unbelievable this season," Ethan Finlay said. "He's like making 30 saves a night, and he's always standing on his head."
Beaufait has yielded 14 goals over seven games for a 2.06 goals-against average, logging 222 saves.
"He's our solid brick wall back there," Coach Finlay said. "He's a big reason why we're in a lot of these games. He's got great stats and helps us in that back end immensely."
Two other key reasons fueling Easton's success has been a balanced scoring attack and a knack for the comeback.
Ethan Finlay scored the tying goal against Crofton with 2 minutes, 15 seconds remaining in regulation Dec. 12, then watched Campbell Taliaferro net the game-winner in overtime for a 4-3 victory. The Warriors pulled out their third consecutive one-goal victory one day later, edging crosstown rival Saints Peter and Paul, 3-2, before closing December with a 9-5 victory over Kent Island — the most goals Easton has allowed in a game all season — and a 7-3 win over Queen Anne's.
Over a month later, the Warriors returned to battle Annapolis/Arundel to a 2-2 tie. The following game they fell behind 2-0 before sophomore Paige Marion — the lone girl on the team — scored to begin a 5-3 come-from-behind victory over Severna Park.
"She's been one of our main players this year," Coach Finlay said of Marion. "She's stepped in, stepped up. This year's she's been playing top line, has been scoring goals and contributing in all the big games. She's done an incredible job this year with us."
Easton routed St. Mary's. Then last Friday, the Warriors fell behind to Broadneck, which ended their season in the first round of last year's playoffs. Again Easton rallied. Ethan Finlay converted assists, first from Newton then Marion to put the Warriors in front 2-1 before netting an empty-net goal to complete a hat trick.
"Just do the simple things really, really well and battle hard and we'll have success," coach Finlay said. "We get a lot of tight games, a lot of one- or two-goal games that are down to the wire. And these guys have dug deep and pulled it out. And it's been exciting."
Easton's balanced scoring has included Paxton Echternach and Taliaferro, who have each netted four goals and four assists, Chris Howie (three goals, four assists), Marion (five goals, two assists) and Shane Gunshenan (three goals, three assists). At the top of that attack though has been Ethan Finlay with 12 goals and nine assists.
"I think he had big shoes to fill with our last captain leaving, Sabin," Beaufait said of Finlay. "He leads our team in points by a significant amount. And he's always there on defense, he's always in the right spot on offense. I think he's really done a good job not only as a captain, as a leader, but also as someone who has been a real playmaker both on our offense and our defense.
"But it's a whole team thing that kind of made us where we are now," Beaufait added.

title: Booker living NFL dream with Eagles
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Booker living NFL dream with Eagles

 February 7, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 735
 Words 

 Read News Document

 NEW ORLEANS — Growing up, Thomas Booker listened to NPR instead of music on the radio. He and his parents discussed geopolitical issues and the stock market at the dinner table. And he had the body of a future NFL lineman.The Ellicott City native had numerous paths to success. He chose football — and it has paid off.
Booker, 25, is living his NFL dream with the Philadelphia Eagles, who meet the two-time defending champion Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX on Sunday at the Superdome. After spending the 2023 season on the practice squad, "President Book" (as his teammates affectionately call him) played in every game in 2024.
Yet many believe the Gilman School graduate's greatest achievements will come after football.
"I would be lying if [I said] I haven't thought about what I want to do after [the NFL], as a businessman, as someone in the community, where I can make my impact," Booker told Capital News Service before Sunday's game.
Booker's high school coach Tim Holley can already see that future, saying of his former star player: "He's going to make much more money after football. At the end of his life, football will be just a piece of what he's done."
Booker's family helped lay the groundwork for his success. Ava Lias-Booker, his mother, is a partner in a Baltimore law firm and was named one of Woodward/White's "Best Lawyers in America" in 2001. His father, EarlThomas Booker III, played football at the University of Wisconsin and is a financial consultant. Both will attend the Super Bowl on Sunday.
A standout student-athlete at Gilman in Baltimore, Booker played five different positions for the Greyhounds and was selected to the 2016 USA Today All-State first team. He also carried a perfect 4.0 grade-point average. Ivy League schools courted Booker, but he decided to attend Stanford University.
Booker thrived at Stanford. He was a two-time team captain, made multiple appearances on All-Pac 12 teams, and was a finalist for the 2021 William V. Campbell Trophy, awarded annually to the college football player with the best combination of academics, community service and on-field performance.
"If 15 years from now, you called me and told me Thomas was the Democratic or Republican [nominee for president], I would not be surprised in the slightest," Holley said.
In the aftermath of George Floyd's murder in Minneapolis in 2020, Booker became a leading voice on Stanford's campus in the fight for social justice and racial equality. He helped found CardinalBLCK, a Stanford program designed to connect and support Black student-athletes.
Booker also was a national co-chair of "Athletes for Harris" in support of Democratic nominee and former Vice President Kamala Harris during the 2024 U.S. presidential campaign.
In addition to politics, Booker has devoted time to charitable work. He and Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean — who called Booker a "very intelligent guy" — worked with the nonprofit Leveling the Playing Field to sort and organize sports equipment donations.
"Thomas doesn't just gravitate to an issue just to be out there. He has to feel he can really contribute to advancing the cause to get engaged," Lias-Booker said of her son. "I think he relishes opportunities to be with the community."
Booker's off-field accolades and maturity were appreciated by NFL scouts ahead of the 2022 NFL Draft. But while the Houston Texans selected the defensive tackle in the fifth round, he was waived from the team just a year later.
"Getting cut [is] very objective. You're unemployed," Booker said. "This is just kind of what sports are, sometimes you just objectively lose and you have to figure out: Am I going to decide to quit or am I going to decide to keep on trying to master my craft?"
Booker, listed at 6-foot-3, 301 pounds, was signed to the Eagles practice squad soon after, but didn't appear in a game in 2023.
Philadelphia signed him to the active roster ahead of this season. He has appeared in every game for the Eagles, recording 1.5 sacks and 18 tackles. And he's expected to suit up Sunday.
Through it all, Booker's ties to Baltimore and to Gilman remain strong. Friends and family turned out when the Eagles beat the Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on Dec. 1. Last year, he attended his fifth high school reunion at Gilman, where his former classmates hadn't forgotten about him either.
"I'm thinking there are going to be a lot of Gilman Eagle fans on Sunday because of him," Holley said.

title: Crusaders extend mastery over Sabres
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Crusaders extend mastery over Sabres

 February 7, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 702
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Sam Gerdano really doesn't have an answer."I've never been able to beat St. Paul's," Saints Peter and Paul High's head ice hockey coach said. "I don't know what it is. I'm just haunted by that team."
Mason Kaplan netted a hat trick and helped set up both of Casey Burkom's goals Friday, as the Crusaders defeated the Sabres, 5-2, at the Talbot Community Center to clinch the second seed in next week's Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association B Conference playoffs.
St. Paul's (6-2-1) is scheduled to host third-seeded Sts. Peter & Paul (5-3-2) on Monday at 4 p.m. in an MIAA B semifinal at the Patterson Park Ice Rink in Baltimore.
"This has been a really fun season," Gerdano said. "We have a really young team. We have 11 freshmen out of 22 rostered. So it's not surprising that maybe they're lacking confidence at times."
The Crusaders controlled the neutral zone through the first period, and put half a dozen shots on goalie Maddie Maloney in the opening 3 minutes.
"It's exactly what we were asking for; a fast start," St. Paul's head coach Sean Baker said. "We wanted to get pucks behind their D, play down in their end at the beginning of the game to set the tone early."
Despite that dominance, Maloney (25 saves) didn't let anything past her until 3 minutes, 24 seconds remained in opening period, when Andrew Breslin and Burkom set up Kaplan's first goal.
St. Paul's extended that lead to 2-0 just 38 seconds into the second period, when Kaplan fed Burkom, who slipped the puck inside the left post.
"Goals in the first minute of the period and the last minute of the period are always big," Baker said. "You want to keep momentum for the beginning of the period and the end of the period. It's something that we talk about; first and last minute. We want to be the ones that score. We don't want to give anything up."
The Sabres cut their deficit to 2-1 with 3:44 left, as Drew Watson scored off a dish from Mason Roland. Sts. Peter & Paul went on the power play a little over a minute later, but put little pressure on St. Paul's goalie Andrew Dugas (13 saves). The Crusaders killed off the 2-minute minor. then immediately restored their two-goal cushion, as Kaplan — the MIAA B's goal-scoring leader with 21 — scored off Burkom's assist with 30.2 seconds left in the period.
"Obviously that's a big momentum shift, Gerdano said. "You cut the lead in half and they get one right back. That's a little bit of a gut punch. But it's a long game and we're always telling our players you just got to keep fighting to the end."
St. Paul's widened its lead to 4-1 with 1:53 elapsed in the third, as Kaplan and Nigel Wilson-Phillippi set up Burkom's second goal. That lead ballooned to 5-1 with 8:32 remaining, when Brendan Townsend and Burkom connected passes to set up Kaplan in the slot for his third goal.
"We seem to be peaking at the right time," said Baker, whose team has won three straight. "We're looking pretty good right now."
After a brief skirmish with a little under 7 minutes remaining left the Crusaders down a man, Sts. Peter & Paul's Buel Jenson scored unassisted with 6:45 to play. But the Sabres couldn't cut any further into their deficit.
"We absolutely came out flat," Gerdano said. "We were throwing the puck away like crazy. I think we were a little afraid to have the puck on our stick, not quite confident enough with the puck. A little uncharacteristic and it's something we can improve on going into next week. If we find that confidence and find good energy we can absolutely take it to that team.
"When they have that confidence you can tell, and we're really hard to play against," added Gerdano, whose team tied St. Paul's 2-2 earlier this season. "We have great goaltending. We're hard to score on and we got great defense. We just need to find ways to score. And if we do that we're going to be really hard to beat against anybody. We have the recipe."
Note: The Sabres have tied St. Paul's three times under Gerdano's direction.

title: Ovechkin's role-model career goes beyond Washington and Russia
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Ovechkin's role-model career goes beyond Washington and Russia

 February 11, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 771
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Logan Cooley was born in Pittsburgh just 17 months before Sidney Crosby debuted in the NHL and his hometown Penguins won multiple Stanley Cup championships during his childhood.Cooley admired Crosby, but he grew up a Washington Capitals fan for a very specific reason: Alex Ovechkin.
"That's the real one," said Cooley, who's now playing for the Utah Hockey Club. "He was my favorite player growing up."
Cooley is not alone. Ovechkin has for two decades been a role model for kids watching hockey all around the world, from his homeland in Russia to the U.S. and Canada, thanks to his powerful slap shot and physical style of play, his familiar yellow skate laces and tinted visor, and that gap-toothed smile. He is one of the most recognizable faces of the sport.
Now closing in on Wayne Gretzky's career goals record, the 39-year-old Ovechkin is now playing against many of those youngsters who grew up watching his highlights and hoping they could be like the "Great 8."
"I had Ovechkin jerseys, and everyone did. Who didn't?" U.S.-born defenseman Brock Faber of the Minnesota Wild said. "Everyone always wanted to be Ovi. ... When he was younger in his career and the yellow laces and just the style and swag he brought to the game, being so loved around the league, it's one of the coolest things in the world to play against guys like him."
The admiration starts at home, from players who were years or decades from putting on skates when Ovechkin was born in Moscow on Sept. 17, 1985. Ivan Miroshnichenko, Washington's first-round pick in 2022 who has been a teammate for 40 NHL games, said: "He's a big, Russian man. He's a legend."
That legend started early. Dmitry Kulikov of the Florida Panthers recently played in his 1,000th regular-season NHL game and is just five years younger than Ovechkin, but he recalls the buzz beginning in the '90s.
"When I was growing up, he was obviously just starting off a few years before me and he was already talked about being great back then," Kulikov said. "Obviously when he came over here, he proved it with his style of play and his goal-scoring ability, how unique of a player he is and how good he was going to be."
How unique? Ovechkin is not only second all time to Gretzky with 879 goals and holds the record for the most on the power play and most shots, but his 3,701 hits rank third among all players over the past 20 seasons. During that time, he won the Calder Trophy as rookie of the year, the Hart three times as league MVP and the Conn Smythe in 2018 as playoff MVP after leading the Capitals to their first Stanley Cup title.
Slightly younger but still with more than 750 games in North America, Winnipeg winger and fellow Russian Vladislav Namestnikov considers Ovechkin a part of multiple iterations of his career.
"I just grew up watching him, an idol growing up," Namestnikov said. "Our generation, he opened up the doors for everyone else."
Wyatt Johnston was still in diapers growing up in Toronto when Ovechkin and Crosby — picked No. 1 in the NHL draft a year apart — became hockey's biggest stars.
"They've dominated the league for as long as I've lived," said Johnston, who entered NHL with Dallas in 2022. "(Ovechkin) was a really fun player to watch, just how dynamic he is. He's one of those guys that I think him and Sid are maybe on a different level of me being kind of starstruck when I've seen them just kind of growing up, and they were dominating the league for my whole life."
Faber credited Ovechkin and Crosby for paving the way for so many players. And that doesn't just include from places like the U.S. and Canada. Florida defenseman Niko Mikkola grew up in the outskirts of Oulu, Finland, across the Gulf of Bothnia from Sweden and was locked in to that rivalry.
"Obviously you know those two big names were Crosby and Ovechkin," Mikkola said. "You followed those guys, obviously, and you see in headlines those guys are usually there. The highlights, also, you see how they score goals."
Now teammates with Mikkola with the Panthers, Nate Schmidt still considers himself lucky to play his first four NHL seasons alongside Ovechkin with the Capitals. That's full circle for a kid who grew up in Minnesota playing minor and high school hockey watching Ovechkin wide-eyed at what he could do.
"It's hard not to," Schmidt said. "Being his teammate and seeing what he does in practice and games firsthand gives you a different appreciation for what he is as a player."

title: Eagles' offensive coordinator Moore becomes New Orleans head coach
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Eagles' offensive coordinator Moore becomes New Orleans head coach

 February 11, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 667
 Words 

 Read News Document

 NEW ORLEANS — Kellen Moore, who oversaw the Super Bowl champion Philadelphia Eagles ' offense this season, has agreed to return to the site of his latest triumph as the next coach of the New Orleans Saints.The 36-year-old Moore will join an organization that has been floundering since the retirement of quarterback Drew Brees and departure of Super Bowl-winning coach Sean Payton. The Saints haven't made the playoffs since the 2020 season — the last of Brees' career.
Their interest in Moore became increasingly evident as the club waited longer to fill its vacancy than any other NFL team seeking a new coach this year.
Moore was the only assistant coach on either Super Bowl team to be interviewed by New Orleans and thus the only candidate who, under league rules, could not be hired until after Sunday's title game was played. The Saints announced their agreement with Moore on Tuesday.
Their decision mirrors that of several teams that have found success after hiring relatively young offensive coaches. They included the Los Angeles Rams with Sean McVay, Green Bay with Matt LaFleur, Miami with Mike McDaniel and Minnesota with 2024 AP Coach of the Year Kevin O'Connell. All four of those coaches were hired while in their 30s.
A standout college quarterback at Boise State, Moore had a six-year career as a practice squad or reserve QB with Detroit (2012-2014) and Dallas (2015-2017). He played in just three regular-season games, all with the Cowboys in 2015.
He moved into coaching in 2018 as a quarterbacks coach and was promoted to offensive coordinator in 2019. He left Dallas to join the Los Angeles Chargers in 2023 before moving to Philadelphia in 2024.
While Moore tended to favor pass-heavy schemes in his early years as a coordinator, he adapted when he joined the Eagles.
Recognizing Philadelphia's strength as a running team — with its big, physical offensive line, star running back Saquon Barkley and mobile quarterback Jalen Hurts — Moore oversaw the NFL's second-ranked ground game in 2024.
The Eagles rushed for a franchise-record 3,048 yards, with Barkley gaining 2,005 of that before adding an additional 499 yards in four playoff games. And when the Chiefs limited Barkley to 57 yards rushing in the Super Bowl, Moore responded with well-timed passing plays that included touchdowns of 46 yards to DeVonta Smith and 12 yards to A.J. Brown.
Moore takes over an offense featuring versatile running back Alvin Kamara and receiver Chris Olave.
While in New Orleans for the Super Bowl this past week, Moore discussed how he tries feature the strengths of available personnel in his play-calling.
"You have certain things that you have strong feelings about from a coaching perspective — certain philosophies — but I think it's important to do what your players do best," Moore said. "Going from Dallas to LA to Philadelphia, we've certainly played three different styles, and it's fun when you team up with people just building it however we want to."
Saints quarterback Derek Carr has two years left on his contract, but his future with the Saints is cloudy following a pair of non-playoff seasons with the club.
Moore will become the Saints' second head coach since Payton briefly retired following the 2021 season, during which New Orleans went 9-7 and narrowly missed the playoffs.
That was the first of what is now four straight seasons without a playoff berth.
Payton's former defensive coordinator, Dennis Allen, took over in 2021, only to go 18-25 during 2 1/2 seasons before being fired following a seven-game skid.
Darren Rizzi, who was a special teams coordinator under both Payton and Allen, took over on an interim basis and went 3-5.
He wanted to remain with the Saints and interviewed for the full-time job after this season. New Orleans also interviewed Miami Dolphins coordinator Anthony Weaver, New York Giants offensive coordinator Mike Kafka, Detroit defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn and Buffalo offensive coordinator Joe Brady.
Former Dallas and Green Bay coach Mike McCarthy also was expected to interview with New Orleans but withdrew his candidacy on Jan. 28, just days after Brady withdrew.

title: Easton advances to conference final
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton advances to conference final

 February 12, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 665
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Easton High head hockey coach Dave Finlay said his team has played well all season, and its unbeaten record supports that claim.But the Warriors closed the regular season with come-from-behind victories in three of their final four games.
They did not start the postseason that way.
Ethan Finlay scored 25 seconds into the second period and added a third-period goal Tuesday, pacing Easton to a 3-1 victory over Broadneck in a Maryland Student Hockey League Eastern Conference semifinal at the Bowie Ice Arena.
The Warriors (11-0-1) advance to Thursday's Eastern Conference final where they will face Annapolis/Arundel (11-2-1) at 4 p.m. at the Piney Orchard Ice Arena in Odenton.
"It was a little bit different," Coach Finlay said during a phone interview Wednesday of his team taking an early lead and never letting go. "We had a good start to the game; had a good bounce there. We came out from the beginning of the game and worked hard."
After a scoreless first period, Ethan Finlay gave Easton a 1-0 lead off a passing combination from Paige Marion and Spencer Gunshenan with 25 seconds elapsed in the second.
"We played nervous the first few minutes," Dave Finlay said. "Being a playoff game, little bit of nerves. So getting that goal early second period, our kids just calmed down and they kind of began to play their game. Forechecked hard. Played smart.
"We had a great second half of that first period and getting that first goal just energized the whole team," the coach continued. "They came out even more ready to go after that first goal."
Easton's second goal came 3:38 after its first, as Shane Gunshenan scored off Campbell Taliaferro's assist.
"We've had multiple players contributing, just always showing up," Coach Finlay said. "And we've probably out-chanced every team, not always scored, but we've always had, I felt, like more good chances to score.
"Last night we just took advantage of those first couple chances to get those first couple goals and it just helped," Finlay continued. "We teach them, 'Pressure the puck, pressure the puck, good things will happen.' And last night was the same way."
Finlay said the Warriors had chances to lengthen their lead but Bruins goalie Braedon Goloboski (25 saves) came up with some big saves to keep Broadneck's deficit at two.
Easton's first-year head coach also noted the Bruins (6-5-2) had chances to tie the game and cut into their deficit during the second period, but Warrior goalie Charlie Beaufait delivered yet another solid performance, stopping 27 of the 28 shots he faced.
"Charlie was strong," Coach Finlay said. "There was a period there where we were kind of on our heels a little bit and Charlie made two or three big saves. They had some good chances that could have tied up the game when it was 1-0 and 2-0 even. And he stood strong in the second period.
"And our defense has been playing well all year," Finlay added. "Those boys back there have been getting their (opposing) players to the outside edges, giving them bad angle shots, and Charlie's been able to make the saves. Even when we have a missed opportunity on our defensive end, he's there just taking that shot from the slot and being able to make that big save that we need. And every game he's got four or five of those big saves that just keeps us in the game."
Easton widened its lead to 3-0 with 6:27 remaining in the game, when Ethan Finlay — the Warriors' leading scorer — added his second goal off an assist from Marion.
"We were a little bit slow in the third period and so when we were able to pop that third one in we really kind of secured it at that point," Coach Finlay said of his son's second strike. "It really lit a fire the last five or six minutes of the game, just to kind of lock it up."
Broadneck avoided the shutout with 2:24 left when Eliot Martin scored off an assist from Gavin Monaco.

title: Sharp Road Park project will bring multiple fields to Denton
author: AHMAD GARNETT agarnett@chespub.com
content:
Sharp Road Park project will bring multiple fields to Denton

 February 12, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: AHMAD GARNETT agarnett@chespub.com | Section: News 
 
 503
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON — Caroline County is working with the Town of Denton on revamping Sharp Road Park into multiple sports fields.The park, when complete, will house a baseball field, softball field and small multipurpose field.
The Sharp Road site will serve as the field used by the town and county for American Legion, junior and senior league baseball and softball, replacing the Lockerman Field on Lockerman Road, which is falling into disrepair.
Sharp Road Park was originally bought by Caroline County about two decades ago with Program Open Space funding. Program Open Space is a state program that allocates funding from transfer tax collections.
The county did not have money to use for any more renovations for the park at the time of the purchase, so it gave the site to the town of Denton.
The town built a basketball court, constructed a parking lot, leveled the fields off and put in some irrigation at the park before running out of funding for more improvements.
The plan is to subdivide the park into three sections of property, according to the county.
"The town is going to give one of those three pieces back to the county," Caroline County Commissioners President Travis Breeding said, "the back piece behind Choptank Community Health, and we're gonna build a baseball field, softball field, a multi purpose field and a parking lot there."
The location for the project comes from Breeding's research on Program Open Space money.
Lockerman Field was not purchased with Program Open Space money, meaning the property is unattached to any stipulations of the program.
If Program Open Space is used to fund improvements on a property, the improvements must stay for 20 years without being altered, a commitment the county was not willing to make at the Lockerman site.
"We had other property in the town, which is the Sharp Road property that was already in program open space," Breeding said. "So it only makes sense to take Program Open Space development funds and use it on a piece of property that is already in Program Open Space so we're not tying down additional property."
The new Sharp Road facility will offer updated fields and equipment.
But open space currently at the site will remain under the town's control, ensuring other sports teams can continue to practice and play there.
"Currently the park is wide open soccer, lacrosse and everybody uses different things," Denton council member Dallas Lester said. "We will continue with that, and now we will have the opportunity to have baseball, softball and American Legion in the town."
One concern for the Denton Town Council is the lights for the fields and keeping the residents across the street from the Sharp Road Park happy.
"It's going to be a good community space where kids will have an opportunity to play under the lights and enjoy athletics and be active and healthy," Breeding said. "The new lighting is designed to pollute less, so there's less light that will actually admit onto neighboring property, it's more efficient. The lighting is directed better. We'll have night shades over it."

title: Wicomico survives Easton scare in OT
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Wicomico survives Easton scare in OT

 February 13, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 606
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Se'Lah Foreman keeps doing this sort of thing and she might earn a nickname like … Magic.Foreman scored a layup as the buzzer sounded in overtime Thursday night, lifting unbeaten Wicomico to a 50-48 victory over Easton.
"I knew I had to do something," said Foreman, whose buzzer-beater lifted the Indians to a two-point victory over Stephen Decatur 10 days earlier. "I knew what to do. So I just took the shot and I made it."
Foreman (game-high 27 points) hit a game-tying 3-pointer with 10 seconds remaining in regulation, sending the game into overtime knotted at 42-42.
Easton (10-6) suffered a big blow just 5 seconds into the 4-minute overtime when star freshman Maia Bailey (14 points) went down with an apparent leg injury. Bailey did not return.
Foreman, who hit a buzzer-beater to end the first quarter to give Wi-Hi (17-0) a 10-6 lead, hit a pair of free throws to put the Indians up 44–42 early in OT. Ki'Mauri Lewis' layup 8 seconds later pulled the Warriors even at 44-all.
Warrior junior guard Serenity Velez (team-high 20 points) then found Jordan Colbert for back-to-back layups, pushing Easton to a 48-44 lead with 1:46 left.
Wicomico drew within 48-46 on Ta'Nia Armwood's only field goal of the game with 1:16 left. Foreman scored on a drive to tie the game at 48-48 with 33 seconds to go. The Indians then got the ball back into Foreman's hands, and watched the junior guard drive through traffic in the lane and put up a shot that dropped as the buzzer sounded.
"I'm getting too old for this," Wicomico head coach Willie Downing said.
"The biggest thing you can say about her is, heart. All heart," Downing said of Foreman. "She plays with it no matter what the score is. And she just brings the rest of the team with her."
The first half turned into a duel between Foreman, who scored 14 of Wi-Hi's 18 first-half points, and Velez, who accounted for 14 of Easton's 16 points in the half.
Up 18-16 at the break, the defending Bayside Conference-champion Indians appeared to be pulling away as they carried a 31-26 lead into the fourth quarter.
But Easton rallied.
Addison Chandler connected on a 3-pointer from the top of the key, pulling the Warriors within 31-29 with 7:24 to go in regulation.
Foreman and Carlisa Johnson (11 points) converted back-to-back steals into layups, nudging Wicomico's lead to 35-29 with 6:10 left.
But Velez drained her fourth 3-pointer of the game, shaving Easton's deficit to 35-32. Sam Murphy made a steal and drove in for a layup, trimming the Indians' lead to one. Natalia Almonte's layup put Wi-Hi ahead, 37-34. But Bailey buried a 3-pointer with 4 minutes left, tying the game at 37-all.
Bailey then scored consecutive baskets to give the Warriors a 41-37 lead with 2 minutes to play in regulation. Trinity Purnell's layup pulled the Indians within 41-39 with 37 seconds to go in regulation. Murphy converted one of two attempts from the foul line, bumping Easton's lead to 42-39 with 35 seconds left in the fourth period before Foreman hit her only 3-pointer of the game from the right side with 10 seconds to go, forging a 42-42 tie.
"I don't think anybody expected us to go into overtime with them that's for sure," Easton head coach Lesley Staehli said. "I think they are a little bit down on themselves, but they don't have anything to be down about. To play with an undefeated team like Wi-Hi. … We did awesome. I have no complaints about it. I'm so proud of them.
"I'm so excited," Staehli added. "Playoffs are coming and we're playing our best ball right now."

title: Sabres rout Jags, earn shot at crown
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres rout Jags, earn shot at crown

 February 14, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 604
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Saints Peter and Paul High's girls basketball team knows the potential is there for a title.The Sabres also recognize there's still work to be done.
"Today wasn't our best," junior forward Avery McCall said.
And though it may not have been one of its best efforts, Sts. Peter & Paul again jumped to an early lead against Salisbury Christian late Friday afternoon en route to a convincing 40-15 victory in an Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference semifinal.
The second-seeded Sabres (12-8) will bid for their second ESIAC crown in three years Monday, when they travel to Georgetown, Delaware to face defending champion Delmarva Christian (15-4) at 3:30 p.m.
"I'm happy that we won," Sts. Peter & Paul head coach Katie Murphy said after her team won for the ninth time in 10 games while stretching its win streak to eight. "But there's things we definitely need to clean up."
Sts. Peter & Paul, which built big leads in its two regular-season victories over the Jags (8-10), took command early again yesterday, moving to a 12-0 lead after the first quarter, with Lucy Rankin and McCall accounting for all but two points in the opening surge.
Natalie Bailey (13 points) drilled a 3-pointer 40 seconds into the second quarter for Salisbury Christian's first points. And though McCall and Rankin continued providing the bulk of the Sabres' scoring while widening the lead to 29-8 at halftime, Murphy didn't think her team's offense flowed as smoothly compared to the previous two meetings.
"It was a very physical game and I think that threw some of the girls off," Murphy said. "But we didn't play our basketball. We didn't play Sabre ball. We hustled after every ball. But they were out-rebounding us at halftime. They're never-give-up, no-quit grit in this game is what helped them win. But we have a list of things to work on."
McCall, who had a game-high 23 points to go with seven rebounds and six steals, hit a half-court 3-pointer to give her 17 first-half points.
"Sometimes I think they seek me to get the game started when we start slow; kind of a boost of confidence," McCall said of her team. "But everyone's capable of starting the game themselves. Today Emma (Hainey) scored first. And there's been games Lucy's had the first points of the game. I don't think I'm expected to get us started every time."
The Jags were held scoreless again in the third quarter, which ended with the Sabres holding a 35-8 lead. Murphy pulled her starters for much of the fourth, but called time to settle her team down in hopes of improved passing and fewer turnovers.
"I tell them all the time, 'Believe it and do it,'" Murphy said. "'When you go out there, just go play basketball. You have everything you need to be successful. You have the skill set.' We've been working all season. They know what they need to do.
"In some games like this, it's high pressure and nerves get to you," Murphy added. "It makes you nervous to go out there and make a mistake. We didn't start out strong. We kind of pulled it together. But we played sloppy."
Rankin agreed her and her teammates may have been battling a case nerves, but like McCall is optimistic about Monday's title clash.
"I feel like in this game we were playing a little scared just because it's a playoff, even though we've played them twice and beaten them twice," Rankin said. "It's just the next level so we need to be a little better. But I think if we just play cool, calm and collected as my coach says, we can do anything."

title: Hemingway, Sabres romp into postseason
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Hemingway, Sabres romp into postseason

 February 14, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 668
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Saints Peter and Paul High boys head basketball coach Gary Gould has been trying to get a more complete-game from Garett Hemingway this season.If the senior standout's latest outing is any indication, he's getting closer to that well-rounded game as he draws closer to the 2,000-point career milestone.
Hemingway splashed five 3-pointers as part of a season-high 43-point performance Friday afternoon, as Sts. Peter & Paul extended its winning streak to 13 with a 65-46 victory over Park School in its regular-season finale.
The defending Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference champion-Sabres (18-9 overall, 11-1 conference) are seeded No. 1 for the approaching playoffs and slated to host a semifinal on Thursday.
"He finally executed what I've been trying to get him to do; (play) a whole game," said Gould of Hemingway, who also had eight rebounds, three blocked shots and three steals. "Don't rely just on your three-point shot. Put more pressure on the defense by penetrating. Get to the (foul) line. And then just rebounding. If he can get defensive rebounds, then that can start our offense. And that's what he did a lot of today."
Hemingway snagged defensive rebounds to trigger the Sabres' transition game, connected from beyond the arc, and consistently drew contact while driving toward the rim.
"He's a great player," Park head coach Edwin Gordon said of Hemingway, who is 31 points away from becoming the first player in school history to score 2,000 career points." It's hard to game-plan for him no matter what you do. He finishes at the rim. He's tough to guard. He's been giving us headaches for the last three years. I'm happy he's graduating. Can't game-plan for a kid like that."
Hemingway drained his first 3-pointer with 4 minutes, 29 seconds remaining in the first quarter to give Sts. Peter & Paul a 14-3 lead.
But the Bruins (8-14) began finding holes in the Sabres zone, and pulled within 20-16 by the end of the first quarter. Park moved to a 21-20 lead 1:28 into the second quarter on Zach Chait's 3-pointer, and made in 23-20 on Sam Polakoff's put-back.
Hemingway answered with a three-point play, a 3-pointer from the top of the key, and a drive through the lane, putting Sts. Peter & Paul ahead at 28-25 with 3:23 left in the half.
Jack Cohen (15 points) and Chait (nine points) kept the Bruins close at 31-29. But Hemingway scored on a baseline drive, converted one of two free throws, then scored a fastbreak bucket to help the Sabres carry a 36-29 lead into halftime.
"I think it's just defense mainly," Hemingway said of Sts. Peter & Paul's hot streak. "We've got so many defenses that people can't plan on. We'll come out in a 2-1-2 usually in most games, and usually get a lot of turnovers from that. And then we'll hop into a man-to-man."
Hemingway scored all 13 of the Sabres' third-quarter points, stretching the hosts' lead to 49-38. A Cohen basket cut the lead to 49-40 early in the fourth. But the Sabres reeled off nine straight points for a 58-40 lead before Polakoff's 3-pointer ended a near 4-minute scoring drought for the Bruins.
"Second half we lost momentum," said Gordon, whose had his full complement of players for only three games this season due to illness and injuries. "We found the looks we wanted. We just couldn't finish. We got every look we wanted to get. We didn't finish, they did. That's the difference in the game."
Gould lifted his starters with 2:44 remaining and the Sabres holding a 62-43 lead.
"This team is really playing well," said Gould, who got 10 points from JJ Rardin and eight from Peter Mangold. "I think they understand that our defense is creating all of our offensive opportunities that we have. And they ask to play certain defenses at certain times in the game. From a coaching standpoint that feels like they are invested and they are locked in, and they know what it's going to take to do it. I'm impressed with the effort."

title: Sabres can't break Royals' rule
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres can't break Royals' rule

 February 18, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 756
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GEORGETOWN, DEL. — They were separated by two points during their two regular-season games.And they were separated by two halfway through their third meeting.
That separation became wider though in the second half Monday, as Delmarva Christian School hit big shots in the paint and beyond the arc on the way to a 53-42 victory over Saints Peter and Paul High, giving the Royals their sixth Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference girls basketball title over the past seven seasons.
"Delmarva Christian played fabulous today," Sabres head coach Katie Murphy said. "I mean Bella (Marinelli), I think she hit just about every shot. I'd love to see her shot percentage from today. She was amazing. They all were. They played really hard. They executed correctly. They deserved to win."
And yet for the third time this season, this rivalry was shaping up to be a duel to the end. Sts. Peter & Paul (12-9), which came in on an eight-game winning streak, broke a 9-9 first-quarter tie when Kaylin Palmer (nine points) hit a bucket and Avery McCall converted one of two from the foul line for a three-point lead after one complete.
But the Royals (16-4) began connecting from beyond the arc in the second quarter. Marinelli, who drained four 3-pointers as part of a game-high 20-point performance, freshman Avery McCoy (nine points) and Layni Dukes (11 points) each hit 3-pointers, with Dukes' tying the game at 19-all with 1:31 left in the half.
Lucy Rankin kept the Sabres close, scoring six of her 12 points in the second quarter. A pair of Marinelli free throws and a Dukes layup moved Delmarva Christian to a 23-19 lead before Sts. Peter & Paul's Annie Albright scored to make it a two-point margin at the half.
The Royals began to widen their lead early in the third, as Marinelli buried a 3-pointer and Eve Bohinski (10 points) made a three-point play for a 29-21 lead. Emma Hainey's two free throws halted Delmarva Christian's mini-burst.
And though Sts. Peter & Paul remained within striking distance, the Royals began patiently working the ball around the perimeter before driving through the lane for layups that steadily extended their lead. Bohinski and Dukes each found an open lane for layups before McCoy's three-point play pushed Delmarva's Christian's lead to 36-26 late in the third.
"We made a couple shots that kind of got us going," Royals head coach Frank Roach said. "The first two games, jump shots weren't really falling much. I think that helped. And then we changed up our defense a little bit in that third quarter and that gave us a little bit of breathing room. I think the defensive switch is what kind of broke the game open."
The switch from man-to-man to a box-and-one helped Delmarva Christian outscore the Sabres, 13-7, in the third. Still, Sts. Peter & Paul stuck around, Palmer scoring the last basket of the third and the first of the fourth, drawing the Sabres within 36-30.
But Marinelli scored on a drive through the paint, hit a 3-pointer, watched Dukes score a layup, then drove through the middle again to give the Royals a 45-32 lead with under 4 minutes remaining.
"I told them to space it out," Roach said of his team's offense. "I know they (SSPP) were in a hurry to try to get some turnovers, get some steals. I said, 'Hey. Space the floor, use your handle. Let's attack the basket.' They did a good job attacking the basket."
Delmarva Christian's lead floated between 13 and 15 points before McCall, who notched her sixth double-double of the season with 15 points and 10 rebounds — both team highs — scored the Sabres' final seven points.
"I think nerves had a lot to do with it," Murphy said of her team. "I think in some cases we may have wanted to win too much instead of playing our game. Not settling into offense was a real huge thing. We were able to do that in the previous two games. And here they couldn't get their offensive rhythm no matter how many times we said, 'Run this offense. Do this. Slow it down.'
"Again, it's a young team," added Murphy, who has no seniors on the team. "They have grown a lot and continue to learn. They're a great group of kids who fought until the very end. There's no reason why they can't do this again next year."
Notes: McCall was named the ESIAC player of the year, and was joined on the all-conference first team by Rankin and Albright. … Hainey was honorable mention.

title: Easton's Weems, QA's Clagett win region crowns
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton's Weems, QA's Clagett win region crowns

 February 18, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 902
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Katie Spies may have felt she was trapped in some kind of time warp.Easton High's first-year head swim coach was next to Maddie Weems as Maddy Finch swam the 200-yard individual medley during Saturday's Class 3A/2A/1A East Regional championships when Weems said, "I'm so nervous for her."
One event later, Spies had Finch by her side, watching Weems compete in the 50 freestyle, when Finch admitted out loud, "I'm so nervous for her."
"I was like having deja vu," Spies said. "Maddy Finch was standing there and I told her, 'You literally are saying the exact same thing as your best friend."
The best friends combined for a first place and three runner-up finishes individually Saturday at the Edward T. Hall Aquatic Center in Prince Frederick, helping Easton to a fourth-place finish in the girls competition.
"Really proud of them in terms of their hard work and dedication and positivity toward always wanting to do better, even when we're small," said Spies, who had eight girls and just two boys on this year's team. "It doesn't hold them back from trying to give it their all. Their performance shows what they have in their heart."
While Northern of Calvert (326 points) won the girls competition, Easton totaled a Bayside-Conference-best 228 points, followed by Stephen Decatur (215), Kent Island (207) and Queen Anne's County (127).
Spies noted before the meet started, Bayside teams gathered around the warmup pool in a show of unity, with one side shouting, "Eastern" and the other "Shore."
"It was really cool," Spies said. "The camaraderie on the Bayside Conference was really fun to watch."
The top three swimmers in each event from each of the state's four regions automatically qualified for Saturday's state championships at the University of Maryland in College Park. The next 12 fastest times in each event between the four regions also qualify.
Weems and Queen Anne's County junior Madelyn Clagett were the lone Bayside swimmers to earn region titles Saturday.
The defending 3A/2A/1A state champion in the 200 freestyle, Weems opted to swim the 50 and 100 freestyles this year. The junior clocked a time of 24.86 seconds in the 50 free, finishing second to La Plata senior Jadyn Woolsey (24.22).
"It was a great race in the 50 freestyle," Spies said. "They weren't in the lanes next to one another because of Maddie's seed time coming in. She hasn't swam the 50 free too many times this season, so her seed time wasn't equal to what I've been seeing in her relay in terms of splits for 50. It would have been cool to see her swim next to that girl and that would have pushed her a little bit more. Not saying she'd win necessarily, but more of a potential when you're next to that person."
Weems came back and took a full second off her seed time to win the 100 freestyle in 54.08, beating runner-up Lily Smith (55.87) of Northern. Clagett was third in 55.93, shaving 3 seconds off her seed time.
Clagett's biggest drop though came in the 200 freestyle, where she won in 2:01.79, lopping more than 10 seconds off her previous career best.
"She did fantastic," Queen Anne's head coach Kelley Moore said of Clagett. "She had goals, and I think part of it started last year at the end of the season when she swam really well. She's worked really hard. She's been doing some extra training to make sure she was ready. She was focused and determined and she made it happen."
Finch also made it happen, logging season-bests in the 200 IM (2:15.35) and 100 breaststroke (1:07.39), finishing second in both.
"She and Maddie are very similar in their mindsets," Spies said of Finch. "She knew she was going to swim somebody in the 100 breaststroke that had a seed time (1:05). But she was up for the challenge.
"Those two are so funny," Spies said of Finch and Weems. "They're literally like each other's left arm."
Claire Morris and Finch went from swimming the 100 breaststroke, to teaming with KC Sauter and Weems to place second in the 400 freestyle relay with a season-best 3:53.50.
"Ninety percent best swims this weekend," Spies said of her team. "It's just incredible the things they can do when they put their minds to it."
The Bayside's other runner-up finish on the girls side was delivered by Kent Island sophomore Maddie Parks, who took 3 seconds off her time in the 100 backstroke, finishing in 1:01.85.
Kent County's Henry Martinez was second in both the boys 50 and 100 freestyles. La Plata's Clinton Couples out-touched Martinez in the 50 free, winning in 21.86, edging the Trojan senior's 21.89. Martinez took over a full second off his 100 free time (48.15), finishing second to La Plata's Gavin Abelende (46.36).
Kent Island's Kara Seymour placed third in the 50 freestyle (25.21) and 100 breaststroke (1:09.80) to automatically qualify for states, and joined Parks, Jordan Sarier and Alexia Grossman to take second in both the 200 medley relay (1:55.94) and the 200 freestyle relay (1:45.79).
Kent Island's Jack Da Rosa was third in the 100 freestyle (52.03), and teamed with Dylan McCormick, AJ Harmse and Keefer Pullen to place third in the 400 free relay (3:38.38), helping the Bucs (200 points) finish fourth in the boys team race, five points ahead of fifth-place Queen Anne's.
Also earning automatic spots at states were Queen Anne's Levi Corcoran, third in the 500 freestyle (5:02.73), and Cambridge-South Dorchester's Rodney Harris, third in the 100 breaststroke (1:07.15).

title: Hemingway reaches 2,000 career points as Sabres reach MIAA C final
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Hemingway reaches 2,000 career points as Sabres reach MIAA C final

 February 19, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 892
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Garett Hemingway wasn't worried about the approaching milestone."I was more nervous about winning the game," Saints Peter and Paul High's senior shooting star said.
That was understandable considering the top-seeded and defending champion Sabres were deadlocked with fourth-seeded Beth Tfiloh halfway through Tuesday night's Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference boys basketball semifinal.
"I told them we had 16 minutes to get it right," Sts. Peter & Paul head coach Gary Gould said of his halftime pitch to his team. "I said, 'We should be down double digits the way we played in that first half. We did not play one minute of our type of defense. In order for us to win we got to play defense.'"
The Sabres held the Warriors to just two fourth-quarter points and watched Hemingway become the school's first player to reach 2,000 career points as part of a game-high 37-point performance that boosted Sts. Peter & Paul to a 61-45 victory.
Winners of 14 straight, the Sabres (20-8) will bid for their second straight MIAA C Conference championship Saturday at 8 p.m., when they face Key School at UMBC's Chesapeake Employers Insurance Arena in Baltimore.
"Awesome," Gould said of reaching the C Conference final for a third consecutive year. "The first time we went, none of us really knew what that was like. I lost focus on a couple things in that game and they got out on us.
"The second time I knew what not to do and the kids did everything 100 percent correct," Gould said of last year's title game. "And this year's team I think is better. I think if we continue to play Saints Peter and Paul basketball we could go back-to-back."
But Gould wasn't thinking about a second straight title at halftime.
Hemingway accounted for 10 of the Sabres' 15 first-quarter points, which ended with Sts. Peter & Paul holding a six-point lead.
But the Warriors (15-19) outscored the hosts 16-10 in the second quarter, as Rafi Samuel scored nine of his team-high 15 points in the period. Samuel hit a layup with 3 minutes, 29 seconds left in the quarter to give Beth Tfiloh its first lead at 21-20, then canned a jumper to make it 23-20.
Hemingway hit his only 3-pointer from the top of the key to knot the game at 23-all with 2:34 left before the break. JJ Rardin (16 points) nudged the Sabres back in front with a layup, but Adam Arfa's basket pulled the Warriors into a 25-25 tie at half.
"At halftime we're just like, 'Defense,'" Hemingway said. "'We got to pick up the defense.' We picked it up, got a couple of steals, moved the ball well."
A layup and three-point play from Hemingway gave Sts. Peter & Paul a 30-25 lead early in the third. But Beth Tfiloh was back even on a pair of free throws and a 3-pointer from Natan Brum (eight points). Rardin scored on a drive, but Samuel buried his third 3-pointer to push the Warriors back in front at 33-32. Evan Rubinstein's trey with 2:24 left in the third forged the game's final tie at 38-38.
But Hemingway turned a Rardin assist into a three-point play, then followed his own shot for a 43-38 Sabres lead.
"Garett is the difference in all the games that we played when they beat us," Beth Tfiloh head coach Ari Braun said. "I thought we defended him as well as we could in the first half (holding him to 13 points). But the discipline required on our part to keep that up for the whole game, it was just probably too tall of a task for our kids at this point. They definitely gave the effort, but he is a tough kid to guard."
Sts. Peter & Paul's lead was only two with 40 seconds to go in the third. Porter Bishop hit a foul shot, missed the second, but Hemingway grabbed the rebound for a put-back that gave the Sabres a 48-43 lead heading into the fourth.
From there, the Sabres took control.
"Their half-court pressure. … I bet we probably had as many turnovers in that fourth quarter as shots," Braun said. "They just did a really good job of clamping down in that fourth quarter, limiting us to one (shot on a possession), and sometimes none.
"For us to win that game we had to maintain our discipline and composure for 32 minutes," Braun added. "I would say we did it for 24 minutes. We kept it and they just were too strong for us in the end."
Hemingway scored on a follow in the first minute of the fourth quarter. Then with 5:01 remaining, he scored on a follow to reach the 2,000-point mark and stop the game.
"I was like, 'Why did they stop the game?'" Hemingway said. "I was looking around, then I heard 2,000, and I was like, 'Oh.' I didn't think I was close to it."
Brum's follow shot with 3:58 left were Beth Tfiloh's only points in the fourth, as the Sabres outscored the visitors, 13-2, in the final 8 minutes.
"I think we got a little angry because of the way we were playing," Sabres reserve Hank Wolters said. "We went in the locker room and kind of talked it over. And we were like, 'Hey, they're playing harder than us. They're playing stronger and more tough than us.' And we just turned it on at the end."

title: Lions ride defense on way to clinching North title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions ride defense on way to clinching North title

 February 19, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 737
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — Mike Kern was never worried about the offense."My biggest focus so far is making sure we play good defense," Queen Anne's County High's girls head basketball coach said at the beginning of the season.
Well, the Lions play defense like they did Wednesday, their head coach is going to be pleased.
"Defense is going to win us championships. And defense won us this game tonight," Kern said after Queen Anne's held rival Kent Island to its lowest point total of the season during a 33-21 victory that clinched the Lions third North Bayside title in three years.
"We were there last year," Kern said of his team playing in the Bayside Conference championship which ended with a loss to Wicomico. "They like playing at the (Wicomico) Civic Center, playing in that environment. It's always fun.
"And we'll play against a 2A school it looks like," added Kern, who figures to face either defending champion Wicomico or Parkside in next Tuesday's conference title game in Salisbury. "So therefore it will give us a good look at a team we might see in the playoffs. Hopefully we come away winners, but if not, at least we'll get a good look, get video on 'em and then be ready to match up against them in the playoffs."
The first time Queen Anne's and Kent Island matched up against each other this season, the Lions scored the game's first 18 points en route to a 49-28 victory Jan. 16 in Centreville. That wouldn't be the case in the rematch, as it was the Buccaneers (15-3 overall, 14-2 North) who took a 5-0 lead in the opening minute. But Kent Island wouldn't score the rest of the quarter, as Queen Anne's (18-2, 15-1) moved to a 9-4 lead.
"Defensive game," Kent Island head coach David Plumer said. "We obviously started better than the last time we played them. We just had trouble scoring. And we had a little foul trouble."
Kent Island senior standout Sydney Riska, who had averaged 16.75 points over her four previous games, picked up her third foul in the second period, got hit with her fourth personal early in the third, and didn't return to the floor until 5 minutes remained in the game.
"We stayed out of foul trouble for the most part, which helped," Kern said. "We were able to be aggressive on the defensive end. Offensively I was a little concerned, but give Kent Island credit. They were very good."
Sophomore center Michaela Thomas (eight points) led the Bucs' inside game, but often watched the Lions intercept entry passes and race the other way.
"Turnovers killed us," Plumer said.
Queen Anne's managed to extend its lead to 22-11 entering halftime, with Bea Holthaus scoring seven of her game-high 11 points before the break. But the Bucs didn't allow the Lions to establish any real type of offensive rhythm, holding Queen Anne's to its second lowest scoring output of the season.
"It was definitely a defensive game on both ends of the court," Kern said. "We had trouble getting good looks. And neither team was really able to get out in transition."
Both teams went cold from the floor over the first 4 minutes of the third quarter. Cheyanne Hollis converted a Laila Coles assist for an inside bucket, bumping the Lions' lead to 24-11. But Lacey Dauses sank a 3-pointer and Thomas scored inside, drawing Kent Island within 24-16 with a little over 3 minutes to play in the third.
Dauses drained her second 3-pointer with one second left in the third, cutting Queen Anne's lead to 26-19. But Kent Island wouldn't score from the field in the fourth quarter, as the Lions steadily lengthened their lead.
"Our free-throw shooting was a little off tonight," said Kern, whose team was 8 of 20 from the foul line. "We could have closed the game out a lot earlier if we made our free throws."
Plumer noted his team's turnover woes may have been the result of over passing, something the longtime head coach thinks can be fixed.
"We try to teach kids not to be selfish, make their teammates better," Plumer said. "And I think sometimes we try too hard to make the perfect play. Sometimes the perfect play would have been just keeping it. But we'll work on that. We have been playing better ball down the stretch. This game is not the end of the season. We lose we learn. The reality is we normally see them again."

title: Queen Anne’s Marks ends silver medal streak with state title in 800 meters at states
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne’s Marks ends silver medal streak with state title in 800 meters at states

 February 21, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 946
 Words 

 Read News Document

 LANDOVER — Queen Anne's County High senior Ben Marks knew the count — seven consecutive silver medals.That streak ended early Friday night.
After another heartbreaking runner-up finish in the 1,600 meters in the late afternoon, Marks returned to the track at the Prince George's Sports and Learning Complex in the early evening, charged to the front of the pack and never relinquished his lead on the way to winning the boys 800-meter title at the Class 2A state indoor track and field championships.
"This is so special to me," Marks said of his first state title which ended in 1 minute, 55.90 seconds. "Seven silver medals at states in a row makes this feel awesome."
The seventh of those came in the 1,600, in yet another duel with Southern of Anne Arundel's Eric Penkala. The two-time defending state champ, Penkala and Marks settled in behind Century's Ryan Hartranft through the opening three laps. Penkala moved into the lead at the halfway point with Marks off his right shoulder.
It quickly became a two-man race, with Penkala increasing his kick with two laps left and Marks staying off his right shoulder, heading into the bell lap and down the backstretch.
"I wanted to make a move with 400 to go," Marks said. "And every time I made a move he (Penkala) responded very well. He's a great tactical racer. He went early, with about half the race left. I think our splits were 2:16, and then 2:01 for the final 800. I tried to make the move and he kept speeding up the race. He'd match it and match it. I tried to make the right move and I just didn't have enough in the tank at the end to get him."
Penkala came off the final turn and pushed down the stretch, winning his third straight indoor state title at 1,600 meters in 4:17.17, just ahead of Marks' 4:17.87.
"When we started the last lap, when we really started kicking, whoever wins that battle, you're pretty much going to be ahead," Penkala said. "That's what I thought and that's what happened. I was working so hard, I was just trying to get to the finish line. I looked back. I saw him right behind me and I just looked away and kicked, and hoped he wasn't going to come up next to me."
As in their other state duels, Marks didn't pull up next to Penkala, but right behind him.
"Great race. Great racer," Marks said of Penkala. "Eric is amazing."
Despite another runner-up finish, Marks gathered himself and started looking ahead to the 800.
"I have one more race," said Marks, who dropped the 3,200 to focus on the 800. "We're going to focus on that one and keep this behind me right now."
The University of Maryland-bound Penkala won the 3,200 in convincing fashion, clocking a 9:44.91, with Hartranft finishing second in 9:50.61.
The Southern senior then lined up in the 800 for one final indoor duel with Marks, who drew confidence from his battle in the 1,600.
"I really appreciated how the 1,600 went, because the first 800 was 2:16 and the second 800 was 2:01," Marks said. "Coming off a sickness (earlier in the week), me being able to close that hard and for that long, for a whole 800 meters, is a confidence-booster for me. I know it didn't work out in the end, but I learned a lot about how I race in that mile and what my strengths are. And I knew I wanted to take the opposite approach in the 800."
He did.
Marks swiftly moved to the front and wasted little time in establishing a solid lead on the field that never got close.
"I felt really, really smooth through the whole race," Marks said. "I went out in about 27 (seconds). Nobody really went with me. Second lap was a 28. Third lap I kept my rhythm and controlled it. And fourth lap I just accelerated and felt smooth through the whole thing. That's the smoothest I've felt in any race so far this season."
Hereford's Eli Aitken finished second in 1:58.90, while Penkala took third in 2:00.45.
"I'm just so proud of him and so happy for him," Queen Anne's coach Natasha Dawson said of Marks. "Because if anybody in the world deserves it he absolutely deserves it. He puts in the time. He's an amazing kid. And he really deserves this championship."
Marks became the first Bayside Conference runner to win the boys 800-meter title indoors since Cambridge-South Dorchester's Matt Koletsky in 2017, and the first runner from Queen Anne's to win the 800 since Warren Staver in 2014.
Kent Island junior Jack Morey cleared 14 feet, 6 inches for a second-place finish and a school indoor record in the pole vault.
"I thought I was going to PR, which I did," said Morey, who was second to Parkside's Reese Howard (15 feet). "I kind of met my expectations.
"I was curious," Morey said when asked how he got into the pole vault. "I was like, what event am I going to do my freshman year, and I thought pole vault looked cool. So I decided to try it and got good at it."
North Caroline's Linda Ridgell, the 2A East Region champion, placed second in the girls 3,200 meters, finishing in 11:44.11. Hereford's Sylvia Snider took first in 11:29.19.
Queen Anne's County junior Makena Fellows was third in the girls shot put with a personal-record 35 feet, 3¼ inches.
"I'm not surprised," Dawson said of Fellows. "She works really hard. Shot put is not my specialty area, so she and I worked through YouTube. She also worked with (Kent Island head coach) Kayln Stout, so she's been working. She's been looking for things to help her get better."
