title: Sabres win second straight MIAA C crown
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres win second straight MIAA C crown

 February 24, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 892
 Words 

 Read News Document

 BALTIMORE — The school's record-breaking scorer pointed at the defense.He wasn't the only one.
"Defense was it. What I heard from other coaches was our defense was our key," Saints Peter and Paul High boys head basketball coach Gary Gould said.
That defense limited Key School to seven first-quarter points while building a lead it never surrendered Saturday night at UMBC's Chesapeake Employers Insurance Arena, as the top-seeded Sabres notched their second consecutive Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference championship with a 60-50 victory over the Obezags.
"Stayed with the process, got here three times, won two of 'em," said senior Garett Hemingway, who added to his school career-scoring record with a game-high 29 points. "Amazing.
"I didn't think I'd be here again from last year," added Hemingway, the lone returning starter from last year's title team. "I didn't know what we had. We had a lot of young guys; lot of jayvee guys. I didn't know what we were going to do this year."
What the Sabres (21-8) did was struggle early in the season, as Gould tinkered and fitted his new cast into their roles around Hemingway. He watched his team lose to Key by two points in overtime Jan. 13. It wouldn't lose again, as Sts. Peter & Paul closed the season on a 15-game win streak.
"Beat us in overtime. But when we played them at their place I think we sent a message," Gould said of the Sabres' 69-46 rout of the Obezags on Feb. 7. "And we knew every team, probably somewhere in the back of their mind, knew that this was the hard game to win. So we were trying to defend against their extra effort. We knew their extra effort was going to take effort."
Key's Angus Lunt Woodward hit a 3-pointer 22 seconds into Saturday's third meeting. The Sabres answered with Robert Mangold's three-point play 42 seconds later.
Anjo Yette (team-high 19 points) scored a layup to inch second-seeded Key (12-9) back in front. Hemingway responded with the equalizer for the game's second and final tie. Less than a minute later, JJ Rardin (eight points) started Sts. Peter & Paul on a 17-2 run that ended with five straight points from Andrew Steinhardt, giving the defending champions a 22-7 lead heading into the second quarter.
"The process is to get the lead and control the game, and then figure out what to do after that," Gould said. "It's hard to put a team away in a game like this. So we just stayed consistent and let things happen."
Seven straight points from Yette capped Key's 12-0 run to start the second quarter, trimming the Sabres' lead to 22-19 with 4 minutes, 17 seconds left before half. But Robert Mangold (eight points), Hemingway and Rardin each scored during a 9-0 Sabres' spurt that helped Sts. Peter & Paul carry a 31-21 lead into the locker room.
"Our team developed into a team throughout the year," Gould said. "They understood that Garett was our guy. But we were creating everyone's offensive confidence throughout the year and it showed up today."
Freshman Jamir Demby turned a steal into a layup and assisted on a transition bucket by Hemingway that was part of a 14-4 surge capped by Porter Bishop's drive, giving the Sabres their biggest lead at 45-25 with 2:22 remaining in the third.
"He stepped up in a big way today," Hemingway said of Demby.
But again, Sts. Peter & Paul often limited the Obezags to just one shot a possession, or forced turnovers with its full-court pressure in the third quarter.
"We have five, six different defenses we throw at you," said Gould, whose team held opponents to an average of 48.1 points a game during its 15-game win streak while the Sabres' averaged 71 a game. "We change up, see what your pulse is. What you can't handle. And we know most teams can't handle the full-court man. It's why we don't do it the whole game. We do it when we need to control the game, and then we'll rest and go back to the zone. We just hope you don't hit shots while we're resting."
Down 48-32 to start the fourth quarter, Key used a 10-0 tear to draw within 48-42 with 3:28 remaining. Sts. Peter & Paul got its first points of the period on Hemingway's finger roll with 2:53 left. Key's Christian Dent made one of two from the line to shave the Sabres' lead to seven with 1:26 to go. Hemingway converted another Demby steal into a layup for a 52-43 lead.
Austin Niese (10 points) scored and Yette made the second of two free throws, pulling the Obezags within 52-46 with 38.7 seconds left. But Key couldn't get any closer. Over the final 37 seconds, Hemingway scored on a drive and went 4-for-4 from the foul line, and Rardin hit pair from the foul line to cement the championship.
"I didn't think we were going to be this good," Gould admitted. "I thought we were going to be just too young. I guess when you're young, and you don't know, you don't have any excuses. Luckily though the young guys went to the championship game at the jayvee level last year. So they understand what it takes.
"Resilience," Gould added. "They played hard for 32 minutes. They understand their roles. They dig in on the defensive end and that's what gave us this win today."

title: BAYSIDE WRESTLING
author: Bill Haufe
content:
BAYSIDE WRESTLING

 February 25, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Bayside Wrestling 
 
 777
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — It may have been its worst showing of the season — a 24-point dual-meet loss at Kent Island on Jan. 15Thirty-nine days later, North Caroline High's wrestling team returned to Kent Island High and delivered one of its best performances, placing six in the finals en route to winning five individual titles Saturday for a runner-up finish at the annual Bayside Conference championships.
Stephen Decatur, which had six individual champs, won its sixth straight conference title with 283 points, while the Bulldogs placed second with 214.
"I don't know if I can say I was surprised," North Caroline head coach Robin Eaton said. "I believe they are living up to the potential I believed they've had all along. They're starting to believe. Some of them got down to the weight classes they should have been at. We're at that spot where you're peaking where you should peak."
Those peak efforts included one pinfall, two technical falls and a pair of major decisions in the championship finals, and Jackson Roberts' tech fall in the consolation finals at 138 pounds.
The Bulldogs avoided a scare in the semifinals, when Corey Bunce (190) appeared to injure his elbow while battling his cousin Zach Bunce of Kent Island.
"I thought he would like wrestling his cousin, but in the end he was like, 'I did not like wrestling him,'" Eaton said of Corey, who shook off the injury to earn a 6-3 decision over Zach, then pieced together a 20-5 technical fall over Parkside's Devin Szewczyk in the finals, raising his record to 36-0 for the season.
Caleb Melvin (29-5) had North Caroline's other tech fall, defeating Kent Island's Silas Brobst, 16-1, in the 132-pound final.
Boosting the Bulldogs' point total were Darly Ortega (22-13), who earned a 15-2 major decision over Kent Island's Shane Bunce at 106, and Connor Frank (32-7), who majored Parkside's Cameron Greene, 12-4, in the 120 final. Caroline sophomore Quinten Doyle (29-8) produced one of four pinfalls in the championship finals, pinning Kent Island's Brian Potter in 42 seconds at 175.
"We've discussed the mental aspect of the sport," Eaton said of his team. "And I think they've all bought into it and realized, match by match, period by period. 'I step on the mat and we're on even playing field. I can beat anybody at any given time.'"
The only other individual champion from a North Bayside school was Kent County's Scottie Ford. The defending champion at 138, Ford (25-1) bumped up to 150 and crafted a 9-0 major decision over Stephen Decatur's Alex Riehl in the final.
"He's definitely hitting a stride better than he had most of the season right now," Trojan head coach Chris Yiannakis said of Ford, who has bounced back from an injury suffered in football. "He's putting more effort into putting workouts in.
"He came out last year tech falling everybody," Yiannakis added. "I think early in the season he was playing it safe, but he's starting to pick up pace, score more points."
Stephen Decatur got title-winning efforts from Juan Hinojosa (36-4) at 113, Elijah Collick (40-1) at 126, Aaron August (32-3) at 138, Jake Saullo (33-7) at 144, Amarian Manuel (17-3) — who decisioned Kent County's Ethan Clark in the 157 final — and Nate McDaniel (37-1), who pinned Caroline's Arif Mohammadi in 1:44 of the 215-pound final.
Snow Hill's German Alvarez (32-4) won the 165-pound weight class, and Parkside's Dontray Fuller (16-3) won the title at 285.
The Bayside Conference crowned a girls team champion for the first time in its history, with defending Class 2A-1A state champion Queen Anne's County totaling 243 points to defeat runner-up Decatur by 32 points.
Leading that charge was senior Ally Conley (19-6), who became the school's first four-time conference champion when she pinned Decatur's Calleigh McBridge in 1:14 to win the 100-pound weight class.
The Lions finished with five champions, including Emmy Falcone (15-9), who pinned Easton's Zelia Proa in 2:25 of the 125-pound final. Falcone lost twice to Proa during the season.
Queen Anne's Lilly Hammond (14-6) majored Decatur's Beyonce Rodriguez, 15-3, to win the 140-pound weight class, first-year wrestler Faith Connolly (7-8) pinned Parkside's Rickelle Simpson-Henry in 1:26 in the 145 final, and Shayla Watson (20-2), another first-year wrestler, pinned Cambridge-South Dorchester's Sienna Mitchell in 34 seconds to finish first at 235.
"To be honest they probably wrestled the best they have all year," said Queen Anne's girls head coach John Waters, who got a runner-up finish from Kaylynn Bryant (19-3) at 190.
Colonel Richardson was the only other North school with a champion, as Landine Dorleans (19-3) decisioned Decatur's Irie Carmack, 10-9, in the 120-pound final, while Hannah Kefauver (16-8) pinned Wicomico's Iyanna Graves in 1:37 to win the 155-pound weight class.

title: Seahawks deny Vikings' bid for history
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Seahawks deny Vikings' bid for history

 February 26, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 696
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — Davin Chandler may not have known Cambridge-South Dorchester High had never won back-to-back Bayside Conference championships in boys basketball.What Stephen Decatur's talented senior guard did know was he was going to do all he could to prevent the Vikings from beating his team for a second straight year
He pretty much did just that Tuesday night.
Attacking the rim from seemingly all angles and adding a few pull-up jumpers, Chandler scored a game-high 30 points while leading the Seahawks to a 60-48 victory over unbeaten Cambridge-SD in the conference championship at the Wicomico Youth & Civic Center.
"Sometimes we take things for granted. But we just witnessed a Division I player," Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Tucker said of Chandler, who is headed to Vanderbilt University on a football scholarship. "He's going to school for football, but we just witnessed what a Division I player looks like. He did everything he needed to do for his team."
And he wasted little time doing it, driving hard to the hoop for the game's first points, then making a three-point play that tied the game at 5-5 with 2 minutes, 31 seconds left in the first quarter. Chandler slashed in for yet another drive to give Decatur (21-1) a 9-5 lead, stirring Decatur's fan base into thinking a potential quick getaway was in the making.
But Cambridge-SD (20-1) stayed close from beyond the 3-point arc.
Thomas Wilson's 3-pointer brought the Vikings within 9-8. Decatur moved to a 13-8 lead, but Kaleal Johnson's trey made it a two-point game. The Seahawks extended their second-quarter lead to 19-11 on buckets by Chandler, Judah Carmack (nine points) and Solomon David. Koby Ennals (11 points) hit one of his game-high three 3-pointers, drawing the Vikings within 19-14 with a little over 5 minutes left in the half.
The Seahawks upped their lead to six, but a field goal and 3 from Sterling Perkins Jr. (team-high 14 points) pulled Cambridge-SD within 20-19 with 2:38 remaining in the first half.
The Vikings though wouldn't get any closer, as Decatur used an 8-0 run to close the first half for a 28-19 edge, then widened its cushion to 32-19 less than 2 minutes into the third quarter.
"I feel like we forced some shots and then we settled, and then we hit the panic button," Tucker said. "We just weren't disciplined early enough to withstand what Stephen Decatur was doing. Hats off to them. They brought the energy."
Cambridge-SD, which hit 10 3-pointers compared to none for Decatur, kept its deficit between 10 and 12 points throughout the third quarter. But Chandler scored 10 of the Seahawks' final 13 points in the third quarter, mostly on drives, to give Decatur a 47-32 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
"He's just a winner," Decatur head coach B.J. Johnson said of Chandler. "There's a reason why he's going to Vanderbilt to play football. He's a coach's dream. And he would not let these guys lose. He's a great teammate. These kids rallied around him, bought into him being the leader, and I'm just so happy for him and all my players."
Chandler added six points during Decatur's 10-2 run over the first 4 minutes of the fourth, giving the South champions their biggest lead at 57-35.
"Big-time players step up in big-time moments," Tucker said of Chandler.
Cambridge-SD narrowed its deficit with a 10-3 game-ending run, but couldn't get any closer than 11.
"We just had one of those games," Tucker said. "Unfortunately, it was on the big stage. But fortunately it wasn't in the state playoffs."
The top-seed in Class 1A East Region II, Cambridge-SD will have a first-round bye and await the winner of Friday's Pocomoke-Crisfield game.
"This is a great opportunity to regroup, refocus and get prepared for the playoffs and make a deep run," Tucker said. "And guess what? It's one game. It doesn't define the rest of our season. So we have to continue to move forward and be positive. You have nothing to hang your head about. I know our guys. They're going to bounce back and they're going to make a run."
Notes: It was Decatur's first conference title since 2017. ... The Seahawks will be the No. 1 seed in Class 3A East Region I.

title: Lions get defensive on way to title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions get defensive on way to title

 February 26, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 759
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — Mike Kern concedes, "defense wins championships", is a well-worn cliché.Queen Anne's County High's girls head basketball coach also acknowledges that line is stuffed with a lot of truth.
Anyone wanting to argue with Kern just had to watch Tuesday night's Bayside Conference championship, as the Lions held defending champion Wicomico to its lowest scoring total of the season on the way to a 46-24 victory at the Wicomico Youth & Civic Center, giving Queen Anne's its second conference crown in four years.
"RJ (Ensor) did a phenomenal job," Kern said of his senior guard who was the main cog in a rotation that held Wicomico star Se'Lah Foreman to just seven points. "Taylor (Jordan) came in, Lexi (Kern) came in and did a great job on her; frustrated her and held her to seven points. I knew if we could keep her from scoring a lot we were going to be in the game."
One year after losing in the conference title game to Wi-Hi, Queen Anne's (19-2) never trailed, as Kariana Hickson (eight points) splashed a 3-pointer and Lucy Taylor scored from close range in the opening minutes for a 5-0 lead.
The Tribe (18-3) closed within 5-3, before Queen Anne's sophomore Bea Holthaus scored eight consecutive points for a 13-3 lead with 2:31 remaining in the first quarter.
"I think everybody was trying twice as hard, knowing last year we fell a little bit short," said Holthaus, who finished with a game-high 21 points, 11 rebounds and seven blocked shots to go with three steals.
Last year Queen Anne's Laila Coles tried driving the lane against Wi-Hi and often got her shot blocked. Tuesday, the sophomore guard not only had some success driving into the paint, but drew contact, helping get Wi-Hi's Carlisa Johnson and Natalia Almonte into first-half foul trouble.
"They got us in foul trouble early, and our shots weren't falling early," said Wicomico head coach Willie Downing, who team entered the game averaging 57.6 points a game. "Then once you get in foul trouble, they did something that we haven't had them do all year; they got really down on themselves. And once they got down, it's hard to get them out."
Foreman's baseline drive and 3-pointer trimmed the Lions' lead to 19-13 with 5:32 left in the second quarter. But the Tribe wouldn't get any closer than six points the rest of the game. Ensor's layup, two Coles free throws, and Hickson's set shot extended Queen Anne's lead to 27-15 at halftime.
The Tribe had no answer for Holthaus, who hit a pair of 3-pointers and drained a turnaround jumper that stretched the lead to 37-16 midway through the third period.
"She's a strong player," Downing said of Holthaus. "And they hit threes early. When she starts hitting her threes, that carries them. As long as we kept that part down, we're fine. But if we don't keep that part down they're going to roll. And tonight we didn't keep it down."
Coach Kern's biggest concern may have come with a little over 4 minutes remaining in the third quarter, when Ensor picked up her fourth foul. But Jordan came in and limited Foreman to a transition bucket with 3:28 to go in the period — her final points of the game.
"I think she's hurt," Downing said of Foreman. "She's used to people playing box-and-one, doubling her all day. But it just seemed like she got a little frustrated."
Holthaus cut to the basket for a layup, then found a cutting Jordan for a lay-in that boosted Queen Anne's advantage to 41-22 heading into the fourth quarter.
"We took what they gave us, kept swinging the ball around, and overall I'm really pleased," Kern said. "And Bea kind of took over. She was shooting well from outside, three-point line. On defense she just covers so much ground, so much length and grabbing boards. She does it all."
Trinity Purnell scored inside with 5:22 left, but Wi-Hi wouldn't score another point the rest of the game.
"We had RJ and Taylor Jordan playing a nice, tight man on her (Foreman) while everyone else was playing more of a zone so we could jump passes," Holthaus said. "She's a great ball-handler so we tried to track her whenever we could."
Wicomico got the No. 1 seed for the Class 2A East Region II playoffs by winning a coin flip over Queen Anne's, which is seeded second. Both have first-round byes.
Notes: It was the second time Queen Anne's has won the title while holding an opponent to 24 points. The Lions defeated Stephen Decatur, 44-24, in the 2022 championship.

title: Riska, Bucs pull away from scrappy Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Riska, Bucs pull away from scrappy Warriors

 February 28, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 904
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — Easton High's girls basketball team was at it again.The Warriors had scared North Bayside champion Queen Anne's. They had upset Class 1A East II top seed Cambridge-South Dorchester. And they had taken South Bayside power Wicomico into overtime.
Now, halfway through its postseason opener, Easton was all even with Kent Island, a team it had lost to twice during the regular season.
But Ellie Burnside hit consecutive baskets midway through the third quarter Friday, and senior Sydney Riska netted nine of her game-high 25 points down the stretch, boosting the fourth-seeded Buccaneers to a 48-39 victory over No. 5 Easton in a Class 2A East II quarterfinal.
Kent Island (16-3) advances to play at top-seeded Wicomico (18-3) on Monday in a regional semifinal.
"Easton is smaller in size so we knew we had the get the ball inside," Kent Island head coach David Plumer said. "But we just weren't playing very well in the beginning. Some of that is you play the same team three times. I'm always nervous about that. They make adjustments and then we're trying to make adjustments. They played a good game. They shot the ball really well."
Serenity Velez (22 points) shot the ball really well for Easton (11-9), draining five 3-pointers, including three in the first quarter, giving the Warriors an 11-5 lead.
Back-to-back buckets by Riska cut Easton's lead to 11-9 early in the second quarter. Then with 6 minutes, 49 seconds left before half, a shot-clock malfunction stalled the game for about 10 minutes.
"The momentum killer for us was when the shot clock messed up," Easton head coach Lesley Staehli said. "We were on a roll kind of. That threw us off a little bit."
Kent Island reeled off the first 13 points of the quarter to take an 18-11 lead. Velez scored Easton's first points of the period, when she sank the first of two free throws with 2:04 remaining before half.
But the Warriors recovered. Sam Murphy grabbed a rebound and went coast-to-coast for a layup. Riska spun in the lane for a baby hook that made it 20-14. Easton closed the half on a 6-0 run though, as freshman Maia Bailey hit a 3-pointer and converted two of three from the foul line after getting fouled on a 3-point attempt. Stella Kabler added a free throw with 4.5 seconds left in the half to forge a 20-20 tie.
Riska, who had 12 first-half points, continued to be a force early in the third quarter, scoring on a follow. Velez answered with another 3-ball. Riska scored inside. Velez converted a steal into a layup and a 25-24 Easton lead with 5 minutes remaining in the quarter.
But Burnside connected for a 3-pointer then hit another set shot to give the Bucs a 29-25 lead. Burnside had a chance to extend that lead, but missed two chances from the foul line. Riska though snagged the rebound and scored for a 31-25 lead.
"Ellie came alive a little bit," Plumer said. "I can't say enough about Burnside. She hit a three and then defensively is where she made her mark tonight."
The Warriors didn't let Kent Island get too far ahead though.
Ki'Mauri Lewis hit a pair of free throws to make it a four-point deficit. Michaela Thomas (10 points) scored a layup for Kent Island, then watched Riska make a steal, draw a foul, and make one of two from the line for a 34-27 Bucs lead. Velez then buried her fifth and final 3 of the game, drawing Easton within 34-30 heading into the fourth quarter.
That's when Kent Island's inside tandem of Riska and Thomas began to widen the Bucs' lead.
Riska scored inside to make it 36-30 early in the fourth. Bailey hit a 3-pointer to make it a three-point difference 30 seconds into the final quarter. Thomas scored on a follow before Lewis answered for the Warriors with a baseline drive.
Riska got the ball down low and spun into the paint for a basket, then came right back and hit a cutting Lacey Dauses for a layup and a 42-35 lead. Thomas scored on a put-back and Riska hit a free throw for a 45-35 lead with 2:17 remaining.
"We made a couple of adjustments to get her the ball more," Plumer said of Riska. "She's just a ballplayer."
Murphy ended a 5-plus minute scoring drought for Easton with a little over a minute remaining to make it 45-37. But Dauses hit a free throw and added another basket before Velez made a layup right before the game-ending buzzer.
"In the beginning it was kind of rough," Riska said. "But we overcome with a lot of aggression and fast-paced ball. Being a captain and being a senior I knew the team would follow me if I had the same aggressive play."
Despite her team's youth, Staehli was impressed Easton's play this season.
"I think we did great," Staehli said. "I don't think anybody expected us to be as close as we were to top teams like Kent Island and Queen Anne's. I think in due time these younger players are going to learn to fight through and I think we'll be fine. This year I thought was going to be a rebuilding year. But we did amazing."
BOYS BASKETBALLPerryville 67, St. Michaels 59ST. MICHAELS — Johnny Mautz scored 25 points and Zavion Goldsborough had 20 points Friday but it wasn't quite enough, as the fourth-seeded Saints fell to No. 5 seed Perryville in a Class 1A East I quarterfinal.

title: Lions rally but fall to Rams
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions rally but fall to Rams

 March 4, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 836
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — The look on Mike Kern's face was genuine surprise.His team had trailed most of the game. Still, Queen Anne's County High's girls head basketball coach believed his Lions would find a way to win in the end.
They didn't.
Kern watched one of his core values — defense — end his team's season earlier than expected Monday night, as Zion Oge made a steal that turned into a game-winning layup then knocked away a last-gasp inbounds pass, lifting Parkside to a 41-40 victory over the Lions in a Class 2A East Region II semifinal.
Third-seeded Parkside (19-3) will host No. 4 seed Kent Island (17-3) in the 2A East II final on Wednesday at 5 p.m. The Bucs advanced Monday with a 52-49 win over top-seeded Wicomico.
"I believed we were going to win until the very end. I really did," said Kern, whose team finished the season 19-3.
Second-seeded Queen Anne's charged to an 8-2 lead, but was only up 12-11 heading into the second quarter.
"We were scrambling out of position," said Parkside head coach Warren White, who is stepping down after this season. "We were running up two people on the ball. I only wanted one. Then when we settled down in the second quarter and stopped doing that, we got back in the game."
The Rams used a 14-4 surge over the final 5 minutes of the first half to take a 27-18 lead into the break.
Queen Anne's, which was plagued by turnovers while suffering one of its toughest shooting night's of the season, rallied to open the third period.
Kariana Hickson scored on a follow. Lucy Taylor (eight points, eight rebounds) hit a short baseline shot before slipping inside for an inside bucket. Sophomore Bea Holthaus (10 points, 12 rebounds, five steals, three blocks) then connected on a jumper to cap an 8-0 burst that shaved the Rams' lead to 27-26 midway through the quarter.
But Parkside's Zion Oge (12 points), who did not play in the 51-23 season-opening loss to Queen Anne's due to injury, then established herself inside. The 5-foot-11 senior hit a foul shot, scored consecutive put-backs, then caught an entry pass and kissed a shot off the glass that gave Parkside a 34-26 lead with 1:48 left in the third.
"Zion Oge, she's just a tough player," White said of his center, who has over a 1,000 career points and rebounds. "She's a walking double-double."
Queen Anne's again slowly crept back.
Damiya Henry hit a set shot and Laila Coles (10 points, six steals) sank a pair of free throws, drawing the Lions within 34-30 entering the fourth. Coles made another free throw to make it a three-point game early in the fourth.
An Oge free throw bumped Parkside's lead to 35-31. Hickson buried a 3-pointer with 4:27 left, again cutting Queen Anne's deficit to one. Oge made a pair of free throws and blocked a shot before Ziyon Smith converted a pair of free throws, giving Parkside a 39-34 lead with 2:31 to play.
Coles made a steal, was fouled and sank both free throws, shrinking Parkside's lead to three. The Rams were called for a charged, but Queen Anne's missed on three cracks at the basket before defensive standout RJ Ensor was whistled for her fifth foul with 1:37 remaining.
Parkside, which was 0 for 6 from the foul line over the final 1:37, couldn't extend its lead. Holthaus then splashed her only 3-pointer to tie the game at 39-all, sending the home crowd into a full roar.
Queen Anne's got the ball back. Holthaus was fouled in transition and made one of two free throws for a 40-39 Lions lead with 46.9 seconds left.
Oge missed a pair of free throws with 37.1 seconds remaining. Queen Anne's grabbed the rebound. Holthaus threw a pass to Taylor, but Oge reached in and deflected the ball. Ta'Layah Clark (game-high 14 points) grabbed the loose ball and raced in for a left-handed layup for a 41-40 Rams led with 25 seconds left.
Holthaus missed a pair of chances, the second rebounded by Oge, who was fouled with 8.8 seconds remaining. Parkside's center missed both foul shots. Taylor grabbed the rebound and Kern called time with 7.1 seconds left.
Queen Anne's raced downcourt. Coles came down the right side of the lane and dished to Hickson, who had the ball glance off her hands and out of bounds with 1.6 seconds left.
On the ensuing inbounds pass, Parkside's Kalayah Hitchens threw the ball toward halfcourt. The ball appeared to touch Oge's hand, but officials ruled the ball had not been touched, returning possession back to Queen Anne's on its own baseline.
Coles inbounded the ball, but this time Oge reached and grabbed the ball, securing the Rams' victory.
"Give Parkside credit," Kerns said. "They came in here and played us really hard. Offensively we just couldn't get our shots down and we were careless with the ball. And it was unfortunate to play like that in a game like this. We've had a great season and we did not play our best basketball tonight by any means."

title: Bunce extends unbeaten run with title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bunce extends unbeaten run with title

 March 4, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 971
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Corey Bunce planned to give basketball a try this season, but the North Caroline High senior didn't make the cut because of an injury concern."My dad and my other coach convinced me to come back to wrestling, not to quit my senior year," Bunce said.
Things have worked out pretty well so far.
Bunce decisioned his younger cousin Zach Bunce of Kent Island, 4-2, to win the 190-pound weight class while extending his unbeaten record to 39-0 Saturday during the Class 2A-1A East Regional championships at Queen Anne's County High.
"When we were little I used to wrestle and I would beat up on him pretty good. But he's a lot bigger and stronger now," Corey said with smile. "It's not fun. He's a strong kid."
The cousins were originally scheduled to meet during a Jan. 15 dual meet, but Kent Island opted to forfeit to Corey. Corey and Zach did meet in the semifinals of the Bayside Conference championships, with Corey earning a 6-3 decision. Then came Saturday's rematch, where Corey broke a 1-1 tie via a takedown with 17 seconds remaining for the victory and his first regional title.
"I didn't really have expectations," Corey said any preseason goals. "And being undefeated right now is definitely not something I saw."
But the Bulldogs senior does have a goal heading into this weekend's state championship tournament at the Show Place Arena in Upper Marlboro.
"Last year I didn't do what I wanted to do," Corey said. "I wanted to get on the podium. This year I want to get on the podium, but I want to place top three."
Corey's win gave North Caroline second-year head coach Robin Eaton a third regional champion Saturday.
"He's wrestling smart," Eaton said of Corey. "And he's proven that. He's been in some silly-tight matches where he just pulls it out by doing something. But he's not undefeated because he doesn't know what to do."
Eaton called last year's regional tournament great after taking seven for states, including some he didn't think would qualify. But it wasn't until Darly Ortega's 14-4 major decision over North East's Caiden Hickey (29-12) in Saturday's 106-pound final that Eaton had his first regional champion.
"It never even dawned on me," Eaton said. "A little bit after Darly's match, Darly was like, 'I'm your first regional champ coach.' So in my second year as head coach I have three regional champions. It just goes back to the kids' hard work and my coaching staff."
A junior, Ortega (25-13) scored a takedown 47 seconds into his match with Hickey, and expanded that lead to 11-0 by the end of two periods.
"Darly's had a rough season wrestling up at 113," Eaton said. "His record doesn't show how well he has wrestled, or how well he can wrestle. He went through a slump and I think he was having doubts about his own ability. So he got down to 106 and he's been very focused."
Bulldog teammate Connor Frank (35-7) also looked focused, as he too scored the first takedown of his match, then added a pair of second-period takedowns on the way to a 12-2 major decision over Parkside's Cameron Greene (31-8) to win the 120-pound title.
"He's starting to watch and pick things up about his opponents, and then kind of use that to his advantage," Eaton said of Frank. "So not only is he working hard and developing his own moves, he's understanding weaknesses."
Kent Island junior Silas Brobst (23-14) became the third wrestler from a North Bayside school to earn his first regional title when he crafted a 7-2 decision over Harford Tech's Nathan Derham (21-10) in the 132-pound championship. Brobst took down Derham with 45 seconds left in the first period, watched his lead get whittled to 3-2 by the end of the second, then got a takedown with 15 seconds left to cement his five-point win.
"In the past he's had upperclassmen come down and bump him to other weights that were not his natural weights," Kent Island head coach Tommy Sitar said of Brobst. "Last year he had to wrestle up. So I think this year with him being able to come down to 132 and wrestle guys who are lighter, I think that had a lot to do with it. But really Silas is just developing his own style, and it's really awesome to bear witness to."
Colonel Richardson's Evan Alexander (35-7), who twice lost to Stephen Decatur's Aaron August — 13-3 dual meet and 6-5 in the Bayside finals — clashed with the Seahawk senior for a third time, and this time pulled out a 6-3 sudden-victory in the first overtime period to win the 138-pound title.
"We were shocked," Colonel Richardson head coach Bryan Hall said. "Evan's only a sophomore. August is a good wrestler. He's gotten a little bit closer every time they've wrestled. I can't believe he beat him."
After a scoreless first period, August (34-4) got a takedown and took a 3-1 lead into the third. Alexander hit a reversal 27 seconds into the third period to tie the score at 3-3, sending the match into overtime. Alexander wasted little time in the 1-minute extra session, shoving August's head to the side before jumping around and behind him for a match-winning takedown.
"He wrestled him really well," Hall said of Alexander. "Evan usually doesn't get tired. He does very well for six minutes."

title: Watson's impressive debut season reaches states
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Watson's impressive debut season reaches states

 March 5, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 660
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Shayla Watson went out for the girls wrestling team at Queen Anne's County High last year, but never had the chance to compete after suffering a preseason ankle injury.Despite that season-ending injury, Watson attended all the Lions' matches, and eventually became the team's stat girl.
She returned this season, and in her first exhibition match got pinned in 18 seconds.
A month and a half later, Watson faced that same opponent in a dual meet and pinned her in 30 seconds. Not long after that, the Queen Anne's junior pinned Northern Calvert's Emily Boling — ranked No. 1 in the state at the time — at the annual Queen of the Jungle tournament.
"She's been amazing all year," Queen Anne's head coach John Waters said of Watson. "She took fourth at Beast of the East and lost to the number two-ranked girl in the nation, 2-0."
Watson continued her impressive first-year roll last Friday night on her home mat, winning the 235-pound title during the girls Class 2A-1A East Regional tournament at Queen Anne's.
"She's very athletic," Waters said of Watson, who heads into Thursday's 2A-1A state tournament at the Show Place Arena in Upper Marlboro as the top-ranked wrestler at 235 pounds in the state. "So she can do things that other heavyweights can't do. That gives her a big advantage. And she's strong."
Watson (21-2) pinned Stephen Decatur's Amelia Gonzalez in 40 seconds in the semifinals before winning the championship final via a medical forfeit, joining senior Ally Conley as Queen Anne's only regional champs.
A two-time state champion, Conley (20-6) became the school's first four-time regional champ — male or female — when she battled off her back twice before earning a pin over Stephen Decatur freshman Calleigh McBride 34 seconds into the second period of the 100-pound championship bout.
"Ally's experience comes in and she doesn't panic when she's gets on her back," Waters said. "Being the first four-time regional champion from Queen Anne's County is pretty special."
Conley and Watson will have plenty of company in Upper Marlboro, as the defending state champion Lions qualified wrestlers in 11 of the 14 weight classes. In addition to Watson, Faith Connolly (2nd, 145), Annalise Michael (3rd, 105), Adyson Kendall (3rd, 120), Emmy Falcone (3rd, 125) and Linda Vail (3rd, 135) all qualified for states for the first time. They will be joined by Lilly Hammond (2nd, 140), Adelina Dickens (3rd, 155), Maggie Rooney (2nd, 170) and Kaylynn Bryant (2nd, 190).
Unlike the boys state tournament, where the top four from each weight class in the four regions qualify for states, only the top three girls advance to states. Queen Anne's Michael, Kendall, Falcone, Vail and Dickens each had to wrestle back and win their respective consolation final to qualify.
"Those girls, they knew that," Waters said. "So after their first loss of the night they knew they had to battle back. And they did. Addy Dickens had to wrestle a girl who pinned her earlier in the night.
"I sent them all messages after we got done cleaning up the mats," Waters continued. "Just told them how proud I was of them, because most of the girls missed at least two practices last week due to sickness. It was rough. We only had five girls at Monday's and Tuesday's practice, and they weren't the same five. For them to battle back and just, one, get their bodies ready to be able to compete, and then for some of them to lose their first match and wrestle back. It's been an awesome ride."

title: Dickerson, Colonel soar into region final
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Dickerson, Colonel soar into region final

 March 5, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 881
 Words 

 Read News Document

 AMERICAN CORNER — He was only in sixth grade, but Ja'Zir Dickerson made a curious first impression."First time I saw him play he was going rebound to layup," Colonel Richardson High boys head basketball coach Brad Plutschak said as he watched Dickerson grab the ball on the defensive end, race the length of the floor then take off for a lay-in. "And I thought, 'I wonder how this is going to play at the high school level?'"
If Tuesday night was any indication, it seems to be playing out just fine.
Dickerson scored 20 of his game-high 32 points in the second half to help rally Colonel Richardson to a 64-61 victory over Perryville in a Class 1A East Region I semifinal before a near packed house at Merrill Morgan Gymnasium.
The top-seeded Colonels (16-5) will host No. 2 seed Bohemia Manor (10-10) for the 2A East I title on Thursday at 5:30 p.m.
"Number two, he is coast-to-coast," Perryville head coach Ron Kidd said of Colonel's outstanding sophomore. "He rebounds and he is a very good athlete; very good basketball player. I was very impressed."
The fifth-seeded Panthers (7-15) impressed during the first half, as they drilled seven 3-pointers just four days after making 14 in a quarterfinal victory over St. Michaels.
"I was in disbelief," Dickerson said.
Back-to-back drives from Dickerson gave the Colonels a 4-1 lead before Perryville's Preston Saccanti (team-high 19 points) scored nine points in an 11-0 Panthers' flurry that gave the visitors a 12-4 lead midway through the first quarter.
Threes from Saccanti and Aiden Gatch helped Perryville maintain that eight-point edge, before the Colonels closed the quarter on an 8-0 run that included Leshaun Allen's 3-pointer from the top of the key, Makiah Batson's three-point play, and a Dickerson drive.
Dickerson and Allen (12 points) scored on back-to-back drives to pull Colonel even at 18-all 1:26 into the second quarter. But Perryville connected on four 3-pointers over the next 5 minutes for its biggest lead of the game at 32-22.
Two Allen free throws and another Dickerson drive narrowed the Panthers' lead to 32-26 at halftime.
"We scouted them at St. Michaels Friday, and we knew if we contest them, we felt like the percentage might be a little less," Plutschak said of Perryville's 3-point shooting. "But we knew we were still going to have to overcome some 3-pointers. It came down to us getting to the rim and their threes, and a matter of could we get enough at the rim and stop enough of their threes?"
Colonel — especially Dickerson — not only got to the rim more in the second half, it limited the Panthers to just one 3-pointer after halftime.
"They did a great job," Kidd said of Colonel's defense. "They went in at halftime, they made some adjustments, and they played really strong defense."
Though Colonel's intensity on the defensive end quieted Perryville's long-range success, it still trailed, a three-point play from Devin Clore (18 points) giving the Panthers a 39-34 lead with 5:10 left.
Tarron Hammond's two free throws and a Dickerson bucket and foul shot evened the game at 39-39 with 4:25 left in the third. Perryville again moved to a modest lead, carrying a 50-43 cushion into the fourth.
Dovonta Clore's 3-pointer with 4:45 left moved the Panthers' lead to 57-50 with 4:45 to go in the game.
But Colonel responded with a 14-4 closing surge.
Batson (10 points) scored first. Allen, limited by foul trouble in the second half, followed, getting a feed from Hammond for a baseline layup. Batson's layup pulled Colonel within 57-56 with 3:34 left. Hammond (eight points) hit a jumper that spun around and dropped for a 58-57 lead Colonel never relinquished. Dickerson soared in for a drive to make it 60-57 with 2:38 remaining.
"He just has a way," Plutschak said of Dickerson. "He did some great things."
Devin Clore made a layup, was fouled, but couldn't complete the three-point play, leaving Perryville down 60-59 with 1:04 remaining.
Dickerson's reverse layup pushed Colonel's lead to 62-59 with 33 seconds left. Saccanti's layup drew Perryville back within one at 62-61.
Then with 4.2 seconds remaining, Perryville fouled Colonel's David Thomas, who had not scored all game. Thomas, who hit a game-winning 3-pointer in the Colonels' 74-73 season-opening victory over Pocomoke, stepped to the line and drained both foul shots for a 64-61 lead.
"I knew I was going to ice the game," Thomas said. "At the beginning and in the second half, my shot wasn't falling. But once I got to that free-throw line I already knew it was cash. I don't miss free throws at practice. And I don't miss them in a game either."
Perryville had one last chance, but Kris Gardner's 3-point attempt from the left wing banged off the iron, sealing Colonel's trip to the final.
"We came out and we just caught fire," Dickerson said. "Big shout out to everybody rebounding. The whole team started rebounding. We played hard, physical defense and we got stops."
CAMBRIDGE-SD 67, POCOMOKE 66CAMBRIDGE-SD — Thomas Wilson scored 18 points and Semaj Pinder had 14 as the top-seeded Vikings edged the Warriors in a 1A East II semifinal.
Cambridge-South Dorchester (21-1) hosts No. 2 seed Snow Hill (17-5) for the 1A East II title on Thursday at 7:30 p.m.
Koby Ennals and Sterling Perkins each added 12 points for the Vikings
Pocomoke was led by Jason Mason's 20 points.

title: Orioles being cautious with star shortstop
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Orioles being cautious with star shortstop

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 269
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SARASOTA, Fla. — Baltimore Orioles star shortstop Gunnar Henderson has a mild right intercoastal strain, manager Brandon Hyde said Wednesday.Hyde said the Orioles are "very, very hopeful" that Henderson will be ready for the March 27 opener at Toronto but are being cautious with the 2023 American League Rookie of the Year. The 23-year-old shortstop was an All-Star last season, when he hit .281 with 37 homers and 92 RBIs.
"We're going to not push a strain there, and we want to make sure that he gets it taken care of," Hyde said. "It's one of those sensitive areas where we don't want anything to reoccur."
An intercostal strain involves the muscles around the ribs. Hyde's update to reporters Wednesday, after the Orioles beat Minnesota in a spring training game, came six days after Henderson exited a game because of lower right side discomfort.
Henderson left that Feb. 27 game after only one inning. He made a jumping catch of a line drive in the field, then grounded out when leading off for the Orioles in the bottom of the inning.
"He's feeling a lot better, but we're just going to obviously slow-play it a little bit and make sure that he is 100%," Hyde said. "But he's getting a lot better every single day."
Henderson, who debuted with the Orioles in 2022 after being drafted in the second round in 2019, has never been on the injured list in the major leagues. He played in 150 games in 2023 and 159 games in 2024, when he set career highs with 31 doubles, 37 homers, 92 RBIs, 21 steals and an .893 OPS.

title: Cambridge-SD falters down stretch
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Cambridge-SD falters down stretch

 March 7, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 768
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — This was better than Courtney Kief had hoped for."We worked the last few days of practice on being within two points with a minute left," Snow Hill High's girls head basketball coach said.
Snow Hill was all even with top-seeded Cambridge-South Dorchester with a minute remaining in Thursday's Class 1A East Region II final. Two free throws and a chaotic 60 seconds later, the second-seeded Eagles had a 36-34 victory for their second regional title in four years.
Snow Hill (15-8), which has won 10 of its last 11 games, is the No. 8 seed in the state playoffs, and travels to top-seeded Southern of Garrett (21-1) Saturday for a 2 p.m. quarterfinal.
"I was devastated," Cambridge-SD head coach Shamya Johnson said. "We beat ourselves at the end."
Cambridge-SD (16-6) twice had leads of five points — the biggest lead for either team in the game — the first coming with 6:41 left in the second quarter, when senior Le'Asia Todd scored on a put-back for a 12-7 lead. Todd, who was three steals shy of a quadruple-double (14 points, 32 rebounds, 10 blocked shots, seven steals) scored on another follow to give Cambridge-SD a 25-20 lead with 46 seconds remaining in the third quarter.
But Snow Hill senior Marrah Milbourne (game-high 17 points) hit a 3-pointer and converted a steal into a layup to create a 25-25 tie heading into the fourth quarter.
Senior Tajanae Ballin (eight points) pushed the Vikings back in front at 29-25, making a pair of free throws before grabbing a loose ball and scoring a layup. Snow Hill answered as A'leigh Daniels hit a 3-pointer before Marrah Milbourne drove in for a layup and a 30-29 led with 4:30 remaining.
"Twenty-three is the heart of this group," Kief said of Marrah Milbourne. "Her and her twin sister (MarLynn). Together they have combined for most of our points all year long."
Destiny Johnson (10 points) hit a free throw to tie the game at 30-all. Ballin converted two of four attempts from the foul line over the next 25 seconds, nudging Cambridge-SD to a 32-30 lead.
Marrah Milbourne again replied for the Eagles, driving right for a bucket and a 32-32 tie, then scoring a put-back for a 34-32 Snow Hill lead with 2:04 on the clock.
Destiny Johnson's layup with 1:14 left tied the game for the eighth and last time. They would be Cambridge-SD's last points of the season.
MarLynn Milbourne (seven points) swished the first of two free throws to move the Eagles to a 35-34 lead with 24.5 seconds left. Todd missed a pair of chances from the line. Jessini Bratten sank the second of two free throws, inching Snow Hill's lead to 36-34 with 14 seconds to go.
Todd missed two foul shots. The Vikings got the ball back on a tie-up before Destiny Johnson fired a shot from the right wing that hit off the side of the backboard with 1.8 seconds left, before Snow Hill grabbed the rebound.
"A lot of preparation and a lot of heart," Kief said. "So they felt prepared I think. They certainly executed (at the end) as if they did. We knew we could beat them, but we knew it was going to be a tough game."
For Shamya Johnson, it was about missed opportunities.
"Same thing I've been preaching all season; layups and free throws," said the Vikings head coach, whose team was 7 of 24 from the foul line — 5 of 14 in the fourth quarter. "I feel like where we went wrong was rushing in the backcourt when we already had them in foul trouble. 'Make them foul you. And then make your free throws.' It was just that panic, trying to hurry up. And it wasn't necessary. And it burned us.
"They had a good run," Coach Johnson said of her team. "I was happy about they didn't settle for jump shots tonight. That was good. It was just decision making at the end. We just left too many points on the floor."
It was the fourth time Cambridge-SD and Snow Hill have met for the region title over the last four years, with the Vikings winning in 2022 and '24.

Junior Lacey Dauses' 15 points led Kent Island (17-4).

title: Vikings tough out fourth straight title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings tough out fourth straight title

 March 7, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1011
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — In-your-face defense and breakneck transition play.Those basic principles have long been threads in the rich history of Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys basketball program.
Vikings third-year head coach Shawn Tucker and staff have pushed two other principles this season that are often linked together — patience and the backdoor cut.
Its 12-point lead trimmed to four, Cambridge-SD executed that combination to perfection Thursday night, as Koby Ennals drew a pair of defenders, leaped and zipped a cross-lane pass to an open Thomas Wilson for a clutch bucket that helped seal a 64-61 victory over Snow Hill, giving the Vikings their fourth consecutive Class 1A East Region II title before a packed house.
Cambridge-SD (22-1) will be the top seed in the reseeded Class 1A state tournament, and hosts No. 8 seed Fort Hill (15-7) in a quarterfinal on Saturday at 4 p.m.
"It feels great," said Ennals, one of four Vikings to score in double figures with 12 points. "To do it my senior year again after I did it my junior and my sophomore year. ... it feels great to be back."
The three-point win was the narrowest margin of victory of Cambridge-SD's four-title stretch, the previous two wins coming against Snow Hill by 18 and 25 points.
"It was the toughest," Ennals conceded. "Past years it's been a couple blowouts. But now it's like we really had to work for it to earn it."
The top-seeded Vikings looked ready to take off on a third runaway, as Ennals' 3-pointer staked the three-time defending champs to a 10-4 lead with under 3 minutes to play in the first quarter. But Snow Hill's Jymire Reveles drained three consecutive 3-pointers in a 1:26 span, giving the No. 2 seed Eagles (17-6) a 13-10 lead.
"Hats off to (Snow Hill) coach Shawn Johnson," Tucker said. "He had those kids prepared."
A Jaden Harris drive and one Sterling Perkins Jr. free throw tied the game at 13-13 and the end of the first quarter.
The opening 3-plus minutes of the second quarter featured four more deadlocks, before Semaj Pinder (team-high 18 points) made a three-point play to start Cambridge-SD on 7-0 flurry for a 28-21 lead with 1:33 left before halftime.
Brooks Crosswell's two free throws stopped that run. But the smooth-shooting Pinder knocked down a pair of jumpers and Harris (10 points) scored on a follow, giving Cambridge-SD a 34-25 halftime edge.
"Teammates, having confidence in me, and I'm having confidence in them," Pinder said. "We kept each other up. Teamwork. Just keep playing as a team and we were going to fight through it."
Ennals' three-point play 35 seconds into the third quarter gave the Vikings a 37-25 lead.
But Keondre Nixon (14 points) hit a 3-pointer and Demar Brunson (game-high 21 points) connected on a pair of treys to fuel a 14-4 Eagles run that trimmed Cambridge-SD's advantage to 41-39 with just over 3 minutes left in the third quarter.
Wilson converted a Pinder assist for a basket and Harris scored before drawing a technical, moving the lead to 45-39. The Eagles again pulled within two before Ennals' put-back gave Cambridge-SD a 47-43 lead heading into the fourth.
Pinder, Ennals, Perkins (10 points), Wilson and Harris each scored to give the Vikings their second 12-point cushion of the game at 58-46 near the midway point of the fourth quarter. Snow Hill crept within six on a bucket from Kam Lucas (10 points) and a basket and two free throws from Brunson.
Cambridge-SD's Anthony Hughes hit a 3-pointer to send a charge into the home crowd while widening the lead to 61-52. Snow Hill wouldn't go away though, whittling the Vikings' lead to 61-57 with a little over 2 minutes remaining.
The Eagles had a chance to get closer but Lucas was whistled for a charge. Then with 1:17 left, Ennals got a pass, waited, jumped and dished to an open Wilson cutting in from the left side of the lane for a layup and a 63-57 lead.
"We executed down the stretch," Tucker said. "They were overplaying us and we've been preaching that all year; 'Just cut backdoor.' The guy finally cuts and guess what happens?
"TJ's struggling from the perimeter," Tucker added of Wilson. "He's a good shooter. 'But TJ, go get an easy bucket. See the bucket go in and the basket will look like an ocean to you.' Those are the things that we work on. And I said, 'Koby just be patient.' Koby's a warrior. He wants to win so bad. For him to be patient and put that ball inside. … that's a senior."
Ennals fouled out about 40 seconds later, but Lucas missed a pair of free throws. Snow Hill finished 14 of 28 from the foul line.
Nixon then scored consecutive baskets, getting Snow Hill within 63-61 with 24.2 seconds left. Cambridge-SD turned the ball over on the inbounds play, but Brunson lost his footing on a drive and was called for a travel with 9 seconds left. Perkins was fouled on the ensuing inbounds, and hit one of two free throws for what proved to be the game's final points.
"We are battled test," Tucker said. "We've been through everything. We've blown out teams. We've had close games. So this right here is a testament of those guys over there. They just want to win and they know how to win. And that's what winners do. Winners win."
COL. RICHARDSON 89 BOHEMIA MANOR 65AMERICAN CORNER — Sophomore Ja'Zir Dickerson scored 43 points as the top-seeded Colonels routed the No. 2 seed Eagles to win the 1A East I crown.
Tarron Hammond added 16 points for the Colonels (17-5), who are the fifth seed in the state tourney and play at No. 4 Liberty (18-4) on Saturday in the quarterfinals at 6 p.m.
KENT ISLAND 66 PARKSIDE 60STEVENSVILLE — Max Hershkowitz had 21 points and Allen Butler scored 16, as the Buccaneers topped the Rams to win the Class 2A East Region II crown.
The fifth seed in the state tourney, Kent Island (14-6) plays at No. 4 Middletown (17-6) in a 6 p.m. quarterfinal on Saturday. Owen Neely had 12 points for Kent Island and Kamm Green 11.

title: Queen Anne's wins 2nd straight state title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's wins 2nd straight state title

 March 11, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 841
 Words 

 Read News Document

 UPPER MARLBORO — Yes, it was the defending state champion.But Queen Anne's County High girls head wrestling coach John Waters discovered on the first day of practice this season how things had changed for his team.
"That first day in the room you realize, 'Wait a second. This is going to be a whole lot different," said Waters, who had graduated half his starting lineup from last season. "The turnover, and expecting certain kids to come back but they didn't. Then you see this whole new group of first-year wrestlers, or second-year wrestlers that got maybe two, three varsity matches the year before. And it's like, 'OK, this is going to be different.'"
The season may have started different, but it ended the same as the year before Saturday night at the Show Place Arena, as the Lions earned their second consecutive girls team title at the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association's state tournament.
"I don't have enough time in the rest of the day to talk about this entire team," said Waters after the Lions totaled 121 points to outdistance runner-up Stephen Decatur (109.5) and third-place Tuscarora (89).
Leading that title charge was senior Kaylynn Bryant (25-4), who after three losses to Azariyah Johnson, pinned the Stephen Decatur senior in 2:48 to win the 190-pound title.
Queen Anne's spirits were crushed though in Saturday's final match, when senior Ally Conley was pinned by Violet Land (22-17) of Marriotts Ridge in 5:27 of the 100-pound championship bout.
Conley, who had won the state title at 100 pounds as a freshman and junior, was bidding to become only the fourth wrestler from a Bayside Conference school to win three state championships, joining Kent County's Davey Blake (1996, '97, '98) and Stephen Decatur's Danny Miller (2007, '08, '09) and Elijah Collick (2023, '24, '25).
But Land scored a takedown and four near-fall points to build a 7-2 first-period lead, expanded that advantage to 11-2 before earning the fall. Conley, who became the school's first four-time Bayside and regional champion this season, finished with a 23-7 record.
"I was heartbroken," said Waters, who watched his team crowd around Conley afterwards in consolation. "To see how much she meant to them. I've been around wrestling a long time and I've seen kids lose. I've never seen teammates come together like that. And it wasn't because of the loss. It's because 'This is the last time we have you.' That's what the girls were saying. She's the team captain. She's the reason they wrestle. She's the one they look up to."
Queen Anne's had six wrestlers making their first trip to states on the girls side. Among that group was junior Shayla Watson (26-3), who lost to eventual state champ Jabea Ewane of Winters Mill in the 235-pound quarterfinals, then pinned her next four opponents, including the Academy for College and Career Exploration's Destiny Dupree in 3:56 of the consolation final to place third
Boosting the Lions' title run were Lilly Hammond (19-10), who went 3-3 to place sixth at 140, Faith Connolly (11-11) — 3-2 at 145 — and Adelina Dickens (18-11) — 2-2 at 155. Adyson Kendall (120) and Maggie Rooney (170) added one win each.
"They way they persevered all year was just awesome," Waters said. "And most of them not knowing what to expect because it was a new sport for them. And then having the target (of being defending state champ) on your back doesn't make it any easier. But these young ladies, they worked hard and they didn't quit. It's every coach's dream to have your kids show up on the grandest stage. And that's what they did."
Colonel Richardson sophomore Landine Dorleans (25-6) pinned Richard Montgomery's Cielo Prieto in 2:28 to place fifth in the girls 120-pound division.
A junior, Decatur's Elijah Collick (47-1) became the Bayside's third three-time state champion, when he earned an 18-5 major decision over Huntingtown's Landon Vercoe to win the 126-pound weight class in the 2A/1A co-ed tournament.
Queen Anne's junior Landon Shanks (43-4), who lost to Vercoe in the quarterfinals, wrestled back to take third at 126, pinning South Carroll's Brody Henry in 3:47 in the consolation final to cap a 5-1 tournament. Shanks' third-place was the highest finish of any North Bayside wrestler in the co-ed tournament.
"After that loss he kind of approached every match kind of loose," Queen Anne's boys head coach David Stricker said of Shanks. "He was like, 'Every match could be my last one, so I'm just going to go out and have fun and let it fly'. After the loss he probably wrestled the best he has all season. He just turned into the best wrestler that he's been all season."
Northern-Garrett's Lucas Wolf scored a takedown with 21 seconds remaining in overtime to earn a 3-0 sudden-victory over Kent County's Scottie Ford in the 150-pound consolation final. A junior, Ford finished the season at 31-4.
North Caroline junior Connor Frank (38-9) earned a 14-12 decision over Parkside's Cameron Greene (34-11) to place fifth at 120.
Decatur's Juan Hinojosa (41-5) and Nate McDaniel (43-2) took runner-up honors at 113 and 215, respectively.

title: 'I'M STATE CHAMP'
author: Bill Haufe
content:
'I'M STATE CHAMP'

 March 11, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1023
 Words 

 Read News Document

 UPPER MARLBORO — She had chased her for three years, losing to her every time, including three times this season.Now, late Saturday afternoon at the Show Place Arena, Queen Anne's County High senior Kaylynn Bryant was in a place she had never been before when wrestling Stephen Decatur's Azariyah Johnson — ahead on the scoreboard.
That lead carried into the second period when Bryant started in the top position.
Forty-eight seconds later, Bryant heard the unmistakeable thud of the referee's hand smacking the mat, leaving her gripped in shock while sending her senses rocketing on a path that easily could have earned her a speeding ticket on the way to cloud nine.
"Oh, my God," Bryant said, trying to replay the moment she realized she had pinned Johnson to win the girls 190-pound weight class at the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association's state tournament. "I didn't even realize it. It just all happened. He (the referee) hit the mat and I was like. … I jumped up and didn't know what just happened. And as I'm celebrating I was like, 'I'm state champ!'"
Her arm raised in victory, Bryant shook hands with Decatur's two coaches then shuffled across the mat and jumped into the open arms of Queen Anne's head coach John Waters, who had ditched the crutch he'd been using for three days to catch the school's third state champion in four years. Once Bryant's feet touched down, she turned and leaped into the arms her father, Lions assistant Rondell Bryant, who while bear hugging his daughter asked, "Do you want to throw me?"
Initially hesitant, Kaylynn grabbed her dad then flung him to the mat, punctuating a performance that clinched Queen Anne's second consecutive state team championship. Bryant's title, Ally Conley's runner-up finish at 100 pounds, and Shayla Watson's third place at 235 helped the Lions amass 121 points followed by Stephen Decatur (109.5) and Tuscarora (89).
"That was awesome," Waters said of Bryant, who did not surrender one point in any of her four matches during the three-day tournament. "She has been chasing her all year. And I know that feeling from my time chasing (Kent County three-time state champion) Davey Blake. Yes, that's your goal, but it can't be your only goal. You have to stay focused in each match."
Bryant (25-4) certainly appeared focused every time she stepped on the mat, starting Thursday, when she earned a 1:37 fall over Lansdowne's Endya Williams in the first round, then pinned Eastern Vo Tech's Arianna King in 3:48 in the quarterfinals. Bryant remained zeroed in during Friday's semifinal, pinning Harford Vo Tech's Nicole Filip in 2:30, setting up Saturday's fourth clash of the season with Johnson.
The defending state champion at 190, Johnson (18-2) pinned Bryant with 1 second left in the first period during a Jan. 28 dual meet at Decatur. Johnson put together a 19-8 major decision over Bryant in the Bayside Conference title match Feb. 22. Johnson prevailed six days later in the Class 2A-1A East Regional final, though this time the margin was 8-3.
"Baysides we came up with a plan," Waters said. "The goal is to wear her out. Kaylynn stepped her conditioning up during her own training outside of practice. And it showed wrestling Shayla every day, and then the boys heavyweights Drew (Sutton) and Ethan (Wheaton). That improved her confidence because AJ is very strong.
"Our strategy was, 'We know she's going to shoot her blast double off the whistle,'" Waters said of Johnson. "'You just got to get through it, defend it.'"
Bryant blocked Johnson's initial shot in Saturday's final. The Decatur senior then got in on Bryant's right leg. Hopping on her left leg, Bryant maintained her balance before rolling through and out of bounds for a restart.
"At that point I saw that look in Kaylynn, like she knew she could win," Waters said.
Then in the closing seconds of the first period, Bryant got in deep on Johnson's left leg with an ankle pick and scored a takedown at the edge of the circle for a 3-0 lead heading into the second.
"I don't know if I'd ever straight up got a point on her like that," Bryant said. "And then it kind of clicked for me. She's beatable. She's so good, but it's not like she's impossible to beat. And that's when it clicked. And that's when I started picking up the tempo."
With the option to take top, bottom or neutral to start the second period, Bryant deferred, allowing Johnson to take bottom. Bryant kept Johnson's head to the mat, maintained her ride, and slowly leveraged her rival onto her back. Then came the sudden stoppage with the referee's hand hitting the mat, leaving Bryant initially with a what-happened look on her face.
"I think she thought, because this happened before when they wrestled, that the referee stopped the match because AJ called for injury time," Waters said of Bryant. "She just had this look like, 'Oh, he stopped the match.'"
Pushing herself up, Bryant's look of curiosity was quickly replaced by one of genuine shock as she looked toward her corner to see Waters and her father in full-blown celebration like a pair of kids on Christmas morning.
"Looking at her and then being by her dad, you can just feel that energy," Waters said. "I couldn't have been happier. We know how hard she's worked for that moment. To wrestle AJ, and all week we were like, 'Can't be focused on AJ. Let's go one match at a time.' But all that just came together. I heard the whistle and when I saw the hand, I think I jumped. I don't really remember. It was like an out-of-body experience. Then I remember pushing on her dad like, 'She did it.'"
After embracing her coaches and flooring her dad, Bryant walked toward her teammates for a group hug, then headed to the other end of the arena for further congratulations, still struggling to fathom what she had done.
"Each year I've been improving just a little bit," Bryant said. "I've been chasing her for three years. She's always been the one person that beat me. And today was the day when it really mattered."

title: Vikings return for another title shot
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings return for another title shot

 March 12, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1130
 Words 

 Read News Document

 UPPER MARLBORO — Thomas Wilson had struggled with his outside shot in recent games.That didn't seem to trouble anyone on Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys basketball team.
"My teammates, they had trust in me," Wilson said. "They wanted me to shoot the ball. My coach wanted me to shoot. So I made sure I shot the ball every time I got it."
Wilson got the ball with 10 seconds remaining Tuesday. The junior forward dribbled to the right side of the key, and with one defender on his left hip, and another flying toward him, let go an off-balance, fadeaway jumper that banked off the glass and through the net for the winning basket with 7.3 seconds left, lifting Cambridge-South Dorchester to a 65-63 victory over Liberty in a Class 1A state semifinal at Dr. Henry A. Wise Jr. High School.
Top-seeded Cambridge-SD (24-1) will bid for its first state title since 1996 Friday, when it meets No. 6 seed The SEED School (17-5) at 2 p.m. at the University of Maryland's XFINITY Center in College Park. The Sabers upset defending state champ Edmondson-Westside, 60-59, on a bank shot with 8 seconds remaining in Tuesday's second semifinal here.
"You've got to find any way to win these games," Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Tucker said after the Vikings earned their second straight trip to the state finals. "And TJ (Wilson) stepped up. That kid played his behind off."
Cambridge-SD never trailed in the first half, taking a 16-8 lead with 1:54 left in the first quarter. Koby Ennals (11 points) hit a 3-pointer to close the quarter, then scored on a pair of drives before Anthony Hughes' layup gave the Vikings their biggest lead of the game at 25-15 with a little over 5 minutes remaining before halftime.
But Liberty guard Gavin Speace (game-high 21 points), his time limited in the playoffs because of fasciitis, hit back-to-back 3 pointers, watched Nate Gitau bury a 3, then canned his fourth trey of the second quarter to knot the score at 27-all with 1:47 to go in the half.
"They're a crazy shooting team," Wilson said of Liberty, which finished with 14 3-pointers, half coming from Speace. "They were not missing."
But Cambridge-SD closed the half on an 8-0 run, as Semaj Pinder (16 points) scored on a put-back, Ennals flushed a two-handed dunk, Sterling Perkins (14 points) glided in for a layup, and Pinder converted another follow for a 35-27 halftime lead.
The fourth-seeded Lions (19-5), who were making their first state semifinal appearance in school history, opened the third quarter on a 14-5 surge. Tristan West — the all-Carroll County football player of the year — connected on a 3 before Speace capped the run with another 3-ball, giving Liberty its first lead at 41-40 midway through the quarter.
"We try to work inside out with having 6-(foot)-8 (Ethan Hart) and 6-4 (West)," Liberty head coach George Sinnott said. "But they did exactly what other teams have tried to do against us; clog the paint. Don't give us layups. We were lucky enough to hit some shots."
The Lions kept hitting shots.
Pinder's jumper put the Vikings back in front at 42-41. Jayden Zumbrun (13 points) made a 4-point play and Noah Gitau drained a 3-pointer, giving Liberty its biggest lead at 48-42 with 1:35 to go in the third.
Cambridge-SD responded. Perkins hit a 3-pointer, Wilson (16 points) scored on a drive and then hit a deep 3 from the corner at the buzzer for a 50-48 Vikings' lead heading into the fourth.
"That one at the end of the third killed us," Sinnott said of Wilson's 3.
"We wanted to slow their pace," Sinnott continued. "We felt because zero (Perkins) and four (Wilson) were shooting the ball so well we couldn't stay in our zone. So we played predominantly man with help, and then we'd trap every now and then. But they shot the ball well."
Zumbrun's deep corner 3 put Liberty back in front at 51-50 just 44 seconds into the third. But Wilson buried a 3, Perkins scored on a drive before Ennals went coast-to-coast for a layup and a 57-52 Vikings lead with 4:47 to play.
Speace's 3-pointer brought Liberty within 57-55. Wilson replied with his fourth and last 3 for a 60-55 lead. Speace connected on yet another 3-ball, shaving the C-SD lead to 60-58 with a little over 4 minutes still to play. A Pinder free throw and K'Marion Hall's follow moved the Vikings' lead to 63-58 with 2:25 remaining.
But Brady Bergen hit a follow and West (13 points) made a 3-ball from the top of the key to tie the game at 63-63 with 1:27 left.
Liberty used its last timeout with 52.3 seconds left. Pinder then made a steal with 32 seconds remaining, prompting a C-SD timeout.
"If we're going to get one shot, we're going to limit them time on the clock," Tucker said. "And that's exactly what we did. We were running set. We were going to wait, wait, wait."
Pinder crossed the halfcourt line with 27 seconds remaining, and maintained his dribble with West defending. Then with 15 seconds left, Pinder broke left, got a step on West, but drew a pair of defenders as he reached the foul line. Pinder's pass to an open Hall on the baseline was slightly deflected. Hall caught the deflection, and with three defenders closing, kicked it back out to Wilson near the 3-point line. Wilson drove to the right side of the foul line and, with West leaping toward, released his game-winner before hitting the floor and almost sliding out of bounds.
"I caught the ball and my teammates are like 'Shoot it,'" Wilson said. "He (West) was closing on (me) fast so I got to shoot something. So I just faded it and I knew it was good. I knew it was going in."
So did Ennals, who was positioned in front of the rim for a potential rebound.
"When he let the ball go I knew it was good," Ennals said. "I looked and I was like, 'Yeah, it's backboard.' And it went straight in."
With no timeouts, Spease hurried the ball upcourt and launched a shot well beyond the 3-point arc that cleared Ennals' outstretched hand and hit the far side of the backboard, ending the game.
"Big-time shot for a big-time kid," Tucker said of Wilson's game-winner. "He's been struggling. But shooting's all about confidence. And you can see it today. He gave up a 3-pointer on the other end and I said, 'TJ, go get it back. You hit a three' And what did he do? Stepped up and hit a three.
"That's what you do," Tucker continued. "You get it back. You can't pout. We've said this before. Nobody's going to feel sorry for you. Nobody. Go get it back. And that's what that kid did. He went and got it back."
