title: Weems, Martinez swim into history books with titles
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Weems, Martinez swim into history books with titles

 March 13, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1067
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Henry Martinez' optimism grew before he stepped on the blocks.Easton's Maddie Weems had a similar feeling after her feet left the blocks.
Four lengths of the pool later, that optimism had turned to gold Feb. 22, as Martinez, then Weems won their respective 100-yard freestyle events during the Class 3A/2A/1A state swimming championships at the University of Maryland's Eppley Recreation Center in College Park.
"It was kind of surreal because I never thought I'd see the one next to my name," Martinez said of turning to see his first-place finish on the scoreboard, making him the first in Kent County history to ever win a state swim title. "I was so used to, the past three years, seeing a four, a five an eight (at states). It was really cool to see the one right there."
The Bayside Conference champion in the 50 and 100 freestyles, Martinez earned runner-up finishes in both events at the 3A/2A/1A East Regional championships, clocking a time of 21.89 seconds to La Plata's Clinton Cupples' 21.86 in the 50, and taking second in the 100 (48.15) to La Plata's Gavin Abelende (46.36).
Cupples beat Martinez again in the 50 at states, posting a first-place 20.71 to the Trojan senior's personal-record 21.13.
"I guess my confidence went down a little, but I was still excited about the placement," Martinez said.
Two boys events later later, Martinez was preparing for the 100, but noticed Abelende wasn't there.
"Before I got to the block, I knew there was one person that was faster than me seed time," Martinez said of Abelende. "And I saw that he wasn't coming to the blocks. So that's when I knew I had a really good chance being the champ. I was pretty excited about that."
Martinez had a slight edge after the first 50, but after making the second turn began opening a slight lead he held through the second lap, touching the wall in personal-record 47.37. Poolesville's Eli Ferrara was second in 48.73.
"Throughout the race I was going as hard as possible," Martinez said. "And I knew what to do at every wall; every stroke. I was pulling as hard as possible. The last turn was the hardest because I could feel my legs going numb.
"I guess the only real difference is I knew this is the last time that I'd have the opportunity to be on that podium, get that (gold) medal," Martinez said. "So it gave me more motivation every practice. I knew it was all leading up to that final. Because that was the final race and final chance I'd get. So when I finished, just seeing my name and the (number) one next to it was a pretty cool feeling."
Martinez became only the fourth swimmer from a Bayside Conference school to win the boys 100 freestyle in the 18-year history of the championships — excluding the canceled 2021 season — and just missed eclipsing the 47.35 set by Kent Island's Wade Boarman in 2009 as the fastest time ever by a Bayside swimmer in the 100.
"Last year he was seeded second in the 50 at states and I think he was a little upset with himself coming in fourth," Kent head coach Grayson Wise said. "But I think that needed to happen. I think he needed to see, like anything can happen. He knew he had to go out there and drop a significant amount of time (in the 100) and that's really just what he did."
The defending 3A/2A/1A girls state champ in the 200 freestyle, Weems couldn't get under 2 minutes in the event, and despite winning the conference championship decide to drop it in favor of the 100.
"I didn't do club swim this year so I didn't really have enough endurance for it," Weems said of the 200. "I swam it at Baysides to see what I would get (first-place 2:00.98) but I still didn't go under 2 minutes. I just didn't feel comfortable swimming it so I decided to stick with the 100 free."
Weems also stuck with the 50 free. The junior was runner-up at regionals (24.86), then was 0.01 off her career best at states, finishing third (season-best 24.47) in a duel with La Plata's Jadyn Woolsey (24.01) and Damascus' Hannah Douglas (24.41).
"It was weird because before the 50 free, I was excited," Weems said. "Once we got to the 100 free, I was so nervous. I was like, 'If I don't win I'm going to be really disappointed.'"
But Weems admitted those nerves dissipated once she sprung from the blocks.
"Right when I dove in the water," Weems said of when she thought she could win the 100. "I felt as long as I kept my underwaters (technique off the turns) good that I could keep the lead.
"Freestyle is so fast," Weems continued. "It's just hard to catch up even a little bit. So I feel like with my lead, even with just that little bit, I felt confident because I know how hard it is to even pick up from that."
Despite her edge on Douglas, Weems said she was swimming with nerves down the stretch.
"During the last lap I was a little nervous just because I feel like I tend to give out," Weems said. "I get too tired. Especially with me not swimming as much as I usually do. But it all worked out."
Weems touched the wall with another PR (53.13) while Douglas took second in 53.55.
While the Bayside has produced 12 back-to-back state champions in the same event, Weems became the first from a conference school to win an event (200) one year, drop it, then win at different distance the following year.
"She was going into the 50 very hopeful, but she knew it was going to be a tighter race," Easton head coach Katie Spies said of Weems. "But then she was even more game-on for the 100. She knew what she had to do, and she knew all the pieces of the puzzle that had to come together to make that race happen. She was ready."
Easton junior Maddy Finch capped her season with a pair of season-bests, placing third in both the 200 individual medley (2:13.62) and the 100 breaststroke (1:07.48). The North Bayside's only other top-three individual finish came from Queen Anne's junior Madalynn Clagett, who was third in the 200 free (1:59.60).
Kent Island's girls 200 medley relay of Maddie Parks, Kara Seymour, Jordan Sarier and Alexia Grossman was third in 1:56.13.

title: Vikings look to complete year-long bid
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings look to complete year-long bid

 March 13, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 739
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The day after last year's loss in the Class 1A state championship, Cambridge-South Dorchester High boys head basketball coach Shawn Tucker received a text message from forward Kobe Ennals."He already had next year's (state-title) date circled on his calendar," Tucker said.
That date has arrived, as the top-seeded Vikings (24-1) will face the The SEED School (17-5) on Friday at 2 p.m. for the Class 1A state championship at the University of Maryland's XFINITY Center in College Park.
"They've got size," Tucker said of SEED, which has three players listed at 6-foot-8 and another at 6-7. "We're going to have to really rebound by committee and get on the glass. But I like our chances."
A chance created Tuesday night, when Thomas Wilson Jr. banked home an off-balance fadeway jumper with 7.3 seconds left to boost the Vikings to a 65-63 victory over Liberty in the semifinals. A chance that was created on the SEED side of the ledger about two hours later, when Khaled Al-Matten Evans banked in a winner with 8 seconds remaining to help the Sabers complete a 60-59 come-from-behind victory over defending state champion Edmondson-Westside.
"I saw them play Edmondson last year," SEED head coach Edward Green Jr. said of Cambridge-SD Thursday during a phone interview. "I've been keeping up on them all year. So of course, very good team. Back in the title game, so that says a lot about their program. So that loss last year in the final, and to be able to come right back and reach the final again, I have a lot of respect for them doing that. I think they have overall good team size, and they're very talented."
A talented team that will bid for the school's first state title since 1996, and can have a different scoring leader any game.
A senior, the 6-5 Ennals has averaged 20 points and 11 rebounds an outing this season, while 6-4 junior Semaj Pinder comes in averaging 19 points a game. Junior guard Sterling Perkins Jr. has scored 15 a game, and Wilson, who has emerged down the stretch, had averaged 10 per contest. The Vikings have also gotten big contributions from seniors Anthony Hughes and Jaden Harris, and sophomore K'Marion Hall.
"We're a year older," said Tucker, who noted his team leaned heavily on graduated guard LaShaun Moody last season. "Our juniors were sophomores last year and they were out there just playing. Now, they're out there understanding our goal.
"And we're better this year because we had a guy like Thomas Wilson on our roster, and nobody knows about him," Tucker continued. "The kid can shoot the cover off the basketball. And he's getting opportunities. Now, he's been in the starting lineup and nobody really talks about him."
Green may have wondered if anybody was going to talk about his team after the Sabers suffered a 59-43 loss to St. Vincent Pallotti on Jan. 28. But SEED hasn't lost since and arrives to its first state final in program history riding a 10-game win streak.
"In our last loss to St. Vincent Pallotti, we didn't really step up and show our best selves," Green said. "So it was as matter of us not taking advantage of opportunity in the big games. As a small school, we're trying to make a name for ourself. But every opportunity we got against like an A Conference school, or we'd play Philly teams and teams in Virginia, and we didn't play our best basketball."
The Sabers played some of their best ball Tuesday against No. 2 seed Edmondson-Westside, erasing a seven-point, third quarter deficit en route to upsetting the defending champs.
"It's about understanding our identity," Green said. "And we have a defensive identity."
SEED has also established a winning identity since February. In addition to junior shooting guard, Al-Matten Evans, the backcourt features sophomore point guard Chase Pralieau and junior Tyler Dubose. Senior Ahmad Evans, a 6-8 center, 6-8 junior forward Merdi Tshiabide and 6-5 junior sixth man Omar Williams will look to make impacts inside and on the boards today.
"We just have to be true to ourselves," Green said. "I think defense travels. If we can limit some of the things they like to do, maybe take one thing away from them, I think it will give us a chance. But they have a lot of guys who can contribute. So we can't really focus as much on what they're going to do as much as what we have control over."

title: Rain, mist don't stop St. Paddy's Day 5K race in Denton

content:
Rain, mist don't stop St. Paddy's Day 5K race in Denton

 March 18, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: AHMAD GARNETT agarnett@chespub.com | Section: Local News 
 
 344
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON — Misty rain conditions did not keep the running faithful from the 17th annual St.Paddy's day 5K race in Denton.Families and friends came out in heavy numbers to participate in the race and show their St.Patrick's Day spirit.
While the rain dampened race participation numbers, the turnout was still in high numbers.
"I think considering the weather the turnout was pretty great," said Jamie Beechey, director of Park and Recreations for Caroline County. "Obviously we always like to see more runners come in, but again great turnout, people are in really great spirits and definitely in the St. Patrick's Day mood."
The race started with the Leprechaun Dash which featured 12-15 racers from 3 to 6 years old participating in an 100-meter dash.
Racing officials called runners participating in the dash "our future."
The race begin with a family in the front. Charles Gailunas, his wife Erika Gailunas and two daughters, Caroline and Charlotte Gailunas, participated in the race together.
Every time the Gailunas family runs it's a full circle moment on how Charles and Erika met.
"We've been running this as long as we've lived here, five years now we've been doing this event," Charles Gailunas said. "My wife and I actually met because of a 5K, so it's a little bit of a family history."
Runners sported their St.Patricks Day green with one running in an inflated leprechaun suit.
The winner of the 5K race was 15-year-old Miguel Castro with a time of 20:45. While Castro was excited to win, he was aiming for an 18-minute target time.
"Under 18 or 18 flat was my goal," Castro said. "It felt really great to finish first, that was my goal. I just keep pushing it through. It's all about mentality and that's pretty much it."
The event proceeds go to scholarships for children who participate in Caroline County programs. Beechey believes they finished with scholarships for 90 kids.
"I would say we're probably in line with with last year," Beechey said. "I think from what we raise for this event, we'll be able to provide about 90 scholarships to children, so pretty awesome."

title: MISTER BOYS
author: Bill Haufe
content:
MISTER BOYS

 March 19, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 570
 Words 

 Read News Document

 WYE MILLS — One opened a modest lead before the other reeled it back in, not wanting the game to get too far away.That ebb and flow continued from start to finish Tuesday night, before Kent Island High's Max Hershkowitz hit a pair of free throws and a layup that helped give the North a 103-101 victory over the South in the 39th annual Bayside Conference Cliff Mister Senior Boys All-Star game at Chesapeake College in front a near packed house.
"Once again, we got to make the game close," said North head coach Shawn Tucker, who four days earlier watched his Cambridge-South Dorchester team pull out a 36-33 overtime victory over The SEED School to win the Class 1A state championship. "I'm kind of spoiled. I like winning. Winning is contagious."
But like the Vikings' postseason run, winning wasn't decided until late in the game.
A pair of buckets from Parkside's Maurice Brown helped the South to an early 11-5 lead. Easton's Darrel Lee (10 points) and Hershkowitz (15 points) each hit 3-pointers as part of a 10-0 run that put the North ahead 15-11 with 3 minutes, 48 seconds left in the first quarter. Two Hershkowitz baskets gave the North a 26-20 edge after one quarter.
The North maintained that six-point edge, but baskets from James M. Bennett's Zakai Smullen (12 points) and Stephen Decatur's Davin Chandler (19 points) preceded a 3-pointer from Decatur's Noah Tucker (19 points), drawing the South within 34-33 with a little over 6 minutes remaining in the first half.
Colonel Richardson's Tarron Hammon canned a 3-pointer and Cambridge-SD's Koby Ennals (18 points), the North Bayside Player of the Year, scored six straight points to give the North its biggest lead of the game at 46-37 with just under 3 minutes still to go in the half. The South reduced its deficit to five before Queen Anne's County's Jimmy Holthaus (eight points) and North Dorchester's Alvin Hutton Jr. gave the North a 50-43 lead at halftime.
A 12-5 South run to open the third quarter tied the game at 55-all. North Caroline's Jarvis Thomas, Kent Island's Kamm Green (18 points) and Hutton combined for a 7-0 North run and a 64-57 lead. The South responded with a 14-2 burst that featured nine points from Tucker, including a four-point play, for a 71-66 edge. But a pair of scores from Green and a basket from North Caroline's Tyson Weber returned the lead to the North at 76-75 entering the fourth quarter.
"They had fun," Tucker said. "It's the last time the folks get to see everybody together, North and South. I think it's a great experience for these young men."
Play continued to seesaw.
Green and Hughes (13 points) moved the North to an 80-75 lead. Bennett's Jayden Colon (15 points) scored consecutive baskets to push the South ahead 81-80. Ennals' 3 put the North up. The South nudged back in front at 86-83. Hughes then hit a 3 before, Ennals scored on consecutive drives, and Holthaus made a layup for a 92-86 North lead with a little over 4 minutes remaining.
The South wouldn't get any closer than 99-98 as Hershkowitz hit two free throws with 47 seconds remaining and scored a layup on a dish from Hughes for a 103-98 lead.
"I was like, 'It's winning time,'" answered Tucker, when asked what he said during his final timeout. "'We're going to win.' I know it's just bragging rights, but it's so much fun."

title: North survives South's late comeback bid
author: Bill Haufe
content:
North survives South's late comeback bid

 March 19, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 575
 Words 

 Read News Document

 WYE MILLS — Whether the game's a scrimmage, holiday play, regular season or playoff, Kent Island High girls head basketball coach David Plumer wants to win.Plumer didn't change his approach Tuesday night as coach of the North Bayside all-stars, and his team appeared headed in that direction as it built a 20-point lead in the opening 10-minute quarter. The South stars steadily whittled that lead down though before rallying into the lead midway through the fourth.
But Cambridge-South Dorchester's Tejanae Ballin hit a free throw before draining a 3-pointer with 1 minute, 37 seconds remaining to secure a 56-52 North win in the 39th annual Bayside Conference Cliff Mister Girls Senior All-Star game at Chesapeake College.
"We got off to a strong start thankfully," Plumer said smiling. "If we didn't it might have been a different outcome."
Cambridge-SD's trio of Destiny Johnson (game-high 15 points), Le'Asia Todd (12 points) and Ballin (nine points) accounted for 19 of the North's 26 first-quarter points. Wicomico's Carlissa Johnson (12 points) gave the South a 2-0 lead. The North proceeded to go on a 15-0 tear that fueled a 26-6 first-quarter lead.
The South started chipping into that lead in the second quarter, and trimmed its deficit to nine at 31-22, when Snow Hill's Marrah Milbourne (13 points) hit a 3-pointer and scored on back-to-back drives.
After a North timeout, Todd, the North Bayside Player of the Year, scored on a putback. Kent Island's Abigail Staton hit a 3 and Ballin scored to help the North take a 38-26 lead into halftime.
Two Destiny Johnson buckets, a jumper from Queen Anne's Lucy Taylor, and Todd's free throw and putback widened the North's lead to 47-30 halfway through the third. But the South started working the ball inside to Wi-Hi's Johnson, who scored six points in a 12-2 run that pulled South within eight heading into the fourth quarter.
"Hey listen, all the post play, it's phenomenal to see," Plumer said. "You don't see that a whole lot with girls basketball. So post play was really good on both sides. They figured out Le'Asia (Todd) a little bit."
Colonel Richardson's Tabria Williams hit a jumper to give the North a 50-40 lead with 43 seconds elapsed in the fourth period. But the South put together its final run, reeling off 10 consecutive points. Stephen Decatur's Allison Swift connected on a 3-pointer, cutting the North lead to 50-49. Parkside's Zion Oge made one of two from the foul line to tie the game, then watched Carlissa Johnson score inside for the South's first lead since 2-0.
But C-SD's Johnson scored in transition off a turnover to knot the game at 52-all with 3:09 remaining. Ballin made the first of two free-throw attempts to inch the North back in front at 53-52 with 2:49 remaining.
The South struggled with turnovers down the stretch and after a North timeout, Ballin buried a 3 for a 56-52 lead.
"Tejanae hit a big three. Not what we asked her to do," Plumer said with a slight chuckle. "We were trying to go to the basket, get the fouls."
Both teams had chances to tighten or increase the score over the final seconds, but combined to miss six free throws.
"We started out hot," Plumer said. "We were doing pretty good on the backside. And then some kids can't make it to the one practice we have so when you're subbing in they don't know exactly what we're trying to do. But it was a lot of fun."

title: Cambridge-SD's Young caps record-setting career with four state title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Cambridge-SD's Young caps record-setting career with four state title

 March 21, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1274
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — Her older brother and sister ran track.And she always liked the sport, but never really had anyone to work out with, or knew of a team to join.
So when Enazajah "Bop" Young got to Cambridge-South Dorchester High as a freshman, she learned the school had an indoor track team.
"That's when I was like, 'OK, I'm going to join track and see where it goes,'" Young said.
By the time she blazed across the finish line in her final race of the high school indoor season Feb. 27 at the Prince George's Sports and Learning Complex, Young had gone where no Bayside Conference athlete had ever gone before.
The Bayside has had 11 back-to-back state champions in indoor track. But when Young won the girls 55-meter hurdles at this year's state meet in a new Class 1A-record time 8.01 seconds, she became the first Bayside athlete — male or female — to go back-to-back in two different events at states: the 55 meters and the 55 hurdles.
"She's just great and talented," Vikings head coach Clint Falduto said of his star senior.
She's also developed a talent for setting records.
The only female to win a state indoor title at Cambridge-SD since the school began its program in 2017, Young's four individual state championships are the most in Bayside indoor history, putting her one ahead of former Kent County greats Francis Ciganek — boys 1,600 (1999, 2000); 800 (2000) — and Katie Stevenson — girls 1,600 ('99, 00); 3,200 ('00) — and former Crisfield standout Kyle Noll — 55 hurdles ('19, '20); high jump ('19).
Young was bidding to become only the fifth female sprinter in the 47-year history of the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association state indoor meet — there was no meet in 2021 — and the first from a 1A school, to win three state titles in the 55 meters this year. She ran the fastest time in the preliminaries, clocking a personal-record 7.15, but placed third (7.22) in the finals, finishing behind Friendly's Tressia Davis (7.14) and Largo's Lailah Fersner (7.19).
"I was actually trying to get (state title number) five in the 55, but that didn't really go as planned," Young said.
What did go as planned — minus a few slivers of time and a slight blip perhaps noticed only by Young — was the 55 hurdles.
"Great start," Young said. "I felt as though maybe in the middle of the race, one of my hurdles, I was just a little too high. So I had to recover. But other than that everything else was good."
Everything?
"I still hit a time that I wanted to a little bit, but not necessarily," said Young, smiling, yet wincing at the time she really wanted. "I was trying to go sub-8. I was trying to get the meet record. I was right there."
Though the state-record 7.73 set by Surrattsville's Tishonna Watson in 1990 remains secure, Young's Class-1A record 8.01 left her in a three-way tie for sixth fastest time in the history of the state meet across all four classifications.
"When you watch her run it is a sight to be seen," Falduto said of Young's blend of speed, grace and near flawless form. "Especially when you see the difference of placement from first to second. Usually that's a tight race. But she's so naturally gifted at understanding that event that she just really took off with it."
Young's 8.01 was the fastest time run in a state hurdles final by a girl from a Bayside school, eclipsing the mark she set last year (8.25), which put her ahead of former North Caroline stars Emily Lewis (8.57) and Samantha Cash (8.78), who won the Class 2A titles in 2019 and '20, respectively.
"I think it's a blessing," Young said of her record-setting indoor career. "It's good to know that my hard work and what I focused my goals on has worked out for me."
It could have easily not worked though.
Young initially ran indoors as way to get into condition for spring softball. That quickly changed after her indoor debut.
"When I ran my first meet, and I'd seen everybody was like, 'Oh my gosh. She's a freshman. She's so fast,'" Young said. "I was like, 'All right. I might have a chance in this.' So I started taking it more seriously, especially the 55 and the hurdles."
It showed, as Young qualified for states in both the 55 sprint and hurdles as a freshman. But in the preliminaries of the hurdles that year she fell, which slowed her in the 55 prelims.
She was hardly deterred.
"It actually gave me more motivation and a reason to do better the next year," Young said. "I wanted to prove that I was better than just falling; that I actually had a chance to do good at states."
One year later, Young wasn't just good at states, she was real good.
The sophomore was second in the 55 hurdles, running an 8.48 that left her just one hundredth of a second behind champion Ayniah Fersner of Largo. She then became only the fourth girl in conference history to win the 55 sprint, crossing the finish line in 7.37 seconds.
One year later, she again made history by becoming the first Bayside athlete to sweep the hurdles and sprint titles at states. Young won the hurdles in 8.25. The 55 sprint though had a little bit more drama to it from start to finish.
"In the (55) finals, the girl that was supposed to win false started," Young said. "When she false started I was thinking in my head, 'You have to win the race now because nobody else here is faster than you.' I got off to a good start and I just finished through the line."
But Young didn't know she had won until after a lengthy review.
"It was a really long wait," Young said. "I was like, 'Did I win? Did I win?' It took a really long time for my name to come up (first)."
Despite her success in the sprint, Young over time had gained a preference for the hurdles, an event where the slightest miscue can cost precious fractions or leave a runner sprawled out on the track, as Young learned her freshman year.
"My main problem when I first started was basically just getting the three-step," Young said of the technique between the five hurdles. "I had the speed. But I would switch (lead) legs a lot, which would take more time."
Young continued improving her skill set. She worked on attacking the hurdles, leading with her left leg. She practiced getting the right snap on her trail leg, making sure she was stepping over the hurdles, instead of jumping or gliding. She worked with her coaches like Falduto, who helped tweak and polish her form.
Then there was the added benefit of having a background in dance.
"Rhythm plays a lot into it," said Young, who did majorette dancing, along with hip-hop and other styles in parades, competitions and events. "When you do hurdles it's a certain tempo, like you're going, 'Three, three, three.' Dancing you have counts. So I feel like coordination and rhythm from dance kind of helped me in hurdles."
That combination helped Young go undefeated in the hurdles this season en route to a fourth gold medal and a list of records.
"Over the years, when she realized the talent she has, and understanding the technique it takes and mastering it, it became more like breathing to her," Falduto said. "It became so normalized. Because it can take kids four years to figure out how to properly do hurdles. But when she learned, and how quick she learned, it just became second nature to her. It was just natural."

title: Bucs, Sabres set sights on titles
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bucs, Sabres set sights on titles

 March 25, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1389
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The postseason is a long ways off, but Saints Peter and Paul High's boys lacrosse team has already faced its toughest competition this season.The Sabres' first five games of the regular season featured Calvert Hall, which is ranked No. 2 nationally in the latest USA Lacrosse Magazine poll, and No. 1 in the state. Sts. Peter & Paul also has had games against three other top-20 ranked teams in Maryland — No. 5 Bullis Prep; No 16. Good Counsel; and No. 19 Severn.
"It's everything I wanted," Sabres head coach Todd Wolters said of the opening gauntlet. "I'm very happy with what we have."
Though Sts. Peter & Paul lost its first five games before routing James M. Bennett 17-1 last week, Wolters said he's not concerned with his personal record, but is focused on preparing his team for another run at a Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association B Conference title after falling shy in last year's championship game.
Though Kent Island has yet to begin its regular season, head coach Bobby Woolley has also been impressed with what he's seen from his team during a tough preseason slate that included dates with No. 18 DeMatha, No. 22 Broadneck and No. 23 South River before Monday's final exhibition against Springside Chestnut Hill Academy of Philadelphia.
"We put our necks out there right away and just started learning about ourselves," said Woolley, whose preseason also included Sherwood, Fallston, Cape Henlopen and Archmere Academy. "I feel like we got a lot of what it takes."
Easton will look to send longtime head coach Dennis Keenan off as a winner. The Warriors graduated the majority of their firepower from a year ago, but look to have the goods for another solid season, along with Queen Anne's and North Caroline.
While Keenan begins his farewell tour, two Mid-Shore teams welcome new head coaches, with Ben Joiner taking over at Kent County, and Teddy Peyton at Gunston. There is also a new kid on the block, with North Dorchester beginning its first year of varsity play under the direction of veteran head coach Steve Hurley.
"We don't have much experience so we're going to learn a lot of game this year and next year," said Hurley, who has 18 out for the team. "We're having fun; kids are learning."
Here's a look at this year's teams.
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Brendan Bromwell.
Who's Where: Goalie: Andrew McMichael (Sr.); Defense: Christian Dockins (Sr.); Jeffrey Sellman (So.); Juan Slaughter (So.); Midfield: Gavin Weber (So.); Tabrion Watts (Sr.); Kimir Lake (Sr.); Attack: Charles Spedden (Jr.); Gibby Robinson (So.); Nate McClaren (Sr.).
Outlook: The Vikings are fast and athletic defensively, led by four-year man Dockins. Bromwell applauded McMichael, who has stepped in at goalie.
"I'm proud of him," Bromwell said. "We didn't have anybody and Andrew came to me and said, 'Hey, I know we're kind of struggling in this spot, I'll give it a try.' And he's done good."
There is also athleticism at the midfield with Watts and Lake. Bromwell likes Weber's old-school style of play and will have him facing off.
Spedden, whose growth in the game is "insane", according to Bromwell, quarterbacks the attack.
EASTON
Head Coach: Dennis Keenan.
Who's Where: Goalies: Mason Quicke (So.); Randall Mills (Sr.); Defense: Eddie Whelan (Sr.); Ethan Finlay (Sr.); Max Smith (So.); Nathan Lapp (Sr.); Ethan Ballance (Jr.); Darren Foxwell (Sr.); Midfield: Spencer Gunshenan (So.); Conner Hensley (Sr.); Logan Friend (Jr.); Cole Murphy (So.); Finn Gunshenan (Sr.); Landon Chaney (Sr.); Blake Royer (So.); Colin Keenan (Sr.); Luke Stanco (Jr.); Grayson Buritsch (Jr.); Miles Chaney (So.); Blake Newton (Jr.); Attack: Campbell Taliaferro (Sr.); Jackson Wieland (Jr.); David Rogers (Jr.); Trace Haddaway (So.); Miles Abell (Jr.).
Outlook: The Warriors lost the bulk of their scoring with the graduation Drew Schmidt (54 points) and Hudson Royer (43 points), who are both at Lynchburg (Va.), and Tyler Rardin (50 points).
While there looks to be plenty of offensive options, Keenan said defense is the team's strength, and was impressed with Quicke's 12-save effort against North Caroline in Friday's opener.
"We're building," Keenan said. "They listen. They're willing to be taught."
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Bobby Woolley.
Who's Where: Goalies: Quinn Burns (Fr.); Chris Lemme (Sr.); Cody Jones (Sr.); Defense: Gavan Henry (Sr.); Ryan Austin (Sr.); Robert Hottel (So.); Eric Hofmann (Sr.); Grayson Corn (So.); Connor Byrne (Jr.); Finn McGrath (So.); Midfield: Keegan Green (Sr.); Connor Gardner (So.); Marshall Dandy (Jr.); Aidan Henry (Sr.); Attack: Mark Rees (Sr.); Brian Rees (Jr.); Colton Schneck (Sr.); Liam Dermer (Sr.); Face-off: Ricky Verger (Sr.); Roy Scott (Jr.).
Outlook: The Bucs' bid last year for a third consecutive Class 2A state title was foiled in the semifinals by eventual state champ Glenelg. All-North Bayside Offensive Player of the Year Tucker Claxton graduated along with fellow first-team all-North picks Owen Wynot and Micah Quinn.
But Woolley thinks this squad is in a more stable place heading into this season compared to last year, when he and his staff seemed to be forever patching holes. A strong returning cast, including all-North first-teamers Gavan Henry and Green, St. Mary's transfers Hottel and Dandy, and promising freshman class figure to have the Bucs challenging for a 10th Bayside Conference title in 13 years.
But nobody has thrilled Woolley more than the return of Hofmann, who missed all last season with an injury.
"Having Eric back is a game-changer, as far as controlling the field between the restraining lines and putting pressure on people to get the ball into their offensive zone," Woolley said.
There's been a three-way battle for starting goalie between Lemme, Jones and freshman Burns, who has really turned heads.
"All in all, I feel like we're more of a complete team heading into this year than we were last year," Woolley said. "We're positioned with high expectations and talent to back it."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: Gavin Houseman.
Who's Where: Goalie: Koen Jackson (Sr.); Defense: Derek Jones (Sr.); Gabe Holt (So.); Sam Heimbuch (Fr.); Midfield: Jimmy Cohoon (Jr.); Owen Walstrum (Jr.); Dylan Robinson (Jr.); Charlie Fleshman; Attack: Jake Hoofnagle (Fr.); Mason Ratcliff (Jr.); Corey Bunce (Sr.)
Outlook: The Bulldogs finished .500 in the regular season a year ago, and after a solid outing in Friday's opener against Easton, Houseman thinks there's potential to improve.
"We thought we'd have to take a step back with having younger guys taking more of a senior role but we really haven't had to," Houseman said. "We've picked up pretty much where we left off last year. We played pretty strong against Easton. We had minor hiccups, which I think are easy to fix."
QUEEN ANNE'S COUNTY
Head Coach: Brad Niesz.
Who's Where: Goalie: Brian Maleski (Jr.); Defense: Brett Bast (Sr.); Ethan Hahn (Sr.); James Rath (Jr.); Conner Cheezum (Sr.); Ryan Lee (Sr.); Brian Patrick; Midfield: Tanner Lyon (Sr.); Conlan Nagle (Sr.); Carter Hercher (So.); Casey Ryan (Jr.); Midfield-Attack: Tyler Crist (Jr.); Charlie Schmidt (Jr.); Jackson Shiley (Jr.); Sam Yetman (Jr.); Attack: Jamison Kendall (Jr.).
Outlook: The Lions graduated a lot of experience, particularly on the defensive end. Gone is first-team all-North Bayside goalie Dino Blue. Niesz said the loss of defenseman Hunter Kelly will also hurt, but the return of Lee, a first-team choice a year ago, should anchor the defense.
"We've had to move around a number of players," Niesz said. "We are a relatively small program in terms of numbers so we're going to ask guys to fill multiple roles."
SAINTS PETER & PAUL
Head Coach: Todd Wolters.
Who's Where: Goalie: Hank Wolters (Jr.); Defense: Porter Bishop (Jr.); Daniel Schwaninger (Jr.); Jackson Jancosko (Fr.); Langdon Anderson (Jr.); Cole Philip (Fr.); Drake Stolba (Jr.); Midfield: Grant Messick (Jr.); Lane Williams (Sr.); Mason Roland (Fr.); Jamir Demby (Fr.); Eddie Albright (Fr.); Attack: JJ Rardin (Jr.); Noah Zimmerman (Sr.); Andrew Steinhardt (So.); Liam Durnbaugh (Jr.).
Outlook: The Sabres lost in last year's MIAA B Conference final to Archbishop Curley, but may be stronger this season.
The defense could be among the conference's best with Hank Wolters back in goal, fronted by Bishop, who Coach Wolters has called one of the best in the country, Schwaninger, Jancosko and Anderson.
The offense also appears loaded with the return of Rardin, Zimmerman, Steinhardt and Durmbaugh. The biggest concern — other than staying healthy — may be between the restraining lines where the midfield struggled through the first five games.
"We're nowhere near full strength," Todd Wolters said. "But they've seen what good teams are like. I'm here to win a B Conference championship and these are the games that will help us."
Editor's Note: Information on Gunston and Kent County was unavailable at press time.

title: Rardin, Sabres handle Lions
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Rardin, Sabres handle Lions

 March 26, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 668
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — It was a win.But Saints Peter and Paul High boys head lacrosse coach Todd Wolters made that concession after emphasizing that if his team really does have championship aspirations this season, it will have to work on the small things and play a lot better.
JJ Rardin scored six goals and the Sabres built a seven-goal halftime lead Wednesday on the way to their second straight win via to a 12-4 victory over Queen Anne's County.
"We didn't hustle," Wolters said. "We can't pick up ground balls. We don't want to make the next pass. We had many opportunities but we don't pass the ball. We don't want to move the ball. And we all want to sit and watch two players do it. We have to be better."
Wolters acknowledged he did see some good things in the first half, as the Sabres (2-5) had four different players score while building a 4-0 lead after the first quarter.
Rardin, who scored three goals in each half, scored from close range 2 minutes, 38 seconds into the game. Less than a minute later, Grant Messick (two goals) beat Lions goalie Brian Maleski low. A little over 2 minutes after that, Noah Zimmerman (three assists) zipped a pinpoint pass to a cutting Liam Durnbaugh, who neatly flipped the ball over his shoulder for a 3-0 lead. Mason Roland capped the opening flurry by converting a Durnbaugh pass for a goal.
"A lot of this roster is back," Queen Anne's head coach Brad Niesz said of Sts. Peter & Paul, which reached the Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association B Conference final last year. "And I know a lot of them are juniors, and even sophomores, but they've played a year or two together. We're still working on that chemistry, especially on our defensive end. We've had a lot of guys step up in roles that are more significant than I guess they've played in the past, and now it's their time to be the man.
"On the offensive side, I think with them scoring a couple of goals out of the gate, I felt like we got a little bit rushed," Niesz continued. "There's a lot of things that we're really good at that we didn't necessarily do today."
Tyler Crist veered in from the left and, while falling forward, put the Lions' first goal of the season past Sabres goalie Hank Wolters (nine saves) early in the second quarter.
But Sts. Peter & Paul answered with four more goals. Zimmerman scored to restore the four-goal edge with 9:37 left in the first half. Durnbaugh patiently waited before finding Messick for a goal and a 4-1 lead with under 5 minutes to go. Rardin added two more, curling in from the right side and slipping a goal inside the post before ripping another one on a tough angle from left wing.
"The first half wasn't horrible," Coach Wolters said.
Durnbaugh notched his second goal early in the third quarter, and Zimmerman assisted on Rardin's fourth goal, fattening the Sabres' lead to 10-1 heading in the fourth quarter.
Rardin somehow came open out front, snagged a Zimmerman feed and sent a sidewinder past Maleski for an 11-1 lead with 31 seconds gone in the fourth quarter.
But Sam Yetman scored twice in less than a minute, and, after Rardin netted his sixth goal, Jamison Kendall beat Sabres backup goalie Jaxson Usilton.
"They're kids hustled," Coach Wolters said of Queen Anne's. "They may not be the most talented but they played hard. They really did. And they never gave up. They never quit and I respect that.
"It's a win," the Sabres head coach added. "And it was a home win. It was never in doubt. But there's a lot of work to do. And they'll bounce back. But we're not playing good fundamental lacrosse. I'm not saying we have to be perfectionists, but this wasn't good lacrosse. We got to start picking up and playing smarter, playing in control. We're going to be fine. But that was not a really good job today."

title: Warriors extend strong beginning
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors extend strong beginning

 March 27, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 489
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton High's girls lacrosse team didn't notch its third win last season until mid-April.The Warriors have already won three games this season, and they still have one remaining this month.
Anna Crist scored four goals and Sam Murphy, Addie Knox and Dakota Lhotsky each recorded hat tricks Thursday, as the Warriors stayed unbeaten via a 17-9 victory over Salisbury School.
"I think it's still early days," Easton head coach Katie Lowman said after the Warriors improved to 3-0, leaving them three wins short of last year's 6-5 record. "And with any game you come away with things to work on. But I'm happy with the overall result."
Salisbury School (0-2) actually took a 1-0 lead, when Alexandra Collins (game-high five goals) beat Easton goalie Zelia Proa 1 minute, 45 seconds into the game.
But Murphy scored on a free position and Knox scored off a face-off just 50 seconds later, giving Easton a lead it never relinquished at 2-1. Lily Tiebosch and Lhotsky each added a goal late in the first to stretch that lead to 4-1 before Salisbury's Jenna Link (two goals) pulled the Dragons within two with 29.2 seconds to go in the first.
Salisbury crept within 4-3 on Collins' free-position strike 2:15 into the second. Knox's second goal and Lhotsky's short-handed goal moved Easton's lead to 6-3. The Dragons continued to stick around, with Alexandra Dawson (two goals) scoring on a free-position chance with 4:22 remaining in the first half.
But Easton blew the game open with nine consecutive goals, starting with Crist's first goal with 3:56 left in the first half, and ending with Murphy's third with 2:27 to go in the third for a 15-5 lead.
"I think when you have momentum and you have energy that is what naturally happens," Lowman said. "One thing we're working on is keeping that same energy the whole game, and maintaining that standard. We're working on it."
Goals from Crist, Myka Motovidlak (two), Knox and Lhotsky extended Easton's lead to 10-4 at halftime. The Warriors' lead ballooned to 14-4 in span of less that 3 minutes in the third quarter, as Motovidlak and Murphy each scored once before Crist slipped a pair of goals past Dragons goalie Elizabeth Donoway, starting the game's running clock.
"Sam was a great transfer in," Lowman said of the senior midfielder who transferred from Saints Peter and Paul at the beginning of the school year. "And most of our starters returned. We've got that experience, but we're still young. So it's kind of like the best of both worlds. We have experience that's going to be here for the next couple years. Just looking to build on it."
Easton carried a 15-5 lead into the fourth period, when Lowman started pulling her starters. The Dragons refused to simply let the remaining minutes play out, outscoring the Warriors 4-2 in the fourth period. Salisbury trimmed its deficit to 15-9 before Crist and Taylor Bowen scored in the final 2 minutes.

title: Henry lifts Bucs just in time
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Henry lifts Bucs just in time

 March 28, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 776
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — Gavan Henry knew he had to do something.And he did it just in time.
Henry scored from about 20 yards out as the final horn sounded Friday night at Andy Schipul Stadium, giving Kent Island High's boys lacrosse team a heart-stopping 14-13 victory over Stephen Decatur in an instant classic that could be replayed two more times this season.
"I knew we were short on time," Henry said. "I told myself, 'If I get the ball I'm going to do something with it.' I thought he (Decatur goalie Declan Horan) saved it. But thank God it went in."
Down 10-6 at halftime, the Seahawks (2-1) outscored the Bucs, 4-0, in the third quarter, as John Fohner and Luke Pop each scored twice in the period to forge a 10-10 tie heading into the final quarter.
Kent Island (2-0) appeared to take control, when it scored the next three goals. Connor Gardner's goal 1 minute into the fourth broke the game's sixth tie. Brian Rees (four goals) scored with 6:23 left, then converted a feed from his brother Mark to put Kent Island up 13-10 with 5:21 remaining
The Bucs maintained that edge until 1:47 left, when the ball appeared to deflect off the stick of Decatur's Graham Geiser, making it 13-11. Fohner (four goals) pulled the Seahawks within 13-12 with 50.8 seconds remaining.
Decatur won the ensuing face-off and called time. Decatur fired wide, and the Bucs regained possession with 15.6 seconds. But Kent Island lost the ball and Fohner gained possession and snapped a quick shot past Bucs freshman goalie Quinn Burns with 6.8 seconds remaining, creating a 13-13 tie that sent the visitors' bench into delirium.
Kent Island won the ensuing face-off. Henry gained possession and passed to Mark Rees, who sent the ball right back to the senior captain, who unloaded a strike into the net as the final horn blared. Henry took off running toward fence opposite the Kent Island bench, and was immediately chased by a stream of euphoric teammates who mobbed their hero on the field's track.
"To be honest I was trying to get it to one of our attackmen," Henry said. "I did and he ended up trusting me and giving me (the ball) back and I executed.
"Decatur's a helluva team," said Henry, who knows this matchup could be replayed in the Bayside Conference championship and in the Class 2A East Regionals. "That's our rival in this conference and we're going to have to see them at least two more times. It'll be fun, but we love the competition."
Kent Island head coach Bobby Woolley said he's been preaching throughout the Bucs' tough preseason and regular-season opener against Cape Henlopen, the need for his team to play to the final whistle. The Bucs did just that Friday.
"Got a give-and-go out of Mark (Rees)," Woolley said of the winning final play. "Mark trusted Gavan to get the ball back. Typically an attackman is going to take that shot every time. But the fact that we have such faith in our poles is awesome to see that Mark was willing to give it back to Gavan to hit the game-winner."
The game was tied four times in the first quarter, which ended with Decatur holding a 5-4 lead compliments of Ashton March's goal with 12.5 seconds to go in the period.
Kent Island promptly reeled off the next six goals for a 10-5 lead.
Colton Schneck tied the game at 5-all 28 seconds into the second quarter. Back-to-back goals from Keegan Green moved the Bucs in front at 7-5. Marshall Dandy cranked a rocket past Horan to make 8-5 midway through the second period. Goals from Mark Rees and Eric Hofmann extended Kent Island's lead to five with 1:11 to go in the half.
Decatur's Owen Sperry scored with 22.2 seconds left in the half to draw the Seahawks within 10-6 at the break. Decatur reeled off the next four goals, setting up the fourth-quarter drama.
"The thing to be said for this game as a whole is a never-quit attitude," Woolley said. "It was tough at times. Very close basically the whole way. Our guys just continued to fight all the way to the absolute final whistle. That's the testament of a good team.
"We've actually been harping on it," Woolley said of playing to the last whistle. "We can't play on their terms. We can't wait until they make us do something. We have to take control of the game, and I think against good teams you have select options as to when that happens, 'cause they're good."
Notes: Henry finished with two goals. … Pop had a hat trick for Decatur and Parker Mason and Geiser each had two goals.

title: QA's, SSPP poised to extend title runs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
QA's, SSPP poised to extend title runs

 April 1, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1504
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Queen Anne's County High's girls lacrosse team will aim for a fourth straight Bayside Conference championship this spring in a bid to match the Lions' 2011-2014 title spree, and Stephen Decatur's four-year rule between 2006-09."I'm not saying it," head coach Kesley Fitzgerald said, briefly trying to steer around the topic. "The (school) banner's pretty full. But that's the goal."
As is pushing for another regional title and state championship, where Queen Anne's fell to Glenelg in last year's Class 2A state final.
While Fitzgerald works to position the Lions for their title runs, Abby Burke takes over a Saints Peter and Paul program that is bidding for a fifth consecutive Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference championship.
"I've been told that," said Burke, whose team extended its ESIAC winning streak to 28 games with Monday's 13-7 victory over Salisbury School. "No pressure [laughing]. Great."
The Lions and Sabres each lost key pieces from last year's successful campaigns, but return enough talent to again challenge for their respective championships.
Queen Anne's could get a serious challenge from an improved Easton team and county neighbor Kent Island, while a tough early schedule could make North Caroline a tough draw come the postseason.
The conference gains another member this year, as North Dorchester begins its first year of varsity play under head coach Kyle Riggin, the longtime Dorchester Youth Lacrosse coach and 1993 Cambridge-South Dorchester graduate who played crease defense under the late Phil Johnson.
Here's a look at this year's teams:
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Marissa Harding.
Who's Where: Goalie: Jamya Bryan (Jr.); Defense: Sydney Marshall (Jr.); Eileen Thibeault (So.); Madison Jackson (So.); Olivia Shifler (Fr.); Midfield: Katie Wheatley (So.); Gaby Higdon (So.); Madalyn Spicer (Jr.); Attack: Christina Hyde (Sr.); Izzy Trissell (So.); Faith Lyles (So.); Ayren Jones (So.).
Outlook: Harding has been encouraged by what she's seen in the preseason, which included a pair of scrimmage victories.
"We lost eight seniors last year, but the girls have done a really great job of stepping up and trying to fill some of those positions," Harding said. "We have a lot of new girls so just helping each other learn the skills of lacrosse and just working together, and just being really patient with each other has been good to see."
EASTON
Head Coach: Katie Lowman.
Who's Where: Goalie: Zelia Proa (So.); Defense: Anna Quidley (Sr.); Grier Kegan (Jr.); Stella Kabler (Jr.); Hannah Dahlen (So.); Abby Jobeck (So.); Midfield: Samantha Murphy (Sr.); Addie Knox (So.); Lily Tiebosch (Fr.); Taylor Bowen (Fr.); Attack: Myka Motovidlak (Sr.); Dakota Lhotsky (Jr.); Anna Crist (Jr.); Miranda Stup (Jr.).
Outlook: The Warriors could be the Bayside's most improved team. Eleven returning starters and Murphy's transfer in from Sts. Peter & Paul already had Easton within two victories of last year's win total (six) heading Tuesday's clash with Queen Anne's.
"We have a pretty deep bench and that is really helpful," Lowman said. "I think we're playing as a team and not as individuals. We have a lot of talent and experience, and we're young. We only have three seniors. If they play at their very best I think there isn't anything they can't do."
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Kaitlin Paukovits.
Who's Where: Goalie: Ava Mason (Sr.); Bri Legg (Jr.); Defense: Rylie Corn (Sr.); Lilliana Mellinger (Jr.); Madison Jordan (Sr.); Alice Phelan (So.); Rita Yost (Jr.); Midfield: Cara Steele (So.); Hailey Offutt (Fr.); Grace Mathews (Fr.); Attack: Ellie Burnside (Sr.); Willow Yost (Jr.); Parker Tengwall (So.); Gabby Polk (Sr.); Caroline Levin (Sr.).
Outlook: The Bucs scored in double digits in all three of their scrimmages, and have hit double digits in two of their first three regular-season games.
"Definitely have a lot more offensive threats this year than previously, Paukovits said. "Some of our new freshmen have come in and are mixing things up a little bit for us. So it's been awesome."
Through the first three games, Steele, a sophomore, has netted a team-high six goals and six assists, followed by classmate Tengwall (4-6) and freshmen Offutt and Mathews, with five goals and two assists apiece.
"We're always hoping to get to that Bayside championship," Paukovits said. "That's the goal."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: Mandie Shockley.
Who's Where: Goalie: Morgan McHenry (Fr.); Emily Seehafer (Sr.); Defense: Amber Baiers (Jr.); Kylie Ogden (Jr.); Irma Sanchez (Jr.); Mackenzie Cahall (Jr.); Sarah Brown (Sr.); Jordyn Roberts (Sr.); Midfield: Ashlynn Bisesi (So.); Reece Bisesi (Jr.); Maddie McNinch (Jr.); Hadley Sullivan (Fr.); Paisley Garland (Jr.); Attack: Ashley Kercheval (Sr.); Gracie Faulkner (Jr.); Maddie Nicholson (Jr.); Claire Jones (So.); Jamie Robey (Fr.).
Outlook: The Bulldogs graduated five off last year's team, including Riley Walstrum (Ashland University), leading scorer Claire Blue (Lindenwood University) and goalie Ashleigh Lawry (Wilmington University).
But Shockley doesn't see this season as a rebuild.
The Bisesi sisters have stepped up to fill the scoring hole created by Blue's loss. McNinch and Garland continue to progress nicely, and McHenry, who has travel experience, could be a mainstay between the pipes the next four years.
"We have a solid base and the girls are filling in roles," Shockley said.
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Kyle Riggin.
Who's Where: Goalie: Maddie Tobat (Sr.); Defense: Amanda Perez (So.); Jaisia Friend (Sr.); Jackie Gravenor (Jr.); Ashley Baiers (So.); Midfield: Jules Tobat (Sr.); Adi Thomas (So.); Shelby Seese (So.); Attack: Katie Bell (Fr.); Payton Turner (Fr.); Kendall Harrington (So.); Ella Era (Fr.); Attack: Taylor Larimer (So.); Rylee Christopher (So.); Isabella Ramos-Curtis (Fr.); Tyjiah Carter (Jr.).
Outlook: Riggin said the first day a practice he had four players come out who had never touched a lacrosse stick.
"Just a lot of teaching fundamentals and basics," Riggin said of his team, which afte rlosing to defending South Bayside champion Decatur in its first game rebounded with a shutout of Wicomico.
But Riggin emphasized that while wins may be few, this season is about establishing a foundation and positive environment that will leave players wanting to come back.
QUEEN ANNE'S
Head Coach: Kesley Fitzgerald.
Who's Where: Goalie: Emma Dulin (Sr.); Defense: Bea Holthaus (So.); Taylor Brown (So.); Kariana Hickson (So.); Tivi Blue (Jr.); Beau Dulin (So.); Midfield: RJ Ensor (Sr.); Riley Klepper (Sr.); Haley Cole (Jr.); Jordan Bilbo (Jr.); Attack: Kaitlyn Horney (Sr.); Charlotte Schmidt (So.); Kaisa Hickson (Sr.): Mel Gill (Fr.); Elle Wick (Fr.).
Outlook: The Lions lost big pieces from last year's 15-3 team, including Baillie Pinder (Florida Southern), Emily Keppler (Shenandoah) and goalie Maddie George (Delaware).
But expectations haven't dipped in Centreville.
"No matter what we're starting out with, there's always going to be the expectation that we keep the success and the standards that we have each year," said Fitzgerald, whose team has won two of its first three games, the lone loss, a one-goal heartbreaker to defending Delaware state champion Cape Henlopen.
Fitzgerald thinks these Lions have more scoring options than they've had in a long time. What may impress the coach even more is her team's lacrosse IQ.
"We have a very smart offense," Fitzgerald said. "Their on-ball, off-ball awareness is really strong. We've got a great goalie between the pipes, and in between there we've got girls that know what it means to have those high-pressure games. People like RJ and Riley they know how to put the ball in the net and do what needs to be done on the field."
GUNSTON
Head Coach: Brian Aiken.
Who's Where: Goalie: Brinley Leech (Fr.); Emma Serravinals (So.); Defense: Genevieve Baughman (Jr.); Emily Steele (Jr.); Olivia Blusk (So.); Brynn Roberts (So.); Midfield: Grace Shepherd (Sr.); Elena Szwaja (So.); Isabel Gerstmyer (Fr.); Attack: Layla Kent (Jr.); Emma Walker (So.); Kate Zottarelli (So.); Emma Morris (Jr.).
Outlook: The Herons' roster has doubled in size from a year ago. Despite those numbers, and the return of Kent and Shepherd — two of the ESIAC's better all-around athletes — Aiken's focus is on one critical component.
"I have expectations that we're going to be successful as long as we can win the draw," Aiken said. "If we can keep possession I think we'll be OK. Because offensively I think Layla Kent is one of best players in the league. She's a competitor."
SAINTS PETER & PAUL
Head Coach: Abby Burke.
Who's Where: Goalie: Kylie Kroniser (Jr.); Defense: Regan Wolters (Fr.); Annie Albright (Jr.); Ashley Handy (So.); Bridget Gillman (Jr.); Claire Bieber (Sr.); Midfield: Avery McCall (Jr.); Kat Murphy (Sr.); Kendall Kroniser (Sr.); Julia Spero (So.); Caroline Corson (8th); Attack: Mary Callahan (Fr.); Kate Sweeney (So.); Eryn Callahan (Jr.); Sadie Jacobs (Fr.); Emma Hainey (Jr.).
Outlook: Burke takes over for Alison Beyer, who guided the Sabres to one of their most successful stretches in program history, winning four straight ESIAC titles.
The South Atlantic Conference MVP as a midfielder at Wingate University, Burke doesn't see any reason for expectations to sag, and thinks a stiff early season schedule will enhance the Sabres' hopes for extending their title string
"I'm very excited for this year," said Burke, who coached the SSPP's middle school team last year, and has also coached the M&D Shore travel team. "We've added schools they've never played before from the other side of the bridge just to add better competition. And even though we might not have won those games, the girls always fought until the last whistle and never made it easy for a team when they did lose."

title: ESCR offering free introductory lessons
author: Bill Haufe
content:
ESCR offering free introductory lessons

 April 2, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 366
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The Eastern Shore Community Rowers (ESCR) are back on the water with a new season, new shells, and new times.ESCR is an adult (18-over) rowing team based at Evergreen on Port Street, supporting a wide range of skill levels, ages, and experience. The group is committed to sharing its passion and knowledge of rowing to anyone interested in learning.
ESCR has scheduled two free information sessions: April 12 and April 19 from 8:30 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. at Evergreen 770 Port Street. The sessions will be a chance to meet coaches and team members, learn about the 60-foot, eight-person rowing shells to singles, and how rowing is a super fun, sweaty good time.
ESCR will host two full Learn-to-Row clinics, April 28-May 1, from 5:30-7:30 p.m., and Saturday, May 3, from 8:30-10:30 a.m. Clinics will also be offered May 12-15 from 5:30-7:30 p.m., and Saturday, May 17, from 8:30-10:30 a.m. The cost is $400 for these 10-hour sessions.
ESCR is dedicated to teaching our community to row and offer more access area rivers. Scholarships are available to encourage everyone who may be interested. Beginners are encouraged to join the Learn-To-Row clinics, or to take private lessons from one of ESCR's accredited rowing coaches to acquire the skills needed for practices.
"The only criteria," said Board Safety Officer Terry Gleim, "is that you be able to swim and (are) strong enough to properly hold an oar. If swimming is an obstacle, ESCR will assist in helping you learn."
The rowing season runs from April-December with afternoon sessions for novices, 5:30 p.m. workouts Monday, Wednesday and Friday, and 7 p.m. rows on Tuesday and Thursday for more advanced rowers. There will also be a 7:30 a.m. row on Saturdays for all members.
"ESCR is open to anyone over 18 interested in having fun, getting healthy, and appreciating our beautiful waters," said Chloe Tong, the executive director. "The health of our rivers, as well as personal health, is an intrinsic part of our conversation."
As a non-profit, ESCR raises money through private donations, grants, and modest membership dues needed to fund the additional boats and necessary equipment for next year's rowing season.
For more information visit www.ESCRowers.org, or email head coach Chloe Allen: Director@escrowers.org

title: Race for North may draw a crowd
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Race for North may draw a crowd

 April 4, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1688
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The 2022 North Bayside softball regular season ended with Colonel Richardson, North Dorchester, Queen Anne's County and St. Michaels all tied at the top of the division with 6-2 records.Queen Anne's emerged from that gridlock as the eventual champion based on its winning percentage against the three Class 1A teams.
Though the names may change, that scenario could play out again this season.
Colonel Richardson, under first-year head coach Scott Christopher, is off to a 6-0 beginning.
"We're off to a great start, but we know it's a long road, and at the end we want to being playing our best in May," Christopher said.
Easton lost its season opener by one run to Broadneck in nine innings and has since reeled off four straight victories.
"Granted you have Queen Anne's, and you have a couple of other teams making noise," Easton second-year head coach Ryan Brice said. "If we play Easton softball I think we've got a good chance of winning the North."
Two-time defending division champion North Dorchester is 2-2 — both its losses coming by one run — and will again make a push for the top.
"I think we've got every chance in the world to make another run for North Bayside," Eagles head coach Carol Hubbard said.
Cambridge-South Dorchester head coach Sara Alpaugh believes her team could also be 4-0 instead of 2-2 had it not been for baserunning miscues. Queen Anne's head coach Aaron Stewart thinks his young cast can be right in the mix if they adjust to the faster pace of varsity ball.
"If we develop quickly enough we should be the favorite in the North," Stewart said.
And Lee Hutchison at North Caroline thinks his team can also contend once the Bulldogs find their groove at the plate.
Here's a look at this year's teams:
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Sara Alpaugh.
Who's Where: Sophia Diaz (Fr., C); Lainey Jones (Sr., 1B); Laila Insley (Sr., 2B); Enazajah Young (Sr., SS); Lilly Moxey (Fr., 3B/P); Evelyn Windsor (So., LF); Camryn Russum (Sr., CF); Makayla Gibson (Fr., RF); Emma Robinson (Sr., P).
Outlook: Though young in some spots, Alpaugh has liked what she's seen so far for the most part, but noted her team has to improve on the base paths.
"If I want to be completely honest I think we should be 4-0," said Alpaugh, who lost to Colonel by a run and St. Michaels by two. "We've had some baserunning errors that have ended up costing us games. I'm confident about the season. I just think we need to get our wits about us on the bases and listen to coaches."
COLONEL RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Scott Christopher.
Who's Where: Kylie Rhinehardt (Sr., C/1B); Brianna Coleman (Jr., 1B); Hannah Kefauver (Jr., 1B/RF/P); Savannah Messick (Jr., 2B); Aubrey Taylor (Jr., SS); Kayleigh Bradley (So., 3B); Montana Davis (Sr., LF); Sophia ZeppPoon (Fr., CF); Emma Brewer (Jr., 2B); Alaina Hall (Sr., OF); Lila Schiefer (Jr., OF); Chloe Simmons (Fr., P).
Outlook: An assistant since 2018, Christopher succeeds Brett Ireland, who stepped down after last season. The new skipper inherits a team that has only three returners with extensive varsity experience — Rhinehardt, Taylor and Davis — and a freshman pitcher.
"I told them, 'Let's maintain the legacy of Colonel softball,'" said Christopher, a Colonel graduate. "'But let's influx a little different system, and try to see what we can do with the kids who have never really played varsity.'"
So far so good.
Simmons, who is being mentored by former Colonel ace Jen Larrimore, is 5-0, and has shown control and the ability to hit her spots. Kefauver is the second option in the circle, and Christopher has already had to juggle his lineup due to injuries and illness.
"It's a new voice to some of them," said Christopher of stepping into the head coaching role. "But they're buying into the process. We want to get to Bachman Park (host of the state championship)."
EASTON
Head Coach: Ryan Brice.
Who's Where: Lailah Janes (Sr., C); Lyla Roe (Jr., 1B/P); Lane Kennedy (Fr., 2B); Leigha Bosley (Jr., SS); Brynlee Buchkoski (Jr., 3B); Gemma Vogel (Jr., LF); Olivia Orrell (Sr., CF); Leilani Brooks (Sr., RF); Samantha Townsend (Jr., P).
Outlook: The Warriors closed the 2024 regular season by winning 10 of their last 11 and challenging for the North title before falling in the first round of the 2A East regional playoffs
"Last year left a bad taste in our mouth how we lost in the first round of the playoffs," Brice said. "And the girls know we should have won last year but we didn't. So we had all year to think about that loss. Ever since March 1 came around we've just been hungry. We've gotten better every day as a unit and it shows."
Easton is on a four-game win streak, with Roe and Townsend combining to yield just three runs to go with two shutouts.
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Michelle Phillips.
Who's Where: Paige Miller (Sr., C); Laila Johnson (Jr., 1B); Macie Cannon (So., 2B); Michelle Menequin (Jr., SS/3B/OF/P); Kate Cannon (Sr., 1B/3B/OF/P); Aaryona Wesley (So., LF); Talicia Wright (So., CF); Heather Bilbrough (Sr., RF); Ariyana Green (So., 2B/SS/P); Julie Dickerson (Fr., P); Alicia Kennard (Fr., OF/1B); Amiah Moore (Fr., 2B/OF); Madison Raleigh (Sr., IF/OF)
Outlook: With seven underclassmen, Phillips knows this will be a year for development.
"We have very inexperienced kids on the team," Phillips said. "But we ware working. We are definitely working. Most of them are focused and they want to get better."
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Jeremy Black.
Who's Where: Mackenzie Mascetti (Jr., C); Emma Fleshman (Sr., 1B); Hayven Applefeld (Sr., 2B); Abby Mahaffey (Jr., SS/LF); Bri Kurtz (Sr., P/SS); Ashley Stevens (So., 3B); Siena Koch (Jr., LF); Avery Eaton (Sr., CF); Emily Saunders (Jr., RF); Aniyah Thompson (Jr., RF); Clare O'Keefe (So., P).
Outlook: The Bucs are off to a solid start at 4-2, but Black said this team is not the same as his past two editions.
"We're off to a decent start, and the kids are playing well," Black said. "We are different. Some of my big drive-it-over-the-fence bats have graduated, so we are just one base at a time."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: Lee Hutchison.
Who's Where: Raylyn Ross (Jr., C); Hadley Eigenbrode (Sr., 1B); Alyssa Garlick (So., 2B/P); Hatteras Ghrist (Sr., SS); Maddie Porter (Sr., 3B); Jordyn Hunt (Jr., LF); Elizabeth Knott (Sr., CF); Natalie Newman (Jr., RF); Ivylynn Porter (Fr., P); Mackenzie Johnson (Fr., 2B/SS); Brooklynn Spencer (Jr., OF); Emma Hemsley (So., P); Haven Jones (Fr., OF); Kaileigh Spiering (Fr., IF).
Outlook: Hutchison thought his young pitching might struggle early, but it's at the plate where the Bulldogs have struggled.
"We're not hitting as a team," Hutchison said. "We're waiting for our bats to wake up. If you told me we weren't hitting a month ago I wouldn't have believed you because that was one thing we carried forward from last year's team.
"With a freshman and two sophomores pitching, that was where I though my weakness would have been. And it hasn't been," Hutchison added.
Like other teams, Hutchison needs his new additions to get accustomed to varsity play. Most everyone is still 0-0 in the division — the second game between teams counts toward the North standings — so the Bulldogs have the potential to be a problem as the season progresses.
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Carol Hubbard.
Who's Where: Journey Pearson (So., C); Alexus Myers (So., 1B/P); Jewels Vroman (Jr., P/1B); Emily Boyle (Jr., 2B); Payten Henry (Fr., 3B); Kinsley Peters (So., SS); Averi Warfield (Sr., LF); Destini Wongus (Fr., CF); Lola Allen (So., RF); Abigail Sann (So., RF); Paige Taylor (Jr., 1B/3B)
Outlook: The Eagles graduated Emily Cohee, Maggie Hubbard, Mackenzie Lewis and Maddie Nagle, who are all playing in college.
Still, Coach Hubbard thinks this team should again be near the top and the first four games have reinforced that feeling.
One of the Bayside's few left-hander pitchers, Vroman was one hit batter away from a perfect game against St. Michaels. North Dorchester already has two shutouts, and its two losses — both by one run — were due to a combination of baserunning errors, passed balls and wild pitches.
"The two games we lost we just had a lot of little hiccups," Hubbard said.
The Eagles are hitting .355 as a team through four games with a .488 on-base percentage.
"We should be good," Hubbard said. "If we can continue put the ball in play and clean up the little stuff, I think we'll be able to hang with anybody."
QUEEN ANNE'S
Head Coach: Aaron Stewart.
Who's Where: Mikayla Livingston (Sr., C); Kaeden Jordan (Jr., 1B); Alison Milligan (So., 2B); Emily Hirschbock (Jr., SS/P); Shayla Watson (Jr., 3B); Blake Quillen (Jr., LF); Reese Brooks (Jr., CF); Kiera Corcoran (Sr., RF); Hannah Martin (Jr., P)
Outlook: The Lions graduated eight seniors and this year's team hasn't had the opportunity to play at the varsity level.
"Now, they're behind because it's just a faster-paced game at the varsity level," Stewart said.
Still, there have been early positives, especially at the plate.
"We're hitting the ball extremely well," Stewart said. "When we do hit the ball extremely well, the games that we win, we're putting it in the spots they're not. The games we lose we're hitting it right to them."
Next to how fast his team develops, Stewart's other concern is defense, where errors due to inexperience could lengthen innings for pitchers.
"From game 1 to game 4 we have improved," Stewart said. "They're finally getting to understand how much faster the game is. We need to get them to understand that sense of urgency needs to be applied every inning, whether we're hitting or whether we are in the field."
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: Dave Fisher.
Who's Where: Evelyn Mautz (Fr., C); Ayla Gowe (Sr., 1B); Kaelyn Hicks (Fr., 2B); Kayleigh Burkhardt (Fr., SS); Lola Browning (Sr., 3B); Emmah Lewis (Sr., LF); Haven Haddaway (Sr., CF); Gabby Pickens (Sr., RF); Mercy Haddaway (So., P); Sophia Miller (So., Utility); Olivia Schlag (So., Utility/OF).
Outlook: The Saints are young and some of their upperclassmen haven't had the chance to gain experience playing behind others in the past.
"We have bright moments," Fisher said. "And then we have inexperienced moments."
Fisher has been encouraged though.
"They're a great group that wants to learn and work well," Fisher said. "We're definitely having growing pains. But I think we are going to be a different team by the end of the season."
