title: Colonel Richardson, St. Michaels look to extend their combine rule of the North Bayside
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonel Richardson, St. Michaels look to extend their combine rule of the North Bayside

 April 8, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 2264
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The North Bayside title has become a time-share of sorts for the Colonel Richardson and St. Michaels High baseball teams.Since 2008, the Colonels have won the division title nine times, and enter this season as the two-time defending North champion. St. Michaels has earned five North crowns during that 17-year span, including its last in 2022. Excluding 2020 and '21 — when COVID canceled the conference championships, — only North Caroline has managed to pry the division title away from the Colonels and Saints, that coming in 2012.
Colonel and St. Michaels are again among the early division favorites this season. Colonel jumped from gate with a 5-0 start before losses last week to St. Michaels and North Caroline, and Tuesday against Kent Island. St. Michaels split its first two games, but has since gone on a five-game win streak that has pushed its record to 6-1.
"I think we've played really good baseball off the start," Colonel Richardson second-year head coach Garrett Nepert said. "We gave up too many free bases (against St. Michaels and Caroline) and it came back to haunt us. Nothing we can't fix. Little things I'm confident we're going to fix. The goal is to be in the mix at the end of it."
The perennial Class 1A powers will again have to fend off challenges this season, the strongest of which appear to be coming from the North's four 2A schools — Easton, Kent Island, North Caroline and Queen Anne's.
"I think Easton is a really talented team," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said. "They've got a lot of pitching. They have some guys that can really swing it. I said coming in, I thought them and Queen Anne's would be the two teams that are coming in with the most talent."
Kent Island and North Caroline can't be counted out. The Bucs saddled Easton with one of its two losses, while two of North Caroline's wins have come against defending conference champion Stephen Decatur and county rival Colonel.
"I think we'll be in a lot more games," Bulldogs second-year head coach Vince Manetti said. "And I'm hoping that we can start to change the narrative of North Caroline."
North Dorchester, which begins its first season under head coach Billy Jackson, has the talent to have a hand in shaping the division, while Kent County — which beat Easton 6-5 Tuesday for its first win of the season — and Cambridge-South Dorchester could knock off one of the big dogs on a given day.
With poor weather conditions creating four-game weeks for several teams, pitching — specifically, who has deep rotations — figures to be one of the more critical factors in terms of who wins the division.
"It will make for an interesting season," Cambridge-SD head coach Mike Tremper said of how pitching staffs hold up in four-game weeks.
Saints Peter and Paul also welcomes a new head coach, though Gary Gould is not exactly new to the school, having led the Sabres to back-to-back Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference championships in basketball.
Here's a look at this year's teams:
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Mike Tremper.
Who's Where: Noah Marshall (Sr., C); Nate Huber (Sr., 1B/RHP); Justin Marshall (Jr., 2B/RHP); Nate Twilley (Fr., SS/LHP); Landon Ludolph (Sr., 3B/RHP); Wyatt Harrington (Fr., LF/RHP); Collin Bair (Jr., CF); Luke Jacobson (Sr., RF); Jacob Mitchell (Sr., RHP); Tanner Coulbourne (Jr., RHP).
Outlook: The Vikings may be one of the division's younger teams, but trying to build momentum has been difficult with cancellations and poor field conditions.
Still, Tremper has been encouraged.
"Shaping up pretty good," Tremper said. "We're a younger team but we're looking good as a team overall. We're meshing well together and playing well together."
Coulbourne figures to get the most innings, but Tremper knows the rest of the staff will have to develop for the Vikings to compete.
COLONEL RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Garrett Nepert.
Who's Where: Jamie Mensonides (So., C/3B/RHP); Caleb Rouser (So., C/3B); Cam Todd (Sr., 1B/RF); Trent Breeding (Jr., 1B/2B/RHP); Jack Walls (Jr., 1B/LHP/CF); Jordan Regulski (Sr., RHP/1B/SS); John Beaven (So., 2B/SS/RHP); Derrick Mitchell (Jr., LF); TJ Wegner (Sr., CF/RF); Preston Rickwood (Sr., DH).
Outlook: The 2024 North Bayside Player of the Year and Wake Forest University commit, Regulski figures to again be one of the conference's premier talents. Walls, a fellow first-team all-North pick from a year ago, is one of the area's top center fielders, and together with Regulski, gives Colonel a nice one-two punch on the mound.
With 2024 Pitcher of the Year Daniel Hesson now at Salisbury, the Colonels will may go with a pitching-by-committee approach when Regulski and Walls aren't starting on the hill.
"We've had a couple staff games already," Nepert said. "Obviously North Caroline didn't turn out like we wanted, but they gave us a chance to win. We didn't get the big hit when we needed it. As long as they give us a chance to win I think we'll be in a pretty good spot. It's definitely going to be a team effort on the mound. I'm excited to see where we take off from here."
EASTON
Head Coach: Albert Pritchett.
Who's Where: Colin Mooney (Sr., C); Michael O'Connor (Sr., 1B); Carter Mooney (Jr., 2B); Dustin Blue (Jr., SS/RHP); Garrett Fink (Sr., 3B/RHP); Chase Raab (Sr., LF); Kayden Webb (Sr., CF/RHP); Dylan Cassell (Sr., RF); Cooper Barletta (So., C/3B); Paxton Echternach (Jr., 3B/RHP); Alex Rhodes (Sr., IF/RHP); Jesus Crespo (Sr., CF/DH); James Shaw (Jr., OF); Alex Frankos (Sr., C/1B); Jackson Diefenderfer (Jr., RHP)
Outlook: Pritchett sidesteps predictions, but if the Warriors, who have scored in double figures in four of seven games — continue hitting as they have they should be tough.
"We've worked a lot on the two-strike approach," Pritchett said. "Being aggressive early in the count; finding your pitch early and defending the strike zone late. When we're aggressive at the plate early it makes a big difference. Don't just see pitches for the sake of it. But when you get two strikes, we're doing a good job of defending the strike zone."
Blue and Webb, both first-team all-North picks a year ago, and Fink could give Easton one of the division's stronger rotations.
"We're throwing first-pitch strikes and our defense has been pretty good behind them," Pritchett said. "It's a combination of throwing strikes and defending the ball.
"We've got some things to work on but it's a good group of kids," Pritchett added. "They've played together since Little League, they enjoy each others company. It's very positive."
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Jason Conner.
Who's Where: Scottie Ford (Jr., C); Noah Iacona (Jr., 1B/3B/RHP); Braden Wilson (Jr., 1B/3B/LF/RHP); Owen Sutton (Fr., 2B); Nate Sutton (So., 2B); Jace Conner (Sr., SS/RHP); Tanner Beck (Sr., SS/RHP); Hunter Hawn (Fr., 3B/CF); Zavion Wilson (Jr., OF); Aidan Crouch (Jr., RF/LHP); Gavin Miller (Jr., RF); Shakur Wilson (Sr., OF); Caiden Pritchett (So., OF); David Shaw (So., C/OF); Noah Taylor (Sr., 1B); Reid Fry (Fr., 1B); Joey Homyack (Fr., C); Drew Haas (Fr., IF)
Outlook: If the defense plays well, Jace Conner — an all-North second-team pick a year ago — could give opponents problems. Coach Conner will also use Beck, Iacona and Crouch on the mound, but knows they too will need the defense to play well behind them.
"We are very young and inexperienced," Jason Conner said. "We've got to hit. We've got to minimize the errors."
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Brendan Schulte.
Who's Where: Derek Grossi (So., C/RHP); Brady Hart (Sr., 1B); Kevin Coe (So., 2B); Jack Grossi (Jr., SS/RHP); Aiden Bonds (Sr., 3B); Gavin Schulte (Sr., OF); Traise Woolford (Jr., OF); Logan Baierlein (Jr., OF/RHP); Henry Greenway (OF); Myles Harmon (So., Util.); Matthew Fisher (So., 1B/2B); Wyatt Offutt (Sr., RHP); Caleb Hess (Fr., RHP); Hayden Austin (Jr., RHP); Paul Horner (Sr., RHP)
Outlook: Offutt, who is bound for Wilmington University, earned the win against Easton and figures to be one of the North's top pitchers. The Bucs appear to have a deep rotation, which could be a difference maker during weeks of four games.
Third baseman Bonds, who is headed to Cairn (Pa.) University, is part of a lineup that gives the Bucs a chance in every game.
NORTH CAROLINE

Outlook: The Bulldogs have won three of their first seven games, but two of those wins have been over Decatur and Colonel.
"We definitely took some lumps last year," Manetti said. "We were really young, but we made a lot of progress compared to the year before. Confidence-wise I think we're feeling pretty good. And I think this year they're kind of starting to see if they play mistake-free, clean baseball, we might not win every game, but we can compete with anybody."

Head Coach: Billy Jackson.

Outlook: Jackson has been with the program for 14 years — the last two as varsity assistant to former head coach Dave Morrissette — and takes over a team that returns first-team all-North catcher Leonard and second-team picks Fraccaroli and Swann.
The Eagles totaled 42 runs in their first two games, but couldn't produce timely hits while losing their next three games.
"We're deep in our batting lineup," Jackson said. "But we left a lot of runners on base. Just not hitting in crucial situations. The fielding's been good. The hitting's been good at times, but just not at the crucial times."
North Dorchester appears to have plenty of arms, though Jackson said he's still trying to figure out his rotation.

Head Coach: Rick Sutch.

"Our relief core has been struggling a little bit because we haven't been on the mound," said Rick Sutch, who after two years as a varsity assistant takes over for Chris Fitzgerald. "We've only played a handful of games and my starters have been going five, six, seven innings. So (relief pitchers) haven't gotten many opportunities. We've been in every game."
Despite those losses, the new skipper likes the way his rotation sets up for the rest of this week — if they don't get rained out on Friday and Saturday.
"All my pitching's aligned," Sutch said. "If we can keep it to where it is now, I think we fall into a good position to make a run here. If we can actually play the games on the days they're scheduled I think we're in pretty good shape. But I think everybody's in the same boat."

Aside from his team's hitting, pitching and fielding during its 5-1 start, what's really impressed Femi this early season has been the Saints ability to handle pressure.
"A lot of them are young so you don't know what to expect; how they'll play in a pressure game," Femi said. "I was real surprised by the Colonel game (which was tied 4-4 before the Saints scored five in the eighth). It just didn't seem to faze them. Before the game I had a coach come up to me and say, 'This is a different group of kids. They just don't care (about the pressure).'
"Adversity doesn't seem to bother them either.," Femi added. "Like in the Snow Hill game, we were kicking the ball around, but they didn't carry it with them. Like a lot of teams I've had, they'll carry that with them to bat, or if they strike out they'll carry it with them in the field. These guys don't seem to do that."

Gould, the program's third different head coach in three years, will focus on building this season.
"Not sure what the win-loss record will be, but I think we will be able to compete and show more improvement," Gould said. We're young so expectations aren't too high. We just want to compete, get better, and develop the program.

title: Bucs halt Saints' win streak at six
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bucs halt Saints' win streak at six

 April 10, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 758
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Kent Island High's Traise Woolford hasn't pitched the season because of elbow issues.He looked pretty healed Thursday in his debut on the mound.
Woolford got an inning-ending strikeout to escape a bases-loaded jam in the sixth, then notched a strikeout with the potential tying and winning runs on base in the seventh, helping the Buccaneers secure a 5-4 victory over St. Michaels on a gray and chilly afternoon at Harold Baines Field.
"He came in and did his job," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said of Woolford, who helped end the Saints' six-game win streak. "I know he'd had some arm problems. Certainly wouldn't know it. He came in cold. That was a big situation. I mean kudos to him. Came in, got the outs when he needed them."
Kent Island (4-5 overall, 2-0 North Bayside) carried a 5-2 lead into the bottom of the sixth. Starting right-hander Wyatt Offutt got Pearson Greenwood to line out to second to start the inning before Brennen Dean reached on a bad-hop single. Offutt got a called third strike on Nathan Spurry for the second out, but hit Lucas Greenwood with a pitch and walked Blake Wheatley, loading the bases.
Offutt walked Brock Grow, plating pinch-runner Eli Wallace, cutting the Bucs' lead to 5-3. Woolford came on to relieve Offutt.
"He was ready to go," said Kent Island assistant Scott Grossi of Woolford. "It's not like we just put him in there for the heck of it. He was ready to go, and this was the time to put him in. He's a senior. We felt he would be able to handle the situation."
Woolford did just that.
The senior left-hander walked Ethan Royer to plate Lucas Greenwood, making it a one-run game, but then struck out Will Sherwood to end the rally.
St. Michaels (7-2, 1-1) wasn't quite finished.
Connor Wheeler walked on a 3-2 pitch to lead off the seventh, and was advanced to second on Pearson Greenwood's sacrifice bunt. Woolford got a called third strike on Eli Wallace for the second out. St. Michaels got the potential winning run on first when Spurry was hit by a pitch. But Woolford ended the threat there, getting a check-swing third strike on Lucas Greenwood to finish the game.
"Wasn't really nervous until the last two pitches," said Woolford, who got the save. "Just trying to throw strikes."
As was Offutt, who allowed four runs, four hits, five walks, and struck out four over 5 2/3 innings until running into trouble in the sixth.
"I thought he was one of the better pitchers we've faced this year," Femi said of Offutt, who earned the win. "He changed speeds early, had a lot of life on his fastball. I thought he threw a great game."
St. Michaels took a 2-0 lead in the third, as Grow and Wheeler each doubled and scored on low, outside deliveries that got away from the catcher.
But the Saints couldn't push anything else across until the sixth.
"Wyatt's been doing well all year," Grossi said. "He was throwing strikes with his fastball, with his slider, off-speed stuff. And the defense was making the plays for him. And that's the big thing for us. Throw strikes, make the plays on defense, and timely hitting. That's all it takes. Sounds easy, but it's not easy."
Grow held the Bucs to no runs and three hits through four innings before the Bucs broke through for five runs in the fifth with two outs.
The Saints right-hander walked Aiden Bonds then hit Matt Fisher with a pitch. Myles Harmon fouled off a bunt attempt on a 3-2 pitch for the first out. Grow fanned Kevin Coe but walked Jack Grossi, loading the bases. Offutt followed with a two-run single to the right-center field gap. Woolford reached on an infield single that plated Jack Grossi with the go-ahead run. Brady Hart singled sharply to right, scoring Offutt for a 4-2 lead. Derek Grossi then belted double to the right-field fence, bringing in Woolford for a 5-2 lead.
"We didn't get the hit with men on base," Femi said. "They got their hits with men in scoring position, we didn't. That was pretty much the game."
It was Kent Island's second straight win.
"They've been battling all year," said Scott Grossi, who was filling in for head coach Brendan Schulte. "Some things didn't go our way either on offense or defense, but they've continued to battle. And today we were able to string together a couple hits in that one inning to get a bunch of runs. And Wyatt Offutt and Traise Woolford pitched a heckuva game."

title: Sherwood, Saints quiet Warrior bats
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sherwood, Saints quiet Warrior bats

 April 15, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 890
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Will Sherwood admitted there were times during previous seasons when not getting a strike call may have bothered him, potentially throwing him off his game.Those times have yet to surface this season.
"This year I realized if it doesn't go my way, next pitch," St. Michaels High's senior right-hander said. "You can't sit there on the mound and complain about it. Just get the next pitch.
"Even with hitting," Sherwood added. "If it doesn't drop (in), no need to take it in the field and make it a bigger problem than it really is."
Sherwood had few problems Monday afternoon, as he pitched 6 2/3 innings of two-hit ball while holding Easton to its lowest run total of the season during a 7-1 victory at Warrior Field.
"He's done it all year," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said of Sherwood, who raised his record to 4-0. "It's not surprising. What he does the best is he'll fall behind (in the count), but then he fights back; doesn't seem to get rattled."
The Warriors (6-4 overall, 1-2 North Bayside) had multiple opportunities to rattle the tall right-hander. Sherwood hit a pair of batters in the first inning, but stranded both with an inning-ending strikeout. Dylan Cassell got Easton's first hit in the third, lacing a sharp single to left. Dustin Blue walked before Sherwood fanned Chase Raab to end the inning.
"We didn't hit," Easton head coach Albert Pritchett said. "You've got to give credit to their pitcher, who threw strikes, challenged us, kept us off balance. We've been hitting the ball. I think we just ran up against a pitcher that had our number."
Trailing 4-0, the Warriors pieced together their biggest threat in the fifth. Kayden Webb hit a clean, one-out single to right field, stole second, and advanced to third on a high throw. Mikey O'Connor walked and stole second before Cassell was intentionally walked, loading the bases. Blue hit a sacrifice fly to center, plating Webb, but Sherwood ended the threat there, inducing an inning-ending flyout to left field.
"He throws a fastball, slider and a change-up," Femi said of Sherwood, who finished with six strikeouts, four walks — one intentional — and three hit batsman. "I just think it (slider) moves enough it misses their barrel.
"And he's really matured, not only physically but I think mentally," Femi continued. "He doesn't seem to get rattled because there were a couple calls that could have gone either way. He just got the ball back and off he goes to the next pitch."
Sherwood, who retired the last seven batters he faced, was relieved with two outs in the seventh after reaching his 105-pitch count. Nathan Spurry completed the two-hitter, getting O'Connor to bounce into an unassisted groundout to first.
"We played really good defense behind him," Femi said. "There was a bad hop on one of the balls, but other than that I would say we played error-free baseball. And anytime you do that, and you get a pitching performance like that, you're going to be hard to beat."
St. Michaels (8-2, 2-1) took a 1-0 lead in the first against Easton starter Garrett Fink (1-1). Sherwood hit a leadoff single and Connor Wheeler singled. Pearson Greenwood's sacrifice bunt advanced the runners. Fink struck out Brennen Dean for the second out, before Brock Grow reached on an error, allowing Sherwood to score the game's first run. Fink escaped any further damage, fanning Jack Brennan to end the inning.
The Saints pushed two more runs across in the second. Ethan Royer stroked a one-out single to center and stole second. Sherwood walked and Wheeler was hit by a pitch, loading the bases. Royer scored on a wild pitch before Greenwood was walked, filling the bags. Dean's sacrifice fly to center plated Sherwood to make it 3-0. Grow bounced into a force to end the frame.
Blue relieved Fink to start the third. The junior worked out of two-on, one-out jam in the inning, but in the fourth issued a leadoff walk to Wheeler, who stole second and scored on Greenwood's base hit to left, making it 4-0.
St. Michaels had a chance to extend its lead in the fifth, when Wheeler launched a potential extra-base hit to right that Cassell made an outstanding running grab on for the final out.
Back-to-back, bases-loaded walks stretched the Saints' lead to 6-1 with two outs in the sixth. Paxton Echternach relieved Blue. After hitting Sherwood with a pitch — scoring Jack Brennan for a 7-1 lead — Wheeler hammered yet another deep drive to right, only to have Cassell rob him a second time with a another brilliant catch on the run to end the rally.
"The two catches he made are as good as any I've ever seen in high school baseball," said Femi of Cassell's two sparkling plays. "I mean they were unbelievable. One he made an adjustment on as he went to it. Otherwise that game is over. He kept them in the ball game."
St. Michaels loaded the bases again in the seventh before Echternach got Blake Wheatley on a pop out to short to end the inning.
"We struggled with the strike zone," said Pritchett, whose pitchers combined to walk 13 and hit four batters. "We walked too many people. We had a few errors. We didn't hit. It's hard to win when you do that. They played better than us."

title: Townsend, Orrell lead Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Townsend, Orrell lead Warriors

 April 16, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 679
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — They weren't together when they spoke, but all three struck a similar theme."We needed this win going into next week," Easton High head softball coach Ryan Brice said Wednesday after the Warrriors churned out 16 hits en route to an 18-0 feel-good victory in five innings over Wicomico.
"We needed it big time," said Olivia Orrell, who celebrated senior day by launching a two-run homer to center field that gave Easton a 3-0 first-inning lead.
"I think the whole team needed it," chimed junior pitcher Sammy Townsend, who registered a season-high 15 strikeouts while spinning a three-hitter.
One day after getting blanked for the first time this year by two-time defending North Bayside champion North Dorchester, Easton (7-4) faced a Wicomico team that has yet to win this season. Sure, the Warriors were a heavy favorite, and took care of business early on the way to just their second win in five games.
But with key dates looming with Kent Island and Cambridge-South Dorchester next week, Easton not only got a desired result against the Indians (0-9) but a much-needed boost of confidence.
"We needed all the hits today because the past couple games we haven't really been hitting," said Orrell, who finished 3 or 4 with three RBIs, four runs scored and her second homer of the season. "So I think that boosted our confidence level. And it definitely boosted the team morale."
Brice agreed, especially after last week's losses to Stephen Decatur and Colonel Richardson, and Tuesday's setback at North Dorchester.
"Dropping the couple games last week really affected us," Brice said. "So we really needed this one today so we can get some traction going into the meat of the season. We have Kent Island coming up. We have Cambridge coming up. Those are good ball clubs so we got to be on our toes."
Townsend (3-3) seemed to be on her game from the beginning, fanning the first two batters she faced before plunking Amber Moore, and then striking out Aleah Shah to end the first.
"I feel my curve was really tight today, and I feel my riser was good as well," said Townsend, who notched all 15 outs via strikeout. "I feel like I had a natural rise going on today and I got a lot of hitters out with that. I was focused. I feel like this is what we needed."
Joseline Gabriel singled through the left side of the infield with one out in the second inning for Wi-Hi's first hit. But Townsend fanned the next two batters to end the frame, then struck out the side swinging in the third.
The Indians had their best chance to spoil Townsend's shutout bid in the fourth. Shah hit a one-out single to right and advanced to second on an error. Townsend struck out Kennedi Hull. Gabriel then reached on an error, sending Shah to third. But the Indians' lone baserunner to reach third would remain there, as Townsend got an inning-ending strikeout.
"I can't say enough about Sammy," Brice said. "There was freshman sensation, then sophomore sensation. Now, she's a junior sensation. She needed this win as well. She had a couple of rough outings the past couple of games, but she needed the win."
Wicomico put two runners on in the fifth with two outs, but Townsend punctuated Easton's third shutout of the year with her 15th K.
After scoring three runs on four hits in the first, Easton batted around in the second, pushing six more runs across with five hits. Gemma Vogel (2 for 3) opened the inning with a double, stole third and scored on an error. Lyla Roe (2 for 3, RBI), Orrell, and Townsend (3 for 4) each stroked singles in the rally, and Lane Kennedy (2 for 4, 2 RBIs) doubled.
Easton widened its lead to 12-0 in the third before scoring six more in the fourth.
"We did what we were supposed to do today," Brice said. "I can't complain. We hit the ball very well today. We haven't in the past couple of games. So today hopefully going into next week we keep the bats rolling."

title: Ovechkin begins second Cup chase
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Ovechkin begins second Cup chase

 April 18, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 910
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Alex Ovechkin has a new chase to focus on in trading his pursuit of Wayne Gretzky's NHL goals record for a second Stanley Cup title as he and the Eastern Conference's top-seeded Washington Capitals prepare to open the playoffs against Montreal.The defending champion Panthers and Tampa Bay Lightning are set for their latest all-Florida faceoff. Toronto and Ottawa are rekindling their provincial playoff rivalry. And then there's the matter of the Carolina Hurricanes seeking to overcome their string of playoff shortfalls, with the New Jersey Devils first up.
All that was missing in the East — aside from a New York team for just the second time since the league's expansion era began in 1967 — was Washington awaiting an opponent, with the Canadiens out-racing the Columbus Blue Jackets to clinch their spot as the eighth seed on Wednesday.
Of more concern in D.C., perhaps, is the Capitals regaining their groove after limping down the stretch with a skid of losses.
"We obviously can score goals but we need to be sharper in our D-zone," defenseman Martin Fehervary said of the Capitals, who are 4-6-1 in their past 11, including a 7-0 loss at Columbus. "Those details are really important and need to be sharper."
TEAMS TO BEATNo matter who they faced, the Capitals are favored following their sixth season with 50 or more wins while no longer having to deal with the hype involving Ovechkin.
"Him getting the goals record is incredible to say the least," goalie Charlie Lindgren said. "What we do in the playoffs is what matters. That's the most important thing."
Auston Matthews and the Maple Leafs are surging into the postseason, appearing ready and eager to put behind their decadelong past of early playoff exits. Toronto won eight of nine and outscored its opponents by a combined 28-12 in clinching its first Atlantic Division title.
"Obviously, we can't change what's happened in the past. I think you wear that," Matthews said of a team that's advanced beyond the first round just once in its past nine playoff appearances.
"I feel really confident in this group," he added. "Earning our division here is a big step for us. But we just want to push forward."
Bolstering the Leafs' confidence is adopting a more responsible defensive style under first-year coach Craig Berube, who led St. Louis to the Cup in 2019. There's also the emergence of journeyman goalie Anthony Stolarz, who is 12-3-1, including eight wins in a row with three shutouts, since missing a 24-game stretch with a knee injury.
In avoiding the division's usually tough 2-3 matchup, the Leafs rekindle their Battle of Ontario playoff rivalry with Ottawa.
In Carolina, the Hurricanes have the talent but not the consistent playoff results. Qualifying for the postseason in each of coach Rob Brind'Amour's seven years, Carolina has lost the East finals twice and been bounced in the second round three times, including last year.
"We always have confidence — it's been a tough couple of bounces the last few years," forward Seth Jarvis said. "Especially in the playoffs when it gets tighter, you can't be giving other teams a lot of chances and it's tough to score, so I think that bodes well for us."
EVEN UPNot much separates the Lightning and Panthers, who have combined to win three of the past five Cups. The teams are meeting in the playoffs for the fourth time in five years, with Tampa Bay winning the first two and Florida last year.
"Certainly the eyes in Florida and the fans in both cities will be wired into it, so it's great for hockey," Panthers coach Paul Maurice said.
The good news in Florida is the possibility of Matthew Tkachuk's return after being sidelined by a lower-body injury during 4 Nations Face-Off in February. Defenseman Aaron Ekblad is due to return in Game 3 after serving a 20-game suspension for violating the league's performance-enhancing drugs policy
The Lightning are making their 11th playoff appearance in 12 years under coach Jon Cooper but first over that span without captain Steven Stamkos, following his departure in free agency last year.
"For sure he's missed and never forgotten," Cooper said of Stamkos. "But he's not with us now, so we've found a way to move on without him. But there was definitely some growing pains."
UNDERDOGSOttawa qualified for the playoffs for the first time since 2017 under first-year coach Travis Green, who is very familiar with the Battle of Ontario history. He played for the Leafs in 2001-02, when Toronto rallied to eliminate Ottawa in a seven-game second-round series.
"Exciting is downplaying it a little bit," Green said. "Really everything you want in a playoffs series, and players are going to love it. Fans are going to love it."
The Devils also feature a new coach in Sheldon Keefe, making just their third playoff appearance since losing the Stanley Cup Final to Los Angeles in 2012. New Jersey will be without star center Jack Hughes (shoulder surgery) but welcomed back defenseman Dougie Hamilton, who returned Wednesday after getting knocked out of the lineup by a lower-body injury in early March.
The Canadiens, meantime, are ahead of GM Kent Hughes' rebuilding timetable and feature a young but relatively untested playoff core from the team that lost to Tampa Bay in the 2021 Stanley Cup Final.
PREDICTIONSFirst round: Washington beats Montreal in six; Toronto beats Ottawa in five; Florida beats Tampa Bay in seven; Carolina beats New Jersey in six.
Second round: Carolina beats Washington in six; Toronto beats Florida in seven.
Conference final: Toronto beats Carolina in seven.

title: Rising Sun woman runs Boston Marathon, honoring her terminally ill father
author: Carl Hamilton cahamilton@chespub.com
content:
Rising Sun woman runs Boston Marathon, honoring her terminally ill father

 April 25, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Carl Hamilton cahamilton@chespub.com | Section: News 
 
 1220
 Words 

 Read News Document

 BOSTON, Mass. — It was a picture-perfect finish for Emma Cease, the 23-year-old Rising Sun woman who ran the Boston Marathon on Monday to honor her terminally-ill father, David Cease.Emma completed the storied 26.2-mile course in three hours and 40 minutes. And her 53-year-old dad, who has been diagnosed with terminal esophageal cancer, was among the family members who saw Emma cross the finish line.
"There is a picture of me, looking up at my family. My dad is cheering and I am absolutely beaming, such a big smile on my face. I was so happy," Emma reflected Wednesday. "It was perfect."
A 2019 Rising Sun High School graduate, Emma ran that long-distance race as a member of the Boston Marathon Cam Neely Cancer Foundation team, which falls under one of three classifications of the 30,000 runners that participated.
The organization made arrangements for Emma's dad; her mom, Lori; her 20-year-old sister, Sophia; her aunt, Melissa Bianco; and her boyfriend, Brenan; to be seated along the home-stretch, a short distance from the finish line.
"They had the best seats in the house. While I was running, I kept thinking about how I was going to see them as I was heading toward the finish line. That gave me motivation to keep going," said Emma, noting that she felt pain in her legs and experienced fatigue during the last six miles of the marathon.
She did a pre-race interview on behalf of the Cam Neely Cancer Foundation. "They are such kind and incredible people," Emma marveled.
Emma raised approximately $13,700 for cancer research, surpassing the requisite $12,000 by the late-March deadline, and that made her eligible to run the famous marathon as a member of the Cam Neely Cancer Foundation team.
The charity provides resources and support to cancer patients and their families, helping them navigate the emotional, financial, and physical challenges of treatment while fostering a sense of community and hope during difficult times.
She dedicated her Boston Marathon run to her dad who, like her mom, showed and continues to show support of Emma in all aspects of her life.
When it comes to Emma's sports-related endeavors, however, her dad is her super-fan.
When she was a girl, her dad taught Emma how to hit whiffle balls and how to throw a spiraled football pass in their backyard. They played street hockey together in their driveway, using a cardboard box as the goal.
Emma transitioned from backyard games to a travel soccer team when she entered the third-grade. And for the next seven years, she competed in organized soccer leagues, encouraged by the cheering of her biggest fan.
"He rarely missed a practice or game, his presence on the sideline being a given, regardless of how far the drive," Emma said of her dad.
Emma ran track during her freshman year at RSHS, turning to that spring sport as a way to stay in shape for the high school's girls soccer team, which competes in the fall.
She fell in love with cross-country running and elected to stop playing soccer to focus solely on it. As Emma remembers, "My dad embraced my newfound passion, rearranging his work schedule to be at every meet in time for the starting gun to go off."
Emma's passion for long-distance running continued to grow during her three years at Washington College, from which she graduated in May 2022 with a Bachelor of Science degree in environmental science. She now works for Washington College in Chestertown as an Experiential Learning Program manager.
She and her dad also have bonded over the years by watching televised broadcasts of NCAA cross country championships, the Olympics and other major running races. Calling it her "personal favorite," the Boston Marathon is on that list.
It had been Emma's dream to run the Boston Marathon "one day far in the future," according to her. When her dad was diagnosed with terminal cancer in late 2023, however, Emma expedited her plans to make that dream a reality.
"I've talked about this dream with my dad countless times, never imagining the possibility that he wouldn't be there to cheer me on. That was until his diagnosis flipped our world upside down," she explained during a Cecil Whig interview in January.
Applying to run for the Cam Neely Foundation's 2025 Boston Marathon team was a "no-brainer," she said in that interview.
"The truth is that tomorrow isn't guaranteed. If there's anything that my family has learned over the past year's rollercoaster ride of emotions, medical bills, and my dad's ongoing treatment, it's that every moment counts. I decided that I wanted to do something to show my dad how much I love him, thank him for his unwavering support of me, and give him something to look forward to when reality feels so heavy," Emma outlined.
She then commented, "The Boston Marathon is the biggest marathon in the world. I am running the Boston Marathon in honor of my father, and I want him to see me cross that finish line."
Emma, her mom, her aunt and her boyfriend made the seven-hour drive to Boston on Friday and attended the marathon expo on Saturday, when she picked up her official numbered bib for the race. (Emma had never been to Boston, but was able to see only a few attractions because of the tight schedule. She plans to return.)
Her father and her sister arrived at Boston on Easter Sunday, which was a "low-key day" for the family before the marathon. Emma's dad is still doing pretty well, but he isn't able to walk long distances — so they allowed plenty of buffer time when making their way to the marathon route on Monday.
Having run many miles daily for the past several months while training, Emma knew she could finish the marathon. Plus, she already had run two marathons, each in under four hours. But those marathons were on earthen trails, which are much easier on a runner's feet and legs.
"This was my first time on concrete," Emma said of Monday's 26.2-mile race.
In addition to a city-setting, concrete course, the Boston Marathon is marked by what most consider to be a dauntingly hilly terrain. "Getting up the hills was easier than I thought it would be. The hills aren't that high and I thought they were overhyped," Emma said.
But then Emma acknowledged that, while the hills aren't as high as she expected, they are quite plentiful and — cumulatively — they take their toll on marathon runners.
"I was cruising until Mile 20. You're finishing up the hilly section. I could go up the hills, but it was harder for me going down the hills because it made my legs hurt even worse. I never experienced doubt that I would finish the marathon, even when it was really painful in my legs, but I knew I had to dig deep," Emma explained.
And dig deep she did, buoyed by the cheers of spectators along the marathon route.
"The crowd was amazing," Emma said.
And for Emma, considering the reason for her running the Boston Marathon in the first place, no one in that crowd was more amazing than her cheering dad.
"It means absolutely everything to me," Emma said, summing up how she feels about her dad witnessing her Boston Marathon accomplishment. "My dad means the absolute world to me. I owe so much of who I am today to the love and unwavering support he's always shown me."

title: Sabres extend ESIAC streak to 32
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres extend ESIAC streak to 32

 April 29, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 691
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — She wasn't looking for anyone in particular.In fact, Kate Sweeney wasn't looking for anyone at all.
"If I see one glimpse of their stick, I make sure I keep that in mind," said Sweeney, who plays attack for Saints Peter and Paul High's girls lacrosse team. "And if they continue to go (forward), which hopefully they do, they've got a pretty easy goal."
The Sabres collected a season-high for goals Monday afternoon, as Sweeney doled out a season-high 11 assists and scored twice, leading Sts. Peter & Paul to a 21-2 victory over Gunston for its 32nd consecutive victory over an Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference opponent.
"She is probably our least selfish player," Sabres' first-year head coach Abby Burke said of Sweeney. "Every single game she has the most assists. She's always looking in the middle; is always looking for that next option. She is a team player through and through. We have more assisted goals than we have goals off a drive, and it's partly because of her."
Sweeney spent the better part of her time on the field at the post, patiently waiting for a cutting teammate to step into open space in front of the goal before delivering on-the mark passes that more often than not resulted in goals.
Gunston (5-6 overall, 2-4 ESIAC) actually took a 1-0 lead a little over a minute into the game on Kate Zottarelli's goal. Just over a minute later, junior Avery McCall (game-high five goals) scored unassisted, starting the Sabres (6-5, 5-0) on a nine-goal spree.
Sweeney dished the first of her two assists less than a minute apart, first setting up Kendall Kroniser (four goals) then McCall for a 3-1 Sts. Peter & Paul lead. But with 4:51 remaining in the first quarter, Burke called time to let the Sabres know what she thought of their play.
"The coaching staff was not happy with how the girls were performing," said Burke, whose team had not played since a 14-1 win over Worcester Prep on April 15. "We had a couple practices before this and there was no reason why their sticks should have looked this rusty. We called team into a timeout and we said, 'Look, everyone needs to get their act together. We are better than this.'"
Burke and company also weren't pleased with their team's defense.
"We weren't communicating, which doesn't help a defensive unit," Burke said. "When we weren't communicating, girls didn't know when to slide. Girls weren't sliding properly. Not having that first or second slide was our big issue in the first quarter."
Sts. Peter & Paul responded, with goalie Kylie Kroniser (seven saves) and the defense holding the Herons — who were without standout Layla Kent (season-ending injury) — to just one goal the rest of the way.
The Sabres continued their nine-goal streak after the timeout, with Caroline Corson — converting a third straight Sweeney assist — Sweeney and McCall scoring over the final 4 minutes to widen the lead to 6-1 after one quarter.
Kat Murphy's two goals 41 seconds apart, and McCall's fourth strike pushed the Sabres' cushion to 9-2. Gunston freshman Jamie Tate ended that run with 7:54 left in the half. But Sweeney scored off Emma Hainey's assist, then set up Corson (four goals) for an 11-2 halftime lead.
The Sabres returned after the break and tallied 10 more goals en route to their most lopsided win of the season.
"'We know the level we should be playing at, and you guys aren't playing at that right now,'" Burke said of her first-quarter timeout message. "They agreed and they went back in and fixed everything that we told them needed fixing. So that was great."
As was Sweeney's passing, as the sophomore consistently snapped lead passes to teammates, who often just had to catch and shoot.
"I just try to lead them to it," Sweeney said. "It's hard to see what person it is. If I see a stick I'm like, that's who can have the opportunity. I'm confident in everyone on the team to control it and handle it. So I don't look for any one specific."
Mary Callahan, Claire Bieber, Hainey and Annie Albright each scored once for the Sabres.

 EASTON — Noah Palmer offered somewhat of an explanation for his latest victory."My curveball," Queen Anne's County High's senior right-hander said with a game-winning smile. "I don't know what to say. I haven't been throwing it all year. It's been iffy. But I came out of the gate and it came out of my hand amazingly. And I was able to throw a split-finger today amazingly, too. I just threw it and it hit spots. That's all I got to say."
Palmer didn't have to say much more late Tuesday afternoon, as he yielded five hits in six-plus innings to help Queen Anne's to an 11-8 victory over Easton, drawing the Lions closer to their first North Bayside title since 1980.
Winners of five straight, Queen Anne's (8-6 overall, 5-1 North Bayside) can clinch the North championship with victories over Cambridge-South Dorchester and Kent County.
Colonel Richardson (11-5, 5-2), which blanked St. Michaels 3-0 yesterday behind Jordan Regulski's complete-game three-hitter, still remains in contention in the North. Should the Lions lose one of their two remaining division contests and finish tied with Colonel, the Colonels would win the North via their 8-1 victory over Queen Anne's in the only head-to-head meeting between the two schools this season.
Kent Island (7-8, 5-2) also has an outside shot. Though they lost to Queen Anne's in the second meeting between the two schools — which counts toward the division standings — the Bucs defeated Colonel and hold the tiebreaker between those two schools.
Easton (10-5, 4-3), which was in the running for its first North crown since 2007, got two first-inning runs against Palmer (5-2) but then was held scoreless by the Lions ace until the bottom of the sixth inning.
"Credit goes to their pitcher," Easton head coach Albert Pritchett said of Palmer, who struck out six and walked two before being relieved in the seventh. "He did a great job. After the first couple of innings he really settled in, working on his pitches, threw strikes."
Palmer and Easton's Kayden Webb (4-1) were locked in a pitcher's duel, tied at 2-2 heading to the top of the sixth.
That's when the Lions busted the game open, scoring six runs on five hits.
With one out, Noah Cramer walked, moved to second on a low pitch and scored the go-ahead run on Chance Hegedus' double down the left-field line. Ethan Keppler singled, sending Hegedus (3 for 4, three runs) to third. Hegedus got caught in a rundown between home and third. Warrior catcher Colin Mooney ran Hegedus back before throwing the ball to third baseman Garrett Fink. But with no one covering home, Hegedus raced across the plate for a 4-2 lead.
Webb was relieved after Brendan Parsley singled. Dustin Blue walked the first man he faced before Travis Sutch (4 for 4, three RBIs), whose solo homer off the left-field pole tied the game at 2-2 in the third, singled through the right side, plating two runs for a 6-2 lead. Two batters later, Dulin Clark belted a two-run double for an 8-2 lead.
"I think we're hitting pretty good right now," Travis Sutch said. "Definitely a big improvement over the last couple games. Everybody's starting to get going now, especially the bottom of our lineup."
Easton ended its scoring drought in the bottom of the sixth. Dylan Cassell doubled and scored when Blue sent a shot over Parsley's head in center field. Chase Raab's sacrifice fly made it 8-4. But Palmer got a strikeout and groundout to end the inning.
"He did a great job today," Queen Anne's head coach Rick Sutch said of Palmer. "He knew this was a big game. We went into it knowing that we were in the driver's seat as far as the Bayside North. He knew how big this was and he had at least five days off, so he was fresh.
"Usually Noah doesn't let anything bother him so once he got the lead I wasn't really too concerned," Coach Sutch added. "Webb's a good pitcher on the other side, so we knew we had to get to him early to get to the bullpen. But Noah did a great job. He controlled the game."
Queen Anne's tacked on three runs on five hits in the seventh, stretching their lead to 11-4.
The Warriors pieced together their biggest inning in the seventh, with Mikey O'Connor hitting a two-run single and Carter Mooney sending a sacrifice fly to center to make it 11-8 before Clough induced a game-ending groundout.

title: St. Michaels extends perfect bid
author: Bill Haufe
content:
St. Michaels extends perfect bid

 April 30, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 888
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Jordan Miller thought St. Michaels High's boys tennis team was still a year away from challenging, and possibly winning the North Bayside title this spring.The Saints' 11-year head coach is perfectly fine with his calculation being a bit off.
"I knew Easton still had a lot of pieces that were going to be tough," Miller said. "I did know that we made a lot of improvement, but I expected theirs to be equal; kind of rising together. So I knew it was definitely going to be a tough match for us.
"But there's been a lot of guys on our team that have made a lot of progress, and more so than other teams in the Bayside (Conference)," Miller continued. "I think that really worked in our favor and allowed us to do some really nice things."
Among the nicer things the Saints have done this year is win their first North Bayside regular-season title in school history.
And they're not done yet.
St. Michaels continued pushing for yet another nice thing — and possibly another first — Wednesday afternoon with a 7-0 victory over North Dorchester that raised its record to a tidy 13-0 overall, 7-0 in the division.
"I feel over the last five years we've been super competitive," said Miller, who was unaware of a St. Michaels tennis team ever going undefeated in the regular season. "We just haven't been able to get over the hump. This year we knew we had a really nice chance to do well, and we just had to kind of find some pieces."
One of those pieces has been Sebastian Cornish, who did not play against the Eagles yesterday, but hasn't lost a match this season.
"We have a guy playing (number) four singles this year that didn't take any lessons, but literally played once a day, every day for 365 days," Miller said of Cornish.
"And then we have another guy, Jeremiah Monroe, is a sophomore who just played every single day and has been a big contributor at three doubles for us," Miller added.
Monroe teamed with Willie Coale at No. 3 doubles yesterday for a 8-1 victory over North Dorchester's Adam Elzey and Robert Smith. Coale then went on to beat Elzey, 8-0, at No. 4 singles.
"It's been a really nice team effort by lots of kids, who have put in lots of work," Miller said.
Another one of those kids who has put in lots of work has been Tom Weller, who reached the Class 1A state final in singles last year. Weller partnered with Patrick Goeller for an 8-1 win at No. 2 doubles against the Eagles before crafting an 8-1 victory over Carter Warfield at No. 3 singles.
"Tom Weller, he's a workhorse and he never loses," Miller said.
Then there's been the one-two punch at the top of the lineup: sophomore No. 1 Sean Kline and junior Miles Fox at No. 2.
"The development up top, where we have a kid last year who made it to state finals in doubles, but was not a doubles player," Miller said of Fox, who along with Cooper Baum advanced to the Class 1A state final in boys doubles. "He was a singles player, who now I would say is a doubles player. He's a doubles player and he likes doubles. I think it fits his game style."
It sure seemed to against North Dorchester, as Fox and Kline rallied for an 8-4 victory over Christian Chase and Vic Lamuth after trailing 3-2, at No. 1 doubles in the closest match on the boys side. Fox then earned an 8-0 victory over Lamuth at No. 2 singles.
Kline and Chase may have taken a 20-minute break before they were back on the court playing No. 1 singles, where the St. Michaels sophomore pieced together an 8-1 victory.
"Sean Kline has put in a lot of work," Miller said. "He's played in tournaments and done all the things that are necessary to improve his game. He's made a big step up from last year. He's really stepped up his game and really started taking it seriously, that's been big for him. And because of that he's had a lot of great results."
Before yesterday's match, Miller gathered his two teams and gave them a message.
"I told them, 'We're playing for different things,'" Miller said. "Our girls are playing to avenge a loss early in the season, and our boys are playing to close out the North. Regardless of what your motivation is today, that's what we're going to use to get those wins."
Miller's boys had already completed their victory just as North Dorchester's Jules Tobat and Maddie Tobat outlasted Lexi Rockwell and Brynn Lizewski, 8-6, at No. 1 doubles in match that almost last two hours.
Shortly after, a St. Michaels player approached Miller, asking what the Saints needed to do to win the girls match.
"We just need to win all three (of the remaining) singles matches," Miller answered.
The Saints did just that, rallying for a 4-3 win.
Rockwell defeated Jules Tobat, 8-1, at No. 1 singles, Tess Weller topped Maddie Tobat, 8-5, at No. 2, and Lizewski beat Emily Freeman, 8-6, at No. 3. North Dorchester's Ellie Sard defeated Kayla Montoya-Guzman, 8-0, at No. 4.
Freeman and Sard defeated Molly Genrich and Tess Weller, 9-7, at No. 2 doubles. St. Michaels' Georgia Crow and Peyton Fugate won 4-1 at No. 3 doubles.

title: JEWELS THROWS A GEM
author: Bill Haufe
content:
JEWELS THROWS A GEM

 May 1, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 AMERICAN CORNER — Graduation left North Dorchester High's softball team with some mighty big holes to fill heading into this season.The biggest of those was arguably in the circle, where ace Emilee Cohee had helped lead the Eagles to their first Class 1A state championship two years ago, as well as back-to-back North Bayside titles.
Well, Jewels Vroman has stepped into the role of ace quite nicely, thank you.
The junior left-hander delivered her fourth no-hitter of the season Thursday afternoon, striking out 12 along the way, as North Dorchester clinched its third consecutive North division championship with a 4-0 shutout of Colonel Richardson.
The Eagles (13-4 overall, 7-1 North Bayside) are slated to play Stephen Decatur (16-2) for the Bayside Conference championship next Tuesday at 5 p.m. at Salisbury University. The Seahawks defeated Mardela 3-1 on Thursday to clinch the South crown.
"Emilee's a hard player to follow," North Dorchester head coach Carol Hubbard said of her former star pitcher now at Wingate University. "But Jewels put in so much work in this offseason, pitching wise; just overall strength training. And it shows with the speed she's picked up on the mound and the confidence she has in her pitches.
"I feel like last year she knew what she was doing, but she didn't quite trust herself as much," Hubbard continued. "And this year she trusts herself and is able to get in there and do what needs to be done."
Vroman pitched in relief during the Eagles' 12-11 loss to Colonel on March 31, and admitted that provided her with an added dose of motivation heading into yesterday's second clash between the two schools. But Vroman also admitted getting a second crack at the Colonels while trying to cement a third straight division title didn't put any extra pressure on her shoulders.
"My rise-ball was really good today," said Vroman after raising her record to 7-3. "Curveball. Change-up was really good. Really any pitch I threw today was working. I just felt like I needed to do what I've been taught to be able to win."
Vroman certainly did that on this warm afternoon, striking out six of the first seven batters she faced, including the side in the first. The closest the Colonels (12-6, 4-4) came to a hit was with two outs in the fifth, when Kayleigh Bradley lined a shot that went off the first baseman's glove and was ruled an error.
That would be Colonel's lone baserunner, though, as Vroman retired the last seven batters she faced.
"She's the class of the North in the circle," Colonel head coach Scott Christopher said of Vroman.
Colonel freshman Chloe Simmons (9-6) got off to a strong start before the Eagles scratched across a run with two outs in the third. Emily Boyle worked a two-out walk. Vroman reached on an error. Alexus Myers then blooped a 1-1 offering into center field, scoring Boyle for a 1-0 lead.
North Dorchester pushed another run across in the fourth. Simmons again retired the first two batters before Abby Sann, Kinsley Peters and Boyle reached on consecutive singles, with Boyle's plating Sann for a 2-0 lead.
The Eagles extended their lead to 3-0 in the fifth, when Vroman scored on an error with two outs.
North Dorchester made it 4-0 in the seventh. Destini Wongus singled sharply to left with one out. Vroman beat out a slow roller to third for an infield hit that allowed Wongus to reach third. Wongus scored when Vroman was thrown out trying to steal second.
"I just feel like as a whole the team is clicking really good right now," Hubbard said. "We're aggressive at the plate. I just feel really good going into the postseason."
Christopher thinks Colonel is also in a good place heading into the playoffs, but needs to tighten its defense and hit.
"I thought Simmons went toe-to-toe with Vroman today," Christopher said. "I mean that was like David versus Goliath. You take away the errors and the walk and that's a 1-0 game. And we've got to hit. But we've worked hard to get 12 wins. I think we'll be all right."

title: Ensor, Lions clinch North
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Ensor, Lions clinch North

 May 2, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1031
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Kesley Fitzgerald and RJ Ensor started texting early Friday morning."I just kind of laid it out to her," Queen Anne's County High's girls head lacrosse coach said of her star senior. "I said, 'You can either hear from me how awesome and how unstoppable you are, or you can just get straight up facts, and that is we must win this game to secure another Bayside championship bid, and we must win this game to get a number one seed.' I knew she wanted to hear both."
Ensor certainly responded early Friday evening, scoring six of her seven goals in the first half to help propel the Lions to a 10-8 victory over Kent Island that clinched a fourth straight North Bayside title and the No. 1 seed in the approaching Class 2A East Region I playoffs.
The three-time defending conference champion, Queen Anne's (11-1 overall, 5-0 North Bayside) is scheduled to face Stephen Decatur for the Bayside championship on Monday at 6:45 p.m. at Decatur.
"We were getting our game plan together," Ensor said of her early-morning text conversation with Fitzgerald. "She was telling me she trusts me, she trusted my stick. This was my last game for the regular season on my home turf, which really hit hard for all of us seniors here. And I was like, 'I've got to go all out here. It's a rivalry game in the county. It's my last home game on the turf and I just got to go.'"
But it was Kent Island (10-2, 4-1) that got on the scoreboard first, when Willow Yost (three goals) scored 5 minutes, 7 seconds into the game on a free-position chance. Ensor answered with a free-position strike with 4:12 left in the first quarter. Just 36 seconds later, Caroline Levin set up Parker Tengwall's goal, moving the Buccaneers back in front at 2-1.
But then Ensor went on a run.
The senior wheeled in from the left and put the equalizer past Kent Island starting goalie Ava Mason (five saves) before getting knocked to the ground, forging the game's last tie with 3:13 to go in the opening quarter. Ensor then put the Lions ahead to stay with 45 seconds remaining in the quarter, when she took possession in transition and whipped a shot into left side of the net from about 12 yards out for a 3-2 lead and an early hat trick.
"RJ's a great player," Kent Island head coach Kaitlin Paukovits said. "She has been an impact player at least since I started watching her play her sophomore year. So we're not surprised. It's something we obviously need to shut down (should Kent Island and Queen Anne's meet in the playoffs)."
Ensor continued piling up the goals in the second quarter, starting with another free-position conversion with a little over 7 minutes left in the period for a 4-2 lead. Kaisa Hickson scored the first of her two goals off Jordan Bilbo's feed 36 seconds later. Thirty-three seconds after that, Ensor got the ball on the left side, made a few fakes and tucked her fifth goal of the half into the net for a 6-2 lead.
Yost's second goal with under 2 minutes left in the half brought Kent Island within 6-3. But Ensor notched her sixth goal with just 4 seconds remaining before the break, giving the Lions a 7-3 cushion.
"She thrives under pressure," Fitzgerald said of Ensor. "She wants the high-pressured games. No team wants to be in a place where you don't know what's going to happen; a team creeping back on you, and a team that every once in a while gets momentum. But she loves those opportunities. Time and time again she proves she thrives when she's under pressure."
Grace Mathews set up Yost's third goal just 12 seconds into the third to get Kent Island within 7-4. Again Ensor had a response, scoring off Kaitlyn Horney's dish before Hickson's second goal gave Queen Anne's its biggest lead at 9-4.
But the Bucs began turning up the pressure on Lions senior goalie Emma Dulin (nine saves). Hailey Offutt banged a shot off the right pipe. Mason made a big stop on Hailey Cole before the Lions extended their lead to 9-4.
Dulin then made a string of stops in the final 3:45 of the third, foiling Levin from close range and then making two saves on free-position shots.
"I just kept the momentum going," Dulin said. "I think it picked the whole team up as well."
Fitzgerald thought her goalie was poised for a big performance.
"I just had a feeling that this would be the game that that happened because she's been wanting a game like that, where's she's in the hot seat," Fitzgerald said. "She put a few saves together when we really, really needed it and took command of her defense."
Winners of nine straight coming into the game, the Bucs began to make things interesting though in the fourth. Cara Steele fed Mathews for a goal 20 seconds into the final period, trimming Kent Island's deficit to 9-5. With Ensor serving a 2-minute penalty, Steele and Mathews each scored free-position goals just 39 seconds apart, pulling the Bucs within 9-7 with 9:23 remaining in the game.
"We've been in that position before," Paukovits said of her team having to rally. "I think we just know it's a game of runs. It can be anybody's couple minutes at a time. So if they can go on a 4-0 run, we can go on a 4-0 run. And they're pretty good at digging in and chipping away at it."
But Ensor returned, setting up Horney's goal with 5:53 left for a 10-7 Lions lead. A Steele-to-Offutt scoring combination cut the Bucs' lead to two with 3:09 remaining. Queen Anne's won the ensuing draw and drained the clock to 52 seconds before Fitzgerald called time.
"Just to take that breath," Fitzgerald said to her team. "Just different scenarios; if this happens, if that happens. They all know when we take that timeout and we're up, they know what to do with the ball."
Kent Island got a turnover with about 35 seconds left and carried into Lions territory, but lost the ball and watched Queen Anne's run out the closing seconds.

title: Decatur finally gets hands on title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Decatur finally gets hands on title

 May 6, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 688
 Words 

 Read News Document

 BERLIN — Stephen Decatur High boys head lacrosse coach Hoffy Hoffman is used to talking postgame with his counterpart from Kent Island, Bobby Woolley.Hoffman spoke with Woolley last year after his Seahawks fell shy to the Bucs in the Bayside Conference championship and Class 2A state quarterfinals. The two coaches conferenced again after this year's March 28 regular-season meeting, when Kent Island scored the winning goal as the final horn sounded.
The two coaches were chatting it up again Monday night, when Woolley told Hoffman, "Get out of here. Go enjoy this."
"It's sweet," Hoffman said minutes after the Decatur had defeated unbeaten Kent Island, 13-11, for its first Bayside Conference championship since 2012. "It's everything I thought it would be and then some. This is as new feeling. And I can't lie to you. I could get used to it.
"It's been 13 years," Hoffman continued of Decatur's conference title draught. "I thought we had the team to do it the year unfortunately our (2020) season got canceled due to COVID. But I was confident with this team. I knew that Kent Island was going to come in and battle. It's always a battle with them. They're a great team from top to bottom. Bobby's a great coach. He's been here. He's done this a bunch of times. But I knew it was our boys' time this time."
Decatur (12-1) and Kent Island (12-1) were tied five times in the first half, which ended in a 6-6 draw. Keegan Green (team-high four goals) gave the Bucs a 7-6 lead with 2:55 elapsed in the third quarter when he buzzed a left-handed rip past Decatur goalie Declan Horan.
But the Seahawks responded with a 6-0 run that proved too deep for the Buccaneers to recover from.
"I think we put ourselves in a position to have to come back instead of playing well through the game, " Woolley said.
John Fohner (game-high six goals) scored the tying goal off an Ashton March pass with 7:51 left in the third quarter, then put the Seahawks ahead to stay with 5:45 remaining in the period courtesy of another March dish.
March, who gave Decatur a 1-0 lead just 7 seconds into the game, scored in transition, nudging the Seahawks' advantage to 9-7. Less than a minute later, Fohner unloaded an overhand crank that beat Bucs freshman goalie Quinn Burns, giving Decatur a 10-7 edge heading into the fourth quarter.
Goals from Parker Mason and Graham Geiser (three goals) stretched the lead to 12-7 with 7:34 remaining in the game.
The defending champs weren't quite through though.
Brian Rees (three goals) scored from close range to trim the Bucs' deficit to 12-8 with 4:46 remaining. Horan made a save on Marshall Dandy, then watched his teammates race downfield before Fohner took a small hop and snapped off a shot that restored Decatur's five-goal cushion with just under 4 minutes remaining.
"I knew it was a matter of time," Hoffman said of winning the conference title. "To really know where you're at, you've got to be battle tested. We're battled tested now, and now we're the heavyweight champs of the Bayside."
Kent Island kept chipping away. Green scored with 2:57 remaining. Eric Hoffman collected the ball off the ensuing faceoff and scored just 13 seconds later, drawing the Bucs within 13-10. Aidan Henry converted Green's pass to make it 13-11 with just 1:35 remaining.
But Kent Island would not find the net the rest of the way. Horan stopped Green, who later sent a shot wide. Henry then ripped a shot that sailed over the right corner of the cage with 14 seconds remaining.
"We kind of went on a 6-0 skid, where they got six unanswered I believe," Woolley said. "And that's a challenge no matter what. We've put in the guys' minds this year if we go down we've got to battle back because lacrosse is a game of runs. So I'm happy with the way they responded. If we had a little bit more time, maybe things would have been different. But all in all I'm not terribly impressed with the way we played. We got a lot of things to work on."

title: Lions get close but can't dethrone Decatur
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions get close but can't dethrone Decatur

 May 7, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 923
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — Sure, Rich Ferro wanted to win.But with the postseason approaching, Stephen Decatur High's head baseball coach also wanted to use the Bayside Conference championship as a primer for his pitchers.
"The worst thing that we can do is bring in a guy that hasn't been in a situation that's a little bit tight," Ferro said. "I don't care if it's 50-0, you pitch in this environment here, you get a little nerved up. We need to do this so everybody feels that little pit in their stomach; so everybody understands this is real baseball. This is different from the regular season."
Queen Anne's County certainly tried to put a pit in the collective stomachs of the Seahawks Tuesday night at Arthur W. Perdue Stadium, when it trimmed an early four-run deficit to one in the top of the fifth inning. But Decatur answered with a two-out, four-run bottom of the fifth before relievers Ben Powers and Caleb Loring pitched back-to-back 1-2-3 innings to seal an 8-3 victory that gave the Seahawks their third conference championship in four years and second straight.
"It always seems when we play these guys, it's always one inning," Queen Anne's head coach Rick Sutch said. "And it's usually late in the game.
"You got to give them credit," Sutch continued. "They got a lot of two-out hits. It was 4-3 until, we weren't making the quality pitch when it was 0-2, 1-2. So it came back to bite us. But you got to tip your hat to them. They swung the bats when they needed to. And our guys, they hung in there when they needed to. It's always been one inning when it comes down to it."
Decatur (17-2) took a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first. Queen Anne's starter Noah Palmer walked Brandon Nadeau and Landon Daniel before Johnny Hobgood hit a two-out single through the middle, scoring courtesy runner Owen Phillips.
The Seahawks expanded their lead in the second. Mason Edelman and Spencer Gaylor worked back-to-back walks before Kolten Zender beat out a bunt single to load the bases. Jackson Cheung bounced into a fielder's choice, plating Edelman. Gaylor scored when Nadeau grounded deep in the hole at short. One batter later, Nate Berzonski grounded out to short, scoring Cheung for a 4-0 lead.
Queen Anne's (10-7), which won seven of its final eight regular-season games to earn its first North Bayside title since 1980, didn't get a hit off Seahawks starter Berzonski, who struck out four and walked one over two scoreless innings. Raj Brachewski, the first of five Decatur relievers, set down the side in order in the third.
The Lions got on the board in the fourth. With one out, Jacob Clough lined a shot off the calf of Decatur's third pitcher, Justin Ujelick, who remained in the game. Palmer followed with a double to left that scored Clough, making it 4-1. Ujelick was relieved by Kyle Springle after walking Dulin Clark. Noah Cramer reached on a low throw to first, but Clark was tagged out in a rundown on the play.
Chase Hegedus then hit a 2-2 offering to right field. Courtesy runner Cole Coppage scored, shaving Decatur's lead to 4-2, but Cramer was thrown out at the plate.
"Chance had a good two-out hit and we got thrown out at the plate," Sutch said. "But we have to make that play there."
Nathan Procopio, who relieved Palmer with one out in the third, walked Cheung and yielded a single to Nadeau to open the fourth. But the right-hander retired the next three to keep the Lions within reach.
Queen Anne's crept within 4-3 in the fifth. Ethan Keppler walked. Springler retired Caleb Hutch and Procopio. Travis Sutch then launched a triple over Hobgood's head in center field, scoring Keppler. But the Lions couldn't get the tying run home, as Springler got a called strike three on Clough to end the inning.
Procopio got a pair of groundouts to third to start the bottom of the fifth. But Gaylor stung a double down the left-field line and scored on Zender's single to right. Cheung got plunked on the helmet by a pitch. Nadeau followed with a single to center that scored Zender for a 6-3 edge. Berzonski stroked a single to center, plating Cheung, and Landon Daniel singled to right, scoring courtesy runner Phillips for an 8-3 lead.
"It speaks about what they do and how they care about each other," Ferro said of Decatur's fifth-inning rally. "The success is really based on them wanting each other to be successful."
Powers and Loring took care of the Lions in the sixth and seventh, but like Ferro, Rick Sutch said the game should benefit his team heading into the playoffs.
"We play on Thursday, so we kind of attacked to where we'd have certain guys set up for Saturday and next Tuesday if we get that far," coach Sutch said of his pitching. "So we were kind of doing the same (as Decatur) but we also wanted to give it our best shot at this game without folding the towel early. I think both teams are well prepared to go into the playoffs now after this game."
Notes: Queen Anne's last appearance in the conference championship was 1980, when it earned a 3-1 victory over Stephen Decatur. ... Clough pitched a scoreless sixth inning for the Lions, striking out two and getting a pop out. ... The Lions are the No. 3 seed in the Class 2A East Region II bracket and will host sixth-seeded Wicomico on Thursday at 4 p.m. in a quarterfinal.

title: Eagles add elusive title to trophy case
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Eagles add elusive title to trophy case

 May 8, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 716
 Words 

 Read News Document

 North Dorchester High head softball coach Carol Hubbard thought she was going to have a strong team this season.But with only one senior and three juniors, even Hubbard admitted she didn't know how strong. Then the Eagles started the season losing two of their first three games, leaving some to perhaps think Hubbard's crew just didn't have it this year.
"I think a lot of people underestimated us at the beginning of the season because we are a young team," Hubbard said. "We dropped some games early to Colonel (Richardson) and C-SD (Cambridge-South Dorchester), and I think some people kind of wrote us off after that."
Well, the young Eagles wrote their names in the school record book Tuesday night at Salisbury University, defeating Stephen Decatur, 7-1, in the Bayside Conference championship to win the only title that has eluded the program.
"It feels good to win," said Hubbard, who has guided North Dorchester to a Class 1A state title, regional crowns, and three straight North division championships. "I told the kids when we were going out onto the field, 'I think there's 18 teams in the Bayside, and only two were playing.' And they were one of them. I said, 'You guys have been playing ball for a long time. You know what you're doing. Go out there on the field and do what you know how to do and have fun. And they did."
And they didn't wait long, scoring four first-inning runs.
Decatur starting pitcher Emily Blume issued a leadoff walk to Kinsley Peters, who advanced to third on Emily Boyle's single. Destini Wongus walked, loading the bases. Jewels Vroman then hit a ball that went off Blume into right field, bringing home Peters and Boyle for a 2-0 lead, while pushing Wongus to third. Alexus Myers' sacrifice fly to right plated Wongus with the Eagles' third run and allowed Vroman to reach third.
After walking Lola Allen, Blume was relieved by Maddie McGinnis, who watched Vroman race home on a passed ball for a 4-0 lead.
North Dorchester padded its lead in the fourth. Abby Sann was walked with two outs. Peters singled. Boyle then singled to center field. Decatur attempted to throw out Boyle at third, but the ball went into left field, scoring Sann and Peters for a 6-0 cushion.
The Seahawks (16-3) got on the scoreboard in the bottom of the fourth, when Bailey Griffin reached on an error, stole second and third, and scored on Ryleigh Smith's groundout to short.
But that proved to be the lone run Decatur managed against Vroman, who pitched a complete-game two-hitter with seven strikeouts and one walk.
"Jewels has just been pitching absolutely lights out here lately," Hubbard said of her junior left-hander, who tossed a no-hitter against Colonel Richardson to clinch the North last Thursday. "She put in a ton of work this offseason and it's really paying off now."
So has the work Peters has put in at catcher.
"Kinsley Peters hadn't caught since like 8U or 10U travel ball," Hubbard said. "So we kind of threw her back there because we needed to fill the position and she's done phenomenal. And the work that Kinsley's put in this season so that Jewels has a catcher back there that she trusts. She knows where to set up for all of Jewels' pitches. If Jewels' balls are breaking more than usual, less than usual, Kinsley's gotten really good at making those adjustments to help her pitcher out. And I think that in turn has helped Jewels be more confident on the mound."
The Eagles tacked on one more run sixth. Wongus drilled a triple to left, center field. Vroman popped out, keeping Wongus at third. Myers flied out to center, plating Wongus for the 7-1 final.
"About four to five games into the season this team really started just working together well and backing each other up," said Hubbard, whose team entered Thursday's Class 1A East Region II quarterfinal having won nine of its last 10, including six straight. "And the chemistry just started jelling, clicking, whatever word you want to use there. And we've been playing really good ball the last few games. I feel like the kids have been hitting the ball well, they've been aggressive on the base paths, and our defense has been solid for the most part. I'm happy."

title: K. Island's late surge eliminates Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
K. Island's late surge eliminates Warriors

 May 9, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 589
 Words
