 STEVENSVILLE — Overtime was needed when they met during the regular-season.Kent Island and Easton High's girls lacrosse teams were trending in that direction again Friday night, as they reached their fifth tie of the game 4 minutes, 37 seconds into the third quarter.
But that's where the seesaw play stopped, as Kent Island went on a 4-1 closing run en route to a 10-7 victory in a Class 2A East Region I semifinal and Andy Schipul Stadium.
The second-seeded Buccaneers (11-2) advance to Monday's 2A East I final, where they will meet No. 1 seed Queen Anne's (13-1) in Centreville at 5 p.m.
"We talked at halftime that they were going to come out with some energy and we had to make sure we came out and matched it," Easton head coach Katie Lowman said. "I think the teams are so evenly matched that this is really a case of who wants it more, and who wants to fight harder. And today they did."
Easton's Myka Motovidlak forged the game's fifth and final tie at 6-6, when she shoveled a shot past Kent Island second-half goalie Brianna Legg with 7:13 remaining in the third quarter.
A little over a minute later, Ellie Burnside put Kent Island ahead to stay, when she scored off a free-position set. Midfielder Hailey Offut (game-high five goals) then scored on a free-position chance and added another strike just 20 seconds later to give the Bucs a 9-6 lead.
"Our team really stepped it up in the second half," Offutt said. "We all worked well together on defense and offense."
Offutt scored at least one goal in every period, including the only goal of the fourth, when she converted Caroline Levin's pass with 8:07 left in the game. The Bucs though also showed patience as the second half progressed, burning clock and passing the ball around until creating an opportunity.
"I think the difference was just their execution and finishing," Kent Island head coach Kaitlin Paukovits said of her team. "We had a lot of missed opportunities in the first half and they decided to lock in and finish it.
"They set a lot of stuff up," Paukovits continued of her offense. "They were being smart about their options, and smart about their play-calling out there. And that's all them."
Anna Crist gave the Warriors (10-3) a 1-0 lead when she scored off a turnover with 8:47 remaining in the first quarter. Parker Tengwall (three goals) tied the game at 1-1 with 5 minutes left in the first quarter, when she curled in from behind the net and dumped a shot past Easton goalie Zelia Proa.
Stella Kabler nudged Easton back in front, when she raced almost the length of the field, dodged defenders along the way, and scored past Ava Mason — Kent Island's first-half goalie — with 1:42 to go in the first. Less than a minute later, Offutt netted her first goal, leaving the teams tied at 2-2 heading into the second quarter.
The back and forth continued in the second period. Miranda Stup scored for Easton. Offutt answered for Kent Island. Addie Knox and Dakota Lhotsky scored about 90 seconds apart midway through the period, giving the Warriors their biggest lead at 5-3 with less than 6 minutes in the half.
But Cara Steele set up Tengwall's second goal with 1:12 left in the half before Grace Mathews beat Easton goalie Zelia Proa with 31.3 seconds left for a 5-5 halftime stalemate.
Notes: Mason finished with three saves and Legg had four. … Kent Island defeated Easton, 11-10 in overtime in their regular-season game.

title: Cambridge-SD wins boys, girls team championships
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Cambridge-SD wins boys, girls team championships

 May 9, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Words

 CAMBRIDGE — This is the first outdoor season the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association has allowed track and field athletes to compete in six events.Cambridge-South Dorchester High senior Tori Willis Jr. ran in five during this week's two-day Bayside Conference championships and finished first in every event he entered. That proved to be a good thing for the Vikings because they needed every single one of those first-place efforts.
Willis won the 100-meters, the 110 high hurdles, the 300 intermediate hurdles and ran a leg on the first-place 4x100-meter relay Thursday, helping Cambridge-SD win the boys team title on their home track by one point over runner-up Kent Island. Willis also ran a leg on the winning 4x200 relay on Tuesday, as Cambridge-SD totaled 102 points for its second consecutive conference title.
Cambridge-SD also won the girls team crown, with Enazajah Young, Le'Asia Todd, Te'Janae Ballin and Al'Janae Jackson each winning individual titles, as the Vikings piled up 100 points to outdistance second-place James M. Bennett by 11 points.
"Tori Willis did his job," Viking head coach Clint Falduto said. "He's the leader of this team and he knows what needs to be done. Even though track in some ways is individualized, he's doing it for the team. Every run he runs is for the team."
On Tuesday, Willis joined Kimir Lake, Antonio Blueford and Zy'Meir Wilson in the 4x200 relay, which won in 1 minute, 30.47 seconds.
Willis started Thursday's Day 2 by winning the 110 high hurdles (14.90), then made a quick turnaround and won the 100 sprint in 11.01. The defending Class 1A state champion in the 300 hurdles, Willis clocked a first-place 38.66 in the event, then teamed with Tekai Drummond, Blueford and Lake to win the 4x100 relay in 43.22.
"Back to back feels great," Willis said of the team title. "We've had some ups and downs this year but we're pulling through at the right time. Every year we just keep progressing and get better.
"Long day," Willis continued. "Getting back in shape to where I want to be at. But from where I am right now, I think I've got room to improve."
Willis had plenty of help, starting with Blueford, who in addition to running legs on the two winning relays, won the long jump (21 feet, 1 inch) and was second in the 300 hurdles with a personal-record 39.83.
"Antonio Blueford; just a strong athlete," Falduto said. "What he's done throughout his career has been pretty amazing."
Falduto also applauded the efforts of Jakuez Snead, who won the shot put Tuesday with a heave of 47-10¼ — edging Kent Island's Josh Fuller (47-6) — and Lake, who competed outdoors for the first time.
"Kimir Lake is a senior rookie that's definitely helped out with a lot of relays, which has been great," Falduto said. "And Jakuez Snead coming back and throwing and getting first on Tuesday was amazing."
A dual-sport athlete who plays softball, Young set a meet record during Tuesday's preliminaries for the girls 100 hurdles with a time of 14.47. Two days later, Young blew away the field, winning the final in 14.54, with James M. Bennett's Merlina Orneus in second (16.28).
"Although few, they really put a powerful punch in today," Falduto said of his girls team. "Getting Enazajah Young back was definitely a solid key in the high hurdles, even though I'd like to have her for a lot more than that. She definitely did her job."
Todd had another strong meet. The senior placed second in the triple jump (35-3) on Tuesday, then won the high jump (4-10) and took second in the long jump (17-¾) on Thursday. Ballin won her first Bayside title, leaping 17-1½ to take first in the long jump. Ballin boosted the Vikings' total with her runner-up finish in the high jump (4-10) and her third place in the triple jump (33-2½).
"Le'Asia Todd is just an all-star," Falduto said. "And bringing Te'Janae Ballin in this year as a rookie, a 12th grader, she definitely has had an impact this year."
Also making impacts were Jackson, who won the pole vault (8-6) and Ja'Naya Stanley, runner-up in the 300 hurdles (49.35).
Kent Island junior Lacey Dauses was one of two North Bayside runners to win two individual titles and add a third in a relay. In a fairly tight time frame on Thursday, Dauses won the 400 (personal-record 1:01.16) took first in the 800 (2:25.25) then held off a late charge from North Caroline on the anchor leg of the Bucs' 4x400 relay.
"The four by four is a hard race to run out in front like that because it's hard to go all out," said Dauses, who teamed with Reese Heyliger, Ava Tippett and Alexia Grossman for a first-place 4:23.95. "It was good. But it was close. Too close for my comfort for sure.
"I'm definitely happy with my 400 time," Dauses added. "Eight-hundred time, still working to get it down to last year (2:19). Getting there."
Though she ran in a different heat, North Caroline's Linda Ridgell was second to Dauses in the 800 with a 2:27.47. Ridgell joined Brooke Sullivan, Morgan Knott and Seanna Rupp to win the 4x800 relay (10:22.50) on Tuesday, then crushed the competition in the 3,200 with an 11:46.45 — 52 seconds ahead of second place. Ridgell added another title Thursday, winning the 1,600 with a PR of 5:21.85.
Despite recently getting over an illness, Queen Anne's senior Ben Marks cruised to victories Thursday in the 1,600 (4:36.33) and 800 (2:02.05).
"Just checking the box for conference and trying to get healthy as fast as possible for the bigger postseason races," Marks said. "Not very happy with times today, but I can't be mad about it either. I had no idea what I could do going into today just because I'm not feeling good."
North Bayside athletes won five of the six field events. In addition to the victories by Blueford (long jump) and Snead (shot put), Kent Island's Jack Morey won the pole vault (14 feet) and Fuller took gold in the discus (139-5). Colonel Richardson's Aydan Downie won the triple jump with a PR of 44-7¾.
Kent Island's near miss in the boys competition was also aided by Giovanni Aguirre's victory in the 400, where clocked a new PR 48.95.

title: Offutt, Kent Island surge past Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Offutt, Kent Island surge past Warriors

 May 9, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 862
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — Overtime was needed when they met during the regular-season.Kent Island and Easton High's girls lacrosse teams were trending in that direction again Friday night, as they reached their fifth tie of the game 4 minutes, 37 seconds into the third quarter.
But that's where the seesaw play stopped, as Kent Island went on a 4-1 closing run en route to a 10-7 victory in a Class 2A East Region I semifinal and Andy Schipul Stadium.
The second-seeded Buccaneers (11-2) advance to Monday's 2A East I final, where they will meet No. 1 seed Queen Anne's (13-1) in Centreville at 5 p.m.
"We talked at halftime that they were going to come out with some energy and we had to make sure we came out and matched it," Easton head coach Katie Lowman said. "I think the teams are so evenly matched that this is really a case of who wants it more, and who wants to fight harder. And today they did."
Easton's Myka Motovidlak forged the game's fifth and final tie at 6-6, when she shoveled a shot past Kent Island second-half goalie Brianna Legg with 7:13 remaining in the third quarter.
A little over a minute later, Ellie Burnside put Kent Island ahead to stay, when she scored off a free-position set. Midfielder Hailey Offut (game-high five goals) then scored on a free-position chance and added another strike just 20 seconds later to give the Bucs a 9-6 lead.
"Our team really stepped it up in the second half," Offutt said. "We all worked well together on defense and offense."
Offutt scored at least one goal in every period, including the only goal of the fourth, when she converted Caroline Levin's pass with 8:07 left in the game. The Bucs though also showed patience as the second half progressed, burning clock and passing the ball around until creating an opportunity.
"I think the difference was just their execution and finishing," Kent Island head coach Kaitlin Paukovits said of her team. "We had a lot of missed opportunities in the first half and they decided to lock in and finish it.
"They set a lot of stuff up," Paukovits continued of her offense. "They were being smart about their options, and smart about their play-calling out there. And that's all them."
Anna Crist gave the Warriors (10-3) a 1-0 lead when she scored off a turnover with 8:47 remaining in the first quarter. Parker Tengwall (three goals) tied the game at 1-1 with 5 minutes left in the first quarter, when she curled in from behind the net and dumped a shot past Easton goalie Zelia Proa.
Stella Kabler nudged Easton back in front, when she raced almost the length of the field, dodged defenders along the way, and scored past Ava Mason — Kent Island's first-half goalie — with 1:42 to go in the first. Less than a minute later, Offutt netted her first goal, leaving the teams tied at 2-2 heading into the second quarter.
The back and forth continued in the second period. Miranda Stup scored for Easton. Offutt answered for Kent Island. Addie Knox and Dakota Lhotsky scored about 90 seconds apart midway through the period, giving the Warriors their biggest lead at 5-3 with less than 6 minutes in the half.
But Cara Steele set up Tengwall's second goal with 1:12 left in the half before Grace Mathews beat Easton goalie Zelia Proa with 31.3 seconds left for a 5-5 halftime stalemate.
Notes: Mason finished with three saves and Legg had four. … Kent Island defeated Easton, 11-10 in overtime in their regular-season game.
QUEEN ANNE'S 18, NORTH CAROLINE 6
CENTREVILLE — RJ Ensor totaled seven goals and three assists, and Kaisa Hickson scored five goals, leading the top-seeded Lions to their 12th straight victory Friday.
Kaitlyn Horney scored twice and set up another goal for Queen Anne's (13-1), Riley Klepper and Charlotte Schmidt each had a goal and one assist, and Haley Cole and Jordan Bilbo each added a goal.
BOYS LACROSSE
KENT ISLAND 27, NORTH CAROLINE 5
STEVENSVILLE — Brian Rees scored seven goals, and Mark Rees, Keegan Green and Zach Bunce each had two goals and an assist Friday, leading No. 1 seed Kent Island past North Caroline in a 2A East I semifinal.
Colton Schneck, Marshall Dandy, Gavan Henry and Brayden Pinder each had two goals for the Buccaneers (13-1), who will host second-seeded Queen Anne's in the region final Monday. Logan Donoway and Dylan Martino each had a goal and one assist, and Liam Deremer, Finn McGrath, Laken Brinkerhoff and Kyle Dalziel each had one goal for the Bucs.
QUEEN ANNE'S 10, EASTON 2
CENTREVILLE — Jamison Kendall had seven goals and Brian Maleski made seven saves, leading Queen Anne's County over Easton in a Class 2A East Region I semifinal.
The second-seeded Lions (9-3) play at top-seeded Kent Island (13-1) Monday for the region title. Carter Hercher, Tanner Lyon and Ryan Scattergood had one goal apiece for Queen Anne's.
CAMBRIDGE-SD 9, SOUTHERN 7
CAMBRIDGE — Tabrion Watts had four goals and Gavin Weber added two, as Cambridge-South Dorchester topped Southern in a Class 1A East II semifinal.
Christen Dockins, Darren Belizaire and Charles Spedden each scored for the No. 2 seed Vikings (3-9), who play at top-seeded Kent County (6-6) for the region title.

title: Court should be revitalized
author: Staff Writer
content:
Court should be revitalized

 May 10, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Editors Inbox 
 
 181
 Words 

 Read News Document

 When I was a kid, my mother and I were one of the first families to move into the Riverview Gardens Apartments in the late 1970s. For those that don't know, Riverview Gardens is in the Town of Denton, near Lockerman Middle School.I still have very vivid memories of living in that neighborhood. Life was amazing back then, didn't have a care in the world.
One of my fondest memories was when my mother would take me to play basketball at the basketball courts on Lincoln Street. I loved that place, so many memories were made there.
Unfortunately, the rims have been taken down, and there is grass growing through the cracks in the asphalt. A once-great neighborhood landmark has been relegated to an empty eyesore. It would be amazing to see that court revitalized and rebuilt so other kids could have the fun I had there as a kid.
Hopefully, someone will read this and decide to do something about it. I think it would be an amazing community project and would be a wonderful addition to that part of town.
SHAWN WILLIAMS
Denton

title: Sabres earn rematch with Curley
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres earn rematch with Curley

 May 13, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 563
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Todd Wolters may often wonder how good his team could really be if its fundamentals matched its talent."I'm taking my hat off to that team," Saints Peter and Paul High's boys head lacrosse coach said of Concordia Prep. "That team played so hard. Luckily it just shows you how good we are to play maybe one of our poorest fundamental games this year and you still win by nine. That shows you how much talent's there."
JJ Rardin scored six goals and Noah Zimmerman added five Tuesday, as the Sabres used a 9-2 second half to pull away from the Saints en route to a 15-6 victory in a Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association B Conference semifinal.
Sts. Peter & Paul (12-7) advances to Friday's 5 p.m. MIAA B championship game at Towson University's Johnny Unitas Stadium, where it will meet defending champion Archbishop Curley (12-4) for the second consecutive year.
"Any win's a good win, especially when it gets you to the championship," Wolters said.
Rardin set up Mason Roland's goal for a 1-0 Sabres' lead a little over 2 minutes into the game. Just 15 seconds later though, Concordia's Chase Meadows (two goals) tied the game. The Saints then went ahead when Ethan Smelcer beat Sabres goalie Hank Wolters (10 saves).
"We were giving them unsettled situations because we can't catch, we couldn't throw, and we wouldn't pick up ground balls," Coach Wolters said.
Andrew Steinhardt set up Zimmerman's first strike with 7:45 remaining in the first half, and Rardin nudged the Sabres to a 3-2 lead with 4:51 to go in the first quarter.
Sts. Peter & Paul pushed its advantage to 4-2 just 46 seconds into the second quarter, when Zimmerman converted a pass from Liam Durnbaugh. The Saints continued to keep it close, when Eric Johnson snagged a rebound and popped it into the back of the net to make it a one-goal difference with a little over 10 minutes to play in the second quarter.
Rardin scored off a Zimmerman feed with 7:34 left in the half, then scored off Andrew Steinhardt's dish to convert on an extra-man opportunity that extended Sts. Peter & Paul's lead to 6-3. Concordia answered 1:22 later with Colton Seifert's goal.
"In the first quarter, we were putting the ball on the ground one on one, not being able to pick up ground balls, not being able to clear it turning into unsettled situations," Todd Wolters said.
Rardin and Meadows exchanged goals in the opening 2 minutes of the third quarter.
But the Sabres took command with a 7-0 run that started with Steinhardt curling from the back of the net and squeezing a shot past Saints goalie Logan Tawney (three saves) with 10:10 remaining in the quarter. Just 26 seconds later, Rardin scored on a low shot. A Rardin-to-Zimmerman scoring connection and Steinhardt's second goal of the period moved Sts. Peter & Paul to an 11-5 edge heading into the fourth.
A goal from Steinhardt and two more from Zimmerman in a 63-second window cushioned the Sabres' lead to 14-5 with 4:11 remaining. Caleb Cruikshank ended the Saints' 19-plus minute scoring slump with 3:08 remaining.
"Hank got really hot in the second half," Coach Wolters said of his goalie. "That helped. But we got to play better. You'd like to get a little bit of momentum going into the championship. But we got two days to practice, and see what they do."

title: Tension grows on the tennis courts in Cambridge
author: Lily Tierney
content:
Tension grows on the tennis courts in Cambridge

 May 13, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Lily Tierney | Section: News 
 
 368
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — As warm weather re-emerged, so did feelings of inequity within Dorchester County's racquet sport community.On May 1, the recently remodeled Glasgow Tennis Courts' Facebook page posted, "We love seeing the courts being used and enjoyed by the community! However, we want to kindly remind everyone not to paint additional lines on the courts. We truly appreciate your cooperation in helping us keep the courts in great shape for everyone."
Under the original post, the tennis facility posted four photos of permanent marker and chalk outlining pickleball boundaries on the resurfaced courts — direct violations of The United States Tennis Association (USTA) grant that helped fund the remodel. Frustration from tennis and pickleball players alike flooded the comments.
Last summer, through the USTA grant and fundraising efforts from the James G. Busick Tennis Foundation, the Glasgow Tennis Courts were repaved with one stipulation — there would be no pickleball playing for at least five years.
The pickleballers of Dorchester pushed back at county council meetings and demanded outdoor court space. "We are very mindful of that. We're not dismissive of what their concerns are," said County Council Member and County Manager Jerry Jones.
On April 15, Dorchester County Council unanimously approved the Hurlock Pickleball Project, heralded by Director of Parks and Recreation Duc Trieu, to convert two tennis courts into pickleball courts. This is now the second pickleball project underway in Dorchester.
However, the projects aren't moving quickly enough for some, and a few pickleball players have taken matters into their own hands by ignoring the grant stipulations for the Glasgow Courts.
"I do know that there was some malicious destruction done to the tennis courts probably a week, 10 days ago," said County Council member Ricky Travers. According to Travers, in addition to the chalk and permanent marker, stones were placed on the courts.
Jones says he hopes that up to six outdoor pickleball courts will be ready by Memorial Day.
"I just want it to be very clear. I don't want it to look like we're condemning the pickleball community for the actions of a few because that's not the case," Jones said. "We know that this is a small number, and we hope that that kind of disrespect does not continue."

title: THE BUCS ARE ALL RIGHT
author: Bill Haufe
content:
THE BUCS ARE ALL RIGHT

 May 13, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 687
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — The score at halftime was 13-0.So was this the best half Kent Island High's boys lacrosse team had played this season?
"Debatable," Bucs head coach Bobby Woolley said.
Woolley wasn't so much concerned about the best way, as he was the right way.
"We ratcheted down the last week or so of practice, really trying to fine tune details of how we're supposed to play," Woolley said. "No emotions. Just choices. Make the right choice. Do it the right way; the way you've been taught to play and a lot of good things happen when you do that."
Well, a lot of good things happened for the Buccaneers Monday night, as they reeled off the game's first 13 goals on the way to a 19-6 victory over Queen Anne's County in the Class 2A East Region I championship at Andy Schipul Stadium.
Kent Island (14-1) will be the No. 1 seed for the Class 2A state tournament and will host No. 8 Century (9-5) on Wednesday at 6:30 p.m. in a state quarterfinal.
"I think the game with (Stephen) Decatur really helped us," Kent Island senior captain and longpole Gavan Henry said of the 13-11 Bayside championship loss to the Seahawks May 5. "In a way it like humbled us, and at the same time got us angry. We knew we didn't play our best versus these guys last time (a 12-7 win over Queen Anne's on May 2) so we knew we had to put on a show and we did."
The scoring part of the show started 1 minute, 19 seconds into the game, when Brian Rees (three goals) collected a loose ball, pulled out of traffic, pivoted and cranked a shot past Lions goalie Brian Maleski for a 1-0 lead. Connor Byrne and Connor Gardner (two assists) scored 1:06 apart for a 3-0 lead, prompting a timeout from Queen Anne's head coach Brad Niesz with 7:41 left in the opening quarter.
Keegan Green (two goals, assist) made it 4-0 before Mark Rees set up the first two of Colton Schneck's game-high five goals for a 6-0 lead after one quarter.
Brian Rees completed his hat trick in the second quarter and watched Schneck, Green, Gavan Henry, Aidan Henry and brother Mark Rees each put one in net for a 13-0 halftime bulge.
"The fact is the boys responded well to the ask," Woolley said. "We really fine tuned some things this past week so it was pleasant to see them put it on full display."
And what did Woolley tell his team at the break?
"Stay the course," Woolley said. "We're playing four quarters of lacrosse today. We're not playing two, and that's the biggest part of this time of the season. You've got to pick your battles on what you're trying to accomplish and today was a challenge for us to make sure we could stay focused for four quarters."
Jamison Kendall (team-high three goals) finally got the Lions (10-4) on the board 29 seconds into the second half, when he put his 100th career goal past Bucs freshman goalie Quinn Burns. The county rivals spent the rest of the quarter trading goals, with Schneck and Finn McGrath scoring for Kent Island, and Kendall and Jackson Shiley (two goals) scoring for Queen Anne's.
Up 16-3 after three quarters, Laken Brinkerhoff, Marshall Dandy and Zach Bunce each scored to stretch the Bucs lead to 19-3 before Queen Anne's Tanner Lyon sandwiched a pair of goals around Kendall's final tally.
"I think we got our confidence up, and we can be the best when our confidence is up," Gavan Henry said. "We've got to believe in ourselves. We got to believe in our guys. I think trust is the our number one thing."
1A EAST II FINALCAMBRIDGE-SD 12, KENT COUNTY 4WORTON — Tabrion Watts scored four goals and Charles Spedden totaled two goals and three assists Monday, as the second-seeded Vikings topped No. 1 seed Kent.
Cambridge-SD (4-9) will be the seventh seed in the 1A state tournament and play at No. 2 Fallston on Wednesday at 5 p.m.
Darren Belizaire (assist) and Gavin Webber each had two goals for Cambridge-SD, and Nate McClarren and Mark Mills scored one apiece.

title: SAINTS PILE INTO STATES
author: Bill Haufe
content:
SAINTS PILE INTO STATES

 May 14, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 849
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Coaches tend to focus a little harder on the details come the postseason, searching for that little extra something.So at practice Tuesday, St. Michaels High's baseball team focused on among other things, the proper technique for … the celebratory dog-pile.
"We just wanted to prepare the kids for anything that might come their way," said Saints assistant Bill Burton, who was in charge of choreography. "We don't want anybody getting hurt. So we told them, you know, 'Come together and then get on your stomach. You don't want your whole team above you on your backs. Just be gentle.'"
St. Michaels erupted for eight first-inning runs and senior Will Sherwood pitched a two-hitter Wednesday en route to an 11-1 victory in five innings over North Dorchester in the Class 1A East Region I championship before he and catcher Pearson Greenwood met near the mound to set the dog-pile in motion.
The Saints seemed to follow Burton's basics fairly well.
As for the gentle piece?
"I think we had it mastered," Sherwood said. "But there was a lot of people coming down I know that. Me and Pearson were on the bottom and we were looking at each other."
"I was looking at him and I was like, 'We won, man. We won.'" Greenwood said. "'We did it.' At least I had the helmet on so I didn't get any knees to the head. I feel bad for Will a little bit. But it's great to be the first people to come together on something like that."
St. Michaels dedicated the game to longtime assistant Donnie Gowe, whose mother, Nora Lee Gowe, passed away early Wednesday morning. The Saints presented the game ball to Gowe, who afterwards gave it to his father, Donald Gowe Sr.
The Saints (14-5) now await the reseeding of the eight regional champions for the state tournament.
"This is just a really good group of kids," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said. "The best thing about them, you got Will Sherwood as your leader, but the seniors don't look down on the young kids. It's a very cohesive unit. It's those kind of teams that are successful."
Sherwood set the Eagles down in order in the top of the first, then was part of an eight-run, five-hit bottom half of the frame.
With one out, Connor Wheeler and Sherwood hit back-to-back singles. Greenwood was hit by a pitch, and lifted for courtesy runner Brandon Toadvine. AJ Dove's sacrifice fly to right plated Wheeler for a 1-0 Saints lead. Eagles starter Gage Kral walked Ethan Royer to load the bases. Jack Brennen roped a single to right-center that scored Sherwood and Toadvine. After Brennen Dean was hit by a pitch, Brock Grow lined a single to right-center, bringing home Royer and Brennen for a 5-0 lead.
Lane Abbey relieved Kral. Blake Wheatley reached on an error that scored Dean and Grow for a seven-run lead. Wheeler punctuated the inning with a double that scored Wheatley for an 8-0 lead.
That was more than enough support for Sherwood, who carried a no-hitter into the fourth inning before Peyton Bleyer beat out an infield single with one out. TJ Leonard walked, but Sherwood squelched the rally there, getting called third strikes on Blake Bramble and Sutton Dukes to end the inning.
"His breaking ball breaks late, and when he has that working he's very difficult to hit.," Femi said of Sherwood. "And he competes."
St. Michaels' senior right-hander, who was facing the Eagles for the seventh consecutive time in his career, gave up a leadoff double to Manny Reyes in the fifth inning. Reyes moved to third on a high pitch and scoring on Abbey's groundout to short.
Sherwood promptly retired the next two batters, getting a sparkling defensive play from freshman third baseman Wheatley, who laid out to snag Brock Warrell's hard grounder before quickly getting to his feet and firing a strike to first, ending the game and triggering the dog-pile.
"It was amazing," Sherwood said of Wheatley's game-ending gem. "I thought it was through. Then I see him lay out and I was like, 'I hope he gets up in time.' And he threw a laser across."
St. Michaels' catcher thought Sherwood was doing the same thing.
"I think he was pretty much dialed in from like the first pitch," Greenwood said. "He looked good in my opinion. He was probably throwing his fastball the hardest he's thrown it all year. I mean I really felt it hitting the mitt. Honestly the way he threw his curveball was the best I've seen all year. He pitched really well."
St. Michaels tacked on three runs in the fourth, when Brennen Dean hit a two-run single to left field and Royer scored on a wild pitch.
But Femi was also impressed by Abbey's effort on the mound.
"I thought the Abbey kid who came in relief, I know he hasn't pitched much this year, but again, that's the epitome of a competitor," Femi said. "He went in there, and 8-0 game and could have just laid down and he didn't. He fought in there. I thought it showed a lot of character on his part."

title: Saints net fourth straight region title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Saints net fourth straight region title

 May 15, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 766
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Having three consecutive Class 1A East Region I titles to its credit has placed St. Michaels High's tennis team in new territory."It's definitely apparent when you go to the region and there is some expectations there," Saints head coach Jordan Miller said. "I think that gives you a different type of nerve to deal with. But I knew we definitely had some strong teams."
Miller's crew proved that, winning three of the five brackets last weekend to earn a fourth straight Class 1A East I championship at Perryville High.
"Feels good," said Miller after the Saints totaled nine points to defeat runner-up Kent County (five) and third-place Perryville (four). "It feels like the culmination of a lot of work. And the kids at this point, four years in, we put up the first (region) banner and everyone was like, 'Oh, that's great.' And now I feel like they're trying and they're starting to believe that maybe there's more than baseball down at St. Michaels, and we can share the wealth."
While the Saints have won five state baseball championships, the tennis program heads into next Thursday's opening round of the state tournament at the Wilde Lake Tennis Club in Columbia searching for its first state crown.
But after finishing fifth in 2023 and fourth a year ago, Miller thinks he has a combination that might put St. Michaels in better contention for that title.
"It used to be you could earn some points just by getting to states toward your team score," Miller said. "So if you sent four teams that was a good thing.
"They've changed the rules," Miller continued. "So now you only earn points if you win rounds. So it was kind of making sure the teams that we were sending had the best chance at states to win rounds, to add points together to hopefully put together a team title."
Heading that lineup is the mixed doubles team of Lexi Rockwell — undefeated at No. 1 singles this year — and Tom Weller, who won the boys singles title at regionals a year ago, but lost in the first round at states to Boonsboro's Hunter Liao, who will bid for his fourth straight state singles title next weekend.
Seeded third, Rockwell and Weller defeated No. 2 seed Rulie Baker and Ryan Kefauver of Colonel Richardson in the semifinals before beating fifth-seeded Sophie Cousineau and Bjorn Birkmire of Kent County, 6-0, 6-1 in the final.
"Having her play mixed doubles is just an absolute step up against any team we play," Miller said of Rockwell. "So her and Tom playing together I knew was going to be a strong team."
Miller also thought pairing his season-long No. 1 and 2 boys singles players, sophomore Sean Kline and junior Miles Fox, would be a strong team. And though Miller admitted to being a bit concerned about a potential letdown after the Saints fell shy of winning their first Bayside Conference boys tennis championship in a 4-3 loss to Stephen Decatur, he also believed his team would move forward after that defeat. They did.
The No. 4 seed, Kline and Fox handled No. 5 Robert Hague and Teo O'Brien of Kent County in the quarterfinals, ousted the top-seeded Aiden Montross and Ethan Woehr of Bohemia Manor in the semis, before earning a 6-0, 6-1 victory over the No. 3 seed, Holden Coe and Tyler Loss (Perryville) in the final.
Junior Tess Weller gave St. Michaels its third champion, when she won the girls singles crown. Seeded fifth, Tess Weller upended top-seeded Maya Charles (Bo Manor) in the semifinals before outlasting No. 3 seed Nina Fahrman (Kent County), 7-5, 7-5 in the title match.
"Tess has been a rock-solid singles player all year, last year as well," Miller said. "And the boys (Kline and Fox) haven't lost a doubles match yet this year. I knew those three (including mixed doubles) were going to be tough. I was hoping we could pull off some upsets in the other couple spots (boys singles, girls doubles) as well. But it's definitely what we expected. But you can't overlook anybody.
"We kind of wanted to stack our deck if we could," added Miller, of trying to set his team up for regional success and a state title shot. "The (mixed doubles) team that won it last year (South Carroll's Sydney Mossman and Michael Mooney is back, and half of the second-place team is back. But I think we have the strongest girl (Rockwell) in the draw, and if Tom plays well we'll be just fine. Sean and Miles, there is nobody that they can't beat and there's several people they could lose to."

title: Cambridge-SD sweeps regional crowns
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Cambridge-SD sweeps regional crowns

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 STEVENSVILLE — The victories started rolling in under Tuesday's gray skies — Le'Asia Todd in the girls triple jump; Al'Janae Jackson in the pole vault; and the girls and boys 4x200-meter relays.The gold-medal count kept growing in Thursday's heat — Enazajah Young and Tori Willis Jr. in the hurdles, Todd in every event she entered, and more from the relays. At one point in Thursday's mid-afternoon heat, Cambridge-South Dorchester High co-head coach Dr. Lois Narr stop in the infield, took a swig of water, smiled, and said, "These kids just have so much talent."
That talent was on display for all to see at Kent Island High's Andy Schipul Stadium, as the Vikings swept the boys and girls team titles at the Class 1A East Region outdoor track and field championships.
"This group, they have so much experience they make it look professional," Narr said. "They're so seasoned that they just know exactly what they have to do, what their job is. They show an incredible amount of confidence, and they just go out there and do it."
Cambridge-SD's girls amassed 150 points, outdistancing runner-up Snow Hill by 53 points. Leading the way was Todd, who started her five gold-medal haul on Tuesday, winning the triple jump (33 feet, 2 inches) and joining Young, Jackson and Te'Janae Ballin on the winning 4x200-meter relay (1 minute, 47.17 seconds).
The senior added to her count Thursday, leading a 1-2 Vikings' finish in the high jump (5-0) — Ballin was second at 4-8 — and a 1-2-3 finish in the long jump (17-½) — Young was runner-up (16-11¾) and Ballin was third (16-2¾). Todd capped her Day 2 by running the third leg on the winning 4x100 relay, again teaming with Young, Jackson and Ballin for a 50.30.
"Le'Asia, she is going to put her best effort into absolutely everything that she does," Narr said. "And she always has that positive attitude."
Young blazed to victory in the 100 hurdles (14.41), followed by teammate Ja'Naya Stanley (16.75), who later Thursday won the 300 hurdles (50.22). Jackson won the pole vault on Tuesday, clearing the bar at 7-9.
North Dorchester freshman Diamond Newbill won the girls 200 in a personal-record 26.11, and Kent County's Ke'yare Hawkins was first in the shot put with a heave of 33-10.
Kent County also had a strong showing on the boys side, where junior Rah'zir Wilson won the 100 sprint (10.84), edging Willis (10.85), and also soared to gold in the high jump (6-1) and long jump (21-10½). Teammate RJ Peterson won the 200 in 22.07.
But that combination could not overcome the Vikings, who romped to the boys title, totaling 173 points, with Bohemia Manor finishing second with 116 points.
After winning five titles — three individual, two relays — at last Thursday's Bayside Conference championships, Willis — earned five gold medals and one silver, that coming in the 100. Willis and senior classmate Antonio Blueford went 1-2 in both the 110 high hurdles and the 300 intermediate hurdles, and teamed with William Jackson and Kimir Lake to win the 4x200 relay (1:30.21) and the 4x100 relay (43.29). Willis also teamed with Tekai Drummond, Zy'Meir Wilson and Lake to win the 4x400 relay (3:29.35).
Willis clocked a 14.82 to win the 110 hurdles, with Blueford finishing in 14.92, and ran a first-place 36.68 in the 300 hurdles.
"Tori, just makes it look so easy," Narr said. "He's just so confident, and this year he has put it all together."
The 300 hurdles had been anything but easy for Blueford, who fell over the same hurdle while working the curve the past two years. Blueford ran a clean 300 this time, finishing in personal-record 39.70 before co-head coach Clint Falduto put him a big bear hug near the finish line.
"I tried not to focus on it too much and just focused on my race," Blueford said. "Once I cleared the first hurdle I was pretty good from there. I was trying not to get out as fast because I was worried about falling, but then once I got loose I was good from there."
Cambridge-SD's William Jackson was second in the pole vault at 13-7.
Colonel Richardson had a pair of regional champions on the boys side, with Aydan Downie winning the triple jump (45 feet) and Pierre Betsaleel winning the 400 meters. North Dorchester's Jase Todd was first in the discus (133-6) and second in the shot put (47-3).
Kent Island's Josh Fuller struck gold twice, winning the 2A East Region title in the boys shot put (46-10½) and the discus (135-7). Teammate Giovanni Aguirre took home first place in the 400, winning in 48.94.
Queen Anne's County senior Ben Marks, who shook off an illness last week to win the 1,600 and 800 at Baysides, admitted he was still not feeling his best, but still managed to win the 1,600 (4:28.44) and 800 (1:56.92) for a second straight week.
"I'm getting through it," Marks said. "Within the next two days I'll be back to where I want to be. Just need to keep my head down and focus."
No athlete from a North school won gold in the 2A girls competition, though Kent Island junior Lacey Dauses was locked in perhaps the finish of the meet, as she dueled North East's Leanan Rogers down the final stretch of the 800 before getting edged at the finish line. Rogers won in 2:21.53, while Dauses finished second in 2:21.63. Dauses also took second in the 400 (1:01.35.).
Harford Tech won the 2A girls competition with Kent Island taking third. Harford Tech also won the 2A boys title, while Kent Island took second.

title: Saints storm into semifinals
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Saints storm into semifinals

 May 16, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 593
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — St. Michaels High head baseball coach Brian Femi wanted to get his pitchers some work Friday.The Saints' batting order certainly did its part to put whoever was on the mound at ease, scoring nine first-inning runs on the way to an 18-1 victory over Chesapeake Math and IT Academy North in a Class 1A state quarterfinal at Harold Baines Field that was stopped in the bottom of the fourth inning due to a severe thunderstorm that rolled through the area.
Umpires halted the game with one out in the bottom of the fourth due to lightning. Not long after the field was cleared, heavy rains pounded the field. Femi said CMIT-North head coach Mark Snyder conceded the game.
Third-seeded St. Michaels (15-5), which has now won seven of its last eight, will wait to learn who it will meet in the state semifinals. Femi said the site had not yet been determined as of early Friday night.
Sixth-seeded CMIT-North finished the season 10-6.
"We figured we'd be able to get all of our pitchers some work that haven't thrown in awhile," Femi said after Brock Grow, Eli Wallace and Bobby Fink combined for a one-hitter. "Brock (Grow) hasn't thrown in a good while so we wanted to give him a couple of innings, And then everybody else an inning. You never know what's going to happen in your next game and how many pitchers you're going to need. So that was our objective that we had coming in; trying to get them loose, get them working."
Grow started and faced seven batters over two innings. The right-hander didn't allow a hit or run, struck out four and walked one. Eli Wallace pitched a scoreless third, yielding no hits and registering two strikeouts. Bobby Fink came on in the fourth, issued a leadoff walk before Andriel Terrero lined a clean, opposite-field single down the left field line for the Golden Tigers' lone run.
CMIT-North starting pitcher Calvin Brown Jr. gave up a leadoff single to Blake Wheatley (2 for 3, two RBIs) in the first, then walked Connor Wheeler (1 for 2, two RBIs) and Will Sherwood (2 for 2, RBI) to load the bases.
After a strikeout, Pearson Greenwood and Ethan Royer were each hit by pitches, driving in a run apiece for a 2-0 lead. Brown logged his second strikeout of the inning before walking Jack Brennen to score Sherwood and reload the bases. Grow (2 for 2, five RBIs) cleared them quickly, drilling a three-run double into the left-field corner for a 6-0 lead before taking third on an error.
Wheatley walked. Wheeler then hammered a 1-2 offering to left field for a two-run double. Sherwood followed with a bad-hop single over the head of CMIT-North shortstop Oswaldo Bonilla, plating Wheeler with the ninth run of the rally.
"We were getting our guys to keep their head down on the ball, trying to advance runners and those kinds of things," Femi said. "I was pleased with the way we hit the ball. We've also been playing really solid defense and we continued to do that today."
Brown retired the Saints in order in the second but then got touched for eight runs in the the third that featured two-run doubles from Wheatley and AJ Dove that fattened the lead to 13-0. St. Michaels added a run on an error before Quinn Gowe hit an RBI double and Grow followed with a two-run double for a 17-0 lead.
CMIT-North reliever Joan Bonilla issued a pair of walks before Lane Cappa's RBI infield single completed the scoring before the storm.

title: Bucs oust defending state champs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bucs oust defending state champs

 May 18, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 678
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Kent Island High's defense knew halftime adjustments were coming.The Buccaneers also recognized they needed to make changes themselves before hearing their coaches instructions at the break.
"I think they just realized they had to do some little things well," Kent Island boys head lacrosse coach Bobby Woolley said of his defense. "They weren't communicating very well I think in the opening quarters. They just realized if they didn't change the way they were playing themselves before we made some coaching adjustments, it was going to come down to win or lose. And they didn't want to let it go based on things they had control over. I think they just kind of settled down and focused, and that was a big help for us in the second half."
It proved to be just that, as the Bucs limited Glenelg to just two second-half goals Friday night en route to a 12-8 victory over the defending state champions in a Class 2A state semifinal at Glen Burnie High.
The top-seeded Bucs (16-1) advance to Tuesday's 2A state championship, where they will face No. 3 seed Stephen Decatur (15-1) at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium at 8 p.m. in a bid for their third state title in four years.
It will be the first time two Bayside Conference schools have met in a state final since 1996, when Cambridge-South Dorchester defeated Kent County for the 1A state football championship.
It will also be the third meeting this season between the two Bayside powers. Kent Island won the March 28 regular-season game, 14-13, on Gavan Henry's goal as the final horn sounded. The Seahawks gained a measure of revenge May 5, when they earned a 13-11 victory in the conference championship.
"Kind of created some adversity for ourselves early," said Woolley, whose team trailed the Gladiators 4-2 after one quarter Friday. "And they're a good enough team to capitalize in pretty much any situation. We just got to eliminate those open-door opportunities to give other offenses a chance. We need to make them find their way, not give them an open door."
That early deficit could have potentially poked a hole in the confidence of the Bucs, whose bid for a third straight state title was ended last year via a 16-8 loss to Glenelg in the state semifinals.
"We talked about that," Woolley said. "'Hey look, it's not any moment. The score is quick to change in this game. So if we find ourselves in a trail position, just stay focused on the job at hand and know we can change the game quickly ourselves.'"
Kent Island outscored the Gladiators 4-2 in the second quarter to forge a 6-6 halftime tie.
The Bucs then moved to 9-7 lead in the third quarter. Mark Rees set up brother Brian Rees' go-ahead goal early in the third before Connor Gardner and Keegan Green (hat trick) added unassisted strikes later.
Colton Schneck gave Kent Island a 10-7 lead, when he converted a feed from Green. Glenelg (12-5) got within 10-8, but Schneck scored off a pass from Mark Rees (three assists), then watched Brian Rees complete his hat trick courtesy of Connor Byrne's dish for a 12-8 lead.
Robert Jones' goal was Glenelg last, as Gavan Henry, Eric Hofmann, Ryan Austin, Robert Hottel, Finn McGrath, Aidan Henry and Bryne tightened their ranks defensively.
"It's six-man defense, not one man trying to make things happen," Woolley said. "That's the way we've been preaching all year."
Then there was freshman goalie Quinn Burns, who made five of his 12 saves in the fourth quarter.
"It's a little tough to look at a freshman and say, 'Hey, we're riding with you,'" Woolley said of his decision to make Burns the starting goalie at the beginning of the year. "The good news there was Quinn had varsity starting experience as the soccer goalie for the entire I think fall season. So I knew he was at least exposed to kind of what it takes to play at that level and perform."
Aidan Henry finished with two goals and an assist, Gardner had two assists, and Marshall Dandy contributed one goal and one assist.

title: CHAMPIONS
author: Bill Haufe
content:
CHAMPIONS

 May 20, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Champions 
 
 1036
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It all felt like a dream for Hank Wolters.That was certainly understandable. After all, Saints Peter and Paul High's goalie had only been dreaming about this moment for 11 years.
"I've been wanting to do this ever since I saw my dad three-peat back in 2014," Hank Wolters said of his father and Sts. Peter & Paul boys head lacrosse coach Freddie Wolters, who was an assistant when the Sabres reeled of three consecutive Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association B Conference championships from 2012-14. "Ever since then, that's been one of my goals in life was to win a championship with my dad."
Father, son and the rest of the Sabres achieved that goal Friday night, dethroning three-time defending champion Archbishop Curley, 11-9, at Towson University's Johnny Unitas Stadium.
"I definitely think we knew we could have done it," said Hank Wolters, who made 13 saves and watched senior teammate Noah Zimmerman net a game-high five goals. "I was always confident that we could have done it. It's just the fact that we actually did it. It feels like a dream almost."
The Sabres' bid for their first crown in 11 years didn't exactly get off to a dream-like start, as a severe thunderstorm forced an over two-hour delay. That was a blessing in the eyes of Coach Wolters, who spoke of Bud Lewis, the Sabres' former head coach who passed away in 2017, and Benedict Dyer, who died in a 2023 automobile accident and would have been a senior on this year's team.
"I think Bud Lewis was definitely there," Freddie Wolters said. "I truly believe him or Benedict Dyer. … Those guys helped us because we were not ready to play. We had a horrible warm-up; no energy.
"And when we came back out after two hours they gave us 10 minutes (to warm up) and it was like a different team," Coach Wolters said. "An absolutely different team. I think their nerves probably calmed down. They relaxed because they had some time and we started off on fire."
Zimmerman, JJ Rardin (two goals, two assists) and Andrew Steinhardt (two goals, assist) each scored goals to stake the Sabres (14-7) to an early 3-0 lead. Sts. Peter & Paul carried a 4-2 lead into the second quarter, and held a 6-5 edge at the break when it got a crucial stop. With the Friars on an extra-man opportunity, Hank Wolters made a big save near the end of the half. Curley (11-6) still had the EMO for the first 17 seconds of the third quarter. But on the opening faceoff, freshman longpole Cole Phillips scooped the ground ball, helping the Sabres kill off the remaining time.
"That was a big spark for us," Coach Wolters said.
Still, the Friars rallied for a 7-6 lead in the third period. That could have potentially swung momentum toward Curley, which defeated Sts. Peter & Paul in last year's championship, 18-9, and rallied for a 10-7 win over the Sabres in this year's regular-season clash.
But this was not the same team matchup from a year ago, when the senior-heavy Friars defeated a Sabres squad loaded with sophomores and freshmen.
"We had a couple of seniors but the core of the team were sophomores and freshmen," Freddie Wolters said. "Curley had 17 seniors and were going for their third straight title. They'd been there. They were experienced. This year we had experience.
"I also think our juniors and seniors are really good leaders," Coach Wolters continued. "We have seven freshmen and they really contributed and those guys prepared them."
Sts. Peter & Paul's head coach noted one other big ingredient in the Sabres' resiliency — a brutal early-season schedule.
"We ran the gauntlet at the beginning of the year," Wolters said of a slate that included games against Calvert Hall — which at the time was ranked No. 2 nationally — Bullis Prep, Good Counsel and Severn. "We played big-time teams. And yeah, maybe we lose but you get use to playing big-time teams, and I think that experience helps."
That resiliency surfaced as the Sabres showed they too could counter punch. Goals by freshman Mason Roland and Zimmerman pushed Sts. Peter & Paul back in front at 8-7, a lead it never relinquished the rest of the way.
Steinhardt found the back of the net in the closing seconds of the third. Rardin then set up Roland's second goal before extending the Sabres' four-goal run with one of his own for an 11-7 lead.
"I thought JJ probably played his best game of the year because they were double-teaming him," Freddie Wolters said. "And instead of trying to force everything himself he was a team player and got everybody involved. So I was really, really impressed."
That five-goal swing proved more than enough for the Sabres defense and its junior goalie.
"That Curley team, they fought extremely hard," Hank Wolters said. "They came back and they were up at one point in the third. The whole team was a little discouraged when they went up. Once that fourth quarter started, we started getting a couple goals in a row and and I was like, 'All right. I think we got this.' It was like 11-7 and I was like, 'We're not letting four goals in in a quarter.' There was no way our defense was going to let in four goals."
The Friars managed to two more, but that was it as the Sabres goalie and defensive standout Porter Bishop stood together in the closing moments before the final horn.
"All I could do was talk to him and say, 'We actually did it,'" said Hank Wolters, who heaped praise on his defense. "They played absolutely amazing, especially when we went into our zone. That's the best we ever ran our zone all year. And it really worked against Curley. They just played their butts off the entire game."
Freddie Wolters also spread praise, applauding Curley head coach Chris Ogle, Sabres assistants Dickie Grieves, Casey Grieves, Josh Patterson, and Liam Helmly, athletic director DJ Davis and principal Scott Wilson. Then the head coach applauded his players.
"We didn't play selfish," Freddie Wolters said. "We weren't pointing fingers. We played as a team, as a brotherhood, a family, and it showed. I'm proud of them. Hard work goes a long way."

St. Michaels Running Festival sells out spots

 May 20, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: AHMAD GARNETT agarnett@chespub.com | Section: Local News 
 
 404
 Words

 ST. MICHAELS — The 2025 St. Michaels Running Festival, hosted by Charm City Run sold out this past weekend with attendance north of 2,600 runners plus their family and friends.Although a heavy rain storm hit the east coast Friday evening, multiple runners came out for a sunny Saturday of running and community engagement.
"The race was a sell-out at a little over 2,600 people," said Will Murdoch, director of events for Charm City Run and race director for St. Michaels Running Festival. "I think we're right around that number in 2024. We restricted it a little bit more in 2025, and so we were back up this year in 2026, but 2,600 runners plus their family and friends and spectators, so it draws a really big crowd."
The Running Festival consists of three races: the half marathon, the 10k run, and the 5k run and walk. According to the race website, 1,184 individuals participated in the half marathon, 659 individuals participated in the 10k and 377 individuals participated in the 5k.
While the race brings competitive racers, Charm City Run's is focused on the experience it provides as well as the race.
"What we found is it's a little bit less about competitive runners, but it's more about people that just want to have a great experience with their friends and their family," Murdoch said. "They run the race together, some of the people make a weekend out of it and then they just enjoy the town.
"It's a little less about, you know, assembling a field of really fast runners versus like let's just try to deliver the best experience we can."
Murdoch credits St. Michaels for being an attractive place which brings runners into town.
"People love being in St. Michaels, especially on a day like we had on Saturday," Murdoch said. "It's a great place to be, the town is beautiful, the area that we host the post-race party at the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum is a beautiful spot. So, people want to be there."
According to Murdoch, the race is a big economic driver for the town.
"On Friday night, all of the restaurants along Talbot Street are full of people who have come to town," Murdoch said. "... And so, while we haven't been able to completely quantify that impact right now, all the hotel rooms in Easton and farther out are sold out Friday night into Saturday. You can't get a hotel room in Talbot County."

title: Kent Island boys win lacrosse state final for third time in four years
author: AHMAD GARNETT agarnett@chespub.com
content:
Kent Island boys win lacrosse state final for third time in four years

 May 21, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: AHMAD GARNETT agarnett@chespub.com | Section: High Schools 
 
 598
 Words 

 Read News Document

 OWINGS MILLS — The Kent Island Boys lacrosse team hoisted the state championship trophy over their heads, as fans cheered loudly above.The celebration followed Kent island 13-12 victory in the 2A state championship on Tuesday.
The celebration was not just the result of the team's preparation earlier that day, although that was a major factor. The boys and their coaches had been working for this trophy long before the season started.
"Taking into this game, we had a lot more emphasis on our game plan prep and really that was the difference," Kent Island head coach Bobby Woolley said. "We really put a lot of extra emphasis on how to play them, not just going out and playing lacrosse but really trying to trigger some things that would potentially prove valuable."
He said the Buccaneers had "...just enough of a game plan to make our guys feel confident so that we can start fast and that's what happened tonight."
The Buccaneers (17-1) won their third state title in four years with a 13-12 win over the Stephen Decatur Seahawks (15-2) on Tuesday at Stevenson University.
This state battle marked the first time two Bayside Conference schools competed in a state championship contest since 1996, when Cambridge defeated Kent County for the 1A state football title.
It also marked the third meeting this year for the Buccaneers and the Seahawks, who split the season series.
Kent Island came out fast in the first two minutes of the contest with three shots on goal, all saved by Stephen Decatur goalie, Declan Horan, but Kent Island sophomore midfielder Connor Gardner drew first blood with a goal at the 10-minute mark.
The Buccaneers went on to score multiple goals on the Seahawks, leading 7-2 at halftime.
Stephen Decatur fought back in the second half with a 4-0 run to bring the contest within one at 7-6 during the third quarter. Seahawks head coach Hoffy Hoffman called the second-half surge just a settling of nerves for his team.
"This is our first ever state championship in lacrosse. ... and we all felt like this was the storybook ending that we should have had," Hoffman said. "We fell short unfortunately tonight. ... We'll be back next year."
Buccaneers midfielder Marshall Dandy fought back for Kent Island as the score tightened, nailing his fourth goal in the third quarter to turn the game into a shootout from that point on.
Dandy credits his fourth goal to his team just slowing the game down after Stephen Decatur's big run.
"We definitely just possess the ball, take care of it," Dandy said. "The other team can't score if they don't have the ball, so we just slowed it down, got into our six on six. We're very confident we could bet anybody six on six."
With the Buccaneers lead sitting at 8-6, the game turned into a shootout through the last quarter with Stephen Decatur tying the score at 12-12 with four minutes left.
Gardner who started the game with the first goal, came in clutch for the Buccaneers hitting his third goal of the day and the last goal of the contest at the 3:24 mark in the fourth quarter giving the Buccaneers the lead, 13-12.
"It was high energy moments, the crowd was buzzing, the boys were buzzing, I had to make impact," Gardner said.
Woolley said that this state championship win felt amazing because of the preparation that went into the season.
"There's no way ... no better way of putting it," Woolley said. "The early mornings, the late nights, the countless hours that you pour into it that those guys, even the players, never know about; it feels really good."

title: St. Michaels baseball advances to state final
author: Bill Haufe

St. Michaels baseball advances to state final

 May 21, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: High Schools

 FREDERICK — St. Michaels High's baseball team used a trick play, Will Sherwood's pitching, and a four-run second inning Tuesday to earn a 4-3 victory over seventh-seeded Pikesville in a Class 1A state quarterfinal at McCurdy Field.The third-seeded Saints (16-5) advance to Saturday's 1A state final, where they will face top-seeded Allegany (17-4) at Prince George's Stadium in Bowie at noon.
Sherwood was working on a two-hit shutout when the Panthers bunched three singles and two walks into a three-run rally in the seventh inning. Pikesville had the tying run on second with two outs, when the Saints executed the hidden-ball trick to perfection. Sherwood spun and faked a throw to second, drawing the Panthers' runner off second. St. Michaels' senior ace, who still had the ball in his glove, raced behind Pikesville's final hope and tagged him out for the final out.
The Saints scored four runs in the second. Pearson Greenwood walked and was lifted for courtesy runner Brandon Toadvine. Ethan Royer walked. Brennen Dean beat out a bunt single. Pikesville ace came back with a pair of strikeouts. But Blake Wheatley dropped a bunt to score a run. Royer scored on a wild pitch. Connor Wheeler then smacked a double to left-center field, plating Dean and Wheatley for a four-run lead.

title: University of Maryland names James E. Smith as athletic director
author: Staff Writer
content:
University of Maryland names James E. Smith as athletic director

 May 22, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Colleges 
 
 1058
 Words 

 Read News Document

 COLLEGE PARK — The University of Maryland has named James E. Smith as its new Barry P. Gossett Director of Athletics. Smith will come to UMD from the Atlanta Braves where he has been serving as the senior vice president of business strategy."We are proud of the athletics tradition here at the University of Maryland and of the accomplishments of our coaches and student-athletes who represent the red, black, white and gold," said UMD President Darryll J. Pines. "As college athletics rapidly evolves, Jim brings valuable administrative and business experience, plus the energy, vision and passion to lead our athletics program to new levels of success and impact."
Smith has worked in athletics for more than two decades at both university and professional organizations, including the Atlanta Braves, the Ohio State University, Atlanta Falcons, AMB Sports & Entertainment, and the Columbus Crew among others. He will oversee the university's Department of Intercollegiate Athletics team of more than 250 full-time staff members who support more than 550 student-athletes.
"It is a great honor to be chosen to lead the athletics department at the University of Maryland and to guide UMD's storied programs into the next era," said Smith. "I am highly motivated to build upon excellence and lead Maryland forward in a dynamic and pivotal time for intercollegiate athletics, with a sharp focus on student-athlete health, well-being and academic success."
In his five-year tenure with the Braves, he has led a team focused on implementing innovative business, brand, marketing and communications strategies to drive revenue, engagement and membership growth. Smith's visionary leadership and strategy team assisted the organization in rapid growth, resulting in significant increases in annual ticket sales, concessions and retail. He is the Braves' point person for the 2025 MLB All-Star Game at Truist Park.
Smith was previously with the Ohio State University Alumni Association, where, as president and CEO, he led one of the largest alumni associations in the world, including a team of more than 80 professionals, and oversaw a $17 million budget. He implemented new strategies focused on innovative alumni engagement and outreach, resulting in a 10% annual revenue growth in two years, and 15% increase in alumni participation. He also led the development of a new marketing and communications strategy focused on increasing affinity for the university, including redesigned publications, social media strategy and the launch of an app to enhance alumni communications.
Smith held a series of senior executive positions at Arthur M. Blank Sports & Entertainment (AMBSE), in charge of all revenue and marketing for the National Football League's Atlanta Falcons, Major League Soccer's Atlanta United, and the design and development of the $1.6 billion Mercedes-Benz Stadium project. He developed a strategic revenue generation plan for the stadium, creating a state-of-the-art facility to meet the needs of an evolving industry. He provided oversight of all sales functions for the stadium, including negotiating naming rights, sponsorships and suite sales. At AMBSE, Smith was the driving force in the creation of Atlanta's MLS franchise, Atlanta United, the most successful launch of a soccer franchise in the country's history.
He is currently a board member for the Mitsubishi Electric Senior PGA, Gwinnett County Chamber, and Arete Scholars. He holds a bachelor's degree in communications from Northwestern University and a master's degree in sports management from the Ohio State University.
Smith's arrival at Maryland follows an era of recent successes and milestones for the Terrapins, beginning with the university's entry into the Big Ten Conference and the Big Ten Academic Alliance in 2014. New facilities, such as the Jones-Hill House Football Performance Center; the new Barry Gossett Basketball Performance Center; and the Barry and Mary Gossett Hall for Academic and Personal Excellence of Student-Athletes, have raised the university's profile as a leader and innovator in athletics.
In addition, Smith takes the helm at a time when Maryland teams have landed significant achievements. Since joining the Big Ten, Maryland has captured 49 conference championships, the third-most of any school during that span. Additionally, Maryland has secured six of its 47 national team championships over the last decade in the Big Ten.
Smith brings with him a network of colleagues and consultants who have led elite college athletics. Smith plans to tap the consulting talents of his former colleague, the retired and legendary athletic director for the Ohio State University, Gene Smith.
Smith's selection follows a national search led by an internal search committee, led by Vice President for Legal Affairs and General Counsel Jay Rosselló and Arts and Humanities Dean Stephanie Shonekan, and supported by TurnKeyZRG. He assumes his new position on July 15. A press conference to introduce Smith to the UMD community will be scheduled, and additional details will follow.What people are saying
"Jim is a proven and exceptional talent who has excelled in a variety of professional sports organizations," said Big Ten Commissioner Tony Petitti. "He will be a wonderful addition to the Big Ten Athletic Director group and I look forward to working with him."
"Intercollegiate athletics is undergoing rapid change. The A.D. position is evolving as well," said Gene Smith, former Senior Vice President and Director of Athletics at The Ohio State University. "Jim Smith's experiences on campus and with pro sports make him uniquely qualified to lead the Terrapins program. Organizations like Ohio State, the Braves, the Falcons and Atlanta United are all exceptional, making Jim a tremendous hire."
"Jim is an outstanding leadership addition for the University of Maryland," said Rich McKay, CEO of AMB Sports and Entertainment. "His track record in sports speaks for itself, and his ability to build strong relationships and navigate complex situations while thinking creatively and strategically is what set him apart during his time with the Atlanta Falcons. I'm certain those same skills will serve him well in this new role. Maryland is getting someone who understands the business of sports and knows how to lead within it."
"The University of Maryland is getting a seasoned sports executive with a proven track record of enhancing championship organizations," said Derek Schiller, President and CEO of the Atlanta Braves. "Jim is bringing more than 20 years of successful experience strategically building revenue and developing talent at the professional and collegiate levels. He is an excellent communicator with an innate ability to lead in complex multifaceted organizations. There is no doubt that he will take Maryland's athletic program to new heights and we wish him nothing but the best."

title: St. Michaels' state title bid falls short
author: AHMAD GARNETT agarnett@chespub.com
content:
St. Michaels' state title bid falls short

 May 24, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: AHMAD GARNETT agarnett@chespub.com | Section: News 
 
 492
 Words 

 Read News Document

 BOWIE — The St. Michaels High's baseball team lost to top-seeded Allegany 6-2 Saturday in the Class 1A state baseball final at Prince George's Stadium.The Campers (18-4) capitalized on three errors and two RBI singles in the bottom of the fourth inning to earn their first state championship since 1990.
Although the inning got rough, St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi decided to keep starting pitcher Brock Grow in the game. Femi credited Grow for his ability to fight back after a tough inning.
"We didn't think that he was an issue. We were making errors," said Femi, who team finished 18-7. "We normally get him around 80 pitches, and then that's where his tiring point is. He had a three-up, three-down inning after the bad inning."
The game was scoreless through three innings. Then St. Michaels' bats came alive with a single to center field by first basemen Brennen Dean.
Senior Bobby Fink came in as a courtesy runner, stole second and third and scored on Grow's sacrifice squeeze, making the score 1-0 after the top of the fourth inning.
The bottom of the fourth kicked off with the Campers reaching on a walk and an error. Campers third baseman Landyn Ansel bunted a comebacker to Grow, whose throw to first was off the mark, which led to the runner on second scoring.
After the error, with two runners on base, designated hitter Liam Buck singled to center field, driving in two runs. After another error on a bunt, the Campers had runners on second and third.
Buck then stole home on a pick-off move to third where he dodged the catcher's glove to score. The runner on second was called out after a throw back from the catcher to third, and with only one out the Campers led 4-1.
After a walk by right fielder Eli Imes, pitcher Myles Bascelli moved Imes up to second on a sacrifice bunt. With two outs, second baseman Cole Ricker singled to center field, scoring Imes for a 5-1 lead. Shortstop Kohen Madden grounded out to end the inning.
After a quiet fifth inning for both teams, the Saints fought back with a run. Dean walked and was lifted for freshman courtesy runner Brandon Toadvine, who stolen second base.
Toadvine then scored on an errant throw to third base by Campers catcher Justin Wakerfield, making the score 5-2.
The Campers came back in the bottom of the sixth with an insurance run by Bascelli with a bloop single to left field, making the score 6-2 at the end of six.
The Saints reached on a base hit by Brody McDaniel with two outs, but McDaniel was caught stealing at second to end the game.
Femi looks forward to working this offseason and building off the momentum of the state final appearance.
"The factor is you have to work hard and do the things in the offseason," Femi said. "We preach do all the little things, so if they do that, these guys will make many trips here."
